In 2023, Flipkart contributed $700 million to the total through ESOP liquidity provided as compensation for the decline in value following the PhonePe spin-off, while other startups together accounted for $102 million in buybacks.
The cumulative ESOP buybacks by Indian startups since 2020 have reached approximately $2 billion ($1,977 million).

In the ongoing calendar year, Mumbai-based software testing platform BrowserStack has led ESOP liquidity events with a $125 million share buyback programme aimed at employees and early investors. The initiative enables nearly 500 employees to sell their shares, with roughly half of the total amount reserved for them, while the remaining portion is allocated to early backers such as Accel.

Healthtech firm Innovaccer has also completed a $75 million ESOP buyback, offering liquidity to both current and former employees holding vested stock options. Media reports indicate that several holders of restricted stock units also benefited, although the exact number remains undisclosed.

Crypto exchange CoinDCX , despite being in the spotlight for multiple developments, repurchased ESOPs worth $12 million. Meanwhile, edtech company Unacademy rolled out a Rs 50 crore ($5.5 million) ESOP buyback programme to provide liquidity to its workforce. Founder Gaurav Munjal stated that eight employees are expected to earn over Rs 1 crore each, 17 employees will receive more than Rs 50 lakh, and 38 employees are likely to make upwards of Rs 10 lakh. This comes at a time when the edtech sector continues to face fundraising challenges, with the SoftBank-backed firm eventually being acquired by upGrad.

title: TraqCheck raises $8 Mn Series A led by IvyCap Ventures
description: TraqCheck, an AI enterprise startup focused on HR systems, has raised $8 million in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures, with participation from IIFL. Snippets
body: TraqCheck, an AI enterprise startup focused on HR systems, has raised $8 million in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures, with participation from IIFL.
The proceeds will be used to expand in Europe, strengthen its AI agent offerings, and scale go-to-market efforts across enterprise customers.
Founded by Armaan Mehta and Jaibir Nihal Singh, TraqCheck is building AI agents to automate hiring workflows, including talent sourcing, screening, and background verification.
The startup offers products such as Trace, an automated background verification agent, and Nina, a conversational sourcing agent that identifies and qualifies candidates.
TraqCheck claims to have nearly 300 enterprise customers across India and Europe using its platform.
Back in September last year, TraqCheck had raised funding from angel investors such as Peyush Bansal and Alok Oberoi.

title: Leegality crosses Rs 80 Cr revenue in FY25, profit jumps over 2X
description: Leegality reported a strong 2.4X growth over the past two fiscal years, with revenue increasing from Rs 33.5 crore in FY23 to Rs 81.1 crore in 2025.
body: Digital documentation and e-signature platform Leegality reported a strong 2.4X growth over the past two fiscal years, with revenue increasing from Rs 33.5 crore in FY23 to Rs 81.1 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2025. The Gurugram-based firm also turned profitable during this period.

Leegality’s revenue from operations grew 30.3% year-on-year to Rs 81.08 crore in FY25 from Rs 62.22 crore in FY24, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr . Including Rs 5.52 crore from other income, its total revenue stood at Rs 86.6 crore in FY25.

The company offers digital document logistics and e-sign APIs (including BharatSign, NeSL, and BharatStamp), along with verification, automated workflows, and tracking. Its eSign and eStamping solutions contributed over 99% of operating revenue, with around Rs 50 lakh coming from other operating streams.

Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost component, rising 22.1% to Rs 44.38 crore. E-sign charges recorded the sharpest increase, up 50.7% to Rs 14.30 crore, followed by technology expenses, which grew to Rs 7.87 crore.

Its advertisement expenses rose to Rs 3.52 crore, while other overheads stood at Rs 11.30 crore during the fiscal year. Overall, total expenses for Leegality increased by 25.3% to Rs 81.37 crore in FY25 from Rs 64.96 crore in FY24.

The revenue growth, combined with relatively moderate cost expansion, helped improve the company’s bottom line. Leegality reported a profit of Rs 3.7 crore in FY25, up from Rs 1.12 crore in FY24. However, its ROCE and EBITDA margins remained negative at -3.07% and -1.27%, respectively.

On a unit basis, the company spent Re 1 to earn a rupee in FY25, compared to Rs 1.04 in FY24. It reported cash and bank balances of Rs 77.37 crore, with total current assets standing at Rs 82.19 crore.
According to media reports, Leegality has raised a total of $6.63 million across funding rounds, including a $5 million Series A led by IIFL Fintech Fund, with participation from Mumbai Angels.

title: Nexus sells another Rs 186 Cr stake in Delhivery via block deals
description: Nexus Venture Partners has continued trimming its stake in Delhivery, selling shares worth Rs 186 crore through block deals on the NSE, just days after offloading a 1.6% stake in the company last week.
body: Nexus Venture Partners has continued trimming its stake in Delhivery, selling shares worth Rs 186 crore through block deals on the National Stock Exchange, just days after offloading a 1.6% stake in the company last week.
Last week, it sold nearly 1.2 crore shares at Rs 442 per share for approximately Rs 530 crore (around $57 million).
Today, Nexus Venture Partners, through its funds Nexus Ventures III and Nexus Opportunity Fund, sold 40 lakh shares of Delhivery at Rs 465 apiece, amounting to a total deal value of Rs 186 crore.

On the buying side, the stake was absorbed by a mix of domestic and foreign institutional investors. Morgan Stanley emerged as the largest buyer, acquiring 12 lakh shares at Rs 465 apiece, amounting to Rs 55.8 crore, followed by Edelweiss Mutual Fund, which purchased shares worth approximately Rs 50 crore.
Other participants in the transaction included Goldman Sachs, Nippon India Mutual Fund, and Hong Kong-based hedge fund Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund.

As of December 31, 2025, Nippon India Mutual Fund held a 2.9% stake in Delhivery and has further increased its holding following a Rs 202 crore investment in the company last week. In contrast, Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs did not hold any stake in the firm prior to this transaction.
On the financial front, Delhivery reported an 18% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 2,805 crore in Q3 FY26, while profit rose 59% to Rs 40 crore.
At the end of today’s trading session, shares of Delhivery closed at Rs 456.6 apiece, valuing the company at a total market capitalization of Rs 34,181 crore (approximately $3.66 billion).

title: Accel raises $5 Bn for AI and late-stage bets
description: Venture capital firm Accel is set to raise a $4 billion Leaders Fund to back late-stage startups globally, according to a report by Bloomberg.
body: Venture capital firm Accel is set to raise a $4 billion Leaders Fund to back late-stage startups globally, according to a report by Bloomberg.

The firm is also raising an additional $650 million sidecar fund to increase exposure in select portfolio companies, as it doubles down on high-conviction bets. The Leaders Fund will be deployed across growth-stage startups, with artificial intelligence emerging as a key investment theme.
Accel has already deployed capital from its Leaders strategy in India, including an investment in Spinny , where it co-led a $160–170 million round alongside Fidelity.
The move comes as global investors concentrate capital into fewer high-quality companies, with a strong tilt toward AI-led businesses amid a prolonged funding slowdown.
Accel’s Leaders Fund typically participates in late-stage rounds of its portfolio companies and select new investments. It helps companies scale ahead of public listings or large exits.

This follows Accel’s $650 million early-stage fund for India and Southeast Asia announced in January 2025. The fund targets pre-seed to Series A startups across sectors such as AI, consumer, fintech, and manufacturing.

Accel has been an active early-stage investor in India for over a decade and claims to be the first institutional backer in a majority of its portfolio companies. Its investments in the region include Flipkart, Swiggy, Freshworks, Acko, BlackBuck, BrowserStack, Urban Company, and Zetwerk.
Beyond capital, Accel supports founders through initiatives such as SeedToScale, its knowledge platform, and Accel Atoms, an early-stage scaling program.

title: PhysicsWallah set to acquire stake in Rojgar With Ankit
description: While this would be the first acquisition for PhysicsWallah since its listing in November 2025, the Noida-based company increased its stakes in Xylem Learning and Utkarsh Classes in December last year.
body: Edtech unicorn PhysicsWallah is all set to acquire a partial stake in edtech platform Rojgar With Ankit, according to a media report. While this would be the first acquisition for PhysicsWallah since its listing in November 2025, the Noida-based company increased its stakes in Xylem Learning and Utkarsh Classes in December last year.
In a stock exchange filing addressing the media report, the company said it is in discussions with relevant parties, including Rojgar with Ankit.

The deal is likely to value Rojgar With Ankit at around Rs 400–500 crore in its initial tranche, sources told Entrackr. The investment is expected to involve a minority stake, although the exact size of the stake could not be immediately ascertained.
Sources indicated that the potential investment aligns with PhysicsWallah’s strategy to strengthen its presence in the upskilling and government job preparation segment.

While the contours of the deal are still being finalised, there could be plans to integrate certain offerings of Rojgar With Ankit with PhysicsWallah’s existing platform to drive user growth and engagement, sources added.
It could not be confirmed whether the transaction will involve multiple tranches or follow-on investments.
PhysicsWallah did not respond to queries sent by Entrackr till the time of publication.

Founded in 2020, Rojgar With Ankit operates in the government job preparation segment. The company reported revenue of Rs 62.26 crore and a profit of Rs 5.35 crore in FY25. It has not raised external funding so far.

title: Euler Motors founder’s stake falls to single digits after fresh funding
description: Euler Motors has raised over $120 million in the past year, including a recent $47 million Series E round led by Lightrock. However, multiple funding rounds have diluted the founder’s stake to below 4% (excluding MSOP).
body: Commercial EV maker Euler Motors has been on an aggressive fundraising spree, raising over $120 million in the past year to fuel its growth. Most recently, the company secured $47 million in a Series E round led by Lightrock. However, successive funding rounds have significantly diluted the founder’s stake, which has now fallen to below 4%, excluding MSOP.

To delve deeper into Euler’s latest Series E round, Entrackr has reviewed the company’s regulatory filings to uncover details such as the round's breakdown, shareholding structure, and current valuation.

According to the filings, the company has issued 5,58,780 Series E Cumulative Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares and 10 equity shares at an issue price of Rs 7,829 to raise Rs 437.5 crore or $47 million.

Lightrock, through its Energy Access Acceleration Fund, led the round with a Rs 225 crore ($24 million) maiden investment in the firm, while Hero MotoCorp followed up its earlier Rs 510 crore investment with an additional Rs 210 crore ($22.6 million) in the Series E round. Existing investor Blume Ventures also participated with Rs 2.5 crore.
Apart from equity, Euler Motors also raised Rs 250 crore in debt from BlackSoil, Trifecta Capital, InnoVen Capital, and Alteria Capital.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, Euler Motors valuation remained flat at Rs 2,137 crore, or approximately $230 million, post allotment. For context, the company’s valuation had also remained unchanged in its Series D round.
Prior to this round, the Delhi-based firm had raised over Rs 1,420 crore (more than $150 million), including a Rs 638 crore Series D round.

Following the latest allotment, Hero MotoCorp remains the largest shareholder with a 36.67% stake. New investor Lightrock will hold 10.53%, while existing backer Blume Ventures owns 5.9%. Founder Saurav Kumar’s stake has diluted to 3.66%, and the company has set aside 5.14% for ESOP and MSOP pools.

title: Brain health platform Ivory raises $1 Mn in seed round
description: Ivory is addressing a critical gap in India’s healthcare ecosystem by making cognitive screening accessible, trackable, and a part of routine preventive care. It has al
body: Brain health platform Ivory has raised $1 million in a seed funding round from Draper Associates, SAGE Venture Fund, MoSJE, IFCI Ventures, and SIDBI. It was also featured on Shark Tank India last year.
The Mumbai-based startup had earlier raised $1 million in a funding round co-led by IIM-A Ventures and Capital A in April last year and $500K from Capital A in February 2024.

The proceeds will be utilised to strengthen the technology stack, expand clinical capabilities, and enhance product offerings, particularly in building scalable, evidence-based solutions, Ivory said in a press release.

Co-founded in early 2023 by Issac John and Rahul Krishnan, Ivory is a brain health startup focused on early detection and proactive cognitive care. By combining neuroscience, neuropsychology, and data-driven interventions, the platform helps individuals maintain and enhance their cognitive well-being.

The company offers clinical-grade cognitive assessments and personalised brain health solutions through its app, enabling users to track and optimise their cognitive health. It is supported by a multidisciplinary clinical team spanning neuroscience, neurology, general medicine, and neuropsychology.

Ivory is addressing a critical gap in India’s healthcare ecosystem by making cognitive screening accessible, trackable, and a part of routine preventive care. It has also been expanding partnerships across the healthcare ecosystem and recently collaborated with Metropolis Healthcare to launch the TruHealth Mind & Body package—an integrated preventive health offering that combines pathology diagnostics with neuroscience-based cognitive assessments.

The company may directly or indirectly compete with global platforms such as Cogstate, Altoida, Pearson, BrainCheck, and Linus Health. Additionally, it competes with traditional pen-and-paper assessments such as MoCA, MMSE, and ACE-III.

title: Paytm becomes majority Indian-owned as domestic investors raise stake
description: Fintech major One97 Communications, which operates Paytm, has become a majority Indian-owned company, according to its latest shareholding disclosure.
body: Fintech major One97 Communications, which operates Paytm, has become a majority Indian-owned company, according to its latest shareholding disclosure.  The development comes amid increasing regulatory focus on ownership structures of fintech firms.

A closer look at the company’s shareholding pattern shows a clear shift over the past two years. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs), which held a dominant 72.11% stake in June 2023, have reduced their holding to 49.4% as of March 2026.

In contrast, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) have significantly increased their stake in the company. Their shareholding has jumped from 3.54% in June 2023 to 23.08% in March 2026. The public shareholding also saw a slight increase, which rose from 24.35% in June 2023 to 27.51% in March 2026.

The decline in foreign ownership, coupled with a sharp rise in domestic institutional holding, has been a key factor in making Paytm a majority Indian-owned firm. With increased participation from DIIs and public shareholders, the overall Indian shareholding has risen to 50.59%.
The data also indicates that domestic capital has been consistently increasing its exposure to the company, even as foreign investors trimmed their positions over multiple quarters.
The change in ownership comes at a time when companies with foreign investments, particularly those linked to entities such as Ant Group, have been under closer regulatory scrutiny in India.
Becoming a majority Indian-owned company could help Paytm address regulatory concerns and improve operational flexibility, especially in its financial services business.

On the financial front, One97 Communications has also shown improvement in its performance. The company reported a 20% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 2,194 crore in Q3 FY26, up from Rs 1,828 crore in the same quarter last year. It also posted a net profit of Rs 225 crore during the quarter.

title: GobbleCube raises $15 Mn in Series A round led by Susquehanna
description: GobbleCube, an AI-based brand analytics platform, has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Susquehanna Venture Capital. News
body: GobbleCube, an AI-based brand analytics platform, has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Susquehanna Venture Capital.
The round also saw participation from existing investors InfoEdge Ventures and Kae Capital.
The startup had previously raised $3.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by InfoEdge Ventures along with Kae Capital in July 2025.
The proceeds will be used for product development, hiring, and expanding its global presence. It is also focusing on advancing its AI capabilities and strengthening go-to-market efforts.

Founded in 2022 by Manas Gupta, Srikumar Nair, and Nitesh Jindal, GobbleCube builds an AI-powered platform for consumer brands. The platform helps brands manage digital commerce operations including demand forecasting, pricing, supply chain, and performance tracking.
GobbleCube aggregates data across multiple marketplaces and internal systems to provide insights and automate decision-making.
It connects functions such as sales, marketing, and inventory to improve revenue outcomes and reduce inefficiencies.
GobbleCube claims to have onboarded over 400 brands across enterprise and D2C segments. Its platform is integrated with multiple digital commerce platforms across India, MENA, and LATAM regions.

title: Proptech startup Helium raises angel funding from Albinder Dhindsa, Kunal Shah, others
description: Helium, a residential rental platform focused on gated society apartments, has raised Rs 5 crore in an angel funding round from startup founders. Snippets
body: Helium, a residential rental platform focused on gated society apartments, has raised Rs 5 crore in an angel funding round from startup founders and operators including Albinder Dhindsa, Kunal Shah, Pankaj Chaddah, Mohit Gupta, Akriti Chopra, Gunjan Patidar, and Nitin Gupta.
The proceeds will be used to expand across Bengaluru and increase supply in gated communities in the coming months.

Founded by Sahil Ludhani and Ashutosh Tandon, the firm operates a full-stack rental model. It works directly with homeowners and offers guaranteed rental income while managing tenant relationships and operations.
Helium focuses on onboarding apartments in gated communities. It claims that a limited share of such homes is listed online, with most transactions happening through brokers or offline networks.

The brand also offers a deposit product called Deposit Saver. This links tenant deposits to credit profiles and allows users to rent homes with deposits as low as one month. The remaining deposit is facilitated through NBFC partners, while homeowners receive the full deposit amount.
Helium launched in Whitefield around six months ago and has onboarded around 170 homes. It reports an average rental cycle of 14 days.

title: Polaris raises $80 Mn from British International Investment
description: Polaris Smart Metering Private Limited has raised Rs 710 crore (around $80 million) in financing from British International Investment (BII) for its subsidiary Hooghly. Snippets
body: Polaris Smart Metering Private Limited has raised Rs 710 crore (around $80 million) in financing from British International Investment (BII) for its subsidiary Hooghly Smart Metering Private Limited.
The funding will be used to deploy over 2.2 million smart meters in West Bengal and expand Polaris’ advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) footprint.
Polaris is an I Squared Capital portfolio company providing end-to-end smart metering solutions, including manufacturing, deployment, communications infrastructure, and software platforms.

The company currently has an order book of around $1.1 billion, covering projects across Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Manipur, with a total of 7.5 million electric meters. It also operates in the smart gas metering segment with 1.6 million meters.

British International Investment is the UK’s development finance institution that invests in businesses across emerging markets. In India, its portfolio includes Ather Energy, ZestMoney, KreditBee, Veritas Finance, and U GRO Capital. It recently invested in Ecofy, a climate-focused NBFC, which raised $42 million in a Series B round.

title: Men’s personal care brand Unbound raises Rs 8 Cr led by Fireside Ventures
description: The Gurugram-based brand focuses on engineering high-performance formulations that combine multiple functions into one seamless experience. This approach is rooted in
body: Men’s personal care brand Unbound has raised Rs 8 crore in a funding round led by Fireside Ventures.
The fresh funds will be utilized to launch its first range of products across skin, hair, and body care, Unbound said in a press release.

Co-founded by Kanika Mittal and Atul Arora, Unbound is a performance-led self-care brand for men designed for modern lifestyles. The brand creates high-efficacy, multi-functional products across skin, hair, and body care.

Unbound addresses everyday stressors such as sweat, sun exposure, pollution, and hard water through solutions that are efficient, intuitive, and effective. The brand is currently preparing for its launch in India.

The Gurugram-based brand focuses on engineering high-performance formulations that combine multiple functions into one seamless experience. This approach is rooted in simplifying grooming and making it more intuitive and time-efficient for modern consumers.

India’s men’s personal care market has largely been shaped by basic hygiene offerings or adapted versions of broader beauty products. However, evolving lifestyles are beginning to shift this narrative. A new generation of men is increasingly engaging in fitness, outdoor activities, and high-performance routines, creating demand for products that are not just functional but also adaptive.

title: The Hosteller raises Rs 150 Cr in Series B round led by PROMAFT and V3 Ventures
description: he Hosteller claims that it operates more than 75 properties across 13 states and has hosted over 20 lakh unique travellers. Over the past 12 months, the company has ad
body: Backpacker hostel chain The Hosteller has raised Rs 150 crore (approximately $16 million) in a Series B funding round co-led by PROMAFT Partners and V3 Ventures, along with participation from ITI Growth Opportunities Fund, Merisis Wealth Trust, and prominent family offices.

The Mumbai-based company had previously secured $5.7 million in a Series A funding round led by existing investor V3 Ventures, in a mix of debt and equity infusion, in November 2024, and $1 million in a pre-Series A round led by FAO Ventures in November 2021.

The fresh capital will be deployed towards accelerating its expansion across key travel destinations, while further strengthening operational efficiencies and brand building, The Hosteller said in a press release.

Founded in 2014 by Pranav Dangi, The Hosteller provides affordable, standardized, and experiential accommodation for young travelers, digital nomads, and explorers. The company offers a network of more than 55–65 locations, including dorms, private rooms, and cafes, focusing on community-driven travel experiences.

The Hosteller claims that it operates more than 75 properties across 13 states and has hosted over 20 lakh unique travellers. Over the past 12 months, the company has added over 30 properties and grown traveller capacity by nearly 70%.

The company is targeting 25,000 beds nationwide within the next 36 months and is preparing to launch a travel super app integrating accommodation, F&B, mobility, and curated experiences into a single platform.
It competes with goSTOPS , Wudstay, and Backpackers Panda, among others.

title: Cohoma Coffee raises Rs 5 Cr seed round led by IPV
description: Cohoma Coffee, a specialty coffee roaster and machine manufacturer, has raised Rs 5 crore ($0.53 million) in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures. Snippets
body: Cohoma Coffee, a specialty coffee roaster and machine manufacturer, has raised Rs 5 crore ($0.53 million) in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures, with participation from Swishin VC.
The proceeds to scale its manufacturing capabilities and expand into international markets.

Founded by Kanika Birla and Paritosh Birla, Cohoma Coffee offers a range of specialty coffee products designed for quick preparation without the need for equipment. It also manufactures super-automatic coffee machines for hospitality and corporate clients.
The startup operates a vertically integrated model, sourcing beans globally, roasting in-house, and building its own brewing machines.
Cohoma has built an omnichannel presence across retail, ecommerce, and B2B partnerships, serving hotels, offices, and cafes. It is also present in retail chains such as Nature’s Basket and Le Marche.
The firm offers naturally flavoured coffee products without added sugar or preservatives and operates café-style kiosks in modern retail stores.
Cohoma claims a repeat customer rate of over 90% across its platform.

title: Aliste Technologies raises Rs 30 Cr in pre-Series A led by Big Global JSC
description: Aliste Technologies, an energy management and IoT solutions startup, has raised Rs 30 crore ($3.2 million) in a pre-Series A round led by Big Global JSC. Snippets
body: Aliste Technologies, an energy management and IoT solutions startup, has raised Rs 30 crore ($3.2 million) in a pre-Series A round led by Big Global JSC, with participation from YourNest VC and HBeon Labs.
The round includes a mix of equity and debt.
The funds will be used to strengthen research in energy-focused solutions and expand distribution of its enterprise offerings.
Founded in 2021 by Anant Ohri, Aakarsh Nayyar, Bhavya Kansal, Konark Gautam, and Shreyansh Jain, Aliste provides energy monitoring and optimisation solutions for commercial spaces.
The startup currently manages over 1.5 lakh IoT assets across more than 20 cities and tracks around 3 million units of energy consumption monthly.
Aliste offers solutions across co-living, retail, restaurants, and hospitality, helping businesses monitor energy usage, reduce costs, and improve operational efficiency.
The brand claims that its systems help reduce energy bills by up to 20% and has enabled savings of around 3,28,000 kilograms of CO2 per month.

title: Pentathlon Ventures leads Rs 17 Cr seed round in industrial AI startup Intellithink
description: ts flagship solution, IntelliVibe, uses AI and proprietary sensors to detect machine faults and help prevent unplanned downtime. The company plans to launch an electric
body: Intellithink, an industrial AI startup focused on machine health and energy efficiency, has raised Rs 17 crore in a seed round led by Pentathlon Ventures, which invested Rs 6.5 crore through its India Fund II. Anicut Capital and Veltis Capital also participated.
The company will use the funds to expand its customer base across India and the Middle East and accelerate commercialization of its AI platform.
Founded in 2017 by Sridhar Venugopal and Aswin Venu, Intellithink provides an IoT-enabled platform for predictive maintenance, remote monitoring, and fault diagnosis to improve industrial efficiency.

Its flagship solution, Intellivibe, uses AI and proprietary sensors to detect machine faults and help prevent unplanned downtime. The company plans to launch an electrical health solution for rotating equipment by mid-2026.
Intellithink says it has served over 50 enterprises, including Jindal Steel, JSW Steel, and Adani, and is seeing growing traction in international markets.
The startup competes with Infinite Uptime, Nanoprecise, Augury, and UptimeAI.

title: IndiGo picks stake in Sarla Aviation, eyes flying taxi market
description: IndiGo has acquired an equity stake worth Rs 10 crore in Sarla Aviation, marking its entry into the electric air taxi segment. The investment was made IndiGo. News
body: IndiGo has acquired an equity stake worth Rs 10 crore in Sarla Aviation, marking its entry into the electric air taxi segment. The investment was made through IndiGo Ventures in January and aligns with the airline’s interest in emerging urban air mobility technologies.

Founded in 2023, Sarla Aviation is developing electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for use as flying taxis. Its flagship product, “Shunya”, is designed for urban transport and is expected to be launched in Bengaluru by 2028.

The aircraft is being designed to carry up to 680 kilograms, with seating for six passengers, excluding the pilot. It is expected to operate using existing helipads at hotels, hospitals, and tech parks.
The startup had earlier raised $10 million in January last year in a round led by Accel, with participation from Binny Bansal, Nikhil Kamath, and Sriharsha Majety.
IndiGo’s investment follows the collapse of its earlier non-binding partnership with Archer Aviation, which did not proceed due to delays in timelines.

Globally, other eVTOL startups have also attracted airline backing. US-based Joby Aviation is supported by Delta Air Lines and Toyota Motor Corporation, while Archer Aviation has received a strategic investment from United Airlines.

title: ZoloStays reports Rs 342 Cr revenue in FY25; margins improve
description: Following its fivefold growth in FY24, co-living and managed accommodation platform ZoloStays continues its growth trajectory, as the company reported a 67% year-on-year
body: Following its fivefold growth in FY24, co-living and managed accommodation platform ZoloStays continues its growth trajectory, as the company reported a 67% year-on-year increase in its operating scale. At the same time, the losses for the firm reduced by 38% to Rs 35 crore.
Bengaluru-based ZoloStays’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 342.3 crore in FY25 from Rs 204.4 crore in FY24, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

ZoloStays derives the bulk of its income from accommodation and allied services provided to students, professionals, and organizations. This segment accounted for 80% of its operating revenue which surged 73.6% to Rs 273 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 99.8 crore in FY24.

ZoloStays also provides services to colleges and universities for managing residential facilities, along with food subscriptions and other related amenities. Income from this segment declined 30.7% to Rs 62.9 crore.
The firm also earned Rs 3.6 crore in interest income, bringing its total income to Rs 346 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2025.

For the accommodation providing platform, property management was the largest cost center, accounting for 67% of the overall expenses which rose by 83.6% to Rs 254.9 crore. Employee benefit expenses remained stable at Rs 82.4 crore, while depreciation declined 28.2% to Rs 12.5 crore.
Advertising and promotional expenses, donation subscriptions, commission and other overheads led  overall expenses rose by 43.3% to Rs 381.1 crore in FY25 from Rs 266 crore in FY24.

Despite strong revenue growth, Zolo remained loss-making at the operating level. Its loss before exceptional items narrowed to Rs 35.2 crore in FY25 from Rs 56.8 crore in FY24, indicating an improvement in core business performance.

title: OTP Ventures leads pre-seed round in fragrance brand FIFTH SENSE
description: According to the Gurugram based brand, its debut collection includes four fragrances, namely The Boyfriend Shirt, The Chosen One, Still Here, and The Athlete In You. The
body: Fragrance brand FIFTH SENSE has secured Rs 6.3 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by OTP Ventures, along with participation from Sadev Ventures, ISV Capital, and key angel investors, including Swiggy CEO Rohit Kapoor and StayVista co-founder Amit Damani.

The proceeds will be deployed for the expansion of its product portfolio, content-driven brand building, and strengthening of its supply chain and distribution capabilities, FIFTH SENSE said in a press release.

Launched this year by Bharat Gupta and Prateek Gupta, FIFTH SENSE is a premium D2C fragrance brand that aims to disrupt India’s fragrance market by offering climate-calibrated and emotion-led perfumes. The brand has officially launched with four debut fragrances.

According to the Gurugram based brand, its debut collection includes four fragrances, namely The Boyfriend Shirt, The Chosen One, Still Here, and The Athlete In You. The brand has worked with independent perfumers using globally sourced ingredients, formulated with over 25% oil concentration that remains effective in Indian weather conditions.
Currently, the brand sells its products through its own website and plans to establish a presence on e-commerce and quick commerce platforms in the upcoming quarters.
It competes with other notable brands in this space, such as Titan Skinn, Contraband, Secret Alchemist, and Fraganote, among others.

title: India adds over 55,000 startups in FY26, highest since Startup India launch
description: India’s startup ecosystem added a record 55,000+ recognised ventures in FY26, the highest annual addition since the Startup India programme launched on January 16, 2016, according to a government release.
body: India’s startup ecosystem added a record number of recognised ventures in FY26, with over 55,000 startups officially registered during the year, according to a recent government release. This marks the highest annual addition since the launch of the Startup India programme on January 16, 2016.

With this, the cumulative number of DPIIT-recognised startups has crossed 2.23 lakh across the country. These startups span across multiple industries, ranging from technology, healthcare, education to agritech and manufacturing, reflecting the broad-based expansion of entrepreneurial activity.

Since inception, these recognised startups have generated over 23.36 lakh direct jobs. More than 1.07 lakh startups have at least one woman director or partner, accounting for approximately 48% of all recognised startups, according to the release.

Geographically, startup growth is becoming more evenly distributed, with a presence across all states and union territories. Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, and Gujarat have emerged as leading hubs in terms of recognised startups and direct employment generation as of March 31, 2026.

The Government continues to back startups through key schemes like the Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS), Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS), and Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS), offering support across different growth stages.

Under FFS, over Rs 7,000 crore has been deployed to 135+ AIFs by FY26, which have in turn invested Rs 26,900+ crore in more than 1,420 startups. Building on this, the government has also launched the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 with a Rs 10,000 crore corpus.
Startup-led innovation has also boosted intellectual property creation, with over 19,400 patent applications filed by startups. Patent filings rose from more than 2,850 in FY25 to over 4,480 in FY26.

Startups are also increasingly participating in public procurement through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), which has emerged as a key demand channel for them. According to the release, startups on GeM have secured cumulative orders worth over Rs 19,000 crore in FY26.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startup this week [Apr 13 - Apr 18]
description: This week, 17 Indian startups raised around $129 million, comprising 2 growth-stage, 12 early-stage deals and 3 startups kept their funding undisclosed. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 17 Indian startups raised around $129 million, comprising 2 growth-stage, 12 early-stage deals and 3 startups kept their funding undisclosed.
In contrast, 31 startups had collectively secured about $594.4 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups saw muted activity this week, with just two deals raising a combined Rs 860 crore. Polaris Smart Metering Pvt Ltd led the tally, securing Rs 710 crore from British International Investment (BII) for its subsidiary, Hooghly Smart Metering Private Limited. Meanwhile, backpacker hostel chain The Hosteller raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B round co-led by PROMAFT Partners and V3 Ventures.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $33 million across 12 deals this week. GobbleCube, an AI-driven brand analytics platform, led the activity with a $15 million Series A round backed by Susquehanna Venture Capital. Meanwhile, AI enterprise startup TraqCheck, which focuses on HR systems, secured $8 million in a Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures, with participation from IIFL.

Aliste Technologies, an energy management and IoT startup, has raised Rs 30 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Big Global JSC, with participation from YourNest VC and HBeon Labs, while Intellithink, an industrial AI startup focused on machine health and energy efficiency, secured Rs 17 crore in a seed round led by Pentathlon Ventures. IndiGo has acquired an equity stake worth Rs 10 crore in Sarla Aviation, marking its entry into the electric air taxi segment.

Brain health platform Ivory, men’s personal care brand Unbound, fragrance brand FIFTH SENSE, a specialty coffee roaster and machine manufacturer, and three other early-stage startups also secured funding this week.

title: Healthcare automation startup Coral raises $12.5 Mn from Z47 and Lightspeed
description: Coral, a healthcare automation startup focused on the US administrative market, has raised $12.5 million from Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Lightspeed. Snippets
body: Coral, a healthcare automation startup focused on the US administrative market, has raised $12.5 million from Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Lightspeed.
The proceeds will be used to scale the engineering team and hire domain experts in healthcare operations.

Founded by IIT Hyderabad alumni Ajay Shrihari and Aniket Mohanty, who were previously founding engineers at LimeChat, the firm automates back-office workflows that typically rely on manual coordination and fax machines.

The platform integrates directly with existing Electronic Health Records (EHRs) and payer portals to handle patient intake, prior authorizations, and insurance verification without requiring providers to change their existing software.

Coral initially launched in the durable medical equipment sector and has since expanded into infusion centers and specialty pharmacies. The firm’s technology handles document processing for handwritten faxes and insurance cards with a reported 99.7% accuracy, reducing complex intake times to under five minutes.

Current product development is focused on an AI workflow builder that allows providers to design custom automations and a co-pilot layer to analyze operational data such as claim denial rates and referral patterns. This investment adds to Z47’s portfolio of AI-driven enterprise companies, which includes firms like Rocketlane and Krutrim.

title: IPO-bound Acko trims 5% workforce
description: Digital insurtech firm Acko has laid off around 60 employees, nearly 5% of its workforce, as part of an internal restructuring linked to the integration of artificial intelligence.
body: Digital insurtech firm Acko has trimmed around 5% of its workforce, with nearly 60 employees impacted, as part of an internal restructuring linked to the integration of artificial intelligence, according to a report by Mint .
The affected employees are expected to remain with the company until the end of June. An Acko spokesperson has confirmed the development to Entrackr .

The move is part of a shift in how the company is organising teams, with a sharper focus on AI-led workflows, evolving performance metrics, and new skill requirements aligned with its next phase of growth, rather than a cost rationalisation effort.

The layoffs come alongside the exit of chief marketing officer Ashish Mishra, who is currently serving his notice period after nearly five and a half years at the company. He is likely to be succeeded by Nitin Khanna, an internal leader with over seven years of experience at Acko.

The company, which had around 1,200 employees as of March 2026, is seeing certain roles become redundant as part of this transition. This is Acko’s second round of layoffs, following job cuts during the Covid-19 pandemic.

The development comes as Acko prepares for a proposed $300–400 million IPO in FY27. Founded in 2016 by Varun Dua and Ruchi Deepak, the company has raised over $458 million to date, according to TheKredible.
Acko’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,837 crore in FY25 from Rs 2,106 crore in FY24, while losses narrowed 37% to Rs 424 crore.

In the same space, rival Digit Insurance reported a 4.5% dip in revenue to Rs 2,142 crore in Q3 FY26, even as profit rose 18% to Rs 140 crore. Meanwhile, Navi has recently entered motor insurance, intensifying competition.

title: Groww crosses Rs 3 lakh Cr in customer assets; to deploy profits and fresh funds into lending biz
description: Groww has crossed Rs 3 lakh crore in customer assets, even as the company continues to report strong profitability and plans to double down on its lending business.
body: Fintech major Groww has crossed Rs 3 trillion (Rs 3 lakh crore) in customer assets, even as the company continues to report strong profitability and plans to double down on its lending business.

According to its Q4 FY26 shareholder letter and financial results, the Bengaluru-based firm posted a total revenue of Rs 1,535.5 crore in the March quarter, up from Rs 849.5 crore in the same period last year. The company also reported a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 686 crore in Q4 FY26.

Groww’s total customer assets rose 36% year-on-year to touch Rs 3 trillion. As per the letter, its user growth remained steady during the quarter. It reported 21.6 million transacting users, while its active user base stood at 16.7 million. Active users grew 6% quarter-on-quarter and 25% year-on-year.

Groww also continues to gain market share across segments. Its mutual fund market share increased to 14%, while its share in stock broking and equity derivatives stood at 15.7% and 10.6%, respectively, as per the shareholder letter. This comes amid rising competition in the broking ecosystem, where pricing and distribution continue to play a key role.

On the profitability front, the firm is improving the contribution from its credit business. Groww said that its lending vertical is now seeing better unit economics and has started contributing meaningfully to overall profits.

Going forward, the company plans to deploy its earnings, along with proceeds from its recent fundraise, towards scaling its lending operations. The focus will be on expanding its balance sheet-led lending business across broking and consumer credit segments.

While the core business remains profitable, some of Groww’s newer bets are still in the investment phase. Its recently acquired wealthtech platform Fisdom, reported a loss of Rs 10.2 crore in Q4 FY26 and is expected to turn profitable by FY28 as integration and scale improve.

Similarly, its asset management arm, Groww Mutual Fund (Groww MF), posted a loss of Rs 21.4 crore during the quarter. The company noted that the AMC business is still in an early “build-out phase” and will require a 5–6X increase in assets under management (AUM) to achieve profitability over the next few years.

title: Axten Hospitals raises Rs 2.5 Cr led by PedalStart
description: Axten Hospitals, a surgical care startup, has raised Rs 2.5 crore in its first structured funding round led by PedalStart, with participation from angel investors. Snippets
body: Axten Hospitals, a surgical care startup, has raised Rs 2.5 crore in its first structured funding round led by PedalStart, with participation from angel investors.

The proceeds will be used to launch three new hospital facilities over the next 12 months through an asset-light expansion model focused on partnerships, branding, legal setup, and working capital. Axten also plans to launch a technology platform for patient discovery, booking, and post-operative care.
Founded by Gauttam Chhabra, Axten Hospitals operates specialised surgical facilities with a focus on standardised care delivery, operational efficiency, and fixed pricing.

The startup launched its pilot facility in East of Kailash, New Delhi, in FY25 and reported around Rs 9 crore in revenue in its first year while remaining EBITDA positive. Axten focuses on high-volume procedures across general surgery, orthopaedics, gynaecology, urology, ENT, and oncology.
The firm’s core model offers fixed-price surgical packages under its “Honest Surgery Price” approach, aimed at reducing surprise billing and improving pricing transparency.
The startup plans to build a network of over 25 facilities across the top five metro cities and target Rs 250 crore in revenue over the next five years.

title: Groww reports Rs 686 Cr profit on Rs 1,500 Cr revenue in Q4 FY26
description: Groww  reported its Q4 FY26 results. During the period, the company more than doubled its profit to Rs 686 crore, while at the same time its revenue from operations rose 88% YoY to cross Rs 1,500 crore.
body: Digital investment platform Groww on Monday reported its Q4 FY26 results. During the period, the company more than doubled its profit to Rs 686 crore, while at the same time its revenue from operations rose 88% year-on-year to cross Rs 1,500 crore.
The company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 1,505 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 801 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from NSE.

Other income contributed an additional Rs 30 crore, which pushed total income to Rs 1,535.5 crore for the quarter. For the full year ended March 2026, Groww reported a 19% year-on-year increase in operating income to Rs 4,645 crore, while its profit crossed the Rs 2,000 crore threshold in FY26.

On the expense side, employee benefits formed the largest component, accounting for 29% of total expenses at Rs 173 crore in Q4 FY26. Finance costs stood at Rs 8 crore, while depreciation expenses rose to Rs 24.45 crore.
Overall, the Lalit Keshre-led firm reported a 38% increase in total expenditure to Rs 599 crore in the quarter, compared to Rs 435 crore in Q4 FY25.
Groww reported net profit of Rs 686 crore in Q4 FY26, more than double from Rs 309 crore in Q4 FY25, as revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses by a notable margin.

Groww continued to add more new stock market users than the rest of the industry combined, even as market activity slowed due to geopolitical tensions. In February, the platform added 2.55 lakh clients, which took its total client base to around 1.27 crore (12.75 million) and pushed its market share to 28.03%.

During the quarter, Ashish Agrawal, former MD at Peak XV Partners, stepped down from the board of Groww as he plans to begin his entrepreneurial journey and set up a new venture capital firm, according to his resignation letter.

title: Artha Venture leads seed round in personal care brand Clarity Labs
description: Since launching its flagship functional soap line, The BAR, in March this year, it has expanded its presence across its D2C website, Amazon, and Flipkart. The roadmap
body: Personal care brand Clarity Labs has raised over Rs 4 crore at the valuation of 20 crore pre-money in a seed funding round led by Artha Venture Fund II, along with participation from angel investors.

The proceeds will be used to accelerate new product development, expand categories, and scale omnichannel distribution across D2C, marketplaces, and quick commerce, Clarity Labs said in a press release.

Launched in November last year by Karan Dokras, Clarity Labs is a personal care brand focused on creating functional, daily-use skincare solutions tailored for Indian consumers. The startup aims to offer affordable, non-complex products that fit seamlessly into daily routines.

The Indian personal care market is characterized by high product proliferation and low regimen adherence. Consumers want outcomes but often struggle to sustain complex routines. Clarity Labs addresses these challenges with transparent formulations and measurable performance, aiming to build trust by embedding effective treatment into habitual steps.

According to the Gurugram-based startup, its products emphasize functional personal care and hygiene, specifically addressing common skincare concerns with products like anti-acne, de-tan, muscle relief, and sensitive skin soap bars.

Since launching its flagship functional soap line, The BAR, in March this year, it has expanded its presence across its D2C website, Amazon, and Flipkart. The roadmap includes expansion into adjacent wash categories, including hair wash, body wash, and face wash, while continuing to build within soaps through new variants and formats.
It competes with other notable brands in this space, such as DERMATOUCH, Ghar Soaps, Chemist At Play, and Hoop.

title: Med-tech tourism startup CureMeAbroad raises pre-seed round
description: The platform currently lives with a directory of over 6,000 hospitals across 47 countries and 45 specialties, and works with more than 380 accredited partner hospitals a
body: Medical tourism discovery platform CureMeAbroad has raised $600K in a pre-seed funding round from Roman Saini, Himanshu Ratnoo, Kunal Gupta, Devaiah Bopanna, and Vikrant Potnis.

The fresh capital will be used for technology investments, including expanding its AI cost estimator, clinical matching models, and multilingual patient intelligence layer that powers the discovery engine, the company said in a press release.
According to a market report, the global medical tourism market is projected to reach $174 billion by 2035.

Co-founded in June 2025 by Aditya Oza and Mikhail Bohra, CureMeAbroad is an AI-first discovery platform that connects international patients with suitable hospitals, surgeons, and destinations. It uses a proprietary AI cost estimator trained on over 634 procedure records and operates under HIPAA certification.

The platform currently lives with a directory of over 6,000 hospitals across 47 countries and 45 specialties, and works with more than 380 accredited partner hospitals across key medical tourism hubs such as Mexico, Turkey, Thailand, India, and Georgia.

The company plans to accelerate growth across target source markets, starting with the GCC, UK, and Africa. It aims to address industry challenges such as lack of trust, opaque pricing, reliance on WhatsApp agents, unverified clinic listings, and limited aftercare accountability.
CureMeAbroad competes with platforms such as Bookimed, PlacidWay, The Medical Tourism Company, and Medical Departures.

title: Zerodha backed Rainmatter invests in wealth tech startup PrimeInvestor
description: PrimeInvestor has raised Rs 19.5 crore in its first external funding round led by Rainmatter, to double down on its newly launched portfolio management services.
body: Wealth-tech platform PrimeInvestor has raised Rs 19.5 crore (around $2 million) in its first external funding round led by Rainmatter, to double down on its newly launched portfolio management services.

The investment from Rainmatter is purely financial, with no strategic involvement, ensuring full independence for the company, co-founder Srikanth Meenakshi told Entrackr . “They have been very clear that this is a financial investment and we continue to operate independently,” he said.

Founded in 2020 by the team behind FundsIndia, PrimeInvestor started as a research platform offering curated insights and portfolio strategies. However, the firm soon identified a gap between advice and execution.

“We realised advice alone isn’t enough, as investors lack time to manage portfolios,” said Meenakshi, citing insights from analysing 12,000 portfolios worth over Rs 25,000 crore, which showed even high-value investors held sub-optimal allocations.

To address this, PrimeInvestor has launched a discretionary PMS offering for investors with a minimum investment of Rs 50 lakh, aiming to bridge the gap between advice and execution through portfolio management.
We are positioning PMS as a wealth solutions platform, combining mutual funds and equities with a focus on asset allocation and risk management,” added Vidya Bala, co-founder PrimeInvestor.
The firm follows a fee-only model, charging 0.6% to 1.2% annually with no performance fees, linking revenue to assets under management.
According to Bala, the use of direct mutual fund plans removes commissions and lowers costs. “Our strategy prioritises downside protection, aiming to outperform while limiting losses,” she said.

title: Audio series platform Pocket FM elevates Lalit Gangwar as COO
description: Pocket FM, which claims over 250 million listeners globally, has been expanding its content formats and investing in AI-driven storytelling tools. The company also opera
body: Pocket FM has elevated Lalit Gangwar to chief operating officer. In his new role, he will oversee its global audio business, managing markets, growth, monetisation, and execution.

According to Pocket FM, Lalit Gangwar is a founding member who built its India growth playbook, scaling the platform to 150 million users in its first year. He later led its US expansion, setting up teams and driving growth.
The move comes as Pocket FM looks to strengthen its operating structure to support more predictable, long-term growth at scale, particularly in overseas markets such as the US.
Gangwar stated that the company will continue to focus on scaling global markets, investing in AI-led storytelling, and strengthening monetisation.

Pocket FM, which claims over 250 million listeners globally, has been expanding its content formats and investing in AI-driven storytelling tools. The company also operates a large creator ecosystem with over 300,000 writers and more than 100,000 audio series on its platform.

Pocket FM recorded a 68% increase in revenue to Rs 1,768 crore in FY25 and recently claimed to have crossed an ARR of Rs 4,167 crore with EBITDA profitability. On the other hand, its rival Kuku FM reported a nearly three-fold year-on-year jump in its revenue to Rs 242 crore in FY25 . The Fundamentum-backed firm’s losses jumped by 60% to Rs 153 crore.

title: Raise Financial acquires algo trading platform Stratzy in cash-and-stock deal
description: Raise Financial Services, the parent company of Dhan, has acquired algorithmic trading and investing platform Stratzy in a cash-and-stock deal.
body: Raise Financial Services, the parent company of Dhan, has acquired algorithmic trading and investing platform Stratzy in a cash-and-stock deal, according to a press release.
While the deal value was not disclosed, Stratzy will continue to operate independently as a wholly owned subsidiary of Raise, the company said in a statement.

Founded as an exchange-registered algo trading platform, Stratzy offers over 100 approved multi-asset algorithms across equities, indices, F&O, and commodities. The platform enables users to deploy ready-made, rule-based trading strategies, catering to the growing demand for systematic investing among retail traders.

According to the release, the acquisition aligns with Raise’s strategy of building a full-stack, technology-led capital markets ecosystem. The company operates stock trading platform Dhan, along with products such as Fuzz AI, Upsurge, and Filter Coffee.
Raise Financial Services acquired new age financial media startup Filter Coffee in January 2025 and is also set to take over wealthtech startup Infinyte Club .

With this deal, Raise plans to introduce a curated and managed algorithmic investing layer on Dhan, making structured, system-driven strategies more accessible to a wider set of users. The company also intends to invest in Stratzy to enhance its product offerings, execution infrastructure, and overall user experience.
Stratzy’s founders and team will continue to run the platform, focusing on scaling its technology and expanding integrations across multiple broking platforms.

In February this year, Dhan crossed the 1 million user mark after adding 19,000 new users in a month. On the financial front, the company has also shown strong growth as its revenue from operations surged 2.3X to Rs 877 crore in FY25, while profits stood at Rs 408 crore.

title: Health QSR chain Acai Theory raises funds from All In Capital, TDV Partners, others
description: Acai Theory, a health-focused quick service restaurant (QSR) brand, has raised Rs 4 crore in a pre-seed funding round co-led by All In Capital and TDV Partners,
body: Acai Theory, a health-focused quick service restaurant (QSR) brand, has raised Rs 4 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by All In Capital along with participation from TDV Partners and a clutch of prominent angel investors, including ex-COO of Zomato Food Delivery Rinshul Chandra, Harpreet Grover, Anurag Prasad, Fragaria CEO Harish Varadarajan, and others.
The proceeds will be allocated towards expansion, team building, and brand visibility, while also strengthening its supply chain and R&D, Acai Theory said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2025 by Rishav Ranjan and Akash Kyal, Açaí Theory is a health-first açaí QSR brand that aims to redefine how consumers experience healthy eating. The brand offers a superfood-led menu anchored in nutrient-dense açaí bowls that are both indulgent and wholesome.

The Bengaluru-based startup aims to build a health-focused yet indulgent QSR platform, bridging the gap between taste, nutrition, and convenience through nutrient-dense açaí bowls. The brand operates on a QSR-first, assembly-only model with no live cooking, enabling speed and consistency.

Açaí Theory claims that it currently operates its flagship outlet in Bengaluru, where it has served over 10,000 bowls in the last six months since its launch in October 2025. Anchored around açaí, a globally popular Amazonian superfood from Brazil, the QSR menu features a range of açaí bowls, smoothies, and superfood-based snacks.

The startup plans to scale to 8–10 stores across Bengaluru, set up a central kitchen to ensure consistent quality, and deploy AI-led tools alongside digitised SOPs to drive operational efficiency and scalability across outlets.
It may directly or indirectly compete with other startups in this space, such as Lyfberry, Acai By The Bay, and Temple of the Senses.

title: Legal-tech startup Lawyered bags $2.5 Mn led by Rainmatter and Turbostart
description: Legal tech startup Lawyered has raised $2.5 million in a pre Series A funding round co led by Rainmatter by Zerodha and Turbostart, along with participation from its existing investor Finvolve.
body: Legal tech startup Lawyered has raised $2.5 million in a pre Series A funding round co led by Rainmatter by Zerodha and Turbostart, along with participation from its existing investor Finvolve.

The Gurugram-based startup had previously secured Rs 8.5 crore on the business reality show IdeaBaaz at a Rs 120 crore pre money valuation from Pawan Jaggi, VC investor Sandesh Sharda, The Sleep Company co-founder Priyanka Salot, and Arjun Vaidya.

The fresh capital will be deployed towards scaling technology infrastructure, strengthening product offerings, and accelerating user acquisition, with a focus on expanding AI led capabilities, Lawyered said in a press release.

Launched in 2018 by Himanshu Gupta, Lawyered is a legal tech company that acts as an AI driven on road legal assistance platform, specializing in "LOTS247" (roadside legal aid) and "ChallanPay" (traffic fine resolution) to serve vehicle owners, drivers, and logistics businesses. The platform aims to build India’s go to platform for identifying and resolving legal risks in mobility.

According to Lawyered, it is creating the legal infrastructure that keeps vehicles, fleets, and businesses compliant and protected, resolving risks before they disrupt lives or operations. By making compliance proactive, the platform reduces financial strain, prevents downtime, and gives both individuals and enterprises the confidence to move forward without legal uncertainty.

With legal services still largely reactive and fragmented in India, Lawyered’s Gen AI led approach transforms it from a reactive service into a proactive utility layer that is always on, embedded, and increasingly indispensable. It plans to extend beyond mobility into every sector where recurring legal risks hold people and businesses back. From finance and real estate to healthcare and e commerce, Lawyered aims to embed legal infrastructure directly into everyday operations.

Lawyered asserts that it covers over 2 million vehicles and works with more than 800 businesses across India. Its platforms, LOTS247 and ChallanPay, have resolved over 200,000 legal matters, helping users avoid more than $6 million in penalties and downtime.

title: NudgeBee raises $3 Mn in seed round led by Kalaari Capital
description: NudgeBee, an AI platform focused on cloud operations, has raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by Kalaari Capital, with participation from technology founders. Snippets
body: NudgeBee, an AI platform focused on cloud operations, has raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by Kalaari Capital, with participation from technology founders.
The funds will be used to strengthen its AI platform, expand its enterprise context layer, and build a partnership-led distribution model alongside direct enterprise sales.
Founded in 2024 by Rakesh Rajendran and Shiv Pratap Singh, NudgeBee develops AI agents for cloud operations teams, helping automate workflows, reduce manual work, and improve incident resolution.
Its platform offers AI agents for SRE, CloudOps, and FinOps functions, including troubleshooting, cloud cost optimisation, and workflow automation.
The startup uses a semantic knowledge graph and enterprise context layer that connects telemetry, infrastructure topology, historical patterns, and workflow data.
The brand is also investing in customer success and deployment capabilities to accelerate adoption among enterprise customers.

title: Rysen School operator AITS raises $4 Mn in pre-Series A round
description: Since inception, AITS has established 15 campuses across nine cities, enrolling over 10,000 students. The company aims to reach 100,000 students over the next three years
body: AITS, or Affordable Innovative Techno Services, the parent company of Rysen School, a K to 12 network with 15 campuses across Rajasthan, has raised 4 million dollars in a pre Series A funding round. The round was led by Big Capital and Redbrook Fund, with participation from Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar, Ramakant Sharma, and Roman Saini.

The company will use the funds to expand Rysen School’s campus network across emerging cities, strengthen its technology led learning infrastructure, and scale standardized school operating models, AITS said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by O.P. Godara, Kapil Arya, Dr. Kapil Jain, and Pritesh Meena, AITS is an education infrastructure and school management company focused on building scalable K to 12 institutions across Tier 2 and Tier 3 India. Through Rysen School, it combines structured academics, experiential learning, and technology enabled instruction within an asset light model.

Since inception, AITS has established 15 campuses across nine cities, enrolling over 10,000 students. The company aims to reach 100,000 students over the next three years by adding 100 new campuses across emerging markets.

It also plans to build a centralized learning ecosystem with smart classrooms, coding labs, blended learning tools, and academic analytics, along with expanding teacher training and performance tracking systems to improve student outcomes at scale.

title: Emversity acquires nurse mobility platform Lanstitut
description: Higher-education embedded training and employability platform Emversity has acquired healthcare mobility platform Lanstitut Technologies in a deal valued. News
body: Higher-education embedded training and employability platform Emversity has acquired healthcare mobility platform Lanstitut Technologies in a deal valued at around $4.25 million through a mix of cash and stock.
According to Moneycontrol, the transaction marks Emversity’s first acquisition as it expands into international healthcare hiring.

The deal has been structured as a share purchase, with Lanstitut continuing to operate independently under its existing brand. Its four cofounders, including CEO Khubaib Abdul Salam, will continue in their current roles.
Founded in 2022, Lanstitut focuses on training Indian nurses in German language skills and facilitating placements in hospitals across Germany.
The company has trained close to 3,000 nurses and employs around 200 people. It also offers visa processing, credentialing, relocation, and on-ground support services.
The acquisition will help Emversity open international demand channels for its talent pool, beginning with Germany, where healthcare worker shortages continue to rise.

Founded by former Unacademy COO Vivek Sinha, Emversity runs an education-to-employment platform embedded within universities, offering training and employer linkages across sectors such as healthcare, hospitality, engineering, and data centre operations.
The development comes months after Emversity raised $30 million in a Series A round led by Premji Invest, with participation from Lightspeed and Z47.

title: Spill Games raises $3.1 Mn in seed round led by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital
description: Mobile gaming startup Spill Games has raised $3.1 million in a seed funding round co-led by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital.
body: Mobile gaming startup Spill Games has raised $3.1 million in a seed funding round co-led by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital.
The Bengaluru-based startup had earlier secured $750K from All In Capital, M-League, and other angel investors in December 2024.
The proceeds will be used to scale its portfolio of live and upcoming titles, deepen its internal technology stack, and selectively expand the team, Spill Games said in a press release.

Co-founded in July 2024 by Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan, and Harsh Garg, Spill Games is a mobile gaming studio focused on building casual and puzzle games for a global audience. The startup leverages its proprietary Spillway engine and internal tooling to enable rapid development, iteration, and scaling of high-quality games.

According to Spill Games, its in-house engine and tooling layer help modularise and accelerate key parts of game development across analytics, retention, monetisation, and live operations. This enables the company to launch significantly faster than traditional studios, ship games roughly 4x faster, and operate with greater capital efficiency.
According to market research, mobile gaming is projected to exceed $107 billion globally in 2026.

The company currently operates in the casual and puzzle gaming segment, with a portfolio of five live games, including Cozy Finds , Sticker by Number , and Zen Math Crossword . Three of its titles have achieved positive unit economics.

Over the next 18 months, Spill plans to test more than 20 additional prototypes across casual and hybrid-casual formats and expand its monetisation mix beyond its ad-led model, including new launches in hybrid-casual and in-app purchase segments.

title: Ajinkya Rahane joins Chupps Footwear as investor and advisor
description: D2C footwear brand Chupps Footwear has onboarded cricketer Ajinkya Rahane as an equity investor and strategic advisor as part of its pre-Series B funding round Snippets
body: D2C footwear brand Chupps Footwear has onboarded cricketer Ajinkya Rahane as an equity investor and strategic advisor as part of its pre-Series B funding round. The investment amount was not disclosed. Existing investors also participated in the round.
The funds will be used to strengthen product innovation, expand its offline presence, and build brand visibility.

Founded in 2020 by Yashesh Mukhi, Chupps operates as a D2C open footwear brand with a focus on comfort wear. Rahane, who had earlier used the brand as a customer, will now collaborate with the founding team on product development, including recovery focused footwear and enhancements to its ERGO Charge technology.

Chupps has built an omnichannel presence through its own website, marketplaces such as Myntra and Amazon, and offline retail stores across key markets. The brand also has a growing presence in the UAE.
The company had earlier partnered with IPL franchises including Gujarat Titans and Mumbai Indians.

title: Bluestone’s revenue jumps 48% to Rs 681 Cr in Q4 FY26
description: Omnichannel jewellery retailer Bluestone reported its Q4 FY26 results, clocking 48% year-on-year revenue growth and a profit of Rs 31 crore. However, on a sequential basis, its profits declined 55%.
body: Omnichannel jewellery retailer Bluestone reported its Q4 FY26 results, clocking 48% year-on-year revenue growth and a profit of Rs 31 crore. However, on a sequential basis, its profits declined 55%.
Bluestone's revenue from operations increased to Rs 681 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 461 crore in Q4 FY25, as per its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

For the full year ended March 2026, the company reported a 38% increase in revenue from operations to Rs 2,436 crore, up from Rs 1,770 crore in FY25. It also turned profitable, posting a net profit of Rs 13 crore compared to a loss of Rs 222 crore in the previous year.

Bluestone generated all its operating revenue from the sale of diamond, gold, platinum, gemstone, and pearl jewellery, though it did not disclose a detailed segment-wise breakdown for the quarter. The company also recorded Rs 15 crore in non-operating income, taking its total revenue to Rs 697 crore in the first quarter.

On the expense front, the cost of materials remained Bluestone’s largest cost center, accounting for 58% of its total expenditure. This expense rose 36% year-on-year to Rs 384 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 283 crore in Q4 FY25. Employee benefits also increased 32% to Rs 73 crore in the last quarter. Overall, Bluestone’s total expenses grew by around 24%, reaching Rs 664 crore in Q4 FY26.

As the company’s revenue growth outpaced its expenses in the last quarter, it reported back-to-back profitability, posting a profit of Rs 31 crore compared to a loss of Rs 51 crore in the same quarter last year. However, on a sequential basis, profit declined 55% from Rs 69 crore in Q3 FY26.
At the close of today’s trading session, Bluestone’s shares settled at Rs 546.6, taking the company’s total market capitalisation to Rs 8,321 crore (approximately $895 million).

title: Amazon India to invest Rs 2,800 Cr to boost logistics, quick commerce push
description: The move comes months after Amazon India announced a Rs 2,000 crore investment in June 2025 to expand and upgrade its operations infrastructure, aimed at making
body: Amazon India has announced that it will invest Rs 2,800 crore (about $300 million) to strengthen its infrastructure and operations across the country, as part of its previously stated commitment to invest $35 billion by 2030.

According to Amazon India, a portion of this investment will be used to double the footprint of its quick commerce vertical. Currently, its quick commerce service, Amazon Now, operates in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, and Bengaluru, supported by around 300 micro fulfilment centres.
In addition to Amazon Now, the company said it will expand its pan India ecommerce network, including warehouses and last mile delivery stations, to improve delivery speeds.

The move comes months after Amazon India announced a Rs 2,000 crore investment in June 2025 to expand and upgrade its operations infrastructure, aimed at making deliveries faster and more reliable. That investment came at a time when horizontal ecommerce platforms were facing increasing competition from quick commerce players.
The June investment enabled the launch of 17 new fulfilment centres, six sortation centres, and 75 last mile delivery stations across India.

Amazon India also plans to deploy part of the new funds toward technology, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, within its operations network. In December last year, the company increased its India investment commitment to $35 billion.
With this, Amazon has committed around $40 billion to India between 2010 and 2024.

In FY25, revenue from operations for Amazon Seller Services, the marketplace arm of the company, rose to Rs 30,139 crore, driven by growth in marketplace services and advertising revenue. The company’s loss narrowed significantly to Rs 374 crore, reflecting improved cost control.

title: Deep Algorithm raises Rs 16 Cr in pre-Series A led by Unicorn India Ventures
description: Deep Algorithm, an AI-powered cybersecurity startup, has raised Rs 16 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Unicorn India Ventures. Snippets
body: Deep Algorithm, an AI-powered cybersecurity startup, has raised Rs 16 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Unicorn India Ventures. The round also saw participation from SB Investment (UAE), Prakash Govindan, and Himanshu Singhal.
The proceeds will be used to expand into international markets, accelerate product development, and strengthen its platform with new identity and AI security features.
Founded in 2021, Deep Algorithm builds cybersecurity products focused on identity risk management, fraud prevention, and threat detection for enterprises.
Its products include adapID-AI, a behavioural identity intelligence platform, and BotShield-AI, a solution for zero-day threat prevention, DDoS mitigation, and runtime application security.
The startup claims to have recorded a threefold rise in closing ARR from FY25 to FY26 and expects this to grow 20 times by FY27.
Deep Algorithm serves clients across BFSI, fintech, and enterprise sectors, including Canara Bank, Karnataka Bank, DCB Bank, CSB, NCRTC, and BVH.

title: Exclusive: Gauri Khan Family Trust to re-invests in Sleepy Owl
description: Sleepy Owl is raising fresh funding of Rs 12 crore from new and existing investors, including Optiscape Network Holdings, Gauri Khan Family Trust, Pramod Bhasin and others.
body: Homegrown D2C coffee brand Sleepy Owl is raising fresh funding of Rs 12 crore from new and existing investors, including Optiscape Network Holdings , Gauri Khan Family Trust , Pramod Bhasin and others.

This funding comes after a 2.5-year gap since the company raised Rs 15 crore in October 2023, led by existing investors Rukam Capital and DSG Consumer Partners . Earlier, it had secured $6.5 million in its Series A round in November 2021.

The board at Sleepy Owl passed a resolution to approve the issuance of 37,944 Series C2 preference shares at an issue price of Rs 3,162.55 per share to raise Rs 12 crore ($1.3 million), according to its regulatory filing reviewed by Entrackr.

Optiscape Network Holdings will lead the tranche with a Rs 5 crore investment, followed by Pramod Bhasin, who will invest Rs 2.5 crore. Existing investor Gauri Khan Family Trust will also contribute Rs 2 crore.
According to Entrackr’s analysis, Sleepy Owl’s valuation will rise by 28% to Rs 172 crore ($18.5 million) post-money, from Rs 134 crore in its previous round of Rs 15 crore in October 2023.

Founded in 2016 by Ajay Thandi , Arman Sood , and Ashwajeet Singh , Sleepy Owl is an Indian coffee brand offering premium 100% Arabica coffee, with a focus on convenience and high-quality flavor. Its portfolio includes instant coffee, hot and cold brew packs, ready-to-drink cold brews, ground coffee, and brewing kits.

Following the allotment of this tranche, DSG Consumer Partners remained the largest shareholder with a 35.35% stake, followed by Rukam Capital at 13.29%. Among participating investors, Optiscape Holdings will hold 2.91%, while Pramod Bhasin will hold 2.26%. The Gauri Khan Family Trust stakes will also increase to 1.91%. Other participating investors will collectively hold the remaining stake.

On the financial front, during FY25, the D2C brand doubled its revenue to Rs 44 crore, while narrowing its losses by 80% to Rs 2.1 crore during the same period. Sleepy Owl competes with Subko Coffee , Blue Tokai , Rage Coffee , Slay Coffee , and abCoffee , among others.

title: Former Zetwerk executives’ startup STCH raises $5.5 Mn led by Omnivore
description: STCH, an AI startup focused on fabric development and textile manufacturing, has raised $5.5 million (around Rs 66 crore) in a pre-Series A round led by Omnivore. Snippets
body: STCH, an AI startup focused on fabric development and textile manufacturing, has raised $5.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Omnivore, with participation from Kae Capital and WVC.
The proceeds will be used to expand its AI capabilities, build a fabric R&D lab, deepen manufacturing partnerships, and scale delivery across key markets.

Founded in 2025 by former Zetwerk executives Narahari Payala and Aseem Chitkara, STCH operates a contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) platform for fashion businesses. It focuses on fabric innovation and sourcing rather than consumer-facing AI use cases.

Its platform analyses product images and descriptions to identify fabric specifications such as texture, weight, and finish, then helps recreate similar materials through local manufacturing partners.

STCH claims that it can take a fabric from concept to production in around 45 days and works with brands mainly in the UK and Europe. Manufacturing is carried out through partner factories across India and Bangladesh.
Earlier this year, Whizzo, a materials science–based manufacturing startup founded by former Zetwerk executive Shrestha Kukreja, raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Fundamentum.

title: LightFury Games raises $11 Mn in pre-Series A round
description: LightFury Games has secured global player roster rights for over 600 professional cricketers, including Chris Gayle, Joe Root, Ben Stokes, Kane Williamson, Pat Cummins,
body: LightFury Games, a AAA-focused game-tech studio, has raised $11 million (approx. Rs 103 crore) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures, V3 Ventures, MIXI, and Times Internet, with participation from Indian cricketers such as MS Dhoni, Jasprit Bumrah, Shreyas Iyer, Ravindra Jadeja, Tilak Varma, Sai Sudharsan, and Hardik Pandya.
