The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised $8.5 million in a seed round led by Blume Ventures in April 2024.
The funds will be used to complete development of its flagship title, eCricket, and to build its live operations stack, including post-launch content pipelines.

Founded in 2024 by Karan Shroff, Anurag Banerjee, and Tina Balachandran, LightFury Games develops high-quality, mobile-first gaming experiences. Its Unreal Engine 5-powered title, eCricket, aims to deliver a competitive and immersive cricket gaming experience for a global audience.
The game will feature tactical batting and bowling systems, physics-driven gameplay, AI commentary, and broadcast-style presentation. It is slated for release in 2026 on mobile platforms.

LightFury Games has secured global player roster rights for over 600 professional cricketers, including Chris Gayle, Joe Root, Ben Stokes, Kane Williamson, Pat Cummins, Jos Buttler, Travis Head, and Andre Russell.
The game will follow a free-to-play model with in-app purchases such as player cards, cosmetic upgrades, stadium enhancements, and season passes, without any real-money gaming element.

title: GobbleCube’s co-founders dilutes over 70% stake post Series A
description: GobbleCube has raised $15 million in a Series A round led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, with participation from InfoEdge Ventures and Kae Capital. However, co-founders stake diluted by over 70%.
body: AI-based brand analytics platform GobbleCube recently raised $15 million in a Series A round led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, with participation from existing investors InfoEdge Ventures and Kae Capital. It is the company’s second funding round within a year. However, following back-to-back deals, the co-founders’ stake has been diluted by over 70%.
To delve deeper into the Gurugram-based firm’s latest Series A round, Entrackr has reviewed the company’s regulatory filings to uncover details such as shareholding structure, and current valuation.

According to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), the company issued 2 equity shares and 37,735 Series A preference shares at an issue price of Rs 35,776 each to raise Rs 135 crore or approximately $15 million.

New investor Susquehanna Venture Capital, through its SAI Global India Fund, led the round with an investment of Rs 81 crore ($9 million). Existing investors Info Edge and Kae Capital also participated, infusing Rs 31.5 crore and Rs 22.5 crore respectively, to increase their stakes in the company.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, GobbleCube’s valuation has surged more than fourfold to Rs 612 crore (around $68 million) post-money, compared to Rs 145 crore in its previous $3.5 million seed round raised in July last year.

GobbleCube has raised over $20 million across three funding rounds. Following the latest Series A allotment, Info Edge remains the largest shareholder with an 18.23% stake, followed by Kae Capital at 16.57%. New investor Susquehanna Venture Capital holds 13.24%, while co-founders Manas Gupta, Srikumar Nair, and Nitesh Jindal each retain a 9.34% stake.
The company has also expanded its ESOP pool by 3,333 options, worth around Rs 12 crore, taking the total to 18,333 shares, representing 10.72% of its total share capital.

Founded in 2022 by Manas Gupta, Srikumar Nair, and Nitesh Jindal, GobbleCube builds an AI-powered platform for consumer brands to manage digital commerce operations, including demand forecasting, pricing, supply chain, and performance tracking.

title: Exclusive: Oolka raises Rs 130 Cr in Series A led by Accel at Rs 730 Cr valuation
description: Fintech startup Oolka has raised Rs 130 crore (nearly $14 million) in a Series A funding round led by Accel India, with participation from existing investors.
body: Fintech startup Oolka has raised Rs 130 crore (nearly $14 million) in a Series A funding round led by Accel India, with participation from existing investors. The board of Oolka has approved a resolution to allot 10 equity shares and 24,995 Series A compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 51,835.79 per share to raise the aforesaid amount, according to regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr. The round was led by Accel India with an investment of Rs 87.22 crore, followed by existing investors Lightspeed and Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners), which infused Rs 20.87 crore and Rs 20.86 crore, respectively. Moreover, Meesho co-founders Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Barnwal also participated personally in the round with Rs 32.65 lakh each. As per the filings, the proceeds from the issue will be used to fund the company’s expansion and growth, including capital expenditure and general corporate purposes. According to Entrackr’s analysis, Oolka is valued at around Rs 730 crore (approximately $87.6 million) post-money. The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised $7 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed and Z47. Queries sent to Oolka, Accel and Z47 did not elicit responses until publication of the story. Founded in 2024 by Utkrishta Kumar, Oolka is building an AI-powered credit management platform that helps users track, manage, and improve their credit health. At the time of its last round, the company claimed to have nearly 2 million users and to have processed over Rs 100 crore in credit repayments, with ARR projected to cross $1 million soon. It has partnered with institutions such as Yes Bank, IDFC Bank, and AU Small Finance Bank to support its credit marketplace.

The Bengaluru-based company was in a pre-revenue stage as of FY25, reporting revenue of Rs 5.52 lakh and a loss of Rs 5.58 crore. The company is yet to file its annual results for FY26. Oolka’s closest direct competitor is GoodScore, as both focus on AI-led credit improvement and personalised guidance. In October last year, GoodScore raised $13 million led by Peak XV. Other platforms like OneScore, Paisabazaar, and CRED overlap through credit score tracking and recommendations, but are less focused on execution-led credit improvement.

title: Pine Labs acquires D2C checkout platform Shopflo in Rs 88 Cr cash deal
description: Fintech firm Pine Labs has acquired 100% stake in Shopflo Technologies, a direct to consumer D2C checkout platform, in a deal valued at up to Rs 88 crore.
body: Fintech firm Pine Labs has acquired 100% stake in Shopflo Technologies, a direct to consumer D2C checkout platform, in a deal valued at up to Rs 88 crore.
According to a regulatory filing, the acquisition will be completed within three months and the transaction is entirely in cash.

Founded in December 2021, Shopflo builds checkout infrastructure and ecommerce enablement tools aimed at improving conversion rates for online brands. The company reported revenue of Rs 14.7 crore in FY25, up from Rs 9.1 crore in FY24 and Rs 0.63 crore in FY23.

Pine Labs said the acquisition will help it offer an integrated platform for merchants across offline payments, online checkout and customer engagement. The move aligns with its strategy to build a full stack commerce and payments platform.

Shopflo offers checkout optimisation tools, analytics and e-commerce solutions that aim to reduce cart abandonment and improve payment success rates. These capabilities will complement Pine Labs’ existing payments infrastructure.
Shopflo serves more than 1,000 online brands and has enabled transactions for over 60 million consumers. Merchants using its platform have reported 15 to 20% improvement in conversion rates.

Founded by Priy Ranjan, along with Ankit Bansal and Ishan Rakshit, the startup gained attention in 2022 when Tiger Global made its first seed investment in India through Shopflo. It has raised about $3.7 million from investors including Tiger Global, TQ Ventures and Better Capital.

Pine Labs’ online payments business reported around 50% year on year growth in Q3 FY26, with revenue rising to Rs 744 crore from Rs 601 crore a year earlier. The company posted a net profit of Rs 42 crore in the quarter, compared to a loss of Rs 57 crore in Q3 FY25. Its Q4 results are awaited.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startup this week [Apr 20 - Apr 25]
description: This week saw muted funding activity, with 19 Indian startups raising around $47 million. The mix included 13 early-stage deals, no growth-stage transactions, while 6 startups kept their funding undisclosed.
body: This week saw muted funding activity, with 19 Indian startups raising around $47 million. The mix included 13 early-stage deals, no growth-stage transactions, while 6 startups kept their funding undisclosed.
In contrast, 17 startups had collectively secured about $129.07 million in the previous week.
[Early-stage deals]

Only early-stage deals were recorded this week, with 13 startups raising a total of $47 million. Healthcare automation startup Coral led the pack with a $12.5 Mn round from Z47 and Lightspeed Venture Partners, followed by LightFury Games, which raised $11 million (Rs 103 crore) in a pre-Series A round backed by Blume Ventures, V3 Ventures, MIXI, and Times Internet, along with participation from cricketers including MS Dhoni, Jasprit Bumrah, and Hardik Pandya.

STCH, an AI startup focused on fabric development and textile manufacturing, has raised $5.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Omnivore. Mobile gaming startup Spill Games secured $3.1 million in a seed round co-led by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital, while cloud operations-focused AI platform NudgeBee raised $3 million in a seed round led by Kalaari Capital, with participation from tech founders.

Legal tech startup Lawyered, Wealth-tech platform PrimeInvestor, AI-powered cybersecurity startup Deep Algorithm, medical tourism discovery platform CureMeAbroad and 3 other early-stage startups also secured funding this week.

D2C footwear brand Chupps, clean food brand Khetika, modern Indianwear label Alaya By Stage3, refurbished electronics platform Grest, and spiritual tech startup 3ioNetra also raised funds this week, although the amounts remain undisclosed.
[City and segment-wise deals]

title: Unicommerce posts Rs 52 Cr revenue and Rs 3 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 51.6 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 45.3 crore in Q3 FY25, according to its financial statement sourced from NSE.
body: After recording a 70% year-on-year rise in Q3 FY26, e-commerce enablement SaaS platform Unicommerce reported a modest 13.9% increase in its revenue during the final quarter of the fiscal year (Q4 FY26).
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 51.6 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 45.3 crore in Q3 FY25, according to its financial statement sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Including other undisclosed income, its total income for Q4 FY26 grew to Rs 52.8 crore. For the full fiscal year, Unicommerce’s operating revenue grew to Rs 204.3 crore as compared to Rs 134.8 crore in FY25.

On the expense side, employee benefits rose 22.3% to Rs 19.2 crore in Q4 FY26. Server hosting, depreciation, finance costs, and other overheads took the total expenses to Rs 46.9 crore in Q4FY26 from Rs 41.5 crore in Q4FY25

At the end, the profits for the Gurugram-based firm remained flat at Rs 3.4 crore in Q4FY26. However, for the full fiscal year, the bottom line grew 15.9% to Rs 20.4 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 17.6 crore in FY25.
Unicommerce’s share price closed at Rs 109 at the end of the trading session with the total market capitalization of Rs 1,225 crore (about $133 million).

title: Metasports Interactive secures $20 Mn in user acquisition funding from Metica
description: Metasports Interactive, a mobile gaming company, has secured $20 million in user acquisition (UA) funding from London-based growth financing firm Metica. Snippets
body: Metasports Interactive, a mobile gaming company, has secured $20 million in user acquisition (UA) funding from London-based growth financing firm Metica.
The capital will be used to scale marketing and user acquisition for Hitwicket, the company’s multiplayer cricket game, and support its next phase of international expansion.
Founded by Kashyap Reddy and Keerti Singh, Metasports Interactive claims that Hitwicket has built a player base of over 18 million users across 109 countries since launch.
Alongside the funding, Metica will also provide its technology platform to help improve in-game revenue performance and strengthen unit economics.
The company is targeting nearly 8x growth over the next 18 months through expansion in priority global markets, AI-led targeting, and further product development.
Metasports had earlier raised $8 million from Prime Venture Partners and Horizon Ventures. The startup is also backed by cricket commentator Harsha Bhogle.
UA funding is a non-dilutive financing model used by gaming and consumer app companies to fund customer acquisition based on performance metrics.

title: Acko ropes in ICICI, Morgan Stanley, Kotak for IPO; targets $2–2.5 Bn valuation
description: Digital insurtech firm Acko has appointed ICICI Securities, Morgan Stanley, and Kotak Securities as book-running lead managers for its upcoming initial public offering, according to sources familiar with the matter.
body: Digital insurtech firm Acko has appointed ICICI Securities, Morgan Stanley, and Kotak Securities as book-running lead managers for its upcoming initial public offering, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The Bengaluru-based company is expected to file its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in the coming months. The public issue is likely to include a mix of fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing investors, the sources said, requesting anonymity as the discussions are private.
The IPO is expected to value the firm in the range of $2 billion to $2.5 billion.
Acko has declined to comment on the story.

Founded in 2016 by Varun Dua and Ruchi Deepak, ACKO is a digital-first insurance and financial services company built around a technology-led, customer-centric approach. It offers a suite of products including motor, health, and travel insurance, along with group health cover for enterprises. Positioned as one of India’s first fully digital insurers, the company has gained traction for its zero-commission model, paperless processes, and quick claim settlements.
The company has raised over $583 million from investors including General Atlantic, Multiples PE, Accel, Elevation Capital, and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.
On the financial front, ACKO’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,837 crore in FY25 from Rs 2,106 crore in FY24, while losses narrowed 37% to Rs 424 crore.
Last week, Acko trimmed around 5% of its workforce, with nearly 60 employees impacted, as part of an internal restructuring linked to the integration of artificial intelligence.

title: JioHotstar posts Rs 31,048 Cr revenue and Rs 3,228 Cr PBT in FY26
description: For FY26, the media segment reported an operating revenue of Rs 31,048 crore, while EBITDA and PBT stood at Rs 4,885 crore and Rs 3,228 crore respectively.
body: Reliance Industries’s media business, led by JioHotstar, scaled up sharply in FY26, led by strong sports viewership, rising subscriptions, and growth in digital advertising.

The platform’s monthly active users (MAUs) reached around 550 million in March 2026, making it one of the largest streaming platforms globally by user base. The growth was largely led by a packed sports calendar and strong engagement across entertainment content.
For FY26, the media segment reported an operating revenue of Rs 31,048 crore, while EBITDA stood at Rs 4,885 crore with a margin of 15.7%. Profit before tax (PBT) came in at Rs 3,228 crore.
During the previous quarter (Q4 FY26), it recorded a revenue of Rs 8,372 crore, a 21.4% quarter-on-quarter growth with profit before tax of Rs 421 crore in the same period.

According to the Reliance Industries investor presentation, sports continued to play a key role in driving traffic and revenues. The ICC T20 World Cup 2026 recorded a peak concurrency of 72.5 million users. Meanwhile, the ongoing IPL 2026 has started on a strong note, delivering a record opening weekend and nearly 60% growth in peak concurrency.

Beyond sports, entertainment content also contributed to higher engagement. Digital watch time in the entertainment segment grew 35% year-on-year in the fourth quarter, supported by a steady pipeline of shows, movies, and regional content.

On the monetisation front, digital advertising emerged as a key growth driver during the year. This was supported by rising connected TV (CTV) adoption, better ad targeting, and a broader advertiser base. However, traditional TV advertising remained under pressure due to muted spending from FMCG companies.

Reliance has also introduced new features to deepen engagement. These include ‘Tadka’, a micro-content hub with over 100 shows, conversational content discovery in partnership with OpenAI, and in-app commerce integration with Swiggy.

title: Kissht files RHP to launch Rs 926 IPO; sets price band at Rs 162-171
description: Digital lending platform Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, has filed its RHP with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in April 2025, and is set to launch its Rs 926 crore IPO on April 30
body: Digital lending platform Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, has filed its RHP with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in April 2025, and is set to launch its Rs 926 crore IPO on April 30.

The company has set a price band of Rs 162–171 per equity share for its IPO, which will open for subscription on April 30 and close on May 5, with the anchor book scheduled to open on April 29. At the upper end of the price band, the issue values the company at around Rs 3,062 crore (approximately $329 million) post-money.

According to its RHP, Kissht has reduced its fresh issue size to Rs 850 crore from the Rs 1,000 crore proposed in its earlier DRHP filed in August 2025. The company has also cut the offer for sale to 4.4 million equity shares from 8.8 million shares, now estimated at around Rs 76 crore.

Vertex Ventures will lead the OFS by offloading 1.7 million shares, followed by Ammar Sdn Bhd and Ventureast Proactive Fund. Other selling shareholders include Endiya Seed Co-creation Fund and AION Advisory, both of which are planning partial stake sales.

A major portion of the proceeds from the fresh issue, amounting to Rs 637.5 crore, will be infused into its subsidiary Si Creva to strengthen its capital base and support future business growth. The remaining funds will be allocated towards general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, Kissht provides small-ticket consumer loans and has scaled aggressively on the back of partnerships with merchants across electronics, fashion, travel and other categories.

As of the RHP filing date, Vertex Ventures is the largest external shareholder with a 22.68% stake, followed by Ammar Sdn Bhd at 12.13% and Ventureast Proactive Fund at 8.95%. Meanwhile, the company’s co-founders Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan hold 18.78% and 13.52%, respectively.

Financially, for the nine-month period ended December 2025, Kissht reported an operating revenue of Rs 1,560 crore with a net profit of Rs 199 crore. In FY25, the company posted Rs 1,337 crore in operating revenue, while its net profit stood at Rs 160 crore.

title: Fintech startup Novio raises Rs 100 Cr in Series A led by Cornerstone Ventures
description: Novio, a fintech startup, has raised Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by Cornerstone Ventures, with participation. Snippets
body: Novio, a fintech startup, has raised Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by Cornerstone Ventures, with participation from Shepherd’s Hill Private Equity, ESV-Arthya AIF, and Roots Ventures. The round also included venture debt from Innoven Capital and Alteria Capital.
The proceeds will be used to expand distribution in tier II to tier V markets, strengthen bank partnerships, and enhance its product stack, including UPI integration and AI-led credit advisory.
Founded in 2024 by Aditya Gupta, Sandeep Ghule, Anand Kapadia, and Manish Sinha, Novio offers credit cards backed by fixed deposits, targeting users without formal credit history.

Users can open a fixed deposit through the app and receive a RuPay credit card within hours without income proof or credit checks. The card can be linked to UPI for payments, while the deposit earns interest.
Novio partners with banks such as SBM Bank and DCB Bank to issue cards and offers features including rewards, travel benefits, and real-time redemption.
The startup claims to have crossed 1 lakh active cardholders within a year of launch and plans to issue 50 lakh cards over the next three years.

title: Go Digit’s profit rises 28% YoY to Rs 149 Cr in Q4 FY26
description: Go Digit General Insurance reported flat revenue in Q4 FY26, with revenue from operations (net premium) at Rs 2,301 crore. However, profit increased over 28% year-on-year to Rs 149 crore during the period.
body: Go Digit General Insurance reported flat revenue in Q4 FY26, with revenue from operations (net premium) at Rs 2,301 crore. However, profit increased over 28% year-on-year to Rs 149 crore during the period.

Meanwhile, gross premium written saw a 6% increase in the quarter to Rs 2,736 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 2,576 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its quarterly results reported on the NSE.

Motor insurance remained the company’s largest segment, contributing Rs 1,500 crore in net premiums, followed by health insurance at Rs 363 crore, along with fire, corporate, marine, crop, and other segments.

The firm’s income from investments grew 20% to Rs 341 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 288 crore in Q3 FY25. Gains from its investment portfolio, along with other non-operating income, pushed total income to Rs 3,111 crore during the quarter.

On the expense front, Commissions and brokerage costs amounted to Rs 567 crore in Q4 FY26, as compared to Rs 598 crore in Q3 FY25. Employee benefits expenses rose 64% to Rs 92 crore from Rs 56 crore in the same quarter in FY25.

Claims paid declined 13% to Rs 1,176 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 1,354 crore in Q4 FY25, while outstanding claims rose 52% to Rs 555 crore. Overall expenses remained largely flat at Rs 2,500 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 2,426 crore in the same period last year.

The company’s PAT rose 28% to Rs 149 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 116 crore in Q4 FY25. For the full year ended March 2026, profit stood at Rs 544 crore, while net premium earned reached Rs 8,414 crore during the period.
At the end of the day's trading session, Go Digit’s share price closed at Rs 317 per share, giving the company a total market capitalization of Rs 29,307 crore ($3.1 billion).

title: Eternal’s profits jumps 4.5X to Rs 174 Cr in Q4 FY26
description: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Eternal (formerly Zomato) released its financial results for Q4 FY26 on Tuesday. The company reported a nearly 4.5X year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 174 crore during the period.
body: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Eternal (formerly Zomato) released its financial results for Q4 FY26 on Tuesday. The Gurugram-based company reported a nearly 4.5X year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 174 crore during the period.

Eternal’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 17,292 crore in Q4 FY26 in contrast to Rs 5,833 crore in Q4 FY25, as per the firm’s consolidated financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The sharp rise in revenue was attributed to its inventory-led quick commerce model. However, on a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue remained flat at Rs 16,315 crore in Q4 FY26. The company operates multiple verticals, including a food marketplace, Hyperpure, and its quick commerce platform, Blinkit.

Meanwhile, its B2B vertical, Hyperpure, declined 47% to Rs 978 crore in Q4 FY26, while the going-out business (District) grew 21% to Rs 277 crore. Including income from other segments and non-operating sources, Eternal Group’s total revenue rose to Rs 17,634 crore in Q4 FY26.
For the full year FY26, the company reported operating revenue of Rs 54,364 crore and a profit of Rs 366 crore.

Material costs accounted for 59.4% of total expenses and stood at Rs 10,340 crore in the quarter. Delivery and related expenses increased 68% to Rs 2,607 crore, while advertising expenses grew 48% to Rs 936 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 634 crore in Q4 FY25. Employee benefits expenses rose 24% to Rs 927 crore during the period. Overall, the company’s overall expenditure stood at Rs 17,406 crore in the fourth quarter of FY26.
In the end, profit jumped 4.5X year-on-year to Rs 174 crore, supported by strong topline growth along with non-operating income.
At the end of today’s trading session, Eternal’s share price stood at Rs 258.28, giving the foodtech platform a market capitalization of Rs 2,49,249 crore (approximately $26 billion).

title: Mojro Technologies raises $5.5 Mn led by Dallas Venture Capital
description: Its products, including PlanWyse and ExecuteWyse, enable real-time planning and operational intelligence for enterprises across FMCG, food and beverage, 3PL, and retail
body: AI-driven supply chain optimization startup Mojro Technologies has raised $5.5 million in a Series A funding round. The round includes a previously announced $3 million investment led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from 1Crowd, along with a $2.5 million extension funded by Dallas Venture Capital (DVC).
The fresh funds will be used to accelerate global expansion and product innovation, the company said.

Founded in 2016 by Kishan Aswath, Amit Kulkarni, and Ranganath Seetharamu, Mojro is a B2B SaaS platform for logistics planning and optimization. It helps mid- to large-sized enterprises across sectors such as CPG, retail, courier and parcel, dairy, and e-commerce reduce logistics costs by up to 20%, using a usage-based pricing model.

Its AI-powered platform uses advanced analytics and heuristic algorithms to deliver optimization across routes, schedules, trips, and capacity constraints. With a library of over 150 constraints, it is designed to handle complex logistics scenarios while delivering measurable improvements within 90 days.
Its products, including PlanWyse and ExecuteWyse, enable real-time planning and operational intelligence for enterprises across FMCG, food and beverage, 3PL, and retail sectors.
According to market research, the global AI in logistics market is expected to reach $38.68 billion by 2026, growing at a CAGR of 46.9%.

title: Battery Smart secures $15 Mn in debt from Mirova
description: Battery Smart, a battery swapping network for electric vehicles, has raised $15 million in debt funding from Mirova, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers. Snippets
body: Battery Smart, a battery swapping network for electric vehicles, has raised $15 million in debt funding from Mirova, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers.
The proceeds will be used to expand its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) infrastructure and strengthen its network of partner-led stations across urban and semi-urban markets.
Founded by Pulkit Khurana, Battery Smart enables EV drivers to swap depleted batteries with charged ones within minutes, reducing downtime and lowering upfront vehicle costs.
The startup currently operates more than 1,600 partner-led stations across 50 cities. Its platform is focused on serving last-mile delivery and passenger mobility segments.
The funding will support expansion of its network and improve access for gig workers and fleet operators.

To date, Battery Smart has raised around $192 million in funding, including its $65 million Series B round and $29 million extended Series B round. Its cap table includes prominent investors such as Tiger Global, Blume Ventures, and Ecosystem Integrity Fund.

On the financial front, the company reported a 52% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 249 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 164 crore in FY24. In a recent announcement, Battery Smart also stated that it has achieved operating break-even and turned EBITDA positive.

title: Cap Alpha Ventures leads Rs 25 Cr in Series A round in House of Chikankari
description: House of Chikankari claims to have recorded over 50% growth in FY26 and is currently operating at an annual revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 50 crore. It has served more th
body: Women-led contemporary ethnic wear brand House of Chikankari has raised Rs 25 crore in a Series A funding round led by Cap Alpha Ventures, formerly known as Client Associates Alternate Fund (CAAF).
The Delhi-based startup had earlier secured $639K from LetsVenture and others. It was also featured on Shark Tank India Season 2 in 2023.

The company said the proceeds will be used to expand its product portfolio, strengthen its omnichannel presence with a push into offline retail, improve working capital efficiency, and invest in team expansion and marketing.

Co-founded in 2020 by Aakriti Rawal and Poonam Rawal, House of Chikankari aims to reimagine the art of chikankari for the modern consumer, making it suitable for everyday wear. The brand blends heritage embroidery techniques with contemporary design to build a scalable ethnic wear business.

The company supports a network of over 10,000 artisans, focusing on preserving the heritage of hand-embroidered chikankari. Its product range includes kurtas, kurta sets, sarees, kaftans, tops, shirts, and bottom wear. The startup operates on a D2C model through its official website and has built a community of over 2 lakh customers.

House of Chikankari claims to have recorded over 50% growth in FY26 and is currently operating at an annual revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 50 crore. It has served more than 2 lakh customers to date and shipped orders to over 20 countries, including the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom.
The company is targeting multi-fold growth over the next 24 months. A majority of its revenue comes from proprietary channels, which see over 9 lakh monthly user sessions across its website and app.

title: HyugaLife raises $10.5 Mn in Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures
description: HyugaLife, a marketplace for proteins and supplements, has raised Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. News
body: HyugaLife, a marketplace for proteins and supplements, has raised Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures, with participation from First Bridge Fund.

The company had previously raised $6.3 million in seed round  from Peak XV and Spring Marketing Capital in February 2024. The company was also backed by Stride Ventures, Getvantage and Indian cricketer KL Rahul.

Founded by Sachin Parikh, Anvi Shah, and Neehar Modi, HyugaLife will use the fresh funds to strengthen its AI-led personalisation stack, build a dark store network for faster deliveries, and expand into offline retail.

The platform focuses on verified and authentic nutrition products through its H-Tested programme, which includes direct sourcing from brands and independent lab reports covering nutrition and heavy metals across a large part of its catalogue.

HyugaLife currently lists more than 450 brands and over 10,000 products across proteins, supplements, health foods, and wellness categories. The startup serves fitness enthusiasts, athletes, working professionals, and families across India.
Additionally, HyugaLife’s parent, Pratech Brands, owns Neesan Ventures and Inaari, a natural healthcare brand focused on female hormones.
On the financial side, Pratech Brands reported revenue of Rs 45.32 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 38.63 crore in FY24, while its losses narrowed to Rs 21.32 crore from Rs 32 crore.

title: Snabbit raises $56 Mn in Series D round
description: Snabbit, a quick home services platform, has raised $56 million in a Series D round from Susquehanna VC, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, and Bertelsmann. News
body: Snabbit, a quick home services platform, has raised $56 million in a Series D round from Susquehanna VC, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, and Bertelsmann India Investments.
The proceeds will be used to expand into new cities, strengthen leadership in existing markets, add more high-frequency service categories, and improve its balance sheet.
As per Entrackr’s sources, the company’s valuation has climbed to $360 million.

Founded as a quick-service platform for recurring household needs, Snabbit operates a hyperlocal model focused on speed, reliability, and convenience. The firm currently operates across five cities including Mumbai Metropolitan Region, Delhi NCR, Pune, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru.

Snabbit claims that it processes more than 40,000 jobs daily across 140 active micromarkets and has over 15,000 service professionals on its platform, all women. The company crossed 1 million monthly jobs in March 2026 and said it scaled from 400 to 40,000 daily orders in less than 12 months.
Snabbit has raised $112 million in total funding to date.

The segment is seeing rising competition from incumbents and new entrants. Urban Company’s InstaHelp crossed 1 million bookings in March , while Snabbit also reported 1 million orders during the same period.

Other players are also expanding in the space. Pronto recently completed one year of operations and reported over 500,000 monthly fulfilled bookings. According to media reports, it is in the process of raising $20 million , months after securing $25 million in Series B round.

title: Workforce mobility platform Kovon raises pre-seed led by TDV Partners
description: Kovon, a cross-border workforce mobility platform, has raised $250K in a pre-seed funding round led by TDV Partners. The proceeds will be used for product. Snippets
body: Kovon, a cross-border workforce mobility platform, has raised $250K in a pre-seed funding round led by TDV Partners.

The proceeds will be used for product development, global employer partnerships, candidate acquisition, and expansion of its skilling and training ecosystem. It also plans to hire across technology, operations, and partnerships.

Founded by Bibartan Roy and Swayamjeet Das, the startup connects India’s blue and grey-collar workforce to overseas job opportunities across sectors such as healthcare, hospitality, construction, and logistics.
Kovon offers an end-to-end platform covering job discovery, upskilling, financing, placement, and post-deployment support.
The startup plans to address labour shortages in markets such as Europe, the UK, the Middle East, and other developed economies while creating structured overseas opportunities for Indian workers.
The firm is focused on building verified and job-ready talent pipelines from India for global employers.

title: Vikra Ocean Tech raises $1 Mn from Finvolve and India Accelerator
description: According to the Chennai-based startup, its integrated hardware stack is supported by indigenous cameras, lighting, diver communication systems, and AI-based video
body: Deeptech startup Vikra Ocean Tech has raised $1 million in a seed funding round co-led by Finvolve and India Accelerator.

The proceeds will be used to scale product manufacturing, strengthen its sales pipeline across defence and public sector undertakings (PSUs), and establish recurring revenue streams, Vikra Ocean Tech said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2019 by Rajeuv Govindan and Rajagurunathan Krishnasamy, Vikra Ocean Tech develops an indigenous, modular ocean robotics ecosystem that includes deep-water ROVs, autonomous surface vessels, amphibious crawling robots, and AI-enabled imaging and communication systems.

Built for interoperability through a unified control platform, its solutions aim to reduce India’s dependence on imported underwater robotics by offering cost-effective, mission-ready systems tailored for defence, subsea inspection, hydrographic surveys, and disaster response.

According to the Chennai-based startup, its integrated hardware stack is supported by indigenous cameras, lighting, diver communication systems, and AI-based video enhancement tools, enabling simplified and scalable operations.

Vikra Ocean Tech claims it has gained strong early traction across both defence and commercial sectors, including securing two iDEX grants from the Indian Army and the Indian Coast Guard. It has also developed deep-ocean camera and lighting systems rated for depths of up to 2,000 meters. Its Autonomous Surface Vehicle (ASV) systems are also seeing wider adoption in offshore marine exploration applications.
It primarily competes with the other startups in this landscape such as Odisha-based Coratia Technologies, Planys, Eyerov, and Sagar Defence.

title: Climate-tech startup Prithu raises Rs 10 Cr in seed round led by Transition VC
description: Over the next 12–24 months, the company plans to expand to 5 lakh hectares in NBS projects, including high-tech biochar. It will also enhance its MRV technology, secure
body: Climate technology startup Prithu has raised Rs 10 crore in a seed funding round led by Transition VC.
Prior to this, the Gurugram-based startup had secured Rs 38 lakh in an angel round from the Startup India Seed Fund and others.
The fresh funds will be used to expand farmer networks, enhance blockchain-powered MRV systems, and secure global carbon credit offtakes, Prithu said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by Sunny Vaish, Prabal Tomar, and Abhinav Pandey, Prithu is a climate technology company that builds a full-stack carbon removal platform focused on nature-based solutions. It enables large-scale climate action by transforming regenerative agriculture, agroforestry, biochar, and biogas interventions into high-integrity carbon credits.

The startup aims to sequester 20 million tonnes of CO₂e by 2030. It addresses challenges such as soil organic carbon depletion, agri-waste burning, and water stress, while enabling small landholder farmers to participate in global carbon markets.
According to market research, the global carbon market is valued at $3–4 billion today and is projected to exceed $40–50 billion by 2030.

Prithu focuses on agriculture in India with regenerative practices that tackle soil depletion, agri-waste burning, and water stress, while supplying high-integrity credits to global voluntary carbon markets across sectors such as manufacturing, technology, energy, aviation, and consumer industries.

Over the next 12–24 months, the company plans to expand to 5 lakh hectares in NBS projects, including high-tech biochar. It will also enhance its MRV technology, secure international partnerships, and explore new geographies.

title: Exclusive: Wow! Momo to raise Rs 110 Cr debt from Anicut Capital
description: Wow! Momo is set to raise Rs 110 crore ($11.6 million) in debt from Anicut Capital, its first fundraise in 2026, after a Rs 75 crore ($8.4 million) infusion from Singularity AMC in December last year.
body: Quick-service restaurant chain Wow! Momo is set to raise Rs 110 crore ($11.6 million) in debt funding from Anicut Capital. This will be its first fundraise in 2026, after an additional Rs 75 crore ($8.4 million) infusion from Singularity AMC in December last year.
Last year, the company raised around Rs 300 crore across three funding rounds through a mix of equity and debt, including Rs 130–150 crore from the Haldiram promoter family and Khazanah Nasional.

The company’s board has approved the issuance of 1,100 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) with a face value of Rs 10 lakh each, aggregating Rs 110 crore, to be raised in three tranches, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
The firm has already received the first tranche of Rs 60 crore. The remaining tranches will be completed within six months as per the debenture terms, the filing said.
The proceeds will be utilised for refinancing existing borrowings, for general corporate purposes, and for growth capital needs.
Launched in 2008 by Sagar Daryani and Binod Homagai, Wow! Momo operates over 850 outlets across more than 90 cities. Its brands include Wow! Momo, Wow! China, Wow! Chicken, and Wow! Kulfi.
As per its last funding round, the company was valued at around Rs 2,838 crore ($316 million) on a post-money basis.
The company has raised over $140 million prior to this funding. This includes a $42 million Series D round led by Khazanah Nasional in January 2024.

title: Eternal’s reality check: Blinkit’s thin margins and District’s  losses
description: Despite operating 2,243 dark stores and deploying over 4 lakh delivery partners, the business reported an adjusted EBITDA of just Rs 37 crore.
body: Eternal Limited ended Q4 FY26 on a strong note, at least on paper. The company reported consolidated adjusted revenue of Rs 17,680 crore, while B2C net order value grew 54% year-on-year. Its cash balance also remained at Rs 18,000 crore. But beyond these headline numbers, two key businesses, Blinkit and District, reveal a more nuanced picture.

Blinkit continues to scale rapidly. Its net order value stood at Rs 14,386 crore in Q4FY26, which indicates the growing demand for quick commerce. However, the profitability remains thin. Despite operating 2,243 dark stores, with 17 million square feet of space, and deploying over 4 lakh delivery partners, the business reported an adjusted EBITDA of just Rs 37 crore. This decodes to a margin of around 0.3% of net order value.

The company has indicated that mature markets such as Delhi NCR are moving towards a steady-state margin of 5–6%, which suggests the model can work. However, scaling this across the country is not straightforward. As per the company, the top eight cities are already largely covered with 80-90% of serviceable pin codes, leaving limited room for easy expansion.

Now, growth from here will come from smaller cities, where online grocery adoption is still low and the customers who have never ordered groceries online, where each new market will require fresh investments and time to stabilise, which could weigh on overall margins in the near term.

According to the shareholders' letter, the average monthly transacting customers grew from 13.7 million in Q4 FY25 to 27.2 million in Q4 FY26, while the net average order value remains flat at Rs 525, which shows that volume growth is coming from more smaller and frequent orders rather than high-value baskets.

We have also noticed that, during FY26, the firm spent around Rs 1,700 crore as capital expenditure into Blinkit from its free cash flow (almost Rs 450 crore in every quarter), which is generating Rs 37 crore adjusted EBITDA in a quarter.

Eternal’s going-out platform, District, also presents a different challenge. The segment recorded Rs 277 crore in revenue on a net order value of Rs 2,736 crore in Q4 FY26, while posting an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 81 crore. Although losses have reduced from Rs 121 crore in the previous quarter, the improvement remains modest given the relatively small revenue base.

The business operates in a highly competitive space where incumbents already have strong supplier networks and user engagement. At the same time, demand is closely tied to external factors such as movie releases, live events, and overall discretionary spending, all of which can fluctuate.

title: IAN Alpha Fund leads Rs 32.7 Cr round in sports-tech startup SportVot
description: portVot claims that it has already streamed over 500,000 matches across more than 30 countries and reaches an audience of over 100 million viewers, with growing traction
body: Sports-tech startup SportVot has raised Rs 32.7 crore in a funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund along with participation from Anicut Capital, Let’s Venture, Capital A, Succeed Innovation, Garima Vohra, and Gaurav Chanana, among others.
The Mumbai-based startup had earlier secured Rs 9.4 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Omidyar Network India in Feb. 2024.
The proceeds will be utilized to expand internationally and invest further in our AI-led production and distribution capabilities, SportVot said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2019 by Sidhhant Agarwal, Shubhangi Gupta and Yash Bhagwatkar, SportVot provides a full suite of online services to stream sports events and help discover sports talent from the grassroots of India. The startup has helped to bring investment to local sports associations, and innovated sports broadcasting by deploying cloud technology.

SportVot claims that it has already streamed over 500,000 matches across more than 30 countries and reaches an audience of over 100 million viewers, with growing traction across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Australia.

The startup primarily monetises its platform by charging tournament organisers and sports bodies for video production and streaming services, while also generating revenue through pay-per-view, subscriptions, and brand partnerships.

According to SportVot, nearly 99% of sports played globally go unstreamed due to high production costs and limited access to technology. It aims to bridge that gap by making professional-grade sports broadcasting accessible to leagues and organisers of all sizes.
The other notable players in this space are the Ahmedabad-based CricHeroes and the Mumbai-based FanCode.

title: Dale Vaz’s stock trading app Sahi raises $33 Mn in Series B round
description: Sahi, the broking platform built for performance-driven traders, today announced a $33 million Series B funding round led by Accel, with participation from Elevation.
body: Sahi, the broking platform built for performance-driven traders, today announced a $33 million Series B funding round led by venture capital fund Accel, with participation from Elevation Capital.
Accel Growth contributed about $20 million , while the remaining capital came from existing backers. The round values the company at around $200 million.

The fresh round has come within a year for the Bengaluru-based company, which raised $10.5 million led by Accel and Elevation in June last year. The valuation has jumped over 3x from $60 million during Series A.
Sahi will use the capital to deepen investment in its technology and AI stack, expand its product suite into new trading categories, and scale its user base, the company said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by former Swiggy CTO Dale Vaz and ex-Kotak Securities executive Manish Jain, the Bengaluru-based startup began operations in January 2025. It currently offers futures and options (F&O) and cash trading services.

Sahi has also secured a research analyst licence to offer investment advisory services. However, it is currently focused on its transactional business rather than entering the broader wealth management segment.

The platform claims to have seen rapid growth, with trade volumes rising 24x and active traders increasing 19x between April 2025 and March 2026. It has executed over 13 crore trades, with 86% in FY26, and onboarded around 4 lakh demat accounts, supporting this funding round.

Operating in a competitive market with players such as Zerodha, Groww, and Dhan, the startup is betting on its AI-native capabilities to stay lean and improve trading outcomes for users. The company claims to have over 400,000 demat accounts and contributes around 3% of daily trades, with its platform recently crossing one million trades per day.

title: Piper Serica leads Rs 10 Cr seed round in AIoT startup Ubiqedge
description: he company’s solutions cover water management, air quality monitoring, solar energy, and construction, helping enterprises improve efficiency and meet regulatory
body: Full-stack AIoT startup Ubiqedge has raised Rs 10 crore in a seed funding round led by Piper Serica, with participation from Atomberg CEO and co-founder Shibam Das and Sumit Chhazed.

The funds will be used to strengthen AI capabilities, scale deployments across water, air quality, solar, construction, and other industrial use cases, and expand its network of system integrators and OEM partners.

Founded in March 2024 by Visat Patel, Archit Khandelwal, Akhilesh Thorat, and Hetvi Shah, Ubiqedge is building an operating system for industrial infrastructure. Its hardware platform KLEON and AI-powered software layer SAMASTH enable real-time monitoring, control, and optimization of critical infrastructure.
The company’s solutions cover water management, air quality monitoring, solar energy, and construction, helping enterprises improve efficiency and meet regulatory requirements.

Ubiqedge addresses fragmented systems, manual monitoring, inefficiencies, and delayed decision-making through an integrated hardware and software stack that converts real-time data into actionable insights and automated controls.
The startup claims it has digitised over 23,000 borewells and reduced issue resolution timelines by more than 80%.
It competes with players such as Samsara, Teltonika, Kristnam, and Datoms.

title: Deep-tech startup Ctruh secures $2.5 Mn in seed funding
description: The company offers a no-code, browser-native infrastructure that enables 3D experiences to run across devices without downloads or specialized hardware. VersaAI
body: Deep-tech startup Ctruh has raised $2.5 million in a seed funding round co-led by Inflection Point Ventures and Avinya Ventures, with participation from India Accelerator, Founder’s Avenue, Anthill Ventures, Finvolve, LVX, Vivek Sinha, and Shivakumar Ganesan.
The Bengaluru-based startup had earlier raised $2 million from Pankaj Jain and Dharmendra Jain in January 2023.
The funds will be used for research and development, product innovation, and international expansion.
Founded in 2022 by Vinay Agastya, Ctruh focuses on AI, 3D, and XR (Extended Reality). It builds a browser-native 3D engine, VersaAI, and a platform, Commverse Studio.

The company offers a no-code, browser-native infrastructure that enables 3D experiences to run across devices without downloads or specialized hardware. VersaAI converts images, text, and video into 3D assets.
Commverse Studio allows brands to create and deploy 3D/XR experiences and integrates content creation, deployment, commerce, and analytics.
Ctruh serves sectors such as retail, e-commerce, real estate, automotive, education, and healthcare. It competes with players like mirrAR, Eccentric, Metadome.ai, and Trezithe.
The company plans expansion into the US and UAE in 2026.

title: Smartworks' revenue crosses Rs 500 Cr in Q4 FY26, maintains profitability
description: Smartworks reported its quarterly results for the Q4 FY26. The firm posted profits for consecutive quarters and crossed the Rs 500 crore revenue threshold during the quarter.
body: Managed office space provider Smartworks reported its quarterly results for the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended March 2026 today. The firm posted profits for consecutive quarters and crossed the Rs 500 crore revenue threshold during the quarter.

Smartworks’ revenue from operations rose 45% year-on-year to Rs 520 crore in the Q4 FY26 from Rs 358 crore in Q4 FY25, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Smartworks generates most of its revenue from developing, designing, and licensing serviced office spaces, along with fit-out services and other ancillary offerings. It also recorded Rs 13 crore in non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 533 crore in the quarter, compared to Rs 362 crore in Q4 FY25.

For the full year ended March 2026, Smartworks reported a revenue of Rs 1,796 crore, a growth of over 30% from Rs 1,374 crore in FY24, and achieved profitability with a profit of Rs 10.5 crore against a loss of Rs 63 crore in FY25.

On the cost side, depreciation (related to lease) was the largest expense at Rs 234 crore, followed by operating expenses, which were at  Rs 139 crore. Finance costs, employee benefits, and other overheads took Smartworks’s total expenditure to Rs 510 crore, compared to Rs 367 crore in the same quarter last year.

As revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses, Smartworks maintained profitability for the consecutive quarter, reporting a profit of Rs 16.6 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 8.3 crore in the same quarter last year.
As of 11:30 PM today, Smartworks shares traded at Rs 445.9 apiece, valuing the company at a market capitalization of Rs 5,102 crore ($537 million).

title: Bluestone’s FY26 glow-up has a gold price problem
description: Its standalone revenue rose from Rs 1,770 crore in FY25 to Rs 2,441 crore in FY26, a 37.9% jump. The EBITDA also surged 420% to Rs 394.5 crore.
body: Bluestone has delivered a headline turnaround that few consumer companies manage in a single year. Its standalone revenue rose from Rs 1,770 crore in FY25 to Rs 2,441 crore in FY26 , a 37.9% jump. The EBITDA also surged 420% to Rs 394.5 crore. Most strikingly, the company moved from a Cash PAT loss of Rs 82.9 crore to a Cash PAT profit of Rs 228.4 crore.

During the last quarter, Bluestone added 65 stores, crossed 340 outlets across 134 cities, and posted same-store sales growth of 34%. For a company that spent years burning cash to prove omnichannel jewellery retail could work in India, FY26 appears to be an inflection point.
But inside the same investor presentation filed with BSE on April 23 is a table that tells a more complicated story.

Bluestone booked an inventory gain of Rs 150 crore in FY26, which reflects the appreciation in value of its gold stockpile as bullion prices surged roughly 25–30% through the year. Under Indian accounting standards, this gain flows directly through the P&L as a reduction in cost of goods sold, which mechanically inflates EBITDA. If we strip it out, and adjust for IND AS 116 lease accounting, and the Pre-IND AS EBITDA excluding inventory gains drops to Rs 180.6 crore, a 7.4% margin. That is still a sharp improvement over FY25’s 1.0%, but a very different number from the 16.2% reported EBITDA margin that headlines the presentation in the report.

Interestingly, the company’s inventory has increased sharply, which raises concerns. Its inventory rose by 60.5% from Rs 1,652.5 crore to Rs 2,651.7 crore, while revenue grew at a slower pace of 38%. This also affected efficiency, with inventory turnover dropping from 1.34X to 1.13X. To build this stock, the company spent Rs 999 crore, which kept its operating cash flow negative at Rs 175.3 crore, even though it reported a paper profit.

The management says this increase is due to new stores, new product categories, and more entry-level pricing options, which sounds reasonable. However, such a big gap between inventory growth (60%) and revenue growth (38%) still needs a clearer explanation.

On top of this, ESOP costs rose sharply to Rs 92.7 crore in FY26, up 80.8% from last year. These are real costs because they reduce shareholder value when employees exercise their stock options. The company’s explanation makes sense,  these costs are higher now because of stock options given before the IPO, and they are expected to drop sharply from Rs 92.7 crore in FY26 to just Rs 4.8 crore by FY30. This means profits will look better in the future even without any major operational change.
However, that benefit is still in the future. For now, in FY26, the ESOP cost is a real expense that impacts the company’s profits.

title: Kissht secures Rs 278 Cr from anchor investors
description: Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, has raised Rs 278 crore from 22 anchor investors at the upper price band of Rs 171 per share on April 29.
body: Digital lending platform Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, has raised Rs 278 crore ($30 million) from 22 anchor investors at the upper price band of Rs 171 per share on April 29.
The anchor round comes a day ahead of the company’s IPO opening for subscription on April 30 (today).

According to the company’s stock exchange filing, it allotted 1.62 crore equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 171 per share, raising Rs 278 crore. Of the total anchor allocation, 92.58 lakh shares, or 57%, were allotted to seven domestic mutual funds across 13 schemes, accounting for Rs 158.32 crore.

Key anchor investors include domestic mutual funds such as HDFC MF, ICICI Prudential, WhiteOak Capital, Bandhan, Quant MF, Tata Banking & Financial Services, and Sundaram MF, along with global institutions including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and BNP Paribas, among others.
The IPO is being managed by JM Financial, HSBC Securities, Nuvama Wealth, SBI Capital and Centrum Capital, while KFin Technologies will act as registrar.

According to its RHP , Kissht has reduced its fresh issue size to Rs 850 crore from the Rs 1,000 crore proposed in its earlier DRHP filed in August 2025. The company has also cut the offer for sale to 4.4 million equity shares from 8.8 million shares, now estimated at around Rs 76 crore.
Existing investors including Vertex Ventures, Ammar Sdn Bhd, Endiya Seed Co-creation Fund, and AION Advisory will partially offload their stakes as part of the offer for sale (OFS).

Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, Kissht provides small-ticket consumer loans and has scaled aggressively on the back of partnerships with merchants across electronics, fashion, travel and other categories.

title: Credit lifecycle platform Oolka raises $14 Mn in Series A led by Accel
description: Bengaluru-based fintech startup Oolka has raised $14 million (around Rs 130 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Accel, with participation from existing investors Lightspeed and Z47.
body: Bengaluru-based fintech startup Oolka has raised $14 million (around Rs 130 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Accel, with participation from existing investors Lightspeed and Z47.

Last week, Entrackr exclusively reported on the funding, round breakup, and valuation, which has increased to Rs 730 crore (approximately $87.6 million) post-money. The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised $7 million in a seed round led by Lightspeed and Z47.
The new proceeds will be used to expand its AI engineering capabilities, enhance its product stack, and deepen partnerships with banks and NBFCs.

Founded in 2024 by Utkrishta Kumar, Oolka is building an AI-powered financial platform that helps users manage and improve their credit health. The startup uses AI agents to assist users across the financial lifecycle, including identifying credit issues, improving scores, and managing loans with personalized recommendations.
Oolka is also working towards building a full-stack financial operating system for consumers, moving beyond credit into broader financial decision-making.

The platform claims to have crossed 6 million registered users and reported around $2.5 million in annual recurring revenue. It has partnerships with lenders such as IDFC First Bank, DMI Finance, L&T Finance, DSP Finance, and InCred.

Oolka’s closest direct competitor is GoodScore, as both platforms focus on AI driven credit improvement and personalised user guidance. In October last year, GoodScore raised $13 million in a round led by Peak XV. Other platforms such as OneScore, Paisabazaar, and CRED operate in adjacent areas by offering credit score tracking and recommendations, but they are less focused on execution led credit improvement.

title: Square Yards crosses Rs 2,000 Cr revenue in FY26; EBITDA jumps 3.7X
description: Square Yards has registered over 8X growth in the last five years, with revenue rising from Rs 246 crore in FY21 to Rs 2,086 crore in FY26, as per the press release.
body: Square Yards has registered over 8X growth in the last five years, with revenue rising from Rs 246 crore in FY21 to Rs 2,086 crore in FY26, according to the company’s press release.
The Gurugram-based prop-tech firm reported a 48% year-on-year increase in revenue in the last fiscal year.

The revenue growth came alongside a jump in profitability. The company posted an EBITDA of Rs 176 crore in FY26, up 3.7X from Rs 48 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA margin expanded significantly from 3% in FY25 to 8% in FY26, which is the third consecutive year of positive EBITDA as per the company’s disclosures.

India continued to remain the primary growth driver for the company. Revenue from India grew 57% year-on-year and accounted for 88% of total revenue in FY26, while international markets, including the GCC and other regions, accounted for the remaining 12%, according to the press release.

On the operational front, the company facilitated 2,73,643 customer acquisitions during FY26. As per the release, Square Yards reported real estate transactions worth Rs 13,236 crore during the year, taking the cumulative transaction value to Rs 70,000 crore to date.

At the gross level, Square Yards reported Rs 476 crore in gross profit in FY26. Its gross margin remained stable at 23% despite the sharp rise in revenue, which suggests consistency in core unit economics.

Its fintech arm, Urban Money, also recorded strong scale. The company disbursed loans worth Rs 87,831 crore in FY26, taking cumulative disbursals to Rs 2,15,000 crore. Mortgages accounted for 86% of the total loan mix, while the remaining 14% came from business loans, personal loans, and other categories.

The company also expanded its presence in adjacent verticals. It designed 1,840 homes during FY26. In the rental and property management segment, Square Yards reported 3,719 homes under management, with 2,783 rental transactions during the year, as per the press release.

title: Indian startup funding declines to $865 Mn in April
description: Startup funding stood at $865 million in April 2026, down from $948 million in March, $100 million-plus deal, with KreditBee raising $280 million. Monthly Funding Report
body: Startup funding stood at $865 million in April 2026, down from $948 million in March, as large-ticket activity remained limited. The month recorded just one $100 million-plus deal, with KreditBee raising $280 million. Key highlights included Snabbit in home services, Palmonas in demi-fine jewellery, Oolka in credit cycle, and Sahi, a broking platform for performance-driven traders. There were no IPOs in 2026 so far, but the pipeline shows activity as Acko, Zepto, Rentomojo, Garuda Aerospace, and Kissht prepare for public listings, which reflects cautious optimism despite the funding slowdown.
This follows a robust Q1 2026, when startup funding climbed to $4 billion, supported by Neysa’s $1.2 billion round.

According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $865 million in funding during April. This amount included 9 growth and late-stage deals totaling $544 million, along with 69 early-stage deals worth $321 million. Additionally, there were 14 undisclosed deals during the month.
M-o-M and Y-o-Y trend
Month-on-month, funding surged to $2 Bn in February from $930.39 Mn in January, then fell to $948 Mn in March and $865.36 Mn in April, indicating a post-February cooldown.
Year-on-year, April funding rose to $865.36 Mn in 2026 from $745.25 Mn in 2025, but stayed below $1.03 Bn in 2024. Deal count also declined from 121 in 2024 to 92 in 2026.
Top growth-stage deals

In April 2026, growth and late-stage deals reflected a mix of fintech, manufacturing, and consumer-focused startups. KreditBee led the chart with a $280 million Series E round, followed by Polaris at $80 million in the smart metering space. Snabbit raised $56 million , while Palmonas and Sahi secured $40 million and $33 million respectively. Kimbal Technologies added $22 million, and The Hosteller raised $16 million. Battery Smart brought in $15 million in debt, while TenderCuts closed the list with $2 million.

title: Palo Alto Networks set to acquire Elevation and Lightspeed-backed Portkey
description: Palo Alto Networks is set to acquire Portkey to strengthen its enterprise AI security capabilities, as businesses scale the use of autonomous agents. News
body: Palo Alto Networks is set to acquire Portkey to strengthen its enterprise AI security capabilities, as businesses scale the use of autonomous agents.

The California-based firm plans to integrate Portkey into its Prisma AIRS platform, where it will function as a centralized AI gateway to monitor, route and secure AI-driven interactions across enterprise environments. The move targets a growing gap in AI security as organizations shift from copilots to autonomous systems that operate with high levels of access across internal and external workflows.

Portkey provides infrastructure to manage AI agents at scale, processing trillions of tokens every month with low latency. Its platform enables runtime inspection of AI traffic, enforces governance policies, and applies identity-based controls to regulate agent behavior. It also offers semantic routing, failover capabilities, telemetry and audit logs to ensure reliability and visibility across deployments.

The integration is expected to help enterprises consolidate fragmented AI tooling into a unified control layer, while improving oversight and reducing operational costs through features such as caching and usage limits. It also supports access to a wide range of large language models and tools through a single interface.
Founded in Bengaluru, Portkey builds software that helps developers and enterprises design, deploy and manage AI applications and autonomous agents in production environments.

The acquisition comes less than 2.5 months after Portkey raised $15 Mn in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital and Lightspeed. Earlier, it had secured $3 Mn in a seed round led by Lightspeed in August 2023.
Palo Alto Networks will continue to support Portkey’s existing customer base after the deal closes, which is expected in the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 2026.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startup this week [Apr 27 - May 02]
description: This week, 17 Indian startups raised around $187.2 million, comprising 4 growth-stage and 13 early-stage deals and an undisclosed deal. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 17 Indian startups raised around $187.2 million, comprising 4 growth-stage and 13 early-stage deals and an undisclosed deal.
In contrast, 19 startups had collectively secured about $47 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised a total of $126 million across four deals, led by quick home services platform Snabbit, which secured $56 million in a Series D round from Susquehanna VC, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, and Bertelsmann India Investments. This was followed by Sahi, which raised $33 million in a Series B round led by Accel, with participation from Elevation Capital.

Smart grid solutions startup Kimbal Technologies has raised $22 million (Rs 210 crore) in a Series B round led by GEF Capital Partners. Meanwhile, Battery Smart has secured $15 million in debt funding from Mirova, an affiliate of Natixis Investment Managers.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised Rs 510 crore across 13 deals this week, led by Oolka, which secured Rs 130 crore in a Series A round led by Accel with participation from Lightspeed and Z47, while HyugaLife raised Rs 100 crore in a Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures.

Fintech startup Novio, has raised Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A funding round led by Cornerstone Ventures. AI-driven supply chain optimization startup Mojro Technologies has raised $5.5 million in a Series A funding round.

title: Milky Mist raises Rs 482 Cr in pre IPO round led by Temasek arm
description: The IPO proceeds will be used for debt repayment, expansion of capacity, and modernization of its Perundurai facility. Funds will also go towards cold chain infrastructure and distribution.
body: Dairy products maker Milky Mist Dairy Food has raised around Rs 482 crore in a pre IPO funding round from Jongsong Investments Pte Ltd, an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Temasek Holdings, according to a public announcement.

The round includes a primary capital infusion of Rs 357 crore from Jongsong Investments and a secondary share sale worth Rs 125 crore by promoters Sathish Kumar T and Anitha S ahead of the company’s planned public listing.

As part of the primary issuance, Milky Mist allotted 5.43 lakh equity shares at Rs 139.76 per share, raising about Rs 7.6 crore. It also issued 25 lakh compulsorily convertible preference shares at the same price, bringing in nearly Rs 349.4 crore. These shares will convert into equity on a one to one basis prior to listing.
Based on the issue price, the company is valued at around Rs 9,300 crore, which is sharply lower than the nearly Rs 20,000 crore it had targeted earlier for its IPO.
The development comes six months after Milky Mist received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India to move ahead with its IPO.

On the financial front, the Erode based company’s revenue from operations grew 29% to Rs 2,349 crore in FY25 from Rs 1,822 crore in FY24. Its profit jumped 2.4X to Rs 46 crore in FY25 from Rs 19 crore in the previous year.

Founded in Tamil Nadu, Milky Mist focuses on premium dairy products such as paneer, cheese, yogurt, ice cream, butter, and ghee. The company does not sell liquid milk. This approach supports higher margins and a strong FMCG style positioning.
The IPO proceeds will be used for debt repayment, expansion of capacity, and modernization of its Perundurai facility. Funds will also go towards cold chain infrastructure and distribution.

title: Aurm raises Rs 42 Cr in seed round led by Earth Fund and Sattva Ventures
description: Aurm facilitates military-grade, fully automated safe deposit lockers integrated directly into gated communities, corporate campuses, and bank branches. The platform a
body: Bank locker infrastructure startup Aurm has raised Rs 42 crore in a seed funding round co-led by Earth Fund and Sattva Ventures along with participation from other angel investors.
The proceeds will be deployed to scale tech-enabled vaulting solutions and secure storage through automation and enhanced accessibility, Aurm said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2023 by Vijay Arisetty, Suraj HS, Pratap Chandana, and Ganesh Balakrishnan, Aurm provides fully automated, high-security private safety deposit lockers for residential gated communities and corporate clusters. The startup’s technology gives residents and employees on-demand access to professional-grade secure storage within their own communities.

Aurm facilitates military-grade, fully automated safe deposit lockers integrated directly into gated communities, corporate campuses, and bank branches. The platform addresses the acute scarcity of traditional bank lockers by offering a tech-led "vault-at-your-doorstep" model.

According to Aurm,its state-of-the-art strong rooms feature 24/7 accessibility, multi-factor authentication, and active intrusion-proof surveillance, all while providing a premium "dressing room" experience.

Earth Fund is a venture platform focused on PropTech and climate-forward real estate innovation, anchored by Brigade Group and Gruhas. Earth Fund's Capital++ model gives portfolio companies direct access to developer networks, industry expertise, and real-world deployment opportunities.

title: AI startup Banza raises pre-seed round led by Campus Fund
description: The Bengaluru-based startup is developing an AI Twin that adapts to a user’s preferences, habits, and context, helping them make better everyday decisions, ranging
body: AI startup Banza has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Campus Fund, with participation from Avalanche and a group of angel investors.
The funds will be used to accelerate product development, enhance user experience, expand the team, and strengthen the foundation for its personal AI category, the company said in a press release.

Founded in January this year by Mehdi A, Suraj Mulla, and Aditya Vijayakumar, Banza aims to enable users to build and own a personal AI Twin that becomes more useful over time by learning from their digital behaviour.

The Bengaluru-based startup is developing an AI Twin that adapts to a user’s preferences, habits, and context, helping them make better everyday decisions, ranging from what to eat and watch to where to go, what to buy, and how to plan experiences.

Banza believes current digital services capture only fragmented user data, resulting in siloed and incomplete experiences. Its platform aims to unify this data, allowing users to build an AI that understands them more deeply and works in their favour.

title: AI computing solutions provider Tsavorite raises $5 Mn led by Pavestone
description: The company’s OPU integrates CPU, GPU, memory, and connectivity into a single device, and can be configured for different power and performance requirements across
body: AI computing solutions provider Tsavorite has raised $5 million (Rs 46.65 crore) in Series a funding round led by Pavestone.
The startup had previously secured $17.9 million in a seed funding round on February 14, 2025.
The fresh capital will be used for product development and future growth initiatives, the company said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by Shalesh Thusoo, Tsavorite Scalable Intelligence is building an Omni Processing Unit (OPU) for the semiconductor industry, aimed at supporting AI inference, training, and reinforcement learning.

The company’s OPU integrates CPU, GPU, memory, and connectivity into a single device, and can be configured for different power and performance requirements across edge, enterprise, and data center applications.
Tsavorite also offers an integrated open software stack designed to simplify AI deployment, enabling developers to run models without code rewrites or proprietary dependencies.

title: Fireside Ventures leads Kisah’s Series A round; valuation jumps to Rs 211 Cr
description: Men’s and kids’ ethnic wear brand Kisah has kicked off its Series A funding round, raising Rs 35.9 crore (around $3.8 million) led by Fireside Ventures.
body: Men’s and kids’ ethnic wear brand Kisah has kicked off its Series A funding round, raising Rs 35.9 crore (around $3.8 million) led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from several individual investors.

The board at Kisah has passed a special resolution to issue 38,220 Series A preference shares at an issue price of Rs 9,393 each to raise the aforesaid amount, according to its regulatory filing sourced by Entrackr .
Fireside Ventures is leading the round with an investment of Rs 34 crore, which has already been infused, while the remaining amount from individual investors is expected to follow soon.
MoneyControl reported the development first.

According to Entrackr’s estimates, the company will be valued at around Rs 211 crore post-money, a 70% jump from its pre-Series A round, where it raised Rs 13 crore (around $1.5 million) from Wow! Momo co-founder Sagar Daryani, along with participation from Apoorv Salarpuria, Rahul Todi, Vinod Dugar, and Inflection Point Ventures.

Co-founded in 2018 by Yash Sarawagi and Yashwi Ladasaria, Kisah offers high-fashion ethnic wear for Gen Z and millennials at accessible price points. The Kolkata-based brand started with a marketplace-first approach and is now evolving into an omnichannel player.
The company has delivered a 65% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 41.8 crore in FY25, up from Rs 25.3 crore in FY24. At the same time, the company's profits jumped over 2X to Rs 2 crore in FY25.

title: Fireside Ventures leads $5 Mn Series A round in skincare brand CHOSEN
description: Skincare brand CHOSEN has raised $5 Mn in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures, along with participation from BOLD, L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund, Alkemi Growth Capital, and other angel investors such as CaratLane co-founder and former CEO Avnish Anand, Chandan Asokan, KC Nischal, Punit Saraogi, Nishita Ranka, and Mikki Singh.
body: Skincare brand CHOSEN has raised $5 Mn in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures, along with participation from BOLD, L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund, Alkemi Growth Capital, and other angel investors such as CaratLane co-founder and former CEO Avnish Anand, and dermatologists Dr. Chandan Asokan, KC Nischal, Punit Saraogi, Nishita Ranka, and Mikki Singh.
Prior to this, the Chennai-based startup had secured $1.2 Mn in an angel funding round in 2024.

The proceeds will be deployed to strengthen R&D capabilities, expand the pipeline of clinically validated, evidence-based products, scale its Centre of Excellence, and invest in high-impact talent across functions, CHOSEN said in a press release.

Launched in 2020 by Renita Rajan, CHOSEN develops science-led skincare for melanin-rich Indian skin, grounded in the science of the exposome and focused on four key domains of aging: pigmentation, skin texture, contour, and hair aging. Its portfolio spans both topical formulations and nutraceuticals, following a dermatologist-developed, clinic-to-consumer model.

According to CHOSEN, it has built its brand on insights from over 150,000 consultations, and its model integrates a B2B network of dermatologists with a direct-to-consumer (D2C) platform, allowing patients to begin treatment through clinical guidance and continue maintenance independently.

The company currently operates with around 58 SKUs across its doctor-led and D2C segments. Its products are prescribed in more than 2,000 clinics nationwide, while its online channel serves customers across India, with nearly 95% of digital sales coming through its own platform.

CHOSEN is also preparing for expansion into global “skin of color” markets, including regions in Latin America and East Asia, where similar dermatological needs exist. Notably, around 70% of its revenue is driven by repeat customers, particularly among women aged 30 to 50.
It directly competes with other notable players in this space, such as Avène, Heliocare, Cetaphil, Sebamed, Shiseido, and Dr. Sturm.

title: HealthFab raises Rs 20 Cr in Series A led by Atomic Capital
description: HealthFab, a menstrual hygiene startup, has raised Rs 20 crore ($2.1 million) in a Series A funding round led by Atomic Capital. The proceeds will be used. Snippets
body: HealthFab, a menstrual hygiene startup, has raised Rs 20 crore ($2.1 million) in a Series A funding round led by Atomic Capital.
The proceeds will be used to expand its period care product portfolio, scale distribution across quick commerce and general trade, and increase manufacturing capacity.

Founded in 2019 by Kiriti Acharjee, Sourav Chakrabarty, and Satyajit Chakraborty, HealthFab focuses on reusable period products and broader menstrual wellness solutions. It is known for its reusable period underwear product, GoPadFree.

The startup claims to have grown 3x year-on-year and ranks among the top brands in the reusable period underwear category on Amazon India. It currently serves over 5 lakh users and is targeting 5 million users over the next three years.
HealthFab is expanding beyond D2C into offline and quick commerce channels to reach new users, including first-time adopters of alternative period care products.
The brand plans to strengthen digital engagement and improve retention as it builds a broader product suite across energy, sleep, and pain management.

title: Ather Energy crosses Rs 1,100 Cr revenue in Q4 FY26; losses trim 57%
description: Ather Energy reported a strong performance in its last quarter of FY26 as its operating revenue grew 74% year-on-year. At the same time, the losses for the Bengaluru-based company reduced by 57%.
