body: Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ather Energy reported a strong performance in its last quarter of FY26 as its operating revenue grew 74% year-on-year. At the same time, the losses for the Bengaluru-based company reduced by 57%.
Ather’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,175 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 676 crore in Q4 FY25, according to its quarterly report sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The sale of electric two-wheelers and related services remains Ather Energy’s sole source of revenue, though the company has not disclosed a detailed breakdown of these earnings. During the quarter, it sold around 79,251 vehicles.
The company also made Rs 39 crore from non-operating sources, which took its total income in the quarter to Rs 1,214 crore.
For the full fiscal year FY26, it posted a 63% year-on-year growth in operating revenue, while narrowing its losses by nearly 37% to Rs 517 crore, compared to Rs 817 crore in the previous year.

Ather’s cost of materials, driven largely by battery and component procurement, accounted for 69% of its total expenses and rose 61% year on year to Rs 905 crore in Q4 FY26. Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses increased 17% to Rs 127 crore, compared to Rs 109 crore in the same period last year.
Depreciation and amortisation, along with legal, advertising, and other overhead expenses, drove the company’s total costs up to Rs 1,314 crore in Q4 FY26, from Rs 922 crore in Q4 FY25.

As Ather scaled up its electric two-wheeler sales and maintained a strong market presence, its operating revenue rose 74%, outpacing expense growth and helping narrow losses by 57% to Rs 100 crore in Q4 FY26.

title: Exclusive: Blue Tokai to raise Rs 175 Cr in its extended Series D round
description: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters is raising Rs 175 crore led by Anicut Capital, with participation from A91 Emerging Fund, Verlinvest, and others.
body: Specialty coffee chain Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters is raising Rs 175 crore ($19 million) in an extension of its Series D round, led by Anicut Capital, with participation from A91 Emerging Fund, Verlinvest, 12 Flags, and others.

The board at Blue Tokai has passed a special resolution to issue 6,194 Series D2 preference shares at an issue price of Rs 2,82,549 each to raise the aforementioned amount, according to regulatory filings sourced by Entrackr.

Anicut Capital will lead the round with Rs 50 crore, while A91 Emerging Fund, Verlinvest, and 12 Flags will invest Rs 35 crore, Rs 30 crore, and Rs 20 crore, respectively. Concatenate Advest, Prudent Advisors, Rama Advisors, Waterfield Fund, and Bhoruka Supply Chain will invest the remaining amount.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company will be valued at around $235 million post-money.

Blue Tokai has raised over $130 million to date, including a $25 million Series D bridge round from existing investors A91 Partners, Anicut, Verlinvest, and 12 Flags. On Monday, a Mint report said that White Whale Ventures also invested in Blue Tokai. According to the filings, post-transaction, A91 Partners will be the largest external shareholder with a 23.51% stake, followed by Verlinvest at 14.62%.
Blue Tokai currently operates over 175 cafes across multiple Indian cities and plans to expand into international markets such as Dubai and Japan.

In FY25, the company reported a 50% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 325 crore , while its losses declined by 20.6% to Rs 50 crore during the same period. The company is yet to file its FY26 annual results.

title: Netradyne acquires Moove to expand into Europe
description: Reliance and SoftBank-backed Netradyne has acquired Moove Connected Mobility, a European fleet intelligence and connected mobility company. Snippets
body: Reliance and SoftBank-backed Netradyne has acquired Moove Connected Mobility, a European fleet intelligence and connected mobility company.

The acquisition marks Netradyne’s expansion into Europe, a key strategic market. By combining its AI-driven platform with Moove’s local expertise, customer base, and operational experience, Netradyne aims to strengthen its presence across the region.

Post-acquisition, Moove will operate as part of Netradyne Europe and serve as a central hub for regional sales, partnerships, and customer engagement. Jeroen Bruinooge, former CEO of Moove, will join Netradyne as SVP and GM for Europe, leading go-to-market strategy and regional growth.

The combined entity will focus on improving fleet safety, driver performance, and operational efficiency for enterprise customers, while offering a unified AI-powered platform across North America, Europe, and Asia.

Founded in 2015, Netradyne has raised over $260 million to date from investors including Reliance Industries and SoftBank. In 2025, the company raised $90 million in a Series D round, pushing its valuation past $1.3 billion and entering the unicorn club.
Netradyne currently serves thousands of fleet customers globally, while Moove supports European enterprises with connected data-driven fleet optimization solutions.

title: Kissht IPO subscribed over 9 times on strong QIB interest
description: Digital lending platform Kissht, saw its IPO subscribed over 9X by the final day, driven by strong institutional demand with the QIB portion nearing 25X oversubscription.
body: Digital lending platform Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, witnessed strong demand for its IPO, which was subscribed over 9 times by the end of the final day of bidding. The momentum was led by institutional interest, as the Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIB) portion saw nearly 25X oversubscription.
According to exchange data, the QIB segment subscribed 24.9X, followed by Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) at 6.5X, while the retail investor quota saw relatively muted interest at 1.83X.
Kissht’s initial public offering (IPO) was open for subscription from April 30 to May 5, with a price band of Rs 162–171 and a minimum investment of Rs 14,094 for a lot size of 87 shares.

According to its RHP , Kissht’s IPO is pegged at Rs 926 crore, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 850 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.4 million shares (around Rs 76 crore). Vertex Ventures will lead the OFS by offloading 1.7 million shares, alongside Ammar Sdn Bhd, Ventureast Proactive Fund, Endiya Seed Co-creation Fund, and AION Advisory.

Ahead of the IPO opening, Kissht raised Rs 278 crore (around $30 million) from 22 anchor investors. The anchor book featured a mix of leading domestic mutual funds and global institutional investors, including HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, WhiteOak Capital, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and BNP Paribas.

Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, Kissht provides small-ticket consumer loans and has scaled aggressively on the back of partnerships with merchants across electronics, fashion, travel and other categories.

For the nine-month period ended December 2025, Kissht reported an operating revenue of Rs 1,560 crore along with a net profit of Rs 199 crore. In FY25, the company posted Rs 1,337 crore in operating revenue, with a net profit of Rs 160 crore.

title: Telephony infra startup Vobiz.ai raises $1 Mn led by Piper Serica
description: The Bengaluru-based startup offers instant DID provisioning, low-latency SIP trunking, real-time streaming, noise cancellation, and compliance automation, enabling dev
body: API-driven telephony infrastructure platform Vobiz.ai has raised $1 million in a seed funding round led by Piper Serica VC Fund.
The funds will be used to strengthen engineering and go-to-market capabilities, the company said in a press release.

Co-founded last year by Suman Gandham and Vikash Srivastava, Vobiz.ai provides low-latency, secure voice infrastructure tailored for AI voice agents and applications, addressing the limitations of traditional telephony in the era of conversational AI.

The Bengaluru-based startup offers instant DID provisioning, low-latency SIP trunking, real-time streaming, noise cancellation, and compliance automation, enabling developers to integrate voice AI quickly. It also provides low-latency call bridging optimized for AI response cycles, real-time streaming for large language model integrations, audio enhancement layers, and compliance workflows aligned with Indian telecom regulations.
According to market research, the voice AI market is expected to reach $32.47 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 29%.
Vobiz.ai aims to solve challenges such as high latency, limited programmability, poor call control, and fragmented developer experiences by building an AI-native communication platform.

Over the next 12 to 18 months, the company plans to expand its DID inventory and carrier partnerships, enhance real-time streaming capabilities, and introduce advanced observability and enterprise-grade compliance tools.
It competes with players such as Exotel, Plivo, Twilio, Telnyx, and Ubona.

title: Jurisphere raises $2.2 Mn led by InfoEdge Ventures
description: Jurisphere, a legal AI startup, has raised $2.2 million in a funding round led by InfoEdge Ventures, with participation from Flourish Ventures, Antler. Snippets
body: Jurisphere, a legal AI startup, has raised $2.2 million in a funding round led by InfoEdge Ventures, with participation from Flourish Ventures, Antler, and 8i Ventures.
The proceeds will be used to expand globally and build a network of AI-native legal professionals.
Founded in 2024 by Manas Khandelwal, Varun Khandelwal, and Sumit Ghosh, the firm is building an outcome-based legal AI platform that combines software with a network of legal professionals.

Jurisphere currently offers an AI-powered workspace used by over 500 teams across law firms, enterprises, and public institutions for workflows such as legal research, drafting, review, and collaboration.
The startup is now expanding its model to integrate AI with a marketplace of lawyers, enabling clients to access legal expertise while using shared AI workflows for execution.
Its platform focuses on improving legal outcomes rather than just productivity by combining technology with human expertise.

title: Krutrim pivots to AI cloud, clocks Rs 300 Cr revenue in FY26
description: Krutrim has shifted its focus to AI cloud services and reported around Rs 300 crore in revenue for FY26, nearly three times higher than last year.
body: Krutrim, the artificial intelligence startup founded by Bhavish Aggarwal, has shifted its focus to AI cloud services and reported around Rs 300 crore in revenue for FY26, nearly three times higher than last year.

The company has stepped back from its earlier plans to build its own large language models and semiconductor chips. Instead, it is now focusing on offering AI infrastructure, including cloud-based compute and tools for businesses.

This change in strategy seems to be working. Krutrim reportedly said it turned profitable during the year and is now running a more capital-efficient business. It also indicated that it does not need to raise fresh funds immediately.

Krutrim has built its own AI cloud platform and is already working with more than 25 enterprise clients across sectors like mobility, fintech, and e-commerce. Growing demand for GPU-based computing has supported this business.

The pivot also comes after a period of restructuring. Last year, the company laid off more than 150 employees as it recalibrated its priorities. Around the same time, Ola Electric, its promoter, pledged 10.71 crore shares , or about 2.43% of its equity, to raise funds for a Krutrim data centre.
The shift also follows challenges on the consumer side. Recently, Krutrim’s AI assistant Kruti went offline and remained inaccessible across web and app stores.
Rather than spending heavily on long-term research projects, the company is now focusing on areas where it can generate revenue faster.

At the same time, questions remain around how much of this revenue comes from outside clients. A part of the early business is believed to come from within the Ola ecosystem, and the company’s ability to grow beyond that will be important.

title: CashKaro revenue grows 72% to Rs 600 Cr in FY26; narrows losses
description: CashKaro, the Gurugram-based cashback and affiliate commerce platform, ended FY26 with Rs 600 crore in revenue, a 72% year-on-year growth from Rs 348 crore in FY25.
body: CashKaro, the Gurugram-based cashback and affiliate commerce platform, ended FY26 with Rs 600 crore in revenue, a 72% year-on-year growth from Rs 348 crore in FY25, as per the press release.

According to the company, the platform, along with its sister app EarnKaro, led over Rs 10,000 crore in gross merchandise value (GMV) for partner brands during the year, compared to Rs 6,000 crore in FY25.

The company reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 17.7 crore in FY26, down from Rs 29.2 crore in FY25, which shows better unit economics. The narrowing losses come despite continued investments in technology, automation, and expansion of the EarnKaro ecosystem.

Founded in 2013 by Swati and Rohan Bhargava, CashKaro described itself as a low-cost acquisition channel for brands at a time when customer acquisition costs (CAC) on platforms like Google and Meta continue to rise. “We are seeing brands increasingly shift budgets towards affiliate-led models where they pay only for actual sales, not just traffic,” Swati Bhargava told Entrackr.

As per the company, growth came from better efficiency.  Revenue rose 72%, while marketing spend for CashKaro and EarnKaro went up only 7.6%, which indicates stronger conversion and better customer acquisition efficiency. Employee and infrastructure costs stayed stable, supported by AI-led automation.
Its sister arm, EarnKaro remained a key growth driver for the group which builds strong traction across platforms such as Telegram, WhatsApp, Instagram, and YouTube.

The company said it has paid over Rs 2,000 crore in cashback to users so far, transferred directly to bank accounts. Categories such as fashion, beauty, and D2C brands remain the largest contributors, while financial services and other high-value segments show early traction.
Backed by investors including Kalaari Capital, Affle Global, Korean Investment Partners, and Ratan Tata, CashKaro has raised over Rs 250 crore to date.

title: Paytm reports Rs 2,264 Cr revenue and Rs 183 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: Paytm, announced its financial results Q4 FY26. The company reported a profit of Rs 183 crore, maintained profitability for consecutive quarters, and achieved full-year profitability in FY26.
body: Fintech major One97 Communications, which operates Paytm, announced its financial results for the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended March 2026 today. The company reported a profit of Rs 183 crore, maintained profitability for consecutive quarters, and achieved full-year profitability in FY26.

Paytm’s revenue from operations rose over 18% year-on-year to Rs 2,264 in Q4 FY26 crore from Rs 1,912 crore in Q4 FY25, according to its unaudited quarterly report filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The company also added Rs 178 crore from other non-operating sources, which took its overall revenue to Rs 2,442 crore in Q4 FY26. On a sequential basis, Paytm’s revenue remained flat.
For the full year FY26, the company’s revenue increased 22% to Rs 8,437 crore from Rs 6,900 crore in FY25. During the period, it achieved profitability with a profit of Rs 552 crore.

For the fintech firm, employee benefits remained the largest cost head, accounting for 32.5% of total costs and remained flat at Rs 739 crore. Payment processing charges followed at Rs 692 crore, which rose 33% year-on-year.

Marketing expenses rose 18% to Rs 169 crore in Q4 FY26. Software, communication, legal, cashback, and other overheads pushed total expenditure to Rs 2,269 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 2,155 crore in Q4 FY25.
Paytm recorded a profit of Rs 183 crore during the quarter, compared to a loss of Rs 545 crore in the same quarter last year, which resulted from exceptional items.
Paytm also rolled out fresh employee stock options (ESOPs) worth nearly Rs 19.5 crore, covering 1.77 lakh equity shares under its ESOP 2019 scheme, according to a separate NSE disclosure.

title: Meesho posts Rs 3,531 Cr revenue in Q4 FY26; losses trim 88%
description: Meesho has announced its financial results for the Q4 FY26 today. The firm reported a 47% year-on-year increase in revenue, while its losses narrowed sharply by 88% during the same period.
body: E-commerce marketplace Meesho has announced its financial results for the last quarter of the previous fiscal year (Q4 FY26) today. The firm reported a 47% year-on-year increase in revenue, while its losses narrowed sharply by 88% during the same period.
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 3,531 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 2,400 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from NSE.
Other income contributed an additional Rs 116 crore, which drove its total income of Rs 3,647 crore for the quarter.

For the full year ended March 2026, Meesho’s revenue rose 35% to Rs 12,626 crore from Rs 9,390 crore a year earlier. During the same period, the company’s losses before exceptional items and tax stood at Rs 1,068 crore.
Other income contributed an additional Rs 116 crore, which drove its total income of Rs 3,647 crore for the quarter.

For the full year ended March 2026, Meesho’s revenue rose 35% to Rs 12,626 crore from Rs 9,390 crore a year earlier. During the same period, the company’s losses before exceptional items and tax stood at Rs 1,068 crore.
While the majority of the expenses were undisclosed in the quarterly financial statements, Meesho spent Rs 232 crore on employee benefits in Q4 FY26, which remained largely unchanged from Q4 FY25.

Its depreciation stood at Rs 19 crore for the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expense rose 44% to Rs 3,807 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 2,637 crore in Q4 FY25. Meesho also narrowed its losses by 88% to Rs 166 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 1,391 crore in Q4 FY25.

title: PB Fintech reports Rs 2,061 Cr revenue in Q4 FY26; profit rises 54%
description: PB Fintech, the parent of PolicyBazaar, reported its Q4 FY26 results, with operating revenue up 37% year-on-year to cross the Rs 2,000 crore threshold, while profit rose 54% in the quarter.
body: PB Fintech, the parent company of online insurance aggregator and brokerage platform PolicyBazaar, announced its Q4 FY26 results. The company reported a 37% year-on-year increase in operating revenue, crossing the Rs 2,000 crore threshold. Its profit also rose 54% during the quarter.

PolicyBazaar’s revenue from operations surged to Rs 2,061 crore in Q4 FY26 in contrast to Rs 1,508 crore in Q4 FY25 , as per the firm’s financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The Gurugram-based company derived 92% of its operating revenue from insurance broking services, which grew 44% year-on-year to Rs 1,901 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 1,322 crore in the same quarter last year. The rest of 160 crore came from other services.

In addition to operating revenue, the firm earned Rs 104 crore from interest and gains on financial assets during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 2,166 crore for the quarter ended March 2026.
For the full year ended March 2026, PB Fintech’s operating scale rose 37% to Rs 6,794 crore from Rs 4,977 crore in FY25. During the same period, its profit increased 90% to Rs 670 crore.

Employee benefit expenses accounted for 37% of the group’s total costs, amounting to Rs 699 crore, and increased by over 37% compared to the same quarter last year. Spending on advertising and promotion also rose 34% to Rs 371 crore in Q4 FY26.

The company did not disclose a detailed expense breakdown in its quarterly financials. Overall expenses rose 31% year-on-year to Rs 1,888 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 1,438 crore in the same quarter last year.
In the end, the firm’s profit rose 54% year-on-year to Rs 261 crore in the quarter ended March 2026 from Rs 170 crore in Q4 FY25, as revenue growth exceeded expense growth.

title: Ecofy secures $15 Mn debt from Mirova
description: o-founded in 2022 by Rajashree Nambiar and Govind Sankaranarayanan, Ecofy provides financing for economically sustainable climate initiatives, including electric
body: Ecofy, a non-banking financial company focused on climate change solutions, has secured $15 million debt from Mirova.

The Mumbai based NBFC had earlier raised Rs 380.5 crore (approximately $42 million) in a Series B equity round co-led by British International Investment and Finnfund in March this year, and Rs 90 crore from FMO, the Dutch Entrepreneurial development bank in Jan. 2024.

The fresh funds will be utilized to support onward lending and finance residential and commercial & industrial (C&I) rooftop solar installations, as well as electric mobility solutions across India, Ecofy said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2022 by Rajashree Nambiar and Govind Sankaranarayanan, Ecofy provides financing for economically sustainable climate initiatives, including electric vehicles (EVs), rooftop solar systems, energy-efficient equipment, energy storage, e-mobility, waste recycling, and water management, among others.
In just three years, the company claims to have scaled to serve over 130,000 customers, with a pan-India presence across 26 states and more than 500 cities.
On the financial front, Ecofy’s revenue from operations surged 4.8X to Rs 93.3 crore in FY25 from Rs 19.19 crore in FY24. At the same time, its losses increased 15.6% to Rs 42.28 crore.

Ecofy aims to be a catalyst in accelerating the transition toward a net-zero carbon world. It partners with individuals and small businesses seeking to reduce their carbon footprint and restore balance to the planet.

The company has grown its assets under management (AUM) to over Rs 1,400 crore, supported by a 100% retail loan book, partnerships with more than 100 OEMs and over 23 banks and financial institutions, strong asset quality, and a capital adequacy ratio of approximately 50% following the fundraise.

title: AI Library raises pre-seed funding round
description: AI Library has also introduced AI Library MCP, a unified infrastructure layer designed to simplify how AI agents operate in real-world enterprise environments. MCP acts
body: Outcome-based AI-native software delivery company AI Library has raised $560K in a pre-seed funding round at a $7.5 million valuation cap from prominent investors.

The fresh funds will be used to enhance product development, expand market presence, and invest in R&D, enabling AI Library to accelerate agent-driven software delivery for enterprises across functions such as finance, operations, sales, and support, AI Library said in a press release.

Launched in Nov. 2023 by Arani Chaudhuri, AI Library is an outcome-based AI-native software delivery company building autopilots for software delivery that enable enterprises to move from AI adoption to real business outcomes by automating the software delivery lifecycle using AI agents with human oversight.

According to AI Library, it enables faster time to production, cost-effective delivery, and continuously improving systems that scale like a flywheel, helping organisations reduce costs, improve efficiency, and accelerate time-to-value.

AI Library has also introduced AI Library MCP, a unified infrastructure layer designed to simplify how AI agents operate in real-world enterprise environments. MCP acts as a single server that equips coding agents with structured access to tools, data, and workflows, eliminating the need for fragmented integrations across search, parsing, storage, retrieval, and APIs. By reducing noisy inputs and redundant reruns, MCP aims to improve efficiency and reliability for enterprise AI deployments.
With deployments across enterprises including Tally, Times Group, Burger Singh, and DeKoder, AI Library is helping reshape software delivery through outcome-led, scalable, and AI-native execution.

title: JobsUPI raises pre-seed round from IIMA Ventures and others
description: obsUPI aims to become a foundational layer for employment infrastructure in Bharat, driven by the belief that access to livelihoods should be as seamless as access to
body: JobsUPI, a multilingual and multimodal employment platform, has raised $250K in a pre-seed funding round from IIMA Ventures along with participation from angel investors including Alok Bansal, Anshoo Sharma, Amit Jain, and Manoj Sinsinwar, among others.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen product capabilities, scale distribution, and expand into new geographies, JobsUPI said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2025 by Shrey Bansal and Shubham Periwal, JobsUPI is a multilingual, multimodal, Voice AI-powered employment platform built to improve access to jobs across India. With a focus on speed, accessibility, and hyperlocal discovery, the platform aims to enable hiring in as little as 30 minutes over time.

JobsUPI is building a “quick commerce for jobs” model with the goal of enabling hiring in as little as 30 minutes by making job discovery, matching, and applications seamless. Built on an open network architecture, the platform is designed to improve access to employment opportunities for blue-collar and skilled workers across Bharat.

JobsUPI aims to become a foundational layer for employment infrastructure in Bharat, driven by the belief that access to livelihoods should be as seamless as access to commerce. Over the long term, the company envisions unlocking 100 million jobs by enabling 10 million MSMEs and enterprises to hire more efficiently.
The platform currently operates in North India and is expanding to other regions. It competes with players such as Apna, Smartstaff, and AamDhanE.

title: Capillary Technologies posts Rs 191 Cr revenue and Rs 43 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: Capillary Technologies recorded a 26% YoY increase in revenue during the quarter, while its profit rose more than fourfold to Rs 43 crore in the same period, aided by a one-time exceptional gain.
body: SaaS firm Capillary Technologies announced its financial results for Q4 FY26 today. The company recorded a 26% year-on-year increase in revenue during the quarter, while its profit rose more than fourfold to Rs 43 crore in the same period, aided by a one-time exceptional gain.
The Bengaluru-based company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 191 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 152 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from NSE.

Founded in 2008 by Aneesh Reddy, Krishna Mehra, and Ajay Modani, Capillary Technologies offers cloud-native loyalty, CRM, and customer engagement solutions to more than 390 brands across 46 countries. Its clientele includes Tata Digital, Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, and Abbott Laboratories.

The company earned Rs 171 crore from subscriptions, which accounted for nearly 90% of its operating revenue, while installation and campaign services contributed the remaining Rs 20 crore. It also generated Rs 6.7 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income for the quarter to Rs 198 crore.
For the full year ended March 2026, its revenue from operations rose 23% year-on-year to Rs 735 crore. During the same period, its profit declined 61% to Rs 5.2 crore.

On the cost front, employee benefit expenses accounted for 56% of the company’s total expenditure. This cost increased 35% to Rs 89.6 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 66.5 crore in the same quarter last year. Software and server charges and professional and consultancy fees stood at Rs 32.7 crore at Rs 25.8 crore respectively for the quarter. Overall, total expenses rose 28% to Rs 181 crore during the period.

While the company’s revenue and expenses grew at a similar pace, its profit surged over fourfold to Rs 43 crore in Q4 FY26, supported by a one-time compensation of Rs 24.96 crore from a seller following a breach of customer retention commitments in a US acquisition deal.
In February earlier this year, the firm approved an investment of $20 million in its wholly owned overseas arm to acquire US-based loyalty and engagement platform Session M Inc.

title: MedVital raises Rs 18 Cr led by Alkemi Growth Capital
description: MedVital, a medtech startup focused on wound care and regenerative aesthetics, has raised Rs 18 crore ($1.89 million) in a growth funding round led by Alkemi Growth Capital Snippets
body: MedVital, a medtech startup focused on wound care and regenerative aesthetics, has raised Rs 18 crore ($1.89 million) in a growth funding round led by Alkemi Growth Capital.
The round also saw participation from Sanjay Arora, Shubhan Ventures, and existing investors. The firm had previously raised funding from 4point0 Health Ventures and other angel investors.
The proceeds will be used to expand operations, accelerate product development, and strengthen capabilities across devices, biomaterials, and biologics.
Founded in 2024, MedVital develops medical technologies across advanced wound care, regenerative aesthetics, and chronic skin conditions.

MedVital currently operates in the advanced wound care segment through its NoWound portfolio, which includes negative pressure wound therapy systems and liquid bandage products designed for hospitals.
The brand claims to have achieved adoption across more than 200 healthcare institutions in India with repeat usage from hospitals.
It has also launched Elyara, a regenerative aesthetics product line focused on non-invasive skin and hair restoration solutions.

title: MochaTrade raises pre-seed funding from Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund
description: MochaTrade, a global trading platform focused on perpetual futures linked to US stocks, commodities, and indices, has raised an undisclosed pre-seed round. Snippets
body: MochaTrade, a global trading platform focused on perpetual futures linked to US stocks, commodities, and indices, has raised an undisclosed pre-seed round from Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund as part of Y Combinator’s Spring 2026 batch.
The funds will be used to build the trading engine and risk infrastructure, complete regulatory and compliance work, and support go-to-market efforts.

Founded by Utkarsh Sinha, Chetan Manda, and Parth Maheshwari, the startup is building a mobile-first platform that aims to offer eligible users leveraged exposure to assets such as Apple, Tesla, gold, and the S&P 500 through perpetual futures products.
Its platform is designed to enable continuous trading and real-time settlement, allowing users to redeploy capital immediately after positions are closed.
MochaTrade plans to launch first in developing markets, subject to regulatory approvals and local laws.

The founding team previously worked across fintech and consumer technology firms. Utkarsh Sinha earlier co-founded Martian Wallet, while Chetan Manda previously worked at Sprinklr and Parth Maheshwari worked at Adobe and Navi.

title: Freshworks posts $228.6 Mn revenue and $4.8 Mn loss in Q1 CY26
description: Freshworks reported a 16% year-on-year growth in its first quarter (Q1 CY26) revenue to $228.6 million, compared to $196.3 million in the same period last year.
body: NASDAQ-listed SaaS company Freshworks reported a 16% year-on-year growth in its first quarter (Q1 CY26) revenue to $228.6 million, compared to $196.3 million in the same period last year.
On a quarter-on-quarter basis, its revenue grew around a modest 2%, compared to $223 million in Q4 CY25.

According to the filing, the company continued to improve its operating performance during the quarter. Its non-GAAP operating income stood at $41 million with a margin of 17.9%. However, its net losses stood at $4.8 million in Q1 CY26, compared to a loss of $1.3 million in the year-ago period.

Freshworks reported a non-GAAP net income per share of $0.11 in Q1 CY26, down from $0.18 in the same quarter last year. The company also generated an operating cash flow of $62.4 million during the quarter.

As per the company, growth during the quarter was led by continued demand for its employee experience (EX) products and rising adoption of its AI-led offerings, including Copilot features across its platforms.

During the quarter, Freshworks announced a workforce reduction of around 500 employees, or nearly 11% of its total staff, as part of a restructuring exercise. The company said the move is aimed at improving efficiency and aligning its operations with increased use of artificial intelligence.

Freshworks expects to incur a one-time restructuring cost of around $8 million, most of which will be reflected in the second quarter of 2026. The company anticipates the revenue to be in the range of $232 million to $235 million in Q2 CY26.

title: Exclusive: BazaarNow set to raise around $8 Mn led by Peak XV
description: As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation will surge to around Rs 270 crore post-money  from nearly Rs 40 crore in its seed round.
body: Quick commerce startup BazaarNow is set to raise Rs 72.3 crore (approximately $7.8 million)  in its Series A round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from existing investors Whiteboard Capital and Antler. The board of BazaarNow has passed a resolution to approve the issuance of 8,123 CCPS at an issue price of Rs 88,851.94 each to the above-mentioned sum, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) . Peak XV Partners is set to lead the round with an investment of Rs 53.92 crore, followed by existing investors Whiteboard Capital and Antler, contributing Rs 7.2 crore and Rs 7 crore, respectively. The remaining capital will come from Nirman Ventures and a group of angel investors, including Vidit Aatrey, founder and CEO of Meesho.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation will surge to around Rs 270 crore post-money  from nearly Rs 40 crore in its seed round. The proceeds will be used for meeting working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes.

In December 2025, as per regulatory filings, the company had previously raised Rs 7.82 crore in its seed round led by Antler and Whiteboard Capital. Launched in January 2026, BazaarNow is a Bengaluru-based quick commerce startup founded by former Zepto executives Priyanshu Jain, Arjun Harish, and Tarithnay Mandal. The company offers sub-10-minute delivery of groceries, daily essentials, and higher-margin categories through a network of dark stores, and is currently operational in select areas of Bengaluru.

BazaarNow competes in India’s rapidly growing quick commerce market dominated by players such as Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and Zepto, while newer entrants including Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now are also expanding aggressively.

title: BigEndian Semiconductors raises $6 Mn in pre Series A round led by IAN Alpha Fund
description: BigEndian Semiconductors has raised $6 million in a pre Series A funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from existing investors Vertex Ventures SEA and India, and others
body: Fabless semiconductor startup BigEndian Semiconductors has raised $6 million in a pre Series A funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from existing investors Vertex Ventures SEA and India, IvyCap Ventures, and strategic angel investors.
Prior to this, the Bengaluru based startup had secured $3 million in a seed funding round from Vertex Ventures in August 2024.

The proceeds will be used to commercialise its first system on chip SoC, scale product engineering, and strengthen partnerships across foundries, IP ecosystems, and OEMs, the company said in a press release.

Co founded in March 2024 by Sunil Kumar, Renuka Prasad, Dinesh Annayya, Kanagaraju Ponnusamy, and Jansen Cheng, BigEndian Semiconductors is a fabless semiconductor startup building secure, high performance SoCs designed in India for global applications. The startup focuses on developing silicon platforms for surveillance, telecom, IoT, and enterprise systems.

BigEndian integrates hardware and software with expertise in VLSI, system architecture, and embedded software. It is developing trusted silicon solutions for both national security and commercial use cases.

Building fabless semiconductors requires long term capital, deep technical expertise, and a high tolerance for early stage risk, areas where India’s ecosystem is still evolving. As global supply chains diversify, the company is navigating complex design, verification, and tape out cycles while building original silicon IP.
With strategic partnerships across Taiwan and India, BigEndian is working to support end to end semiconductor innovation from architecture and tape out to product launch.
Major players in this space include Netrasemi, L&T, Mindgrove, and Novatek.

title: InMobi acquires MobileAction to strengthen iOS advertising business
description: InMobi has acquired MobileAction, an AI powered platform focused on iOS app growth and analytics, as the Bengaluru and San Francisco based company looks to strengthen its advertising business globally.
body: InMobi has acquired MobileAction, an AI powered platform focused on iOS app growth and analytics, as the Bengaluru and San Francisco based company looks to strengthen its advertising business globally.
The financial details of the deal were not disclosed.

Founded in 2013 and headquartered in San Francisco, MobileAction offers tools for Apple Ads and App Store Optimization, helping app developers and marketers improve app visibility and user acquisition. The platform is used by brands such as Google, Meta, Doordash, Square, Zalando, Playtika, and Priceline.

The acquisition is expected to strengthen InMobi Advertising’s capabilities across the iOS ecosystem by combining MobileAction’s expertise in app discovery and performance marketing with InMobi’s advertising infrastructure and consumer commerce platform Glance.

According to the company, MobileAction has access to data across more than 90 million creatives, 6 million keywords, 5 million apps, 100,000 publishers, and 500,000 advertisers. InMobi said the acquisition will help brands improve user targeting and campaign optimization through AI driven tools.

Following the acquisition, MobileAction will continue to operate as an independent platform while its teams across the United States, Europe, and Turkey join the InMobi Group. InMobi also plans to expand MobileAction’s product and market presence across the US, APAC, and MENA regions.

In December 2025, InMobi raised $350 million in funding from Varde Partners, Elham Credit Partners, and SeaTown Holdings. The funding included a $200 million loan at the operating company level and a $150 million loan at the holding company level, both secured against the founders’ stake.
The founding team of InMobi, which offers mobile advertising network software, had also reportedly bought back around 25 to 30% stake from Japanese investor SoftBank.

title: Ola Cabs’ revenue plunges 42% to Rs 1,171 Cr in FY25; losses double
description: Bhavish Aggarwal-led ride-hailing platform Ola Consumer (formerly Ola Cabs) reported a 42% decline in operating scale in FY25 after crossing the Rs 2,000 crore revenue mark in FY24.
body: Bhavish Aggarwal-led ride-hailing platform Ola Consumer (formerly Ola Cabs) continues to lose market share as rival Rapido gains traction in the four-wheeler ride-hailing segment. The impact became visible in Ola’s FY25 financial performance, with its operating scale declining 42% after crossing the Rs 2,000 crore revenue mark in FY24.
Importantly, the company’s losses also doubled in FY25.

Ola Cabs’ revenue from operation declined to Rs 1,171 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2025, compared to Rs 2,012 crore in FY24, its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) show.
Income from Ola Cabs’ ride-hailing business accounted for 79% of its total operating revenue in FY25, but declined more than 47% to Rs 925 crore from Rs 1,761 crore in FY24.

OlaMoney, Ola Cabs’ financial services arm, also reported a 19% decline in revenue to Rs 185 crore during the period. The segment offers insurance and vehicle financing services, primarily for Ola Electric customers, along with wallet services and the OlaMoney credit card.

The SoftBank-backed firm also generated Rs 61 crore from commerce, logistics, and other services, while non-operating income stood at Rs 198 crore, largely from interest on fixed deposits and current investments. As a result, the company’s total income for FY25 reached Rs 1,369 crore.

For Ola Cabs’ ride-hailing business, driver-related costs accounted for nearly 20% of the total expenditure. Amid lower mobility operations, these expenses declined 34% to Rs 401 crore in FY25 from Rs 607 crore in FY24. Employee benefit expenses also fell 39% to Rs 205 crore in FY25, following a 42% decline in the previous fiscal year.

Advertisement expenses more than doubled to Rs 233 crore in FY25 from Rs 107 crore in FY24 as Ola Cabs stepped up efforts to boost operations. Legal, rent, IT, and other overhead expenses pushed the company’s total expenditure to Rs 2,038 crore in FY25, largely flat compared to FY24.

title: InCred posts Rs 1,849 Cr revenue in first 9 months of FY26
description: InCred company also reported strong financial performance for the first nine months of FY26, with revenue rising 39% year-on-year, while profit remained steady at Rs 290 crore during the period.
body: InCred Holdings, the parent company of NBFC arm InCred Financial Services, has filed its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) with SEBI to raise Rs 1,250 crore through a fresh issue in its IPO. The company also reported strong financial performance for the first nine months of FY26, with revenue rising 39% year-on-year, while profit remained steady at Rs 290 crore during the period.
According to its updated DRHP, the Mumbai-based company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,849 crore during the first nine months of FY26 from Rs 1,334 crore in the corresponding period of FY25.

Founded by Bhupinder Singh in 2017, InCred Finance is a retail-focused diversified NBFC offering lending products across five verticals, including personal loans, student loans, secured business loans, specialised MSME loans, and loans to financial institutions.

Interest income from loan disbursements formed the bulk of InCred’s revenue, accounted for over 91% of the total operating income at Rs 1,689 crore, and rose 39% year-on-year. Fees and commission income stood at Rs 150 crore, while the remaining operating income came from net gains on fair value changes in financial assets.
The firm also made Rs 21 crore from other income, tallying its total revenue to Rs 1,849 crore during the period.

For the fintech firm, finance costs formed 46% of the overall expenditure and rose 51% to Rs 673 crore during the nine-month period. Employee benefit expenses also increased 28% to Rs 311 crore from Rs 243 crore in the corresponding period of FY25.
Losses from impaired financial instruments, including loan write-offs during the period, jumped 86% to Rs 234 crore.

Depreciation along with legal, collection expenses, advertising, traveling, and other expenses took the firm’s overall cost up 52% to Rs 1,471 crore in 9M FY26 from Rs 966 crore in the same period of FY25.

title: Emami acquires 60% stake in Vedix, SkinKraft parent IncNut for Rs 321 Cr
description: FMCG major Emami Ltd has signed a definitive agreement to acquire a 60% stake in IncNut Digital, the parent company Vedix and SkinKraft, for Rs 321 crore. Snippets
body: FMCG major Emami Ltd has signed a definitive agreement to acquire a 60% stake in IncNut Digital, the parent company of personalised beauty and wellness brands Vedix and SkinKraft, for Rs 321 crore.

The deal includes performance-linked adjustments over a 24-month period. Emami will also acquire the remaining stake in two tranches over the next four-and-a-half years based on future performance metrics.
Founded in 2011, Hyderabad-based IncNut operates personalised beauty and wellness brands Vedix and SkinKraft through a D2C model.
Vedix offers customised Ayurvedic haircare and wellness products, while SkinKraft focuses on dermatology-led personalised skincare and haircare solutions.
According to Emami, the acquisition will strengthen its presence in the fast-growing personalised beauty and personal care segment.
The FMCG company already operates brands such as The Man Company and Brillare in the beauty and grooming category.

IncNut uses data-driven diagnostics, AI-led assessments, and customised formulations to offer tailored beauty products. The company has built a strong subscription-led business with high repeat usage.

title: Fintech startup Freo acquires IndiaLends
description: Fintech startup Freo has announced the acquisition of digital lending marketplace IndiaLends in a deal that will give it full ownership of the company. Snippets
body: Fintech startup Freo has announced the acquisition of digital lending marketplace IndiaLends in a deal that will give it full ownership of the company.
The acquisition brings together Freo’s financial products and regulatory licences with IndiaLends’ lending marketplace and distribution network.
Following the deal, Freo's ecosystem will serve more than 50 million users.

Founded by IIT-ISB alumni, Freo offers products across payments, credit, insurance, and investments. The company operates with licences including a TPAP licence for UPI, an NBFC licence, and an insurance corporate agent licence.

IndiaLends, founded by Gaurav Chopra, operates a digital marketplace for loans and credit cards and has integrations with over 80 banks, NBFCs, and financial institutions., IndiaLendson had raised $5.1 million in a financing round led by existing investors ACP Partners and DSG Consumer Partners
The combined entity plans to focus on AI-led workflows, customer analytics, underwriting, and integrated product offerings as it scales operations.
The integration is expected to improve operating metrics and strengthen product execution over the coming months.
Freo also said the merged entity is planning a large capital raise to support its next phase of growth.

title: CarTrade crosses Rs 200 Cr revenue in Q4 FY26; profit rises 54%
description: CarTrade released its financial results Q4 Fy26 and reported over 19% year-on-year growth in revenue, which crossed the Rs 200 crore mark during the quarter, while profit rose 54% to Rs 71 crore in the same period.
body: Automobile classifieds platform CarTrade released its financial results for the fourth quarter of FY26 and reported over 19% year-on-year growth in revenue, which crossed the Rs 200 crore mark during the quarter, while profit rose 54% to Rs 71 crore in the same period.

CarTrade’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 203 crore in Q4 FY26 in contrast to Rs 170 crore in Q4 FY25, as per the firm’s unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
On a sequential basis, its revenue declined marginally by over 3% during the quarter from Rs 210 crore in Q3 FY26.

The Mumbai-based company operates across three segments: Consumer, Remarketing, and Classifieds (OLX India). The consumer segment contributed 39% of the total operating revenue, with income rising to Rs 79 crore in Q4 FY26. Revenue from the remarketing and classifieds segments stood at Rs 72 crore and Rs 55 crore, respectively, during the quarter, before Rs 3 crore in intersegment eliminations.

The company also earned Rs 17.6 crore from interest income on bank deposits, gain on fair valuation of financial assets and other sources, which took its overall income in the quarter to Rs 221 crore.

For the full year FY26, the firm reported over 21% year-on-year growth in operating income to Rs 779 crore from Rs 641 crore in FY25. Its profit also rose more than 68% to Rs 244 crore during the same period.

On the expense front, employee benefit expenses accounted for over 53% of the overall expenditure and increased 10% to Rs 78 crore during the quarter. Including finance costs and depreciation & amortization expenses and other expenses, CarTrade’s total expenditure rose a modest 7% to Rs 146 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 136 crore in Q4 FY25.

Controlled expenditure and steady growth in operating scale across all three segments enabled CarTrade to increase its profit by over 54% year-on-year to Rs 71 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 46 crore in the same quarter last year.

title: Piper Serica leads $1 Mn seed round in airport operations tech company Blunav
description: he Chennai based Blunav’s first deployment is at Chennai International Airport under the Airports Authority of India’s Startup India initiative. Following deployment, i
body: Airport operations technology company Blunav has raised $1 million in a seed funding round led by Piper Serica.
The proceeds will be deployed towards team expansion, continued product development, and scaling deployments across India and international markets, Blunav said in a press release.

Co founded by Suseendar Marimuthu and Cherukuru Sridharan, Blunav is an airport technology company building a full stack, cloud based Airport Operating System that integrates operational, passenger, and enterprise systems into a unified platform. The company enables airports, particularly small and mid sized hubs, to modernise operations, improve efficiency, and enhance passenger experience.

Blunav aims to address a persistent challenge across the aviation ecosystem. Smaller regional airports often rely on manual processes, while mid sized facilities operate through fragmented vendor systems. Large hubs, meanwhile, manage complex multi terminal environments where operational data exists in silos with limited interoperability between systems.

The Chennai based Blunav’s first deployment is at Chennai International Airport under the Airports Authority of India’s Startup India initiative. Following deployment, its Airside Management software enabled the airport to record a 22% reduction in runway occupancy time during a 20 day study covering more than 3,500 flights.

Blunav’s Airport Operating System is designed to unify multiple operational systems into a single connected platform, enabling real time access to operational data across teams, systems, and passenger touchpoints.
The startup competes with global airport technology firms such as SITA and Amadeus.

title: Skyroot becomes India’s first spacetech unicorn after $60 Mn funding round
description: Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Skyroot Aerospace has raised $60 million (around Rs 570 crore) in a funding round co-led by Sherpalo Ventures and Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC. News
body: Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Skyroot Aerospace has raised $60 million (around Rs 570 crore) in a funding round co-led by Sherpalo Ventures and Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC.
The round also saw participation from BlackRock, Arkam Ventures, Playbook Partners, Shanghvi Family Office, and existing investors, including the founders of Greenko Group.
Entrackr had exclusively reported on Skyroot’s debt funding last month.

With the fresh round, Skyroot’s valuation has crossed $1.1 billion, making it India’s first spacetech unicorn. The startup was valued at around $550 million in 2023 after raising $27 million in a pre-Series C round.
The proceeds will be used to scale manufacturing, increase the frequency of Vikram-1 launches, and accelerate the development of Vikram-2, a heavier launch vehicle powered by a cryogenic stage.
As part of the latest investment, Sherpalo Ventures founder Ram Shriram will join Skyroot’s board.
Founded in 2018 by former ISRO scientists Pawan Kumar Chandana and Naga Bharath Daka, Skyroot Aerospace builds small and medium-lift launch vehicles for the global satellite market.

The company is working on its Vikram series of rockets, including Vikram-I and Vikram-II, aimed at providing on-demand, cost-effective, and flexible satellite launch services. It also became the first private Indian company to launch a rocket into space with its Vikram-S mission in 2022.

title: Chiratae backs 5 startups in Sonic DeepTech batch with $10 Mn commitment
description: From the competitive pool of applicants, Chiratae selected a focused cohort of high-conviction startups and committed up to $10 million in investments across CtrlB, Int
body: Venture capital firm Chiratae Ventures has announced its Sonic DeepTech batch following its Demo Day hosted yesterday in Bengaluru. The program drew thousands of applications, showcasing the depth and breadth of frontier innovation emerging across the country.

From the competitive pool of applicants, Chiratae selected a focused cohort of high-conviction startups and committed up to $10 million in investments across CtrlB, Interact AI, SuprSend, TakeMe2Space, and a stealth startup.

The selected startups will benefit from resources offered through the NVIDIA Inception program, designed to help startups accelerate technical innovation and business growth at all stages. Through the program, they will gain access to advanced AI developer tools and training, preferred pricing on NVIDIA hardware and software, exclusive partner offers, and exposure to a global network of investors and ecosystem players.

Among the selected companies, TakeMe2Space is developing nanosatellite infrastructure for edge AI computing and Earth observation, with a roadmap toward interconnected on-orbit data systems. CtrlB is building a serverless data lake platform designed to reduce observability data storage and analytics costs through a diskless, cloud-native architecture.

Interact AI offers AI avatars that replace static chatbots with audio-visual, product-aware conversational agents trained on sales and marketing content. SuprSend has developed a multi-channel notification infrastructure that helps orchestrate communications through a single API. The final investment is in a stealth vertical AI platform.

The Sonic DeepTech program offers up to $2 million in seed funding and covers sectors such as energy and climate, quantum technologies, robotics and advanced manufacturing, space technologies, applied AI/ML, bio and med-tech, and the digital economy.
Chiratae has backed companies such as AgroStar, Cult.fit, Fibe, FirstCry, Flipkart, Lenskart, Myntra, Pixis, PolicyBazaar, and Vayana.

title: Pronto raises additional $20 Mn in Series B round at $200 Mn valuation
description: Pronto has extended its Series B round to $45 million with a fresh $20 million investment from Lachy Groom. The round values the company at $200 million.
body: Instant household services startup Pronto has extended its Series B round to $45 million with a fresh $20 million investment from Lachy Groom. The round values the company at $200 million and doubles its valuation within about a month.

The latest funding comes shortly after the startup closed the first tranche of its Series B round at $25 million. Existing investors include General Catalyst, Bain Capital Ventures, Glade Brook Capital Partners, Epiq Capital and Lachy Groom. The startup has raised about $60 million to date.

Founded in 2025 by Anjali Sardana, Pronto connects households with trained and background-verified professionals for services such as cleaning, laundry, utensil washing, meal preparation, car washing and gardening.

According to the company, its daily bookings have risen to 26,000 from around 18,000 since the first close of the Series B round. The figure translates to nearly 780,000 monthly bookings. Its professional workforce has also expanded from 1,440 in January to 6,500 over the past four months. The company added that the platform is currently operating at over 65% utilization.

“Organizing informal labor is going to be one of the defining shifts of the next decade in services. The longer-term vision of Pronto is to be the world's largest labor organization platform,” said Sardana.

The startup plans to deepen its presence in existing cities over the next six months. It has also expanded into categories such as car washing, gardening and home cooks in select micromarkets including Bengaluru.

The segment is witnessing rising competition from both incumbents and new entrants. Urban Company said its InstaHelp service crossed 1 million bookings in March, while Snabbit also reported 1 million orders during the same period.

The category has also attracted significant investor interest over the past year. Combined funding raised by Snabbit and Pronto has reached nearly $170 million since January 2025, including around $100 million in 2026 alone. Snabbit also closed a $56 million Series D round last month.

title: Tencent offloads 1.05% stake in PB Fintech for Rs 805 Cr via block deal
description: Tencent, Chinese tech giant has offloaded a 1.05% stake in PB Fintech, the parent company of PolicyBazaar for Rs 805.45 crore or approximately $85 million through block deal on the NSE.
body: Tencent, Chinese tech giant has offloaded a 1.05% stake in PB Fintech, the parent company of PolicyBazaar for Rs 805.45 crore or approximately $85 million through block deal on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

According to exchange data, Tencent through its Tencent Cloud Europe BV has sold 48.4 lakh shares at Rs 1,664 per share. Earlier this year in March, Tencent, through the same entity, had also sold a 1.06% stake for Rs 695 crore.

Several institutional investors participated in the block deal. Morgan Stanley was the largest buyer, which acquired 21.4 lakh shares worth Rs 356.2 crore while Societe Generale bought 10.76 lakh shares valued at 179 crore. Ghisallo Master Fund LP also bought 7,93,00 shares around Rs 132 crore.
Domestic institutional investors also participated in the block deal, with HDFC Mutual Fund and Tata AIA Life Insurance acquiring shares worth Rs 83.2 crore and Rs 55 crore, respectively.

As of March 31, 2026, Tencent held around 7.52% stake in PB Fintech through two entities — Tencent Cloud Europe B.V. and Macritchie Investments Pte Ltd. Following the transaction, it has fully exited through the Tencent Cloud Europe B.V. entity.
On the financial front, PB Fintech reported a 37% year-on-year rise in operating revenue to Rs 2,061 crore , while its profit increased 54% to Rs 261 crore during the quarter.
At the end of Friday’s trading session, shares of PB Fintech closed at Rs 1,647.9, taking its total market capitalization to Rs 76,247 crore (about $8 billion).

title: Swiggy posts Rs 6,383 Cr revenue and Rs 800 Cr loss in Q4 FY26
description: Swiggy reported a 44.7% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue, which rose to Rs 6,383 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 4,410 crore in Q4 FY25.
body: Foodtech and quick commerce major Swiggy reported a 44.7% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue, which rose to Rs 6,383 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 4,410 crore in Q4 FY25. At the same time, the company managed to reduce its losses by 26% during the period.
For the complete fiscal year (FY26), Swiggy’s revenue from operations grew 51% year-on-year to Rs 23,052 crore. However, the company’s losses widened by 33% to Rs 4,154 crore during the same period.

Scootsy Logistics remained the largest contributor to Swiggy’s operating revenue, accounting for nearly 49% of the total. Revenue from the segment grew to Rs 3,135 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 2,004 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Swiggy’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses were the other major growth drivers. Revenue from food delivery increased 27.4% to Rs 2,075 crore, while quick commerce revenue jumped 53% to Rs 1,057 crore during the quarter.
The remaining operating revenue came from segments such as dine-out services and other initiatives, including Bolt and Toing.
The company also recorded Rs 266 crore as other income, taking its overall revenue to Rs 6,649 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 4,531 crore in the year-ago quarter.

On the expense front, procurement of FMCG products for supply chain distribution remained the largest cost center. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 667 crore, while advertising, sales promotion, delivery, and other operational expenses pushed the company’s total expenditure to Rs 7,448 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 5,610 crore in Q4 FY25.
As revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses, Swiggy’s losses narrowed 26% to Rs 800 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 1,081 crore in Q4 FY25.

title: Urban Company’s losses balloon to Rs 100 Cr in Q4 FY26 amid InstaHelp push
description: Home services marketplace Urban Company posted its Q4 FY26 results today with a strong 43% year-on-year growth in topline, but at the same time, its losses ballooned to Rs 99.86 crore.
body: Home services marketplace Urban Company posted its Q4 FY26 results today with a strong 43% year-on-year growth in topline, but at the same time, its losses ballooned to Rs 99.86 crore.

According to the company’s quarterly financial results, Urban Company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 425.56 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 298.45 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The company’s India Consumer Services business (excluding InstaHelp) remained the largest contributor and accounted for 68% of the operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew over 26% to Rs 288.47 crore during the quarter.

Urban Company’s Native brands business recorded over 75% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 70.22 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 40 crore in Q4 FY25. The international business also posted a strong growth of 89% which contributed Rs 57.93 crore.
The company’s newly launched quick-service housekeeping vertical, InstaHelp, posted revenue of Rs 8.94 crore during the quarter, but at the same time incurred a segmental loss of Rs 118.73 crore.

In the previous quarter (Q3 FY26), InstaHelp clocked 1.61 million orders and reported revenue of Rs 6.8 crore . In March this year, the platform crossed 1 million bookings after recording 50,000 daily bookings in February.

The company also earned Rs 36.74 crore from non-operating sources during the quarter, taking its overall income to Rs 462.3 crore. For the full year ended March 2026, the company recorded a 36% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 1,555.54 crore. However, it slipped into the red with a loss of Rs 234.8 crore.

On the cost front, its employee benefits expenses surged 40% to Rs 129.31 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 92.27 crore in Q4 FY25, while its cost of materials rose 37% year-on-year to Rs 88.83 crore. Finance cost, depreciation & amortization expenses and other undisclosed expenses took the overall expenditure of the firm to Rs 556.85 crore in the quarter from Rs 320.35 crore in Q4 FY25, reflecting a 74% year-on-year increase.

title: Kissht makes stock market debut at 12% premium over IPO price
description: Digital lending platform Kissht  made a strong debut on the Indian stock exchanges, with its shares listing at Rs 191 apiece on the BSE, nearly 12% higher than the issue price of Rs 171.
body: Digital lending platform Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, made a strong debut on the Indian stock exchanges, with its shares listing at Rs 191 apiece on the BSE, nearly 12% higher than the issue price of Rs 171.

The shares debuted at Rs 190 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). Following the listing, the stock gained over 10% to trade around Rs 210 as of 11:20 AM today. At the current price, the company commands a market capitalization of approximately Rs 3,532 crore ($372 million).

The company received strong interest from the investors during the subscription period, which was subscribed over 9 times. According to exchange data , the QIB segment subscribed 24.9X, followed by Non-Institutional Investors (NIIs) at 6.5X, while the retail investor quota saw relatively muted interest at 1.83X.
Kissht’s initial public offering (IPO) was open for subscription from April 30 to May 5, with a price band of Rs 162–171 and a minimum investment of Rs 14,094 for a lot size of 87 shares.

According to its RHP , Kissht raised around Rs 926 crore through its initial public offering (IPO), which included a fresh issue of equity shares worth Rs 850 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.4 million shares aggregating to Rs 76 crore.

The OFS participants included early investors in Kissht who offloaded their partial stake such as Vertex Venture, Ammar Sdn Bhd, Ventureast Proactive Fund, Endiya Seed Co-creation Fund, and AION Advisory.

Ahead of the IPO launch, Kissht secured Rs 278 crore (around $30 million) from 22 anchor investors. The anchor round saw participation from a mix of prominent domestic mutual funds and global institutional investors, including HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, WhiteOak Capital, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, and BNP Paribas.

For the nine-month period ended December 2025, Kissht reported an operating revenue of Rs 1,560 crore and a net profit of Rs 199 crore. In FY25, the company recorded Rs 1,337 crore in operating revenue and a net profit of Rs 160 crore.

title: Ola Consumer begins IPO process despite revenue decline and surge in losses
description: Ola Consumer (formerly Ola Cabs) has formally initiated preparations for an IPO, according to the company’s FY25 consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
body: Ride hailing major Ola Consumer (formerly Ola Cabs) has formally initiated preparations for an initial public offering (IPO), according to the company’s FY25 consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.

ANI Technologies Private Limited, the parent entity of Ola Cabs, said its board has approved the IPO proposal and commenced necessary steps toward the proposed listing. The company also began incurring IPO related expenses during the fiscal year and spent Rs 4.2 crore on audit services and certifications linked to the public issue.
The development comes at a time when the SoftBank-backed company faces slowing business performance, regulatory scrutiny, and restructuring challenges.

In its filings, Ola said management believes the IPO process, along with ongoing cost optimization efforts and available financial resources, will help the company continue as a going concern and meet its financial obligations.

However, the company also disclosed several operational concerns. Ola continues to operate as a cab aggregator in some states where its aggregator licenses have expired. While renewal applications have been submitted, approvals from state authorities are still pending.

Its financial services subsidiary, Ola Financial Services Private Limited, also faced regulatory attention during FY25. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) inspected the subsidiary’s prepaid payment instruments (PPI) license and later issued observations, to which the company submitted preliminary responses.

The filing further sheds light on multiple business shutdowns and impairment charges. Ola had earlier discontinued its used cars, cloud kitchen, and grocery businesses, which resulted in a goodwill impairment of Rs 146.8 crore.

Another subsidiary, Goddard Technical Solution Private Limited, acquired to strengthen the financial services vertical, underperformed against expectations. The company said it currently lacks a viable business plan for the business, which led to an impairment charge of Rs 318.7 crore in FY24. Ola also suspended operations at certain loss making subsidiaries to reduce cash burn.

title: Figtree Pharmacy raises seed funding from AJVC Fund
description: Mumbai-based pharmacy startup Figtree Pharmacy has raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round from AJVC Fund and other investors. Snippets
body: Mumbai-based pharmacy startup Figtree Pharmacy has raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round from AJVC Fund and other investors.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen logistics, build its technology stack, launch private-label medicines, and expand store operations.
Figtree plans to scale its network to 25 stores.
Founded in 2025 by former Nomura healthcare analyst Adrit Chaturvedi and Flipspaces’ Yatin Sharma, Figtree operates neighbourhood-focused pharmacies across Mumbai and Delhi.
The startup is building small-format pharmacy stores focused on hyperlocal demand instead of large-format retail models with extensive product catalogues.
Figtree currently operates four stores across Bandra, Altamount Road, and Babulnath in Mumbai, along with ASIAD Village in Delhi. A fifth store in Greater Kailash II is set to open shortly.
The firm claims that more than 90% of its business comes from repeat customers, with average order values exceeding Rs 1,000.

AJVC, an early-stage investment firm led by Aviral Bhatnagar, continues to expand its footprint across emerging startups in India. Its portfolio spans companies such as Bubble Me, Finanjo, Mindcase, Care Dale, HandyPanda, Multibagg AI, Nuyug, Mithila Foods, Jaagruk Bharat, TruFides AI, Chop Finance, Gaadi Mech, and Iztri.

title: PB Fintech enters debt broking space with SEBI approval
description: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, has received approval from the SEBI to operate as a stock broker in the debt segment of the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
body: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its wholly-owned subsidiary PB Marketing and Consulting Pvt Ltd to operate as a stock broker in the debt segment of the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The company disclosed the development on a stock exchange filing today.

Unlike a full-fledged stockbroking license that permits equity trading, derivatives, commodities, and other market activities, the approval received by PB Fintech is limited to the debt segment. This means the company can facilitate transactions in instruments such as corporate bonds, government securities, treasury bills, and other fixed-income products, but cannot offer equity or F&O trading without obtaining separate approvals.

The move marks PB Fintech’s continued expansion in financial services beyond insurance aggregation. Over the past few years, the company has been steadily building its presence across lending, payments, and wealth-related offerings.
In the latest development around the company, Chinese internet giant Tencent recently offloaded a 1.05% stake in PB Fintech through a block deal worth Rs 805 crore.

On the financial front, PB Fintech reported a 37% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 2,061 crore during the quarter, while its profit rose 54% to Rs 261 crore. At the end of Friday’s trading session, shares of PB Fintech closed at Rs 1,647.9, taking the company’s total market capitalization to Rs 76,247 crore (around $8 billion).

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startup this week [May 04 - May 09]
description: This week, 24 Indian startups raised around $158.8 million, comprising 3 growth-stage, 18 early-stage deals and 3 startups kept their funding undisclosed. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 24 Indian startups raised around $158.8 million, comprising 3 growth-stage, 18 early-stage deals and 3 startups kept their funding undisclosed.
In contrast, 18 startups had collectively secured about $187.21 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised a total of $120 million across three deals this week, led by spacetech startup Skyroot Aerospace, which secured $60 million in a round co-led by Sherpalo Ventures and GIC, entering the unicorn club in the process.

It was followed by instant household services startup Pronto, which extended its Series B round to $45 million with a fresh $20 million investment from Lachy Groom. Meanwhile, climate-focused NBFC Ecofy secured $15 million in debt funding from Mirova.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $38.3 million across 18 deals this week, led by Fabless semiconductor startup BigEndian Semiconductors has raised $6 million in a pre Series A funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund followed by Skincare brand CHOSEN has raised $5 Mn in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures.

AI computing solutions provider Tsavorite has raised $5 million (Rs 46.65 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Pavestone. Meanwhile, bank locker infrastructure startup Aurm secured Rs 42 crore in a seed funding round co-led by Earth Fund and Sattva Ventures, with participation from several angel investors.

title: Google-backed Adda247 lays off over 200 employees
description: Google-backed edtech startup Adda247 has reportedly laid off over 200 employees, or nearly 20% of its workforce. The layoff is a part. News
body: Google-backed edtech startup Adda247 has reportedly laid off over 200 employees, or nearly 20% of its workforce.
The layoff is a part of a restructuring exercise ahead of its planned IPO, according to a Business Standard report.

The layoffs reportedly impacted teams across product, design, content, CUET, UPSC, judiciary preparation, and teaching functions. The exercise was carried out at the company’s Gurugram office on April 30.

In an email statement, Adda247 said that it periodically reviews its organisational structure to improve execution and better serve learners. As part of this exercise, the company made certain structural adjustments across functions while continuing to hire selectively for key roles. It added that its overall headcount has remained broadly stable and affected employees are being supported in line with company policies.
Founded by Anil Nagar and Saurabh Bansal, Adda247 offers online test preparation courses for government exams, UPSC, banking, SSC, railways, and other competitive exams.
To date, the startup has raised around $67 million from investors including Google, WestBridge Capital, Info Edge, and Asha Impact.

The restructuring comes as Adda247 prepares for a public listing within the next 12–18 months. Founder and CEO Anil Nagar recently said the company reported around Rs 240 crore in revenue in FY25, while losses stood at nearly Rs 70 crore.

According to the report, the layoffs could help the company save nearly Rs 5 crore annually in salary expenses. Employees also cited slowing growth in some segments, weaker traction in StudyIQ’s online business, and concerns around cash runway.

title: Rebalance leads pre seed round in travel gear brand NORI
description: NORI, a travel gear brand designed specifically for women, has raised $350K in a pre seed funding round led by Rebalance, with participation from Vijay Shekhar Sharma, VSS Investco, and other angel investors.
body: Bengaluru based NORI, a travel gear brand designed specifically for women, has raised $350K in a pre seed funding round led by Rebalance, with participation from Vijay Shekhar Sharma, VSS Investco, and other angel investors.
The fresh funds will be used to expand its product portfolio and strengthen its presence across digital and offline channels, NORI said in a press release.
Co founded in 2025 by Meenakshi Vyas and Rashika Nayak, NORI designs luggage, bags, packing cubes, and travel organisers tailored to the way women actually travel.

As India’s travel market scales rapidly, women, especially solo and business travellers, are emerging as one of the fastest growing consumer segments. Yet travel gear continues to be largely designed around generic use cases, often overlooking how women actually pack and travel.

NORI’s newest launch, the Carry On Wheelie, is built around how women actually pack and travel, with better organisation, ergonomics, and a design language that does not shy away from being feminine. The brand’s Organisers range, which anchored its early traction, follows the same product philosophy.

Within months of launch, NORI has served more than 4,000 customers and is tracking toward an annual run rate of Rs 2 crore. Internal data points to an NPS above 9 and a 20% repeat purchase rate within a 60 day window, early indicators that are rare for Indian D2C brands at this stage and suggest a clear market gap.

title: Exclusive: Centricity in talks to raise $30 Mn round led by MUFG and SIG
description: Gurugram-based wealthtech startup Centricity is in talks to raise around $30 million in a fresh funding round, according to sources aware of the matter.
body: Wealthtech startup Centricity is in talks to raise around $30 million in a fresh funding round, according to sources aware of the matter. The proposed financing comes less than two years after the Gurugram-based company’s previous fundraise.

“Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) and Susquehanna International Group (SIG) are among the lead investors in discussions for the proposed financing,” said one source requesting anonymity as the talks are private. “The round is likely to value the company at around $250 million.”

If completed at the proposed valuation, the round would double the company’s valuation from its previous financing. In September 2024, Centricity had raised $20 million in a seed funding round led by Lightspeed at a valuation of $125 million.
The seed round also saw participation from Paramark VC, Burman Family Office, Shantanu Agarwal, and angel investors including Ritesh Agarwal, Vishal Dhupar, and the MS Dhoni Family Office.

Founded in 2022 by Manu Awasthy, Centricity offers plug-and-play solutions for transitions from employee to entrepreneur (E2E). The company operates through its platforms Invictus and One Digital, enabling financial advisors to access and transact in financial products while simplifying portfolio management for users.

According to sources, the fresh capital is expected to be deployed towards technology development, expansion of private banking services, and strengthening the company’s distribution and advisory ecosystem.
Centricity declined to comment on the story, while queries sent to MUFG and SIG did not elicit a response till the time of publication.

Centricity reported strong growth in FY25, with its operating revenue rising more than threefold to Rs 61.26 crore from Rs 19.02 crore in FY24. However, the company’s losses also increased to Rs 31.72 crore in FY25 from Rs 9.31 crore in the previous fiscal year.

title: Construction robotics startup Flo Mobility raises $2.5 Mn in pre-Series A round
description: Bengaluru-based construction robotics startup Flo Mobility has raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Mela Ventures and Arali Ventures. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based construction robotics startup Flo Mobility has raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Mela Ventures and Arali Ventures.
The proceeds will be used to scale manufacturing, strengthen its AI and autonomy stack, expand deployments across India, and enter international markets, particularly the Middle East.

Founded in 2021 by Manesh Jain and Pratik Patel, Flo Mobility builds Physical AI and robotics solutions for the construction sector. The startup develops autonomous robots designed for material movement and other construction workflows across large project sites.

The company’s flagship product, Flo Hauler, is a battery-powered autonomous mobile robot capable of transporting loads up to 1.5 tonnes across construction sites, including multi-floor operations. The robot is designed to operate in unstructured environments with changing layouts and harsh weather conditions.

Flo Mobility claims to have deployed more than 60 robots across 10 Indian states with developers including L&T, Godrej Properties, Embassy Group, Sobha, and Capacite Infra. According to the company, clients have reported nearly 45% cost savings, 50% faster material movement, and a 67% reduction in accidents.

title: Sindhuja Microcredit raises $5 Mn in pre-Series D round
