description: Noida-based NBFC-MFI Sindhuja Microcredit has raised $5 million (around Rs 47 crore) in a pre-Series D funding round from existing investors Abler Nordic. Snippets
body: Noida-based NBFC-MFI Sindhuja Microcredit has raised $5 million (around Rs 47 crore) in a pre-Series D funding round from existing investors Abler Nordic, GAWA Capital through Huruma Fund, and Oikocredit.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen its capital base, expand lending operations, and improve access to credit for underserved communities, including women entrepreneurs and MSMEs.

Founded by Abhisheka Kumar and Malkit Singh Didyala, Sindhuja Microcredit provides financial services to self-employed women entrepreneurs, traders, shopkeepers, and farmers in rural and semi-urban markets.
The firm claims to have served more than 5 lakh borrowers across 12 states over the last eight years. It currently operates 366 branches and manages assets worth over Rs 1,100 crore.
Sindhuja primarily focuses on borrowers in rural and remote regions through joint liability group (JLG) loans and individual lending products.

Sindhuja had previously raised Series A funding from Carpediem Capital. It later secured Series B funding during the Covid-19 period and a pre-Series C round in 2023 led by Abler Nordic with participation from Carpediem Capital. Its Series C round in 2024 was led by Huruma Fund managed by GAWA Capital along with participation from Oikocredit.

title: Kathy’s Beverages raises Rs 6 Cr in pre-Series A round
description: Mumbai-based beverage startup Kathy’s Beverages, which operates bubble tea and beverage brand Bobakat, has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-Series A funding round Snippets
body: Mumbai-based beverage startup Kathy’s Beverages, which operates bubble tea and beverage brand Bobakat, has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-Series A funding round.
The proceeds will be used for product innovation, team expansion, marketing, and offline expansion across India. Bobakat currently operates compact-format outlets across food courts and high streets.

Founded in 2024 by Dr Rupali Ambegaonkar and Sannjeev Rao, Bobakat offers bubble tea and other beverages targeted at urban consumers. The brand claims to have served more than 10 lakh consumers so far and is targeting Rs 100 crore in net sales value over the next 36 months.
According to the company, India’s beverage market is expected to grow from $80 billion in 2025 to around $155 billion by 2035.

Dr Rupali Ambegaonkar previously founded Tea Culture of the World (TCW), a tea retail chain with over 200 stores across India. Rao has held leadership roles at companies including Future Group, Aditya Birla Retail, Landmark Dubai, Raymond, and Being Human.
Bobakat focuses on quality-led products, curated in-store experiences, audience-focused branding, and scalable store formats.
The startup plans to open 35 stores during FY27, followed by 50 stores each over the next two financial years. The expansion will cover metro cities as well as emerging urban markets.

title: Stock trading app Sahi founders dilute over 60% stake after Series B round
description: Sahi has raised over $43 million within a year, including a $33 million Series B round led by Accel and Elevation Capital. The funding boosted its valuation by 3.5X, while the founders’ combined stake dropped below 40%.
body: Looking to scale up and take on established players such as Zerodha, Groww, and Dhan, stock trading platform Sahi has raised over $43 million within a year, including its most recent $33 million Series B round from its existing investors Accel India and Elevation Capital.
The fundraise, however, came with a trade-off: even as the firm’s valuation surged over 3.5X, the founders’ combined stake fell below 40%.
To better understand the Bengaluru-based firm’s latest Series B round, Entrackr reviewed its regulatory filings, analysing details such as the round’s structure, shareholding, and valuation.
Sahi operates under Aartiya Technologies Private Limited, its board has allotted 42,860 Series B preference shares at an issue price of Rs 69,911 each to raise around Rs 300 crore or $33 million.

Accel India led the Series B round with an investment of Rs 240.6 crore ($26.5 million), increasing its stake in the company, while existing backer Elevation Capital infused Rs 59 crore ($6.5 million). Prior to the round, both venture capital firms held an equal 20% stake in the company.
As per the company’s disclosures, its valuation surged over 3.5X to Rs 1,816 crore (around $200 million) on a post-money basis, compared to Rs 514 crore in its previous Series A round.

Following the latest allotment, Accel India emerged as the largest shareholder with a 29.58% stake, while Elevation Capital held 19.58%. Meanwhile, co-founders Dale Vaz and Manish Jain collectively retain a 38.5% stake. The company has an ESOP pool of 12.02% of the capital, valued at Rs 218 crore (around $24 million).

Founded in 2023 by Vaz and Jain, Sahi is a trading platform for stocks and options, designed for fast and easy F&O trading. It offers a chart-based interface with real-time data, open interest, technical indicators, and one-click order execution.

title: Wingreens acquires Safe Harvest; raises Rs 120 Cr in Series D round
description: Packaged food and beverage company Wingreens has acquired pesticide-free food brand Safe Harvest through a share swap deal and also closed its Rs 120 crore Series D round
body: Packaged food and beverage company Wingreens has acquired pesticide-free food brand Safe Harvest through a share swap deal and also closed its Rs 120 crore ($12.6 million) Series D round led by Ashish Kacholia with participation from Alchemy Fund. With this round, Wingreens’ total capital raised so far has reached Rs 556 crore.
The company’s last major fundraise came in November 2021 when it secured Rs 124 crore (around $17 million) in an equity round led by Investcorp .
The acquisition comes as Wingreens looks to expand its presence across the farm-to-consumer segment through three brands: Wingreens Farms, Raw Pressery and Safe Harvest.

Safe Harvest works with more than 100,000 farmers, most of them women, through Self Help Groups (SHGs) and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). The company focuses on sustainable rural livelihoods and pesticide-free food products for Indian consumers.

Its portfolio includes cereals, grains, pulses, millets, flours, whole spices, cold-pressed oils, natural sugars and honey. The company also claims 100% batch-wise pesticide testing and certification across products.
The fresh capital will support expansion of the product portfolio, wider distribution, supply chain integration and investments in innovation and farmer partnerships.
Together, Wingreens Farms, Raw Pressery and Safe Harvest aim to build a large food and beverage platform focused on health, transparency, sustainability and inclusive growth.

Wingreens owns brands such as Wingreens Farms, Raw Pressery, Wingreens Harvest, Saucery and now Safe Harvest. Its portfolio spans dips, spreads, sauces, mayonnaise, baked chips, muesli, granola bars, oats, juices, protein shakes, almond milk, iced teas and lemonades.

title: Nazara records 13X surge in Q4 profit despite revenue decline
description: The sharp reduction in overall costs, including content, advertising, employee benefits, and platform fees, led Nazara’s profit to jump more than 13X in Q4 FY26
body: Nazara Technologies, a gaming and sports media firm, witnessed a 23.5% year-on-year decline in its revenue during the last quarter of the previous fiscal year (Q4 FY26). In contrast, the company’s profit surged more than 13X during the same period.
Nazara’s operating revenue declined to Rs 398 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 520 crore in Q4 FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The gaming segment continued to remain the company’s primary revenue driver, accounting for 70% of the total operating revenue. Revenue from the segment increased 78% year-on-year to Rs 278 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 156 crore in Q4 FY25.

Revenue from its other business segments, including esports and ad-tech, declined by 85% and 40% to Rs 32 crore and Rs 89 crore, respectively, in Q4 FY26. The decline was mainly due to the deconsolidation of NODWIN Gaming, lower sponsorship spending in esports, and weaker digital advertising demand from gaming and startup companies.
Including other income, the company’s total income stood at Rs 448 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 538 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.
For the full fiscal year, Nazara’s revenue from operations grew 12.6% to Rs 1,829 crore in FY26, while the company’s profit increased 60.8% to Rs 82 crore during the same period.

On the expense front, the company’s total expenditure declined by 29% to Rs 375 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 528 crore in Q4 FY25. Marketing remained the largest cost center at Rs 111 crore, followed by employee benefits and content-related expenses.

The sharp reduction in overall costs, including content, advertising, employee benefits, and platform fees, led Nazara’s profit to jump more than 13X year-on-year to Rs 55.7 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 4.07 crore in Q4 FY25.

title: InCred Capital acquires fund management firm S Cube Capital
description: The acquisition strengthens InCred Capital’s offshore product suite by adding regulated fund vehicles to its Singapore platform. It also builds on the firm’s recent acq
body: InCred Capital, the institutional, wealth and asset management arm of the InCred Group, has announced the integration of S Cube Capital into InCred Global Wealth Pte in Singapore, subject to regulatory approvals.

The acquisition strengthens InCred Capital’s offshore product suite by adding regulated fund vehicles to its Singapore platform. It also builds on the firm’s recent acquisition of Arrow Capital DIFC, enhancing its ability to serve clients investing across the Singapore-GCC-India corridor.
Singapore-based S Cube Capital is regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and provides institutional investment expertise focused on local markets and global networks.
As part of the transaction, Balaji Swaminathan and Hemant Mishr of S Cube Capital will join InCred Global Wealth as Joint Vice Chairmen of its global asset management business.

With operations across India, Singapore, Dubai and London, InCred Capital operates businesses spanning wealth management, asset management and institutional equities. The firm manages over Rs 1 lakh crore ($10.5 billion) in wealth AUM and around Rs 10,000 crore ($1 billion) in asset management AUM.

title: Semiconductor startup HrdWyr raises $13 Mn led by Ideaspring Capital
description: Semiconductor startup HrdWyr has raised $13 million in a Series A funding round led by Ideaspring Capital, with participation from Singularity AMC, Avatar Growth Capital. News
body: Semiconductor startup HrdWyr has raised $13 million in a Series A funding round led by Ideaspring Capital, with participation from Singularity AMC, Avatar Growth Capital, and existing investor Persistent Systems.
The proceeds will be used to accelerate development of its AI-native System-on-Chip (AISoC) products and expand customer engagements across global markets.
Founded by Ramamurthy Sivakumar, HrdWyr builds AI-native semiconductor chips designed for edge computing and physical AI applications.

HrdWyr develops purpose-built chips for sectors including consumer electronics, EVs, industrial systems, and data centres. Its chips are designed to deliver low-latency processing and improved power efficiency for AI workloads at the edge.

The startup operates as a fabless semiconductor company and focuses on integrating AI capabilities directly into chip architecture to enable real-time processing and autonomous decision-making on devices.
The company recently partnered with audio and wearable brand boAt as part of its customer expansion efforts.

title: Enterprise intelligence startup SCIKIQ secures $1.5 Mn in pre-Series A
description: SCIKIQ serves sectors including BFSI, retail, e-commerce, manufacturing, and healthcare, with enterprise clients and associations such as London Stock Exchange,
body: Enterprise intelligence platform SCIKIQ has raised $1.5 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Triton Fund II.
The proceeds will be used to support global expansion, strengthen AI capabilities, and scale the platform, SCIKIQ said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by Gaurav Shinh and Rohit Kumar, SCIKIQ is an AI-native enterprise intelligence platform that helps enterprises convert fragmented data into business-ready intelligence. Its platform integrates data governance, analytics, conversational AI, AutoML, and GenAI tools within a unified Data Hub.
The Gurugram-based company focuses on helping enterprises unify siloed data, accelerate AI adoption, simplify data operations, and improve decision-making across complex environments.
SCIKIQ serves sectors including BFSI, retail, e-commerce, manufacturing, and healthcare.
It competes with the other players in this space such as Atlan Delboomi, Microsoft Data Fabric, Databricks, and Incorta.

title: Mobikwik reports Rs 289 Cr revenue and Rs 4.4 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: MobiKwik reported an 8% YoY increase in operating revenue and swung to a profit of Rs 4.4 crore in the quarter against a net loss of Rs 56 crore in the same quarter last year.
body: Fintech platform MobiKwik reported its Q4 FY26 results on Tuesday. The company posted an 8% year-on-year increase in operating revenue and swung to a profit of Rs 4.4 crore in the quarter against a net loss of Rs 56 crore in the same quarter last year.
MobiKwik’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 289 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 268 crore in Q4 FY25, its unaudited financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show.

For MobiKwik, commissions from recharges and loan servicing, along with income from payment gateway and technology platform services, were the key revenue contributors in Q4 FY26. The company, however, did not disclose a segment-wise revenue breakup in its quarterly filing.
For the full fiscal year ended March 2026, MobiKwik reported flat revenue at Rs 1,119 crore, while its losses halved to Rs 62 crore from Rs 122 crore in FY25.

For the Gurugram-based firm, payment gateway charges remained the largest expense in Q4 FY26, accounting for over 41% of total costs which stood at Rs 119 crore. Its Employee benefit expenses were recorded at Rs 46 crore, while lending operational costs dropped sharply by 95% to Rs 2 crore from Rs 41 crore in the year-ago quarter.

For MobiKwik, financial guarantee costs stood at Rs 30 crore in Q4 FY26, while legal, advertising and marketing, finance, and other overheads pushed total expenses to Rs 288 crore. The overall cost base declined 14% from Rs 335 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The firm reported a profit of Rs 4.4 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to a loss of Rs 56 crore in the same quarter last year, aided by controlled expenses, particularly lower lending operational costs. On a sequential basis, its profit increased 10%.
Recently, Mobikwik’s early backer Peak XV Partners fully exited the firm in a block deal worth Rs 130 crore, offloading its 7.7% stake in the firm.

title: Appliance manufacturing startup Mekr raises Rs 67 Cr led by Avaana Capital
description: Consumer electronics design and manufacturing startup Mekr has raised Rs 67 crore ($7 million) in a Series A funding round led by Avaana Capital. Snippets
body: Consumer electronics design and manufacturing startup Mekr has raised Rs 67 crore ($7 million) in a Series A funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from Titan Capital Winners Fund.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen R&D, expand manufacturing automation, localise supplier networks, improve quality systems, and scale exports.
Founded in 2022 by Anand Yadav and Gaurang Kuchhal, Mekr operates as a full-stack design and manufacturing platform for consumer appliances.
The startup provides end-to-end services across product design, prototyping, tooling, certification, and mass manufacturing for appliance brands.

Mekr currently works across categories such as home and kitchen appliances, personal care, and car accessories. The firm claims to have developed more than 100 SKUs and partnered with over 40 brands including Croma, Wipro, Amazon Basics, and Flipkart.
Mekr builds products using modular engineering systems including BLDC motor systems, heating systems, load cells, and in-house mould design capabilities.

title: Fractal posts Rs 886 Cr revenue in Q4 FY26; profits jump 2X
description: Fractal has announced its first quarterly financial results after going public. The company reported a 17% YoY increase in revenue for the quarter ending March 2026
body: AI and advanced analytics firm Fractal has announced its first quarterly financial results after going public. The company reported a 17% year-on-year increase in revenue for the quarter ending March 2026, while its profit more than doubled during the same period.
Fractal’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 886.3 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 757.5 crore in Q4 FY25, according to disclosures sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
For the full fiscal year, the company’s revenue rose to Rs 3,363 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,816 crore in FY25.

On the expense side, employee benefits remained the largest cost component, accounting for nearly 75% of the total expenses, which rose 8.6% to Rs 570 crore in Q4 FY26. Depreciation, finance costs, and other overheads pushed the company’s total expenditure up by 12% to Rs 755.6 crore during the quarter, compared to Rs 674.6 crore in Q4 FY25.

As revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses, Fractal’s profit surged 109% to Rs 116 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 55.5 crore in Q4 FY25. For the full year, the company’s profit grew 30% to Rs 286.8 crore in FY26.
Founded in 2000, Fractal generates revenue through analytics and consulting services, along with licensing and subscription income from its AI platforms, including Cogentiq, Iqigai, and Kalaido.ai.

Fractal made its stock market debut earlier this year, listing at a discount of nearly 3% to its issue price on the NSE. The company had raised Rs 2,834 crore through its IPO, which comprised a mix of fresh issue and offer-for-sale components backed by investors including Apax Partners and TPG Capital.
Fractal’s shares were trading at Rs 1,064.65, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 18,443 crore.

title: Zoho invests Rs 70 Cr in ONDC to support MSMEs
description: Zoho Corporation has invested Rs 70 crore in ONDC to support the development of sovereign digital infrastructure in India and strengthen technology access for MSMEs.
body: Zoho Corporation has invested Rs 70 crore in Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) to support the development of sovereign digital infrastructure in India and strengthen technology access for MSMEs.
The Chennai-based SaaS firm said the investment is aimed at making digital commerce more inclusive and interoperable for small businesses.

“India’s economy depends heavily on MSMEs, yet they face challenges on all fronts, from limited market access to structural constraints imposed by conventional digital platforms,” said Sivaramakrishnan Iswaran, CEO of Zoho Payment Technologies and Global Head of Finance and Operations BU at Zoho.

ONDC, backed by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), is building an interoperable ecommerce network designed to reduce entry barriers for businesses. The network processed 218 million transactions in FY26.
Zoho said products such as Vikra, Zoho Books, Zoho Inventory and Zoho Commerce are already helping MSMEs digitise operations and connect with the ONDC network.
ONDC added that its DigiDukaan initiative has onboarded over 10,000 kirana stores within months of launch, while order volumes for farmers, artisans and rural sellers grew 11X in FY26.
Last month, ONDC appointed Vibhor Jain as its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer. Jain previously served as the Chief Operating Officer and was acting CEO during the leadership transition.

title: Secured lending startup Nivasa Finance raises $3 Mn from Prime Venture, Blume, others
description: Nivasa Finance has raised $3 million (around Rs 25 crore) in a seed funding round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from Blume Ventures, Whiteboard Capital and a group of angel investors.
body: Secured credit startup Nivasa Finance has raised $3 million (around Rs 25 crore) in a seed funding round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from Blume Ventures, Whiteboard Capital and a group of angel investors.

The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand geographically, strengthen its distribution network and deepen partnerships with lenders. It is also exploring the possibility of securing an NBFC licence.
Founded in 2025 by Samit Shetty and Hitesh Saraf, Nivasa Finance is building a distribution and fulfilment platform for affordable housing loans and loans against property (LAP) in non-metro markets.

The Bengaluru-based startup helps underserved borrowers, including self-employed individuals, gig workers and small business owners, access secured credit through a hybrid model combining technology-led workflows with on-ground field operations. It supports customers across the loan lifecycle, including assessment, documentation, lender matching and disbursal.

Nivasa currently works with over 10 lending partners, including banks, small finance banks, housing finance companies and NBFCs. Since launch, the startup claims to have facilitated hundreds of loans worth more than Rs 20 crore across Mysore and Mandya in Karnataka.

title: Toy subscription startup The EleFant raises $1 Mn in pre-Series funding
description: Toy subscription startup The EleFant has raised $1 million in a pre-Series funding round led by Growth Sense Venture Fund, with participation from JIIF. Snippets
body: Toy subscription startup The EleFant has raised $1 million in a pre-Series funding round led by Growth Sense Venture Fund, with participation from JIIF, Arian Capital, Asit Oberoi, Vimal Saboo and other angel investors.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen its technology infrastructure and expand its presence across key markets.
Founded by Sourabh Jain and Srishti Jain, The EleFant operates a toy subscription and circular play platform for children aged 0–12 years.
The platform allows families to subscribe to toys and books from over 90 brands through monthly plans starting at Rs 599. Users can return toys after use and choose new ones through the platform.
The startup currently offers more than 1,000 toys and books and operates through a Franchise-Invested, Company-Operated (FICO) model. It has over 125 franchise partners across 18 cities.
The EleFant aims to cross 50,000 subscribers and expand to over 20 cities in the next 12 months.

title: Peak XV turns Rs 232 Cr investment in Groww into Rs 22,000 Cr value
description: Peak XV Partners has turned its Rs 232 crore investment in Groww into an estimated Rs 22,000 crore, including exits and remaining stake value.
body: Peak XV Partners has emerged as one of the biggest gainers from its investment in Groww, turning an investment of around Rs 232 crore into a holding worth around Rs 22,000 crore, including realised exits and remaining stake value.
According to Groww’s red herring prospectus (RHP), Peak XV had invested nearly Rs 232 crore in the company before its IPO and held 19.87% stake in the firm at the time of filing.

The investor had partially exited the company during Groww’s IPO through the offer-for-sale (OFS) route, where it sold shares worth around Rs 1,583 crore. Peak XV further pared its stake during Tuesday’s block deal transaction, where it sold 6.20 crore shares and gathered around Rs 1,116 crore

Despite the partial exits, the venture capital firm continues to hold shares worth nearly Rs 19,048 crore in Groww at the current market price (Rs 191.1), making it one of the most valuable startup investments for the firm in India.

As per the company’s offer documents, Peak XV acquired shares in Groww at a weighted average cost of Rs 1.91 per share . Compared to the latest transaction price of Rs 180 per share, the investor is estimated to have generated returns of nearly 95X on its investment.

The Groww investment has also emerged as one of the biggest wins for Peak XV in India. Earlier, Entrackr had reported that the venture capital firm held over Rs 30,000 crore worth of stakes across listed and IPO-bound startups, with Groww being among its most valuable portfolio companies.

Founded in 2016 by Lalit Keshre, Harsh Jain, Neeraj Singh and Ishan Bansal, Groww started as a mutual fund investment platform before expanding into stock broking, derivatives trading and wealth management products.
Over the years, the Bengaluru-based company has emerged as India’s largest stock broking platform by active users, competing with firms such as Zerodha, Angel One and Upstox.

title: Groww investors sell 4.7% stake worth Rs 5,352 Cr via bulk deals
description: According to NSE data, around 29.52 crore shares changed hands at an average price of Rs 180.4 per share. The total transaction value stood at over Rs 5,352 crore.
body: Early investors in the stock broking platform Groww sold around 4.7% stake in the company through bulk deals on Tuesday.
According to NSE data, around 29.52 crore shares changed hands at an average price of Rs 180.4 per share. The total transaction value stood at over Rs 5,352 crore.

The bulk deal involved investors including Peak XV Partners, YC Holdings, Ribbit Capital and other institutional investors. The transaction came after the expiry of the six-month lock-in period for pre-IPO shareholders.
Among the investors, Ribbit Capital emerged as one of the key sellers in the transaction. However, Peak XV continues to remain one of the largest shareholders in Groww even after the partial exit.
Founded in 2016 by Lalit Keshre, Harsh Jain, Neeraj Singh and Ishan Bansal, Groww started as a mutual fund investment platform and later expanded into stock broking and wealth management products.

According to its Q4 FY26 shareholder letter and financial results, the Bengaluru-based firm posted a total revenue of Rs 1,535.5 crore in the March quarter, up from Rs 849.5 crore in the same period last year. The company also reported a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 686 crore in Q4 FY26.

Groww has also strengthened its leadership position in India’s retail broking market over the past few years. According to NSE data , the company had around 1.3 crore active users in April 2026 with over 28.48% market share, making it the largest stock broking platform in the country by active clients.
The Bengaluru-based company competes with firms such as Zerodha, Angel One and Upstox.

title: Dhan parent Raise acquires GreenLife to enter insurance distribution biz
description: Raise Financial Services, the parent company of stock broking platform Dhan, has acquired GreenLife Insurance Broking Pvt Ltd (GIBL). News
body: Raise Financial Services, the parent company of stock broking platform Dhan, has acquired GreenLife Insurance Broking Pvt Ltd (GIBL), an IRDAI-registered insurance broker, in an all-cash-and-stock deal to enter the insurance distribution space, for an undisclosed amount.
The company plans to invest $15 million in GreenLife to build a consumer-focused insurance distribution platform with a focus on technology, product, and customer experience.

Founded in 2013 by Subir Mukherjee, GreenLife operates across 50+ cities and towns in East and North-East India through an offline distribution network. The company works with over 60 insurers across life, health, motor, and travel insurance segments.
Post-acquisition, GreenLife will operate as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Raise and plans to launch a new consumer platform for insurance buying and management by the end of 2026.
According to Raise, the move will help it expand its financial services ecosystem beyond investing and wealth products into financial protection.

Founded in 2021 by Pravin Jadhav, Alok Pandey, Jay Prakash Gupta, and Raunak Rathi, Raise operates platforms including Dhan, Upsurge, Fuzz AI, ScanX, and Stratzy. The company is backed by investors including Hornbill Capital, MUFG, BEENEXT, and 3one4 Capital.

The company recently acquired algorithmic trading and investing platform Stratzy in a cash-and-stock deal and took over new-age financial media startup Filter Coffee in January 2025. It is also set to take over wealthtech startup Infinyte Club .

In February this year, Dhan crossed the 1 million user mark and, as of April, the platform retained its ninth position with a 2.3% market share . On the financial front, the company has also shown strong growth, as its revenue from operations surged 2.3X to Rs 877 crore in FY25 , while profits stood at Rs 408 crore.

title: Doorstep smartphone repair startup Instafix raises pre-seed round led by Titan Capital, 8i Ventures
description: The Gurugram-based startup brings certified technicians to a customer’s location. Customers book a repair, and a technician arrives on-site and completes the repair in 30
body: Instafix, a 30-minute doorstep smartphone repair service, has raised Rs 7.55 crore in a pre-seed funding round co-led by Titan Capital and 8i Ventures, along with participation from Anish Srivastava and Bharat Kalia.

The proceeds will be used to scale its Gurugram operations, expand coverage beyond iPhones to premium Android models, and build the technology stack behind on-site, sub-30-minute repairs, Instafix said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2025 by Aniket Kale and Chetan Chauhan, Instafix offers a 30-minute doorstep smartphone repair service backed by a 12-month warranty. Its mission is to make quality repair the default choice for every Indian household, starting with smartphones and expanding across consumer electronics.
As per market research, India’s consumer electronics market is valued at nearly $73 billion and is growing at nearly 20% year-on-year.

The Gurugram-based startup brings certified technicians to a customer’s location. Customers book a repair, and a technician arrives on-site and completes the repair in 30 minutes, in front of the customer. Every repair is backed by a warranty of up to 12 months and priced up to 50% below OEM service centres. Together, this aims to deliver a 10x better repair experience.

Since its launch in Gurugram in Oct ’25, Instafix says it has grown 100% month-on-month. It plans to expand beyond smartphones and build a trusted on-demand repair platform across consumer electronics.
Titan Capital has invested in more than 300 startups, including Mamaearth, Ola, Razorpay, Urban Company, Shadowfax, OfBusiness, Credgenics, and Giva, among others.

title: ED freezes Rs 526 Cr assets in Gameskraft probe, alleges Rs 1,154 Cr user losses
description: ED has alleged that Bengaluru-based Gameskraft used bots and manipulated gaming structures to cause financial losses worth over Rs 1,154 crore to users.
body: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has alleged that Bengaluru-based real money gaming platform Gameskraft Technologies used bots and manipulated gaming structures to cause financial losses worth over Rs 1,154 crore to users, according to a press release issued on Wednesday.

The agency said it conducted search and seizure operations between May 7 and May 13 at the company’s offices and residences linked to its directors and key employees in Bengaluru and the NCR region. During the searches, the ED said it froze and seized movable assets worth around Rs 526.49 crore, including bank balances, mutual funds, bonds, and fixed deposits. It also seized jewellery worth Rs 3.5 crore and cash amounting to Rs 11 lakh.

The development comes days after the ED arrested Gameskraft co-founders Deepak Singh, Prithvi Raj Singh, and Vikas Taneja under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The probe stems from multiple FIRs filed across states alleging cheating and unlawful gains through the company’s online gaming platforms.

According to the ED, Gameskraft operated real money gaming applications under brands such as RummyCulture, RummyPrime, Playship, RummyTime, and RummyCorner. The agency alleged that the company continued offering services in states where online real money gaming is restricted or banned by tampering with users’ geo-locations.

The agency further claimed that users were initially allowed to win and withdraw small amounts to build trust, after which they were allegedly made to play against automated BOT accounts. “The genuine users were lost to BOT user IDs,” the ED said, alleging that the platform deployed bots strategically once users started playing with higher stakes.

The ED also alleged that the proceeds generated through these activities were routed into foreign entities, dividend payments, mutual funds, bonds, and movable and immovable properties. Further investigation is underway.

title: Shadowfax crosses Rs 1,200 Cr revenue and Rs 56 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: Shadowfax Technologies announced its Q4 FY26 results today, reporting another strong quarterly performance since filing for its listing on Indian stock exchanges.
body: Shadowfax Technologies announced its Q4 FY26 results today, reporting another strong quarterly performance since filing for its listing on Indian stock exchanges. The logistics and last-mile delivery firm recorded a 74% year-on-year growth in operating revenue while it posted Rs 56 crore profit during the quarter.
The company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 1,253 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 712 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from NSE.

Shadowfax operates in the last-mile and hyperlocal logistics space, serving ecommerce marketplaces, D2C brands and quick commerce players. It competes with players such as Delhivery, XpressBees, Ecom Express and Ekart, in a segment marked by intense competition. Other income contributed an additional Rs 16 crore, which took its total income in the quarter to Rs 1,253 crore. For the full year FY26, Shadowfax’s revenue from operations surged 69% to Rs 4,202 crore. At the same time, its profit jumped over 17 times to Rs 112 crore from Rs 6.4 crore in FY25. The company did not provide proper expense breakup, employee benefit expenses rose 46% to Rs 112 crore, while finance costs increased 32% to Rs 6.5 crore. Overall expenditure for the firm increased 64% year-on-year to Rs 1,198 crore.

In the end, Shadowfax Technologies turned profitable in Q4 FY26, posting a profit of Rs 56 crore against a loss of Rs 10 crore in the same quarter last year, as its revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses.
At the end of today’s trading session, Shadowfax’s share price closed at Rs 165, giving the firm a total market capitalization of Rs 9,822 crore ($1.15 billion).

title: Matrimony.com posts Rs 117 Cr revenue and Rs 10 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: Matrimony.com Ltd reported a steady 8% year-on-year growth in revenue in the last quarter of FY26, while its profit increased by over 18% to Rs 9.7 crore.
body: Matrimony.com Ltd, the parent company of Bharat Matrimony, has announced its financial results for the last quarter of FY26. During the period, the company reported a steady 8% year-on-year growth in revenue, while its profit increased by over 18% to Rs 9.7 crore.

The group’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 116.8 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 108.3 crore in Q4 FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Matrimony.com operates online matchmaking platforms led by Bharat Matrimony and multiple regional services such as Punjabi, Gujarati, Marathi and others.

The company primarily generated revenue from subscriptions to its matchmaking services, which contributed Rs 116 crore during the quarter. It also earned Rs 84 lakh from marriage and allied services, along with Rs 5 crore in finance income, taking its total quarterly income to Rs 121.9 crore.
For the full fiscal year ended March 2026, Matrimony.com reported flat revenue at Rs 460 crore, while its profit declined over 24% year-on-year to Rs 34 crore from Rs 45 crore in FY25.

On the expense front, advertisement and marketing remained the company’s largest cost centre, rising to Rs 44.7 crore in Q4 FY26. Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses increased marginally by 5% year-on-year to Rs 37.2 crore.

Finance costs, depreciation and amortisation expenses, along with other overheads, pushed the company’s total expenditure to Rs 110 crore in Q4 FY26, which remained largely flat compared to the same quarter last year.
Steady revenue growth and controlled spending helped Matrimony group increase its profit by over 18% to Rs 9.7 crore in Q4 FY26, compared to Rs 8.2 crore in the same quarter last year.

title: Flipkart leads GMV, MAUs as India e-comm market may hit $214 Bn by FY30: ICICI Securities
description: News: Among leading players, Walmart-owned Flipkart retained its position as the market leader with an estimated 50–60% gross merchandise value (GMV) market share.
body: India’s e-commerce market is expected to nearly triple to $174–214 billion by FY30 from around $70 billion in FY25, aided by higher internet penetration, a rise in online shoppers, demand from rural markets, and expansion of digital payment infrastructure, according to a report by ICICI Securities.

The report said that India’s digital commerce ecosystem has evolved rapidly over the past decade, shifting from traditional online retail to hyperlocal and quick commerce models. It added that the sector gained significant momentum after 2016 with the rise of smartphones, UPI-led payments infrastructure, and stronger logistics networks.
The brokerage also said the Covid-19 pandemic acted as a structural catalyst for online shopping, especially in groceries and essentials, which accelerated digital adoption across the country.
E-commerce penetration to rise to 13% by FY30
According to the report, India’s total retail market was valued at around $978 billion in FY25, of which e-commerce contributed nearly 7%, or approximately $70 billion.
By FY30, the country’s retail market is projected to expand to $1.4–1.6 trillion, with e-commerce expected to account for 13% of the overall market.
The report added that the share of unorganised retail is expected to decline from 79% in FY25 to 66% by FY30 as organised retail and online commerce continue to gain share.
Rural India and internet growth to support demand

title: Inflection Point Ventures records 16 exits in FY26 with 41% IRR
description: Startup investing platform Inflection Point Ventures has announced 16 exits in FY26 with an aggregate IRR of 41% and a 2.86x money multiple. Snippets
body: Startup investing platform Inflection Point Ventures has announced 16 exits in FY26 with an aggregate IRR of 41% and a 2.86x money multiple.
The exits included both partial and full exits across startups such as Secret Alchemist, Aerem, Qubehealth, Kazam, Stage, Hudle, AFK Gaming, and GeoiQ, according to a press release.
The fund claims that Secret Alchemist delivered the highest return with 192% IRR and 4.56x multiple. Other notable exits included Aerem with 60% IRR, Qubehealth with 49% IRR, and Kazam with 34% IRR.

AFK Gaming was acquired by Nodwin Gaming, while GeoiQ was acquired by Lenskart. IPV also saw strategic and secondary exits involving investors such as Blume Ventures, Unicorn India Ventures, Avishkaar Fund VI, and Amazon.
The angel investment platform said more than 50% of its startups with over two years of vintage have either achieved exits or raised follow-on rounds.
In FY26, 26 IPV portfolio startups raised follow-on funding rounds, delivering a blended IRR of 84.22% and a 3.33x money multiple through secondary transactions.

Inflection Point Ventures has invested over Rs 1,200 crore across more than 280 startups to date and made 18 investments in Q4 2025. Its recent investments include Cohoma Coffee , Pinq Polka , Reneonix and Roopya among others.

title: Evenflow Brands claims positive EBITDA in FY26
description: Evenflow Brands reported an improvement in profitability during FY26 and turned EBITDA positive for the full fiscal year, as per its investor update reviewed by Entrackr.
body: House of brands startup Evenflow Brands reported an improvement in profitability during FY26 and turned EBITDA positive for the full fiscal year, according to its investor update reviewed by Entrackr .

The company recorded Rs 53.06 crore in net sales in FY26 and posted a positive EBITDA of Rs 41.19 lakh with a margin of 0.8% for the year, as per the investor update. However, the GMV of the firm stood at Rs 81.5 crore in FY26.

Evenflow’s EBITDA margin improved during the year and reached 4.5% in Q4 FY26, compared to 1.6% in the corresponding quarter Q3 FY26. As per the company, its EBITDA for the March quarter stood at Rs 73.65 lakh.
The strong Q4 performance helped us end FY26 on a positive note. We are now the only profitable player in this space with zero debt on our books,” co-founder Utsav Agarwal said

The company said that its profitability improved due to better sourcing, lower marketing spends, and operational efficiencies. Cost of goods sold declined to 47.9% of net sales in Q4 from 50.2% in Q3, while marketing expenses reduced to 20.6% from 25.4% in Q1 FY26.
Its contribution margin after supply chain costs improved to 16% in Q4 from 7.7% in Q1 FY26. Employee costs remained stable at around 8% of net sales during the fiscal year.
Founded by former Uber and Decathlon executives Utsav Agarwal and Shashank Ranjan, Evenflow acquires and scales digital-first consumer brands across marketplaces and quick commerce platforms.
Evenflow operates brands such as Xtrim, Yogarise, Rusabl, BabyPro, Trendy Homes, Cinagro, and Frenchware across categories including fitness, home, kitchen, gardening, and baby care.

title: Rapido raises $240 Mn led by Prosus at $3 Bn valuation
description: Ride-hailing platform Rapido has raised $240 million in a fresh primary round led by Prosus, with participation from WestBridge Capital, Accel and other investors.
body: Ride-hailing platform Rapido has raised $240 million in a fresh primary round led by Prosus, with participation from WestBridge Capital, Accel and other investors.
According to the company’s press release, the fundraise is part of a larger $730 million primary and secondary transaction that values the company at $3 billion on a post-money basis.

The Bengaluru-based company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards expanding demand across new and existing markets, scaling its captain network, strengthening technology infrastructure, and hiring talent. Rapido will also deepen its footprint across tier II and smaller cities where affordable mobility demand continues to rise sharply.

Founded in 2015, Rapido operates in more than 400 cities and has emerged as one of the country’s largest mobility platforms across bike taxis, auto rides, and cab services. The company has positioned itself around affordable transportation and flexible earning opportunities for captains.

The latest financing comes at a time when India’s ride-hailing market is witnessing intense competition and rapid expansion beyond metro cities. Rapido said it aims to improve platform efficiency, strengthen first and last-mile connectivity, and create new demand corridors across high-growth regions.

Rapido’s financial performance also improved significantly during FY25. Its revenue from operations increased to Rs 934 crore in FY25 from Rs 648 crore in FY24. The strong growth helped the company cut its net loss by 30.5% to Rs 258 crore in FY25 from Rs 371 crore in the previous fiscal year. The firm has yet to file its FY26 financial numbers.

Rapido’s rapid scale-up has started reshaping the competitive landscape in India’s mobility sector. In August 2025, Dara Khosrowshahi said Uber now considers Rapido its biggest rival in India , ahead of Ola, which he described as a distant third player. Ola, meanwhile, has initiated IPO preparations despite reporting a 42% decline in FY25 revenue to Rs 1,170.9 crore and a widening net loss of Rs 662.4 crore.

Khosrowshahi is currently on a visit to India as Uber prepares to launch its first data centre in the country through a partnership with Adani Group to strengthen its technology and infrastructure footprint. The company also plans to open two new engineering campuses in Bengaluru and Hyderabad by 2027, with capacity for around 9,600 employees, as it expands its technology and product development operations in India.

title: Legend of Toys raises Rs 21 Cr in pre-Series A round
description: egend of Toys said it is focused on expanding its presence in the premium toy segment through design, storytelling, performance, community engagement, and product supp
body: Toy brand Legend of Toys has raised Rs 21 crore in a pre-Series A funding round, with participation from Singularity Early Opportunities Fund, Veltis Capital, Enzia Ventures, DeVC, Atrium Angels and Stride.
The proceeds will be used to expand into new play categories, consumer marketing, digital expansion, manufacturing, and international markets, the company said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by Afshaan Siddiqui and Vinay Jaisingh, Legend of Toys is a toy brand focused on character-led products. Its portfolio includes RC Drift Cars, Off-Road RC Trucks, 1:64 tabletop RC Drift Cars, and High-Speed RC Cars, priced between Rs 1,599 and Rs 8,799.
According to government data, India’s toy imports declined by 52%, while toy exports increased by 239% between FY2014-15 and FY2022-23.
Legend of Toys said it is focused on expanding its presence in the premium toy segment through design, storytelling, performance, community engagement, and product support.

The company claims it achieved an ARR of Rs 30 crore within 18 months and is currently growing at 20% month-on-month. It also said that a significant share of its sales through the direct-to-consumer channel is unit economics positive.

Funding activity in the toy and children-focused startup ecosystem has continued in recent months. Earlier this week, toy subscription startup The EleFant raised $1 million in a pre-Series funding round led by Growth Sense Venture Fund.
In March 2026, toy manufacturing startup BIDSO secured Rs 63 crore in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures.

title: Exclusive: Scripbox plans Rs 170 Cr debt and equity raise; gears up for IPO
description: Scripboxis planning to raise up to Rs 170 crore through a mix of equity and debt as it looks to acquire the mutual fund distribution business of a Delhi-based IFA.
body: Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup Scripboxis planning to raise up to Rs 170 crore through a mix of equity and debt as it looks to acquire the mutual fund distribution business of a Delhi-based Independent Financial Advisor (IFA).

According to its regulatory filing reviewed by Entrackr, the company’s board passed a resolution to approve a proposal to raise up to Rs 60 crore from a select group of friends and family investors through equity shares, preference shares, convertible instruments, or other securities.
The filing noted that the proceeds will be used to support Scripbox’s accelerated growth strategy, strengthen its balance sheet, and prepare for its targeted initial public offering (IPO).

Separately, Scripbox also secured approval to avail debt facilities of up to Rs 110 crore from banks, financial institutions, NBFCs, or other lenders. The debt will primarily be used to finance the acquisition of an Independent Financial Advisor (IFA).
However, the filing did not disclose the name of the Delhi-based Independent Financial Advisor (IFA) whose mutual fund distribution business is being acquired.

As part of the company’s expansion strategy, the company approved a draft business transfer agreement to acquire the mutual fund distribution business of a Delhi-based IFA through the purchase and transfer of its AMFI Registration Number (ARN), along with associated client relationships and obligations.

Founded in 2012, Scripbox is a Bengaluru-based digital wealth management platform that helps retail investors invest across mutual funds, fixed deposits, US stocks, ETFs, and NPS, while offering personalised investment and financial planning solutions.
Scripbox has raised over $55 million to date and holds a valuation of around Rs 1,150 crore (approximately $137 million). Its investors include Accel, LetsVenture, DMI, and others.

title: Delhivery revenue grows 30% in Q4 FY26; profit remains flat
description: Delhivery announced its Q4 FY26 results on Saturday, reporting a 30% year-on-year increase in revenue, while its profit remained largely flat during the period.
body: Delhivery announced its Q4 FY26 results on Saturday, reporting a 30% year-on-year increase in revenue, while its profit remained largely flat during the period.
Delhivery’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 2,850 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 2,192 crore in Q4 FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The company primarily earns revenue from its logistics services, including warehousing, last-mile delivery, and the design and deployment of logistics management systems. Delhivery also recorded Rs 59 crore from non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 2,909 crore in Q4 FY26.

Freight handling and servicing costs remained the company’s biggest expense component, accounting for nearly 70% of the total expenditure. These costs increased 28% to Rs 2,006 crore during the quarter. Employee benefit expenses rose 23.7% to Rs 417 crore. Finance costs, legal expenses, and other overheads pushed the company’s total expenditure to Rs 2,853 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 2,249 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Despite strong revenue growth, Delhivery’s profit remained almost unchanged at Rs 72.3 crore in Q4 FY26. A decline in other income along with higher employee costs, freight expenses, and operational overheads impacted the company’s bottom line during the quarter.

For the full fiscal year ending March 2026, Delhivery’s revenue from operations increased 17.6% to Rs 10,508 crore from Rs 8,932 crore in FY25. However, its profit declined 6% to Rs 152.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 162.1 crore in the previous fiscal.

Recently, Nexus Venture Partners sold shares worth Rs 716 crore in Delhivery through a block deal. The shares were bought by institutions including Morgan Stanley, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Goldman Sachs, Nippon India Mutual Fund, and Hong Kong-based Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund.
Delhivery’s shares were trading at Rs 476.2 apiece on Friday, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 35,654 crore.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [May 11 - May 16]
description: This week, 20 Indian startups raised around $292.52 million, comprising 3 growth-stage deals, 13 early-stage deals, while 4 startups kept their funding undisclosed. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 20 Indian startups raised around $292.52 million, comprising 3 growth-stage deals, 13 early-stage deals, while 4 startups kept their funding undisclosed.
In contrast, 24 startups had collectively secured about $158.8 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]
Growth-stage startups raised a total of $257.6 million across three deals this week, led by ride-hailing company Rapido, which secured $240 million in a round led by Prosus.

It was followed by F&B startup Wingreens, which raised $12.6 million in a round led by Ashish Kacholia. Meanwhile, fintech NBFC Sindhuja Microcredit secured $5 million in a pre-Series D round from Abler Nordic, GAWA Capital, and Oikocredit.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $34.92 million across 13 deals this week, led by fabless semiconductor startup HrdWyr, which raised $13 million in a Series A funding round led by Singularity AMC and Avatar Growth Capital, followed by Mekr, which secured $7 million from Titan Capital Winners Fund.
Fintech startup Nivasa Finance raised $3 million in a seed round led by Blume Ventures and Whiteboard Capital. Meanwhile, robotics startup Flo Mobility secured $2.5 million in a seed funding round.

title: Recovery-tech platform Owners ID raises pre-seed round led by Crucifer Investments
description: Owners ID’s products are designed for everyday use across multiple categories, including luggage and travel accessories, keys and wallets, passports and important docum
body: Recovery-tech startup Owners ID has raised $260K in a pre-seed funding round led by Crucifer Investments.

The fresh funds will be allocated towards product development, technology enhancement, manufacturing scale-up, mobile app improvements, AI-powered recovery systems, brand expansion, and global market expansion, Owners ID said in a press release.

Founded in November last year by Jesintha Louis, Owners ID is a smart recovery-tech company building a digital identity layer for physical belongings through privacy-first QR technology. It aims to make lost valuables instantly returnable.

The Bengaluru-based startup addresses the problem of lost or misplaced valuables through smart QR-based recovery products that allow finders to instantly connect with owners without exposing personal phone numbers or private information. The platform is designed to work globally using universally accessible technologies such as smartphone cameras and QR scanning, without requiring batteries, charging, expensive hardware, or app installation for finders.

Owners ID’s products are designed for everyday use across multiple categories, including luggage and travel accessories, keys and wallets, passports and important documents, electronics and gadgets, vehicles and car stickers, pet tags and health ID solutions, and personal valuables and lifestyle products.
According to industry estimates, India witnesses nearly 82 million lost-item-related incidents annually, while the global figure exceeds 319 million cases every year.

Positioned at the intersection of smart recovery, digital identity, and consumer safety technology, Owners ID is building what it calls a “digital identity layer” for physical belongings across pets, people, vehicles, luggage, electronics, and personal valuables.

title: Trading app Trackk raises $3.7 Mn from Lightspeed, Info Edge Ventures, others
description: Trackk has raised $3.7 million in an extended seed funding round led by Lightspeed India, with participation from Info Edge Ventures.
body: Updated version : Trackk, the investment platform built for Gen Z investors, has raised $3.7 million in a seed funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from Info Edge Ventures and angel investors including Gaurav Munjal, Roman Saini, Tanmay Bhatt, Varun Mayya, and Gaurav Kapoor.

The company will use the fresh capital to strengthen its broking infrastructure, expand product capabilities, accelerate user acquisition and customer onboarding, grow its team across key functions, and build additional financial products aimed at younger Indian investors.
Original story follows :
Mumbai-based trading-first platform Trackk has raised Rs 30 crore (around $3.16 million) in an extended seed funding round led by Lightspeed India, with participation from Info Edge Ventures.
The development comes nearly nine months after the company raised $1 million in a seed funding round from investors including Mga Ventures, GSF Ventures, GNP Group, and others.

According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , the board of Trackk approved the issuance of 1,23,630 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 2,429 apiece to raise Rs 30 crore.
Lightspeed India led the round with an investment of Rs 23.66 crore, while Info Edge Ventures contributed Rs 6.37 crore.

Entrackr estimates that the company has been valued at around Rs 118 crore (approximately $12.4 million) post-allotment. The fresh proceeds will be used towards capital expenditure, marketing, working capital requirements, and general corporate purposes, according to filings.

title: MapMyIndia records Rs 145 Cr revenue and Rs 51 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: CE Info Systems, the parent company of MapMyIndia, announced its quarterly results today, reporting modest revenue growth and largely flat profits in Q4 FY26.
body: CE Info Systems, the parent company of MapMyIndia, announced its quarterly results today, reporting modest revenue growth and largely flat profits in Q4 FY26.

MapMyIndia’s revenue from operations grew marginally to Rs 145 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 143.6 crore in Q4 FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
For the full fiscal year ending March 2026, the company’s operating revenue increased 2.3% to Rs 474.1 crore from Rs 463.3 crore in FY25.

Income from digital map data, GPS navigation, location-based services, and IoT remained the company’s primary revenue driver, contributing 87.69% of the total operating revenue. Revenue from this segment stood at Rs 127.2 crore in Q4 FY26. Meanwhile, revenue from device sales was recorded at Rs 17.9 crore during the quarter.

On the cost front, the company reduced its total expenses by 2.1% to Rs 88.3 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 90.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Employee benefit expenses continued to be the largest cost component, accounting for 24.6% of the total expenditure, followed by cost of material consumed and technical services outsourced expenses at 21.9% each.

The Delhi-based company reported a 3.9% increase in profit to Rs 50.93 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 49.02 crore in Q4 FY25. On a sequential basis, profit surged nearly threefold from Rs 18.76 crore recorded in Q3 FY26.
Following the results, MapMyIndia closed at Rs 996.60 per share, with a market capitalization of Rs 5151 crore.

title: Music streaming and distribution platform Damroo secures investment from Hindustan Times
description: Damroo currently offers digital music distribution, publishing administration, YouTube growth management, marketing support, artist collaborations, A&R guidance, royalty
body: Damroo, an artist-first music streaming, distribution, and growth platform, has raised a strategic investment of Rs 5 crore from Hindustan Times.

The proceeds will be used to strengthen its technology infrastructure, scale artist networks, enhance regional music discovery, expand its content catalogue, and create new monetization and fan engagement opportunities for creators across the country, Damroo said in a press release.

Launched in 2021 by Ram Mishra, Damroo focuses on empowering independent and regional artists across India through distribution, publishing support, marketing, audience growth, royalty support, and monetization solutions aimed at helping artists build sustainable music careers.

The Mumbai-based startup aims to address some of the biggest challenges faced by independent artists today, including discoverability, audience reach, monetization, and long-term career sustainability.

Damroo currently offers digital music distribution, publishing administration, YouTube growth management, marketing support, artist collaborations, A&R guidance, royalty collection support, and financial assistance for content production. The platform also helps artists become members of publishing societies such as Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS), enabling them to access long-term publishing royalties and sustainable revenue opportunities.

title: Oxyzo to acquire GoldenPi, enters retail fixed income investment space
description: Gurugram-based Oxyzo Financial Services is set to acquire 100% stake in bond investment platform GoldenPi Technologies and its affiliate GoldenPi Securities.
body: Oxyzo Financial Services is set to acquire a 100% stake in bond investment platform GoldenPi Technologies and its affiliate GoldenPi Securities, a move that takes the NBFC into the retail fixed income investment segment.
The acquisition will help Oxyzo expand its debt capital market offerings for retail and high-net-worth investors, according to a company statement.

Oxyzo, a technology-driven NBFC focused on SME financing, had assets under management (AuM) of around Rs 10,700 crore as of March 2026. The company had also announced the launch of its private credit fund earlier this year.

“We are excited to welcome the GoldenPi team into the Oxyzo family. This will enable us to significantly enhance our fixed income offerings and capture a larger share of the fast-growing debt investment market,” said Anuj Sharma, Business Head – Fixed Income at Oxyzo.

Founded in 2017 by Abhijit Roy and Samir Baran Pratihar, GoldenPi operates a SEBI-registered online bond platform that allows retail investors to invest in listed corporate bonds, government bonds, fixed deposits, and non-convertible debentures (NCDs).

The Bengaluru-based platform claims to have built a community of over 16 lakh users who have cumulatively invested more than Rs 6,000 crore through the platform, with zero defaults recorded till date.
GoldenPi has previously received backing from Rainmatter Capital and Utpal Sheth.

In March, Oxyzo launched Oxyzo Credit Fund I (OCF-I), a performing credit fund under its alternative investment platform. The company also entered the fund management business through a new subsidiary, Oxyzo Investment Manager Private Limited.

title: MakeMyTrip crosses $250 Mn revenue in Q4; profit drops 16.8%
description: Online travel platform MakeMyTrip reported a modest growth in revenue for the fourth quarter of FY26, while its profit declined due to a sharp rise in finance costs.
body: Online travel platform MakeMyTrip reported a modest growth in revenue for the fourth quarter of FY26, while its profit declined due to a sharp rise in finance costs.

The Nasdaq-listed company’s revenue from operations increased 1.9% year-on-year to $250.1 million in Q4 FY26 from $245.5 million in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its earnings release. On a constant currency basis, revenue grew 6.7%.

MakeMyTrip’s profit declined 16.8% to $24.3 million in Q4 FY26 from $29.2 million in Q4 FY25. During the quarter, the company’s finance costs more than doubled to $16.6 million from $7.5 million a year ago.

Among its key verticals, air ticketing revenue declined 4.7% year-on-year to $58.7 million in Q4 FY26 from $61.6 million in the same quarter last year. However, adjusted margin from the segment rose 5.4% to $99.3 million.
Hotels and packages, which remained the company’s largest revenue contributor, saw revenue dip marginally by 1.2% to $121.8 million during the quarter.
Bus ticketing continued to outperform other segments for the company during the quarter. Revenue from the segment grew 7.3% to $35.9 million, while adjusted margin rose 12.7% to $41.1 million.

On the expense front, other operating expenses rose 5.4% year-on-year to $63.6 million in Q4 FY26, while marketing and sales promotion expenses remained largely flat at $42.1 million. Personnel expenses declined 11% to $38 million during the period.

For the full fiscal year ending March 2026, MakeMyTrip’s revenue crossed the $1 billion mark, growing 6.7% to $1.04 billion from $978.3 million in FY25. However, annual profit fell 45.8% to $51.7 million.

title: BlackBuck reports Rs 185 Cr revenue and Rs 66 Cr profit in Q4 FY26
description: BlackBuck released its Q4 FY26 results today, posting a 52% year-on-year growth in revenue. The company also posted a profit of Rs 66 crore during the quarter.
body: Bengaluru-based online trucking platform BlackBuck released its Q4 FY26 results today, posting a 52% year-on-year growth in revenue. The company also posted a profit of Rs 66 crore during the quarter.
Blackbuck’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 185 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 122 crore in Q4 FY25. according to its unaudited financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show.

For the full fiscal year ending March 2026, Blackbuck’s operating revenue rose 52.7% to Rs 652 crore in FY26 from Rs 427 crore in FY25. Truck operator services contributed 99% of the total operating revenue which increased 52.5% to Rs 183.5 crore from Rs 120.4 crore in the year-ago quarter, while the rest of the operating revenue came from the lending business. Including other income, the company’s total income rose to Rs 200 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 137 crore in Q4 FY25.

Blackbuck’s total expenses surged 67.5% year-on-year to Rs 159.2 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 95.1 crore in Q4 FY25. Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost component which rose by 23.9% to Rs 40.8 crore in the quarter.

Blackbuck posted a profit of Rs 66 crore during Q4 FY26, This includes a benefit of Rs 28.59 crore from deferred tax credit. If we remove the same, the figures come around at Rs 37. For full fiscal year ended March 2026, its profits figures stood at Rs 160 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 38 crore in FY25.

During the quarter, the company's chairman and CEO, Rajesh Kumar Naidu Yabaji also sold 20 lakh shares amounting to Rs 135 crore bulk deal, reducing his stake from 11.81% to 10.7% of the company’s total equity base.
As of 3.30 PM, Blackbuck’s share price was trading at Rs 532.45, valuing the company at Rs 9597 crore

title: NODWIN eyes $100-200 Mn fundraise ahead of IPO
description: NODWIN Gaming is planning to raise $100-200 million through a mix of primary and secondary funding as it gears up for an IPO, , according to founder Akshat Rathee.
body: Nazara-backed esports and youth media platform NODWIN Gaming is planning to raise $100-200 million through a mix of primary and secondary funding as it gears up for an IPO, according to founder Akshat Rathee.
Speaking during Nazara Technologies’s Q4 FY26 earnings call, Rathee said the company aims to go public “as soon as possible.”

Nazara had first acquired a majority stake in NODWIN Gaming in 2018 and later increased its holding over the years. However, the company was deconsolidated from Nazara’s books during FY26 after a stake dilution , with Nazara now holding around 46-47% in the company.

The development comes at a time when NODWIN has improved its financial performance significantly. Nazara said the company posted an EBITDA profit of Rs 21 crore in FY26, compared to a loss of Rs 14 crore in FY25.
NODWIN also remained operationally profitable during the quarter despite taking a Rs 50 crore goodwill write-off linked to the acquisition of OML assets, including NH7 Weekender.

Founded in 2015 by Akshat Rathee and Gautam Virk, NODWIN started as an esports company and has since expanded into gaming content, youth entertainment, creator-led IPs, live events, and Comic Con operations. The company has also expanded internationally through acquisitions and partnerships across multiple regions.

According to Rathee, NODWIN’s core business registered organic growth of 25-35% during the year. The company has been positioning itself as a “live youth media company” with gaming at the center of its operations.

Nitish Mittersain also indicated that Nazara Technologies may look to monetise stakes in non-core businesses such as NODWIN Gaming in the future as it sharpens its focus on the core gaming segment. Meanwhile, the company is also planning to divest its esports and adtech businesses as part of this strategy.

title: Fintech startup Kalpi raises seed round from Rainmatter Capital
description: Hyderabad-based fintech startup Kalpi has raised Rs 3.75 crore in a seed funding round from Rainmatter Capital. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the team
body: Hyderabad-based fintech startup Kalpi has raised Rs 3.75 crore in a seed funding round from Rainmatter Capital.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the team, acquire datasets, improve product capabilities, and expand distribution across retail and institutional segments.
Founded in 2025 by Ashwar Gupta, Kalpi is building a rule-based systematic investing platform for retail and institutional investors.
The platform allows users to build, backtest, automate, and execute quantitative investment strategies across equities, ETFs, and mutual funds.
Kalpi offers two separate products, Kalpi.ai for retail investors and KalpiQuant.com for institutional investors such as PMS firms, AIFs, RIAs, brokers, and family offices.

The retail platform allows users to create stock baskets, analyse portfolios, and invest directly through broker integrations. The institutional platform provides tools such as portfolio optimisation, backtesting, factor analysis, and risk attribution.
According to the company, institutional-grade quant infrastructure that usually costs hedge funds Rs 1–2 crore to build can now be accessed through its platform.

title: Exclusive: Country Delight raises debt from Alteria Capital
description: Gurugram-based dairy and daily essential brand Country Delight  raised Rs 65 crore through the issuance of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) from Alteria Capital
body: Gurugram-based dairy and daily essential brand Country Delight  raised Rs 65 crore through the issuance of non-convertible debentures (NCDs) from Alteria Capital

The company’s board has approved the issuance of 6,500 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) having a face value of Rs 1 lakh each to raise the aforesaid amount, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
According to the filings, the proceeds from the debt raise will be used for general corporate activities of the company.
In March 2025, the company had raised Rs 212.5 crore (approximately $25 million) in its Series E round from Temasek.

Launched by Chakradhar Gade and Nitin Kaushal, Country Delight provides a range of dairy products, bakery goods, poultry, and farm produce to its customers. The company sources its products directly from dairy farms and caters to 1.5 million customers. It currently operates in more than 25 cities, including Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, and Chandigarh.
Country Delight had reportedly raised $220 million to date, including both debt and equity. Temasek remains the company’s largest external stakeholder, holding a 13.63% stake post-allotment.

The Gurugram-based company also recently entered into the quick commerce fray and launched a pilot for its 10-15 minute delivery service in Gurugram. With these offerings, the firm will also compete with players like Zepto, Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes, and Amazon Now (previously Amazon Tez).

The daily essential platform has not reported its financial numbers for FY24 officially. As per a report by The Arc, Country Delight posted a revenue of Rs 1,380 crore in FY24, surging 50% from Rs 917 crore in FY23, while incurring a loss of Rs 260 crore during FY23.

title: Agri finance startup ONO raises $1.2 Mn led by Aeravti Ventures
description: Agri-finance startup ONO has raised $1.2 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Aeravti Ventures. The round also saw participation from Angels and Tremis Capital. Snippets
body: Agri-finance startup ONO has raised $1.2 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Aeravti Ventures. The round also saw participation from Angels and Tremis Capital.
This marks Aeravti Ventures’ second investment in the startup after previously leading its seed round.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its technology platform, expand into new markets, and deepen its lending infrastructure.
Founded by Rama Rao Kancharapu and David Pokuri, ONO builds a data and AI-led platform focused on post-harvest agriculture supply chains and lending for Agri-SMEs.
The startup helps farmers, traders, transporters, and buyers with market intelligence, pricing data, logistics support, and access to formal credit.

ONO currently operates across 12 states and over 125 districts, serving more than 1.3 lakh participants in the agriculture ecosystem. The platform has over 2,000 paid subscribers and has facilitated more than Rs 200 crore in payouts.
The company claims it have enabled movement of over 25,000 metric tonnes of produce through long-distance agricultural trade routes..
As part of its expansion plans, the startup has acquired a significant stake in an NBFC to strengthen its lending operations and improve credit access for Agri-SMEs.

title: IAN Alpha Fund leads $5.4 Mn Series A round in ANSCER Robotics
description: ANSCER Robotics has raised $5.4 million (Rs 45 crore) in a Series A funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from Info Edge and other angel investors.

title: Lenskart posts Rs 2,516 Cr revenue in Q4 FY26; profit slips 7%
description: Eyewear brand Lenskart announced its financial results for Q4 FY26 today, reporting a 45.7% year-on-year growth in its consolidated operating revenue during the quarter.
body: Eyewear brand Lenskart announced its financial results for Q4 FY26 today, reporting a 45.7% year-on-year growth in its consolidated operating revenue during the quarter, while its profit slipped amid higher expenses.
The company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 2,516 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 1,727 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statements sourced from NSE.

India continued to remain the key growth driver for the company. Revenue from the India business grew 44.1% year-on-year in Q4 FY26, while the international business expanded 35.4% during the same period. According to the company, Lenskart added 603 net new stores during FY26, taking its total active store count to 3,327 globally.
For the full fiscal year ending March 2026, the firm’s revenue increased 28% to Rs 8,988 crore from Rs 7,009 crore a year earlier.

On the expense side, the cost of materials remained the largest expense head, accounting for 33% of the total expenditure. This cost increased 36% to Rs 764 crore in Q4 FY26. Employee benefit expenses also rose 26% to Rs 548 crore during the quarter from Rs 435 crore in Q4 FY25. Finance costs and depreciation expenses were other major overheads that pushed the company’s total expenses up by 36% to Rs 2,308 crore in Q4 FY26.

Despite strong revenue growth, the rise in expenses and higher tax outgo impacted the company’s bottom line. Lenskart’s profit declined 7% to Rs 204 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 220 crore in Q4 FY25. However, on a full-year basis, the company posted a profit of Rs 680 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 385 crore in FY25.

The SoftBank-backed company also expanded its global footprint during the year. Its Singapore subsidiary acquired an 84.21% stake in Spain-based Stellio Ventures S.L, while Lenskart increased its stake in QuantDuo Technologies and invested in Dimension NXG and South Korea-based iiNeer Co Ltd.
At the end of Wednesday’s trading session, Lenskart’s share price stood at Rs 484, taking its total market capitalization to Rs 84,042 crore (around $8.8 billion).

title: Ola Electric revenue falls 57% to Rs 265 Cr in Q4 FY26; plans QIP fundraising
description: Ola Electric continued to witness a sharp slowdown in business during Q4 FY26 as its revenue dropped more than 56% year-on-year amid weak scooter sales and continued cash burn
body: Electric vehicle maker Ola Electric continued to witness a sharp slowdown in business during Q4 FY26 as its revenue dropped more than 56% year-on-year amid weak scooter sales and continued cash burn. However, the Bengaluru-based company managed to narrow its losses during the quarter through aggressive cost controls.

Ola Electric’s revenue from operations declined to Rs 265 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 611 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Total income, including other income, also fell sharply to Rs 304 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 728 crore in Q4 FY25.

The company’s automotive business continued to remain the primary revenue contributor, while its cell business generated only Rs 4 crore during the quarter. Segment data also showed that Ola’s automotive revenue for the full fiscal year fell nearly 50% to Rs 2,245 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,514 crore in FY25.

Ola Electric reduced its total expenses by 58% year-on-year to Rs 546 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 1,306 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Procurement costs stood at Rs 163 crore, while employee benefit expenses dropped 37% to Rs 58 crore during the quarter.

Controlled spending and lower operational scale helped the Bhavish Aggarwal-led company cut its losses by 42.5% to Rs 500 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 870 crore in Q4 FY25. On a full-year basis, the company reported a net loss of Rs 1,833 crore in FY26.

The latest financial statements also highlighted growing concerns around the company’s financial health. Ola Electric reported a negative operating cash flow of Rs 775 crore during FY26 due to continued losses and lower-than-expected sales growth. The auditors also included an emphasis on the company’s “going concern” assumptions in their report.

To improve liquidity, Ola Electric has already reallocated a portion of its IPO proceeds and is now preparing to raise fresh capital through a qualified institutional placement (QIP). The company said it has initiated discussions with institutional investors and substantially completed investor engagement for the proposed fundraising.

title: Skydo secures GIFT City PSP licence and RBI outward payments license
description: GIFT City IFSC gives Skydo access to a globally aligned financial ecosystem designed specifically for international financial services. The ecosystem enables companies
body: Cross-border payments platform Skydo has received in-principle approval to operate as a Payment Service Provider (PSP) at GIFT City International Financial Services Centre (IFSC), making it among the first cross-border fintechs to secure a GIFT City licence.

GIFT City IFSC gives Skydo access to a globally aligned financial ecosystem designed specifically for international financial services. The ecosystem enables companies to build products and infrastructure tailored for businesses operating across borders.

The approval enables Skydo to expand capabilities such as multi-currency collections, e-money accounts and merchant acquisition, while building new payment corridors for Indian businesses operating globally. Over time, this could also create the foundation for more globally oriented financial products for Indian businesses.

Skydo has also received regulatory approval to support outward payment flows under the Reserve Bank of India’s Payment Aggregator-Cross Border (PA-CB) framework. Earlier this year, the company secured final authorisation from the RBI to operate as a PA-CB for export collections.

With these approvals, Skydo will be able to support both sides of a business’s global payment journey. Indian companies will be able to receive payments from international clients and make payments to overseas vendors, software platforms, service providers and partners through a compliant platform.
Skydo said it currently serves more than 40,000 Indian businesses across over 50 cities and supports collections from more than 150 countries.

The company currently supports collections in multiple currencies and enables exporters to receive payments locally from international clients with transparent pricing and faster settlements.
