body: Voice-first AI tutoring platform YoLearn.ai has raised $500,000 in a pre-seed funding round at a valuation of $5 million , co-led by DataAlpha.ai and White Swan Global, with participation from a group of angel investors.

The proceeds will be deployed to scale its AI tutoring products, including a voice-first audiovisual tutor with live sketchpad capabilities, and expand distribution across India's school and competitive exam ecosystem, YoLearn said in a press release.

Launched in January 2025 by Kirti Prakash Mishra, YoLearn.ai operates a voice-first AI tutoring platform designed around real-time audio conversations and a live interactive sketchpad, allowing the AI tutor to draw diagrams and work through problems visually while explaining concepts aloud, similar to a teacher at a whiteboard.

While the platform serves K-12 students across NCERT, CBSE, ICSE, and state board curricula, usage is concentrated among students in Grades 9 through 12, the segment juggling board exam preparation alongside competitive exams including JEE, NEET, and CUET. The company says its content is mapped with 100% syllabus accuracy across board and competitive exam curricula, with the AI tutor adapting explanations to each student's pace, language, and identified knowledge gaps.

The platform supports voice interaction in 22 Indian languages, including Hindi and Hinglish, and offers AI tutor personas modelled on the teaching styles of popular educators, alongside "AI Avatar" versions of real school teachers for partner institutions.

The platform is available as a web application (yolearn.ai) and as native apps on Android and iOS under the name YoTutor.ai, available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store. Across all three platforms, YoLearn.ai has crossed 200,000 cumulative users .
It competes with other notable players in the space, including SiglQ.AI, Fermi.AI, Arivihan.AI, CK-12, MagicSchool.AI, and Lytmus.AI.

title: Exclusive: Apna Mart to raise fresh funds in Series C from Accel, Fundamentum, Peak XV
description: Apna Mart is set to raise Rs 120 crore (around $12.7 million) in a Series C funding round co-led by existing investors Accel India and Fundamentum
body: Franchise-driven omnichannel grocery and FMCG chain Apna Mart is set to raise Rs 120 crore (around $12.7 million) in a Series C funding round co-led by existing investors Accel India and Fundamentum, with participation from Peak XV Partners. This is the company's second funding round in just over a year. Previously, the Gurugram-based startup raised around $25 million in its Series B round led by Fundamentum and Accel in March last year. Entrackr exclusively reported the development.

The company's board has passed a special resolution to issue 2,367 Series C compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 5,06,757 apiece to raise Rs 120 crore in fresh capital, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
Existing backers Accel India and Fundamentum will invest Rs 55 crore each, while Peak XV Partners will infuse the remaining Rs 10 crore.

As per Entrackr's estimates, Apna Mart's valuation will jump 2X to Rs 1,470 crore from Rs 738 crore in its previous funding round. The proceeds will be used towards capital expenditure, working capital requirements, and general corporate purposes. Founded by Abhishek Singh and Chetan Garg, Apna Mart operates a franchise-led omnichannel quick commerce platform focused on Tier II and Tier III cities. The startup delivers groceries in around 10 minutes through a neighborhood store-led model and competes with Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and Zepto. Following the fresh allotment, Accel India will remain the largest external shareholder with a 22.83% stake in Apna Mart, followed by The Fundamentum Partnership with 14.14%, while Peak XV Partners will hold 12.60%. For the fiscal year ended March 2025, Apna Mart reported operating revenue of Rs 185 crore and a net loss of Rs 76 crore. The company claimed its revenue grew 2.5X to Rs 500 crore in FY26, without disclosing its bottom line.
Last month, Apna Mart laid off 10% of its workforce and shifted its headquarters from Bengaluru to Gurugram.

title: OYO parent PRISM posts Rs 6,941 Cr revenue and Rs 748 Cr profit in 9M FY26
description: OYO parent PRISM reported strong financial performance for the first nine months of FY26, posting a net profit of Rs 748 crore, including a Rs 559 crore deferred tax credit during the period.
body: OYO parent PRISM, which has filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for a Rs 6,650 crore IPO, reported strong financial performance for the first nine months of FY26. The company posted a net profit of Rs 748 crore, including a Rs 559 crore deferred tax credit during the period.

OYO reported Rs 6,941 crore in revenue from operations during the first nine months of FY26, surpassing its full-year FY25 revenue of Rs 6,253 crore by 11%, according to its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP).

The sale of accommodation services (Rs 3,811 crore) and booking commissions (Rs 2,215 crore) remained the largest revenue contributors for the SoftBank-backed firm, accounting for over 86% of its operating revenue. OYO also earned Rs 152 crore from rental income, while other operating income, including the sale of tours and packages, cancellation charges, value added services, and food and beverages, contributed another Rs 763 crore.

Notably, more than 83% of OYO's revenue came from international markets, which contributed Rs 5,814 crore during the first nine months of FY26, while India accounted for the remaining Rs 1,127 crore. According to the company, its US business has emerged as one of its biggest growth drivers following the acquisition of G6 Hospitality, the operator of the Motel 6 and Studio 6 brands across the US and Canada.
The company operates 43 brands across more than 35 countries. As of December 31, 2025, its network comprised 24,303 hotels, 124,668 homes and 144,583 listings, including 14,937 storefronts in India.

The firm also booked around Rs 225 crore in non operating income, primarily from interest income and fair value gains following the loss of control over subsidiaries, taking its total income to Rs 7,166 crore during the first nine months of FY26.

On the expense side, lease rentals and the service component of leases accounted for 26% of OYO's total expenditure, amounting to Rs 1,821 crore during the first nine months of FY26. This was significantly lower than the Rs 2,763 crore incurred during the full FY25.
Finance costs and depreciation and amortisation expenses rose sharply to Rs 1,089 crore and Rs 793 crore, respectively, during the first nine months of FY26.

title: Cookware brand The Indus Valley raises $17 Mn led by Gaja Capital
description: Toxin-free cookware brand The Indus Valley has raised $17 million in a funding round led by Gaja Capital, with participation from investors DSG Consumer Partners. News
body: Toxin-free cookware brand The Indus Valley has raised $17 million in a funding round led by Gaja Capital, with participation from existing investors DSG Consumer Partners, Rukam Capital, and The Chennai Angels.
The round includes primarily primary capital along with a partial secondary sale by some early investors.
The fresh capital will be used to enter new product categories, strengthen its omnichannel distribution network, and invest in brand building and marketing initiatives.
Founded by Jagadeesh Kumar, the firm sells cookware and kitchen products made from materials such as cast iron, iron, copper, clay, and wood.
The company operates in the premium kitchenware segment, where consumer demand for chemical-free and toxin-free products has been growing steadily.

The fundraise comes nearly 18 months after The Indus Valley raised Rs 23.1 crore (around $2.75 million) in a pre-Series A round led by DSG Consumer Partners. The Chennai-based startup was valued at about Rs 303 crore ($36 million). Entrackr had exclusively reported the development.

For Gaja Capital, the investment adds another portfolio company. The private equity firm has backed consumer brands such as Eggoz as well as enterprise software company LeadSquared. In December last year, the homegrown private equity firm filed an updated draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) for its Rs 656 crore initial public offering, becoming the first Indian private equity firm to seek a public listing.

title: OYO parent PRISM files UDRHP to raise Rs 6,650 Cr via fresh issue only
description: OYO parent PRISM has filed its Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus (UDRHP) with SEBI for a Rs 6,650 crore IPO comprising only a fresh issue and no OFS.
body: OYO parent PRISM has filed its Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus (UDRHP-I) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), moving a step closer to its long-awaited public listing after receiving the regulator's approval earlier this month.

The proposed initial public offering (IPO) comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 6,650 crore, with no offer for sale (OFS) component. The company may also undertake a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 1,330 crore, which would reduce the size of the fresh issue if completed.

The shares will be listed on the NSE and BSE. Since the issue is entirely a primary raise, existing shareholders including SoftBank, founder Ritesh Agarwal, Microsoft, Airbnb, Peak XV, Lightspeed, Greenoaks and Khazanah will not dilute their stakes through the IPO.
According to the company, PRISM plans to use Rs 4,987.5 crore from the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings, while the remaining funds will be deployed for general corporate purposes.

PRISM has appointed Axis Capital, Citigroup Global Markets India, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities, ICICI Securities, SBI Capital Markets, JM Financial, InCred Capital and Intensive Fiscal Services as book-running lead managers for the issue.

As of the DRHP filing, SoftBank is the company's largest shareholder with a 40.04% stake, followed by founder Ritesh Agarwal, who holds a combined 26.71% stake through RA Hospitality Holdings and in his personal capacity. The Oravel Employee Welfare Trust, represented by trustee Dinesh Ramamurthi, owns 5.39%, while Patient Capital and Five Stars Capital hold 3.81% and 2.77%, respectively. Lightspeed, Airbnb, and Peak XV Partners own 1.74%, 1.22%, and 1.06% stakes, respectively.

The updated filing comes amid a sharp improvement in the hospitality technology firm's financial performance. During the first nine months of FY26, PRISM reported revenue from operations of Rs 6,941 crore, while its net profit surged threefold to Rs 748 crore from Rs 245 crore in FY25.

The company said it operates 43 brands across more than 35 countries. As of December 31, 2025, its network included 24,303 hotels, 124,668 homes and 144,583 listings. It has also expanded its company-serviced hotel business in India, where storefronts increased to 1,573 from 1,053 at the end of FY25, with the segment contributing nearly half of the company's India gross booking value (GBV).

title: Bajaj Finserv Ventures leads $10 Mn pre Series B round in Kapture CX
description: Verticalized full stack agentic AI platform Kapture CX has raised $10 million in a pre Series B funding round led by Bajaj Finserv Ventures (BFSV).
body: Verticalized full stack agentic AI platform Kapture CX has raised $10 million in a pre Series B funding round led by Bajaj Finserv Ventures (BFSV), part of Bajaj Finserv, with participation from its existing investors Cactus Partners and India Alternatives.

Prior to this, the Bengaluru based company had secured $4 million led India Alternatives extended Series A round in December 2023 and $4 million in a Series A round led by Cactus Venture Partners (CVP) in July 2023.
The fresh proceeds will be utilized for expansion into multiple global markets and continued investment in R&D and product development, Kapture CX said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2014 by Sheshgiri Kamath and Vikas Garg, Kapture CX is a verticalized, full stack agentic AI platform built to orchestrate high stakes workflows for large enterprises. Through its deep tech capabilities, it brings AI agents, operational intelligence, and human oversight into one system, allowing enterprises to run complex operations at scale.

Kapture CX said that enterprises face a fragmented market with point products from multiple providers, making AI adoption a high effort exercise. According to the company, enterprises need a full stack agentic AI platform that understands industry specific requirements and delivers customized solutions for complex workflows. This is the gap Kapture aims to address.

By owning and optimizing the full technology stack, from the models to the agentic layer and the user interface, Kapture says it enables enterprises to deploy AI at scale without the complexity of integrating multiple solutions from different providers. The platform is deeply verticalized and backed by deep tech capabilities that allow it to fine tune models for each industry vertical.

Kapture claims that its platform is trusted by over 1,000 enterprises across 18 countries, including Bajaj Finance and multiple companies within the Tata Group and Reliance Group. The company added that several consulting firms and hyperscalers also work with it as partners.
It competes with major players in the space such as Salesforce, Decagon, and Sierra AI.

title: Property management platform Crib App acquires CirclePe
description: Crib App, an AI-powered property management platform for co-living spaces, hostels, and PGs, has acquired CirclePe, a rent financing startup.
body: Crib App, an AI-powered property management platform for co-living spaces, hostels, and PGs, has acquired CirclePe, a rent financing startup that enables tenants to rent without paying a security deposit while providing operators with rent payments in advance.

The acquisition integrates financing into the rental lifecycle, allowing tenants to avoid upfront security deposits while enabling operators to receive rent and deposit-related financing upfront, which could improve their working capital.

CirclePe was founded by Navan Jaiswal and Ankur Yadav. In May 2024, the company raised nearly Rs 7.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round at a valuation of around Rs 35 crore. The round was led by OTP Ventures, with participation from 1947 Rise, iSeed, IIT Delhi, Venture Catalysts, and other investors.
With the acquisition, Crib and CirclePe will operate under a single platform.
CirclePe partners with NBFCs to finance tenants' security deposits or rent commitments. The funds are disbursed upfront to property operators, while tenants repay the amount in monthly installments.

Co-founded by Sunny Garg, Shaifali Jain, and Archit Chauhan, Crib is an AI-powered property management platform for co-living spaces, hostels, and PGs in India. The platform enables operators to manage occupancy, payments, residents, and day-to-day operations through a single system. It says it works with more than 2,500 operators and has raised approximately $3.64 million across seven funding rounds to date.
CirclePe offers a rent financing solution that eliminates the need for upfront security deposits for tenants while paying operators their rent in advance.

title: Banking infra startup Spense secures $2.8 Mn in seed funding
description: Spense has raised $2.8 million in a seed funding round led by Arkam Ventures, with participation from Razorpay Ventures, GrowthCap Ventures, and Atrium Ventures.
body: Banking infrastructure startup Spense has raised $2.8 million in a seed funding round led by Arkam Ventures, with participation from Razorpay Ventures, GrowthCap Ventures, and Atrium Ventures. The round also saw participation from angel investors including Kunal Shah, Madhusudhan E, Ravishankar, Suresh Rayasam Venkatasubbaih, and Sayandeb Banerjee.

The fresh funds will be used to deepen banking partnerships, accelerate product development, expand its engineering and go to market teams, and launch Credit Line on UPI (CLOU), Spense said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2022 by Pawan Kumar and Srinivas Krishnamurthy, Spense enables banks to launch credit cards and credit lines backed by customer assets without replacing their existing technology infrastructure.

The startup's bank native platform connects core banking systems, deposit systems, and card management systems in real time, enabling financial institutions to launch modern credit products significantly faster than traditional approaches.

The platform is powered by AI. Spense deploys agentic AI to automate workflows that have historically required large operations teams for onboarding, servicing, collections, and customer support. These autonomous agents run continuously, handling the operational complexity that has long made scaling secured credit products expensive and slow.

title: Lab grown diamond brand Limelight Diamonds raises Rs 275 Cr
description: Limelight Diamonds plans to expand its retail presence across metro cities, Tier I cities, and emerging Tier II markets. The company aims to significantly increase its
body: Lab grown diamond jewellery brand Limelight Diamonds has raised Rs 275 crore in a strategic funding round led by the company's core promoters, the Bhathwari Group, along with participation from key strategic partners from the jewellery industry.

The capital was raised through a combination of equity and cash consideration and will be utilised to strengthen the company's vertical integration capabilities, expand manufacturing infrastructure, enhance design and innovation capabilities, and accelerate retail expansion across India, Limelight Diamonds said in a press release.

Founded in 2019 by Pooja Madhavan, Limelight Diamonds is a lab grown diamond jewellery brand specialising in pure CVD lab grown diamonds. The brand offers consumers jewellery with exceptional brilliance, purity, and contemporary design.

Over the past few years, the brand says it has witnessed rapid nationwide expansion and now boasts the widest retail footprint for lab grown diamond jewellery in India, with over 75 exclusive brand outlets across more than 45 cities. Its collections span solitaires, everyday fine jewellery, and statement pieces, catering to modern Indian consumers.

Limelight Diamonds plans to expand its retail presence across metro cities, Tier I cities, and emerging Tier II markets. The company aims to significantly increase its national retail footprint through a combination of company owned and franchise operated stores, with a target of adding 100 stores in 2026 and scaling up to 200 stores by 2027.

According to Limelight Diamonds, lab grown diamonds represent a modern, technology led manufacturing opportunity for India. With strong domestic manufacturing capabilities, skilled craftsmanship, and growing consumer demand, the category aligns closely with India's ambition to emerge as a global manufacturing and export hub.

title: Dovetail Capital raises Rs 100 Cr led by Elev8 Venture Partners
description: Headquartered in Mumbai, the firm has a presence in GIFT City and regulated entities in Mauritius, Dubai (DIFC), and Singapore. It is regulated by the International Fi
body: Independent asset servicing firm Dovetail Capital has raised Rs 100 crore in a mix of primary and secondary funding in a Series A round led by Elev8 Venture Partners.
The proceeds will be used to expand its global business, Dovetail Capital said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2017 by Dev Sampat, Mahesh Shekdar, and Vivek Singhania, Dovetail Capital is an independent asset servicing firm that provides third party fund management (TPFM), fund administration, derivative clearing, investment advisory, and compliance services to foreign portfolio investors, alternative investment funds, family offices, insurers, mutual funds, and algorithmic funds.

Headquartered in Mumbai, the firm has a presence in GIFT City and regulated entities in Mauritius, Dubai (DIFC), and Singapore. It is regulated by the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), and the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA).
According to market research, mutual fund average assets under management (AAUM) reached Rs 83.5 trillion in May 2026.

Founded by Navin Honagudi in 2022, Elev8 Venture Partners is a growth stage venture investment firm focused on backing category leading technology companies across India. The firm invests in high growth businesses across sectors including fintech, consumer, SaaS, mobility, and enterprise technology.

title: Indian startups raise $7.4 Bn in H1 2026 as CRED-Meta deal lifts funding
description: Indian startups raised around $7.4 billion in H1 2026 across 551 disclosed deals, including $5.61 billion in 106 growth and late-stage rounds and $1.77 billion in 445 early-stage deals. Another 71 deals remained undisclosed.
body: The first half of 2026 was driven by artificial intelligence, with startups such as Neysa and Sarvam AI securing some of the largest funding rounds. But the biggest headline arrived towards the end of the period when CRED raised $900 million from Facebook parent Meta, followed by founder Kunal Shah's appointment as Global CEO of WhatsApp. These developments lifted startup funding to nearly $7.4 billion, making H1 2026 the second highest funded first half after the 2021 and 2022 boom. The six month period also saw D2C beauty and health brands emerge as attractive acquisition targets, while the IPO pipeline gained momentum with OYO, Zepto, Razorpay, Kuku and Zetwerk moving closer to listings. Turtlemint, Fractal, Shadowfax and Kissht also made their stock market debut.
[Overview]

According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $7.4 billion in funding during the first half of 2026. This amount included 106 growth and late-stage deals totaling $5.61 billion, along with 445 early-stage deals worth $1.77 billion. Additionally, there were 71 undisclosed deals during this period.
During this period, six startups including S quare Yards, Sarvam AI, Skyroot, KreditBee , Neysa , and Juspay entered the unicorn club. During H1 2025, five startups achieved the feat.
[Y-o-Y and M-o-M trend]

H1 2026 ended on a stronger note than the previous two years, with startups raising $7.39 billion, the highest first half total since 2022. The total surpassed H1 2025 ($6.72 billion) and H1 2024 ($7 billion) but remained well below the $20 billion raised in H1 2022 and the $13 billion recorded in H1 2021.
On a month on month basis, funding more than tripled to $2 billion in June from $630 million in May. This came after three consecutive months of decline.
[Top 10 growth stage deals in H1]

title: Transition VC leads $1.05 Mn pre Series A round in Albatross Energetics
description: The company uses proprietary liquid desiccant technology to remove moisture directly from the air, reducing the energy required for humidity control. It designs, manufa
body: Deep tech company Albatross Energetics has raised $1.05 million (around Rs 10 crore) in a pre Series A funding round led by Transition VC.
The Mumbai based startup had previously secured Rs 1.3 crore in 2024 from Social Alpha and SINE.

The fresh funds will be used to establish pilot scale manufacturing capabilities, expand commercial deployments across industrial sectors, strengthen its engineering and quality teams, and accelerate research and development, Albatross Energetics said in a press release.
Founded in 2021 by Sudarsan M S and Srihari B, Albatross Energetics develops energy efficient air conditioning and dehumidification systems for industrial applications.

The company uses proprietary liquid desiccant technology to remove moisture directly from the air, reducing the energy required for humidity control. It designs, manufactures, and deploys industrial cooling systems for sectors including pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, electronics, batteries, food processing, chemicals, and textiles, helping customers reduce operating costs and carbon emissions.
According to the company, its proprietary liquid desiccant platform addresses humidity management, one of the most energy intensive and operationally critical aspects of industrial cooling systems.
Albatross plans to expand its technology beyond industrial applications into commercial buildings and broader global cooling markets.
The startup competes with global players including BlueFrontier, Mojave, and Transaera.

title: Nutrition startup Supply6 raises Rs 48 Cr led by Unilever Ventures
description: Nutrition startup Supply6 has raised Rs 48 crore ($5 million) in a funding round led by Unilever Ventures, with participation from existing investor Zeropearl VC. Snippets
body: Nutrition startup Supply6 has raised Rs 48 crore ($5 million) in a funding round led by Unilever Ventures, with participation from existing investor Zeropearl VC.
The round also saw participation from actor and entrepreneur Kriti Sanon.

Back in September last year, Supply6 had raised $1.1 million (Rs 9.1 crore) in a seed round led by Zeropearl VC and others. The startup had previously raised Rs 10 crore in funding and received a Rs 25 lakh grant from the Karnataka government.
The proceeds will be used for product innovation, clinical research, supply chain expansion, digital experience, and growth across D2C, marketplaces, and quick commerce channels.

Founded by Vaibhav Bhandari and Rahul Jacob, Supply6 offers daily supplements across vitamins, hydration, and fibre categories. Its flagship product, Supply6 360, combines over 63 ingredients, including probiotics, micronutrients, and adaptogens.

The startup sells its products through its website as well as platforms such as Amazon and Blinkit. According to the company, a significant share of its revenue comes from two flagship products, with repeat purchases contributing substantially to growth.
With over 2 lakh customers and ex-cricketer AB de Villiers as brand ambassador, the firm is building a strong repeat-purchase base (45%) while expanding reach into preventive health markets abroad.
The company currently operates at an annualised revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 75 crore and expects to reach Rs 100 crore ARR within the next three to four months.

title: Ananta Capital acquires majority stake in Phitku in Rs 100 Cr deal
description: The company aims to redefine body odour management through science-backed, ingredient-conscious products developed for Indian climate conditions and everyday use.
body: Private equity firm Ananta Capital has acquired a majority stake in direct-to-consumer personal care brand Phitku in a deal worth around Rs 100 crore, valuing the startup at approximately Rs 200 crore, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The proceeds will be used to accelerate product innovation, strengthen brand building, deepen the company's presence across D2C, marketplaces and quick commerce, and selectively expand into international markets, Phitku said in a press release.

Structured as a combination of a primary capital infusion and a secondary share purchase, the transaction provides Phitku with fresh growth capital while enabling partial liquidity for its founders. Sumit Marda, Neha Marda and Rahul Dokania will continue to lead the company while retaining a significant stake in the business.

Co-founded in early 2025, Phitku is a personal care brand focused on clean, alcohol-free and skin-friendly formulations that neutralise body odour at its source instead of masking it with synthetic fragrances.
The company aims to redefine body odour management through science-backed, ingredient-conscious products developed for Indian climate conditions and everyday use.
Phitku claims to have scaled rapidly in its first year, earning the trust of more than 6 lakh customers across the country through its D2C platform, marketplaces and quick commerce channels.
The brand is targeting 4x to 5x growth over the next two years to achieve an ARR of Rs 300 crore, while remaining committed to building a globally relevant, science-led hygiene brand from India.

title: AI native coordination startup Brekfuz raises $525K
description: Brekfuz integrates communication platforms, documentation systems, meeting records, code repositories, and project management tools to create a searchable record of
body: AI native coordination startup Brekfuz has raised $525K at a valuation of $7.5 million in a funding round from investors including Pear VC, Pareto Holdings, Collective Global, and several angel investors.
Co-founded by Arhan Singhal and Sarthak Ahuja, Brekfuz operates as an AI native coordination platform designed to make organisational knowledge searchable, accessible, and actionable.
The platform automatically maps ownership, responsibilities, and domain expertise within an organisation to reduce dependence on repetitive status updates and fragmented handoffs.

It allows employees and AI systems to search for information across tools such as Slack, email, documents, meeting records, and GitHub using natural language. According to the company, the software is designed to reduce dependence on individual employees for information related to processes, decisions, and ownership within organisations.

Brekfuz integrates communication platforms, documentation systems, meeting records, code repositories, and project management tools to create a searchable record of organisational knowledge. Users can ask questions in natural language and receive responses linked to the underlying source material.
The company says it aims to serve as an infrastructure layer that helps organisations make their people, processes, and decisions more searchable, accessible, and actionable.

title: Data Science Wizards raises $5 Mn in pre-Series A round
description: Designed for enterprises and regulated industries, UnifyAI OS enables organizations to operationalize AI while maintaining ownership, governance, interoperability, secur
body: Enterprise tech company Data Science Wizards (DSW) has raised $5 million in a pre-Series A funding round from angel investors.
Previously, the Mumbai-based startup had secured $1.4 million in a seed funding round at a valuation of $16.4 million in October 2024, led by an angel investor.

The proceeds will be used to accelerate product innovation, expand its North American operations, strengthen its engineering and customer success teams, deepen strategic partnerships, and scale the adoption of UnifyAI OS across enterprises and regulated industries, DSW said in a press release.

Founded in 2019 by Pritesh Surendra Tiwari, Sandhya Oza, Sandeep Khuperkar, and Shivam Thakkar, Data Science Wizards has developed UnifyAI OS, an enterprise AI operating system that enables organizations to build, integrate, deploy, govern, monitor, and operate AI and agentic AI through a unified operating layer.

Designed for enterprises and regulated industries, UnifyAI OS enables organizations to operationalize AI while maintaining ownership, governance, interoperability, security, and long-term control over their AI ecosystem.

Operating AI securely across business functions while maintaining governance, interoperability, compliance, and enterprise control remains one of the biggest challenges for large organizations. DSW aims to address this challenge through UnifyAI OS, which provides a unified operating layer for building, integrating, deploying, governing, monitoring, and operating AI and agentic AI applications.
DSW currently serves enterprises across the banking, financial services, insurance, and public sectors. It competes with companies such as Palantir, Dataiku, DataRobot, H2O.ai, C3 AI, and SAS Viya.

title: TVS widens lead in June as EV two-wheeler registrations rise 12%
description: India's electric two-wheeler market continued its upward trajectory in June, with registrations climbing 12.2% month-on-month to 1.93 lakh units. TVS Motor retained the top spot with 46,999 registrations, with a 24.29% market share
body: India's electric two-wheeler market continued its upward trajectory in June, with registrations climbing 12.2% month-on-month to 1.93 lakh units. TVS Motor strengthened its lead over Bajaj Auto, while Hero MotoCorp recorded the fastest growth among the top five manufacturers. Ola Electric, meanwhile, continued to trail its larger rivals despite reporting a modest increase in registrations.
According to Vahan data, TVS Motor retained the top spot with 46,999 registrations, with a 24.29% market share. The company sold 4,034 more units than in May and posted 9.4% month-on-month growth.
Bajaj Auto continued to narrow the gap with the leader and sold 43,234 units to capture 22.34% market share. The company added 3,727 units during the month, also posting 9.4% growth over May.
Ather Energy held on to the third position with 31,188 registrations and 16.12% market share, as its sales increased 9.4% from 28,512 units in May.
Hero MotoCorp remained fourth with 21,792 units and an 11.26% market share. Among the top five players, Hero posted the fastest month-on-month growth at 13.4%, with sales up by 2,578 units.
Ola Electric continued to trail the top four despite a modest recovery. The company registered 16,144 units in June, up 6.1% from 15,218 units in May, taking its market share to 8.34%.

Outside the top five, Greaves Electric Mobility emerged as one of the strongest performers, with registrations surging 41.9% month-on-month to 10,928 units, while River Mobility and BGauss recorded 16% and 18.7% growth, respectively.
Among smaller manufacturers, E-Sprinto Green Energy posted the sharpest growth, nearly doubling its registrations to 1,878 units.

title: Omnichannel sports retail startup PlayBlue raises $2.7 Mn in seed round
description: The platform says that it brings more than 100 global and homegrown brands across athleisure, footwear, equipment and nutrition into curated experiential stores,  back

title: Ninjacart raises $6 Mn after 4.5 years, claims EBITDA profitability ahead of IPO
description: Fresh produce supply chain startup Ninjacart has turned EBITDA profitable, raised $6 million in the first tranche of a multi tranche investment round from existing investors.
body: Fresh produce supply chain startup Ninjacart has claimed that it turned EBITDA profitable, raised $6 million in the first tranche of a multi tranche investment round from existing investors, and begun preparations for an initial public offering over the next two years.
The funding was led by existing backers Accel, Tiger Global, and Nandan Nilekani, with more existing investors expected to join the round.

The latest investment comes after more than four and a half years for the Bengaluru based company. Ninjacart last raised $145 million at a valuation of $815 million in December 2021 from Walmart and Flipkart.
The company has not disclosed its latest valuation.

“In the last few years, profitability has been our biggest focus, while growing steadily. First, we improved our margins through the right category and channel mix and by going backwards on the sourcing side. Second, we leveraged technology and data to minimise wastage and reduce supply chain costs,” said Kartheeswaran KK, co-founder and CEO of Ninjacart.

Founded in 2015 by Kartheeswaran KK, Thirukumaran Nagarajan, and Ashutosh Vikram, Ninjacart operates a full stack fresh produce supply chain connecting farmers with retailers, quick commerce platforms, modern trade chains, exporters, and HoReCa customers.

The company claims to be the largest fresh produce supplier to India's quick commerce industry. It operates across more than 40 cities and manages a portfolio of over 150 products, ranging from onions, potatoes, and tomatoes to blueberries, avocados, and apples. According to the company, its core businesses have grown threefold over the past year.

Ninjacart counts Walmart, Flipkart, Accel, Tiger Global, Nandan Nilekani, Syngenta Group Ventures, and Steadview Capital among its investors. The company believes its profitability and business scale position it for a public listing within the next two years.

title: BCT Ventures launches AI native consumer brands platform, raises Rs 42 Cr from 3one4 Capital
description: The platform is built on three proprietary AI engines. Resonance focuses on audience building and consumer insights through practitioner led content and AI workflows.
body: BCT Ventures, an AI native consumer brands platform, has launched its operations and raised Rs 42 crore in a seed funding round led by 3one4 Capital.

The company will initially focus on the nutrition and wellness segment, using its three proprietary AI engines, Nucleus, Resonance and Meridian, across insights gathering, product development and go to market.

According to the company, it plans to build consumer brands around protocol led products, practitioner led audiences and AI enabled growth systems. Over time, it intends to expand the same approach to other consumer categories.

BCT Ventures was co founded by Kashyap Vadapalli, KV Ravi Shekhar and Anubhav Sonthalia. The founding team brings experience in consumer brands, digital growth, audience development, mergers and acquisitions, and venture building.

The platform is built on three proprietary AI engines. Resonance focuses on audience building and consumer insights through practitioner led content and AI workflows. Nucleus is designed to translate practitioner expertise, audience demand signals and AI based analysis into products. Meridian supports marketing functions such as creative testing, media buying, budget allocation and return on ad spend optimisation.
The company said the three engines work together in a closed loop system, where consumer demand informs product development, marketing execution and future product iterations

title: Swara Baby Products files Rs 1,000 Cr IPO papers; FirstCry parent to sell Rs 300 Cr shares
description: Brainbees Solutions-owned Swara Baby Products, manufacturer of disposable hygiene products, has filed its DRHP with the SEBI for an initial public offering (IPO).
body: Brainbees Solutions-owned Swara Baby Products, manufacturer of disposable hygiene products, has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for an initial public offering (IPO).
The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to Rs 500 crore by existing shareholders.

The OFS includes shares worth Rs 300 crore by Brainbees Solutions Ltd (FirstCry), which held a 76.59% stake in Swara Baby at the time of the DRHP filing, and Rs 200 crore by promoter entity Anadya Bon Merchari LLP.

According to the DRHP, the company plans to use Rs 198.2 crore from the fresh issue to set up a new manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh. Another Rs 100 crore will be used to repay certain borrowings, while Rs 27.5 crore will be infused into its subsidiaries, Solis Hygiene, Swara Hygiene, and KAEHPL for repayment of their debt. The remaining proceeds will be used for inorganic growth through acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
JM Financial and Avendus Capital are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India Private Limited is the registrar to the issue.

The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 100 crore in consultation with the book-running lead managers. If such a placement is completed, the size of the fresh issue will be reduced accordingly.

Founded in 2016, Swara Baby manufactures disposable hygiene products, including baby diapers, adult diapers, sanitary napkins, disposable underpads, and wet wipes. The company operates as a contract manufacturer for several consumer brands while also selling products under its own brands.

Swara Baby claims to be India's largest contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products by value in FY25. It manufactures for domestic as well as international customers across the baby care, feminine hygiene, and adult incontinence segments.

title: Heatronics raises Rs 1.8 Cr seed round led by IPV
description: Noida-based preventive pain-management and wellness startup Heatronics has raised Rs 1.8 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV).  Snippets
body: Noida-based preventive pain-management and wellness startup Heatronics has raised Rs 1.8 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV).
The round also saw participation from angel investors Nitin Agarwal, former executive at GlobalBees, and Shivam Mishra of String Ventures.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen marketing and branding initiatives, upgrade manufacturing facilities, and expand its distribution network.
Founded in 2022 by Hargun Singh Chawla, Heatronics develops medical-grade heat therapy and recovery devices under its hCore brand.

The firm offers a portfolio of 10 heat-therapy products designed for pain relief and recovery. According to Heatronics, the products were developed based on feedback from over 500 customers and feature temperature-control technology along with automatic shut-off functionality.

Heatronics operates a 12,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Noida and employs more than 40 people. The startup sells through channels including Amazon, Blinkit, its own website, and offline retail outlets.
The company claims to hold ISO 13485, CDSCO Class B, and BIS certifications. It also says it manufactures its products domestically through a vertically integrated supply chain.
Heatronics reported more than 100% year-on-year growth and said its monthly revenue has increased nearly fourfold ahead of the peak demand season.

title: Specialty chemical startup Tulon Materials raises Rs 10 Cr in seed round
description: ts portfolio includes a plastic waste upcycling technology that converts complex polymer waste into chemical resins for industrial use, aiming to support circular materi
body: Tulon Materials, an R&D-led engineering startup developing high-performance and sustainable specialty chemicals, has raised Rs 10 crore in a seed funding round led by investor Karthik Sundar Iyer. The round also saw participation from Karan Goshar and Prakhar Pandey, partners at Valour Capital, along with Agam Shah.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate engineering and commercialisation of products for applications in paints and coatings, printing inks, and adhesives, the company said in a press release.

Founded in June 2022 by Asesh Sarkar, Rabindranath Mandal, and Harsh Bhatt, the Mumbai-based startup develops proprietary specialty chemicals and advanced materials for industrial applications with a focus on sustainability.

Its portfolio includes a plastic waste upcycling technology that converts complex polymer waste into chemical resins for industrial use, aiming to support circular material adoption and address plastic waste challenges.

Tulon also operates an open innovation platform that works with industry partners, research institutions, and customers to accelerate product validation and application development. The company uses artificial intelligence across chemical simulation, validation, and R&D workflows to shorten development timelines.

According to the company, its material platforms are designed to reduce reliance on virgin fossil-derived feedstocks, enable lower-carbon industrial processes, and support circular economy initiatives across its target sectors.

title: BatX Energies raises Rs 105 Cr in Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures
description: Battery recycling and critical minerals recovery startup BatX Energies has raised Rs 105 crore ($11 million) in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. News
body: Battery recycling and critical minerals recovery startup BatX Energies has raised Rs 105 crore ($11 million) in a Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures.
The round also saw participation from existing investors Zephyr Peacock, Mankind Pharma Family Office, Excel Industries Family Office, and JITO.
Prior to this round, BatX had raised $5 million in pre-Series A round led by Zephyr Peacock and others in December 2023.
The Gurugram-based startup will use the fresh funds to expand its recycling and refining capacity, strengthen R&D, and accelerate the development of a domestic supply chain for battery materials.

Founded by Utkarsh Singh and Vikrant Singh, BatX focuses on battery recycling, critical mineral recovery, and refining. The company recovers materials such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, and graphite from end-of-life batteries and manufacturing scrap.
BatX claims to have built a commercial-scale battery recycling and critical minerals recovery platform and is already supplying recovered battery-grade materials to the market.
The company is also working on the development of Cathode Active Materials (CAM), which are used in lithium-ion battery manufacturing.

title: Burma Burma posts Rs 156 Cr revenue and Rs 14 Cr loss in FY26
description: Burma Burma’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 155.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 106 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the RoC.
body: Burma Burma, a vegetarian pan-Asian restaurant chain, came close to breaking even in FY25. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, the company recorded a 47% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to cross the Rs 150 crore mark, while EBITDA grew 35% to Rs 29 crore. However, depreciation and amortisation expenses nearly doubled during the year, weighing on the bottom line.
Burma Burma’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 155.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 106 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The company operates a chain of restaurants serving Burmese cuisine with Indian, Chinese, and Thai influences across more than a dozen outlets in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, and Chandigarh.

Bengaluru remained the company's largest market in FY26, contributing over 32% of total revenue, or nearly Rs 50 crore. Mumbai followed with Rs 38.4 crore, while Delhi and Gurugram contributed around Rs 15 crore each. The remaining revenue came from Hyderabad, Noida, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, and Chandigarh.
Dine-in remained the company's largest revenue source in FY26, which contributed 82% of operating revenue at Rs 128 crore. Online sales through food delivery platforms contributed Rs 15.9 crore.

Employee benefits and material costs together accounted for over 44% of the restaurant chain's total expenses in FY26. Employee benefit expenses rose 44% year-on-year to Rs 48.5 crore, while material costs increased 50% to Rs 30 crore. Depreciation and amortisation expenses nearly doubled to Rs 40.8 crore during the fiscal year.
Restaurant rent expenses climbed 43% to Rs 8.3 crore, while advertising expenses doubled to Rs 5.6 crore.
Higher spending on power and fuel, utilities, transportation, and other overheads pushed the company's total expenses up nearly 60% year-on-year to Rs 175.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 110 crore in FY25.

title: Elder care startup Age Care Labs raises $9 Mn from Rainmatter and others
description: Epoch follows an asset-light model by leasing properties and partnering with operators, while the company is expanding through franchise partnerships, institutional
body: At-home elder care startup Age Care Labs has raised Rs 85 crore (around $9 million) from Zerodha-backed Rainmatter, Pegasus Finvest, the Shrem Group, and several family offices. The investment is part of a larger Rs 250 crore (around $30 million) round that the company plans to complete in the coming months.

Entrackr had exclusively reported in August last year that the Gurugram-based company was raising the first tranche of its Series B round. Prior to the latest investment, Age Care Labs had raised more than $20 million, including an $11 million pre-Series B round in 2023 led by Rainmatter Capital and Gruhas.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen operations, expand service offerings, invest in technology, and support the company’s next phase of growth across the country, Age Care Labs said in a press release.

Age Care Labs provides integrated elder care services through two brands: Emoha, an at-home and app-based elder care platform, and Epoch Elder Care, which operates assisted living and dementia care homes.

Epoch follows an asset-light model by leasing properties and partnering with operators, while the company is expanding through franchise partnerships, institutional collaborations, and acquisitions. Together, the two brands serve more than 60,000 seniors across 120 cities.
Emoha offers services including 24x7 emergency response, health monitoring, telemedicine, and wellness programmes for seniors living at home.
According to the company, its asset-light model enables it to expand across tier I and tier II cities while addressing gaps in India’s fragmented at-home and clinical elder care ecosystem.

title: Temasek continues reducing stake in PB Fintech, sells shares worth Rs 1,633 Cr
description: Temasek has continued to reduce its stake in PB Fintech, by offloading shares worth Rs 1,633 crore through a bulk deal. The transaction marks its second stake sale in the company in less than two months.
body: Temasek-backed Macritchie Investments Pte Ltd has continued to reduce its stake in PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, by offloading shares worth Rs 1,633 crore through a bulk deal. The transaction marks its second stake sale in the company in less than two months.

According to the bulk deal data on the NSE, Macritchie Investments sold 1.01 crore shares at a price of Rs 1,604.12 per share, representing around 2.2% stake in PB Fintech. The transaction was valued at approximately Rs 1,633 crore.

Prior to the transaction, Temasek, through Macritchie Investments, held a 6.47% stake in PB Fintech. The latest sale follows its Rs 805 crore block deal in May, when it offloaded a 1.05% stake in the company, further reducing its shareholding.
In May, PB Fintech co-founders Yashish Dahiya and Alok Bansal also collectively sold shares worth around Rs 665 crore (approximately $70 million) in the company through a block deal.
On the financial front, PB Fintech reported a 37% year-on-year rise in operating revenue to Rs 2,061 crore in Q4 FY26, while its profit increased 54% to Rs 261 crore during the quarter.
Following the transaction, shares of PB Fintech declined 5.71% to Rs 1,586 on Friday, taking the company's market capitalization to around Rs 73,383 crore.

title: Decoding: SolarSquare valued at $470 Mn after Series C; co-founders retain 27.5% stake
description: Solar rooftop startup SolarSquare recently raised $53 million in a Series C round led by B Capital, with participation from existing investors. The company has now raised over $90 million in less than two years.
body: Solar rooftop startup SolarSquare recently raised $53 million in its Series C funding round led by B Capital, with participation from existing investors including Lightspeed, Lowercarbon, Rainmatter. With this round, the company has raised over $90 million in less than two years.
Previously the company raised $40 million in Series B round led by Lightspeed in December 2024.
Entrackr examined SolarSquare's regulatory filings to decode the company's latest funding round, updated captable, and post-money valuation.

According to the company's regulatory filings accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC), SolarSquare's board passed a special resolution to issue 11,969 Series C compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) and one equity share at an issue price of Rs 4,26,112 each to raise Rs 510 crore ($53 million).

B Capital emerged as the largest investor in the round with an investment of Rs 287.7 crore (around $30 million), followed by existing investor Lightspeed Venture Partners with Rs 79.85 crore (around $8.3 million), Lowercarbon with Rs 65.83 crore (around $6.8 million), Good Capital with Rs 40.73 crore, Mangum LLC with Rs 21.94 crore, and Zerodha-backed Rainmatter with Rs 11 crore.
The remaining amount will be contributed by Better Capital, while former Indian cricket captain MS Dhoni also participated in the round through his family office, Midas Deals.

According to Entrackr's estimates, SolarSquare's post-money valuation nearly doubled to around Rs 4,500 crore (approximately $470 million), compared to around $253 million in its $40 million Series B round.

Following the allotment, Lowercarbon remains the largest external shareholder with a 16.09% stake, followed by Elevation Capital at 15.23%. Lightspeed Venture Partners holds 9.91%, Good Capital owns 8.24%, new investor B Capital acquired 6.4%. The ESOP pool accounts for 5.74%, Lightrock owns 3.49%, and Rainmatter Capital holds 2.69%. Meanwhile, co-founders Neeraj Jain, Shreya Mishra, and Nikhil Nahar collectively retain a 27.54% stake in the company.

title: CUNIN raises $450K pre-seed round co-led by All In Capital and Huddle Ventures
description: NIN offers carryable perfume accessories, a category of fragrance products designed to be worn, clipped, and carried. The products are currently available through the
body: Culture-led lifestyle brand CUNIN has raised $450K in a pre-seed funding round co-led by All In Capital and Huddle Ventures.
The proceeds will be used to accelerate product development, strengthen its team, invest in brand building, and expand its offline presence, CUNIN said in a press release.

Co-founded by Kunal Shukla, Amish Bibhu, and Afsal, CUNIN operates in the fragrance segment and plans to expand into the broader lifestyle category. The company aims to build a global lifestyle brand through products centered on identity, community, and storytelling.

CUNIN offers carryable perfume accessories, a category of fragrance products designed to be worn, clipped, and carried. The products are currently available through the company’s website. Its debut collection, The World of Antonyms , introduces a creative theme across its products, packaging, and branding.
According to the company, the collection features personalities such as IM-Perfect, DIS-Loyal, MIS-Placed, and MIS-Aligned, encouraging consumers to express different aspects of their identity.

The startup plans to expand its fragrance portfolio while investing in content, brand experiences, and community initiatives. It also intends to enter adjacent lifestyle categories and collaborate with international creators and cultural tastemakers over time.

title: Emami-owned The Man Company’s losses widen 49% in FY26 amid modest revenue growth
description: Emami-owned men’s grooming and personal care brand The Man Company reported modest topline growth during the fiscal year ended March 2026. At the same time
body: Emami-owned men’s grooming and personal care brand The Man Company reported modest topline growth during the fiscal year ended March 2026. At the same time, higher spending weighed on its bottom line, resulting in a 48.7% increase in its losses.
The Man Company’s revenue from operations increased 4.5% to Rs 161.17 crore in FY26 from Rs 154 crore in the previous fiscal , according to the regulatory document reviewed by Entrackr .

The Gurugram-based firm manufactures and sells grooming products across skincare, haircare, beard care, fragrances, and other personal care categories. It also recorded Rs 12 lakh in non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 161.29 crore during the year.

The cost of materials consumed was the largest expense head, increasing 12.9% to Rs 64.15 crore from Rs 56.82 crore a year ago. Employee benefit expenses declined 8.5% to Rs 21.24 crore, while finance costs rose 26% to Rs 4.07 crore. Meanwhile, other expenses climbed 13.6% to Rs 101.68 crore.
Higher spending across key cost heads pushed the company’s total expenditure up 9.6% to Rs 194 crore in FY26 from Rs 177 crore in FY25.
The firm’s loss widened 48.7% to Rs 32.54 crore in FY26 from Rs 21.88 crore in the previous fiscal. Its EBITDA margin also weakened to -15.91%, compared with -9.66% a year earlier.

On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.20 to earn a rupee of operating revenue during FY26, up from Rs 1.15 in FY25. At the end of the fiscal year, it held Rs 4.09 crore in cash and bank balances, while its current assets stood at Rs 46 crore.

Emami completed the acquisition of a 100% stake in The Man Company in July 2024, seven years after making its first investment in the men’s grooming brand. The FMCG company acquired an initial 30% stake in 2017 and gradually increased its holding over the years. In 2022, it became the majority shareholder with a 50.4% stake before acquiring the remaining shares in July 2024 to take full ownership of the D2C brand.

title: M1xchange’s Mynd Fintech acquires C2FO India
description: C2FO India Technologies is a fintech company specializing in on demand working capital solutions and dynamic discounting for businesses. It operates as a subsidiary of
body: Supply chain financing platform Mynd Fintech, a subsidiary of M1xchange, has acquired fintech company C2FO India for an undisclosed amount.

As part of the acquisition, around 100 employees and 140 clients of C2FO India will become part of Mynd Fintech’s operations. The combined entity will process Rs 60,000 crore worth of transactions annually across the buy and sell sides.

M1xchange is an RBI licensed TReDS (Trade Receivables Discounting System) platform. C2FO operates C2TReDS and also holds the same licence, which it may surrender after the acquisition. The deal will allow Mynd Fintech to operate C2FO India’s platform while also adding its employees and clients.

C2FO India Technologies is a fintech company specializing in on demand working capital solutions and dynamic discounting for businesses. It operates as a subsidiary of the US based C2FO, accelerating invoice payments for suppliers in over 180 countries.

The C2FO India marketplace allows vendors to access low cost capital and receive early invoice payments without complex paperwork or hidden fees. The company serves around 50% of the Nifty50 companies and supports the supply chain financing requirements of around 200,000 suppliers across sectors such as cement, pharmaceuticals, and others.

Mynd Fintech is a Gurugram based digital lending marketplace specializing in supply chain finance (SCF). As part of the Mynd Group and powered by the RBI licensed TReDS platform M1xchange, it provides automated, off balance sheet, and unsecured working capital solutions.

title: Kissht parent crosses Rs 8,000 Cr AUM in Q1 FY27; loan disbursements rise 37%
description: OnEMI Technologies, the parent of Kissht and RING, reported strong business momentum in Q1 FY27, with AUM crossing Rs 8,000 crore and loan disbursements rising sharply year-on-year.
body: OnEMi Technologies Pvt Ltd, the parent company of digital lending brands Kissht and RING, reported strong business momentum in the first quarter of FY27, with its assets under management (AUM) crossing the Rs 8,000 crore mark and loan disbursements posting healthy year-on-year growth, according to the company's provisional business update on NSE.

The Mumbai-based company’s assets under management (AUM) grew 61% to approximately Rs 8,001 crore as of June 30, 2026, from Rs 4,972 crore a year earlier. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, AUM rose 13.2% during the June quarter.
Kissht disbursed loans worth nearly Rs 3,812 crore during Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 2,780 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The growth stood at 37.1% year-on-year.

The company also continued to expand its customer base. Its registered users rose 33% year-on-year to 74.6 million, while cumulative customers served increased 26.4% to 12.25 million. During the quarter, the company added around 0.5 million customers.

Kissht also continued to diversify its loan book. Its Loan Against Property (LAP) portfolio accounted for 7.7% of the overall AUM at the end of June 2026, up from 2.5% a year ago and 7.3% at the end of March 2026.
The company said the disclosed figures are provisional and remain subject to review by its statutory auditors.
In the fourth quarter, the company reported a 68% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 619 crore , while profit rose 52% to Rs 82 crore during the quarter.
For the full fiscal year FY26, operating revenue climbed 63% to Rs 2,179 crore from Rs 1,337 crore in FY25, while profit surged nearly 75% to Rs 281.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [June 29 - July 04]
description: This week, 25 Indian startups raised nearly $137 million across 5 growth-stage and 19 early-stage deals, while a startup kept its funding undisclosed. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 25 Indian startups raised nearly $137 million across 5 growth-stage and 19 early-stage deals, while a startup kept its funding undisclosed. The week also witnessed four acquisitions, three key leadership appointments, 2 fund launches, and the shutdown of a platform.
In contrast, 20 startups had collectively secured about $1.1 billion in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised a total of $68.1 million across five deals this week, led by lab-grown diamond jewellery brand Limelight Diamonds, which secured Rs 275 crore in a strategic funding round led by the Bhathwari Group.

Managed workspace provider Incuspaze raised Rs 150 crore (around $15.6 million) from Bharat Value Fund, while agentic AI platform Kapture CX secured $10 million in a pre-Series B round led by Bajaj Finserv Ventures.

At-home elder care startup Age Care Labs raised Rs 85 crore (around $9 million) from Rainmatter, Pegasus Finvest, the Shrem Group, and several family offices. Meanwhile, fresh produce supply chain startup Ninjacart closed a $6 million funding round after a gap of 4.5 years.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $68.92 million across 19 deals this week, led by toxin-free cookware brand The Indus Valley, which secured $17 million in a funding round led by Gaja Capital with participation from DSG Consumer Partners.

title: Info Edge takes full control of Coding Ninjas after acquiring remaining 45.36% stake
description: Info Edge has approved the acquisition of the remaining 45.36% stake in Coding Ninjas from the edtech platform's founders for about Rs 39.91 crore.
body: Info Edge has approved the acquisition of the remaining 45.36% stake in Coding Ninjas from the edtech platform's founders for about Rs 39.91 crore, a move that will make the company a wholly owned subsidiary. The decision was approved by the board at its meeting held on July 6.
The Naukri parent will acquire 74,741 equity shares of Sunrise Mentors Private Limited, which operates Coding Ninjas, at Rs 5,340.23 per share. The transaction is expected to close within 45 days.

Info Edge will pay 25% of the consideration, or about Rs 9.98 crore, at the closing of the share purchase agreement, while the remaining Rs 29.93 crore will be paid in three equal tranches on March 31, 2027, March 31, 2028 and March 31, 2029.

The company said that the acquisition is aimed at deepening synergies between Naukri and Coding Ninjas, while enabling Naukri to build mini AI course offerings for its users. As part of the arrangement, the founders of Coding Ninjas will join Info Edge and receive salary and performance linked incentives.

In October 2022, the company invested Rs 135.4 crore (around $17 million) to increase its stake in the startup from 26% to 51%. It has subsequently raised its ownership through follow on transactions, and the current acquisition will take its holding to 100%.

Founded in 2016, Coding Ninjas offers online coding and upskilling courses. The company reported revenue of Rs 97.43 crore in FY26 from Rs 67.15 crore in FY25 and Rs 53.31 crore in FY24. It posted a net loss of Rs 13.36 crore in FY26, while its net worth stood at negative Rs 34.98 crore as of March 31, 2026.

Separately, Info Edge's board also approved an additional commitment of up to Rs 180 crore to B8 Fund I, a Category II Alternative Investment Fund managed by its wholly owned subsidiary Smartweb Internet Services. The fresh commitment is over and above the Rs 250 crore approved earlier this year.

Coding Ninjas joins Zwayam, DoSelect and Highorbit Careers, the parent of iimjobs and hirist, among startups that have come under Info Edge's full ownership. Unlike those deals, Info Edge increased its stake in Coding Ninjas over multiple investment rounds before taking full ownership.

title: Rentomojo gets SEBI nod for IPO with Rs 150 Cr fresh issue
description: Furniture and appliance rental platform Rentomojo has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its IPO.
body: Furniture and appliance rental platform Rentomojo has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO), moving a step closer to its public market debut.

According to the company's draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), the IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 28.4 million equity shares by existing shareholders. Geetansh Bamania is the promoter of the company.
The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to repay or prepay certain borrowings, pay lease rentals and licence fees for warehouses and experience stores, and for general corporate purposes.

The SEBI observations come months after Rentomojo's IPO plans faced a legal hurdle. In March this year, former co-founder Ajay Nain had approached the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), seeking to halt the proposed IPO . According to the company's DRHP, Nain filed a petition before the Bengaluru bench against the company, its promoter, directors, chief financial officer, RM Employee Benefit Trust and others.

Founded in 2014, Rentomojo operates a technology driven direct to consumer rental and subscription platform for furniture and home appliances. As of September 30, 2025, it served 227,511 live subscribers across 22 cities through 67 experience stores, 21 warehouses, and a portfolio of 728,773 live products.

Citing a Redseer report, the company said it held an estimated 42% to 47% share of the organised home furniture and appliances rental market, excluding water purifiers, based on subscription revenue in fiscal 2025.

For the six months ended September 30, 2025, Rentomojo reported revenue from operations of Rs 176.61 crore and a profit after tax of Rs 61.38 crore. In fiscal 2025, the company posted revenue of Rs 265.96 crore and a profit after tax of Rs 43.11 crore.
Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Axis Capital, and IIFL Capital Services are the book running lead managers to the issue. The company's equity shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE.

title: EV fleet startup TOCAL secures Rs 9 Cr in seed round
description: Over the next four to five years, TOCAL aims to expand to more than 15 cities, deploy over 20,000 electric vehicles, operate 75 fulfillment centres, and partner with mo
body: EV fleet and fulfillment infrastructure company TOCAL has raised Rs 9 crore in a seed funding round led by XB Group, the parent group of K-Indev Logistics, with participation from Navyug Global Ventures and Nivetha Muralidharan.

The proceeds will be used to expand operations, establish strategically located fulfillment centres, scale its EV fleet and operational infrastructure, enhance fleet, warehouse and order management technology, and strengthen enterprise sales and strategic partnerships, TOCAL said in a press release.

Launched in 2021 by Dhairyasheel Deshmukh and Hidayathulla Shareef, TOCAL is a technology driven EV fleet and fulfillment infrastructure company enabling sustainable commerce through EV powered last mile delivery, fulfillment centres, and fleet management technology. The company is building an integrated logistics platform that helps businesses deliver faster, operate more efficiently, and reduce their carbon footprint.

As businesses seek faster fulfillment, more efficient deliveries, and sustainable logistics solutions, the Bengaluru based startup addresses these evolving needs through its integrated technology platform, which combines EV powered delivery services, fulfillment centres, fleet management software, and rider enablement into a single ecosystem. This enables brands to simplify their supply chain operations while improving efficiency, scalability, and sustainability.
Over the next four to five years, TOCAL aims to expand to more than 15 cities, deploy over 20,000 electric vehicles, operate 75 fulfillment centres, and partner with more than 1,000 brands.
It competes with notable players in the segment such as Zypp Electric, Shadowfax, LoadShare Networks, and Fyn Mobility.

title: Next Bharat Ventures launches Rs 2,000 Cr impact fund with Suzuki as anchor investor
description: Next Bharat Ventures (NBV) has launched its second venture fund with a corpus of Rs 2,000 crore. The fund will be anchored by Suzuki Motor Corporation and will focus. Snippets
body: Next Bharat Ventures (NBV) has launched its second venture fund with a corpus of Rs 2,000 crore.

The fund will be anchored by Suzuki Motor Corporation and will focus on backing startups working in sectors such as agriculture, rural supply chains, financial inclusion, healthcare, rural mobility and AI for social good.

The new fund follows NBV’s first Rs 340 crore fund, through which the firm invested in more than 20 startups and supported over 50 impact-focused ventures through funding, mentorship and ecosystem initiatives.

Founded in 2024, Next Bharat Ventures focuses on entrepreneurs building businesses that address challenges in rural India and underserved communities. The firm said the second fund will help expand support for startups working to improve livelihoods, access to services and economic opportunities across the country.

According to founder and CEO Vipul Jindal Nath, more than 90% of the firm’s portfolio companies are moving towards profitability in their early years. He added that the fund aims to back founders creating both business value and social impact.
Apart from capital, NBV provides founders with mentorship, market access and networking opportunities through its residency programme and founder community initiatives.

The firm's portfolio includes startups such as MeMeraki, E-Bik, SGB Agro and Atypical Advantage. With the new fund, NBV plans to increase investments in startups building solutions for rural and informal economies across India.

title: ekincare acquires claims adjudication SaaS platform Superclaims
description: The acquisition is expected to unlock new growth opportunities by expanding ekincare's presence across insurers and TPAs, increasing wallet share within its existing en
body: Digital health platform ekincare has acquired AI powered claims adjudication SaaS platform Superclaims.

As part of the acquisition, Bhavish Ramaswamy, cofounder and CEO of Superclaims, and Maneesh Daithala, cofounder and CTO, along with the leadership team, will continue in their respective roles and report to the senior leadership at ekincare.
The Superclaims brand will continue to operate independently while benefiting from ekincare's broader platform and distribution network.

The acquisition is expected to unlock new growth opportunities by expanding ekincare's presence across insurers and TPAs, increasing wallet share within its existing enterprise customer base, and creating cross sell opportunities across both businesses. It also positions ekincare and Superclaims to expand beyond India as an AI powered SaaS platform for insurance companies globally.

Co-founded in 2014 by Kiran Kalakuntla and Srikanth Samudrala, ekincare is a personalized, full stack, customizable health benefits platform that helps employers design health benefits packages that best suit the needs of employees and their families.

The Hyderabad-based company raised $15 million in its Series B round led by HealthQuad and Sabre Partners, with participation from existing investors Ventureast, Eight Roads Ventures, Siana Capital, and Endiya Partners in March 2022.

ekincare claims that it serves 2 million employees across more than 1,000 organizations, including Fortune 500 companies such as PepsiCo, BlackRock, and Visa. It also has a network of more than 90,000 healthcare providers across over 500 cities.

Superclaims is an AI powered claims adjudication SaaS platform that integrates directly with an insurer's or TPA's existing workflow. It automates one of healthcare's most document heavy and error prone processes.

title: Exclusive: Wow! Momo to raise $20 Mn debt led by InCred
description: Wow! Momo is all set to raise Rs 185 crore ($20 million) in debt funding from InCred Credit Opportunities, RevX Capital Fund, and Anicut Capital, its second debt raise this year.
body: Quick-service restaurant chain Wow! Momo is all set to raise Rs 185 crore ($20 million) in debt funding from InCred Credit Opportunities, RevX Capital Fund, and Anicut Capital, its second debt raise this year.
Earlier this year in April, Wow! Momo secured Rs 110 crore debt from Anicut Capital, which was exclusively reported by Entrackr.

The company’s board approved the issuance of 18,500 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) across multiple filings to raise the above-mentioned sum, according to its filings with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

As per the filings, InCred Credit Opportunities will lead the debt round with an investment of Rs 125 crore, followed by RevX Capital Fund with Rs 40 crore, while Anicut Capital contributed the remaining Rs 20 crore, taking the total debt infusion to Rs 185 crore.
The proceeds from the proposed debt round will be utilised towards refinancing existing borrowings, meeting general corporate requirements, and funding the company’s growth capital needs.

Founded in 2008 by Sagar Daryani and Binod Homagai, Wow! Momo operates more than 850 outlets across 90+ cities. Its portfolio includes brands such as Wow! Momo, Wow! China, Wow! Chicken, and Wow! Kulfi.
As per its last funding round, the company was valued at around Rs 2,838 crore ($316 million) on a post-money basis.
The company has raised over $140 million prior to this funding. This includes a $42 million Series D round led by Khazanah Nasional in January 2024.

title: Nikhil Kamath’s WTF acquires creative agency BTG
description: Nikhil Kamath-led WTF has acquired Mumbai-based creative agency BTG (By The Gram), marking its second acquisition in the creative services. Snippets
body: Nikhil Kamath-led WTF has acquired Mumbai-based creative agency BTG (By The Gram), marking its second acquisition in the creative services space after One Hand Clap (OHC).

Founded in 2018 by Aaliya Amrin, Eman Batliwalla and Danisha Kohli, BTG will continue to operate independently under its existing leadership. The founders and current team will retain operational and creative control of the agency.

As part of the deal, BTG will gain access to capital, WTF’s network and its distribution infrastructure. The acquisition is expected to help the agency pursue larger client mandates and expand its business.

BTG works with brands including Netflix, Prime Video, IKEA, Volkswagen, Bumble, Soho House, Marriott and Nykaa. The agency provides strategy and creative services across sectors such as beauty, hospitality, entertainment, technology, tourism and consumer brands.

The acquisition comes amid increasing investor interest in founder-led creative agencies. Through the acquisitions of OHC and BTG, WTF is building a portfolio of creative businesses focused on branding, content and strategy.
Going forward, BTG plans to focus on deeper client relationships, investment in owned content and intellectual property, and expansion of its senior leadership team.

title: AscentHR acquires OS HRS to expand APAC payroll footprint
description: AscentHR, a provider of HR, payroll, compliance, and workforce solutions, has acquired OS HRS for an undisclosed amount to expand its payroll operations across. Snippets
body: AscentHR, a provider of HR, payroll, compliance, and workforce solutions, has acquired OS HRS for an undisclosed amount to expand its payroll operations across the Asia Pacific and Middle East regions.
The deal was completed in June 2026 through the acquisition of 100% equity in OS HRS Malaysia, OS HRS Japan, and OS HRS India from BREXA Inc.

With this acquisition, AscentHR will increase its presence in markets including India, Japan, China, Malaysia, Singapore, and Korea. The combined company will provide payroll, compliance, and workforce management services to businesses operating across multiple countries.

According to AscentHR, the acquisition is expected to nearly double its revenue and expand its customer base across the region. The deal will help it strengthen payroll delivery and compliance support for multinational and regional businesses.

OS HRS provides payroll outsourcing services through its operations in Malaysia, Japan, and India. Its services include payroll processing, statutory compliance, reporting, and regulatory management. The company serves multinational businesses, including Fortune 500 firms.

Following the acquisition, the combined organization plans to offer multi-country payroll services through a single operating model. It will also provide local compliance support, integration with HRMS platforms, payroll implementation services, and country-specific support.

title: Nykaa projects around 30% revenue growth in Q1 FY27
description: FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of Nykaa, expects its consolidated net revenue to grow by around 30% year-on-year in the quarter ended June 2026.
body: FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, expects to report one of its strongest quarterly performances in recent years, with consolidated net revenue projected to grow close to 30% year-on-year in the quarter ended June 2026.

According to the company's quarterly business update, both Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) and Net Sales Value (NSV) are expected to grow in the early thirties, led by a sharp recovery in the fashion business and continued momentum in its core beauty segment.

According to the update, Nykaa's beauty vertical is expected to post NSV and net revenue growth in the late twenties. The company said its omnichannel beauty business continued the strong momentum seen in the previous quarter, aided by healthy store expansion and customer acquisition.
Its offline network expanded to 324 stores as of June-end, while owned brands such as Kay Beauty, Nykaa Cosmetics and Dot & Key continued to witness rapid growth.

The fashion vertical is expected to record NSV growth in the mid-fifties, a sharp acceleration from previous quarters. The company attributed the improvement to lower leakages between GMV and NSV, wider brand assortment and sustained marketing investments that helped drive customer acquisition across women, men, kids and home categories. Its partnership with Nike also delivered encouraging early results, strengthening its premium brand portfolio.

The update indicates that Nykaa's fashion business is growing strongly again after slowing down over the past few quarters. Investors will now wait for the company's detailed quarterly results to see whether this growth has also helped improve margins and profits, and what the management expects for the rest of FY27.
After the update, Nykaa’s share price is currently trading at Rs 317.35 (as of 10.07 AM) with a total market capitalization of Rs 90,883 crore.
