title: Nazara gets NCLT approval to withdraw Paper Boat Apps merger
description: Nazara Technologies has withdrawn the proposed merger of its wholly owned subsidiary, Paper Boat Apps Private Limited, after the National Company Law Tribunal
body: Gaming company Nazara Technologies has withdrawn the proposed merger of its wholly owned subsidiary, Paper Boat Apps Private Limited, after the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) approved the company's request to withdraw the scheme.

In a stock exchange filing on Tuesday, the company said the NCLT has allowed its application to withdraw the Scheme of Amalgamation. Nazara's board had approved the withdrawal of the merger proposal in May 2026 due to changes in the company's restructuring plans.

Nazara first acquired a 50.91% stake in Paper Boat Apps in 2019. In July 2024, it bought the remaining 48.42% stake from promoters Anupam and Anshu Dhanuka for Rs 300 crore, making Paper Boat Apps its wholly owned subsidiary.

Founded by PR Rajendran, R Kalpana, and PR Jayashree, Paper Boat Apps develops and publishes Kiddopia, a subscription-based digital learning app for children aged two to seven years. The app derives a majority of its revenue from the US market.
According to the NCLT order dated June 18, 2026, the tribunal allowed the company's application to withdraw the merger scheme and dismissed the application as withdrawn.
The withdrawal comes after Nazara announced plans to sharpen its focus on core gaming and divest non-core businesses such as esports and adtech.

title: CCI approves upGrad's acquisition of Unacademy
description: Ronnie Screwvala-led upGrad has received approval from the Competition Commission of India (CCI) for its proposed acquisition of edtech unicorn Unacademy.
body: Ronnie Screwvala-led upGrad has received approval from the Competition Commission of India (CCI) for its proposed acquisition of edtech unicorn Unacademy.

According to a release issued by the competition watchdog on Tuesday, the regulator approved the acquisition of certain shareholding in Sorting Hat Technologies Private Limited and its subsequent merger with and into upGrad Education Private Limited.

The approval comes nearly two months after upGrad filed a merger application with the CCI for the proposed transaction. In March this year, the company signed a term sheet to acquire Unacademy in a deal valued at around Rs 2,055 crore (approximately $218 million).

In May, upGrad was valued at around $1.73 billion after raising Rs 361 crore (around $38 million) in a funding round led by co-founder and chairman Ronnie Screwvala. Existing investors Temasek, International Finance Corporation (IFC), and 360 ONE Opportunities Fund also participated in the round.

upGrad posted a provisional profit after tax of Rs 38.8 crore during the 11 month period ended February 2026, compared to a loss of Rs 273.7 crore in FY25. The company also turned EBITDA positive at Rs 56.9 crore from a negative Rs 65.4 crore in the previous fiscal, while revenue from operations stood at Rs 1,531.7 crore during the period.

Founded in 2015, upGrad is a higher education and upskilling platform, while Unacademy is an online learning company focused on test preparation and professional education. The transaction is expected to create India's first combination of two edtech unicorns.

title: Alchemic raises Rs 2.5 Cr pre-seed round led by AJVC
description: Bengaluru-based AI startup Alchemic has raised Rs 2.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by AJVC, with participation from angel investors. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based AI startup Alchemic has raised Rs 2.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by AJVC, with participation from angel investors.
The fresh capital will be used to enhance its AI platform, expand its engineering and commercial teams, and increase enterprise adoption.

Founded in 2025 by Sreenadh Narayanan and Maurice Dhara, Alchemic develops AI agents for customer research. Its platform automates the customer-insights process, covering interviews, analysis and reporting, tasks that are traditionally handled by research teams.

According to the company, its AI can conduct interviews with hundreds of customers simultaneously and generate reports backed by video clips and customer quotes within hours. The platform is available as both a research service and an enterprise integration product.

The company claims that its revenue has grown fivefold over the past six months. The startup operates in the AI-driven customer insights segment, where companies are using artificial intelligence to automate research and feedback collection. Global players in the space include Listen Labs, Outset, Conveo and Strella.

AJVC, an early-stage investment firm led by Aviral Bhatnagar, continues to expand its footprint across emerging startups in India. Its portfolio spans companies such as Bubble Me, Finanjo, Mindcase, Care Dale, HandyPanda, Multibagg AI, Nuyug, Mithila Foods, Jaagruk Bharat, TruFides AI, Chop Finance, Gaadi Mech, and Iztri.

title: Info Edge posts Rs 737 Q1 FY27 billings; Naukri contributes 75%
description: Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri, 99acres, Jeevansathi, and Shiksha, reported a steady start to FY27, with its standalone billings rising 14.4% year-on-year during the June quarter.
body: Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri, 99acres, Jeevansathi, and Shiksha, reported a steady start to FY27, with its standalone billings rising 14.4% year-on-year during the June quarter.

According to the company's quarterly business update, standalone billings increased to Rs 737 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 644.2 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company released the unaudited numbers ahead of its detailed quarterly financial results.

The recruitment solutions segment, which includes its flagship job marketplace Naukri, remained the largest contributor, accounting for 75% of total billings. Billings from the segment rose 17.5% to Rs 552.7 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 470.3 crore in the year-ago quarter.

The real estate vertical, 99acres contributed nearly 15% of total billings, with billings growing 16.6% to Rs 110.1 crore from Rs 94.4 crore a year earlier. Jeevansathi accounted for 5.37% of billings and posted a 14.1% increase to Rs 39.6 crore, compared to Rs 34.7 crore in Q1 FY26.
Shiksha remained the only business to report a decline, with its billings falling 22.8% to Rs 34.6 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 44.8 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Info Edge clarified that the reported figures are unaudited and have been disclosed ahead of its detailed financial results for Q1 FY27.

As of 1:30 PM, Info Edge shares surged 12.7% to around Rs 1,155 after the company announced the Rs 39.9 crore acquisition of the remaining 45% stake in Coding Ninjas, making the edtech platform its wholly owned subsidiary. At the prevailing market price, the company commanded a market capitalization of Rs 74,967 crore (around $7.9 billion).

title: Rainmatter leads Rs 40 Cr pre Series A round in Econovus Packaging
description: Econovus says its packaging solutions reduce logistics costs, improve container utilisation, and lower the carbon footprint of supply chains across the automotive,
body: Engineered sustainable packaging company Econovus Packaging has raised Rs 40 crore in a pre Series A funding round led by Rainmatter by Zerodha, with participation from Rockstud Capital.

The fresh funds will be used to expand into high growth sectors, extending its sustainable packaging platform across automotive, lithium ion batteries, solar infrastructure, steel, defence, and broader industrial supply chains, Econovus said in a press release.

Founded in January 2019 by Ramesh Prasad, Econovus provides bespoke end to end packaging and design solutions using its engineered, IP backed materials, space optimisation, and design to cost methodology to help customers reduce their packaging carbon footprint and total cost of ownership.

The Pune based company says its portfolio includes UN certified lithium ion battery packaging, heavy duty export packaging, returnable and expendable packaging, and automotive packaging across CKD, SKD, and CBU formats.

According to the Government of India, the country's engineering exports reached a record $122.43 billion, making the sector the largest contributor, accounting for nearly 28% of India's total merchandise exports. As cross border industrial supply chains expand, demand for high quality, internationally compliant, and sustainable packaging solutions is expected to grow.

Econovus says its packaging solutions reduce logistics costs, improve container utilisation, and lower the carbon footprint of supply chains across the automotive, electronics, clean energy, industrial machinery, and electrical equipment sectors.

title: Physical AI startup Mowito raises $3 Mn led by Version One Ventures
description: Industrial robots typically rely on rigid programming that can take days to configure and often needs to be rewritten whenever a product, process, or component changes.
body: Physical AI startup Mowito has raised $3 million in a pre seed funding round led by Version One Ventures, with participation from All In Capital, Unisol, iSeed, and angel investors including Soumith Chintala, Adarsh Kulkarni, Ashish Kulkarni, and Vaibhav Domkundwar of Better Capital.
The startup had previously secured $540K in an angel funding round.

The proceeds will be used to expand into the United States, strengthen its engineering and go to market teams, and scale deployments across automotive and electronics manufacturers, Mowito said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by Puru Rastogi, Adityanag Nagesh, and Safar V, Mowito develops Physical AI foundation models for industrial robot arms. Its software enables robots to learn manufacturing tasks directly from demonstrations instead of conventional programming, allowing manufacturers to deploy automation faster while using existing robotic hardware.

Industrial robots typically rely on rigid programming that can take days to configure and often needs to be rewritten whenever a product, process, or component changes. Mowito is developing Physical AI models that enable robots to learn directly from task demonstrations, reducing the need for traditional programming while maintaining the precision required for manufacturing applications.

According to the Bengaluru based startup, its technology is already being deployed in production environments. Its software powers robots operating on manufacturing lines at a Fortune 500 automotive company, supporting high precision assembly applications across the automotive and consumer electronics sectors.
Mowito competes with companies such as Cognex, Keyence, Omron, and Fanuc in the industrial automation and machine vision space.

title: Stylework raises $1 Mn in pre-Series B second close
description: Flexible workspace platform Stylework has raised $1 million in equity funding in the second close of its pre-Series B round, led by Auxano Capital. Snippets
body: Flexible workspace platform Stylework has raised $1 million in equity funding in the second close of its pre-Series B round, led by Auxano Capital. The round also saw participation from family offices, institutional investors and HNIs.

The latest investment follows the first close of the round backed by Equentis Angel Fund, Karekeba Ventures/Cogniphy AIF Fund, MoneyVyapaar and LetsVenture Fund, taking the total pre-Series B raise to over $3.5 million .
It has raised more than $6.5 million across four funding rounds to date.
The proceeds will be used to expand into tier I and tier II markets, strengthen its technology platform, and deepen enterprise partnerships.
Founded in 2016 by Spaarsh Khandelwaal, Stylework operates a platform that helps enterprises access and manage flexible workspaces across India.

Stylework currently connects businesses to more than 10,000 workspace centres across 125 cities. The company reported a GMV of over Rs 340 crore this year, with an annual net revenue run rate exceeding Rs 50 crore. It also claims that it has remained profitable for the second consecutive year, reporting over Rs 2 crore in profit.

Its offerings include coworking and managed office solutions, meeting room access, Flexipasses and multi-location workspace services. Through its SaaS platform, Flexboard and Stylework.ai, enterprises can manage occupancy, employee rostering, workspace budgets and access controls.

title: Cult.fit posts Rs 1,720 Cr revenue in FY26; turns EBITDA positive
description: Fitness tech company Cult.fit reported 41% year-on-year growth in FY26, with operating revenue crossing Rs 1,700 crore ahead of its planned IPO. The company also turned EBITDA positive during the fiscal.
body: Fitness tech company Cult.fit, after posting a strong 31% growth in FY25, delivered another solid performance in the fiscal year ended March 2026, with operating revenue rising 41% year-on-year to surpass the Rs 1,700 crore mark ahead of its planned stock market debut. The company also turned EBITDA positive during the period.
Cult.fit reported operating revenue of Rs 1,720 crore in FY26, up 41.4% from Rs 1,216 crore in FY25, according to the consolidated financial statements in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).

Fitness subscriptions, which include flagship offerings such as Cultpass, Cult.fit centres and platform services, remained the company's largest revenue source and contributed 64% of operating revenue. Revenue from this segment grew 31% year-on-year to Rs 1,104 crore in FY26.

Revenue from the sale of products, which include sportswear for men and women along with gym and fitness equipment, rose 60% to Rs 523 crore during the fiscal, while other operating income such as advertising income, royalty, center set up income and platform fees added another Rs 93 crore to the revenue.
Cult.fit also earned Rs 81 crore from other income, including interest on current investments and miscellaneous non-operating sources, which pushed its total revenue to Rs 1,802 crore in FY26.

On the expense side, cost of materials remained the company's largest expense, which rose 42% year-on-year to Rs 363 crore in FY26. It was followed by service costs, which primarily include payments to trainers and fitness instructors, increasing 37% to Rs 356 crore.

Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses declined 12% to Rs 305 crore from Rs 347 crore in FY25, largely due to a sharp fall in non-cash ESOP expenses, which dropped to Rs 22 crore from Rs 100 crore a year earlier.

Advertising and promotional expenses rose 15% to Rs 171 crore in FY26. Depreciation and amortisation expenses stood at Rs 227 crore, while legal and professional expenses and utility expenses came in at Rs 151 crore and Rs 156 crore, respectively.

title: Koo co-founder Mayank Bidawatka shuts down second startup PicSee, to return capital to investors
description: Koo co-founder Mayank Bidawatka has shut down his latest startup, PicSee, less than a year after its launch and will return the remaining capital to investors.
body: Koo co-founder Mayank Bidawatka has decided to shut down his latest startup, PicSee, less than a year after launching it, and will return the remaining capital to investors instead of pursuing another pivot.

According to a Moneycontrol report, Bidawatka informed investors that the company could not find a strong enough opportunity to continue building. Rather than spending the remaining funds on uncertain experiments, the startup has chosen to wind up operations and return the unused capital.

PicSee, an AI-powered photo-sharing app, was launched in October last year by Bidawatka and former Koo executive Sarthak Gupta under their venture studio, Billion Hearts. The startup had raised $4 million in seed funding from investors including General Catalyst, Blume Ventures, Peak XV Partners' Surge, Kae Capital, and several angel investors.
Entrackr has reached out to Bidawatka for more information.

The app was designed to solve a common problem in group events by using AI to help users find photos of themselves from large collections of images. However, the founders reportedly felt the product had not reached the level of conviction needed to build a large and sustainable business.

Returning capital to investors is relatively uncommon in the startup ecosystem, where founders often continue to pivot or deploy the remaining runway in search of a new growth opportunity. In PicSee's case, the founders chose to preserve the remaining cash rather than continue spending without a clear direction.

The development is another startup closure for Bidawatka after Koo, the Indian microblogging platform he co-founded, shut down last year following unsuccessful acquisition talks and mounting financial challenges
While the exact amount being returned to investors has not been disclosed. Neither Bidawatka nor PicSee has publicly shared further details on the shutdown or their future plans as of now.

title: Rewards platform Onpoint raises $600K in pre-seed round
description: Onpoint, a consumer rewards platform, has raised $600k in a pre-seed funding round co-led by First Cheque, an entity under IndiaQuotient, and Whiteboard Capital.
body: Onpoint, a consumer rewards platform, has raised $600k in a pre-seed funding round co-led by First Cheque, an entity under IndiaQuotient, and Whiteboard Capital.
The round also saw participation from several angel investors, including former directors from Meta and Google, as well as alumni of the Kellogg School of Management.

Founded in 2025 by former Meta employees Nakul Khanna and Anurag Gupta, Onpoint helps users earn rewards on everyday purchases across brands and merchants. The company said the fresh capital will be used to strengthen its product, expand its merchant network and grow its user base in India.

The platform operates through a payment-agnostic model, allowing users to earn rewards, known as Onpoints, when they purchase gift vouchers or shop with partner brands through its app, website or browser extension. These rewards can be earned irrespective of the payment method used and can be combined with existing credit card rewards and loyalty benefits.

Users can redeem Onpoints across travel and loyalty programs such as Air India’s Maharaja Club, IndiGo BluChip and Flipkart SuperCoins. The points can also be redeemed for gift cards from more than 300 brands, including Amazon Pay, Flipkart, Myntra and Uber.
The founding team brings experience from companies including Meta, Google, Uber and Zeta, with expertise across consumer technology, payments and platform engineering.

title: Piper Serica leads seed round in deep tech startup eNLife Research
description: eNLife says it is working with leading Indian research institutions to build a diagnostic platform designed specifically around Indian genetic and lifestyle risk profil
body: Deep tech startup eNLife Research has raised Rs 6 crore in a seed funding round led by Piper Serica VC Fund.

The proceeds will be deployed to build and validate its blood based biomarker platform, expand its Bengaluru based R&D team, and take its first diagnostic assay from prototype to clinical grade validation, eNLife said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2025 by Deepak Kumaran Nair, Jojo Jacob, and Anish Mathew, eNLife Research is a deep tech startup building affordable, AI powered diagnostic platforms to detect Alzheimer's and other neurodegenerative diseases years before clinical symptoms appear.
The Bengaluru based startup combines highly sensitive biomarker detection from accessible body fluids with machine learning to identify the earliest biological signatures of disease onset.

eNLife says it is working with leading Indian research institutions to build a diagnostic platform designed specifically around Indian genetic and lifestyle risk profiles, with the broader goal of making early neurodegenerative disease detection accessible, scalable, and affordable.

The startup is currently collaborating with researchers associated with leading institutions, including IISc, NIMHANS, TIFR Hyderabad, and CBR Bengaluru, to develop India specific biomarker datasets. It expects to begin filing patents over the next 9 to 18 months across biomarker binders, diagnostic assays, and its detection platform.

eNLife's test can be administered through routine diagnostic centres and is designed to deliver results within two to five hours. The company's AI engine is being trained to identify subtle correlations between these biomarkers, helping detect early signs of disease progression years before clinical symptoms emerge.

title: Voice AI platform Edysor.ai raises pre-seed round
description: Edysor's voice AI agents address the hassle of slow lead response where the average Indian business takes six to twelve hours to follow up on an inbound lead. The agen
body: Edysor.ai, a voice AI platform that deploys intelligent agents for enterprise lead conversion, has raised Rs 1.2 crore in a pre seed funding round led by angel investor Jasmine Sarupria.
The fresh funds will be used to accelerate product development, enhance AI capabilities, expand the customer base, grow the team, and scale operations, Edysor.ai said in a press release.

Co-founded in January 2020 by Atishaya Jain, Abhinav Jain, Gunjan Pancholi, and Fivos Radis, Edysor.ai is a voice AI platform that enables businesses to engage, qualify, follow up with, and convert leads through AI powered voice conversations.

The Udaipur based startup pivoted to AI in 2024 and now offers voice AI agents to enterprises across sectors such as real estate, BPO, D2C, automotive, edtech, healthcare, and BFSI. The platform follows an outcome based pricing model, charging businesses based on results rather than runtime.

According to the company, its voice AI agents are designed to reduce lead response time by calling potential customers within seconds of an inquiry, conducting adaptive conversations, qualifying prospects, handling objections, and moving leads through the sales funnel without human intervention.

Edysor.ai said it has added 15 enterprise customers in the two months since launching the platform, with two to three new customers joining every week, and recorded a 300% month on month increase in voice minute consumption. It also claims customers have reported a 15 to 20 times return on investment from AI powered sales qualification.

The startup said several clients are handling between 50,000 and 100,000 AI powered calls per month using its platform. It is currently deployed across real estate, BPO, D2C, automotive, edtech, healthcare, and BFSI, with customers including Chanakya University, Madanapalle Institute of Technology & Science, Global Tree, Ambuja, Rainmaker, Pyrotech, and PU Sterling College, among others.
According to a market report, the global conversational AI market is projected to exceed $50 billion by 2030.

title: Caret Capital leads $2.4 Mn seed round in Milo Drive
description: The Gurugram based startup claims to have powered more than one million rides since its launch. It uses data intelligence and machine learning led ride assignment to i
body: EV mobility platform Milo Drive has raised $2.4 million in a seed funding round led by Caret Capital, with participation from Antler India, Alteria Capital, IAN Capital, Climate Angels, Aureolis Capital, and other investors.
The proceeds will be used to support EV adoption and formalise employment opportunities for India’s driver workforce, Milo Drive said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Monil Jayeshkumar Khatri and Vishal Jewrajka, Milo Drive is building an asset light, technology led EV mobility platform for India’s ride hailing and urban transportation ecosystem. The company combines vehicle access, multi platform demand, charging intelligence, operator tools, and data driven automation to help drivers, fleet operators, and mobility entrepreneurs manage EV operations.

The Gurugram based startup claims to have powered more than one million rides since its launch. It uses data intelligence and machine learning led ride assignment to improve vehicle utilisation, driver earnings, and service reliability across demand channels.
According to market research cited by the company, India’s EV ride hailing market is projected to grow from $0.24 billion in 2025 to $4.2 billion by 2030, at a CAGR of 77%.

Milo Drive says its real time operating system provides live fleet visibility across thousands of vehicles, while AI driven charging recommendations, predictive maintenance alerts, and automated geofencing are designed to reduce operational downtime and driver idle time. The company adds that its driver app, which includes payment collections, charging guidance, and earnings tracking, has helped increase driver incomes by 20%.

title: Elevate Education raises Rs 170 Cr in Series D round from WestBridge Capital
description: Elevate Education, formerly known as Sunstone, has secured Rs 170 crore ($17.7 million) in Series D funding from WestBridge Capital. News.
body: Elevate Education, formerly known as Sunstone, has secured Rs 170 crore ($17.7 million) in Series D funding from WestBridge Capital.
Back in August 2022, Elevate had raised $35 million in a series C funding round led by WestBridge Capital with participation from existing investor Alteria Capital

The Gurugram-based higher education platform will use the funds to strengthen its technology and AI capabilities, expand its partner institution network, improve student outcomes, and invest in academic programmes aligned with industry requirements.

Founded by Ashish Munjal, Ankur Jain and Piyush Nangru, Elevate Education partners with colleges and universities to offer undergraduate and postgraduate programmes supported by technology, placement assistance and student success services.

The company currently supports more than 25,000 active students and works with 22 campuses across 15 cities. It expects to achieve revenue of Rs 300 crore in FY27 and reach profitability during the year.

Looking ahead, Elevate Education plans to expand its student base to 60,000 and increase its network to 40 partner institutions by FY29. The company is also investing in AI-driven solutions across the student lifecycle, including learning, career support and engagement.
With the latest funding, Elevate Education aims to strengthen its presence in the higher education ecosystem and expand access to industry-focused learning programmes across India.

title: Zostel seeks SEBI review of PRISM’s IPO filing over litigation disclosures
description: Zostel has approached the SEBI, urging the market regulator to examine disclosures made by Oravel Stays, the parent company of Oyo(PRISM) in its UDRHP.
body: Zostel has approached the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), urging the market regulator to examine disclosures made by Oravel Stays, the parent company of Oyo(PRISM), in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) filed for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
In a representation submitted on July 7, the company alleged that Oyo's IPO document presents an incomplete and selective account of the long-running legal dispute between the two firms.

Zostel has asked SEBI to examine whether the disclosures meet the standards of completeness, fairness and materiality prescribed under the SEBI Act and the ICDR Regulations before allowing the IPO process to move forward.

The company argued that the dispute is not an ordinary commercial case as it concerns Zostel's claim to around 7% equity in Oyo, or its corresponding economic value, arising from the failed acquisition deal between the two companies. It contended that the outcome of the litigation could have implications for Oyo's capital structure, valuation and investors' assessment of litigation risk, and therefore deserves more comprehensive disclosure in the IPO papers.

The dispute dates back to 2015, when Oyo signed a non-binding term sheet to acquire Zostel's business. In 2021, an arbitral tribunal ruled in Zostel's favour. However, the Delhi High Court later set aside the award, holding that the term sheet was non-binding and did not create enforceable rights. In July 2025, the Supreme Court refused to entertain Zostel's appeal against that order. Zostel, however, maintains that appellate proceedings arising from the dispute are still pending before the Delhi High Court and should be adequately reflected in Oyo's IPO disclosures.

In its representation, Zostel further alleged that the UDRHP understates the evidentiary record, selectively characterises the underlying transaction and does not sufficiently explain the commercial significance of the pending proceedings. It has requested SEBI to direct Oyo to make corrective or supplementary disclosures, ask the book-running lead managers to undertake further due diligence, and consider whether the IPO should progress only after the disclosure concerns have been addressed.
Entrackr has reached out to Oyo for more information.
Last month, the hospitality major filed an updated draft red herring prospectus with SEBI to raise Rs 6,650 crore through a fresh issue of shares, with no offer-for-sale component.

title: Doodhvale Farms raises $1 Mn from Atomic Capital
description: Doodhvale Farms, a direct-to-consumer dairy and daily essentials brand, has raised $1 million in a follow-on funding round from existing investor Atomic Capital Fund I. Snippets
body: Doodhvale Farms, a direct-to-consumer dairy and daily essentials brand, has raised $1 million in a follow-on funding round from existing investor Atomic Capital Fund I.
Prior to this round, Doodhvale had raised $3 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Atomic Capital and Singularity Early Opportunities Fund in November 2024.

The fresh capital will be used for market expansion, increasing distribution in existing markets, product development, and investments in AI and technology to improve demand forecasting and route optimization.

Founded by Aman J Jain, Doodhvale Farms operates a vertically integrated model and delivers dairy products and daily essentials directly to consumers. The firm currently serves customers across Delhi-NCR, Chandigarh, Ambala, Karnal and Meerut, while shipping products such as ghee and wood-pressed oils across India.

According to the company, its direct-to-consumer business nearly doubled over the past year, contributing to overall revenue growth of around 65%. D2C sales now account for nearly 90% of its revenue, while value-added products contribute about 35% of total revenue.
Doodhvale Farms has also expanded beyond milk and dairy products into protein-focused offerings and household staples including atta and wood-pressed oils.
Over the next 12 to 18 months, Doodhvale Farms aims to expand into more cities, strengthen its presence in existing markets and more than double its business.

title: Women's health brand Avni Wellness raises seed round
description: Women's health brand Avni Wellness has raised Rs 4 crore in a seed funding round led by Proteus Partners, with participation from Puru Gupta, Sreejith Moolayil, A. Velumani, and Somya Nigam.
body: Women's health brand Avni Wellness has raised Rs 4 crore in a seed funding round led by Proteus Partners, with participation from Puru Gupta, Sreejith Moolayil, A. Velumani, and Somya Nigam.

The proceeds will be used to strengthen its digital commerce engine, expand its cycle nutrition portfolio, scale its women-led micro entrepreneur network, and expand its marketplace presence, Avni Wellness said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2021 by Sujata Pawar and Apurv Agarwal, Avni Wellness is a science-backed, toxin-free, holistic cycle care brand built to address women's health across every phase of life, from adolescence to menopause.

The company operates at the intersection of women's health, livelihood, and sustainability, and aims to address overlooked gaps in India, including hormonal health, nutrition, and long-term well-being.
According to market research, the feminine hygiene products market is projected to reach Rs 70.20 billion by 2025.

According to the Mumbai-based startup, its portfolio includes a patented antimicrobial reusable pad and a liposomal iron supplement designed for better nutrient absorption to address widespread iron deficiency among Indian women. The brand also offers solutions for PCOS care, calcium support, UTI and vaginal health, and seed-based hormonal nutrition, creating a comprehensive lifecycle approach to women's health.
It competes in the broader women's wellness space alongside brands such as Pee Safe, Nua, and Plush.

title: Fundamentum launches third Series B fund with target corpus of Rs 2,200 Cr
description: Fundamentum, which focuses exclusively on Series B investments in India, is launching its third fund after its 2017 and 2022 vintages. Fund III continues the firm’s thes
body: Series B focused investment firm The Fundamentum Partnership has launched Fundamentum Fund III with a target corpus of Rs 2,200 crore, including a Rs 400 crore greenshoe option. The firm said cofounder Nandan Nilekani has made his largest investment in any venture capital firm as the fund’s anchor limited partner.

Fundamentum, which focuses exclusively on Series B investments in India, is launching its third fund after its 2017 and 2022 vintages. Fund III continues the firm’s thesis driven strategy of investing in early growth stage startups that have achieved product market fit and are preparing to scale.
Over the past decade, Fundamentum has backed companies including Kuku, Spinny, PharmEasy, AppsForBharat (Sri Mandir), and Stable Money.

Fund III will remain sector agnostic, with consumer technology, fintech, and AI native and AI enabled businesses as its primary focus areas. The fund plans to invest Rs 100 crore to Rs 150 crore per company on average.

Within consumer technology, the firm will continue to invest across digital commerce, content, healthcare, edtech, and emerging sectors. In fintech, it will focus on credit, savings, wealth management, insurance, and financial infrastructure. The fund will also evaluate AI native and AI enabled businesses as standalone investment themes as well as capabilities transforming sectors such as financial services and consumer technology.

Fund III will be led by Sanjeev Aggarwal, Prateek Jain, Mayank Kachhwaha, and CFO Sanjay Chaturvedi. According to the firm, Fund II has generated a gross IRR of 26%, while its portfolio companies recorded 123% growth over the past year.

Founded in 2017 by Nandan Nilekani and Sanjeev Aggarwal, Fundamentum typically leads or co leads funding rounds of $15 million to $40 million and invests in four to five startups annually. The firm focuses on technology driven startups across consumer internet, fintech, B2B commerce, enterprise technology, and AI native and AI enabled businesses.
Its portfolio includes companies such as Spinny, PharmEasy, Kuku, Wishlink, ProcMart, AppsForBharat, FlexiLoans, Apna Mart, Stable Money, TransBnk, and Olyv.

title: Mukesh Bansal’s Nurix AI acquires enterprise conversational AI company Verloop.io
description: Nurix, founded in 2024 by Mukesh Bansal, builds AI agents that help enterprises automate complex workflows and drive measurable business outcomes. Backed by
body: Nurix AI, an enterprise AI company building autonomous AI software and agents for complex business workflows, has acquired enterprise conversational AI company Verloop.io.

The acquisition builds on NuPlay, Nurix's flagship voice AI platform for customer engagement, and adds Verloop.io's chat automation expertise and regional customer base. It aims to expand Nurix's conversational AI capabilities across voice and chat for businesses in India and the Middle East.

With this acquisition, Nurix AI and Verloop.io are positioned to help enterprises deploy production grade AI agents across voice, chat, and emerging AI native channels, delivering measurable business outcomes at scale.

Nurix, founded in 2024 by Mukesh Bansal, builds AI agents that help enterprises automate complex workflows and drive measurable business outcomes. Backed by General Catalyst, Accel, and Prosus, the company has focused on helping enterprises move beyond AI pilots to production deployments that improve efficiency, reliability, and operational performance.
In September 2024, Nurix AI also secured $27.5 million in funding co-led by General Catalyst and Accel, with participation from Meraki Labs.

Founded by Gaurav Singh in 2015, Verloop.io built its business around helping enterprises automate customer conversations across digital channels in banking, fintech, retail, and telecommunications. As part of Nurix AI, Verloop.io's team and operations will support the company's expansion across chat led customer engagement use cases.

The acquisition expands Nurix's ability to support enterprises that need AI agents across both synchronous voice interactions and asynchronous chat led journeys. Following the transaction, Verloop.io will become part of Nurix AI. The companies are not disclosing further product integration plans at this time.
Verloop.io claims that it currently powers more than 20 million customer interactions every month.

title: IPV leads pre-seed round in space-tech startup BAAS Technologies
description: The Pune-based startup says it designs and develops its own solid and liquid rocket propulsion systems. Its upcoming 100 kN Rocket Propulsion Testing Facility will sup
body: Space-tech startup BAAS Technologies has raised Rs 5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures, with participation from SINE IIT Bombay and a group of private angel investors.

The proceeds will be utilized for R&D on liquid and solid propulsion systems, building a static test facility and manufacturing infrastructure, procuring equipment and raw materials, and expanding the engineering and operations team, BAAS Technologies said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by Tanmay Kanmahale, Prashant Patil, Atharva Pingale, Swayam Sonar, and Shriniwas Hase, BAAS Technologies is a space-tech company developing reusable sub-orbital and orbital launch vehicles. The company specializes in indigenous rocket propulsion systems, launch vehicle development, and affordable launch solutions for commercial, research, and government customers.

The Pune-based startup says it designs and develops its own solid and liquid rocket propulsion systems. Its upcoming 100 kN Rocket Propulsion Testing Facility will support static fire testing, engine validation, and commercialization as BAAS moves to its next stage of growth.
According to market research, India's domestic satellite launch services market is expected to grow from $399 million in 2025 to $1.58 billion by 2033, at a CAGR of 18.2%.
The startup says it has already completed paid pilot programs in India and is now expanding commercially into Latin America, the Middle East, Southeast Asia, and Australia.

title: Wealth-tech startup Fincart launches AI driven investment app
description: With the new app, the company aims to transition from a relationship driven advisory model to an AI led platform that provides personalised financial guidance to a wider
body: Financial planning and wealth management platform Fincart has launched a new version of its Fincart app.
The app offers financial planning tools with goal based investing and AI driven personalisation across mutual funds, digital gold, unlisted stocks and other investment products on a single platform.
According to the company, the app enables users to plan, invest, manage and track their finances independently, with features aligned to their financial goals.

Founded in 2013 by Tanwir Alam, Fincart Finvest is a technology enabled financial planning and wealth management platform. It offers services across financial and investment planning, wealth creation, retirement planning, tax optimisation and risk management.

With the new app, the company aims to transition from a relationship driven advisory model to an AI led platform that provides personalised financial guidance to a wider user base, irrespective of portfolio size.

The app categorises users into investor personas such as Explorer, Grower and Anchor based on their financial behaviour and goals. These profiles are used to personalise recommendations, including mutual fund suggestions and portfolio allocation.
The platform also offers investment options across mutual funds, digital gold, unlisted stocks, Portfolio Management Services (PMS) for larger portfolios, and health and term insurance.
Other features include budgeting tools, portfolio tracking, financial recommendations, external asset synchronisation, family account management, and AI based insights.

title: Physical AI startup Hakimo raises $12 Mn
description: Hakimo, an AI-powered physical security platform, has raised $12 million in a growth funding round led by existing investor Zigg Capital.
body: Hakimo, an AI-powered physical security platform, has raised $12 million in a growth funding round led by existing investor Zigg Capital. The round also saw participation from Neotribe Ventures, Vertex Ventures, Defy.vc and Rocketship.vc.
With this investment, the company’s total funding has reached $32 million.

The fresh capital will be used to accelerate product development, expand into new markets and industry segments, and grow the company’s team. Hakimo also plans to broaden its platform beyond security use cases into areas such as safety, compliance and customer experience.

Founded by Indian origin co-founders Sam Joseph, Sagar Honnungar and team, Hakimo develops AI-based security monitoring solutions that work with existing surveillance camera infrastructure. The platform uses computer vision and AI to detect incidents, monitor properties and support security operations in real time.

The firm claims that it has tripled its revenue over the past 12 months. This marks its third consecutive year of threefold revenue growth. During the same period, Hakimo expanded its customer base to more than 300 clients and doubled its workforce.

Hakimo serves a range of customers, including Fortune 500 companies, real estate operators and commercial properties. The company recently launched new features such as AI-powered forensic search, which helps users analyze security footage more efficiently.

According to Hakimo, its platform enables a single operator to monitor areas that would traditionally require multiple security personnel. Customers have reported reductions in security incidents and lower guard-related costs after deploying the platform.
Based in Menlo Park, California, Hakimo integrates with existing camera systems and provides AI-driven monitoring without requiring customers to replace their hardware infrastructure.

title: BlackSoil acquires Credit Fair’s solar financing business
description: Alternative credit platform BlackSoil has acquired the solar financing business of Credit Fair, for an undisclosed amount. Snippets
body: Alternative credit platform BlackSoil has acquired the solar financing business of Credit Fair, for an undisclosed amount.
As part of the deal, BlackSoil will acquire Credit Fair’s solar financing business, including its management team, technology platform, brand and operating infrastructure.

Credit Fair’s solar financing unit currently manages assets worth Rs 152.6 crore. The acquisition gives BlackSoil an established platform to finance residential solar projects and MSMEs adopting solar energy solutions.

Founded in 2018, Credit Fair operates a B2B2C lending model and has processed more than 3.5 lakh loans across over 20 states. The company has disbursed more than Rs 1,300 crore and works with solar ecosystem partners including Tata Power, Waaree, SolarSquare, UTL Solar, Livguard, Navitas and Adani Solar.

According to BlackSoil, the acquisition will strengthen its presence in the renewable energy value chain through a partner-led distribution network. The company plans to work with solar installation partners while offering financing solutions directly to customers.

Founded in 2016, BlackSoil operates an RBI-registered NBFC and a SEBI-registered AIF. The company manages assets worth around $275 million and provides credit solutions to startups, MSMEs and other businesses.

title: Exclusive: WizCommerce raises $8.3 Mn from Blume, Alpha Wave, Peak XV and others
description: WizCommerce has raised Rs 79.5 crore ($8.3 million) in a fresh funding round from existing investors Blume Ventures, Alpha Wave, Z47, 100X VC, and Peak XV Partners.
body: WizCommerce, an AI-native sales and ecommerce platform for wholesale distributors, has raised Rs 79.5 crore (around $8.3 million) in a fresh funding round from existing investors Blume Ventures, Alpha Wave, Z47, 100X VC, and Peak XV Partners.
The fresh capital comes less than a year after WizCommerce raised $8 million in its Series A round led by Peak XV Partners in August 2025.
The Wizcommerce’s board allotted 7,565 Bridge CCPS at an issue price of Rs 1,05,051 each to raise the above-mentioned amount, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) .

Blume Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 28.72 crore (around $3 million), followed by Alpha Wave, which infused Rs 23.94 crore. Peak XV Partners and Z47 invested Rs 14.36 crore and Rs 7.65 crore, respectively, while 100X.VC contributed Rs 4.79 crore.

According to Entrackr’s estimates, the firm’s valuation stands at Rs 443 crore or $46.6 million post-money, compared to Rs 333 crore in the previous $8 million Series A round. The company may raise more funds in the latest round.

Founded by former Bessemer Venture Partners and EY-Parthenon executive Divyaanshu Makkar and ex-Zomato executive Vikas Garg, WizCommerce offers an AI-native SaaS platform for wholesale distributors. The company follows a subscription and transaction-based revenue model, earning from its AI-powered sales tools, transaction facilitation, and value-added services.

Following the allotment, Blume Ventures emerged as the largest external shareholder with a 17.49% stake, followed by Peak XV Partners at 15.57%. Alpha Wave and Z47 held 14.85% and 10.38%, respectively, while 100X.VC owned 2.61%.

While the Bengaluru-based startup is yet to file its FY26 financials, its India entity reported Rs 6.15 crore in operating revenue and a net loss of Rs 17.36 crore in FY25, according to consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). The figures reflect only its India operations and may not represent the company's overall business, as a significant portion of its revenue is generated from the US.

title: Honasa expects double-digit margins, 30% revenue growth in Q1 FY27
description: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, expects a strong start to FY27, with revenue likely to grow around 30% year-on-year in the first quarter.
body: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, expects a strong start to FY27, with revenue likely to grow around 30% year-on-year in the first quarter, led by good demand across its brands and continued momentum in offline channels.

In a quarterly business update released on Thursday, the company said its reported revenue growth is expected to be in the mid-twenties after adjusting for a change in revenue recognition related to the Flipkart group. The company clarified that the adjustment is linked to changes in settlement practices for marketplace sellers.

Honasa's flagship brand, Mamaearth, is expected to post high-teen year-on-year growth during the quarter. The company attributed the performance to improving consumer demand and stronger offline distribution.
Its younger brands, including The Derma Co., Aqualogica, BBlunt, Dr. Sheth's, Staze, Lumineve and Reginald Men are expected to continue their strong run, with growth projected in the early forties.

The offline business remained the key growth driver during the quarter, supported by stronger general trade distribution, better in-store execution across modern trade, and expanding direct reach. The online channel is also expected to record healthy growth, according to the company.
On profitability, Honasa said it expects to maintain a double-digit operating margin in Q1 FY27, aided by operating leverage as the business scales.

The company noted that the update is provisional and does not constitute its financial results or formal earnings guidance. Detailed financial results will be announced after the board approves the company's Q1 FY27 financial statements.
Honasa's shares were trading at Rs 467.25 at 10:03 AM on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalisation of around Rs 15,250 crore.

title: Zetwerk secures SEBI approval for IPO
description: Bengaluru based manufacturing platform Zetwerk has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO). Snippets
body: Bengaluru based manufacturing platform Zetwerk has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO), according to sources aware of the development.

The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a mix of a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale by existing investors. The final issue size and valuation will be determined through the book building process.

Founded in 2018 by Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Zetwerk operates a technology driven manufacturing platform that connects industrial customers with a network of suppliers and manufacturing facilities. The company serves sectors including energy, electronics, defence, aerospace, capital goods, industrial supply, and raw materials.
Its proprietary software platform, Zetwerk OS, is used to manage sourcing, production planning, supplier coordination, and project execution across its manufacturing network.

Zetwerk has expanded through a combination of owned manufacturing facilities and a global third party supplier network. The company has also benefited from increasing manufacturing demand driven by supply chain diversification beyond China, infrastructure and data centre investments, the energy transition, and India’s push for domestic manufacturing.
The company is backed by investors including Khosla Ventures, Baillie Gifford, Rakesh Gangwal, Accel, Peak XV, GreenOak, and Lightspeed.
Entrackr has reached out to Zetwerk for comments. The story will be updated if the company responds.

title: Aukera raises Rs 90 Cr in fresh funding led by Alteria Capital
description: Lab-grown diamond jewellery brand Aukera has raised Rs 90 crore (over $10 million) in a funding round led by existing investor Alteria Capital. News
body: Lab-grown diamond jewellery brand Aukera has raised Rs 90 crore (over $10 million) in a funding round led by existing investor Alteria Capital. The round also saw participation from InnoVen Capital, Lighthouse Canton and a bank.

The fundraise comes less than a year after the company secured $15 million in an equity round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Fireside Ventures, Sparrow Capital, Prath Ventures and Alteria Capital.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its store network, strengthen its omnichannel operations, and invest in product development and talent.
Founded in 2023 by Lisa Mukhedkar and Kumar Saurabh, Aukera sells lab-grown diamond jewellery through company-owned retail stores.

Over the past year, Aukera has expanded its retail footprint from 13 stores to 35 stores. The company has entered new markets including Pune, Lucknow, Dehradun and Visakhapatnam, in addition to its presence in Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Delhi NCR.
According to the company, the expansion has helped it establish a presence across multiple cities as demand for lab-grown diamond jewellery continues to grow in India.
The company is backed by investors including Peak XV Partners, Fireside Ventures, Sparrow Capital, Prath Ventures and Alteria Capital.

title: thumpN raises $3.75 Mn in pre-seed round
description: Behind it is a network of contributing curators - artists, promoters, venue insiders, and genre specialists embedded across cities, whose on-the-ground signals continuo
body: thumpN, a discovery and ticketing platform for live entertainment, has raised over $3.75 million in a pre-seed funding round from bollywood musicians such as Arijit Singh, Sunidhi Chauhan, and Badshah, alongside Paytm founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma, Madhur Deora, Shray Chandra, and VG Jairam.
The proceeds will be used to expand its AI-native live entertainment platform, thumpN said in a press release.

Founded in 2025 by Varun Khare, thumpN is an AI-native discovery and ticketing platform that unifies discovery, ticketing, and on-ground tools for fans, artists, venues, and promoters. Its conversational AI agent, Shadow, is backed by a network of co-curators - genre specialists, venue insiders, and city-embedded tastemakers.

At the centre of the platform is Shadow , thumpN's conversational AI agent designed to help fans find highly contextual live experiences through natural conversation rather than traditional search. Shadow understands intent, maintains conversational context, and reasons across events from multiple sources.

Behind it is a network of contributing curators - artists, promoters, venue insiders, and genre specialists embedded across cities, whose on-the-ground signals continuously sharpen Shadow's taste. The result is recommendations that carry both AI precision and human cultural instinct, growing more personalised with every interaction.

The platform also simplifies life for organisers, artists, venues, and promoters through AI-native onboarding and partner-first infrastructure, giving them sharper insights into their audiences and stronger tools to plan, market, and scale their events.
thumpN launches with a growing pipeline of live experiences across a broad mix of music, theatre, comedy, festivals, nightlife, sports, and community-led experiences.

title: Dhan parent Raise Financial to rebrand insurance arm GIBL as Pluto Insurance
description: Raise Financial Services, the parent company of stock broking platform Dhan, has rebranded GreenLife Insurance Broking Pvt Ltd (GIBL). Exclusive
body: Raise Financial Services, the parent company of stock broking platform Dhan, has rebranded GreenLife Insurance Broking Pvt Ltd (GIBL), the insurance broker it acquired in May this year, as Pluto Insurance, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The move comes as the company doubles down on the insurance distribution space and prepares to invest Rs 100 crore in the newly rebranded entity. The investment aligns with Raise’s earlier commitment to invest $15 million in the insurance business following the acquisition.

Raise had acquired the IRDAI registered insurance broker in an all cash and stock deal for an undisclosed amount. At the time, the company had said the acquisition would help it build a consumer focused insurance distribution platform with an emphasis on technology, product innovation, and customer experience.

Founded in 2013 by Subir Mukherjee, GIBL operated across more than 50 cities and towns in East and North East India through an offline distribution network, working with over 60 insurers across life, health, motor, and travel insurance segments.
With the rebranding, Pluto.hq will spearhead Raise’s insurance ambitions and operate as its dedicated insurance platform.
Led by Pravin Jadhav, Raise operates platforms including Dhan, Upsurge, Fuzz AI, ScanX, and Stratzy. The company is backed by investors such as Hornbill Capital, MUFG, BEENEXT, and 3one4 Capital.

The insurance business adds to Raise’s growing portfolio of acquisitions. Recently, the company acquired algorithmic trading and investing platform Stratzy in a cash and stock deal and took over new age financial media startup Filter Coffee in January 2025. It is also set to acquire wealthtech startup Infinyte Club.

On the financial front, Raise reported a 13.8% increase in net operating income to Rs 905 crore in FY26 from Rs 795 crore in FY25, according to an ICRA rating report. However, its profit after tax declined 20.1% to Rs 326 crore in FY26 from Rs 408 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Exclusive: Indifi set to raise over $8 Mn led by ICICI Venture
description: Digital lending platform Indifi is set to raise Rs 79 crore (around $8.3 million) in its first funding round in three years, led by ICICI Venture
body: Digital lending platform Indifi is set to raise Rs 79 crore (around $8.3 million) in its first funding round in three years, led by ICICI Venture with participation from British International Investment (BII), Accel India, and Parul Alok Mittal. In June 2023, The Gurugram-based company had raised $35 million in its Series E funding round led by ICICI Venture, with participation from existing investor British International Investment (BII) and others. The company's board has approved the issuance of 43,55,975 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 181.36 each to raise the capital, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.

ICICI Venture, through its India Advantage Fund, will invest Rs 29 crore in the round. British International Investment (BII) will invest Rs 27 crore, while Accel India and Parul Alok Mittal will contribute Rs 14 crore and Rs 9 crore, respectively.

According to Entrackr's estimates, the company will be valued at Rs 1,418 crore, flat from its Series E round. The company plans to utilize the fresh proceeds for business expansion, infrastructure development, capital expenditure, working capital requirements, debt repayment, and general corporate purposes.
The company may raise more capital in this round.

Founded in 2015 by Alok Mittal and Siddharth Mahanot, Indifi provides technology-driven unsecured business loans to small and medium enterprises (SMEs). The platform has disbursed more than 1.5 lakh loans across more than 400 cities through partnerships with over 80 lending institutions.

Following the allotment, British International Investment (BII) will remain the largest external shareholder with a 17.10% stake, followed by India Advantage Fund S5 I with 15.33%. Accel India IV (Mauritius) Limited will hold 10.94%, while Parul Alok Mittal will own a 1.56% stake in the company on a fully diluted basis. The company is yet to file its financial statements for FY26. In FY25 , Indifi's operating revenue grew 22.4% to Rs 360 crore from Rs 294.24 crore in FY24. However, its losses widened 64% to Rs 45.04 crore from Rs 27.46 crore during the same period.

title: Exclusive: BiofuelCircle secures Rs 35 Cr in fresh funding
description: Biomass and biofuel marketplace BiofuelCircle, has raised Rs 35 crore in a fresh funding round led by Pooja Unichem LLP, with participation from Varanium Venture
body: Biomass and biofuel marketplace BiofuelCircle, has raised Rs 35 crore in a fresh funding round led by Pooja Unichem LLP, with participation from Varanium Venture, Rajeev Kumar, Karma Capital Advisors Private Limited, and other investors. In Aug 2025, the company had raised Rs 70 crore ($8.2 million) funding from existing investor Spectrum Impact, along with a group of angel investors and company promoters. The company's board has approved the issuance of 113,306 Non-Cumulative Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares (NCCCPS) at an issue price of Rs 2,648 per share to raise the capital, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr. In a separate resolution, the board also approved the issuance of 500 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) with a face value of Rs 1 lakh each to Varanium Venture, raising an additional Rs 5 crore.

Pooja Unichem LLP invested Rs 22.40 crore in the round, followed by Rajeev Kumar with Rs 3 crore, Ashish Kumar with Rs 2 crore, and Karma Capital Advisors Private Limited with Rs 1 crore. Better Advisors LLP and Shridhar Shukla infused Rs 50 lakh each, while Amitabha Mukhopadhyay and Lexcelon Corporate Advisors Private Limited invested Rs 25 lakh each. Ratnaprabha Mahendra Shukla, Shubham Khandelwal, and Aruna Khandelwal collectively contributed Rs 10 lakh.

As per Entrackr's estimates, the company's valuation increased to approximately Rs 638 crore, up 21.5% from its previous valuation of around Rs 525 crore. The proceeds from the issue will be used to support the company's growth plans.

Founded in 2020, BiofuelCircle is a digital marketplace for biomass and biofuels that connects farmers, suppliers, and industries. Working on a subscription and transaction model, it enables price discovery, logistics, and trade finance while helping farmers monetize agri-residue. While the Pune-based company is yet to file its FY26 financials, its operating revenue rose to Rs 50.7 crore in FY25 from Rs 29 crore in FY24. During the same period, its losses increased to Rs 6.51 crore from Rs 4.9 crore.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [July 06 - July 11]
description: This week, 18 Indian startups raised nearly $70.4 million across 3 growth-stage and 15 early-stage deals. The week also witnessed six acquisitions, Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 18 Indian startups raised nearly $70.4 million across 3 growth-stage and 15 early-stage deals. The week also witnessed six acquisitions, three key leadership appointments, two departures, three fund launches, and 2 shutdowns.
In contrast, 25 startups had collectively secured about $137 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised a total of $30.7 million across three deals this week, led by edtech platform Elevate Education, which secured $17.7 million in its Series D round led by WestBridge Capital.
Physical AI startup HakimoIncuspaze raised $12 million in a growth round from Bharat Value Fund, while workspace provider Stylework secured $1 million in a pre-Series B round led by Auxano Capital.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $39.75 million across 15 deals this week, led by e-commerce brand Aukera, which secured $10 million in a funding round led by Alteria Capital with participation from InnoVent Capital and Lighthouse Canton.

Among the other notable deals, e-commerce startup WizCommerce raised Rs 8.3 million in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures and others. Packaging firm Econovus Packaging secured $4 million in a pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter, while events tech startup thumpN raised $3.75 million in a pre-seed round from actors and singers.

title: Augusta TBO offloads 2% stake in TBO Tek for Rs 327 Cr
description: Augusta TBO (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., an early investor in travel distribution platform TBO Tek, has offloaded its 2% stake in the company through an open market transaction worth Rs 327.5 crore.
body: Augusta TBO (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., an early investor in travel distribution platform TBO Tek, has offloaded its 2% stake in the company through an open market transaction worth Rs 327.5 crore.

According to its exchange filing, the investor sold 21.82 lakh equity shares, equivalent to 2.01% of TBO Tek's equity capital, on July 13. Based on TBO Tek's closing price on Monday of Rs 1,500.3 per share on the BSE, the transaction is estimated to be worth around Rs 327.5 crore.
Prior to the sale, Augusta TBO held a 5.45% diluted stake in the travel tech firm. Following the transaction, its holding declined to 3.44%, or 37.35 lakh shares.
The regulatory filing did not disclose the buyer.

Founded in 2006, TBO Tek simplifies travel distribution for suppliers such as hotels, airlines, car rental firms, insurance providers, cruise lines, and railways, while enabling buyers to discover and book travel globally, offering inventory and booking solutions that facilitate seamless transactions across flights, hotels, and other travel services.
In Q4 FY26, TBO Tek reported an 82% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 814 crore, with a profit of Rs 60 crore during the quarter.
At the end of Monday’s trading session, TBO Tek shares were closed at Rs 1500.3 on BSE, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 16,291 crore.

title: Exclusive: OneCard to raise Rs 72 Cr in its ongoing Series D round led by Peak XV
description: OneCard is raising Rs 72 crore (around $7.6 million) in a fresh funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from existing investor Z47
body: Mobile-first credit card startup OneCard is raising Rs 72 crore (around $7.6 million) in a fresh funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from existing investor Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India), Hummingbird Ventures, and several angel investors.
In Nov 2024, the company had raised around $28.5 million from Better Tomorrow Ventures, Peak XV (previously Sequoia Capital), and Z47 (previously Matrix Partners).

The board at OneCard has passed a special resolution to issue 21,639 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 33,228.35 each to raise Rs 72 crore, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.

Peak XV Partners will lead the round with an investment of Rs 30 crore, followed by Z47 with Rs 9.5 crore. The remaining capital will come from Shalini Warrier, Kakarla Karunamaye, Sumana Mallick, and Ranu Madhivanan, who invested Rs 5 crore each. Sathish Krishnan will infuse Rs 3 crore, while Pragnyat Lalwani, Gautam Jain, and Gaurang Shah will contribute Rs 2.5 crore each. Hummingbird Ventures will invest Rs 1.9 crore.
As per Entrackr's estimates, the fresh round values the company at around Rs 12,050 crore (approximately $1.27 billion), reflecting a slight increase from its previous valuation of Rs 11,747 crore.

Founded in 2019 by Anurag Sinha and Rupesh Kumar, OneCard (FPL Technologies) offers a mobile-first credit card platform in partnership with banks including IDFC FIRST Bank, Federal Bank, Indian Bank, and SBM Bank. The company also operates OneScore, a credit score management app that enables users to track their credit score, monitor spending, manage credit cards, and convert transactions into EMIs through a digital-first experience.

In December 2025, the RBI reportedly asked partner banks to halt the onboarding of new OneCard customers to review data sharing arrangements. In April 2026, Entrackr reported that the fintech firm was in discussions with the regulator through its partner banks to restart co-branded credit card issuance. However, the company is yet to resume issuing new co-branded credit cards.

Post-allotment (excluding ESOPs), Peak XV Partners will remain the largest shareholder with a 22.88% stake, followed by Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India), which will hold a combined 17.66% stake, as per the company's regulatory filings.

title: Exclusive: Naturis Cosmetics to raise maiden funding led by Sharrp Ventures
description: Naturis Cosmetics is raising Rs 33.74 crore ($3.5 million) in its maiden funding round led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from Mirabilis Investment Trust.
body: Naturis Cosmetics, a contract manufacturer for beauty brands including Nykaa, Plum, Pilgrim, and Bare Anatomy, is raising Rs 33.74 crore ($3.5 million) in its maiden funding round led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from Mirabilis Investment Trust.

According to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), the company’s board passed a special resolution to approve the issue of 12,784 preference shares at an issue price of Rs 26,400 to raise the above-mentioned amount.
Sharrp Ventures will lead the tranche with Rs 22.5 crore while Mirabilis Investment Trust will contribute with Rs 11.25 crore in the round.
The current tranche may be part of a larger funding round, as an earlier Economic Times report said Naturis Cosmetics was looking to raise Rs 80–100 crore.
According to Entrackr’s estimates, the Jammu-based company will be valued at around Rs 364 crore or around $38 million post-money.

Founded in 2011 by Rahul Tandon, Naturis Cosmetics is a B2B contract manufacturer that develops and manufactures skincare, haircare, personal care, fragrance, and cosmetic products for beauty brands. It provides end-to-end OEM/ODM, private label, product formulation, R&D, packaging, manufacturing, and regulatory support services. Its clients include Nykaa, Plum, Purplle, Bare Anatomy, and Ustraa, among other beauty and personal care brands.
Following the allotment of this tranche, Sharrp Ventures will acquire a 6.19% stake in the firm, while Mirabilis Investment Trust will own a 3.09% stake.

While the company is yet to file its FY26 financials, Naturis Cosmetics reported a 40% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 154 crore in FY25 from Rs 110 crore in FY24. The company also remained profitable, posting a net profit of Rs 12 crore during the year.

title: Exclusive: Inside CRED’s new funding, Meta’s stake and ESOP expansion
description: Meta's $900 million investment marked CRED's first fundraise in nearly four years. Entrackr decoded the filings to reveal Meta's primary investment, stake acquisition, and CRED's $112 million ESOP expansion.
body: Meta's $900 million investment in CRED represented the fintech unicorn's return to fundraising after nearly four years, valuing the company at $4.54 billion, up from $3.63 billion in its previous round but still well below its peak valuation of around $6.4 billion.

While the headline drew attention, the deal structure tells a deeper story. Entrackr analysed the company's regulatory filings to decode how much fresh capital Meta infused, the stake it acquired, and why the company expanded its ESOP pool by more than $110 million.
As part of the deal, CRED founder Kunal Shah has joined Meta as the global CEO of WhatsApp, while Miten Sampat will assume the role of interim CEO.

The board at Dreamplug Technologies Pvt Ltd, passes a special resolution to approve the issuance of 4,82,167 Series H CCPS at an issue price of Rs 1,05,912 each to raise Rs 5,107 crore or $537 million from Facebook Overseas Inc. (Meta), according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

While the filing does not disclose details of the secondary transaction, it shows that Meta will acquire an 11.84% stake in Cred through the primary transaction. The final shareholding for Meta will increase post the completion of the secondary transactions.
The latest round valued CRED at around Rs 43,129 crore ($4.53 billion) post-money.
According to the company's latest shareholding pattern, Kunal Shah no longer appears as a promoter of the firm.
In a separate resolution, CRED's board approved the addition of 1,00,451 stock options to its existing ESOP scheme, taking the total ESOP pool to 4,72,223 options.

title: After SoftBank and ADIA, Temasek sells 2.05% stake in Lenskart for Rs 1,940 Cr
description: Temasek-backed MacRitchie Investments has sold a 2.05% stake worth Rs 1,940 crore or $204 million in omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions through open market transactions.
body: Temasek-backed MacRitchie Investments has sold a 2.05% stake worth Rs 1,940 crore or $204 million in omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions through open market transactions.
According to Lenskart's exchange filing dated July 14, The Singapore-based investor divested 3.56 crore equity shares on July 10, reducing its direct stake in the company to 2.21% from 4.26%.

Despite the latest sale, Temasek continues to hold a 4.75% stake in Lenskart through MacRitchie Investments and its affiliated entities, Jongsong Investments and V-Sciences Investments, down from 6.80%.
While the filing did not disclose the transaction value, the stake sale is estimated to be worth around Rs 1,940 crore, based on Lenskart's closing price of Rs 544 on July 10.

Early investors have continued to monetize their holdings after Lenskart's listing. Last month, SoftBank exited a 3.25% stake for Rs 2,873 crore, while ADIA-backed Platinum Jasmine A 2018 Trust sold a 2.3% holding for Rs 1,960 crore, with both transactions attracting strong institutional demand.

Founded by Peyush Bansal, Amit Chaudhary, and Sumeet Kapahi, Lenskart has a presence across online and offline channels. The company operates thousands of stores across India and international markets while also manufacturing eyewear products through its in-house facilities.

During its latest quarterly results (Q4 FY26), the company posted 46% year-on-year growth in its revenue to Rs 2,516 crore with a profit of Rs 204 crore. As of 12:00 PM (today), Lenskart’s share is currently trading at around Rs 538.9, with a total market capitalization of Rs 93,639 crore ($9.85 billion).

title: Avendus Future Leaders Fund invests Rs 140 Cr in PPFAS ahead of final close of Fund III
description: Avendus Future Leaders Fund (FLF) III has invested around Rs 140 crore in Parag Parikh Financial Advisory Services (PPFAS) through a secondary transaction. Snippets
body: Avendus Future Leaders Fund (FLF) III has invested around Rs 140 crore in Parag Parikh Financial Advisory Services (PPFAS) through a secondary transaction.
The investment involved the acquisition of promoter shares from Neil Parag Parikh, Chairman and CEO of PPFAS, and Khushboo Joshi, President of Wealth Management at the company.

Founded in 1992, PPFAS operates across mutual funds, wealth management, GIFT City funds, private equity and the National Pension System (NPS). Its flagship offering, the Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, managed assets worth around Rs 1.43 lakh crore as of June 2026.

According to Avendus, the investment aligns with its strategy of backing established businesses with long-term growth potential. The firm claims PPFAS has recorded strong growth in recent years, with its assets under management growing at a CAGR of around 70% over the last five years.

With this transaction, Avendus Future Leaders Fund III is expected to achieve its final close at around Rs 1,800 crore by the end of July. The fund is currently around 30% deployed and plans to make five to six additional investments over the next 12 months.
Avendus Future Leaders Fund manages more than Rs 4,000 crore in assets across its funds and invests in late-stage companies across sectors.

title: Elevation Capital closes $500 Mn India fund to back AI startups
description: Venture capital firm Elevation Capital has closed its ninth India-focused fund at $500 million, with a focus on backing early-stage startups building . News
body: Venture capital firm Elevation Capital has closed its ninth India-focused fund at $500 million, with a focus on backing early-stage startups building AI-led products and applications.

The new fund will invest primarily in seed and Series A startups, particularly those building on the application layer of artificial intelligence. The firm believes the next wave of AI companies will emerge by solving business and consumer problems using AI technologies.
Alongside Fund IX, Elevation Capital also manages a separate $400 million fund launched in August last year, taking its total deployable capital to around $900 million.

Elevation Capital has been one of the most active early-stage investors in India, backing startups across consumer internet, fintech, SaaS and AI. The firm said India is entering a phase where AI-native startups can build products for both domestic and global markets.

Partners at the firm said that while foundational AI models are largely being developed by global technology companies, significant opportunities exist for Indian founders to build AI applications and businesses on top of these models.
Elevation Capital has invested in listed firms like FirstCry, Ixigo, MakeMyTrip, Paytm, Swiggy, Meesho and Urban Company. The fund made back-to-back partial exits from travel-tech firm Ixigo.

title: Emergent becomes third AI unicorn of 2026 with $130 Mn Series C led by Creaegis
description: Emergent has raised $230 million across three funding rounds within a year. The startup secured $23 million in its Series A round in September 2025, followed by a $70 million Series B round in January 2026.
body: AI software creation platform Emergent has raised $130 million in a Series C funding round led by Creaegis, with participation from Claypond, Sentinel Global, Khosla Ventures, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Lightspeed and Y Combinator.

The fresh round values the company at $1.5 billion, a fivefold jump in valuation within four months. The latest fundraise also makes Emergent one of the fastest startups to enter the unicorn club, just a year after its public launch.
The company said the proceeds will be used to expand its AI software creation platform, strengthen its autonomous AI capabilities, and support its growing global user base.

Founded in 2025 by Mukund and Madhav Jha, Emergent enables founders, entrepreneurs and small businesses to build production ready web and mobile applications using autonomous AI agents, without requiring coding expertise. According to the company, more than 12 million applications have been built on its platform, with nearly 70% of users having no prior coding experience.

"The real impact of the AI revolution will be a complete democratization of who gets to build software and how much it costs," said Mukund Jha, co-founder and CEO of Emergent. "With Emergent, entrepreneurs and business owners can build and run the software their businesses need without depending on traditional engineering resources."
The company allows users to build products such as CRMs, ERPs, marketplaces, mobile applications, internal tools, and customer facing software through AI agents.

Emergent has raised $230 million across three funding rounds within a year. The startup secured $23 million in its Series A round in September 2025, followed by a $70 million Series B round in January 2026.

With this round, Emergent has become the third AI startup and the seventh overall startup to enter India's unicorn club in 2026, following KreditBee , Neysa , Juspay , Skyroot , Sarvam AI, and Square Yards. Last month, AI startup Sarvam AI raised $234 million in the first close of its $300 million Series B round at a post money valuation of $1.5 billion.

title: Maternal and baby care brand Promom raises Rs 30 Cr from Fireside Ventures
description: The Lucknow-based startup addresses the hassles like Indian mothers face a limited choice between premium international brands that are often expensive and challenging to
body: Maternal and baby care brand Promom has raised Rs 30 crore in a funding round led by Fireside Ventures.

The fresh funds will be used to  focus on product innovation, expand offerings across the broader maternal and baby care ecosystem while increasing accessibility for mothers across the country, Promom said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2023 by Anavi Kalia, Manas Tripathi, and Aditya Srivastava, Promom is a maternal and baby care brand that develops thoughtfully designed products that help address the challenges of feeding and early parenting, combining reliability, quality, and accessibility for modern Indian families.

The Lucknow-based startup addresses the hassles like Indian mothers face a limited choice between premium international brands that are often expensive and challenging to service, and local alternatives that may not consistently deliver on quality and performance. The startup bridges this gap through reliable, thoughtfully designed maternal and baby care products that combine quality, functionality, and affordability.

According to Promom, it  has built its products through close collaboration with mothers, doctors, and lactation consultants, continuously refining its offerings based on real-world feedback and lived experiences.
