Delivery and related expenses grew 68.5% year-on-year to Rs 3,150 crore, while employee benefits expenses rose 29% to Rs 1,068 crore. Advertising expenses also increased 41% to Rs 945 crore during the period. Overall, Eternal's total expenditure rose to Rs 20,314 crore in Q1 FY27.

Segment-wise, the food delivery business reported a positive EBITDA of Rs 621 crore, up over 33% year-on-year. Meanwhile, Blinkit turned EBITDA positive with Rs 365 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 42 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26, while District reported a negative EBITDA of Rs 62 crore during the same period.
At the bottom line, Eternal's net profit jumped 3.7X year-on-year to Rs 92 crore in Q1 FY27, aided by strong topline growth and non-operating income.

title: Smartworks posts Rs 546 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; EBITDA grows over 37%
description: Smartworks reported its financial results for the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 FY27). The company posted 44% year-on-year growth in revenue during the period, while its EBITDA rose over 37% to Rs 346 crore.
body: Managed office space provider Smartworks reported its financial results for the quarter ended June 2026 (Q1 FY27). The company posted 44% year-on-year growth in revenue during the period, while its EBITDA rose over 37% to Rs 346 crore.

Smartworks’ revenue from operations rose to Rs 546 crore in the Q1 FY27 from Rs 365 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Smartworks derives the bulk of its operating revenue from developing, designing and licensing serviced office spaces, along with fit out services and other ancillary offerings. The company also reported Rs 13.4 crore in non operating income, which took its total income to Rs 560 crore in Q1 FY27.
On a sequential basis, the firm’s operating revenue grew 5% from Rs 520 crore in Q4 FY26 .

On the cost side, depreciation (related to lease) was the largest expense at Rs 246 crore, followed by operating expenses, which were at  Rs 154 crore. Finance costs, employee benefits, and other overheads took Smartworks’s total expenditure to Rs 542 crore, compared to Rs 394 crore in the same quarter last year.

Coming to the bottom line, Smartworks turned profitable on a year-on-year basis with a net profit of Rs 13 crore in Q1 FY27, aided by other income.However, its EBITDA grew over 37% year on year to Rs 346 crore during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of 63.4%.
As of 12:35 PM today, Smartworks shares traded at around Rs 494 apiece, valuing the company at a market capitalization of Rs 5,634 crore ($593 million).

title: Zappfresh revenue grows 58% to Rs 74 Cr in Q1 FY27
description: DSM Fresh Foods, the parent company of Zappfresh, reported a 58% year-on-year growth in its revenue from operations to around Rs 74 crore during the first quarter of FY27.
body: DSM Fresh Foods, the parent company of omnichannel meat delivery and processed foods brand Zappfresh, reported a 58% year-on-year growth in its revenue from operations to around Rs 74 crore during the first quarter of FY27, according to its provisional business update filed with the stock exchanges.

Following the completion of the Meevaa Foods acquisition in the first week of July, the combined business currently operates at an approximate pro forma quarterly revenue run rate of Rs 85 crore, including Meevaa.
The company attributed the growth to retail expansion, wider omnichannel distribution and higher traction across its consumer and institutional businesses.

During the quarter, DSM Fresh Foods added over 70 enterprise customers across domestic and export markets. It also expanded its presence across e-commerce, quick commerce and modern retail channels, with Blinkit deliveries commencing in Mumbai.

Zappfresh expanded its retail footprint to nearly 200 co-branded outlets, surpassing its FY27 target of 150 outlets ahead of schedule. The company plans to accelerate its retail expansion through FY27 as it seeks to increase the contribution of its higher margin B2C business.

On the supply side, the company onboarded 10 new sourcing partners and initiated 270 acre land aggregation as part of its backward integration efforts. DSM Fresh Foods now works with more than 1,700 seafood farmers across its sourcing ecosystem. It also incorporated Varuna Aquatech Pvt Ltd to support the long term development of its aquaculture platform.
Internationally, the company expanded its distribution network across the UK, Canada and GCC markets and onboarded a distribution partner in Dubai.

DSM Fresh Foods reiterated its FY28 guidance of Rs 600 crore in revenue with an EBITDA margin of 18% to 20%, backed by retail expansion, value added products and deeper backward integration across its farm to fork platform.

title: Medtech startup Bioscan Research raises $1 Mn in seed round led by Unicorn India Ventures
description: Mumbai-based medtech startup Bioscan Research has raised $1 million in a seed funding round led by Unicorn India Ventures. Snippets.
body: Mumbai-based medtech startup Bioscan Research has raised $1 million in a seed funding round led by Unicorn India Ventures.
The proceeds will be used for market expansion, securing additional regulatory approvals, upgrading its products and creating new intellectual property.

Founded in 2017 by Anupam Lavania and Shilpa Malik, Bioscan Research develops non-invasive medical devices for the early detection of brain injuries. Its flagship product, CEREBO, uses near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and machine learning to detect intracranial injuries, enabling early diagnosis of traumatic brain injuries even before visible symptoms appear.
According to the company, its technology is designed to help healthcare providers identify brain injuries during the critical treatment window and improve patient outcomes.
Bioscan Research said it recorded 5x growth over the past 12 months. It aims to grow threefold over the next year by expanding its presence in India and overseas markets.

Founded in 2016, Unicorn India Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on deeptech startups across sectors including semiconductors, spacetech, AI infrastructure and medical diagnostics.

title: Bira 91 founder Ankur Jain exits after settlement with lenders; says company needs fresh capital
description: The company's financial troubles and disputes with creditors also led to proceedings before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). Its situation worsened after an
body: Ankur Jain, the founder of Bira 91 parent B9 Beverages, has stepped down from the board and his executive role after signing a settlement with lenders and investors, clearing the way for the company's restructuring and a fresh capital raise.

A letter by Jain, accessed by Entrackr, reveals that the settlement includes the withdrawal of all litigation, release of personal guarantees extended by the founder, and the promoter family's exit from the company's board and executive positions.
According to Jain, the settlement took much longer than expected as it involved nearly 30 stakeholders with "genuinely different, often competing interests."
"We have now reached that settlement. As part of it, my family and I will be stepping away from the board, and from our executive positions, with immediate effect," Jain wrote.

He added that all parties have agreed to withdraw claims and legal proceedings against each other, bringing the dispute to a close. Jain also confirmed that the personal guarantees he had provided for corporate loans over the years would be released as part of the agreement.
"It is, in every sense, a clean and full close of this chapter," he said.

Jain acknowledged that the prolonged negotiations had affected employees awaiting salaries, vendors awaiting payments, lenders seeking resolution, and shareholders looking for clarity. He described reaching an agreement among nearly 30 stakeholders as "close to a miracle."

The founder said Bira 91 now requires fresh capital, a clean balance sheet, and a new management team to lead the business into its next phase. He added that he would support a smooth transition and continue to back the brand from the sidelines.

title: Go Digit reports 38% decline in Q1 FY27 profit as claims surge
description: Go Digit's shares closed at Rs 283 per share at the end of Thursday's trading session, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 26,166 crore (around $2.7 billion).
body: Go Digit General Insurance reported a 7.6% year-on-year increase in its net premium during Q1 FY27. However, its profit declined 37.7% during the same period.
The company's net premium rose to Rs 2,007 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,865 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its regulatory filings.
Meanwhile, gross premium fell 8.4% to Rs 2,731 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,982 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, as per its quarterly results filed with the NSE.

Motor insurance continued to be Go Digit's largest business segment, contributing Rs 1,510 crore in premium, followed by health insurance at Rs 366 crore. The company also generated premium from fire, corporate, marine, crop, and other insurance segments.

Income from investments increased to Rs 352 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 314 crore in the year-ago quarter. Supported by gains from its investment portfolio and other non-operating income, the company's total income grew to Rs 2,359 crore during the quarter.

On the expense side, commission and brokerage costs rose to Rs 615 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 572 crore in Q1 FY26. Employee benefit expenses increased 10% to Rs 99 crore from Rs 90 crore a year earlier.
Claims paid surged 16% to Rs 1,046 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 902 crore in the same quarter last year. As a result, total expenses rose 11.2% to Rs 2,289 crore from Rs 2,058 crore.
The increase in claims and operating expenses weighed on the company's profitability, with net profit declining 37.7% to Rs 86 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 138 crore in Q1 FY26.

title: Exclusive: Urban Harvest board to approve Rs 341 Cr Series D round from 58 investors
description: B2B food-tech startup Urban Harvest is set to raise Rs 341.4 crore or $35.9 million in a Series D round led by Info Edge, with participation from Sandeep Kapadia
body: B2B food-tech startup Urban Harvest is set to raise Rs 341.4 crore or $35.9 million in a Series D round led by Info Edge, with participation from Sandeep Kapadia, J & A Partners, and several other investors.

The board at Urban Harvest will consider approving the issuance of 42,013 Series D compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 81,260 each to raise the capital, according to its regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.

The round will be led by Info Edge, with an investment of Rs 30 crore, followed by Sandeep Kapadia and J & A Partners, which will invest Rs 27 crore and Rs 25 crore, respectively. Renu Sehgal Trust and Lc Nueva Advisors will contribute Rs 20.01 crore each.

Other notable investors include Saburi Projects LLP at Rs 15 crore, Madhuri Madhusudan Kela at Rs 13.09 crore, and Viral Amal Parikh at Rs 11.56 crore. Gauri Khan Family Trust, will also participate with Rs 5.01 crore. Several other individual and institutional investors will contribute the remaining capital, taking the total number of investors in the round to 58.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, Urban Harvest will be valued at around Rs 1,541 crore or $162 million following the Series D round. The company plans to use the fresh proceeds to fund its business expansion and growth, meet working capital requirements, support marketing initiatives, and for general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2019, Urban Harvest is a B2B food-tech platform that supplies fresh produce, food ingredients, and automated coffee machines to restaurants and cloud kitchens. The company operates a quick-commerce model focused on the HoReCa segment and currently serves around 16,000 restaurants every month across multiple cities.

Urban Harvest operates five dark warehouses across four cities and plans to add five more as it expands into new markets. The company also owns packaged water brand Hello Fresh and acquired gourmet food brand Cocosutra for Rs 2.5 crore in an all-cash deal. Following the allotment of the Series D round, Info Edge will hold an 18.83% stake, followed by Sandeep Kapadia at 5.01%, Madhuri Madhusudan Kela at 4.25%, Viral Amal Parikh at 3.75%, and J & A Partners at 3.12%. Mint had earlier reported that Urban Urban Harvest in talks to raise Rs 300 crore

According to the report, Urban Harvest’s revenue surged to Rs 385 crore in FY26 from Rs 118 crore in FY25, while it posted a profit of Rs 3.5 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 35 lakh in the previous fiscal year.

title: Meesho records Rs 3,713 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; narrows losses by 54%
description: E-commerce marketplace Meesho reported a 48% year on year increase in revenue, while its losses narrowed sharply by 54% to Rs 133 crore during the same period.
body: E-commerce marketplace Meesho has announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 48% year on year increase in revenue, while its losses narrowed sharply by 54% to Rs 133 crore during the same period.

The company’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 3,713 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,504 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements filed with the NSE.

The revenue breakdown was not disclosed in the financial statements. The company also recorded Rs 114 crore in non operating income, taking its total income to Rs 3,826 crore in the quarter ended June.
On a quarter on quarter basis, the company's revenue from operations grew 5% from Rs 3,531 crore in Q4 FY26.
While the majority of its expenses were not disclosed in the quarterly financial statements, Meesho spent Rs 243 crore on employee benefits in Q1 FY27, a 17% increase from Rs 207 crore in Q1 FY26.
Its depreciation expense stood at Rs 20 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenses grew 43% year on year to Rs 3,959 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,778 crore in Q1 FY26.
Segment wise, Meesho's marketplace segment reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 139 crore, while its new initiatives segment posted an EBITDA loss of Rs 39 crore on revenue of Rs 6 crore.
At the bottom line, Meesho narrowed its losses by 54% to Rs 133 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 289 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.

title: Healthtech startup CARPL.ai raises $10 Mn Series A led by IFC
description: Healthtech startup CARPL.ai has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), with participation. Snippets
body: Healthtech startup CARPL.ai has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), with participation from existing investor Stellaris Venture Partners and other undisclosed investors.
Prior to this round, the startup had raised $6 million in 2023 from Stellaris Venture Partners and angel investors.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the company's technology stack, accelerate product development, and expand its global sales and delivery teams.

Founded in 2018 by Vidur Mahajan, CARPL.ai operates an AI-powered platform that enables hospitals and radiologists to discover, deploy, manage, and monitor multiple medical imaging AI applications through a single interface.
The startup's marketplace hosts more than 300 AI applications from over 100 vendors.
CARPL.ai currently serves 30 hospitals and medical centres across North America, Europe, the Middle East, India, Southeast Asia, Australia, and Latin America.
Its customers include the Singapore government, RadNet, I-MED Radiology, Fleury, Medica, and the Clinton Health Access Initiative in India.

title: Earth Fund leads $3 Mn Series A round in Wiffy
description: Wiffy has raised $3 million in a Series A funding round led by Earth Fund, with participation from Japan's Persol Holdings and existing investor Capria Ventures.
body: Organized post sales installation and services platform Wiffy has raised $3 million in a Series A funding round led by Earth Fund, with participation from Japan's Persol Holdings and existing investor Capria Ventures.

The Mumbai based startup had earlier raised Rs 25 crore (around $3 million) in a pre Series A round co-led by Mount Judi Ventures and existing investor Capria Ventures in July 2024, with participation from Blume Founders Fund and other investors. It had also secured $2 million in a seed round in July 2022.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its technology platform, strengthen AI powered workforce management, deepen enterprise partnerships, and accelerate category expansion, Wiffy said in a press release.
Founded in 2019 by Vikram Sharma and Deepanshu Goyal, Wiffy operates a field services platform for home improvement and consumer durables brands.

The company provides installation, maintenance, warranty, and field services across more than 100 cities through an AI powered platform and a network of over 5,000 certified technicians. It partners with more than 100 brands, including IKEA, Panasonic, Godrej, Hettich, and Amazon, and says it has served more than one million homes across India.
Wiffy automates technician scheduling, deployment, and quality assurance through its proprietary AI powered SaaS platform, enabling brands to manage pre and post sales service operations.

According to the company, it has served more than one million homes across over 100 cities since inception. Wiffy also said that demand is driven directly by its enterprise and brand partners, resulting in minimal customer acquisition costs.

title: Ashneer Grover launches employer backed lending platform Fund My Staff
description: Ashneer Grover, former MD and co-founder of BharatPe, has launched Fund My Staff, a new fintech platform that enables employers to facilitate loans for their employees by acting as guarantors.
body: Ashneer Grover, former MD and co-founder of BharatPe, has launched Fund My Staff, a new fintech platform that enables employers to facilitate loans for their employees by acting as guarantors. Grover announced the launch of the platform in a LinkedIn post on Thursday.

The platform is designed for employers who want to support their workforce with access to credit, and for staff members with limited or no credit history who require financing backed by their employer's guarantee.

According to the website, employers can onboard staff, set the loan amount, review loan requests, and approve them by acting as guarantors. Once approved, the loan is disbursed to the employee, who repays it through monthly EMIs.
Employees can also initiate the process by sending a loan request to their employer. After the employer approves the request, the loan is processed and repaid in EMIs.

The platform says that it operates as a Lending Service Provider (LSP) in compliance with the Reserve Bank of India's digital lending guidelines. Loans are originated and sanctioned by RBI registered lending partners. The website currently lists Ash Grove Capital Private Limited, an RBI registered NBFC, as its lending partner.
The website also clarifies that employers do not pay the loan amount. Instead, they act as guarantors while the employee receives the funds and repays the loan over the selected tenure.

Fund My Staff has been developed by Delhi based Third Unicorn, the venture founded by Grover and Aseem Ghavri after Grover's exit from BharatPe . In 2024, the company launched ZeroPe, a fintech app focused on financing medical expenses. It had also introduced fantasy cricket platform CrickPe, which ceased operations in February last year.

title: PedalStart leads pre-seed round in extracurricular learning platform UpKraft
description: Over the next 12 to 18 months, Upkraft plans to increase student enrollments, expand its presence across Bengaluru and Gurugram, improve learning outcomes, and strengthen
body: Extracurricular learning platform UpKraft has raised Rs 1.6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by PedalStart, with participation from a group of angel investors.

The proceeds will be used to accelerate AI product development, expand its presence across Bengaluru and Gurugram, strengthen its technology platform, operations, and customer experience, and build teams across product, technology, growth, sales, and tutor operations, UpKraft said in a press release.

Co-founded in July 2025 by Tejasvi Singh Kushwah, Varun Mangal, and Kritika Varandani, UpKraft is an AI-powered extracurricular learning platform that offers structured learning at home, in residential communities, and in schools through verified expert tutors.

According to the Bengaluru-based startup, it combines AI tools such as its AI Practice Companion and Progress Insights with standardized, level-based curricula to help students build skills while giving parents visibility into their progress. The company says it has developed standardized learning programs across music and other extracurricular disciplines and partnered with residential communities across Bengaluru and Gurugram.

Over the next 12 to 18 months, UpKraft plans to increase student enrollments, expand its presence across Bengaluru and Gurugram, improve learning outcomes, and strengthen teams across product and engineering, AI and data science, sales and business development, community and field marketing, customer success, and tutor onboarding and operations.

PedalStart is an operator-led startup accelerator focused on supporting early-stage startups. In addition to capital, it works with founders on growth strategy, operations, and market expansion through its network of operators and investors.

title: Farm Watt Innovations raises Rs 32.5 Cr co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter
description: Climate-focused agribusiness startup Farm Watt Innovations has raised Rs 32.5 crore ($3.36 million) in a funding round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter. Snippets
body: Climate-focused agribusiness startup Farm Watt Innovations has raised Rs 32.5 crore ($3.36 million) in a funding round co-led by IAN Alpha Fund and Rainmatter.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its biomass supply chain, expand its biomass collection network, build additional aggregation hubs, invest in machinery and grow its workforce.

Founded in 2023 by Kumar Neelendu, Farm Watt Innovations aggregates and supplies agricultural biomass to compressed biogas (CBG) plants and other bioenergy facilities. The startup aims to address crop residue burning by converting agricultural waste into feedstock for renewable energy projects.

The company currently operates 15 biomass aggregation hubs across six states and plans to expand its presence to Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Bihar.
The startup said it plans to develop its own portfolio of CBG, bio-pellet and biochar plants as it expands its presence in India's bioenergy ecosystem.

title: Incred Finance posts Rs 438 Cr PAT on Rs 2,546 Cr revenue in FY26
description: InCred Financial Services, delivered strong financial results in FY26. The company reported 36% YoY growth in operating revenue, while profits grew by 17% in the same period.
body: InCred Financial Services, the lending arm of InCred Holdings, delivered strong financial results in FY26 ahead of its proposed IPO. The company reported 36% year-on-year growth in operating revenue, while profits grew by 17% in the same period.
According to its consolidated financial statements, the Mumbai-based company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,546 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,872 crore in FY25.

Founded by Bhupinder Singh in 2017, InCred Finance operates as a diversified retail-focused NBFC, offering a range of lending products across personal loans, student loans, secured business loans, specialised MSME financing, and loans to financial institutions.

Interest income from loan disbursements accounted for 91% of its total operating revenue, which grew 38% year-on-year to Rs 2,331 crore. Income from fees and commission added Rs 213 crore, while the remaining operating income came from net gains on fair value changes in financial assets.
The firm also made Rs 20 crore from other non-operating sources, which pushed its total income to Rs 2,567 crore.

For the lending firm, finance costs accounted for 47% of InCred’s total expenditure and rose 47% year-on-year to Rs 922 crore in FY26. Its employee benefit expenses also increased 23% to Rs 416 crore.

Losses from impaired financial instruments, including loan write-offs, jumped 62% year-on-year to Rs 305 crore. Depreciation expenses, along with legal, collection, advertising, travel and other overheads, pushed the company's total expenditure up 43% to Rs 1,970 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,381 crore in the previous fiscal year.

With strong growth in loan disbursements, InCred Finance increased its profit by 17% to Rs 438 crore in FY26 from Rs 374 crore in the previous fiscal year. On a unit level, it spent Rs 0.8 to earn every rupee in FY26.

title: Akumentis Healthcare records Rs 446 Cr revenue and Rs 77 Cr profit in FY26
description: Akumentis Healthcare recorded modest revenue growth over the past two fiscal years, with its operating revenue rising from Rs 398 crore in FY24 to Rs 446 crore in FY26.
body: Akumentis Healthcare recorded modest revenue growth over the past two fiscal years, with its operating revenue rising from Rs 398 crore in FY24 to Rs 446 crore in FY26. The company, however, remained profitable and reported moderate growth in its net profit. Akumentis’ revenue from operations increased to Rs 446 crore in FY26 from Rs 434 crore in FY25, according to its annual standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The Thane-based company markets a portfolio of more than 167 branded prescription products across therapeutic segments, including gynecology, cardiology, orthopedics, pediatrics, and dermatology. The sale of pharmaceutical products remained its sole source of operating revenue.
The company also recorded Rs 17.3 crore in other income, primarily from interest on deposits, taking its total income to Rs 464 crore in FY26 from Rs 449 crore in FY25.

Employee benefits remained the company's largest expense, decreasing to Rs 130 crore in FY26. The cost of materials consumed stood at Rs 115 crore, followed by advertising expenses of Rs 37 crore. Travelling expenses and legal and professional fees came in at Rs 28 crore and Rs 23 crore, respectively. Overall, the company's total expenditure declined marginally to Rs 360 crore in FY26 from Rs 362 crore in the previous fiscal.
Akumentis' profit increased to Rs 77 crore in FY26 from Rs 66 crore in FY25. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at 39.21% and 20.14%, respectively.
Note: We have excluded the exceptional expense of Rs 63 crore related to the impairment of loans while calculating the net profit to present the company's underlying financial performance.

On a unit basis, Akumentis spent Re 0.81 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. As of March 2026, it held current assets worth Rs 271 crore, including Rs 199 crore in cash and bank balances.

Akumentis has raised a total of $19 million in funding to date, with Peak XV Partners as its largest external investor. Recently, AKUM Drugs, along with its subsidiary Akumentis Healthcare, received an income tax demand notice of Rs 134 crore.

title: AI insurtech startup NeuralKart raises seed funding led by Inflection Point Ventures
description: Bengaluru-based AI insurtech startup NeuralKart has raised Rs 2.35 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures. Snippets.
body: Bengaluru-based AI insurtech startup NeuralKart has raised Rs 2.35 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures.
The proceeds will be used for product development, AI and machine learning engineering, customer acquisition, go-to-market expansion and working capital.
Founded in 2024 by Manoj Raju, Shreyas R. Halageri and Vidvath Kamireddy, NeuralKart develops AI platforms for insurance operations and industrial safety.

Its insurance platform, InsureMind, automates underwriting, claims, renewals and audits by analysing insurers' policy documents. The company's FieldSense platform uses computer vision with drone, CCTV, IP camera and sensor data to identify safety risks at industrial sites and generate risk assessments.

NeuralKart claims to have onboarded paying enterprise customers and has maintained a 100% customer retention rate since inception. The startup works with general insurers and industrial risk services firms across health underwriting, claims automation and field safety, and has also entered a co-development partnership for its FieldSense platform.
NeuralKart operates at the intersection of insurtech and industrial safety technology, targeting enterprise customers in India and overseas.

title: BusinessNext raises $40 Mn from ServiceNow Ventures at $700 Mn valuation
description: BusinessNext, a banking software startup, has raised $40 million in a Series B funding round from ServiceNow Ventures, the investment arm of US cloud software company ServiceNow.
body: BusinessNext, a banking software startup, has raised $40 million in a Series B funding round from ServiceNow Ventures , the investment arm of US cloud software company ServiceNow.

The round values the Noida based company at $700 million, nearly four times its last reported valuation of $181 million in 2021. According to Reuters, ServiceNow has acquired around a 5% stake in BusinessNext as part of the transaction.

According to the company, it will use the fresh capital to strengthen its autonomous banking platform, enhance its Private AI capabilities for financial institutions, and support its expansion into Australia and New Zealand.
The partnership with ServiceNow is also expected to help BusinessNext expand its presence across Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand.

Founded by Nikhil Singh , BusinessNext provides AI powered software for banks and financial institutions. According to the company, its platform is used by more than one million bankers across over 75,000 bank branches globally.
BusinessNext raised $16 million in 2021 in a funding round co led by Avataar Ventures and Ascent Capital.
The startup's customers include HDFC Bank, SBI General, Axis Bank, Jana Small Finance Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, IndusInd Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, and Ujjivan Small Finance Bank.
According to media reports , BusinessNext reported Rs 312 crore in revenue and Rs 3.1 crore in net profit in FY25. The firm’s FY26 results couldn’t be ascertained.

title: WhatsApp overtakes CRED in UPI volume in June; PhonePe retains lead
description: WhatsApp overtook CRED in Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transaction volume in June, processing 150.48 million transactions compared with CRED's 141.78 million.
body: WhatsApp overtook CRED in Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transaction volume in June, processing 150.48 million transactions compared with CRED's 141.78 million, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

The crossover comes in the same month that CRED founder Kunal Shah stepped down from the fintech firm to take over as the global CEO of WhatsApp. Miten Sampat was named interim CEO of CRED following Shah's move.
In May, CRED had processed 157 million UPI transactions, ahead of WhatsApp's more than 150 million transactions.

Despite its lower transaction volume in June, CRED processed transactions worth Rs 55,117 crore and accounted for 1.91% of UPI transaction value. WhatsApp's transaction value stood at Rs 11,392 crore, translating to a 0.39% share.
Meanwhile, Walmart-backed digital payments platform PhonePe retained its dominance in the UPI ecosystem with 10.48 billion transactions in June, compared with 10.73 billion in May.
This was the fourth consecutive month that PhonePe processed more than 10 billion UPI transactions. The platform first crossed the 10 billion monthly transaction milestone in March 2026.

UPI recorded 22.72 billion transactions during June, compared with 23.2 billion transactions in May. The total transaction value declined to Rs 28.92 lakh crore from Rs 29.90 lakh crore in the previous month.
PhonePe accounted for 46.15% of total UPI transaction volume in June. In value terms, the platform held a 49.07% share after processing transactions worth Rs 14.19 lakh crore.

title: Fractal reports Rs 72 Cr profit on Rs 913 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27
description: Fractal reported a 20% year on year increase in revenue in Q1 FY27, crossing the Rs 900 crore mark, while its profit surged 90% to Rs 72 crore during the period.
body: AI and advanced analytics firm Fractal has announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 20% year on year increase in revenue, crossing the Rs 900 crore mark, while its profit surged 90% to Rs 72 crore during the period.
Fractal’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 913 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 761 crore in Q1 FY26, according to disclosures sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Founded in 2000, Fractal earns revenue from analytics and consulting services, as well as licensing and subscription fees from its AI platforms, including Cogentiq, fflyfish.ai, and Kalaido.ai.
The firm also generated Rs 20 crore from non operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 932 crore during the quarter.

Employee benefit expenses, the company’s largest cost component, accounted for more than 77% of total spending and grew 14% year-on-year to Rs 632 crore in Q1 FY27. Higher depreciation, finance costs, and other overheads drove total expenses up 17% to Rs 818 crore during the quarter from Rs 700 crore in Q1 FY26.

As revenue grew at a slightly faster pace than expenses, Fractal reported a 90% year-on-year jump in profit to Rs 72 crore in the first quarter of FY27 from Rs 38 crore a year ago. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, however, profit declined 38% from Rs 116 crore recorded in Q4 FY26.

Fractal went public in February this year through a Rs 2,834 crore IPO, comprising both a fresh issue and an offer for sale. The public offering provided exits to existing investors, including Apax Partners and TPG Capital. The stock debuted at a 3% discount to its issue price. At the end of Thursday’s trading session, Fractal’s share price closed at Rs 866, with a total market capitalization of Rs 14,892 crore ($1.56 billion).

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [July 20 - July 25]
description: This week, 16 Indian startups raised nearly $164 million across 4 growth-stage including one undisclosed deal and 12 early-stage deals. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 16 Indian startups raised nearly $164 million across 4 growth-stage including one undisclosed deal and 12 early-stage deals. The week also witnessed one departure, two fund launches, and one ESOP.
In contrast, 19 startups had collectively secured about $271 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]
Growth-stage startups raised a total of $208.2 million across six deals this week, led by deeptech platform Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group with its $40 million Series B round.
Fintech startups Veriqus and BusinessNext also raised $40 million in a Series B each.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $44 million across 12 deals this week, led by quick commerce startup Plazza, which secured $15 million in a Series A round led by Accel, Elevation Capital and Nexus Venture Partners.

Among the other notable deals, healthtech startup CAROL.ai raised $10 million in a Series A round led by International Finance Corporation. Travel tech firm 30 Sundays secured $6.7 million in a pre-Series A round led by Bessemer Venture Partners and others.

title: Decoding PhonePe FY26: The Rs 364 Cr loss behind the Rs 2,792 Cr headline
description: Walmart-backed fintech PhonePe reported modest growth in FY26, but its reported loss of Rs 2,792 crore doesn't tell the complete story.
body: Walmart-backed fintech PhonePe reported modest growth in FY26, but its reported loss of Rs 2,792 crore doesn't tell the complete story. A closer look at the company's financial statements shows that a significant part of the loss came from non-cash accounting adjustments instead of its core ops.
Let's first look at where PhonePe's revenue came from.

The company reported operating revenue of Rs 7,920 crore in FY26. The bulk of this came from payment services, including transaction processing fees from bill payments, digital gold, and travel bookings. It also earned from platform fees, subscription fees for payment devices and smart speakers, advertising income, and its financial services businesses such as insurance, lending, stock broking, and mutual fund distribution. Together, these businesses contributed Rs 7,619 crore during the year.
In addition, PhonePe received Rs 286 crore as incentives from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Interest income and other non-operating gains pushed its total income to Rs 8,388 crore in FY26.

On the expense side, employee benefits remained the largest cost at Rs 4,386 crore. However, only Rs 1,994 crore, or around 45%, was paid as salaries. The remaining Rs 2,390 crore was booked as ESOP (employee stock option) expense.

Notably, around Rs 2,197 crore, or 91% of the ESOP expense, was a non-cash accounting charge. Since this does not involve an actual cash outflow, we have excluded it to understand the company's underlying operating performance.

Payment processing charges stood at Rs 1,907 crore during the year. Meanwhile, advertising and sales promotion expenses nearly doubled to Rs 956 crore. Including technology infrastructure, licensing fees, customer support, legal, logistics, and other administrative expenses, the company's total expenditure reached Rs 10,589 crore in FY26.

PhonePe also reported an exceptional loss of Rs 231 crore, largely due to goodwill impairment. Since this is another non-cash accounting adjustment and not related to regular operations, it has also been excluded from our adjusted loss calculation.

title: Electric commercial vehicle manufacturer Omega Seiki Mobility raises Rs 50 Cr
description: The company plans to expand its footprint across cargo three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, premium electric two-wheelers, and electric light commercial vehicles. It has
body: Electric commercial vehicle manufacturer Omega Seiki Mobility (OSM) has raised Rs 50 crore in a funding round from Securocorp Securities, Sangeeta Pareekh, Saket Aggarwal Family Office, and Vanshika Sharma.

The proceeds will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development (R&D), enhance its nationwide dealer and service network, and accelerate the rollout of next-generation electric mobility solutions, OSM said in a press release.

Founded in 2018 by Uday Narang, Omega Seiki Mobility is an electric vehicle manufacturer that focuses on commercial electric three-wheelers, two-wheelers, and light trucks for last-mile logistics. It operates under the Anglian Omega Group and has manufacturing facilities in Faridabad and Pune.

The Delhi-based company reported approximately Rs 333 crore in revenue in FY26, with Rs 7.3 crore in profit after tax (PAT) and an EBITDA margin of 7.7%. Its customers include Amazon, Flipkart, Zomato, BigBasket, Porter, Maersk, and Nestlé.
OSM has a presence in India’s commercial EV market across multiple vehicle categories.

The company plans to expand its footprint across cargo three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, premium electric two-wheelers, and electric light commercial vehicles. It has also collaborated with financial institutions and green mobility firms such as cKers Finance and Mufin Green to support retail financing and fleet deployment.

title: Bombay Shaving Company revenue jumps to Rs 635 Cr in FY26, nears break even
description: Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt. Ltd., the parent of Bombay Shaving Company, reported 2.4X growth in operating revenue in FY26 and posted its first-ever positive adjusted EBITDA of Rs 2 crore, led by strong sales growth.
body: Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt. Ltd., the parent company of Bombay Shaving Company, reported a 2.4X year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026. The company also posted its first-ever positive adjusted EBITDA of Rs 2 crore, led by strong sales growth during the fiscal year.
Bombay Shaving Company’s revenue from operations surged 139% to Rs 635 crore in FY26 from Rs 266 crore in FY25, its consolidated financial report sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) shows.

Visage Lines operates three businesses: Bombay Shaving Company, its flagship men's grooming brand; Bombae, focused on women's personal care; and 100Days, which provides digital commerce and e-commerce growth solutions for consumer brands.
The sale of men's and women's personal care products through Bombay Shaving Company and Bombae accounted for over 91% of the operating revenue at Rs 581 crore in FY26 from Rs 241 crore in FY25.
Meanwhile, revenue from sale of services doubled to Rs 48 crore in FY26. The company made an additional Rs 6 crore from interest income, which pushed its total revenue to Rs 641 crore in FY25.

In line with its sales growth, the cost of materials consumed was the largest overhead, which grew 2.8X to Rs 370 crore in FY26. To boost sales and strengthen brand visibility, the firm spent 24% of its overall expenditure on advertising and promotional activities, which increased by 55% to Rs 158 crore during the previous fiscal year.

Employee benefits expenses rose modestly by 9% to Rs 47 crore, which notably included Rs 7 crore in non-cash ESOP costs. Other overheads like delivery and handling charges, rent, IT, legal & professional expenses pushed overall expenses for Bombay Shaving Company parent by 98% to Rs 650 crore in FY25 from Rs 329 crore in FY25.

The Gurugram-based Company managed to reduce its net loss by 85% to Rs 9 crore in FY26 from Rs 58 crore in FY25. Notably, the firm posted an adjusted EBITDA (net of ESOP cost) of Rs 2 crore during FY26. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at -5.2% and -0.79%, respectively. On a unit basis, the company spent Rs 1.02 to earn a rupee in FY26.

title: Cactus Partners targets Rs 1,600 Cr Fund II, plans 13-15 investments: Report
description: Early-stage venture capital firm Cactus Partners is targeting a corpus of Rs 1,600 crore for its second fund, with plans to invest in 13–15 startups over the coming years. Snippets
body: Early-stage venture capital firm Cactus Partners is targeting a corpus of Rs 1,600 crore for its second fund, with plans to invest in 13–15 startups over the coming years.

According to Financial Express, citing an interview with Cactus Partners General Partner Amit Sharma, the firm plans to write initial cheques of Rs 60–100 crore and primarily back companies raising $10–20 million. It intends to lead funding rounds with investments of $6–10 million while syndicating the remaining capital with other investors.

Cactus Partners invests across advanced manufacturing, enterprise technology and consumer technology. Its key focus areas include robotics, semiconductors, defence, spacetech, electronics manufacturing, AI, machine learning, cybersecurity, healthtech and vertical software.

The firm's first fund, with a corpus of Rs 630 crore, has been deployed across 13 companies, including Lohum, Bellatrix Aerospace, Kapture CX, Indigrid Technologies and Brandworks. Over the past 15 months, it has made new investments in Bellatrix Aerospace, Showroom B2B and Brandworks Technologies, while participating in follow-on rounds of existing portfolio companies.

The firm remains focused on startups with proven product-market fit, sustainable unit economics and long-term growth potential rather than chasing high-valuation sectors. Cactus Partners is also evaluating opportunities in cybersecurity and quantum technologies.

title: Piper Serica leads Rs 15 Cr seed round in deep tech startup Yaanendriya
description: Its portfolio includes the SynCore series of navigation controllers for autonomous robotic platforms and the YDX series of high precision inertial sensors deployed across
body: Yaanendriya, a Bengaluru-based deep tech company building indigenous sensor, navigation, and control technologies for mobile robots and critical applications, has raised Rs 15 crore in a seed funding round led by Piper Serica.

The fresh funds will be used to strengthen research and development, accelerate product development, and expand its portfolio of high precision navigation systems for mission critical environments, Yaanendriya said in a press release.

Co-founded in February last year by Vamshi Bharadwaj M V, Vyshak Y, Vijay HP, and Aravind Thumbur, Yaanendriya develops indigenous sensor, navigation, and control technologies for robotics, aerospace, and other critical applications.

Its portfolio includes the SynCore series of navigation controllers for autonomous robotic platforms and the YDX series of high precision inertial sensors deployed across commercial applications globally. The company is also developing navigation systems and a hardware agnostic platform for space and other critical missions, along with high precision MEMS inertial sensors for the NewSpace sector.

Yaanendriya builds sensor and control platforms that enable autonomous systems, including drones, ground robots, spacecraft, and underwater vehicles, to sense motion, estimate their state, and maintain control in environments where GNSS is unavailable, unreliable, or intentionally disrupted.

Its SynCore navigation controllers combine inputs from multiple sensors to estimate orientation, position, and velocity while supporting real time stabilization and control. The platform is deployed by robotics companies across aerial, ground, and underwater applications in sectors such as defence, surveillance, and agriculture.
The company's YDX series of high precision inertial sensors is deployed across four continents in applications including motion capture for gaming, unmanned vehicles, and surgical robots.

title: Circular economy company Recykal invests Rs 10 Cr in Walbha Industries
description: Founded in 2015, Recykal develops digital platforms for waste management, deposit return systems, circular commerce, and AI enabled reverse vending machines. The
body: Circular economy company Recykal has made a strategic investment of Rs 10 crore in biomass briquette and pellet manufacturer Walbha Industries.

The investment marks Recykal’s entry into the bioenergy value chain, expanding its focus beyond waste management to biomass based industrial fuel. The partnership aims to connect Walbha’s biomass production with Recykal’s network of more than 620 brands and manufacturers, creating a demand channel for biomass fuel.

Walbha will also gain access to Recykal’s technology platform to digitise and streamline its supply chain, while Recykal’s enterprise customers will get access to verified biomass fuel. The investment will also support Walbha’s expansion into South India.
Walbha Industries operates a biomass production plant in Jhansi and supplies biomass briquettes and pellets to industrial customers across North and Central India.

Founded in 2015, Recykal develops digital platforms for waste management, deposit return systems, circular commerce, and AI enabled reverse vending machines. The company says it has channelised over 3 million metric tonnes of waste and works with more than 650 brands and over 5,000 aggregators and recyclers.

title: Pine Labs reports  Rs 737 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps over 4X
description: Fintech major Pine Labs has announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 20% year-on-year
body: Pine Labs reports  Rs 737 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps over 4X

Fintech major Pine Labs has announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 20% year-on-year growth in operating scale, while its profits jumped 4X to Rs 20 crore during the period.
Pine Labs’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 737 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 616 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Revenue from its digital infrastructure and transaction platform was the largest contributor, which grew 14.9% to Rs 499.12 crore in Q1 FY27. Its issuing and acquiring platform grew by 31% to Rs 237.8 crore during the same period.
The company added Rs 29 crore from non-operating activities, taking its total income to Rs 766 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 653 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a sequential basis, the Bengaluru-based firm’s revenue increased marginally by 5% compared to Rs 701 crore in Q4 FY26.

Employee benefits remained the largest cost centre for Pine Labs, accounting for 36.8% of its overall expenditure. Interestingly, this cost declined 7.9% to Rs 268 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 291 crore in Q1 FY26.

The cost of materials consumed increased 39% to Rs 107 crore, while transaction and related costs surged 61.7% to Rs 97 crore. Depreciation rose 12.3% to Rs 73 crore, whereas other expenses increased 10.9% to Rs 183 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenditure increased 10.6% to Rs 728 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 658 crore in Q1 FY26.

title: Global student living technology startup House of Student raises $2 Mn in seed round
description: The Gurugram and US-based startup says it has more than 2.5 million verified student rooms across over 25 countries, including the UK, US, Australia, Canada, New Zealand,
body: Global student living technology company House of Student has raised $2 million in a seed round through a combination of equity and debt. The round was co-led by Saltwater Sutra and Nirmitsu Inspirational Ventures, with participation from Gautam Verlekar, Glen Fernandes, Richard McCallum, Ali Moosa, and existing investor Unilodgers.
The fresh capital will be used to drive product innovation, expand housing supply, strengthen AI capabilities, and support global expansion, the company said in a press release.

Founded in February last year by Vaibhav Verma, House of Student operates a technology platform for student accommodation across global education destinations. It offers online booking and housing network management, and plans to expand into AI-enabled student support services.

Before House of Student, Verma founded Unilodgers, which the company says was the world’s first student housing marketplace. According to the company, Unilodgers was valued at $109 million in its first institutional funding round.

The Gurugram and US-based startup says it has more than 2.5 million verified student rooms across over 25 countries, including the UK, US, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UAE, Singapore, and 18 European countries.
House of Student competes with Uhomes, Amber, and Uniplaces.

title: UpGrad set to close Unacademy acquisition in three weeks; deal valued at Rs 1,955 Cr
description: The acquisition of Unacademy by upGrad has entered its final phase, with the transaction expected to close within the next three weeks, according to sources.
body: The acquisition of edtech platform Unacademy by upGrad has entered its final phase, with the transaction expected to close within the next three weeks, according to sources familiar with the matter.

Sources said that almost all institutional investors have signed the Share Subscription Agreement (SSA), while all angel investors have signed the Share Purchase Agreement (SPA), which leaves only the final formalities before the deal is completed.

According to sources, the all-stock transaction has been pegged at around Rs 1,955 crore. The current deal is slightly lower than the valuation discussed when the deal was announced earlier this year.

As part of the transaction, Unacademy co-founder Gaurav Munjal will continue as the company's CEO after the merger. Meanwhile, language learning platform Airlearn, which was incubated within Unacademy, is also part of the acquisition and will move under the upGrad umbrella.

Following the acquisition, upGrad is also consolidating the operations of Unacademy and its businesses. PrepLadder's headquarters has already been shifted from Chandigarh to Bengaluru, and Unacademy, PrepLadder, Airlearn and Graphy will operate from Bengaluru going forward.
In another key development, Unacademy's existing investors will receive one board seat in upGrad after the transaction is completed, according to sources.
Entrackr has reached out to Unacademy and upGrad for comments.

The acquisition, first announced earlier this year, marks one of the biggest consolidation moves in India's edtech sector. The transaction received regulatory clearance from the Competition Commission of India (CCI) earlier this month, paving the way for its completion. Once closed, the combined entity will bring together upGrad's higher education and upskilling business with Unacademy's test preparation, medical education and creator-led learning platforms.

title: BigBasket's B2C arm losses cross Rs 3,000 Cr in FY26
description: BigBasket's consumer-facing business reported a 7.7% rise in turnover to Rs 8,223 crore in FY26, while its losses widened 66% to Rs 3,073 crore during the fiscal year.
body: The battle for India's online grocery market has become more intense as platforms chase scale, speed, and profitability. While demand remains strong, profitability continues to remain elusive for most players. Against this backdrop, BigBasket posted marginal growth in FY26 with its operating revenue crossing Rs 8,000 crore, even as its core B2C business continued to bleed. The Tata Digital-backed firm's performance mirrors broader sector trends, where grocery delivery platforms continue to post heavy losses despite rapid expansion.

According to Tata Sons' FY26 annual report, Innovative Retail Concepts, which operates BigBasket's consumer-facing business, recorded a 7.7% increase in turnover to Rs 8,223 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,634 crore in the previous fiscal year. However, its losses widened 66% to Rs 3,073 crore from Rs 1,850 crore during the same period.

BigBasket's losses have risen sharply since its complete pivot to quick commerce in August 2024. The shift has raised operating costs as the company spends more on logistics, dark stores, discounts, and customer retention to compete in the rapidly expanding segment.

Meanwhile, BigBasket's B2B arm, Supermarket Grocery Supplies, which handles procurement and backend operations, reported flat revenue of Rs 2,298 crore in FY26, while its losses remained unchanged at Rs 102 crore during the fiscal year.
Together, the two entities reported Rs 10,521 crore in revenue in FY26, compared to Rs 9,861 crore in the previous fiscal year. Their combined losses stood at Rs 3,175 crore during the year.
Tata Digital, which acquired a majority stake in BigBasket in 2021, remains its largest shareholder with an 84.23% stake.

BigBasket's rival Zepto reported Rs 22,624 crore in revenue and a loss of Rs 5,905 crore in FY26, while quick commerce leader Blinkit posted Rs 15,664 crore in revenue and a positive adjusted EBITDA of Rs 102 crore in Q1 FY27.

At the group level, Tata Digital reported a 12% increase in revenue to Rs 35,990 crore in FY26 from Rs 32,188 crore in FY25. However, its net loss widened to Rs 4,974 crore from Rs 4,610 crore during the same period. The company's gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at Rs 46,515 crore in FY26.

title: Nykaa appoints former Instamart COO Ankit Jain to lead Nykaa Now
description: Beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has appointed former Instamart Chief Operating Officer Ankit Jain to lead Nykaa Now, its quick commerce business. Snippets
body: Beauty and fashion retailer Beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa has appointed former Instamart Chief Operating Officer Ankit Jain to lead Nykaa Now, its quick commerce business has appointed former Instamart Chief Operating Officer Ankit Jain to lead Nykaa Now, its quick commerce business, as the company expands its presence in the rapid delivery segment.
Jain joins Nykaa weeks after exiting Swiggy owned Instamart, where he served as COO. His departure was part of a series of leadership changes at the quick commerce platform.
He brings more than two decades of experience across supply chain, logistics and operations. Prior to Instamart, Jain held leadership roles at Flipkart and Unilever.

At Nykaa, Jain will lead Nykaa Now, the company's quick commerce vertical, which delivers beauty and personal care products within 30 to 60 minutes. He will oversee expansion of the business, supply chain operations, fulfilment infrastructure and technology led logistics.
Nykaa Now is currently available across 13 cities, including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru and Kolkata, and offers products across beauty, personal care and wellness categories.
As of June 30, Nykaa operated 324 offline stores across formats. The company has also been expanding its portfolio of owned brands, including Kay Beauty, Nykaa Cosmetics and Dot & Key.

title: Tata 1mg revenue nears Rs 3,000 Cr in FY26; loss narrows to Rs 287 Cr
description: Tata 1mg, the digital healthcare platform backed by Tata Digital, continued its growth momentum in FY26, with revenue nearing the Rs 3,000 crore mark
body: Tata 1mg, the digital healthcare platform backed by Tata Digital, continued its growth momentum in FY26, with revenue nearing the Rs 3,000 crore mark while reducing its losses during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Tata 1mg’s consolidated revenue grew 23% to Rs 2,936 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,392 crore in FY25 , according to Tata Sons’ annual report.

Tata 1mg is a healthtech platform that enables users to order allopathic, ayurvedic, and homeopathic medicines, vitamins, nutrition supplements, and other healthcare products online. The platform also offers diagnostics and other healthcare services.

The company’s revenue came from two entities: Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions Private Limited, which contributed Rs 2,440 crore, and Tata 1mg Technologies Private Limited, which added Rs 496 crore. Together, the two entities generated Rs 2,936 crore in revenue during FY26.

On the bottom line, Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions reported a loss of Rs 310 crore, while Tata 1mg Technologies remained profitable with a net profit of Rs 23 crore. On a combined basis, Tata 1mg posted a net loss of Rs 287 crore in FY26.

On the balance sheet, the combined Tata 1mg entities had total assets of Rs 2,268 crore at the end of FY26. Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions accounted for Rs 805 crore, while Tata 1mg Technologies held assets worth Rs 1,463 crore.
Their combined liabilities stood at Rs 1,601 crore, including Rs 1,509 crore for Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions and Rs 92 crore for Tata 1mg Technologies.

The combined entities reported a negative reserves and surplus balance of Rs 167 crore. While Tata 1mg Healthcare Solutions had a negative reserves and surplus balance of Rs 1,538 crore, Tata 1mg Technologies reported a positive reserves and surplus of Rs 1,371 crore.

title: Snitch acquires Berrylush to enter women's fashion segment
description: D2C fashion brand Snitch has acquired women's fashion label Berrylush, marking its entry into the women's apparel segment as it expands beyond menswear.
body: D2C fashion brand Snitch has acquired women's fashion label Berrylush, marking its entry into the women's apparel segment as it expands beyond menswear.
The company did not disclose the financial details of the transaction.

Berrylush will continue to operate under its existing brand while leveraging Snitch's capabilities across product development, technology, supply chain, marketing, and omnichannel retail, the company said in a press release.

"Entering women's fashion has always been part of our long-term vision. Instead of starting from zero, we saw an opportunity to build on Berrylush's strong foundation," said Siddharth Dungarwal, founder and CEO of Snitch.

As part of the integration, Snitch will work with Berrylush co-founder Anusha Chandrashekar and the existing team to accelerate product innovation, expand its omnichannel presence, and strengthen the customer experience.

The acquisition comes a little over a year after Snitch raised $40 million in its Series B funding round led by 360 ONE Asset, with participation from existing investors IvyCap Ventures and SWC Global. The company has raised more than $53 million to date.

According to the company's annual financial statements, Snitch's revenue from operations grew 81% to Rs 900 crore in FY26 from Rs 498 crore in FY25, while continuing to scale its omnichannel business. The acquisition of Berrylush marks the company's first major expansion beyond the menswear category as it looks to build a broader portfolio of fashion brands.

title: Kissht clocks Rs 670 Cr revenue and Rs 95 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
description: Digital lending platform Kissht reported its first quarterly results for the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company's operating revenue grew 45% year-on-year in the quarter, while its profit increased 58% to Rs 95 crore.
body: Digital lending platform Kissht reported its first quarterly results for the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company's operating revenue grew 45% year-on-year in the quarter, while its profit increased 58% to Rs 95 crore.
Kissht’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 670 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 463 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.

Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, provides small-ticket consumer loans and has scaled aggressively through partnerships with merchants across electronics, fashion, travel, and other categories. The company primarily earns interest income from these loans, although a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter was not disclosed.
The company also earned Rs 7 crore from non operating sources, raising its total revenue to Rs 677 crore.

Kissht continued to expand its lending business during the quarter, with its assets under management (AUM) growing 61% year-on-year and 13% sequentially to Rs 8,001 crore. The company has cumulatively served over 12.25 million customers, a 26% increase from a year ago. Its off-book AUM stood at Rs 4,284 crore, accounting for 53.6% of the total portfolio, reflecting its capital-light partnership model.

Impairment on financial instruments remained one of the largest expense heads for the fintech platform, accounting for over 23% of the total cost base. The expense grew 28% year on year to Rs 128 crore in Q1 FY27, while finance costs increased 39% to Rs 82 crore.

Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 71 crore, while spending on marketing, legal and professional services, and IT expenses drove the company's total expenditure up 42% year on year to Rs 549 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 386 crore in the same quarter last year.

In the end, strong revenue growth helped the Mumbai-based company post a 58% year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 95 crore in Q1 FY27. On a sequential basis, profit rose 16% from Rs 82 crore in the preceding quarter (Q4 FY26).

title: TBO Tek’s Q1 FY27 revenue jumps 81% to Rs 926 Cr; profit grows 32%
description: Travel distribution platform TBO Tek reported an 81.2% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue for the first quarter of FY27, while its profit increased 31.7%
body: Travel distribution platform TBO Tek reported an 81.2% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue for the first quarter of FY27, while its profit increased 31.7% during the same period.
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 926 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 511 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Hotel and package bookings remained TBO Tek’s largest revenue stream, contributing Rs 800 crore in Q1 FY27, up 89.1% from Rs 423 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from air ticketing increased marginally to Rs 81 crore from Rs 78 crore, while other operating revenue climbed to Rs 45 crore from Rs 10.4 crore.
Including Rs 13 crore in other income, the company’s total income stood at Rs 939 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 524 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a sequential basis, operating revenue grew 13.8% from Rs 814 crore in Q4 FY26.

On the expense front, service fees remained the largest cost component, rising to Rs 373 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 179 crore, while depreciation and finance costs stood at Rs 33 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively.
Overall expenditure grew 83.1% to Rs 835 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 456 crore in Q1 FY26.
Despite higher expenses, TBO Tek’s profit increased to Rs 83 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 63 crore in Q1 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit rose 38.3% from Rs 60 crore in Q4 FY26.

title: Blackbuck crosses Rs 200 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit rises 24%
description: Online trucking platform BlackBuck reported a 42% year-on-year growth in its operating scale in Q1 FY27, while its profit increased 24% to Rs 42 crore.
body: Online trucking platform BlackBuck has released its financial results for the first quarter of FY27 today. The Bengaluru-based company reported a 42% year-on-year growth in its operating scale during the quarter, while its profit increased 24% to Rs 42 crore.
Blackbuck's revenue from operations grew to Rs 204 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 144 crore in Q1 FY26, its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show.

Revenue from truck operator services remained BlackBuck's primary source of income, contributing 98.5% of its operating revenue of Rs 201 crore in Q1 FY27. Its lending business added Rs 3.2 crore during the quarter. The company also earned Rs 16 crore from interest income, taking its total revenue to Rs 220 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 160 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.
On a quarterly basis, Blackbuck’s operating revenue increased over 10% compared to Rs 185 crore in Q4 FY26.

Employee benefit expenses accounted for over 24% of BlackBuck's total expenditure and increased 16% year-on-year to Rs 43 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 37 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.
Depreciation and other operating expenses pushed BlackBuck's total expenditure to Rs 178 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 114 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.

BlackBuck reported a 24% year-on-year growth in profit to Rs 42 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 34 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. On a sequential basis, however, the company's profit declined 36% from Rs 66 crore in Q4 FY26.
As of 2:35 PM (today), Blackbuck’s share trading at around Rs 530, with a total market capitalization of Rs 9,679 crore ($1.02 billion).

title: Anicut Capital launches Rs 250 Cr seed fund to back 20 early-stage startups
description: Alternative investment firm Anicut Capital has launched a Rs 250 crore seed fund to invest in around 20 early-stage startups over the next three years. Snippets
body: Alternative investment firm Anicut Capital has launched a Rs 250 crore seed fund to invest in around 20 early-stage startups over the next three years. The fund will focus on seed and pre-Series A companies across sectors, excluding real estate.

The firm plans to invest up to $1 million in each startup and will follow up with additional capital through its growth equity platform as portfolio companies scale. The fund follows Anicut's first seed fund launched in 2020.

According to the firm, the new fund will back startups building scalable businesses with strong unit economics and large market opportunities. It will also provide founders with post-investment support, including strategic guidance, fundraising assistance and access to its investor network.
Founded in 2015, Anicut Capital manages more than Rs 3,500 crore in assets across private credit, seed, growth equity and late-stage equity strategies.
Its portfolio includes startups across sectors such as SaaS, consumer, fintech, logistics and deeptech.
Recently, Anicut has invested in Wow! Momo in debt round. Entrackr exclusively reported the dent round.

title: Exclusive: OfBusiness reports consolidated profit of Rs 724 Cr on Rs 20,645 Cr revenue in FY26
description: IPO-bound B2B commerce and financing platform OfBusiness reported a 21% year-on-year growth in its profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 724 crore in FY26 from Rs 597 crore in the previous fiscal.
body: IPO-bound B2B commerce and financing platform OfBusiness reported a 21% year-on-year growth in its profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 724 crore in FY26 from Rs 597 crore in the previous fiscal.
Its consolidated revenue declined 7% to Rs 20,645 crore in FY26 from Rs 22,241 crore in FY25, as the company discontinued select low return business lines.

The company's commerce business, which spans metals, chemicals, apparel and food processing, recorded a revenue of Rs 19,174 crore during the fiscal year. Its EBITDA grew 39% to Rs 769 crore in FY26 from Rs 575 crore in FY25, while EBITDA margin expanded to 4% from 2.6% a year ago.

OfBusiness also reported a sharp improvement in cash generation, with operating cash flow from its commerce business rising to Rs 1,302 crore in FY26 from Rs 715 crore in the previous fiscal. The company turned free cash flow to firm (FCFF) positive for the first time, reporting Rs 390 crore during the year.

Its financing arm, Oxyzo Financial Services, reported an asset base of Rs 11,800 crore in FY26, 28% higher than the previous fiscal. The lending business posted a return on assets of 3.8% and maintained a gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio of 0.75%.

Founded in 2015 by Asish Mohapatra, Ruchi Kalra, Bhuvan Gupta and Vasant Sridhar, OfBusiness operates a technology-led platform that offers SMEs raw material procurement, working capital financing, and tender intelligence solutions.

Its tender intelligence platform, BidAssist, has crossed 1.5 million business users and aggregates over 50,000 live tenders daily from authorities and portals across India. The platform uses AI to match tenders with business profiles, helps users track win rates and competitors in live bids, and serves as a customer acquisition channel for OfBusiness's commerce and financing businesses.
The company's workforce has also crossed 30,000 employees, nearly doubling over the past year, led by the expansion of its apparel business in South India.

title: Revspot raises $4.8 Mn in Series A round co-led by Inflexor and Info Edge Ventures
description: Bengaluru-based AI startup Revspot has raised $4.8 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Inflexor Ventures and Info Edge Ventures. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based AI startup Revspot has raised $4.8 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Inflexor Ventures and Info Edge Ventures. The round also saw participation from Pentathlon Ventures, Silicon Road Ventures and existing investor Titan Capital.
The startup had previously raised $1.4 million in a seed funding round in 2024 led by Info Edge Ventures and Titan Capital, with participation from Kunal Shah.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its product and engineering teams, expand its AI-powered buyer intelligence and lead qualification platform, enter new high-ticket B2C sectors and grow its presence in selected international markets.
Founded in 2024 by Darshan Subash, Chirag Wadhera and Varun Garg, Revspot develops an AI-native platform that automates lead generation and qualification for businesses.
Its platform combines consumer intelligence, campaign analytics, lead enrichment, Voice AI, WhatsApp engagement and sales handoff to help companies identify and qualify potential customers.
Revspot currently serves more than 50 customers across sectors including real estate, education, automotive and wealth management. The startup is also expanding into the broader BFSI segment.

Alongside its expansion plans, Revspot is developing Spot, an orchestration platform that integrates campaign planning, lead enrichment, Voice AI and lead quality feedback into a single workflow for qualified pipeline generation.

title: CarTrade reports Rs 201 Cr revenue and Rs 57 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
description: Automobile classifieds platform CarTrade announced its financial results for the first quarter of FY27 on Wednesday, reporting over 16% year-on-year
body: Automobile classifieds platform CarTrade announced its financial results for the first quarter of FY27 on Wednesday, reporting over 16% year-on-year growth in its revenue from operations. The company's profit also increased 21% to Rs 57 crore during the quarter.
CarTrade’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 201 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 173 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The Mumbai-based company operates across three key segments: Consumer, Remarketing, and Classifieds. The Consumer segment remained the largest contributor, with Rs 78 crore in revenue during Q1 FY27, followed by Remarketing at Rs 67 crore and Classifieds at Rs 62 crore, before Rs 6.4 crore in intersegment eliminations.
Besides its core operations, CarTrade recorded Rs 29 crore in non-operating income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 230 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 199 crore in Q1 FY26.
On a quarterly basis, its operating revenue declined marginally from Rs 203 crore in the previous quarter (Q4 FY26).

On the cost side, employee benefits remained the largest expense, accounting for nearly 55% of the company’s total expenditure. This cost increased to Rs 83 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 75 crore in Q1 FY26. Other expenses stood at Rs 55 crore, while depreciation and finance costs were Rs 11 crore and Rs 3.2 crore, respectively.
CarTrade’s overall expenditure increased 7% to Rs 152 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 142 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.

Growth across its operating segments, coupled with a relatively controlled increase in expenditure, helped CarTrade's profit rise 21.3% to Rs 57 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 47 crore in Q1 FY26. On a sequential basis, however, its profit declined nearly 20% from Rs 71 crore in Q4 FY26.

title: Ferns N Petals plans 2028 IPO as it eyes 25% annual growth
description: Ferns N Petals (FNP), an omni-channel gifting and floral retail company, is planning to go public by the end of 2028 as it looks to accelerate its expansion plans and pursue acquisitions, according to Reuters.
body: Ferns N Petals (FNP), an omni-channel gifting and floral retail company, is planning to go public by the end of 2028 as it looks to accelerate its expansion plans and pursue acquisitions, according to Reuters.

The Lighthouse-backed company is targeting an annual revenue growth of around 25% over the next few years, Global CEO Pawan Gadia told Reuters. The IPO proceeds will be deployed towards expanding its business and acquiring brands in the gifting space.

FNP reported a revenue of Rs 1,085 crore in FY26, reflecting a 25% year-on-year growth. The company is also sharpening its focus on profitability and expects its core earnings margin to improve to 5–6% this fiscal from 2.5% in the previous year.

Founded in 1994, Ferns N Petals (FNP) is an omnichannel gifting platform that sells flowers, cakes, and personalized gifts through its website, third-party e-commerce marketplaces, company-owned stores, and franchise outlets.
FNP operates across India, the UAE, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar, with India contributing nearly 55% of its revenue, and plans to expand into Malaysia and additional Gulf markets.

As part of its expansion strategy, the company plans to increase its retail footprint to 350 stores by FY28 from around 280 currently. While the brand will continue opening company-owned stores in metro cities, it plans to adopt a franchise-led model in smaller towns.

FNP has raised around $27 million in funding to date, with Lighthouse among its key investors. Beyond its gifting business, the company also operates hospitality and wedding ventures under Udman Hotels and FNP Weddings and Events. It competes with players such as IGP (Indian Gifts Portal), FlowerAura, Winni, and Archies.

title: Building materials quick commerce startup Fixxly raises $5.5 Mn in seed round
description: Bengaluru-based building materials quick commerce startup Fixxly has raised $5.5 million in a seed funding round from Accel, Fireside Ventures. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based building materials quick commerce startup Fixxly has raised $5.5 million in a seed funding round from Accel, Fireside Ventures and Lightspeed India Partners.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its technology platform and scale operations ahead of its commercial launch on September 1. It will begin operations in Bengaluru before expanding to other cities.

Founded in 2026 by Shezan Bhojani and Sachith Varma, Fixxly is building an AI-powered quick commerce platform for building materials. The platform enables contractors, electricians, plumbers, carpenters, painters, interior designers and homeowners to order products such as plywood, paint, electricals, lighting, hardware and plumbing supplies, with deliveries in as little as 30 minutes.
The startup operates an AI-powered supply network that fulfils orders through a network of local dark stores, matching real-time inventory, proximity and demand.

Before launching Fixxly, Bhojani co-founded home interiors startup DesignCafe, which merged with HomeLane in 2024. His cofounder, Sachith Varma, previously led supply chain design at Zepto and managed last-mile operations at Flipkart.

title: Zepto postpones IPO, may raise Rs 1,000 Cr in pre IPO round
description: Quick commerce major Zepto has postponed its IPO plans, according to multiple media reports, amid ongoing valuation discussions with investors.
body: Quick commerce major Zepto has postponed its IPO plans, according to multiple media reports, amid ongoing valuation discussions with investors.

The company may also raise more than Rs 1,000 crore (around $105 million) through a pre IPO placement, according to a Moneycontrol report. Existing investors including Glade Brook, General Catalyst, Goodwater Capital and Nexus Venture Partners are expected to participate in the round.

Under SEBI regulations, IPO bound companies can raise up to 20% of their proposed fresh issue through a pre IPO placement, with the amount raised adjusted against the fresh issue component of the public offering.

Zepto had originally planned to raise around Rs 8,000 crore through its IPO. In June, the company filed its updated draft red herring prospectus with SEBI for a fresh issue of Rs 8,010 crore and received the regulator's approval about a month later. The IPO size has also reportedly been trimmed to around Rs 5,000–6,000 crore
Entrackr has reached out to Zepto for comments.

The Bengaluru based company doubled its operating revenue to Rs 11,110 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,454 crore in FY25. However, its losses widened 26% to Rs 5,905 crore , making it one of the largest loss making startups in the country.
As of the end of FY26, it had current assets of Rs 9,638 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 973 crore.
