title: Aham Housing Finance raises Rs 100 Cr led by Sanmar Group
description: According to the company, it has recorded growth across key operating metrics over the past few years while maintaining a prudent risk management framework.
body: Technology-led affordable housing finance company Aham Housing Finance has raised Rs 100 crore in a follow-on funding round led by The Sanmar Group.
Existing investors, including Negen Capital, one of the company’s early institutional backers, also participated in the round.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the company’s lending capacity, expand its presence in underserved housing markets, deepen its footprint in existing geographies, enter select new markets, and continue investing in technology, Aham Housing Finance said in a press release.
Led by Venkatesh Kannappan, Aham Housing Finance is focused on providing affordable home loans to underserved and emerging borrower segments across India.
The company uses data-driven underwriting, localized distribution, and risk management practices to serve self-employed and first-time homebuyers who are often underserved by traditional lenders.

According to the company, it has recorded growth across key operating metrics over the past few years while maintaining a prudent risk management framework. It said it remains focused on expanding financial inclusion through responsible lending.

title: IPV leads seed round in hair beauty and styling brand Truth & Hair
description: Hair beauty and styling brand Truth & Hair has raised Rs 5.4 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV). The brand also featured on Shark Tank India Season 5,
body: Hair beauty and styling brand Truth & Hair has raised Rs 5.4 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV). The brand also featured on Shark Tank India Season 5, where it secured an on air deal offer from Varun Alagh, co-founder of Mamaearth.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the brand's positioning in the hair makeup and styling segment, drive product innovation, expand marketing efforts, and scale its distribution network, Truth & Hair said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Saumya Alagh and Shailesh Singh, Gurugram based Truth & Hair is a D2C hair beauty and styling brand focused on products beyond the traditional shampoo and conditioner category. Its portfolio includes the Root Touch Up Hair Mascara, 3 in 1 Curly Styler, and Flyaway Wand, designed for straight, wavy, and curly hair.
According to the company, its products are formulated to address multiple hair textures rather than focusing on a single hair type.
As per market research, India's hair care and styling products market was valued at $5.85 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach $8.93 billion by 2029, growing at a CAGR of 8.8%.
The company says it focuses on science backed formulations and aims to make hair styling and hair makeup products accessible to a wider consumer base.

title: Vault onboards Virat and Vikas Kohli as strategic investors
description: Founded in 2023 by Mukesh Gogia, Vault by Virat Kohli is a premium fitness and wellness chain. The company has partnered with fitness equipment and recovery brands such
body: Premium franchise led fitness chain Vault by Virat Kohli has onboarded cricketer and entrepreneur Virat Kohli and his brother Vikas Kohli as strategic investors, formalising a combined 28% equity stake in the company.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate the company's national expansion through its franchise partner led growth strategy, Vault by Virat Kohli said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by Mukesh Gogia, Vault by Virat Kohli is a premium fitness and wellness chain. The company has partnered with fitness equipment and recovery brands such as Matrix, Torque USA, and Precor for strength and cardio equipment, while Hyperice powers its dedicated recovery rooms.

According to the company, Vault combines fitness equipment, structured training programmes, and recovery focused facilities. Its offerings span strength training, functional fitness, recovery, and lifestyle wellness.

The Delhi based company has a presence across Tier I and Tier II cities, including Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Gorakhpur, and Hyderabad. As part of its next phase of expansion, it plans to increase its presence in Tier III cities, targeting demand for organised premium fitness infrastructure.

According to the company, Vault serves more than 30,000 members across its network. Following the revised equity structure, it plans to expand to more than 50 operational clubs by the end of the year, with club sizes ranging from around 6,000 sq ft to 25,000 sq ft.

title: Swiggy Q1 FY27 revenue jumps 37% to Rs 6,812 Cr, loss narrows 34%
description: Swiggy reported a 37% YoY increase in its operating revenue to Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4,961 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company also narrowed its losses by 34% during the period.
body: Foodtech and quick commerce major Swiggy reported a 37% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue to Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4,961 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company also narrowed its losses by 34% during the period.

Scootsy Logistics, Swiggy’s supply chain and distribution arm, remained its largest revenue contributor, accounting for nearly 47% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from the segment rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 3,195 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,259 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Swiggy’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses also posted strong growth during the quarter. Revenue from food delivery increased 23% year-on-year to Rs 2,208 crore, while quick commerce arm Instamart recorded a 53% jump to Rs 1,232 crore.
The remaining operating revenue came from segments such as dine-out services and other initiatives, including Bolt and Toing.
The company also reported Rs 211 crore in other income. As a result, its total income rose to Rs 7,023 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 5,048 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

On the expense front, procurement of materials remained Swiggy's largest cost centre at Rs 2,975 crore during the quarter. Employee benefit expenses declined marginally by 3.5% to Rs 662 crore. Advertising and sales promotion expenses stood at Rs 1,160 crore, while delivery costs amounted to Rs 1,750 crore. Other operational expenses pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 7,813 crore in Q1 FY27.

Segment-wise, Swiggy's food delivery business remained EBITDA positive with an EBITDA of Rs 299 crore, while its quick commerce arm, Instamart, continued to incur losses and reported a negative EBITDA of Rs 651 crore during the quarter.
Swiggy's losses narrowed 34% year-on-year to Rs 791 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,197 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, aided by strong revenue growth.

title: Arboreal Bioinnovations raises Rs 230 Cr in Series A led by Edelweiss’s EAAA and Omnivore
description: Specialty food and nutraceutical ingredients technology company Arboreal Bioinnovations has raised Rs 230 crore (over $24 million) in a Series A funding round co-led by EAAA.

title: InCred Finance reports Rs 759 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit jumps 83%
description: InCred Financial Services, the lending arm of InCred Holdings, posted a 31% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue, while profit surged 83% to Rs 172 crore in Q1 FY27.
body: InCred Financial Services, the lending arm of InCred Holdings, carried its growth momentum into FY27 after reporting a strong financial performance in FY26. The company posted a 31% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue, while profit surged 83% to Rs 172 crore in Q1 FY27.
According to its standalone financial statements sourced from BSE, the Mumbai-based company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 759 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 580 crore in Q1 FY26.

Founded in 2017 by Bhupinder Singh, InCred Finance is a retail-focused NBFC that provides personal loans, education loans, secured business loans, MSME financing, and lending solutions for financial institutions.

Interest income remained the company's largest revenue driver, contributing nearly 90% of its operating revenue. Revenue from this segment rose to Rs 682 crore in Q1 FY27. Fee and commission income added Rs 67 crore, while the rest came from gains on fair value changes in financial assets.
Including Rs 3 crore from non-operating income, InCred Finance's total income stood at Rs 762 crore during the quarter.

InCred Finance's loan book (excluding assigned loans) grew to Rs 14,809 crore at the end of June 2026, driven by continued momentum across its five lending verticals. The company also reported an improvement in asset quality, with gross NPAs declining to 2.0% from 2.3% a year ago and net NPAs easing to 0.7% from 0.9%. Its net worth stood at Rs 4,244 crore as of June 30, 2026.

Finance costs remained the largest expense for InCred Finance, accounting for 51% of its total expenditure. These costs rose 26% year-on-year to Rs 270 crore in Q1 FY27. Employee benefit expenses increased 39% to Rs 131 crore during the quarter.

Losses from impaired financial instruments, including loan write-offs, declined 44% year-on-year to Rs 43 crore. Depreciation charges, along with legal, collection, advertising, travel and other overheads, pushed the company's total expenditure up 15% to Rs 533 crore from Rs 465 crore in Q1 FY26.

title: Apna Mart raises Rs 120 Cr in Series C round led by Accel, Fundamentum
description: Franchise-led omnichannel grocery and FMCG startup Apna Mart has raised Rs 120 crore (around $12.7 million) in a Series C funding round co-led by existing. News
body: Franchise-led omnichannel grocery and FMCG startup Apna Mart has raised Rs 120 crore (around $12.7 million) in a Series C funding round co-led by existing investors Accel India and Fundamentum, with participation from Peak XV Partners.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the company's working capital and support its expansion across India. The transaction was advised by VERTICES PARTNERS, which acted as legal counsel to Apna Mart.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the funding round in June after accessing the company's regulatory filings.
The round valued the Gurugram-based company at around Rs 1,470 crore, nearly double its previous valuation of Rs 738 crore, as per Entrackr's estimates.

Founded by Abhishek Singh and Chetan Garg, Apna Mart operates a franchise-led omnichannel quick commerce platform focused on Tier II and Tier III cities. The startup delivers groceries through a neighborhood store-led model and competes with Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and Zepto.
The Series C round comes a little over a year after Apna Mart raised around $25 million in its Series B funding led by Accel and Fundamentum.

The company recently said its operating revenue grew 2.5X to Rs 500 crore in FY26, although it did not disclose its bottom line. In FY25, it reported operating revenue of Rs 185 crore and a net loss of Rs 76 crore.
Apna Mart also laid off around 10% of its workforce this year and shifted its headquarters from Bengaluru to Gurugram.

title: Sid’s Farm raises over Rs 81 Cr in pre-Series B round
description: Hyderabad-based dairy brand Sid’s Farm has raised over Rs 81 crore ($8.4 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by Omnivore. News.
body: Hyderabad-based dairy brand Sid’s Farm has raised over Rs 81 crore ($8.4 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by Omnivore, NSFO, Dodla Dairy, Next Bharat Ventures and LIO, along with a consortium of other investors.

In June 2024, Sid's Farm raised $10 million in a Series A round co-led by Omnivore and Narotam Sekhsaria Family Office (NSFO), after securing $1 million in a bridge round from its customers and their referrals in January 2023.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its supply chain, expand manufacturing and distribution capabilities, invest in product innovation, deepen partnerships with dairy farmers and enter new markets.

Founded in 2016 by Dr. Kishore Indukuri, Sid’s Farm operates a direct-to-consumer dairy business offering milk and other food products. The company claims each batch of milk undergoes testing across more than 45 quality and safety parameters, with over 10,000 quality tests conducted daily.
Sid’s Farm currently works with more than 5,000 dairy farmers and provides support through fair procurement practices, veterinary services and farmer education programmes.
The firm  serves over 50,000 families across multiple cities and plans to use the latest funding to accelerate its next phase of growth while expanding access to its dairy products in new regions.
It competes with Country Delight and Akshayakalpa Organic.

title: Drone startup SUIND raises Rs 20.5 Cr in seed round led by Transition VC
description: Agriculture drone startup SUIND has raised Rs 20.5 crore ($2.2 million) in a seed funding round led by Transition VC. The round also saw. Snippets
body: Agriculture drone startup SUIND has raised Rs 20.5 crore ($2.2 million) in a seed funding round led by Transition VC. The round also saw participation from IIMA Ventures.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the development recently.

The fresh capital will be used to scale the commercial deployment of its agriculture drone platform, accelerate the development of its autonomous surveillance and infrastructure inspection drone, strengthen its proprietary autonomy technology and expand its engineering team.

Founded in 2020 by Kunal Shrivastava and Kevin Kleber, SUIND develops autonomous unmanned aerial systems that use computer vision for navigation instead of relying primarily on GPS. Its technology enables drones to operate in low-altitude and GPS-denied environments.

The startup has commercially deployed its DGCA-certified autonomous spraying drone, Bumblebee, across farms and plantations. It is also developing WASP, an autonomous aerial platform for industrial monitoring, security, surveillance and defence applications.

Over the next 12 to 24 months, SUIND plans to scale the manufacturing and deployment of Bumblebee while preparing WASP for commercial launch. The agriculture drone ecosystem in India has witnessed growing interest in recent years, driven by demand for precision farming and government support for drone adoption. Suind competes with startups such as Marut Drones, Garuda Aerospace, IoTechWorld Avigation, BharatRohan, and Dhaksha Unmanned Systems.

title: InstaHelp earns Rs 29 per order while losing Rs 346 in Q1 FY27
description: Urban Company’s quick home services platform InstaHelp recorded an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 346 per order in Q1 FY27, an improvement from Rs 447 per order in Q4 FY26,
body: Urban Company’s quick home services platform InstaHelp recorded an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 346 per order in Q1 FY27, an improvement from Rs 447 per order in Q4 FY26, even as its overall losses widened during the quarter.

InstaHelp’s adjusted EBITDA loss stood at Rs 132 crore in Q1 FY27 as compared to Rs 119 crore in the preceding quarter. The platform fulfilled 3.82 million orders during the quarter, up 43% from 2.67 million orders in Q4 FY26.

The platform generated Rs 11.22 crore in revenue during the quarter, up from Rs 9 crore in Q4 FY26 . Its net transaction value (NTV) increased 32% quarter on quarter to Rs 52.9 crore from Rs 40.1 crore.

Launched in March 2025, InstaHelp’s NTV has grown steadily since its launch, increasing from Rs 27.6 crore in Q3 FY26 to Rs 40.1 crore in Q4 FY26 and Rs 52.9 crore in Q1 FY27. Fulfilled orders also increased from 1.6 million in Q3 FY26 to 2.67 million in Q4 FY26 and 3.82 million in Q1 FY27.

At the same time, average order value declined to Rs 138 in Q1 FY27 from Rs 150 in the previous quarter amid competitive pricing in the segment. Based on its operating revenue and fulfilled orders, InstaHelp’s revenue per order also declined to around Rs 29.4 from Rs 33.3 in the preceding quarter.

Despite the increase in absolute losses, InstaHelp’s loss per order declined nearly 23% quarter on quarter to Rs 346 from Rs 447. Urban Company attributed the improvement to higher network density as order volumes scaled. In Q3 FY26, the platform’s adjusted EBITDA loss per order stood at Rs 381.
“In this phase of category development, we are prioritising market leadership over everything else,” Urban Company said in its shareholder letter.

The company expects margins to remain under pressure in the near term as aggressive discounting continues across the market. Urban Company said current pricing levels are unsustainable for the industry and that pricing normalisation could lead to a one-time adjustment in demand across the category.

title: Urban Company posts 92 Cr loss on Rs 528 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27
description: Home services marketplace Urban Company reported a strong 44% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in Q1 FY27. However, the company slipped into a loss of Rs 92 crore during the quarter amid its continued push for InstaHelp.
body: Home services marketplace Urban Company reported a strong 44% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in Q1 FY27. However, the company slipped into a loss of Rs 92 crore during the quarter amid its continued push for InstaHelp.

According to the company’s quarterly financial results, Urban Company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 528 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 367 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The India Consumer Services business, excluding InstaHelp, remained Urban Company's largest revenue contributor, accounting for more than 67% of its operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew 31% year-on-year to Rs 356 crore during the quarter.

The company's Native brands business recorded a 58% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 95 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 60 crore in the year-ago period, while its international business grew 81% to contribute Rs 65 crore.

Meanwhile, InstaHelp, Urban Company's quick-service housekeeping vertical launched in March last year, generated Rs 11.11 crore in revenue during the quarter. However, the segment reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 131.58 crore, up 11% sequentially from Rs 118.73 crore in Q4 FY26.

The company also earned Rs 38 crore from non-operating sources during the quarter, taking its overall income to Rs 566 crore. On a quarterly basis, overall revenue grew by 23% from Rs 462 crore in Q4 FY26.

On the expense side, Urban Company's employee benefit expenses rose 53% year-on-year to Rs 151 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 99 crore in the same quarter last year, while its cost of materials increased 45% to Rs 100 crore.
Finance costs, depreciation and amortisation expenses, along with other undisclosed costs, pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 640 crore during the quarter from Rs 384 crore in Q1 FY26.

title: Shadowfax clocks Rs 1,358 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27, profit rises over 8X
description: Shadowfax Technologies reported a 65% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in Q1 FY27. Its profit also surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore during the quarter.
body: Shadowfax Technologies reported a strong performance in Q1 FY27, with the logistics and last-mile delivery firm recording a 65% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. Its profit also surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore during the quarter.
The company’s revenue from operations surged to Rs 1,358 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 824 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from NSE.

Shadowfax operates in the last-mile and hyperlocal logistics segment, catering to ecommerce marketplaces, D2C brands, and quick commerce platforms. The company competes with Delhivery, XpressBees, Ecom Express, and Ekart in a highly competitive market.
The company also recorded Rs 21 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,379 crore in Q1 FY27. On a sequential basis, total income grew 10% from Rs 1,253 crore reported in Q4 FY26.

The company did not disclose a detailed expense breakup. Its employee benefit expenses rose 49% year-on-year to Rs 124 crore, while depreciation and amortisation costs increased 82% to Rs 40 crore. Overall, Shadowfax's total expenditure grew 60% year-on-year to Rs 1,314 crore during the quarter.

Shadowfax Technologies' profit surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 8 crore in the year-ago quarter, as the company's revenue growth continued to outpace the increase in its expenses.
As of 12:41 PM today, Shadowfax's share price was up 8% at around Rs 237, valuing the company at Rs 13,848 crore (approximately $1.45 billion).

title: Exclusive: Atomberg converts into public company, appoints independent directors ahead of IPO
description: Consumer appliances startup Atomberg has converted itself into a public company, marking a key milestone in its journey towards an initial public offering (IPO).
body: Consumer appliances startup Atomberg has converted itself into a public company, marking a key milestone in its journey towards an initial public offering (IPO).

The company's shareholders have approved a special resolution to change the name of its parent entity from Atomberg Technologies Private Limited to Atomberg Technologies Limited, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.

As part of its IPO preparations, the company has appointed three independent directors: Subhasis Chaudhuri, former Director of IIT Bombay; Suman Gopalan, former CHRO at Freshworks; and Anand Vora, former CFO of UPL. The appointments strengthen its board ahead of the filing of its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).

Founded in 2012 by Manoj Meena and Sibabrata (Shibam) Das, Atomberg is best known for its BLDC motor-powered ceiling fans and has since expanded into mixer grinders, smart locks, water purifiers, and other home appliances. In Apr 2026, the company elevated Shibam Das as CEO , while Meena took over as Chairman and Managing Director. He now also leads Atomberg Innovation, the company's engineering arm focused on motors, drives, and cooling technologies.

As per an Economic Times report, Atomberg's engineering arm is in talks to raise Rs 150–200 crore in a funding round led by General Catalyst at a valuation of Rs 1,500–1,700 crore. The report added that the company is targeting a Rs 2,000 crore IPO, with Avendus and IIFL Capital appointed as bankers for the proposed issue.

Atomberg is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, the Mumbai-based company crossed the Rs 1,000 crore total income mark, with operating revenue rising 20% to Rs 958.4 crore from Rs 796.9 crore in FY24. The Temasek-backed firm also narrowed its net loss by 41% to Rs 117.4 crore

title: Zepto confirms pre IPO private placement, says listing within SEBI approved timeline
description: Bengaluru-based quick commerce major Zepto has officially confirmed that it will undertake a pre-IPO private placement ahead of its planned public listing.
body: Quick commerce major Zepto has officially confirmed that it will undertake a pre-IPO private placement ahead of its planned public listing, while indicating that it will continue to focus on business execution before launching its IPO.

In a statement issued on Friday, the company said it has agreed with major shareholders to close a pre IPO private placement of equity. The financing will strengthen its balance sheet, which stood at Rs 5,681 crore in cash with no debt as of March 31, 2026.

"As part of the IPO process, the Board and Founders have received terms from public market investors to list the company and are appreciative of the expressed interest. However, at this time, and afforded by the company's strong balance sheet, Zepto will focus on continued execution," the company said.

Zepto added that it will update its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with its operating results and financials in the coming quarters and intends to list within the timeframe permitted by SEBI under its approved UDRHP.

The announcement comes days after multiple media reports indicated that the company had postponed its IPO plans amid valuation discussions with investors. Reports had also suggested that Zepto was in talks to raise more than Rs 1,000 crore through a pre IPO placement from existing investors including Glade Brook, General Catalyst, Goodwater Capital, and Nexus Venture Partners.

Zepto had initially planned an IPO of around Rs 8,000 crore. In June, the company filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for a fresh issue of Rs 8,010 crore and subsequently received the regulator's approval. Recent reports had indicated that the company may reduce the IPO size to around Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 6,000 crore.
According to its FY26 financial statements, Zepto doubled its operating revenue to Rs 11,110 crore from Rs 5,454 crore in FY25. Its net loss, however, widened 26% to Rs 5,905 crore.

title: Indian startup funding drops to $662 Mn in July after June spike
description: Indian startups raised $662 million in July, a sharp decline from the blockbuster $2 billion recorded in June, when Meta's investment in CRED accounted for a significant share.
body: Indian startups raised $662 million in July, a sharp decline from the blockbuster $2 billion recorded in June, when Meta's investment in CRED accounted for a significant share of the month's funding. July saw only one funding round above $100 million as Emergent raised fresh capital and became the seventh unicorn of 2026. The second largest deal stood at just $40 million, a sign of the limited availability of large ticket funding during the month. Despite the month on month decline, July's funding remained above May's $630 million . Early stage startups accounted for 38% of the total capital raised. IPO activity remained strong, although Zepto postponed its public listing amid valuation discussions with investors. The month also saw four startup shutdowns, while no major layoffs were reported separately in the media, a rare occurrence in recent months.
[Funding overview]

According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $662 million across 85 deals in July. The total included 16 growth and late stage deals worth $410 million and 64 early stage deals worth $252 million. Additionally, five deals were disclosed without their funding amounts during the month.
[M-o-M and Y-o-Y trend]

Month on month, startup funding fell 67% to $662.2 million in July from $2 billion in June , the second lowest monthly total in the past 13 months. Year on year, funding rose 11% from $597.6 million in July 2025 to $662.2 million in July 2026, while the number of deals declined from 105 to 85.
[Top 10 growth stage deals]

Growth and late stage funding in July was led by AI startup Emergent, which raised $130 million in a Series C round. Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group, Veriqus, and BusinessNext followed with $40 million each, while Neo Group secured $36.3 million in a Series C round. Other notable deals included Limelight Diamonds, Elevate Education, Quick Clean, Apna Mart, and Naturis Cosmetics, with investments spread across AI, fintech, deeptech, consumer, edtech, and manufacturing.
[Top 10 early stage deals]

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [July 27 - Aug 01]
description: This week, 17 Indian startups raised nearly $82.2 million across 2 growth stage deals, 13 early stage deals, and 2 undisclosed deals. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 17 Indian startups raised nearly $82.2 million across 2 growth stage deals, 13 early stage deals, and 2 undisclosed deals. The week also witnessed 8 key hires, 4 fund launches, 1 M&A deal, and 1 ESOP buyback.
In contrast, 16 startups had collectively secured about $164 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised a total of $21.1 million across two deals this week, led by Apna Mart, which raised Rs 120 crore (around $12.7 million) in its Series C round co-led by Accel India and Fundamentum, with participation from Peak XV Partners.
Hyderabad-based dairy brand Sid’s Farm followed with over Rs 81 crore (around $8.4 million) in a pre-Series B round led by Omnivore, NSFO, Dodla Dairy, Next Bharat Ventures, and LIO.
[ Early-stage deals ]
Early-stage startups raised $61.1 million across 13 deals this week, led by Arboreal Bioinnovations, which secured Rs 230 crore (over $24 million) in a Series A round co-led by EAAA and Omnivore.

Aham Housing Finance followed with Rs 100 crore in a follow-on funding round led by The Sanmar Group, while Omega Seiki Mobility raised Rs 50 crore from Securocorp Securities, Sangeeta Pareekh, Saket Aggarwal Family Office, and Vanshika Sharma.

title: TVS extends lead in July as Ola Electric, Ather record decline in EV two-wheeler sales
description: EV two-wheeler registrations in India stayed above 1.93 lakh in July 2026. TVS Motor strengthened its leadership by crossing 50,000 registrations, while Ola Electric and Ather Energy witnessed a drop in sales.
body: EV two-wheeler registrations in India stayed above 1.93 lakh in July 2026. TVS Motor strengthened its leadership by crossing 50,000 registrations, while Ola Electric and Ather Energy witnessed a drop in sales.

According to the latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the EV two-wheeler market with 52,538 registrations in July and a 27.15% market share. The company posted 10.8% month-on-month growth, with 5,125 more registrations than in June.
Bajaj Auto retained the second spot with 43,607 registrations and a 22.53% market share in July. Its registrations rose marginally from 43,504 units in June.
Ather Energy retained the third position with 28,819 registrations and a 14.89% market share in July. The company recorded an 8.3% month-on-month decline, with 2,616 fewer registrations than in June.
Hero MotoCorp ranked fourth with 21,174 registrations and a 10.94% market share in July. The company reported a marginal 3.3% month-on-month decline.

Ola Electric remained fifth with 13,170 registrations and a 6.80% market share in July. The company recorded one of the steepest declines among the leading EV two-wheeler makers, with sales falling 19% month on month, or by 3,079 units, from 16,249 registrations in July.
Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 9,701 registrations and a 5.01% market share after its sales dropped 11.3% over June.

Among the fastest-growing players in the top 10, BGauss recorded the strongest month-on-month growth at 33.9%, with registrations rising to 5,324 units. River Mobility followed with a 24.8% increase to 5,554 units.

title: Snabbit crosses 115,000 daily jobs, says burn per job drops below Rs 250 in Q1 FY27
description: Snabbit has crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a single day, according to the company. It also reported improvements in its unit economics during the first quarter of FY27.
body: Quick home services startup Snabbit has crossed 115,000 fulfilled jobs in a single day, according to the company. It also reported improvements in its unit economics during the first quarter of FY27.

According to Snabbit, it completed around 4 million jobs in its core househelp category during Q1 FY27, while its consolidated Net Order Value (NOV), after accounting for customer discounts, crossed Rs 130. During the quarter, burn per job declined by more than Rs 100 quarter on quarter to below Rs 250.
The company scaled from around 400 daily jobs to more than 115,000 a day in under two years. It had crossed 50,000 daily jobs and one million monthly jobs earlier this year.

Snabbit currently operates across 10 cities including Mumbai, Delhi, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Gurgaon, Ghaziabad, Noida, Faridabad, Pune and Hyderabad, covering more than 150 micromarkets. According to the company, it continues to focus on increasing density within existing neighbourhoods to improve fulfilment efficiency and customer retention.
The company also reported early traction in newer categories such as Home Cooks and Salon at Home.

Founder and CEO Aayush Agarwal said that mature micromarkets are now completing more than 2,500 jobs a day, while several residential communities generate over 500 daily jobs. He added that the company expects its consolidated NOV to improve by another 15% to 20% over the coming months.
Snabbit currently facilitates more than 100,000 earning opportunities every day for its network of over 25,000 Experts and has enabled eShram registration for eligible workers on its platform.
The announcement comes months after Snabbit raised $56 million in a Series D funding round, taking its total capital raised to $112 million.

title: Nazara’s Q1 FY27 results hit by associate losses and impairment; Nitish Mittersain steps down as CEO
description: Nazara Technologies, a gaming and sports media company, reported a 14% year on year decline in operating revenue during the first quarter of FY27.
body: Nazara Technologies, a gaming and sports media company, reported a 14% year on year decline in operating revenue during the first quarter of FY27. The company also slipped into a loss during the quarter.

This is a rare quarterly loss for Nazara, which last reported a net loss of Rs 34 crore in Q2 FY26 following a write off related to its investment in PokerBaazi after the enactment of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.
Nazara’s operating revenue declined to Rs 429 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 499 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.

Gaming remained the company’s largest revenue contributor, accounting for 60.4% of operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew 14.1% year on year to Rs 275 crore from Rs 241 crore in the same quarter last year. Meanwhile, esports revenue declined 81.8% to Rs 28 crore, while ad tech revenue increased 18.9% to Rs 126 crore.
Including Rs 9 crore in other income, Nazara’s total income stood at Rs 438 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 576 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.

On the expense front, total expenditure declined 12.7% to Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 521 crore in Q1 FY26. Advertising and business promotion remained the largest cost at Rs 153 crore, followed by employee benefits at Rs 82 crore and content, event and web server expenses at Rs 63 crore.

Nazara slipped into a net loss of Rs 82 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a net profit of Rs 51 crore in the same quarter last year. The loss included Rs 62 crore as the company’s share of losses from associates and a Rs 22 crore impairment loss.

On a sequential basis, operating revenue grew 7.8% from Rs 398 crore in Q4 FY26 to Rs 429 crore in Q1 FY27, while the company swung from a net profit of Rs 55.7 crore in the previous quarter to a net loss.

title: MakeMyTrip reports $286 Mn revenue in Q1 FY27; profit plunges 65%
description: Online travel platform MakeMyTrip reported a mixed performance for the first quarter of FY27, with revenue growing in single digits while profit declined 65% to $9.1 million due to higher finance costs linked to its convertible notes.
body: Online travel platform MakeMyTrip reported a mixed performance for the first quarter of FY27, with revenue growing in single digits while profit declined 65% to $9.1 million due to higher finance costs linked to its convertible notes.

The Nasdaq-listed company recorded 6.2% year-on-year growth in revenue to $285.6 million in the quarter ended June 2026 from $268.8 million in the corresponding period last year. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 16.1%.

MakeMyTrip said the quarter was affected by a more than 10% depreciation in the Indian rupee against the U.S. dollar, as well as subdued international outbound travel due to the ongoing West Asia conflict. However, strong domestic travel demand helped offset part of the impact.

Hotels and packages remained the company's largest business with revenue of $151.2 million, recording a 6.7% year-on-year increase. Bus ticketing revenue climbed 15.9% to $44.9 million. Revenue from the air ticketing segment fell 7.5% to $55.6 million, while the others segment recorded 19.6% growth to $33.9 million.

Gross bookings grew 9.4% to $2.85 billion, led by growth across hotels, bus ticketing and air travel. Hotel room nights rose nearly 20% to 12.8 million, while bus ticket volumes increased 23.9% to 43.6 million.

On the expense front, service costs rose 10.4% year-on-year to $82.7 million, driven by strong demand for packages and car bookings in India. Marketing and sales promotion expenses increased 11.1% to $48.8 million, while other operating expenses edged up 2.3% to $65.3 million. Personnel expenses, however, declined 3.4% to $38.8 million.

Finance costs surged to $35 million in Q1 FY27 from $10.8 million a year earlier, primarily due to higher interest expenses on convertible senior notes. As a result, net finance costs jumped to $28.3 million from $4 million in the year-ago quarter.

In the end, the Gurugram-based company reported a 64.7% decline in profit to $9.1 million during the quarter, as higher finance costs weighed on its bottom line. Its Adjusted EBITDA stood at $55.5 million during the quarter.

title: Exclusive: Spinny converts into public company; FY26 topline touches Rs 6,000 Cr
description: Gurugram-based used car retailing platform Spinny is preparing for its planned initial public offering (IPO) by converting into a public company.
body: Used car retailing platform Spinny is preparing for its planned initial public offering (IPO) by converting into a public company.

The board has passed a special resolution to change the name of its parent entity from Valuedrive Technologies Private Limited to Valuedrive Technologies Limited, a move that typically precedes a public listing, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
According to a recent Bloomberg report, Spinny has appointed Kotak, Morgan Stanley, and Citi as lead bankers for an IPO in CY27.

Founded in 2015 by Niraj Singh and Mohit Gupta, Spinny operates a full stack used car marketplace, offering vehicle buying, selling, financing, insurance, and after sales services. The company also owns Truebil and completed the acquisition of auto service platform GoMechanic in 2024. It further expanded its portfolio with the acquisition of Autocar India, an automotive media and car content platform, in March 2025.
According to sources, Spinny is currently selling close to 15,000 cars every month. The company serves car buyers across 25 cities and enables car sellers from more than 100 cities.
Sources also said Spinny plans to expand its buyer footprint to around 35 cities in the near term by adding 10 more locations.

For the fiscal year ended March 2025, Spinny's revenue from operations grew 25% year on year to Rs 4,657 crore from Rs 3,730 crore in FY24. According to sources, the company is expected to close FY26 with revenue of around Rs 6,000 crore.
Entrackr has reached out to Spinny for comments.

title: Ather Energy reports Rs 1,217 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27, loss drops to Rs 51 Cr
description: Electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy reported strong growth in the first quarter of FY27, with its operating revenue surging 89% year-on-year while losses narrowed 71% to Rs 51 crore
body: Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ather Energy announced its Q1 FY27 results today. During the period, the company reported 89% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue. At the same time, the losses for the Bengaluru-based company narrowed by 71% to Rs 51 crore.
Ather’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,217 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 645 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its quarterly report sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The sale of electric two-wheelers and related services remained Ather Energy's sole source of operating revenue, although the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup. During the quarter, it sold 88,655 vehicles, up 9% quarter-on-quarter from 81,072 units in Q4 FY26.
The company also recorded Rs 43 crore in other income, taking its total income for the quarter to Rs 1,260 crore.

Ather's largest expense continued to be the cost of materials, primarily battery cells and other components, which surged 88% year-on-year to Rs 977 crore in Q1 FY27 and accounted for nearly 75% of the company's total expenditure. Employee benefit expenses remained largely unchanged at Rs 118 crore during the quarter.

Depreciation and amortisation charges, along with spending on legal, advertising, and other operating expenses, pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 1,311 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 851 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Higher electric two-wheeler sales helped Ather significantly improve its bottom line during the quarter. The company more than doubled its vehicle sales to 88,655 units from 41,083 units in Q1 FY26, which contributed to a 71% decline in net loss to Rs 51 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 178 crore in the year-ago quarter.
According to Vahan data, Ather Energy retained its third position in July despite a 8.3% decline in registrations to 28,819 units and 14.89% market share.

title: Transition VC-backed Matel raises Rs 130 Cr in Series B round led by UC Impower
description: Pune based Matel Motion & Energy Solutions has raised Rs 130 crore (around $15 million) in a Series B funding round led by UC Impower. News.
body: Pune based Matel Motion & Energy Solutions has raised Rs 130 crore (around $15 million) in a Series B funding round led by UC Impower. The round also saw Catamaran join as a new investor, while existing investor Transition VC also participated.
In May 2024, Matel had raised $4 million in its Series A round led by Transition VC and others.

The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen research and development, accelerate product development, increase hiring across engineering and production teams, and support the company's international expansion.
Founded in 2017 by Sunil Patel and Netaji Patro, Matel designs and manufactures motors, motor controllers, and integrated powertrains for automotive and industrial applications.

The startup offers solutions for a wide range of electric vehicles, including two wheelers, three wheelers, four wheelers, buses, and off road vehicles. It commenced mass production of its powertrains in April 2024 after receiving validation and certification from multiple EV OEMs.
Its products are used across electric vehicles, pumping and cooling systems, and other industrial applications.

The company has also developed magnet free motor technology and offers IE5 industrial motors, while an IE6 motor is under development. Matel currently supplies products to multiple OEMs across the two wheeler, three wheeler, and industrial segments.
Founder and CEO Sunil Patel previously led the Chetak EV development programme at Bajaj Auto's R&D division, while co founder Netaji Patro has held R&D roles at Maruti Suzuki and Bajaj Auto.

title: Imarticus Learning acquires Singapore-based BELLS Institute of Higher Learning
description: According to the company, the acquisition will provide Indian learners with access to Singapore exchange opportunities and ASEAN career pathways, while learners in
body: Professional education company Imarticus Learning has acquired Singapore based BELLS Institute of Higher Learning.

The acquisition brings together two institutions focused on professional education and workforce development. Imarticus Learning, which says it has served over 1 million learners, joins BELLS' network of more than 150,000 alumni, seven training centres across Singapore, and its collaborations with the Singapore government, SkillsFuture Singapore, and enterprises across the region.
The combined organisation has more than 1,100 employees and operates from over 25 offices across India and Singapore.

While Imarticus Learning has built a presence in finance and professional education in India, BELLS adds capabilities in enterprise learning, artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, technology, and workforce development, along with relationships with the Singapore government.

According to the company, the acquisition will provide Indian learners with access to Singapore exchange opportunities and ASEAN career pathways, while learners in Singapore will gain access to Imarticus Learning's programmes in finance, data science, analytics, and technology.

The combined entity plans to offer programmes spanning AI literacy, applied machine learning, AI for finance and fintech, and AI enabled business transformation. The programmes will be developed in collaboration with industry partners and aligned with employer demand across Singapore, India, and the broader ASEAN region.

Co-founded by Nikhil Barshikar and Sonya Hooja, Imarticus Learning offers undergraduate education through the Imarticus School of Finance & Business (ISFB), along with career launch programmes, Prodegrees, global certifications, executive education, corporate learning, and government skilling initiatives.

title: Exclusive: Sarvam AI board to approve $74 Mn funding from NVIDIA, Glade Brook, others
description: AI startup Sarvam is set to raise $74 million (around Rs 700 crore) in a Series B extension led by NVIDIA, with participation from Glade Brook Capital, Gaja Capital, Indigo Ventures, and others.
body: AI startup Sarvam is set to raise $74 million (around Rs 700 crore) in an extension of its Series B round, led by NVIDIA Corporation, with participation from Glade Brook Capital, Gaja Capital, Indigo Ventures, and other investors.
The development comes soon after Sarvam raised $234 million in a round led by HCL Technologies, which propelled the company to unicorn status.

The Sarvam AI’s board passed a special resolution to approve the issuance of 20,244 Series B preference shares and 7 equity shares at an issue price of  Rs 3,44,570 each to raise Rs 698 crore or $74 million, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) .

Global technology giant NVIDIA will lead the round with an investment of Rs 238 crore ($25 million), followed by Glade Brook Capital, which will invest Rs 190.3 crore ($20 million). Gaja Capital and Sanjay Kalra & Jyotika Kapoor will also participate, investing Rs 95 crore and Rs 50 crore, respectively. Other participants, including angel investors and family offices such as Vrijesh Agarwal, KJ Trust, and AL Trust.
In March, Moneycontrol reported that NVIDIA and other investors were in talks to invest in Sarvam AI.

Founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar, Sarvam develops AI models, inference infrastructure, and enterprise AI products tailored for Indian languages and use cases. The startup has recently released several foundational models trained from scratch in India, including Sarvam 105B, Sarvam 30B, and Sarvam Vision
According to Entrackr’s analysis, the firm will be valued at around Rs 14,342 crore or $1.51 billion post-money.

Following the allotment of this tranche, NVIDIA Corporation will hold a 1.66% stake in the company, while Glade Brook Capital will own 1.33%. HCL Technologies' stake will be diluted to 9.95%, while the founders will retain a 38.44% stake in the company.

title: Coffee equipment and services provider Kaapi Machines raises Rs 50 Cr from Sedna HoReCa
description: Led by Abhinav Mathur, Kaapi Machines serves coffee businesses and the broader farm to cup coffee ecosystem. Its clients include large café chains, QSRs, specialty coffee
body: Coffee equipment and services provider Kaapi Machines has secured an equity infusion of Rs 50 crore from Sedna HoReCa (Sedna), a private equity backed B2B HoReCa solutions provider, while also entering into a strategic partnership.
The partnership is expected to expand Kaapi Machines' product portfolio, strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, and enhance its technology stack, warehousing, and service infrastructure.
The company also plans to explore select opportunities in adjacent product categories for its existing customer base by leveraging Sedna's capabilities.

Led by Abhinav Mathur, Kaapi Machines serves coffee businesses and the broader farm to cup coffee ecosystem. Its clients include large café chains, QSRs, specialty coffee roasters, hotels, retailers, corporates, and coffee vending businesses across India.

With coffee consumption continuing to grow in India, the company aims to support both existing and new HoReCa businesses through its product portfolio, training programs, R&D capabilities, and after sales support.

Kaapi Machines supplies equipment including automatic and semi automatic espresso machines, commercial blenders, roasters, and grinders. It is the official distributor for brands such as La Marzocco, Mahlkönig, Rancilio, and Probat. The company also offers barista training, latte art courses, consulting for new cafés, technical maintenance and repair services, and operates the Something's Brewing e-commerce platform for home brewers.

title: MobiKwik reports Rs 281 Cr revenue and Rs 7.6 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
description: Fintech platform MobiKwik announced its quarterly results today. The company reported a marginal increase in operating revenue and turned profitable
body: Fintech platform MobiKwik announced its quarterly results today. The company reported a marginal increase in operating revenue and turned profitable, posting a net profit of Rs 7.6 crore in the quarter, compared to a net loss of Rs 42 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

MobiKwik's revenue from operations increased 3.7% year-on-year  to Rs 281 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 271 crore in Q1 FY26 , its unaudited financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show. The company’s total income stood at Rs 289 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to Rs 282 crore a year earlier.

For MobiKwik, commissions from recharges and loan servicing, along with income from payment gateway and technology platform services, were the key revenue contributors in Q1 FY27. The company, however, did not disclose a segment-wise revenue breakup in its quarterly filing.

For the Gurugram-based firm, payment processing charges continued to be the largest expense at Rs 117 crore, accounting for 41.6% of total expenses. Employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 53 crore, while lending operational expenses declined sharply to Rs 1.8 crore.
Financial guarantee expenses rose to Rs 28 crore, while other expenses stood at Rs 81 crore, taking the company's total expenses to Rs 281 crore, down 13.3% from Rs 324 crore in Q1 FY26.

The company reported a net profit of Rs 7.6 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a net loss of Rs 42 crore in Q1 FY26, aided by lower overall expenses and a sharp decline in lending operational costs. Its EBITDA stood at Rs 16 crore during the quarter compared to Rs 31 crore EBITDA loss in Q1 FY26.

On a sequential basis, MobiKwik's operating revenue declined marginally to Rs 281 crore, while its net profit nearly doubled to Rs 7.6 crore, reflecting improved profitability despite a slight moderation in revenue.
At 11:38 AM, MobiKwik's shares were trading at Rs 290 apiece, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 1,614 crore at the time of writing.

title: KKR-backed LEAP India files RHP for Rs 2,480 Cr IPO; issue opens August 7
description: Logistics solutions firm LEAP India Limited has filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) with SEBI for its Rs 2,480 crore IPO, which is scheduled to open on August 7.
body: Logistics solutions firm LEAP India Limited has filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) with SEBI for its Rs 2,480 crore initial public offering (IPO), which is scheduled to open on August 7.
The IPO will open for subscription on August 7 and close on August 11, with the anchor book opening on August 6. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 151 to Rs 159 per share.
The company received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its IPO in December last year.

According to its RHP, LEAP India has increased the fresh issue size to Rs 480 crore from the Rs 400 crore proposed in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed in August last year. The remaining Rs 2,000 crore of the IPO comprises an offer for sale (OFS).

The OFS will be led by Vertical Holdings II Pte. Ltd., a promoter entity backed by KKR, which plans to sell shares worth Rs 1,998.6 crore. Another KKR-backed promoter group entity, KIA EBT Scheme 3, will offload shares worth around Rs 13.8 crore.

Founded in 2013, EAP India provides pallet pooling, container pooling, and related material-handling solutions across industries. The company counts leading FMCG, pharma, and e-commerce players among its clients.
JM Financial, Avendus Capital, IIFL Capital, and UBS Securities are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India is the registrar.
Of the proceeds from the fresh issue, Rs 360 crore will be used to repay certain borrowings, while the remaining amount will be allocated for general corporate purposes.

title: EV charging startup RoadGrid secures Rs 13 Cr from Technology Development Board
description: EV charging technology startup RoadGrid has secured Rs 13 crore in financial assistance from the Technology Development Board (TDB). Snippets
body: EV charging technology startup RoadGrid has secured Rs 13 crore in financial assistance from the Technology Development Board (TDB) under the Department of Science and Technology for a Rs 27.5 crore manufacturing project.
The firm will use the funds to establish a manufacturing and assembly facility for its patented Universal EV Charger.
The facility will have an annual capacity of 2,000 chargers, with commercial production expected to begin in March 2027.

Founded in 2020, RoadGrid develops EV charging hardware, software and energy management solutions. Its Universal EV Charger supports electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial EVs through a single platform.

The brand claims that its facility will manufacture and assemble components including power electronics, thermal management systems, communication modules, control hardware and metering systems. The project will use locally manufactured components and is expected to create more than 100 jobs.

RoadGrid currently employs over 40 people and has deployed more than 100 EV chargers while managing over 200 charging points. It works with six enterprise customers and has partnerships with companies including VinFast, HPCL and IOCL.
Earlier this year, RoadGrid raised Rs 12 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Venture Catalysts to support product development, manufacturing and charging infrastructure deployment.
The company expects the new facility to generate around Rs 100 crore in annual revenue at an initial production level of 1,000 chargers.

title: UN:BLOC onboards Yuvraj Singh as investor and founding team member
description: UN:BLOC is currently operating in stealth mode, with its business model and product yet to be unveiled. The startup is in early discussions with a select group of people
body: Cricketer Yuvraj Singh has joined UN:BLOC , the new healthcare venture from serial entrepreneur Deepak Sahni, as an investor and a member of its founding team. It marks the second time the two have built a company together.
Yuvraj was among the earliest backers of Sahni's previous company, Healthians, which went on to become one of India's largest at-home diagnostics networks.

UN:BLOC is currently operating in stealth mode, with its business model and product yet to be unveiled. The startup is in early discussions with a select group of people close to Sahni from healthcare, business, and other sectors, some of whom are expected to participate in its pre launch funding round in the coming weeks.

Led by Deepak Sahni and headquartered in Gurugram, UN:BLOC is currently in its pre launch phase. According to the company, it aims to address longstanding challenges in healthcare by focusing on areas that have received relatively less attention.

Over the past decade, Indian cricketers have increasingly evolved from brand ambassadors to startup investors. More than 20 current and former Indian cricketers have invested in startups across sectors including fintech, healthtech, D2C brands, fitness, gaming, EVs, sports technology, and consumer products.

Virat Kohli has built one of the largest startup investment portfolios among Indian athletes, while Yuvraj Singh has made investments through YouWeCan Ventures. More recently, cricketers including MS Dhoni, Jasprit Bumrah, and Hardik Pandya have invested in gaming startup LightFury Games.

title: Exclusive: SuperManager AGI in acquisition talks with Fortune 100 firm
description: Enterprise AI startup SuperManager AGI, formerly known as Oqlous AGI, is in an active acquisition process with a Fortune 100 global firm, according to sources aware of the development.
body: Enterprise AI startup SuperManager AGI, formerly known as Oqlous AGI, is in an active acquisition process with a Fortune 100 global firm, according to sources aware of the development.

Sources told Entrackr that the proposed transaction is valued at around Rs 50 crore and is currently under process, with both sides working towards closing the deal. The identity of the prospective acquirer could not be ascertained, and it is not immediately clear whether the parties have signed a definitive agreement.

Founded in early 2025 by Nirmal Nambiar and Aditya Sharma, SuperManager AGI develops an enterprise agentic AI platform that enables businesses to deploy autonomous AI agents across Project Management & Execution . If completed, the deal would transfer ownership of the startup's technology stack to the acquiring Fortune 100 firm, while the founding team is expected to join the acquirer to help scale the platform globally.

Nambiar, an IIT Dharwad alumnus, previously worked as a product manager at Microsoft before starting the company with Sharma, who leads the startup's technology development. SuperManager AGI was initially launched as Oqlous AGI before rebranding earlier this year.

The startup's platform is built on its proprietary Beehive Agentic Architecture and Agentic Data Architecture (ADA), with the underlying research published as a peer reviewed paper. The startup's platform is built on its proprietary Beehive Agentic Architecture and Agentic Data Architecture (ADA), with the underlying research published as a peer reviewed paper.

According to SuperManager AGI, it serves more than 100 organizations, including Fortune 100 companies, is backed by Perplexity, and has strategic partnerships with Z.ai, Eternal, Sarvam AI and Swiggy.
Entrackr has reached out to Nirmal Nambiar and SuperManager AGI for comments.

If completed, the acquisition would come less than two years after the company's incorporation in early 2025. The proposed transaction also reflects growing acquisition activity in the enterprise AI space, as consulting firms and technology companies look to add agentic AI capabilities through acquisitions.

title: Peak XV, Elevation Capital sell 2.27% stake in Meesho for Rs 1,949 Cr via block deals
description: Meesho's early investors Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital on Tuesday divested a combined 2.27% stake in the e-commerce marketplace through block deals on the NSE worth Rs 1,949.28 crore.
body: Meesho's early investors Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital on Tuesday divested a combined 2.27% stake in the e-commerce marketplace through block deals on the NSE worth Rs 1,949.28 crore.
According to exchange data, both investors offloaded 5.24 crore shares each at Rs 186 apiece, taking the total shares sold to 10.48 crore.
The shares were acquired by a mix of domestic and global institutional investors. Axis Mutual Fund and Fidelity emerged among the largest buyers in the transaction.

Other participants included UTI Mutual Fund, HSBC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, Franklin Templeton Mutual Fund, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore Pte, Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE, Prudential Hong Kong, Societe Generale, BNP Paribas Financial Markets, Ashoka WhiteOak funds, Ghisallo Master Fund LP, India Acorn Fund, Susquehanna Pacific Pty Ltd, NRSGVCC and several other institutional investors.

As of June 2026, Elevation Capital and Peak XV Partners held 12.04% and 10.06% stakes in Meesho, respectively. Following the block deal, Elevation Capital pared nearly 9.4% of its holding, while Peak XV Partners reduced around 9.9% of its stake.

The transaction comes weeks after Meesho reported a strong June quarter. The company posted a 48% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 3,713 crore in Q1 FY27, while its net loss narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.
At the end of Tuesday's trading session, Meesho’ shares were priced at Rs 191.88, taking the company's market capitalization to Rs 88,750 crore (around $9.34 billion).

title: OfBusiness doubles exports to Rs 2,500 Cr in FY26
description: SME-focused supply chain and financing platform OfBusiness more than doubled its exports to over Rs 2,500 crore in FY26, accounting for 12% of its consolidated revenue.
body: Small and medium enterprise focused supply chain and financing platform OfBusiness' exports more than doubled to over Rs 2,500 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026, accounting for 12% of its consolidated revenue, according to a company press release.

The Gurugram-based firm attributed the export growth partly to global buyers diversifying sourcing away from China. It said India's growing position as a manufacturing and sourcing base has supported demand across its apparel and food processing businesses.

According to the release, the company now exports to more than 70 countries, including the US, the UK, the EU, and Japan. It expects exports to grow further in FY27. The company said the recently implemented India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement will support this growth by removing tariffs on nearly 99% of Indian export lines entering the UK, including textiles and apparel.

The US remains OfBusiness' largest export market, the company said. In apparel, it supplies seven of the world's top 10 apparel retailers. The company is also expanding sourcing and manufacturing capacity in Bangladesh while increasing its manufacturing footprint across India.

Exports from its food processing business, which ships products from Karnataka to the US, Canada, the EU and Australia, are expected to double again in FY27. Towards the end of FY26, OfBusiness also started exporting bulk chemicals to South Asia and the Middle East.

"Winning global customers today takes more than competitive pricing. It demands vertical integration, consistent quality, traceability and reliable execution," said Asish Mohapatra, cofounder and CEO of OfBusiness.

OfBusiness reported consolidated revenue of Rs 20,645 crore and profit after tax of Rs 724 crore for FY26. Its commerce business generated Rs 19,174 crore in revenue with EBITDA of Rs 769 crore, while operating cash flow stood at Rs 1,302 crore. The company also reported positive free cash flow of Rs 390 crore during the fiscal year. Entrackr had exclusively reported OfBusiness financial numbers last month.

title: Nykaa’s profits jump 3.3X to Rs 80 Cr in Q1 FY27; acquires 51% stake in skin care brand Aminu
description: Online beauty and fashion platform Nykaa announced its Q1 FY27 results today. The company reported a 29% year-on-year increase in operating revenue, while profit surged 3.3X to Rs 80 crore during the quarter.
body: Online beauty and fashion platform Nykaa announced its Q1 FY27 results today. The company reported a 29% year-on-year increase in operating revenue, while profit surged 3.3X to Rs 80 crore during the quarter.
According to its financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,782 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,155 crore in the year-ago quarter.

The beauty segment remained the company's largest business, contributing over 90% of operating revenue at Rs 2,516 crore, while the fashion segment added Rs 253 crore, accounting for around 9% of the total.

For Nykaa, Cost of materials remained Nykaa's largest expense, accounting for 57% of total expenditure at Rs 1,506 crore in Q1 FY27. Employee benefit expenses rose over 23% to Rs 225 crore, while finance, marketing, technology, and other overheads pushed the company's total expenditure to Rs 2,662 crore during the quarter.

Strong revenue growth and better cost efficiencies helped Nykaa post a 3.3X jump in profit to Rs 80 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 24 crore in the year-ago quarter.  Sequentially, the firm’s profit remained flat compared to Rs 79 crore in the previous quarter.

Separately, Nykaa approved the acquisition of a 51% stake in Aminu Wellness Private Limited for up to Rs 32 crore in cash. Incorporated in 2019, Aminu Wellness manufactures and sells skincare products. It had a turnover of Rs 19.4 crore in FY26.
Nykaa said the acquisition will strengthen its presence in the premium beauty and personal care segment by adding Aminu's R&D capabilities and omnichannel distribution network.
At the close of Tuesday's trading session, Nykaa's shares were priced at Rs 342.5, taking the company's market capitalization to Rs 98,088 crore (around $10.3 billion).

title: Zoppler Systems raises Rs 6.5 Cr led by Finvolve
description: o-founded in November 2024 by Om Rana, Prakash Ramachandra, and Shridhar YB, Zoppler Systems develops indigenous RF sensing products and a vendor agnostic
body: Defence and dual use technology company Zoppler Systems has raised Rs 6.5 crore in a funding round led by Finvolve.

The proceeds will be used to accelerate product development, strengthen field validation of indigenous technologies, expand engineering capabilities, and scale deployments across defence and dual use sectors, Zoppler Systems said in a press release.

Co-founded in November 2024 by Om Rana, Ganesh Kashyap, Prakash Ramachandra, and Shridhar YB, Zoppler Systems develops indigenous RF sensing products and a vendor agnostic decision and autonomy platform. Its technology integrates sensing, intelligence, and response across localized and networked deployments, with applications spanning airborne, ground, naval, and future space domains.

Powered by Edge AI, Zoppler's open architecture enables defence organisations to enhance compatible existing systems with advanced sensing, decision intelligence, and response capabilities without replacing legacy infrastructure.

The Bengaluru-based startup supports both localized and networked autonomy, enabling multiple assets to share intelligence and coordinate mission critical responses across diverse operational environments.

According to the company, its platform is designed to enable faster decision making, greater operational flexibility, and seamless interoperability without requiring customers to replace compatible existing infrastructure. Beyond defence, it also sees dual use applications across critical infrastructure, ports, airports, energy, industrial facilities, and logistics, where real time sensing and intelligent decision making are becoming increasingly important.

title: MapMyIndia reports Rs 140 Cr revenue and Rs 50.4 Cr profit in Q1 FY27
description: C.E. Info Systems, the parent company of MapMyIndia, reported its Q1 FY27 results today. The company posted a 15% year-on-year increase in operating revenue.
body: C.E. Info Systems, the parent company of MapMyIndia, reported its Q1 FY27 results today. The company posted a 15% year-on-year increase in operating revenue, while profit remained nearly flat at Rs 50.4 crore.
According to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), revenue from operations rose to Rs 139.7 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 121.6 crore in the year-ago quarter.

MapMyIndia is a deep-tech company that provides digital maps, geospatial software, location-based APIs, IoT solutions, and mapping platforms to enterprises, automakers, government agencies, developers, and consumers.
MapMyIndia serves customers across automotive, enterprise, and government segments, offering mapping and geospatial solutions to automakers, businesses, and public sector organizations.

Revenue from map data and related services, including royalties, subscriptions, software, and projects, remained the company's largest revenue stream at Rs 114 crore, largely flat year-on-year. Meanwhile, revenue from hardware device sales more than tripled to Rs 23.1 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 7.6 crore in the year-ago quarter.

MapMyIndia also made Rs 19.65 crore from non-operating sources, which pushed its total income in the quarter to Rs 159.4 crore. Sequentially, overall income declined marginally by 2% from Rs 162.8 crore in Q4 FY26.

Employee benefit expenses remained the company's largest cost, accounting for over 27% of total expenditure. The expense stood flat at Rs 25.6 crore, followed by material costs of Rs 21.7 crore and technical services outsourced expenses of Rs 13.3 crore.

The Delhi-based company reported a 6.3% year-on-year increase in profit to Rs 50.4 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 47.4 crore in the year-ago quarter. EBITDA stood at Rs 56 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 40.2%.

title: Vaaree raises Rs 65 Cr in Series A led by Hero Enterprise and Cap Alpha Ventures
description: Bengaluru-based home décor and furnishings marketplace Vaaree has raised Rs 65 crore ($6.6 million) in a Series A funding round led by Hero Enterprise and Cap Alpha Ventures, formerly known as Client Associates Alternate Fund. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based home décor and furnishings marketplace Vaaree has raised Rs 65 crore ($6.6 million) in a Series A funding round led by Hero Enterprise and Cap Alpha Ventures, formerly known as Client Associates Alternate Fund.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its fulfilment network, enable faster deliveries and invest in its AI-powered product discovery and home styling technology, including its VibeCheck platform.

Founded in 2022 by Garima, Varun Vohra and team, Vaaree operates a curated marketplace for home products across décor, furnishings, bed and bath, kitchen and lighting. The platform currently offers more than 1.5 lakh products.
Vaaree’s VibeCheck platform helps users discover products based on their preferences, create moodboards, visualise product combinations and shop coordinated looks.

The startup will also expand its fulfilment and quality verification centres across key markets to bring inventory closer to customers and reduce delivery times, with plans to move towards next-day deliveries across major Indian cities.
Vaaree’s existing investors include Peak XV’s Surge, PeerCapital, All In Capital, Better Capital, OTP Ventures and Kunal Shah.

title: Legal tech startup NYAI raises $1.5 Mn in seed round
description: According to the Pune based startup, its AI models are trained on millions of Indian court judgments, tribunal orders, acts, rules, and regulatory updates. The platform
body: AI native legal infrastructure platform NYAI has raised $1.5 million (approximately Rs 13 crore) in a seed funding round from a consortium of prominent Indian family offices, with participation from strategic angel investors.

The fresh capital will be used for technology development, expanding its AI native compliance ecosystem, and strengthening its presence among enterprises, listed companies, and law firms, along with supporting the deployment and assurance functions these institutions require, NYAI said in a press release.

Founded in March 2025 by Chinmay Bhosale and Vikrant Labde, NYAI is a compliance focused legal AI and regulatory intelligence platform that offers citation based legal research, contract analysis, and automated document drafting tailored to the Indian legal system.

According to the Pune based startup, its AI models are trained on millions of Indian court judgments, tribunal orders, acts, rules, and regulatory updates. The platform prioritises verifiable citations, audit trails, and source integrity over simple text generation. It also assists with contract drafting, case document summarisation, and real time policy tracking.

NYAI said its architecture supports on premises deployment, integrates with enterprises' existing large language model infrastructure, and keeps privileged legal data within the client's environment. The company added that its platform is designed to provide citation backed outputs while working within enterprises' existing legal workflows.

According to market research cited by the company, Indian businesses collectively incur an estimated Rs 95,000 crore in legal and regulatory penalties every year, while listed companies alone account for more than Rs 1.65 lakh crore in value erosion.

title: GetVantage secures Rs 63 Cr in Series A1 round
description: MSMEs, has secured Rs 63 crore in hybrid capital. The Series A1 round takes the Mumbai-based company's total committed funding capacity to over Rs 700 crore.
body: GetVantage, a B2B fintech platform for MSMEs, has secured Rs 63 crore ($6.6 million) in hybrid capital (equity and debt). The Series A1 round takes the Mumbai-based company's total committed funding capacity to over Rs 700 crore. The round was co-led by Rajeev Ahuja and SanRaj Group, with participation from Chiratae Ventures, Varanium Fintech Fund, and VCMint.

GetVantage launched the Rise Up Fund, dedicated to supporting women entrepreneurs with growth capital, with an initial corpus of Rs 100 crore in March 2024. In January the same year, it also launched the SaaS Accelerator Fund II to support B2B SaaS businesses.

The proceeds will be used for expansion while accelerating its evolution into an AI native capital gateway, enabling faster and smarter access to growth capital for Indian MSMEs, GetVantage said in a press release.

Founded in 2020 by Bhavik Vasa, GetVantage embeds seamless financing solutions into marketplaces and merchant ecosystems, enabling businesses to access growth capital without equity dilution or heavy collateral. The platform directly addresses India's Rs 30 lakh crore MSME credit gap and is backed by investors including Chiratae Ventures, Varanium Fintech Fund, Sony Fund, InCred, and industry veterans.

GetVantage utilizes alternate data and predictive analytics to underwrite businesses based on actual cash flows. This approach allows it to significantly reduce the friction Indian founders and SMEs face when seeking growth capital.

GetVantage plans to scale its capital gateway, a plug and play API ecosystem that enables B2B ecommerce platforms, marketplaces, and logistics hubs to embed financing options directly into their merchant ecosystems. In the coming months, it plans to announce several strategic seller financing partnerships with leading digital ecosystems, further strengthening its position as an embedded finance partner for platforms looking to accelerate their merchants' growth.

title: Capillary Technologies’ revenue grows 43% to Rs 257 Cr in Q1 FY27
description: SaaS firm Capillary Technologies reported a 42.6% year-on-year increase in revenue for Q1 FY27 but slipped into losses due to a Rs 33.4 crore exceptional loss from a cyber fraud at its Czech Republic subsidiary.
body: SaaS firm Capillary Technologies announced its financial results for Q1 FY27 today, reporting a 42.6% year-on-year increase in revenue. However, the company slipped into losses during the quarter after reporting a Rs 33.4 crore exceptional loss related to a cyber-enabled banking fraud at its Czech Republic subsidiary.
The Bengaluru-based company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 256.6 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 179.9 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statement sourced from BSE.

Founded in 2008 by Aneesh Reddy, Krishna Mehra, and Ajay Modani, Capillary Technologies offers cloud-native loyalty, CRM, and customer engagement solutions to more than 465 brands across 53 countries. Its clientele includes Tata Digital, Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, and Abbott Laboratories.

The company earned Rs 242.4 crore from subscription services, which contributed 94.5% of its operating revenue, while installation and campaign services brought in the remaining Rs 12.2 crore. It also reported Rs 5.7 crore as other income, which took its total income to Rs 262.3 crore in Q1 FY27.
On a quarterly basis, the firm’s operating revenue grew 34% from Rs 191 crore in Q4 FY26.

Employee benefits remained the company's largest expense, rising 40% year-on-year to Rs 119.8 crore and accounting for more than half of its total expenditure. Software and server charges stood at Rs 45 crore, while professional and consultancy fees came in at Rs 34 crore. Overall, total expenses increased 31.6% to Rs 237.5 crore during the quarter.

In the end, the company slipped into the red during the quarter due to a Rs 33.4 crore exceptional charge related to a cyber-enabled banking fraud at its Czech Republic subsidiary. Its adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 44 crore.
As of 2:10 PM today, shares of Capillary Technologies rose over 15% to Rs 571, taking its total market capitalization to Rs 4,539 crore (about $477 million).

title: Exclusive: Gen AI startup Simplismart set to raise $9 Mn in Series B led by Dallas Venture Capital
description: Generative artificial intelligence startup Simplismart is set to raise nearly Rs 97 crore (around $9 million) in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital
body: Generative artificial intelligence startup Simplismart is set to raise nearly Rs 97 crore (around $9 million) in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from existing investors Accel India and Shastra VC, as well as new investor Micromax Informatics.
The board of Simplismart has approved a resolution to issue 12,100 CCPS at an issue price of Rs 37 lakh each to raise the capital, according to its regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.

Dallas Venture Capital will invest Rs 44.84 crore, followed by Accel India with Rs 24.09 crore. Shastra VC will infuse Rs 22.24 crore, while Micromax Informatics will invest Rs 5.19 crore. Tarusa Capital and Simraan Teckchandani will also participate in the round with investments of Rs 37 lakh each.

According to Entrackr's estimates, the Bengaluru-based company will be valued at around Rs 826 crore post allotment. The fresh capital will be used to support the company's long term growth plans, including business expansion, working capital requirements, and other general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2022 by former Oracle and Google engineers Amritanshu Jain and Devansh Ghatak, Simplismart develops AI infrastructure software that enables enterprises to deploy, manage, and optimize production grade AI models without writing code. Its inference-first platform improves GPU utilization and reduces inference costs across workloads such as large language models (LLMs), vision language models, speech recognition, and image and video generation.
The startup counts Tata 1mg, Mindtickle, InVideo, and Dashtoon among its customers, and has partnered with Nvidia to make its AI inference platform available on the chipmaker's infrastructure.
In May 2026, The Economic Times reported that Nvidia was in talks to lead a $20 million funding round in Simplismart. Previously, it raised $7 million in October 2024.
