Following the allotment, Accel India will remain the company's largest institutional shareholder with a 19.92% stake. Dallas Venture Capital and Shastra VC Fund II will hold 6.23% and 2.69%, respectively, while Micromax Informatics will own 0.63% of the company.

title: Mintoak acquires loyalty and rewards tech company ICC Loyalty
description: Mintoak, a payments and engagement OS for acquirers, has acquired ICC Loyalty. The acquisition expands Mintoak's presence across the Middle East, Africa, Eastern Europe and Asia.
body: Mintoak, a payments and engagement OS for acquirers, has acquired ICC Loyalty. The acquisition expands Mintoak's presence across the Middle East, Africa, Eastern Europe and Asia, while strengthening its ability to help banks generate revenue beyond payments.
Entrackr exclusively reported about this deal in March this year.

ICC Loyalty provides loyalty and rewards technology to more than 30 banks. Its platform enables financial institutions to offer personalised rewards, targeted campaigns and lifecycle engagement programmes aimed at improving customer retention and transaction frequency. The company serves over 11 million customers across more than 10 countries.

According to the company, the acquisition expands Mintoak's capabilities beyond merchant payments and value added services to include customer engagement, loyalty and rewards. It also enables banks to serve both acquiring and issuing businesses through a unified platform.

The combined business generates more than $30 million in annual revenue with a profitability margin exceeding 30%, according to the company. It said the combined platform will enable banks to connect merchants, consumers and payment data to improve customer engagement and create additional revenue opportunities.

Following the acquisition, Mintoak now partners with more than 50 banks across over 20 countries, including HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and SBI Payments in India, Emirates Islamic and RAKBANK in the Middle East, and Absa Bank in Africa. Backed by investors including PayPal Ventures, British International Investment, Pravega Ventures, HDFC Bank and Z3Partners, the company says its platform supports over 5 million merchants and 11 million customers while processing more than $93 billion in annual payment volume.

Mintoak said the acquisition will help it expand its payments and engagement platform for banks across emerging markets as financial institutions increasingly look beyond transaction processing to strengthen customer relationships and diversify revenue streams.

title: Exclusive: Stable Money kicks off Series C with $14.3 Mn from existing investors
description: Wealthtech startup Stable Money has kicked off its Series C round with Rs 136 crore ($14.3 million) from existing investors led by The Fundamentum Partnership.
body: Wealthtech startup Stable Money has kicked off its Series C funding round, raising Rs 136 crore ($14.3 million) from existing investors. The round was led by The Fundamentum Partnership, with participation from Peak XV Partners, RTP Global, and Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners).
This is Stable Money's second fundraise this year. In February, the startup raised $25 million at a $175 million valuation in a round led by Peak XV Partners.

The board at Stable Money allotted 1,318 equity shares and 20,591 Series C preference shares at an issue price of Rs 62,167.9 each to raise Rs 136.2 crore or $14.3 million, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) .
The Fundamentum Partnership led the tranche with an investment of Rs 73.76 crore ($7.8 million), followed by Peak XV Partners with Rs 22 crore. RTP Global and Z47 invested Rs 20.2 crore each.
As per Entrackr's estimates, Stable Money's valuation rose 56% to Rs 2,507 crore ($264 million) from Rs 1,607 crore ($175 million) in its previous $25 million pre-Series C funding round.
Queries sent to Stable Money did not elicit an immediate response. We will update the story once the company responds.

Co-founded in 2022 by Saurabh Jain and Harish Reddy, Stable Money is a wealthtech platform that enables users to compare and invest in fixed deposits, bonds through Stable Bonds, and other fixed-income products across multiple banks.

Following the allotment, Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners) remained the largest external shareholder with a 17.73% stake, followed by RTP Global at 12.82% and Peak XV Partners at 11.69%. The Fundamentum Partnership increased its stake to 9.9%, while the founders' collective holding diluted to 29.04%.

title: Superleap raises Rs 36 Cr in pre-Series A round led by Peak XV’s Surge
description: Enterprise AI CRM startup Superleap has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.7 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Peak XV’s Surge. Snippets.
body: Enterprise AI CRM startup Superleap has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.7 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Peak XV’s Surge.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its enterprise go-to-market operations, develop its AI-based CRM platform and strengthen its product capabilities.

Founded in 2024 by former Unacademy operators Subham Kumar Boundia, Alok Maurya and Saurabh Maheshwari, Superleap provides an AI-native CRM platform for sales and revenue teams. The platform combines revenue data, customer intelligence and AI agents to automate tasks across the sales cycle.
Superleap claims to have grown 10X over the past year and serves customers across BFSI, SaaS, education, healthcare, travel, hospitality and media.
Its customers include Razorpay, Aakash Education, MediBuddy, HCL GUVI, Cars24, PagarBook, Plum, Qube Cinema and Superhealth.
Razorpay migrated more than 10 million data records to Superleap in 45 days, while Aakash Education moved around 5,000 counselors across 400 locations to the platform in under 60 days.

Superleap’s platform includes SuperOS for data management, SuperSense for customer intelligence and SuperAgents for automating revenue tasks. It also offers AI voice bots and integrations with tools including WhatsApp, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Claude and ChatGPT.
The startup is also backed by Gruhas, Supermorpheus Group and angel investors including Deepinder Goyal, Kunal Shah, Gaurav Munjal, Anupam Mittal, Mukesh Bansal and Nikhil Kamath.

title: Agentic AI startup Kily raises Rs 30 Cr in round led by Sorin Investments
description: Agentic enterprise AI startup Kily has raised Rs 30 crore ($3.1 million) in a funding round led by Sorin Investments, with participation from Razorpay and Wyser Capital. Snippets
body: Agentic enterprise AI startup Kily has raised Rs 30 crore ($3.1 million) in a funding round led by Sorin Investments, with participation from Razorpay and Wyser Capital.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its product capabilities, expand go-to-market operations and increase adoption among consumer brands in India.
Founded in 2025 by Sankalp Mehrotra, Anurag Singh and Sharad Chitlangia, Kily develops AI agents that help brands and sellers manage operations across e-commerce and quick commerce platforms.

Its platform collects marketplace data and combines it with a brand's business goals and operating requirements to automate decisions and workflows. It helps brands manage areas such as product visibility, advertising, pricing, inventory and other commerce operations across digital platforms.
Kily works across e-commerce and quick commerce platforms including Amazon, Flipkart, Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart. Since its launch, the startup has worked with consumer brands including ITC.
According to Kily, its AI agents are designed to reduce the use of spreadsheets, dashboards and manual processes by automating commerce management and decision-making.

title: Former Swiggy, Zomato executives launch AI startup Profound with $1.5 Mn seed round
description: Bengaluru based AI startup Profound has raised $1.5 million in a seed funding round as it launched an AI powered platform for professional networking and hiring. Snippets
body: Bengaluru based AI startup Profound has raised $1.5 million in a seed funding round as it launched an AI powered platform for professional networking and hiring.
The startup was founded by Anuj Rathi and Prashant Parashar, former product and technology leaders with experience across Swiggy, Zomato, Cleartrip, Flipkart, Ola and Walmart Labs.

The seed round saw participation from angel investors including Swiggy CEO Sriharsha Majety, Swiggy cofounder Nandan Reddy, former Zomato cofounder Pankaj Chaddah, Razorpay CEO Harshil Mathur, WhatsApp Global Head Kunal Shah, and OfBusiness cofounder Bhuvan Gupta, along with venture capital firms Stellaris Venture Partners and 3one4 Capital.

The company will use the fresh capital to expand its engineering and product teams, enhance its AI capabilities, and develop its matching and introductions engine. It plans to onboard one million professionals globally before opening beta access to more users.

Profound offers every professional an AI powered representative that starts with a voice conversation to understand a user's experience, expertise, work style and career goals. Based on this, the platform recommends opportunities and facilitates professional introductions.

The startup also enables hiring managers to create AI representatives for roles and teams, allowing companies to capture hiring requirements through voice conversations instead of traditional job descriptions.
"Just as actors have agents and athletes have managers, Profound gives each professional their own AI Rep," cofounder and CEO Anuj Rathi said in a statement.
The company has opened early access for its first cohort, while a wider beta launch is planned later this year.

title: Policybazaar parent PB Fintech's profit jumps 92% to Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27
description: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar announced its Q1 FY27 results today. The company reported a 92% year-on-year jump in profit after tax to Rs 163 crore.
body: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar announced its Q1 FY27 results today. The company reported a 92% year-on-year jump in profit after tax to Rs 163 crore.

The Gurugram-based company posted operating revenue of Rs 1,888 crore in Q1 FY27, a 40% increase from Rs 1,348 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, as per the firm’s financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Revenue from the core online business was led by Policybazaar, which contributed Rs 1,067 crore, while Paisabazaar added Rs 127 crore. The company's new initiatives, including PB Partners, PB for Business, PB UAE and PB Connect, collectively generated Rs 694 crore.

In addition to operating revenue, the firm earned Rs 93 crore from interest and gains on financial assets during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 1,981 crore for the quarter ended March 2026.
On a quarterly basis, PB Fintech’s revenue dropped over 8% from Rs 2,061 crore in Q4 FY26.
The company's total insurance premium rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 8,372 crore during the quarter, led by a 53% increase in new protection premium, including a 59% growth in health insurance premium.

Employee benefit expenses remained the group's largest cost, accounting for 40% of total expenditure at Rs 716 crore, a 28% increase from the year-ago quarter. Advertising and promotional expenses also climbed 50% year-on-year to Rs 379 crore in Q1 FY27.

The company did not provide a detailed breakup of other expenses in its quarterly financials. Overall expenditure rose 33% year-on-year to Rs 1,800 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,356 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

title: River Mobility raises $120 Mn in Series C led by Elev8, Claypond Capital
description: River Mobility has raised $120 million in a Series C funding round comprising equity and venture debt, one of the largest private funding rounds in India's electric two wheeler segment.
body: Electric two wheeler maker River Mobility has raised $120 million in a Series C funding round comprising equity and venture debt, one of the largest private funding rounds in India's electric two wheeler segment.

The equity round was led by Elev8 Venture Partners and Claypond Capital, with participation from Singularity AMC, Anicut Capital, 360 ONE Asset, JIF Capital and HDFC AMC. Existing investors including Yamaha Motor Corporation, Al Futtaim Group and Mitsui & Co also participated, while Alteria Capital, Innoven Capital and Stride Ventures joined through venture debt.

Founded in 2021 by Aravind Mani and Vipin George, River Mobility manufactures electric two wheelers with a focus on utility oriented products. Its flagship electric scooter, Indie, was launched in 2023.

The company will use the fresh capital to expand capacity at its existing manufacturing facility, set up a new greenfield plant, launch new products in the utility lifestyle segment, and improve gross margins and EBITDA profitability.

"This funding marks an important milestone in River's journey. The confidence shown by both our existing and new investors reinforces our belief that there is tremendous opportunity to build India's first utility and design based mobility brand," said Aravind Mani, co-founder and CEO of River Mobility.
River currently operates more than 75 retail stores across India and plans to expand its network to over 350 stores by March 2028.

According to the company, monthly sales have reached around 5,000 units over the past year as it continues to expand its manufacturing capacity and distribution network. It also plans to introduce new electric vehicle models over the coming years.

In February 2024, River raised $40 million in a Series B funding round led by Yamaha, with participation from Al Futtaim Group, Lowercarbon Capital, Toyota Ventures and Maniv Mobility. Prior to that, it had secured $15 million in a Series A round in June 2023.

title: Tracxn slips into loss as revenue remains flat in Q1 FY27
description: Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q1 FY27 results on Wednesday. The Bengaluru-based company reported flat revenue during the quarter
body: Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q1 FY27 results on Wednesday. The Bengaluru-based company reported flat revenue during the quarter, while it slipped into losses.

Tracxn’s revenue from operations declined 0.6% to Rs 21.08 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 21.20 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal (Q1 FY26), according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Tracxn derived its entire operating revenue from subscription sales that provide access to its data and software. However, the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter.
The company also earned Rs 1.52 crore from non operating sources, taking its total revenue to Rs 22.60 crore in the first quarter of FY27.

Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost head, increasing 16% to Rs 21.98 crore and accounting for 86.64% of the overall expenditure during the quarter. The company’s total expenses rose 18.4% to Rs 25.37 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 21.43 crore in Q1 FY26.
Due to the sharp increase in expenses, Tracxn reported a loss of Rs 3.01 crore in Q1 FY27, compared to a profit of Rs 1.12 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

On a quarter on quarter basis, Tracxn reported a marginal 2.9% growth in operating revenue to Rs 21.08 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 20.49 crore in Q4 FY26. However, its losses widened 14.4% to Rs 3.01 crore during the same period from Rs 2.63 crore in the preceding quarter.
At the close of trading on Monday, Tracxn's shares settled at Rs 30.62, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 319 crore.

title: Beardo nears Rs 300 Cr revenue in FY26; profit jumps 70%
description: Beardo reported a strong financial performance in FY26, with revenue nearing the Rs 300 crore mark and improving profitability by 70%  during the fiscal year.
body: Marico-owned men's grooming brand Beardo reported a strong financial performance in FY26, with revenue nearing the Rs 300 crore mark and improving profitability by 70%  during the fiscal year.

According to its standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC), revenue from operations rose 40% to Rs 299 crore in FY26 from Rs 214 crore in FY25. The company's entire operating revenue came from the sale of products, with domestic sales contributing 99% and exports accounting for the remaining 1%.
The Ahmedabad-based company also recorded Rs 1 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 300 crore in FY26.

Coming to expenses, in line with the company's scale, material consumption, its largest cost, increased 36% to Rs 128 crore. Advertising and promotional spend jumped 59.6% to Rs 83 crore as the company stepped up investments to drive sales and strengthen brand visibility, while employee benefit expenses rose 30.2% to Rs 18.3 crore.
Other overheads like transportation cost, legal & professional, travelling pushed the overall expenses by 37% to Rs 270 crore.

Higher advertising and marketing spend helped Beardo drive a 40% increase in revenue, which, coupled with operating efficiencies, lifted its profit after tax (PAT) by 70% to Rs 22.12 crore in FY26 from Rs 13 crore a year earlier.

On a unit level, the company spent Rs 0.90 to earn one rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Beardo's EBITDA margin improved to 10.57% in FY26 from 9.17% in FY25, while its ROCE stood at 66.52% during the fiscal year ending March 2026.
On the balance sheet front, total assets increased to Rs 126 crore from Rs 72 crore in FY25, while current assets stood at Rs 115 crore, compared to Rs 60 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Lighthouse Canton closes Rs 1,050 Mn private credit investment in Emerald Leisures
description: Lighthouse Canton, a global investment firm with over $6 billion in assets under management, has closed a Rs 1,050 million private credit investment in Emerald Leisures Limited.
body: Lighthouse Canton, a global investment firm with over $6 billion in assets under management, has closed a Rs 1,050 million private credit investment in Emerald Leisures Limited through its India based Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), the LC Luminere Credit Fund, and affiliated entities.
Emerald Leisures is a BSE listed leisure and hospitality company that owns and operates Club Emerald, a multi sport, hospitality and recreational destination in Mumbai.

The investment will provide long term capital to support Emerald Leisures' growth plans. Structured as secured non convertible debentures, the facility is backed by the company's operating cash flows and supported by collateral, escrowed cash flows, promoter support and identified liquidity events.

The transaction adds to Lighthouse Canton's private credit portfolio in India, where it provides structured financing solutions to established businesses. Through its India private credit platform, the firm offers capital solutions tailored to the financing requirements of businesses across sectors.

Lighthouse Canton manages assets for ultra high net worth individuals, family offices, institutional investors and global investors. Its investment capabilities span private credit, growth debt, venture capital, real estate private equity, public equities and global macro hedge fund strategies.

The firm's private credit platform is supported by an origination network with access to more than 500 issuer relationships and over 1,000 promoter families, providing a pipeline of proprietary investment opportunities across sectors.

title: Freshworks turns profitable with $237 Mn revenue in Q2 CY26
description: Nasdaq-listed SaaS firm Freshworks reported a 16% year-on-year increase in revenue to $237.4 million in the second quarter ended June 2026, while achieving its first quarterly GAAP profitability this year.
body: Nasdaq-listed SaaS firm Freshworks reported a 16% year-on-year increase in revenue to $237.4 million in the second quarter ended June 2026, while achieving its first quarterly GAAP profitability this year.

The company posted a GAAP net profit of $3.2 million in Q2 CY26, compared to a net loss of $1.7 million in the corresponding quarter last year. Operating income stood at $6.1 million, against an operating loss of $8.7 million a year earlier.
According to the filing, non-GAAP operating income grew to $55.9 million, translating into a 23.6% operating margin, compared to 21.9% in the year ago quarter.

For Freshworks, sales and marketing costs rose nearly 12% to $106.5 million from $95.2 million in Q2 CY26, while research and development expenses increased to $43.8 million from $39.9 million. General and administrative expenses declined to $37.9 million from $47 million, although the company incurred $7 million in restructuring charges during the quarter.
Total operating expenses increased to $195.2 million from $182.2 million.

The company generated $58.5 million in operating cash flow and $57.7 million in adjusted free cash flow during the quarter. Cash & cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities stood at $665.3 million as of June 30, 2026.

Freshworks also continued to expand its enterprise customer base. The number of customers contributing more than $100,000 in annual recurring revenue (ARR) rose 25% year-on-year to 1,746, while customers contributing over $50,000 in ARR increased 18% to 4,091. Net dollar retention rate stood at 104%.
Freshworks raised its full-year guidance and now expects CY26 revenue between $963.5 million and $966.5 million, with non-GAAP operating income projected at $222 million to $228 million.

title: C2C marketplace Vingo raises Rs 10 Cr seed round led by IndiaQuotient
description: Vingo, a consumer-to-consumer marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned products, has raised Rs 10 crore ($1 million) in a seed funding round led by IndiaQuotient Snippets
body: Vingo, a consumer-to-consumer marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned products, has raised Rs 10 crore ($1 million) in a seed funding round led by IndiaQuotient. Inuka Capital and Credgenics founder Rishabh Goel also participated in the round.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen its product, invest in trust and payment infrastructure, study user behaviour and support marketing across key user groups.

Founded in March 2026 by Parth Sarthi, Saransh Goyal and Krish Vashistha, Vingo enables users to buy and sell pre-owned products directly. The platform currently operates in Bengaluru and is available on Android and iOS.

Vingo combines identity verification, community-based product discovery, escrow-backed payments and bidding to address trust issues between buyers and sellers. Its categories include smartphones, cameras, gaming consoles, musical instruments, fashion and sports equipment.

As per market research, India's recommerce market is projected to grow from $5.91 billion in 2026 to $8.61 billion by 2030. Vingo plans to focus on the C2C segment as it expands its platform and user base.

title: Personal assistance startup Hulp secures $2.6 Mn seed funding
description: Personal assistance and concierge platform Hulp has raised $2.6 million (around Rs 22.7 crore) in a seed funding round co-led by Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures.
body: Personal assistance and concierge platform Hulp has raised $2.6 million (around Rs 25 crore) in a seed funding round co-led by Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures, with participation from DeVC (Z47) and angel investors, including PB Fintech co-founder and chairman Yashish Dahiya.

The proceeds will be used to expand AI workflows across lifestyle, household, and operational management, strengthen the senior leadership team, and enhance the company's technology and product capabilities, Hulp said in a press release.

Founded in April this year by Tarun Mathur, Neha Kulwal, and Vishal Singh Khutel, Hulp operates a personal assistance and concierge platform for urban households. The platform enables users to delegate daily, weekly, monthly, and one-time tasks across more than 15 categories through dedicated personal assistants supported by AI coordinated operations.
Before launching Hulp, Mathur was co-founder and chief business officer at PolicyBazaar (PB Fintech), where he led several of the company's business verticals.

According to the company, users can assign tasks through WhatsApp or its mobile app using voice notes. The platform offers services across categories such as government documentation, kitchen management, runner services, laundry, gardening, event bookings, restaurant reservations, and travel.

The Gurugram-based startup currently operates in Delhi, Gurugram, and Noida, and plans to expand to Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai. It says it is supported by a 50-member operations team that manages routine household and lifestyle tasks.

title: InRisk Labs raises $27 Mn in Series A round led by Bessemer, Northpoint Capital
description: The company said the licence marks its transition from a technology led insurtech platform to an integrated reinsurance group with licensed risk bearing capacity. While
body: Technology-led risk and reinsurance platform InRisk Labs has raised $27 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Northpoint Capital.

The funding comes alongside a regulatory milestone for the company. Its subsidiary, EarthRe Insurance IFSC Limited, has received a licence from the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) to operate as a reinsurer. The company said EarthRe is the first incorporated reinsurer to receive a licence from the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) at GIFT City.

The fresh capital will be deployed to strengthen underwriting, actuarial, catastrophe modelling and AI capabilities, expand into natural catastrophe and climate risk as well as other non life segments including marine cargo and motor, develop parametric and structured reinsurance products, and meet regulatory capital requirements for scaling EarthRe’s operations in India’s $10 billion reinsurance market.

The company said the licence marks its transition from a technology led insurtech platform to an integrated reinsurance group with licensed risk bearing capacity. While InRisk Labs will continue to build technology, data and risk intelligence infrastructure, EarthRe will underwrite reinsurance business through its regulated balance sheet.

EarthRe is focused on non life reinsurance across natural catastrophe, climate risk, property, crop and specialty lines. The company said its platform integrates climate, geospatial, satellite, exposure and claims data to improve underwriting, pricing, portfolio construction and capital allocation. It also plans to offer treaty, facultative, structured and parametric reinsurance products designed for India and other Global South markets.

“India will be the most consequential insurance market over the next two decades. To drive sustainable growth, we must build indigenous capacity and tailored solutions built by India, for India,” said Malay Kumar Poddar, chief executive officer of EarthRe.

Vishal Gupta, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, said the firm backed the company at the seed stage and has now doubled down on its investment, while Sameer Brij Verma, founder and CIO of Northpoint Capital, said EarthRe combines a licensed balance sheet with an AI native risk platform and deep underwriting expertise.

title: Deep-tech energy startup Adiabatic Technologies raises Rs 8.3 Cr in seed round
description: Adiabatic Technologies has raised Rs 8.3 crore in a seed funding round co-led by Malpani Ventures and Avinya Ventures, with participation from Appreciate Capital, DeVC.
body: Deep-tech energy startup Adiabatic Technologies has raised Rs 8.3 crore in a seed funding round co-led by Malpani Ventures and Avinya Ventures, with participation from Appreciate Capital, DeVC, Operators Studio, and UPES Incubator.
The company had previously raised Rs 1.1 crore in an angel funding round from Soonicorn Ventures and other investors in November last year.

The fresh proceeds will be used to expand its manufacturing capacity to 100 MWh annually, accelerate product development, strengthen its engineering team, and scale deployment of its battery systems across robotics, defence, and other sectors, Adiabatic said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Darshan Meher, Adiabatic develops custom lithium ion battery packs, smart chargers, and proprietary Battery Management Systems (BMS) for OEMs operating in high reliability industries. The company says it has deployed more than 20,000 battery systems across over 25 OEMs serving sectors such as robotics, defence, drones, agriculture equipment, electric vehicles, and solar energy.

According to the Pune-based startup, it designs its battery systems in house, covering cell selection, pack architecture, thermal management, and its proprietary Battery Management System. Its products are built for applications requiring high discharge performance, fast charging, intelligent battery management, and thermal safety.

The company plans to focus on specialised battery platforms for robotics, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), industrial automation, unmanned aerial systems, and other applications where reliability and performance are critical.
Adiabatic competes with startups such as EMO Energy, Clean Energy, Neuron Energy, and Inverted Energy.

title: Ixigo posts Rs 357 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit rises 81%
description: Online travel aggregator (OTA) Ixigo released reported an 13% year-on-year growth in revenue in Q1 FY27, while its profit rose 81% to Rs 34 crore during the same period.
body: Online travel aggregator (OTA) Ixigo released its financial results for the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year ending March 2027 on Thursday. The company reported an 13% year-on-year growth in revenue, while its profit rose 81% to Rs 34 crore during the same period.

Ixigo’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 356.75 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 316.05 crore in Q1 FY26, according to the company’s unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The Gurugram-based company derived the largest share of its operating revenue from train ticketing, which contributed more than 39% of the total in the quarter. Revenue from the segment rose to Rs 141.05 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 129.92 crore in the year ago period. Flight and bus ticketing generated Rs 104.56 crore and Rs 102.55 crore, respectively.
Apart from operating revenue, the company reported Rs 29.15 crore from interest income and gains on financial assets, pushing its total income to Rs 385.9 crore in Q1 FY27.
According to its press release, Ixigo's gross transaction value (GTV) increased 19% year on year to Rs 5,524.33 crore during the quarter.

The company did not disclose a detailed expense breakup in its quarterly financial statements. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 58.59 crore, while total expenses rose 14.7% to Rs 337.76 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 294.35 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Ixigo's profit rose 81% to Rs 34.34 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 18.94 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. On a sequential basis, profit increased 6.8% from Rs 32 crore in Q4 FY26.
Its listed peer MakeMyTrip reported revenue of $286 million in Q1 FY27, while profit declined 65% to $9.2 million during the same period.

title: Shiprocket crosses Rs 2,000 Cr revenue in FY26; loss rises 7% to Rs 79 Cr
description: Logistics and e-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket crossed the Rs 2,000 crore revenue mark in FY26, with operating revenue rising 24% year-on-year
body: Logistics and e-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket crossed the Rs 2,000 crore revenue mark in FY26, with operating revenue rising 24% year-on-year, while its losses widened 7% to Rs 79 crore ahead of its public listing.

Zomato-backed Shiprocket reported a 24% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 2,024 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,632 crore in the previous fiscal, according to its financial statements disclosed in the RHP.

While Shiprocket's core business, comprising its domestic shipping platform and value-added technology offerings, grew 13.7% year-on-year to Rs 1,485 crore, contributing 73.4% of total operating revenue, its emerging businesses, including the cross-border platform, marketing, and omnichannel offerings, generated the remaining Rs 539 crore, up 65% year-on-year.
The firm also earned Rs 53 crore from non-operating sources such as interest on fixed deposits, which took its total income to Rs 2,077 crore during the year.
Shiprocket's largest cost, materials consumed, increased 24.1% year-on-year to Rs 1,515 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 380 crore, including Rs 112 crore towards ESOPs.

Server and communication costs stood at Rs 58 crore, while advertising and promotional expenses jumped 71% year-on-year to Rs 36 crore. Higher spending across warehouse management, depreciation and amortisation, finance costs, and other overheads pushed the company's total expenditure up 23% to Rs 2,153 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,749 crore in the previous fiscal.

With revenue and expenses growing at a similar pace, Shiprocket's net loss increased marginally by 7% to Rs 79 crore in FY26 from Rs 74 crore a year earlier. The loss included Rs 112 crore in ESOP expenses.

The company spent Rs 1.06 to earn every rupee of operating revenue compared with Rs 1.07 in the previous fiscal. Its EBITDA margin and ROCE -3.31% ROCE stood at -6.39% in FY26. As of March 2026, It reported current assets of Rs 1,017 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 188 crore. Shiprocket has trimmed its IPO size by 31% to Rs 1,617.48 crore from Rs 2,342.35 crore proposed in the UDRHP. The reduction includes a cut in the fresh issue to Rs 885.5 crore from Rs 1,100 crore and the OFS to Rs 731.98 crore from Rs 1,242.35 crore.

title: Mela Ventures co leads $5.5 Mn Series A1 round in Solinas Integrity
description: Chennai based deeptech startup Solinas Integrity has raised $5.5 million in a Series A1 funding round co led by Mela Ventures and Hero Enterprise Family Office.
body: Chennai based deeptech startup Solinas Integrity has raised $5.5 million in a Series A1 funding round co led by Mela Ventures and Hero Enterprise Family Office.
The round also saw participation from Luthra Group along with follow on investments from existing backers SVL SME Fund, managed by SBI Ventures, Rainmatter Capital, and 8X Ventures Fund I.

The fresh capital will be deployed to expand manufacturing capacity, accelerate product development, strengthen the company's software infrastructure, and support working capital requirements. Solinas also plans to expand its presence in international markets, particularly the Middle East and Southeast Asia, while developing new robotics solutions for the water, sanitation, industrial, and defence sectors.

Founded in 2018 by Divanshu Kumar and Moinak Banerjee, the IIT Madras incubated startup builds robotics and AI powered solutions for underground water and sanitation infrastructure. Its product portfolio includes Endobot for pipeline inspection, HomoSEP for mechanised sewer and septic tank cleaning, and SWASTH AI, an infrastructure intelligence platform that uses inspection data for asset mapping and predictive analytics.
According to the company, its solutions have been deployed across more than 30 cities in 15 Indian states and are also in use by Dubai Municipality.
The company said it is also expanding into adjacent sectors such as oil and gas and defence, where its robotics and inspection technologies can be applied to critical infrastructure.

Solinas operates in the water, sanitation and hygiene segment, where utilities increasingly rely on mechanised inspection and maintenance tools to reduce water losses and improve underground infrastructure management. The startup says its integrated robotics platform enables inspection, cleaning, digitisation, and lifecycle management of underground water and wastewater networks.

title: Nazara approves Rs 733.5 Cr preferential share issue; new CEO to hold 4.67% stake
description: Nazara Technologies has approved a preferential issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 733.5 crore. The proposal awaits shareholder and regulatory approvals.
body: Nazara Technologies has approved a preferential issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 733.5 crore. The proposal awaits shareholder and regulatory approvals.
The board approved the issuance of up to 2,39,70,676 equity shares at an issue price of Rs 306 apiece, including a premium of Rs 304 per share, to six identified investors on a preferential basis.
The proposed allottees are Raymond Albaladejo Stauffer, Marc Sylvester Schutze, Maxime Loppin, Alexandre Paul Jean Noirot Cosson, Alexander Osou and Hugo Rémy Gaston Blavin.

Stauffer, who was appointed Nazara's chief executive officer earlier this week and will assume the role from September 1, is set to receive the largest allotment of 1,90,67,969 shares. Following the allotment, he will hold a 4.67% stake in the company.

The remaining investors will receive 28,32,273 shares, 10,03,628 shares, 7,10,946 shares, 2,66,895 shares and 88,965 shares, respectively. Collectively, the six investors will own a 5.87% stake in Nazara after the preferential issue.

The fundraising comes three days after Nazara reported a weak start to FY27. The company posted a 14% year on year decline in operating revenue to Rs 429 crore in the June quarter from Rs 499 crore in the year ago period. It also slipped to a net loss of Rs 82 crore against a net profit of Rs 51 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal. The loss included Rs 62 crore as its share of losses from associates and a Rs 22 crore impairment charge.

The board also announced a leadership transition earlier this week. Founder Nitish Mittersain stepped down as chief executive officer and will continue as managing director, focusing on the company's long term strategy and strategic partnerships, while Stauffer will take over as CEO from September 1.

title: BlackSoil funds Rs 80 Cr debt for Mintoak's ICC Loyalty acquisition
description: Mintoak, a Mumbai-based fintech SaaS startup backed by PayPal Ventures, has secured Rs 80 crore (approximately $9 million) in acquisition financing from BlackSoil.
body: Mintoak, a Mumbai-based fintech SaaS startup backed by PayPal Ventures, has secured Rs 80 crore (approximately $9 million) in acquisition financing from BlackSoil. The facility financed the debt component of Mintoak's acquisition of Dubai-based loyalty and rewards technology company ICC Loyalty.
Following the acquisition, Mintoak now partners with more than 50 banks, including HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, SBI Payments, Emirates Islamic and Absa Bank, across over 20 countries.

The combined platform supports more than 5 million merchants and 11 million customers while processng over $93 billion in annual payment volume. Together, Mintoak and ICC Loyalty offer capabilities across payments, merchant engagement, loyalty and customer engagement, which help banks unlock additional value beyond payments.

According to BlackSoil, the investment was driven by Mintoak's bank-led distribution model, deep integrations with leading financial institutions and track record of profitable growth. ICC Loyalty, which serves more than 30 banks across 10 countries, complements Mintoak's business. The combined entity generates more than $30 million in annual revenue with an EBITDA margin exceeding 30%.

Founded in 2016, BlackSoil is an alternative credit platform that operates an RBI registered systemically important NBFC and a SEBI registered AIF. The firm manages assets worth $275 million and provides credit to high-growth new economy businesses across India and Southeast Asia. Its portfolio includes 11 unicorns and 14 listed companies.

Mintoak provides a payments and engagement operating system for banks, enabling financial institutions to convert payment transactions into customer engagement, recurring revenue and long-term value through a unified white label platform.

title: Shiprocket IPO: Early investors set for up to 78X returns, late-stage backers face losses
description: The public listing of logistics unicorn Shiprocket is set to reward several of its early investors with multi-fold returns, while some late-stage backers are expected to incur losses on their partial exits.
body: The public listing of logistics unicorn Shiprocket is set to reward several of its early investors with multi-fold returns, while some late-stage backers are expected to incur losses on their partial exits.

According to the company's Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) , Shiprocket has reduced its IPO size by 31% to Rs 1,617.48 crore from Rs 2,342.35 crore proposed in the updated DRHP. The fresh issue has been cut to Rs 885.5 crore from Rs 1,100 crore, while the offer for sale (OFS) has been reduced to Rs 731.98 crore from Rs 1,242.35 crore.

According to Entrackr's analysis, at the upper price band of Rs 97 per share, early investor 500 Global is set to emerge as the biggest winner, generating an estimated 77.6X return on its Rs 16 crore OFS. Tribe Capital is expected to earn around 7.7X on its Rs 120 crore OFS, while Agility International Investment and March Capital are likely to generate returns of 2.6X and 2.1X on their Rs 21 crore and Rs 56 crore OFS, respectively.

However, the picture is marked differently for investors who entered Shiprocket at higher valuations in later funding rounds. Lightrock, the largest selling shareholder with an OFS worth Rs 272 crore, is expected to earn only 0.72X on the shares being sold. McKinsey through AFOS and Moore Strategic Partners are also likely to exit with returns of 0.59X and 0.67X, respectively, indicating that they are selling below their acquisition cost.

Founder shareholders Saahil Goel, Gautam Kapoor and Vishesh Khurana will also partially pare their holdings through the OFS. Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel are each selling shares worth Rs 61 crore, while Vishesh Khurana will offload shares worth Rs 20 crore.

Notably, Shiprocket's largest shareholder, Bertelsmann India Investments, which was included in the OFS in the earlier UDRHP, has opted out of the final offer. Major shareholders Eternal (formerly Zomato) and Temasek will also not participate in the OFS.
The IPO will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14, with the anchor book opening on August 11.

title: Leap India raises Rs 371 Cr in pre-IPO round led by GIC arm
description: KKR-backed supply chain solutions firm Leap India has raised Rs 371.3 crore in a pre-IPO placement led by Singapore-based GIC's subsidiary Gamnat Pte Ltd.
body: KKR-backed supply chain solutions firm Leap India has raised Rs 371.3 crore in a pre-IPO placement from Singapore-based sovereign wealth fund GIC's subsidiary Gamnat Pte Ltd, hedge fund Dymon Asia Multi-Strategy Investment (Singapore), and promoter Sunu Mathew, a day before its public issue opens.

According to a public advertisement published by the company, Leap India allotted 2.33 crore equity shares at Rs 159 apiece. Gamnat Pte Ltd emerged as the largest investor in the round, investing Rs 280 crore for 1.76 crore shares. Dymon Asia Multi-Strategy Investment invested Rs 50 crore, while Matyas Possessiones Private Limited, in which promoter Sunu Mathew owns a 99% stake, infused Rs 23 crore.

Leap India had filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) last week for a Rs 2,480 crore initial public offering, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 480 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 2,000 crore by existing shareholders. The issue is scheduled to open on August 7 and close on August 11.
The fresh capital will be used to repay borrowings, fund capital expenditure for the purchase of pallets, crates and intermediate bulk containers, and for general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2013, Leap India operates an asset pooling platform that enables enterprises to rent reusable pallets, crates and containers instead of owning them. As of March 31, 2026, the company managed 14.7 million pooled assets across more than 10,100 customer touchpoints nationwide.

For the fiscal year ended March 2026, Leap India reported 57% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue to Rs 730 crore from Rs 466 crore in FY25. At the same time, its profits also jumped over 70% to Rs 63 crore.

title: Exclusive: Get My Parking to raise Rs 40 Cr from IvyCap Ventures at flat valuation
description: AI based parking management startup Get My Parking is set to raise Rs 40 crore (approximately $4.21 million) in an extended Series A round from existing investor
body: AI based parking management startup Get My Parking is set to raise Rs 40 crore (approximately $4.21 million) in an extended Series A round from existing investor IvyCap Ventures.
The funding comes more than a year after the company raised $2.5 million in its Series A round in June 2025, led by IvyCap Ventures.

The company's board has passed a resolution to issue 7,261 Series A3 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 55,088 each to raise Rs 40 crore, according to its regulatory filing accessed by Entrackr.

According to Entrackr's estimates, the round values Get My Parking at around Rs 375 crore, up from Rs 335 crore in the previous round. The proceeds will be used to fund the company's business operations.

Founded in 2015 by Chirag Jain and Rasik Pansare, Get My Parking offers AI and IoT powered parking management solutions that enable operators to digitize parking facilities with features such as automated entry, digital payments, and real time parking availability.
The Bengaluru based company has raised over $12.5 million to date. Following the investment, IvyCap Ventures will remain the largest external shareholder with a 31.43% stake in the company.
Get My Parking is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. For the fiscal year ended March 2025, its operating revenue grew 22.6% to Rs 36.04 crore, while losses widened 66.2% to Rs 10.87 crore.
Get My Parking competes with Park+, Parky, Park Smart, and others.

title: Aramco Ventures leads $9.5 Mn funding in climate tech startup Mitti Labs
description: Climate tech startup Mitti Labs has raised $9.5 million in a funding round led by Aramco Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco. Existing and new investors,
body: Climate tech startup Mitti Labs has raised $9.5 million in a funding round led by Aramco Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco. Existing and new investors, including Lightspeed India, Godrej Industries Group, Cisco Foundation, Francis Family Fund, and Volta Circle, also participated.
The startup had previously raised $3 million.
The fresh funds will be used to expand its presence across India and enter the Philippines and Indonesia, Mitti Labs said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2023 by Devdut Dalal and Xavier Laguarta Soler, Mitti Labs uses satellite imagery and AI to support water efficient farming practices. The company generates carbon credits by verifying emission reductions from these practices and sells them to corporations pursuing net zero emission goals.

Headquartered in Bengaluru and New York, Mitti Labs operates in the AgTech, climate smart agriculture, digital Measurement, Reporting and Verification (dMRV), and carbon credits segments. According to the company, it works with tens of thousands of farmers across multiple Indian states, covering more than 70,000 hectares.

Mitti Labs says its technology can reduce water usage by up to 40% and methane emissions by around 50%. It combines synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery with ground level field measurements to build digital twins of individual rice plots for monitoring and carbon accounting. The company also said its projects in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh received an 'A' rating from carbon credit ratings agency Sylvera.

title: Healthcare AI startup Consint.AI raises Rs 22 Cr in Series A round
description: Consint.AI,  a deeptech company transforming healthcare and insurance risk management through artificial intelligence, has raised Rs 22 crore ($2.3 million) Snippets
body: Consint.AI , a deeptech company transforming healthcare and insurance risk management through artificial intelligence , has raised Rs 22 crore ($2.3 million) in a Series A funding round backed by BIG Global Investment JSC, Equanimity Ventures Trust II and Seafund Venture India Scheme I.

The proceeds will be used to expand globally, strengthen its AI research and enterprise delivery capabilities, and develop a foundational model for detecting fraud, waste and abuse across healthcare, insurance, banking and financial services.
Founded by Ashish Chaturvedi, Consint.AI develops AI platforms for healthcare and insurance risk management.

The company has assessed more than 100 million transactions and identified over Rs 1,000 crore in fraud using more than 500 AI and machine learning models, fine-tuned LLMs and over 500 digitised clinical protocols.

The startup also works across claims processing, document forensics and clinical intelligence. Its new foundational model will be designed to improve fraud detection and support insurers, healthcare providers and government health programmes.

With the latest funding, Consint.AI plans to expand its operations across India, the Middle East, Africa, the United States and Southeast Asia while adding more AI-based healthcare and insurance solutions to its platform.

title: Stellaris Venture leads $8 Mn Series A round in equity research startup Pinegap
description: Pinegap says it works directly with investment teams to understand their workflows before building custom AI agents tailored to each team's research style.
body: Equity research startup Pinegap has raised $8 million (around Rs 76 crore) in a Series A funding round led by Stellaris Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors including Silicon Valley Quad and DeVC.
The startup had previously raised $2.5 million in a seed funding round in 2024.
c, Pinegap said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Ankit Varmani and Deepak Sharma, Pinegap is an AI powered equity research platform that automates workflows for institutional buy side analysts at hedge funds and mutual funds using custom AI agents. The company develops agentic AI platforms and custom AI workflows for institutional equity research, earnings analysis, and investment thesis tracking.

Pinegap says it works directly with investment teams to understand their workflows before building custom AI agents tailored to each team's research style. The company claims to have deployed more than 1,000 AI agents across over 100 customers, which have generated over 50,000 research reports to date.

Pinegap is addressing a growing opportunity where startups are using AI to automate established enterprise workflows. Similar approaches are being adopted across sectors such as healthcare, ecommerce, marketing, and financial services to improve productivity and streamline operations.

title: HomeRun raises $12 Mn in Series A+ round led by Nexus Venture Partners
description: Bengaluru-based construction materials quick commerce startup HomeRun has secured $12 million in a Series A+ funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners. News
body: Bengaluru-based construction materials quick commerce startup HomeRun has secured $12 million in a Series A+ funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners.
The round also included participation from existing investors Sorin Investments, Titan Capital, Sparrow Capital, and Consumer Collective by Atrium.

The fundraise follows the company's $6.6 million round earlier this year. HomeRun plans to use the fresh capital to expand into new markets while strengthening its supply chain, technology, and product portfolio.

Founded by Pukhraj Grewal, HomeRun delivers construction and interior materials to contractors and homeowners within 60 minutes. Its catalogue spans cement, plywood, wires, paints, hardware, and other building materials.
The startup says it has fulfilled more than 100,000 orders and recorded 8X growth over the past year. It currently operates in Bengaluru and has expanded across its core product categories.
Before founding HomeRun, Grewal co-founded interior contracting startup Tornado and construction labour marketplace Project Hero.

HomeRun is part of a growing category focused on the rapid delivery of construction materials. Last week, Bengaluru-based Fixxly raised $5.5 million in a seed round from Accel, Fireside Ventures, and Lightspeed India Partners. The company also competes with established building material retailers and startups such as IBO and Material Depot.

The investment also adds to Nexus Venture Partners' portfolio of early stage startups. Last year, the venture capital firm closed its eighth fund at $700 million to back companies across artificial intelligence, enterprise software, consumer, and fintech sectors in India and the US.

title: Shiprocket trims IPO size by 31% in RHP to Rs 1,617 Cr; issue to open on August 12
description: Logistics and e-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket has reduced the size of its initial public offering (IPO) by 31% in its red herring prospectus (RHP).
body: Logistics and e-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket has reduced the size of its initial public offering (IPO) by 31% in its red herring prospectus (RHP), lowering the issue size to Rs 1,617.48 crore from earlier proposed Rs 2,342.35 crore in UDRHP.

The IPO will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14, with the anchor book opening on August 11. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 92 to Rs 97 per share. At the upper price band, the company will be valued at around Rs 7,057 crore or $743 million.

According to the RHP, the company has reduced the fresh issue size to Rs 885.5 crore from the Rs 1,100 crore proposed earlier. The offer also includes an offer for sale (OFS) worth Rs 731.98 crore by existing shareholders, down from the previously proposed size.

The OFS will be led by Lightrock, which plans to sell shares worth Rs 271.7 crore, followed by Tribe Capital and March Capital (through MCP3 SPV LLC), which will offload shares worth Rs 120 crore and Rs 55.53 crore, respectively. Other selling shareholders include AFOS, 500 Global, Agility International Investment , and Moore Strategic Ventures.
The company's co-founders Gautam Kapoor and Saahil Goel have reduced their OFS to Rs 61 crore each, while Vishesh Khurana will sell shares worth Rs 20 crore.
Notably, Arvind Ltd and Bertelsmann India Investments, which were part of the OFS in the earlier UDRHP, have opted not to participate in the RHP.

The company plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue primarily to expand its platform across both its core and emerging businesses. Of the total, Rs 365.6 crore has been earmarked for growth initiatives, including Rs 205.8 crore for marketing and Rs 159.8 crore for technology infrastructure and capabilities. Another Rs 210 crore will be used to repay borrowings, while the remaining proceeds will support inorganic growth through acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
The IPO is being managed by Axis Capital, BofA Securities, JM Financial and Kotak, while KFin Technologies will act as registrar.

title: Ola Electric's Q1 FY27 revenue drops 45% to Rs 455 Cr, loss narrows 22%
description: Ola Electric continued to struggle during Q1 FY27 as its revenue declined 45% year-on-year. However, the Bengaluru-based company managed to narrow its losses by 22%.
body: Electric vehicle maker Ola Electric continued to struggle during Q1 FY27 as its revenue declined 45% year-on-year. However, the Bengaluru-based company managed to narrow its losses by 22% to Rs 336 crore

Ola Electric’s revenue from operations declined to Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 828 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The company's automotive business generated Rs 455 crore, contributing 98.91% of segment revenue, while its cell business contributed Rs 5 crore, taking the combined segment revenue to Rs 460 crore during the quarter, without considering inter-segment eliminations. During the quarter, Ola Electric recorded 43,908 EV registrations, a 25% year-on-year decline.
Apart from operating revenue, the company reported Rs 29 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 484 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 896 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Ola Electric reduced its total expenses by 41.8% year-on-year to Rs 620 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,065 crore in Q1 FY26. Procurement (cost of materials) stood at Rs 317 crore, while employee benefit expenses declined 46.1% to Rs 48 crore during the quarter.

Despite a 45% decline in operating revenue during Q1 FY27, Ola Electric reduced its net loss by 21.1% to Rs 336 crore from Rs 426 crore in Q1 FY26, aided by lower spending on manufacturing. On a sequential basis, Ola Electric's operating revenue jumped 71.7% to Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 265 crore in the preceding quarter, while its losses declined 32.8% to Rs 336 crore from Rs 500 crore during the same period. In June 2026, Ola Electric had raised Rs 780 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), with the issue being oversubscribed by 56% against its initial fundraising target of Rs 500 crore. At the close of trading on Friday, Ola Electric's shares settled at Rs 41.07 apiece, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 19,185 crore.

title: Elevation Capital clocks nearly Rs 6,000 Cr from IPOs and secondary stake sales over past 15 months
description: Elevation Capital has realised nearly Rs 6,000 crore through partial stake sales in listed Indian tech companies over the past 15 months, while retaining listed startup investments worth over Rs 20,000 crore across Meesho, Paytm and Urban Company.
body: Elevation Capital, one of India's oldest venture capital firms, has realised nearly Rs 6,000 crore from partial stake sales in listed Indian technology companies over the past 15 months through IPO offer for sale transactions, block deals and bulk deals, while continuing to hold listed startup investments worth more than Rs 20,000 crore (over $2 billion) across Meesho, Paytm and Urban Company.

The latest stake sale came on Tuesday, when Elevation Capital sold shares worth Rs 974.5 crore in Meesho through a block deal by offloading 1.49 crore shares. The transaction followed another major stake sale earlier this week, when Elevation Capital, through its investment entities, sold a 2.33% stake in Paytm in a block deal worth Rs 2,038 crore by offloading 1.49 crore shares at Rs 1,367.8 apiece.

These transactions are part of a series of partial stake sales over the past 15 months. In November 2025, Elevation sold shares worth Rs 1,556 crore in Paytm. It also pared its holding in ixigo through four transactions between May and October 2025, realising around Rs 808 crore. Apart from secondary market stake sales, the firm also monetised part of its investments through IPO offer for sale transactions, selling shares worth Rs 271 crore in Meesho's public issue and Rs 346 crore in Urban Company 's IPO.

Overall, Elevation Capital has realised nearly Rs 5,993 crore through partial stake sales in Indian technology companies over the past 15 months via IPO offer for sale transactions, block deals and bulk deals. The transactions illustrate how venture capital firms monetise mature investments during IPOs and through secondary market transactions after listing.

Despite these partial stake sales, the firm continues to hold sizeable stakes in several listed startups. Following the latest block deal, Elevation's remaining stake in Meesho is valued at around Rs 9,550 crore (over $1 billion) at the prevailing market price. It also holds a stake worth around Rs 9,015 crore (about $950 million) in Paytm through SAIF III Mauritius and SAIF Partners India IV , while its holding in Urban Company is valued at approximately Rs 1,793 crore (about $189 million). The remaining stake values are based on prevailing market prices following Tuesday's block deal.
Queries sent to Elevation Capital on Wednesday did not receive a response until the publication of this story.
The sizeable residual portfolio underscores that despite selective stake sales, Elevation Capital remains among the largest institutional shareholders in several listed new-age technology companies.

title: D2C athleisure brand BlissClub raises Rs 160 Cr in Series B led by Singularity AMC
description: BlissClub has yet to file its annual financial report for FY26. In FY25, its operating revenue grew 51% to Rs 131.5 crore in FY25 from Rs 87 crore in FY24. During the s
body: D2C athleisure brand BlissClub has raised Rs 160 crore ($16.8 million) in a Series B funding round led by Singularity AMC. Founder Minu Margeret and her partner Vidit Aatrey also participated in the round, alongside existing investors Elevation Capital and Eight Roads Ventures.
The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised $15 million in its Series A round in May 2022, led by Eight Roads Ventures with participation from Elevation Capital.

According to the company, the fresh capital will be used to expand into new categories, scale its offline retail presence, strengthen product development, and hire talent to support its next phase of growth.

Founded in 2020 by Minu Margeret, BlissClub is a direct-to-consumer (D2C) athleisure and functional apparel brand. The company initially focused on technical activewear for Indian women and has since expanded into an omnichannel business with more than 40 retail stores and a recently launched menswear line.

Its portfolio includes leggings, tops, outerwear, and accessories developed through in-house research and sourcing. The brand sells through its own website, marketplaces, and offline retail stores across India.

BlissClub has yet to file its annual financial report for FY26. In FY25, its operating revenue grew 51% to Rs 131.5 crore in FY25 from Rs 87 crore in FY24. During the same period, the company also reduced its losses by more than half, aided by lower employee costs.

title: Exclusive: PayGlocal set to raise fresh funding at $120 Mn valuation
description: Cross-border payments startup PayGlocal is set to raise Rs 36.38 crore ($3.84 million) from existing investor BEENEXTin its first funding round in more than four years.
body: Cross-border payments startup PayGlocal is set to raise Rs 36.38 crore ($3.84 million) from existing investor BEENEXTin its first funding round in more than four years.
PayGlocal last raised $12 million in its Series B round led by Tiger Global, with participation from Sequoia Capital India and BEENEXT. Entrackr had exclusively reported the round.

The board at PayGlocal has passed a special resolution to issue 5,074 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 71,693.02 per share to raise Rs 36.38 crore, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr . As per Entrackr’s estimates, the Bengaluru based company's valuation will increase 31.8% to Rs 1,140 crore or ($120 million) from Rs 865 crore in its previous funding round.

Founded in 2021 by Prachi Dharani, Rohit Sukhija, and Yogesh Lokhande, PayGlocal provides RBI-authorised cross-border payment infrastructure that enables Indian businesses to accept international payments. The company earns revenue by offering payment gateway, multi-currency collection, export documentation, fraud prevention, and settlement solutions to exporters, SaaS firms, D2C brands, marketplaces, and freelancers.

Following the allotment, Peak XV will remain the largest external shareholder with a 34.04% stake, followed by BeeNext (6.14%) and Tiger Global (5.21%), while co-founders Prachi Dharani, Rohit Sukhija, and Yogesh Lokhande will hold 18.92%, 14.19%, and 13.37%, respectively.

Prior to this round the company has raised around $17 million to date. Key investors Tiger Global, Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners), BEENEXT, and other existing investors. The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, PayGlocal's operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 25.11 crore from Rs 12.20 crore in FY24, while its losses declined to Rs 14 crore from Rs 15.31 crore.

title: Exclusive: Dosa chain Benne raises Rs 35 Cr led by Rajan pai's Claypond Capital
description: Mumbai-based dosa chain Benne has raised Rs 35 crore (around $3.70 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Ranjan pAi’ Claypond Capital.
body: Mumbai-based dosa chain Benne has raised Rs 35 crore (around $3.70 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Ranjan pAi’ Claypond Capital.

The company's board has passed a resolution to issue 1,799 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 20,349 each to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its regulatory filing accessed by Entrackr.

The round was led by Ranjan Pai's family office, Claypond Capital, which invested Rs 28.75 crore. AL Trusts invested Rs 3.5 crore, followed by Mukul Agrawal with Rs 1.75 crore. Madhukeshwar Desai and Cortado Advisory Services also participated, investing Rs 75 lakh and Rs 25 lakh, respectively.

According to Entrackr's estimates, the round valued the company at around Rs 364 crore (approximately $38.3 million) on a post-money basis. The fresh proceeds will be deployed towards expanding the company's operations and supporting its growth plans.
In April, Moneycontrol reported that Benne was in talks to raise Rs 35–40 crore in a funding round led by Claypond Capital.

Founded by husband-wife duo Akhil Iyer and Shriya Narayan, Benne is a quick service restaurant (QSR) chain focused on authentic Bengaluru-style dosas. The brand generates revenue through dine-in, takeaway, and food delivery, with a limited menu and compact outlets driving operational efficiency and consistent quality.

Following the allotment, Infinyte Club remains the largest external shareholder with a 9% stake, followed by Claypond Capital Partners (8.21%), Mukul Mahavir Agrawal (5%), Madhukeshwar Desai (3.85%), AL Trust (1%), and Cortado Advisory Services (0.07%). Peercheque is also among Benne's earliest investors.
Benne competes with The Rameshwaram Cafe, Cafe Amudham, and other premium South Indian QSR brands.

title: Delhivery posts Rs 2,931 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; profit declines 65%
description: Logistics company Delhivery reported a 27.8% year-on-year increase in revenue in Q1 FY27, while its profit declined sharply during the quarter.
body: Logistics company Delhivery reported a 27.8% year-on-year increase in revenue in Q1 FY27, while its profit declined sharply during the quarter.
Delhivery’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 2,931 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,294 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The company primarily earns revenue from its logistics services, including warehousing, last-mile delivery, and the design and deployment of logistics management systems. Other income declined 12.3% to Rs 114 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 130 crore in the year-ago quarter. As a result, the company’s total income rose 25.6% to Rs 3,045 crore from Rs 2,424 crore in Q1 FY26.

Freight handling and servicing costs remained Delhivery’s largest expense, accounting for 71.45% of total expenses. The cost increased 31.4% to Rs 2,152 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 1,638 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Employee benefit expenses increased 21.9% to Rs 429 crore from Rs 352 crore, while depreciation rose 28.6% to Rs 189 crore from Rs 147 crore. Finance costs remained flat at Rs 34 crore, whereas other expenses climbed 33.5% to Rs 207 crore from Rs 155 crore.
The company’s total expenses rose 29.4% to Rs 3,012 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,327 crore in Q1 FY26.

Despite the strong growth in revenue, Delhivery’s profit declined 64.8% to Rs 32 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 91 crore in Q1 FY26. On a sequential basis, Delhivery’s operating revenue increased 2.8% to Rs 2,930.73 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 2,850 crore in the preceding quarter, while its profit declined 55.9% to Rs 31.91 crore from Rs 72.40 crore during the same period.
Delhivery’s shares were closed at Rs 473.30 apiece on Friday, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 35,198 crore.

title: Easebuzz revenue crosses Rs 700 Cr in FY26; profit plunges 42%
description: Easebuzz saw single-digit growth in the fiscal year ended March 2026, while its profit fell 43%. The slowdown came largely from the ban on real-money
body: Full-stack payments solutions provider Easebuzz saw single-digit growth in the fiscal year ended March 2026, while its profit fell 43%. The slowdown came largely from the ban on real-money gaming apps at the start of the fiscal year, which affected the firm’s growth and profitability.
The Beesemer-backed company’s revenue from operations grew 9.1% to Rs 716 crore in FY26 from Rs 656 crore in FY25 , according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Easebuzz, a B2B payment gateway for SMEs, provides plug-and-play APIs for payments, disbursements, and financial operations. In the last fiscal year, the firm generated Rs 697 crore from  transaction fees, which accounted for 97.35% of its operating revenue, while information tech and support fees contributed Rs 14 crore and SaaS fees Rs 5 crore.
Apart from operations, Easebuzz earned Rs 7 crore in other income in FY26, taking its total income to Rs 723 crore from Rs 659 crore in FY25.

For the digital payments firm, payment processing charges remained the largest cost centre, rising 2% to Rs 557 crore in FY26 from Rs 546 crore in FY25 and accounting for 78.67% of total expenses during the last fiscal year.

The $30 million funding round at the start of the fiscal year was followed by a sharp increase in Easebuzz's operating expenses. Employee benefit expenses surged 82.7% to Rs 95 crore, while information technology expenses rose 68.8% to Rs 27 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses jumped 350% to Rs 9 crore, while other expenses increased 11.1% to Rs 20 crore.
Overall, Easebuzz’s total expenses outpaced its revenue growth and rose 11.7%  year-on-year to Rs 708 crore in FY26 from Rs 634 crore in FY25.

With expenses growing faster than revenue, the company’s profitability declined in FY26. Easebuzz’s profit fell 42.1% to Rs 11 crore from Rs 19 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA declined to Rs 14 crore from Rs 28 crore, while the EBITDA margin dropped to 1.96% from 4.27%.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Aug 03 - Aug 08]
description: This week, 28 Indian startups raised nearly $383.5 million across 5 growth stage deals, 21 early stage deals, and 1 undisclosed deal. The week also witnessed. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 28 Indian startups raised nearly $383.5 million across 5 growth stage deals, 21 early stage deals, and 1 undisclosed deal. The week also witnessed 8 key hires, 2 fund launches, 3 M&A deals.
In contrast, 17 startups had collectively secured about $82.2 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised nearly $273.7 million across six deals this week, led by River Mobility's $120 million Series C round from Elev8 and Claypond Capital. Leap India also raised Rs 371.3 crore in a pre-IPO placement from GIC subsidiary Gamnat Pte Ltd. It was followed by AI unicorn Sarvam’s $74 million in an extension of its Series B round, led by NVIDIA Corporation.

Among other deals, BlissClub secured Rs 160 crore in Series B funding from Singularity AMC, Matel Motion & Energy Solutions raised Rs 130 crore (around $15 million) from UC Impower, while Mintoak bagged Rs 80 crore (about $9 million) in acquisition financing from BlackSoil.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $109.8 million across 19 deals this week, led by InRisk Labs' $27 million Series A round co-led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Northpoint Capital. HomeRun followed with a $12 million Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners, while Mitti Labs and Pinegap raised $9.5 million and $8 million, respectively.
Other startups that secured funding this week included Vaaree, GetVantage, Kaapi Machines, Solinas Integrity, Benne, and 14 more early-stage ventures.

title: Paper Boat parent reports Rs 760 Cr revenue in FY26; profit shrinks 96%
description: Paper Boat maker Hector Beverages reported a steady increase in revenue during the fiscal year ended March 2026, but a sharp rise in operating expenses eroded profitability.
body: Paper Boat maker Hector Beverages reported a steady increase in revenue during the fiscal year ended March 2026, but a sharp rise in operating expenses eroded profitability.

According to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC), the company's operating revenue increased 13.8% year-on-year to Rs 760 crore in FY26 from Rs 668 crore in FY25.

Hector Beverages sells beverages under the Paper Boat brand and competes with established players such as Dabur, PepsiCo, Coca-Cola and several regional juice and traditional beverage brands in India.
Including Rs 18 crore in other income, Hector Beverages' total income stood at Rs 778 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 682 crore in the previous fiscal year.

A shift in product mix drove the company's top line during the year. Revenue from traded goods rose 30.2% to Rs 574 crore in FY26 from Rs 441 crore in FY25 and contributed over 75% of the operating revenue. In contrast, revenue from manufactured goods declined 18.6% to Rs 184 crore from Rs 226 crore a year earlier.
The company's expenses grew at a faster pace than revenue. Total expenditure increased 22% to Rs 776 crore in FY26 from Rs 636 crore in FY25.

Consumption of materials remained the largest cost head at Rs 485 crore, accounting for 62.5% of the total expenditure, compared to Rs 447 crore in the previous year. Employee benefit expenses declined marginally to Rs 88 crore from Rs 90 crore.

The company also ramped up spending on growth and operations. Advertising and promotional expenses jumped 55.6% to Rs 28 crore, while selling and distribution expenses increased 15.5% to Rs 67 crore. Job work charges more than doubled to Rs 25 crore during the year. Other operating expenses like legal & professional, travelling expenses, rent added another Rs 83 crore in the last fiscal year.

title: IdeaForge’s revenue jumps over 5X to Rs 69 Cr in Q1 FY27; loss narrows 89%
description: Drone maker IdeaForge Technologies saw revenue balloon more than fivefold in Q1 FY27, while losses narrowed sharply. However, it slipped back into the red after
body: Drone maker IdeaForge Technologies saw revenue balloon more than fivefold in Q1 FY27, while losses narrowed sharply. However, it slipped back into the red after a profitable March quarter, with revenue also falling sequentially.

IdeaForge’s revenue from operations jumped to Rs 68.58 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 12.78 crore in Q1 FY26, registering a 436.6% YoY growth, according to financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The company reported Rs 1.96 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 70.5 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 16.7 crore in Q1 FY26.

Cost of materials remained the company’s largest expense, jumping 7.15X to Rs 34.97 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4.89 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased 20.9% to Rs 15.1 crore from Rs 12.49 crore, while depreciation rose 44.9% to Rs 14.2 crore from Rs 9.8 crore.

Meanwhile, finance costs jumped 5.49X to Rs 2.03 crore from Rs 0.37 crore, while other expenses increased 11.9% to Rs 16.2 crore from Rs 14.48 crore. Overall, IdeaForge’s total expenses rose 96.4% to Rs 82.5 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 42 crore in Q1 FY26.
As a result, IdeaForge’s loss narrowed 89% to Rs 2.59 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 23.56 crore in Q1 FY26.

On a sequential basis, the company’s operating revenue declined around 51% from Rs 141 crore in Q4 FY26. IdeaForge had reported a net profit of Rs 60 crore in Q4 FY26, before slipping back into the red in the June quarter.
In June 2026, ideaForge Technology had raised Rs 500 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP) by allotting 62.89 lakh shares at Rs 795 per share.
IdeaForge’s shares were closed at Rs 902.10 apiece on Friday, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 4,483 crore.

title: Info Edge posts Rs 490 Cr profit on Rs 881 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27
description: Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri and 99acres, reported an over 11% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue in Q1 FY27. Its profit rose 43% year-on-year to Rs 490 crore during the quarter.
body: Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri and 99acres, reported an over 11% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue in Q1 FY27. Its profit rose 43% year-on-year to Rs 490 crore during the quarter.
According to its filing with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Info Edge’s consolidated revenue rose to Rs 881 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 791 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.
Its recruitment solutions business, led by Naukri, remained the largest revenue contributor, with revenue rising 12% year-on-year to Rs 629 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 562 crore in Q1 FY26.
Meanwhile, real estate platform 99acres reported revenue of Rs 130 crore in Q1 FY27, up from Rs 111 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.

The company’s matchmaking segment, which includes Jeevansathi and Aisle, contributed Rs 38 crore and Rs 12 crore, respectively, during the quarter. Meanwhile, Shiksha’s revenue declined 12% year-on-year to Rs 44 crore.
The company added Rs 192 crore non operating income, which pushed its overall income to Rs 1,073 crore in Q1 FY27.

On the expense side, employee benefit expenses remained the company’s largest cost component at Rs 341 crore in Q1 FY27, followed by advertisement expenses of Rs 119 crore. Overall expenses remained largely flat at Rs 580 crore during the quarter.

Led by steady year-on-year growth in operating revenue, controlled costs, and healthy non-operating income, the company’s profit rose 43% year-on-year to Rs 490 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 343 crore in Q1 FY26.

title: GalaxEye acquires spacecraft engineering company StarOps
description: StarOps has expertise across spacecraft systems engineering, mission operations, propulsion, avionics, flight computing, guidance and navigation, structures and
body: Space technology startup GalaxEye has acquired Bengaluru-based spacecraft engineering company StarOps.

The acquisition brings StarOps’ proprietary technologies, qualified satellite platforms and systems engineering expertise to GalaxEye, along with an experienced engineering team. Several members of the team previously worked at TeamIndus on its Lunar Lander and Rover projects. Their experience across mission design, spacecraft development and end-of-life operations will add to GalaxEye’s capabilities across the satellite value chain.

Founded in 2022, StarOps develops satellite platforms and works on the indigenisation of spacecraft technologies in India. The acquisition adds its experience in satellite design, development and qualification to GalaxEye’s internal capabilities.

StarOps has expertise across spacecraft systems engineering, mission operations, propulsion, avionics, flight computing, guidance and navigation, structures and mechanisms, electrical systems, programme management and ground operations.
