description: Consumer appliances brand Atomberg’s revenue grew 34.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 1,294 crore in FY26, even as its losses widened during the year.
body: Consumer appliances brand Atomberg’s revenue grew 34.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 1,294 crore in FY26, even as its losses widened during the year. The company’s revenue and financial performance details were disclosed in its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).
The Mumbai-based company makes energy-efficient brushless direct current (BLDC) and smart fans, along with mixer grinders, smart locks, water purifiers and juicers.

Home appliances remained Atomberg’s biggest revenue driver, contributing Rs 1,153 crore, or nearly 89% of its operating revenue, in FY26. Revenue from the segment grew 23.1% from Rs 937 crore in FY25.
The company’s kitchen appliances business saw sharper growth, with revenue jumping over sixfold to Rs 124 crore in FY26 from Rs 19.3 crore in the previous fiscal.

Atomberg also generated Rs 17.2 crore from proprietary components, compared with Rs 3.63 crore in FY25. Its other income stood at Rs 30 crore, taking its total income to Rs 1,324 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,001 crore a year earlier.
On the cost front, materials remained the company’s largest expense at Rs 738 crore, accounting for 50.55% of its total expenditure. The cost increased 37.9% from Rs 535 crore in FY25.

Employee benefit expenses also rose 32.1% to Rs 210 crore from Rs 159 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses stood at Rs 135 crore, while labour charges and depreciation and amortisation expenses came in at Rs 57 crore and Rs 71 crore, respectively.
Overall, Atomberg’s total expenditure increased 30.6% to Rs 1,460 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,118 crore in FY25.

title: A91 invests Rs 143 Cr in Atomberg, sells Rs 445 Cr stake while retaining 21%
description: The investment has generated a significant return for A91. Against its total investment of around Rs 143 crore, the fund has sold shares worth approximately Rs 445 crore.
body: A91 Partners has invested around Rs 143 crore in consumer appliances startup Atomberg through primary and secondary transactions, and has already sold shares worth around Rs 445 crore, according to the company’s draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed ahead of its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

The disclosures show that A91 invested around Rs 118 crore as primary capital in Atomberg, while another Rs 25 crore was invested through secondary transactions. The secondary purchases helped provide an exit to some of the company’s early shareholders, including founders and Parampara Early Stage Opportunities Fund.

The investment has generated a significant return for A91. Against its total investment of around Rs 143 crore, the fund has sold shares worth approximately Rs 445 crore. Despite these partial exits, A91 continues to remain Atomberg’s largest shareholder with a 21.02% stake as of the DRHP date.
A91’s investment in Atomberg dates back to 2019, when it led the company’s Series A round. The investor also participated in Atomberg’s Series B round in 2020.

The latest DRHP disclosures also highlight the broader secondary transactions that have taken place at Atomberg over the years. Early investors, founders and other shareholders have sold shares worth around Rs 683 crore since 2019. A91 was the largest seller, with sales worth about Rs 445 crore, followed by Parampara, which sold shares worth around Rs 116 crore. Atomberg’s co-founders Manoj Meena and Sibabrata Das also sold part of their holdings.

Founded by Meena and Das, Atomberg started with energy-efficient BLDC fans and has expanded into other home and kitchen appliances. The company reported Rs 1,293.77 crore revenue from operations in FY26, up 34.8% year-on-year, while its net loss stood at Rs 149 crore.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Aug 17 - Aug 22]
description: This week, 21 Indian startups raised $198.33 million across 3 growth-stage deals, 14 early-stage deals and 4 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 8 key hires. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 21 Indian startups raised $198.33 million across 3 growth-stage deals, 14 early-stage deals and 4 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 8 key hires, 2 departures and 2 mergers and acquisitions.
In contrast, 14 startups had collectively secured about $151.5 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]

Growth-stage startups raised $118.3 million across three deals this week. Fintech unicorn Navi led the segment with a $100 million investment from Prosus in its first institutional funding round. Electric two-wheeler maker BGauss raised Rs 110 crore ($11.6 million) in a Series D round, while Mumbai-based paediatric behavioural health platform Butterfly Learnings secured Rs 65 crore ($6.7 million) in a Pre-Series B round led by Inflexor Ventures.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $80.03 million across 14 deals this week. CtrlS led the segment with Rs 250 crore, including Rs 200 crore from Zerodha cofounder Nikhil Kamath and Rs 50 crore from entrepreneur Sreeram Reddy Vanga. NeoGeo raised $20 million in a Series A led by Neev II Fund and Aavishkaar Capital, while Rezolv secured $12.5 million in a Series A led by Norwest.
Peeko raised over $7 million in a Series A led by Chiratae Venture, while healthtech platform Lissun raised Rs 48 crore in a Series A led by Colossa Ventures.

Other startups that secured funding this week included DeHaat Honest Farms, a pesticide-free food brand by DeHaat, deeptech startup AlgoFET, specialty coffee brand First Coffee, reusable packaging platform Yantra Packs and five other early-stage ventures.

title: Lenskart investors sell over $1 Bn stake in 3 months; SoftBank offloads another $300 Mn
description: Together, these four transactions, including SoftBank's two sales, amount to around Rs 9,660 crore worth of shares sold by large institutional investors since June.
body: SoftBank has sold another 4.5 crore shares of eyewear retailer Lenskart for around Rs 2,888 crore (over $300 million) through a block deal, making its second large sell-off in the company since June.

According to the stock exchange, the shares were sold at Rs 641.75 each, taking the total value of the transaction to Rs 2,888 crore. SoftBank held 17.14 crore Lenskart shares, or a 9.69% stake, as of July. Following the latest sale, its holding has fallen to around 12.64 crore shares, or about 7.15%.

The latest transaction comes less than three months after SoftBank sold Lenskart shares worth around Rs 2,873 crore in June. It had sold around 5.65 crore shares at Rs 508.55 each in that transaction.

SoftBank is not the only early investor to have reduced its stake in Lenskart in recent months. Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) sold shares worth around Rs 1,960 crore in June, while Temasek offloaded shares worth around Rs 1,940 crore in July.
Together, these four transactions, including SoftBank's two sales, amount to around Rs 9,660 crore (over $1 billion) worth of Lenskart shares sold by large institutional investors since June.

The sell-offs come as Lenskart continues to see strong investor interest in the listed eyewear company. The company made its stock market debut in November 2025 and has since seen several large institutional transactions.
The latest block deal saw shares picked up by a mix of institutional investors, including Societe Generale, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, Sundaram Mutual Fund and global funds.

During its latest quarterly results (Q1 FY27), the company posted 43% year-on-year growth in its revenue to Rs 2,714 crore with a profit of Rs 228 crore. The company closed its trading session at  Rs 658.75, with a total market capitalization of Rs 1,14,225 crore.

title: Y Combinator sells Rs 970 Cr Meesho stake in block deal
description: The deal comes weeks after other early backers of Meesho, including Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital, offloaded Rs 1,949 crore worth of holdings in the company.
body: Global startup accelerator Y Combinator has sold shares worth around Rs 970 crore in Meesho through a block deal on the stock exchanges, marking another major exit by an early investor in the ecommerce company.

According to data available on the NSE, Y Combinator sold around 4.84 crore shares worth Rs 969.63 crore in the transaction. The deal comes weeks after other early backers of Meesho, including Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital, offloaded Rs 1,949 crore worth of holdings in the company.

The latest transaction is part of a broader trend of early Meesho investors monetising their investments after the company went public. Meesho listed on the stock exchanges in December 2025 following its IPO.

Prior to the transaction, Y Combinator was expected to sell up to a 1.05% stake in Meesho for around Rs 957.5 crore, with the proposed sale price set at Rs 197.5 per share. However, the executed transaction on the NSE was valued at Rs 969.63 crore.

Earlier this month, Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital sold around 10.48 crore Meesho shares in a block deal worth nearly Rs 1,949 crore. Both investors sold around 5.24 crore shares each at Rs 186 apiece.
Meesho, founded by Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Barnwal, operates an ecommerce marketplace focused on value-conscious consumers and sellers across India.

The latest exits also highlight the significant liquidity available to Meesho’s early investors after its public listing. While these transactions allow investors to book returns, continued selling by large shareholders can also keep the stock under pressure.

During the previous quarter (Q1 FY27), the company posted a 48% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 3,713 crore , while its net loss narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal.

title: Healthify merges with US-based Berry Street
description: Bengaluru-based healthtech startup Healthify has merged with US-based nutrition care company Berry Street in an all-stock deal.  Snippets.
body: Bengaluru-based healthtech startup Healthify has merged with US-based nutrition care company Berry Street in an all-stock deal.
The merger will combine Healthify’s AI-led health platform with Berry Street’s insurance-backed clinical care network in the US.

The combined company will operate under the Healthify brand in India and other international markets, while continuing with the Berry Street brand in the US. Healthify founder and CEO Tushar Vashisht and Berry Street founder and CEO Noah Kotlove will serve as co-CEOs.
Healthify’s AI platform, including its nutrition assistant Ria, will be integrated with Berry Street’s network of more than 2,000 clinicians operating across all 50 US states.
Berry Street provides virtual nutrition care through registered dietitians and handles insurance, billing and administrative services.
The merger is aimed at building an insurance-covered AI-powered metabolic health platform in the US, with a focus on conditions such as obesity and diabetes.
Healthify had been expanding in the US and identified insurance coverage as a key requirement for scaling its nutrition and health services there.

Founded in 2012, Healthify has raised around $150 million from investors including Khosla Ventures, Blume Ventures and Chiratae Ventures. The company said the combined business will continue expanding its AI capabilities and explore new international markets.

title: Morgan Stanley-backed Sterling Accuris reports Rs 231 Cr revenue in FY26; losses widen 38%
description: Sterling Accuris’ revenue growth slowed to 16% yoy during FY26, compared with in FY25. Meanwhile, the firm also saw its losses widened by 38% during the year.
body: Diagnostic and pathology services chain Sterling Accuris’ revenue growth slowed to 16% year-on-year during the fiscal year ending March 2026, compared with in FY25. Meanwhile, the Ahmedabad-based firm also saw its losses widened by 38% during the year.
Sterling Accuris’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 230.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 198.3 crore in FY25, its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) show.

Founded in 2014, Sterling Accuris Diagnostics provides a range of diagnostic and pathology testing services across India. The company offers more than 2,000 tests through a network of over 250 laboratories and collection centres spanning 50+ cities. It claims to have conducted more than 10 million tests to date. Testing services remain the company’s sole source of revenue.
The firm earned an additional Rs 2.9 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 233.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 201.8 crore in FY25.

For the diagnostics firm,  employee benefits remained its largest expense at Rs 59 crore, rising 14% year-on-year. Materials used for testing and diagnostics increased 16% to Rs 52.2 crore, while fees paid to doctors and pathologists stood at Rs 42.8 crore.

Depreciation and amortisation expenses stood at Rs 20.66 crore, while advertising and promotional expenses surged 84% to Rs 10.5 crore. Overall, the company’s total expenses increased 17.5% to Rs 259.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 220.9 crore in FY25.
With expenses growing faster than revenue, Sterling Accuris Diagnostics’ profitability weakened in FY26. The company’s net loss widened 38% to Rs 32 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23.2 crore in FY25.
However, the firm remained EBITDA positive at Rs 2.8 crore during FY26, with an EBITDA margin of 1.2%. Its ROCE stood at -7.9% during the year.

title: Endiya Partners leads $2.5 Mn seed round in bio physical AI startup WATER
description: The fresh funds will be used for technical validation as the company works to develop an intelligence layer for adaptive surfaces, with potential applications across aut
body: Bio physical AI company WATER has raised $2.5 million in a seed funding round led by early-stage venture capital firm Endiya Partners, with participation from Pullela Gopichand, Rohit Chennamaneni, Nandan Reddy, and other angel investors.

The fresh funds will be used for technical validation as the company works to develop an intelligence layer for adaptive surfaces, with potential applications across automotive, aviation, and other sectors, WATER said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Teja Vinukollu and Haneesh Mourya Desu, WATER develops adaptive surfaces, including the FLOW chair and CAMA bed, powered by VORTEX, its foundational model for understanding how the human body interacts with the physical environment.

The Hyderabad-based startup said its products use a combination of sensing, decision-making, and physical actuation to respond to the human body in real time. FLOW focuses on posture, movement, and load during seated interaction, while CAMA focuses on sleep, recovery, and respiration.
WATER said it plans to extend the underlying technology beyond chairs and beds to other physical environments, where surfaces and systems can adapt to individual needs.
The adaptive intelligent surfaces segment is still at an early stage in India, while the broader Physical AI and deeptech ecosystem is seeing growing investor interest.

Recently, Invisel raised Rs 4 crore in a funding round led by IAN Angel Fund, while Bengaluru-based Mowito secured $3 million in pre-seed funding to develop Physical AI foundation models for industrial robots. Flo Mobility also raised $2.5 million in a pre-Series A round to scale its Physical AI-powered autonomous solutions for construction. Yaanendriya secured Rs 15 crore to develop sensing, navigation, and autonomous-control technologies for robotics and aerospace.

title: Third Wave Coffee raises Rs 408 Cr led by WestBridge
description: Bengaluru-based coffee chain Third Wave Coffee has raised Rs 408 crore (43 million) in a funding round led by existing investor WestBridge Capital. News
body: Bengaluru-based coffee chain Third Wave Coffee has raised Rs 408 crore (43 million) in a funding round led by existing investor WestBridge Capital, with most of the capital coming through a primary issuance. The round also saw participation from existing investor Creaegis and other angel investors.
The new funding will support expansion in existing markets, increase presence in high-potential cities and accelerate its Third Rush Desserts segment, the company said in a press release.
According to a Mint report, the latest round values Third Wave Coffee at around Rs 2,000 crore ($210 million), compared to Rs 1,200 crore (150 million) during the previous funding round.
The company plans to enter nine new cities in the coming months, including Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Amritsar and Lucknow. It also plans to deepen its presence in tier II and tier III cities.

Third Wave Coffee, founded in 2017 by Sushant Goel, Ayush Bathwal and Anirudh Sharma, operates cafes and sells products such as coffee beans and cold brew bags. The company is present across Bengaluru, Delhi, Pune, Mumbai and Hyderabad, among other cities.
WestBridge has been an investor in Third Wave Coffee since its Series A round. It led the company’s $21 million Series B round in 2022, while Creaegis led its $35 million Series C round in 2023.
The latest round takes Third Wave Coffee’s total funding to more than $105 million.

Soon after the 2023 fundraise, Third Wave Coffee laid off around 100 employees. Around the same period, co-founder and then CEO Sushant Goel stepped down from the CEO role and moved to the company’s board. Rajat Luthra, former CEO of KFC India and Nepal, was appointed as his replacement.

title: D2C skincare brand Asaya raises Rs 88 Cr from RPSG Capital, OTP Ventures, others
description: ounded in 2021 by Neeraj Biyani, Eeti Sharma and Mandeep Singh Bhatia, Asaya offers skincare products targeting hyperpigmentation, dehydration and acne. Its portfolio
body: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) skincare brand Asaya has raised Rs 88 crore ($9.2 million) in a funding round from RPSG Capital, OTP Ventures, Huddle Ventures, Hyperscale Ventures and 72 Ventures at a post-money valuation of Rs 400 crore.
The round comprised primary and secondary capital, with some early angel investors selling their stakes.

The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised Rs 28 crore in a pre-Series A round led by RPSG Capital, with participation from existing investors OTP Ventures and Huddle Ventures, as well as angel investors Suyash Saraf and Anisha Agarwal Saraf, in September last year.
The proceeds will be used for research and development, product expansion, distribution and hiring, Asaya said in a press release.

Founded in 2021 by Neeraj Biyani, Eeti Sharma and Mandeep Singh Bhatia, Asaya offers skincare products targeting hyperpigmentation, dehydration and acne. Its portfolio includes dark spot correcting serums, even tone creams, body sprays, cleansers and sunscreens.
The brand follows a D2C model and sells through its own online channels, quick-commerce platforms and select offline retail outlets.
Asaya has developed a proprietary molecule called MelaMe, which it says is designed to address pigmentation and uneven skin tone, particularly for Indian skin types.
The Indian D2C skincare segment has seen growing investor interest, with brands focusing on science-backed, ingredient-led and premium skincare products.

title: Honasa Consumer calls off Fluence Pharma acquisition
description: Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer has called off its proposed acquisition of a 58% stake in nutraceuticals company Fluence Pharma due to the non-fulfilment of closing conditions under the share purchase agreement.
body: Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer has called off its proposed acquisition of a 58% stake in nutraceuticals company Fluence Pharma due to the non-fulfilment of closing conditions under the share purchase agreement.
The company informed the stock exchanges on August 25 that it had terminated the proposed transaction.

Honasa had announced the acquisition in June at an enterprise value of around Rs 135 crore. As part of the deal, the company was set to acquire 58% of Fluence Pharma, with the remaining 42% to be purchased in two tranches over the next five to seven years.

The company had also planned to incorporate a wholly owned subsidiary, Honasa Health, to build a business-to-consumer nutraceuticals business by combining Fluence Pharma’s clinical science and practitioner network with Honasa’s brand-building and digital distribution capabilities.

Founded in 2012 by Amit Bhusari and Dr Rajendra Singh Rajput, Fluence Pharma offers hair and skin health supplements through dermatologists under brands including Hair Fact, Skin Fact and Pro Fact. It has built a network of over 3,000 dermatologists in India and uses its patented Cyclical Nutrition Therapy (CNT) platform.
Fluence Pharma reported revenue of around Rs 40 crore in FY26, with an EBITDA margin of over 20%, according to Honasa’s presentation. Over 70% of its revenue came from hair-focused products.

Despite calling off the transaction, Honasa said it remains committed to its nutraceutical strategy and will continue evaluating organic and inorganic opportunities to build a consumer-focused business in the category.

title: Exclusive: DealShare in talks for acquisition as it stares at shutdown
description: The journey of DealShare, an e-commerce platform focused on groceries and household essentials, is nearing its end as the company’s board weighs potential acquisitions
body: The journey of DealShare, an e-commerce platform focused on groceries and household essentials, is nearing its end as the company’s board weighs potential acquisitions by online pharmacy platform TrueMeds and meat and seafood e-retailer Captain Fresh, sources told Entrackr.

Talks between DealShare, TrueMeds and Captain Fresh are underway but have not reached a final agreement. If neither transaction materialises, DealShare is likely to wind down its operations, said three sources requesting anonymity as the discussions are yet to be made public.

“DealShare is effectively at a point where it has two options: find a buyer or shut down. The discussions with TrueMeds are more advanced than those with Captain Fresh, but nothing has been finalised yet,” said one of the sources mentioned above.

The potential transaction is not being driven by DealShare’s existing business or scale, the source added. The company’s operations have contracted significantly after years of declining revenue, making the talks more of a financial transaction than an acquisition of a substantial operating business.

“DealShare does not have much of a business left to acquire. If the deal goes through, it would largely be a money-transfer transaction rather than TrueMeds buying a meaningful ecommerce business,” another source said.

TrueMeds and DealShare also have a common investor in WestBridge Capital, which could help facilitate discussions between the two companies. Captain Fresh, meanwhile, has been expanding through acquisitions and building businesses across fresh food and retail. The company also has common investor links with DealShare through Matrix Partners India, now known as Z47.

DealShare has been struggling for several years. The company laid off more than 100 employees in FY24 and shut down its B2B vertical as part of a restructuring exercise. Despite these measures, its revenue continued to decline.

Its gross revenue from operations fell 13.4% to Rs 432 crore in FY25 from Rs 499 crore in FY24 and Rs 1,963 crore in FY23. At the same time, the company narrowed its losses to Rs 87.65 crore in FY25 from Rs 167 crore in FY24. Its FY26 financials are yet to be filed.

title: IAN Angel Fund and Rainmatter co-lead Rs 12.5 Cr seed round in climate-tech startup CarbonStrong
description: Cement accounts for over 8% of global CO2 emissions, while existing solutions have limited capacity to replace it without compromising performance. CarbonStrong converts
body: Climate-tech startup CarbonStrong has raised Rs 12.5 crore in a seed funding round co-led by IAN Angel Fund and Rainmatter along with participation from Social Alpha, Full Circle Ventures, and its existing investors Momentum Capital and Spectrum Impact.
The startup had previously secured 3.6 crore in a pre-seed funding round from Momentum Capital, Spectrum Impact, and other angels in 2023.

The proceeds will be used to set up its first production facility, expand the team, develop and test products, and scale from customer trials to commercial production, CarbonStrong said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Harsh Jain and Vikramaditya Singh, CarbonStrong produces low-carbon binders by upcycling industrial waste to replace up to 50% of cement in concrete. The company claims its solution reduces costs and carbon emissions while maintaining concrete performance without requiring changes to existing plants or processes.

The Bengaluru-based startup said it has conducted several customer trials and paid pilots, with its materials used in demonstration projects across Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai. It is also targeting precast concrete and paver block manufacturers and aims to build an annual production capacity of up to 100,000 tonnes over the next two years.

Cement accounts for over 8% of global CO2 emissions, while existing solutions have limited capacity to replace it without compromising performance. CarbonStrong converts industrial waste from sectors such as coal and steel into cementitious materials that can replace a larger share of cement.

Other startups in the space include GreenJams, which develops low-carbon construction materials using crop residues and industrial by-products, and CarbonCraft, which uses construction and industrial waste for geopolymer-based wall claddings and other building products.

The sector has also attracted institutional backing. In February, the Technology Development Board (TDB) extended financial assistance to CarbonCraft to commercialise its ultra-low-carbon wall claddings. In June 2026, CarbonStrong and Satiq Concrete Manufacturer were among nine climate-tech startups selected for urban sustainability deployments, with grants of up to Rs 35 lakh.

title: Airbound raises $37 Mn from Greenoaks, DoorDash, Lachy Groom and others
description: Airbound has raised $37 million in a Series A round led by Greenoaks, with participation from DoorDash, Lachy Groom, Lightspeed and Humba Ventures.
body: Bengaluru-based aerospace startup Airbound has raised $37 million in a Series A round led by Greenoaks, with participation from DoorDash, Lachy Groom, Lightspeed and Humba Ventures.

The latest round takes Airbound’s total funding to nearly $50 million since its launch in 2023. The company plans to use the fresh capital to accelerate engineering, commercial-scale manufacturing and go-to-market initiatives.
Founded by Naman Pushp, Airbound is developing lightweight autonomous aircraft designed to transport people and goods at a lower cost than conventional aircraft.

The startup claims its aircraft can carry a single passenger or around 100 kg of cargo while significantly reducing the aircraft weight required to carry the payload. Its approach is aimed at lowering the economics of air-based transportation and making autonomous aerial delivery commercially viable.

“Better physics leads to better economics, which unlocks the potential to move people and goods for a fraction of a cent. That is what we’re building at Airbound,” said Naman Pushp, founder and CEO of Airbound.

Airbound has already completed more than 1,000 autonomous flights in partnership with Narayana Health, transporting diagnostic samples between healthcare facilities. The company said these deployments have reduced delivery times from hours to minutes.
Alongside the fundraise, Airbound has signed a commercial deployment agreement with the Andhra Pradesh government to build an autonomous drone delivery network connecting three cities.

Under the programme, the company plans to scale the network to 10,000 daily flights, catering to retail, ecommerce and healthcare deliveries. Airbound said the Andhra Pradesh deployment will serve as a model for expanding aerial delivery networks across India.

title: Utsav raises Rs 36 Cr in Series A led by Atomic Capital
description: Utsav has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.8 million) in a Series A round led by Atomic Capital, with existing investors India Quotient and Equanimity Investments also participating.
body: Kolkata-based s piritual and devotion platform Utsav has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.8 million) in a Series A round led by Atomic Capital, with existing investors India Quotient and Equanimity Investments also participating.

The latest round takes Utsav’s total capital raised to Rs 42 crore, including Rs 6.35 crore funding in January 2025. The company plans to use the fresh funds to expand its temple network, strengthen its technology and fulfilment capabilities, and scale its team.

Founded by Sourajit Basu, Ankita De and Prajata Samanta, Utsav works with temple priests, scholars and acharyas to offer devotional services through its platform. Its offerings include puja bookings, pujari consultations, e-prasad, consecrated prasad and personalised rituals.
The startup is also looking to expand its services for the Indian diaspora, enabling devotees outside India to participate in rituals at temples across the country.
Utsav co-founder and CEO Sourajit Basu said the company aims to make devotional experiences more accessible without compromising on their authenticity and sanctity.
The startup plans to expand its temple network and offerings while investing in personalisation, discovery, logistics and fulfilment over the next 12 to 24 months.
The company said its revenue has grown 8X since its previous funding round of Rs 6.35 crore in February 2025. It currently fulfils around 2.5 lakh orders per month.
Utsav competes with the likes of Vama.app, AppsForBharat, Astrotalk, Astroyogi, DevDham and others.

title: Edtech unicorn LEAD Group posts Rs 387 Cr revenue in FY26; losses narrow 20%
description: After flat revenue in FY25, edtech unicorn LEAD Group returned to double-digit growth in FY26, with operating revenue rising 10%. Its operating EBITDA jumped sevenfold, while losses narrowed 20% YoY.
body: After flat revenue in FY25, edtech unicorn LEAD Group returned to double-digit growth in FY26, with operating revenue rising 10%. The company also improved its operating EBITDA, which jumped sevenfold, while cutting its losses by 20% year-on-year during the fiscal year.

The company’s operating revenue grew to Rs 386.6 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 351.5 crore in FY25 , its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) show.

Founded in 2012 by Sumeet Mehta and Smita Deorah, LEAD provides integrated curriculum and technology solutions, including books, workbooks, smart classes, teacher training, ERPs, Math-Science kits, teaching aids and devices.
The company currently has a presence across more than 9,000 schools in over 400 towns and cities, reaching nearly 41 lakh students and supporting more than 65,000 teachers.

Revenue from products such as books, teaching aids and devices accounted for over 71% of the company’s operating income at Rs 275.4 crore, while platform services contributed the remaining Rs 76.5 crore.
LEAD’s total income stood at Rs 392 crore in FY26, including Rs 5.4 crore in non-operating income, compared with Rs 367.4 crore in the previous fiscal.

For the edtech firm, employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost head, although they declined 6% to Rs 131.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 139.7 crore a year earlier. The cost of materials also fell 5.4% to Rs 104.9 crore, while travel and conveyance expenses increased 7.1% to Rs 25.5 crore.
Advertising expenses rose 10% to Rs 18.9 crore during the year. Depreciation and amortisation, meanwhile, jumped 84.3% to Rs 47.9 crore from Rs 26 crore in FY25.

title: Sanlayan Technologies turns profitable as revenue jumps 5.6X to Rs 125 Cr in FY26
description: The company’s operating revenue grew 5.6X YoY to Rs 125 crore in FY26 from Rs 22 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated annual report reviewed by Entrackr.
body: Aerospace and defence startup Sanlayan Technologies saw a sharp jump in its revenue in FY26, while turning profitable during the year. The company’s operating revenue grew 5.6X year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 125 crore in FY26 from Rs 22 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated annual report reviewed by Entrackr .

Founded in 2023 by former Zetwerk employees Abhijit Kothawale, Rohan Gala, and Rahul Vamsidhar, Sanlayan develops electronic systems for the aerospace and defence sectors, including radar, electronic warfare and avionics. The company operates through a portfolio of technology businesses.

The sale of electronic systems was the company’s main source of revenue in FY26. Sanlayan also earned Rs 3 crore as other income, taking its total revenue to Rs 128 crore in FY26 from Rs 24 crore in FY25.

Its customer base includes HAL, BEL, DRDO, the Indian Armed Forces and private defence system integrators, while its product portfolio spans radar, electronic warfare, avionics, power electronics and mission-critical embedded systems.

According to the press release, Sanlayan Technologies ended FY26 with a Rs 286 crore order backlog and a confirmed opportunity pipeline of over Rs 2,000 crore, as several of its defence programmes moved from development to series production. The company recently secured a Rs 70+ crore production order for the Uttam AESA Radar programme, along with development orders for DRDO’s next-generation drone detection radar and electronic warfare systems for unmanned platforms.

On the cost side, material costs rose nearly 4X to Rs 43.24 crore in FY26 from Rs 10.9 crore in FY25, accounting for around 43% of the company’s total expenditure. Employee benefit expenses also increased 4.4X to Rs 39.51 crore during the year.
Overall, Sanlayan’s total expenditure stood at Rs 104 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 29 crore in FY25.

The sharp growth in revenue helped the company turn profitable, with a profit of Rs 25 crore in FY26 against a loss of Rs 4 crore in FY25. Its ROCE stood at 8.04%, while its EBITDA margin improved to 20.54%.

title: Wealthtech startup Nexedge Capital raises $20 Mn in maiden funding round
description: New Delhi-based wealth management firm Nexedge Capital has raised $20 million in its maiden funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment. News
body: New Delhi-based wealth management firm Nexedge Capital has raised $20 million in its maiden funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment and Elev8 Venture Partners.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen Nexedge’s technology platform, expand its senior banker network and increase its presence across India, including tier 2 and tier 3 cities. The company also plans to build a dedicated NRI proposition and launch an NBFC business.

Founded by Anirudha Taparia in February 2025, Nexedge provides wealth management and multi family office services covering investments, portfolio management, estate planning, business expansion and global mobility. The company aims to manage a family’s overall net worth rather than only its investible assets.
Nexedge caters to high net worth individuals (HNIs), ultra high net worth individuals (UHNIs), families and corporates.

The company claims to have surpassed $3 billion in assets under management (AUM) across around 1,300 clients within 18 months of starting operations. It has onboarded more than 95 senior bankers and expects another 50 to 60 bankers to join in 2026.

Taparia previously served as co-founder and Joint CEO of 360 ONE Wealth, where he helped build the wealth management business. He is joined at Nexedge by co-founders Sidhartha Shaw, Vijeeta Sharma and Pankaj Walia, along with 15 founding partners with experience across Citibank, Kotak Wealth, 360 ONE and Standard Chartered.

As per data compiled by Entrackr, Indian wealthtech startups raised more than $634 million across 51 funding deals involving 39 startups during 2024 and 2025. In the ongoing calendar year, Veriqus raised Rs 387 crore (around $40 million) in a funding round led by Norwest Venture Partners. AssetPlus raised $19.3 million, Wint Wealth secured $28 million, Neo Group bagged $36.3 million, Bachatt raised $12 million, while Prime Investor, Rovia, CREST and HyperNorm also attracted fresh capital.

title: Electric motorcycle maker Matter raises $25 Mn growth round
description: Ahmedabad-based electric motorcycle maker Matter has raised $25 million (around Rs 250 crore) in a growth equity round from existing investors Helena. News
body: Ahmedabad-based electric motorcycle maker Matter has raised $25 million (around Rs 250 crore) in a growth equity round from existing investors Helena, Capital 2B, Japan Airlines, TransLink Innovation Fund, and the Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community (SMSC).
In July 2024, Matter raised the first tranche of $35 million in its Series B round led by US-based venture capital firm Helena.
The latest round takes Matter’s total capital raised to more than Rs 1,000 crore ($105 million). The company makes the AERA electric motorcycle.

Matter will use the fresh capital mainly to expand its distribution network, increase manufacturing capacity, and develop new products. The company started manufacturing in October 2024 and has produced around 1,500 to 1,600 vehicles so far.

Matter currently has a production capacity of nearly 1,000 vehicles per month, up from 100 to 200 units during its pilot phase. It plans to increase monthly production to 5,000 vehicles by the end of the financial year.

The company also plans to expand its retail network from 30 dealerships across 21 cities to around 50 by the end of the year. It will focus on western and southern India and plans to add around 100 more touchpoints next year.
Matter is also developing four motorcycles based on the AERA platform. The new models will target the 150cc to 200cc segment and will be priced between Rs 1.6 lakh and Rs 2.2 lakh.
In the premium electric motorcycle segment, Matter competes with Bharat Forge-backed Tork Motors, TVS-backed Ultraviolette, and RattanIndia Enterprises-controlled Revolt.

title: Agentic AI startup Runable raises $21 Mn in Series A led by Susquehanna and Nexus
description: Runable claims to have grown from zero to $2 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) within three weeks of its launch and reached 1.5 million users. The platform offers
body: Agentic AI startup Runable has raised $21 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Susquehanna Venture Capital and Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors Together Fund and Array VC.

The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its growth capabilities, including adding more marketing channels, improving campaign measurement and enabling AI agents to identify and make campaign changes independently, Runable said in a press release.

Founded in 2025 by Umesh Kumar and Saksham Sarda, Runable helps small businesses build, manage and grow their operations. Its AI agents are designed to go beyond simple code generation and handle business operations and growth. The platform can generate websites, internal apps, mobile applications, slides and media assets using natural language.

The Bengaluru-based startup also plans to scale Runable Academy, a free module designed to help small business owners learn how to build and grow their businesses. It will also hire across engineering, machine learning, product, growth and support functions.

Runable claims to have grown from zero to $2 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) within three weeks of its launch and reached 1.5 million users. The platform offers business operations and growth tools, including paid advertising across ChatGPT Ads, Meta, Google, LinkedIn and TikTok, along with social media management, cold email, direct messaging and voice calls.

Runable also tracks competitors and brand sentiment and provides search engine optimisation (SEO), answer engine optimisation (AEO) and customer support tools. Most of its users are small business owners, with the typical user running a two-person business such as an agency, consultancy or cleaning company. Its users are spread across markets including the US, UK, Japan and Brazil.
AI agent platforms are emerging as a new layer in India’s startup ecosystem, helping small businesses build, manage and grow their operations through autonomous, AI-driven workflows.

Other recently funded players in the broader Indian agentic AI landscape include Kapture, which raised $10 million in pre-Series B funding to advance its enterprise-grade agentic AI platform, and Edysor.ai, which secured Rs 1.2 crore in a pre-seed round for its voice and chat AI agents that automate lead qualification and conversion.

title: Zerodha reports Rs 4,283 Cr profit in FY26; revenue remains flat
description: Zerodha posted a net profit of Rs 4,283 crore in FY26, up around 1.2% from Rs 4,231 crore in the previous fiscal, even as its revenue remained around the same level.
body: Zerodha posted a net profit of Rs 4,283 crore in FY26, up around 1.2% from Rs 4,231 crore in the previous fiscal, even as its revenue remained around the same level, co-founder and CEO Nithin Kamath said in the company's latest update.

Kamath said Zerodha's revenue has not grown in real terms as the bull market has paused and transaction-fee income has fallen. However, the loss of transaction-fee revenue is now being offset by income from its margin trading facility (MTF) business.
MTF, which Zerodha started in December 2024, now contributes around 10% of its revenue. Its MTF book has reached Rs 9,000 crore, while customers have borrowed around Rs 6,000 crore.

Kamath also expressed concern over the MTF business as customers are borrowing money to invest. Customer borrowing through MTF is around 25% of Zerodha’s net worth. He said this may not be a problem when markets are rising, but could increase risks if markets fall sharply.
As per the business update, Zerodha has also seen slower growth in new accounts as the stock market has remained weak.

According to Kamath, Zerodha is now India’s largest broker by total AUM. Around Rs 1 lakh crore of this AUM came from customers acquired from IL&FS. While Zerodha’s share of active NSE customers and total demat accounts has fallen, its share of retail AUM continues to grow.

The company also admitted that mutual funds are one area where it “may have slipped up a little”. Zerodha expects its upcoming mutual fund integration with Kite to improve product discovery and the customer experience.
The company also needs around Rs 11,000 crore of capital to operate at its current size. Kamath said this requirement itself acts as a moat for Zerodha.

title: Kitchen and lifestyle brand Cüraa raises Rs 40 Cr in Series A led by 3one4 Capital
description: Cüraa has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A round led by 3one4 Capital, with participation from existing investors Kae Capital, Lumikai, and Better Capital.
body: New Delhi-based kitchen and lifestyle brand Cüraa has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A round led by 3one4 Capital, with participation from existing investors Kae Capital, Lumikai, and Better Capital. ValueBridge Capital, a Merisis company, advised on the transaction.

The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its portfolio across pre-cook and cooking categories, strengthen its warehousing and supply chain infrastructure, and scale its presence across D2C, marketplaces, and quick commerce. It will also hire senior executives across key functions.
Founded in 2024 by chef and content creator Sanjyot Keer and entrepreneur Neeraj Kumawat, Cüraa makes kitchen appliances and tools designed for Indian cooking use cases.

Cüraa said it has served more than three lakh households since its launch in September 2024. Its monthly net revenue has grown 25 times since launch, while the company is currently adding around 25,000-30,000 customers every month.
The brand sells through its website, Amazon, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart, with Amazon accounting for the largest share of its sales.
Cüraa follows an India-first manufacturing model, with most value addition taking place domestically, while some components are sourced overseas to optimise costs and supply chain efficiency.
“The investment allows us to accelerate that vision and help more Indian households cook better,” said Keer, who also runs food content platform Your Food Lab.
Kumawat said the fresh capital will help the company strengthen product development, supply chain, customer experience, and distribution as it scales.

title: boAt profit jumps 38% to Rs 84 Cr in FY26
description: boAt reported a 38% YoY increase in PAT to Rs 84.5 Cr in the fiscal year ended March 2026, compared with Rs 61.1 Cr in FY25, while PBT grew 53% YoY to Rs 114.3 Cr.
body: Consumer electronics brand boAt reported a 38% year-on-year increase in profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 84.5 Cr in the fiscal year ended March 2026, compared with Rs 61.1 Cr in FY25, while profit before tax (PBT) grew 53% YoY to Rs 114.3 Cr, according to the company’s press release.

The company’s revenue from operations declined 4.6% YoY to Rs 2,931 Cr in FY26 from Rs 3,073 Cr in FY25. This marks the third consecutive year of decline for the consumer electronics brand, with revenue falling from a peak of Rs 3,373 Cr in FY23 to Rs 3,122 Cr in FY24 and Rs 3,073 Cr in FY25.

Despite flat revenue, the company improved its return on capital employed (ROCE) to 15.2% in FY26 from 11.5% in FY25, and ended the year with around Rs 397 Cr in cash reserves and zero bank debt, as per the release.

According to the company, its inventory has been reduced by around 10% to Rs 294 Cr from Rs 326 Cr, while trade receivables have remained broadly stable at around Rs 255 Cr.  The company also cut warranty expenses by around 30% to Rs 57.5 Cr in FY26 from Rs 82.6 Cr in FY25.

At the segment level, boAt’s wearables business turned profitable, from a loss of Rs 54 crore in FY25 to Rs 7 Cr profit in FY26. Its other segment, comprising categories such as charging solutions, cables and gaming, saw segment profit rise to Rs 46 Cr from Rs 14 Cr.

Audio continued to remain the company’s core business, while boAt expanded into newer categories. The company is also exploring international markets, with overseas revenue more than doubling to Rs 45 Cr in FY26 from around Rs 20 Cr in the previous fiscal year.
boAt plans to expand into projectors, personal grooming, charging solutions and other lifestyle tech products under its “boAt 2.0” strategy.

On boAt’s FY26 performance, Gaurav Nayyar, CEO, boAt, said the company strengthened its financial position, with PAT rising 38%, ROCE improving to 15.2%, and cash reserves reaching around Rs 397 Cr with zero bank debt. He added that wearables turned profitable, while newer categories are emerging as growth and profit drivers.

title: Exclusive: Even Healthcare set to raise Rs 208 Cr in Series B led by Khosla Ventures
description: Bengaluru-based healthcare startup Even Healthcare is set to corner a second round of funding this year. The company is set to raise Rs 208 crore or $22 million
body: Bengaluru-based healthcare startup Even Healthcare is set to corner a second round of funding this year. The company is set to raise Rs 208 crore or $22 million in a Series B funding round led by Khosla Ventures, participation from DLB Ventures,  Simon Fiduciaria and others.

In January 2026, it raised $20 million led by Lachy Groom and Alpha Wave. The board at Even passed a special resolution to issue 1,91,228 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at price of Rs 10,889.91 each share to raise Rs 208.24 crore, according to the company’s regulatory filings.

Khosla Ventures is investing Rs 145 crore in the round, followed by DLB Ventures with Rs 38.88 crore and Simon Fiduciaria with Rs 22.67 crore. ADBEEV LLP and Better Capital will also participate with Rs 1 crore each.
As per Entrackr’s estimate, the firm will be valued at around $300 million in the Series B round. The funds will be used to meet the company’s business funding requirements, as per filings.
A recent Mint report suggested that Even would raise around $50 million in the new round.

Founded in 2020, Even Healthcare operates a membership-based healthcare model offering primary care, diagnostics, and hospital services. Unlike traditional hospital chains, the company focuses on continuity of care and patient recovery, with its care teams managing patients across consultations, diagnostics, hospitalisation, and post-discharge recovery.

Even Healthcare is yet to file its FY26 financials with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). In FY25, the company’s revenue surged over 4X to Rs 25.43 crore from Rs 6.24 crore in FY24, while its losses increased 24.5% to Rs 90.15 crore from Rs 72.40 crore during the same period.

title: Voice AI startup Ringg raises $10 Mn led by Peak XV
description: Bengaluru-based AI startup Ringg AI has raised $10 million in an extended Series A funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Arkam Ventures and Capital 2b. News
body: Bengaluru-based AI startup Ringg AI has raised $10 million in an extended Series A funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Arkam Ventures and Capital 2b.
The firm had previously raised $5.5 million in Series A funding in January this year, taking the total size of the round to $15.5 million.

The new capital will be used to strengthen Ringg’s AI platform, expand its voice, WhatsApp and browser agents, deepen investments in its proprietary AI models and context graph, and accelerate enterprise go-to-market efforts across India and international markets.

Founded by Siddharth Tripathi, Utkarsh Shukla and Kali Charan Vemuru, Ringg builds AI voice agents for enterprises. The startup started as a text-to-speech company called DesiVocal but shifted its focus to enterprise voice AI after finding the cost of developing speech models difficult to sustain.

Ringg currently processes around 20 million call attempts every month and counts companies including Flipkart, Practo, Groww, Supernova, Goodscore and PolicyBazaar among its customers. Its voice agents are used for applications such as outbound calling, lead qualification and loan collection.

The company is now moving into more complex workflows, including healthcare appointment booking, e-commerce cart recovery, and fintech onboarding and KYC. Its voice agents are deployed across 1,200 Practo clinics, where they help patients book appointments and follow up after visits.

While voice calls account for more than 70% of Ringg’s business, the startup is expanding into chat, WhatsApp and browser-based support. It aims to build an AI agent platform that can complete business tasks rather than only handle enterprise phone calls.

title: TDV Partners leads $250K pre-seed round in dog care platform Scooby’s Club
description: Scooby’s Club, a network of premium dog care hubs in residential neighbourhoods, has raised $250K in a pre-seed funding round led by TDV Partners.
body: Scooby’s Club, a network of premium dog care hubs in residential neighbourhoods, has raised $250K in a pre-seed funding round led by TDV Partners.

The Bengaluru-based startup will use the funds to expand to two new properties across Bengaluru over the next 6-12 months, along with hiring and training canine coaches to deliver an expert-led experience.

Co-founded in 2025 by Animeha Singh and Ankit Gupta, Scooby’s Club is a pet care startup that provides professionally managed neighbourhood daycare and overnight boarding services for dogs. It focuses on high-standard short-term and overnight pet care for working professionals and modern pet parents.

According to the company, its model combines canine behavioural principles with purpose-built indoor spaces in residential neighbourhoods. Every dog undergoes temperament testing and is grouped by size, enabling safer, lower-stress socialisation.

The fully indoor and climate-controlled spaces use sound, scent and colour elements to provide mental enrichment. The company also offers allergen-sensitive care, personalised attention and 24x7 CCTV access, giving pet parents visibility into their dog’s experience.
Scooby’s Club aims to build a network of 100 properties across major Indian cities, using its neighbourhood-led model to bring care closer to where pet parents live.
India’s pet care market is estimated at Rs 6,000 crore and is growing at around 20% CAGR, while pet ownership is growing at around 5% year-on-year, according to market research cited by the company.

The organised pet care segment has also attracted investor interest. Vetic raised $40 million in June to expand its clinic network, while Supertails secured $30 million in February 2026 to scale veterinary clinics, at-home care and rapid delivery services. Premium D2C pet care brand Moe Puppy also raised Rs 2 crore in pre-seed funding in March.

title: Raise Financial’s Pluto Insurance appoints Abhishek Singh as CEO
description: Insurance broker Pluto Insurance has appointed Abhishek Singh as CEO, with around 23 years of experience in the insurance industry. Snippets
body: Insurance broker Pluto Insurance has appointed Abhishek Singh as CEO, with around 23 years of experience in the insurance industry. Singh joins from Upstox, where he worked on its insurance business, and previously spent over 11 years at OneInsure, according to his LinkedIn post .
Pluto is being built under Raise Financial Services, the parent of stockbroking platform Dhan, which acquired GreenLife Insurance Broking earlier this year and rebranded it as Pluto Insurance.
Singh has also held senior roles at Edelweiss Life Insurance and PNB MetLife, with experience across insurance distribution, broking, bancassurance and business partnerships.

At Pluto, Singh will focus on building a technology- and AI-led insurance platform aimed at simplifying insurance buying and servicing. The company plans to reduce complexity, limit unnecessary sales communication and improve customer support around claims, as per his LinkedIn post.
Ranjeet Walunj, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Pluto, will lead the product and technology side of the platform, the post added.

Last month, Raise Financial Services rebranded GreenLife Insurance Broking Pvt Ltd (GIBL), the insurance broker it acquired in May, as Pluto Insurance. Entrackr had exclusively reported the development. Raise also plans to invest Rs 100 crore in the new entity.

title: PRISM’s FY26 profit jumps 4X to Rs 994 Cr, revenue jumps 50%
description: OYO’s parent company PRISM reported a sharp improvement in profitability in FY26, with profit after tax (PAT) jumping over four-fold to Rs 994 crore from Rs 245 crore in FY25, while revenue grew nearly 50% year-on-year.
body: OYO’s parent company PRISM reported a sharp improvement in profitability in FY26, with profit after tax (PAT) jumping over four-fold to Rs 994 crore from Rs 245 crore in FY25, while revenue grew nearly 50% year-on-year.
The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 9,358 crore from Rs 6,353 crore in FY25, according to its annual report accessed by Entrackr.

PRISM’s EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 2,594 crore during the fiscal year. However, the bottom line included a deferred tax credit of Rs 678 crore. The company also incurred Rs 1,414 crore in interest expenses during FY26.

PRISM’s gross booking value (GBV) surged 88.5% YoY to Rs 30,683 crore, led by higher business volumes, premium and company-serviced hotels, and the full-year contribution from G6 Hospitality, PRISM’s American motel company.

G6 Hospitality contributed Rs 14,107 crore to the GBV in FY26, compared with Rs 3,529 crore in FY25. Excluding G6, hotel GBV grew 36.5% to Rs 10,939 crore, while the homes business grew 19.4% to Rs 5,447 crore.

North America emerged as a key growth driver after G6 made its first full-year contribution following its acquisition in December 2024. PRISM said it integrated G6’s technology stack into its unified platform within a year and deployed AI-led pricing and service tools across its properties.

Around 67% of room nights in FY26 came through non-commissionable channels, supported by the OYO app and other direct channels. The company launched its premium-focused CheckIn app in September 2025 to strengthen direct customer engagement and drive repeat demand.

PRISM continued to operate across more than 35 countries through a centralised technology and operating platform built largely from India. The company said the model helped it scale international operations while improving operating leverage.

title: Logistics startup OORJAA raises Series A funding led by Equentis Angel Fund
description: OORJAA’s proprietary AI stack, Datashastra, powers route optimisation, reconciliation and 24×7 control-tower visibility. The platform is also offered as a standalone Saa
body: OORJAA, a technology-led logistics platform, has raised Rs 9.7 crore ($1 million) in a Series A funding round led by Equentis Angel Fund, with participation from Inflection Point Ventures (IPV). This is the first close of a larger round, for which the company is in advanced discussions with a few VC funds.

The fresh funds will be used for technology and product development, scaling Datashastra, its proprietary AI/SaaS logistics stack, and strengthening its control-tower and automation capabilities, OORJAA said in a press release.

The Mumbai-based startup had earlier secured $1.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Micello Fund, with participation from Capital-A, Java Capital, Anicut Capital and Lead Angels in September 2023. In October 2023, it raised Rs 5.35 crore in a pre-Series A 2 round from Inflection Point Ventures (IPV), Vinners Platform, Soonicorn Ventures and HEM Angels.

Co-founded in 2019 by Sandeep Patil, Prashant Mohite, Yogesh Parab and Umesh Singh, OORJAA is a technology-led logistics company operating mid-mile and last-mile networks across more than 200 Indian cities.

OORJAA’s proprietary AI stack, Datashastra, powers route optimisation, reconciliation and 24×7 control-tower visibility. The platform is also offered as a standalone SaaS suite internationally. Its differentiator is an outcome-linked cost-per-unit model, under which clients pay for units moved rather than assets deployed.

According to market research, the global logistics market is valued at $10 trillion, while the logistics SaaS segment, which Datashastra focuses on, is growing at a high single-digit to double-digit CAGR.

OORJAA claims to move more than 3 million products and 50,000 last-mile orders daily across over 200 cities, while maintaining 95% SLA compliance for enterprise clients including Zepto, Blinkit, Amazon and Swiggy. The company is also deploying EVs across dense urban clusters to further lower unit costs and emissions.

Technology-led logistics platforms are becoming an increasingly important part of India’s startup ecosystem, using AI, SaaS, automation, real-time tracking, data analytics and digital marketplaces to address inefficiencies in the country’s fragmented freight and supply-chain sector.

title: Temple acquires London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous
description: Deepinder Goyal-led healthtech startup Temple has acquired London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous to strengthen its clinical and scientific capabilities ahead of its launch.
body: Deepinder Goyal-led healthtech startup Temple has acquired London-based Longevous, an evidence-based longevity medicine practice, as it looks to strengthen its clinical and scientific capabilities ahead of its launch.
The acquisition will bring Longevous founders Dr Robert Mohr and Dr Avi Roy, along with their team, into Temple full time, Goyal said in a post on X.

Dr Mohr will join Temple as Chief Medical Officer. A board-certified physician with nearly two decades of clinical experience, Mohr moved from emergency medicine to longevity medicine, with expertise spanning preventive and precision medicine.

Meanwhile, Roy will join Temple as Head of Science. An Oxford-trained biomedical scientist, Roy has worked at the intersection of longevity science and business. He is the co-founder of Founders Health and UDA and was previously a research fellow at the Centre for the Advancement of Sustainable Medical Innovation at the University of Oxford.
According to Goyal, the duo first met him at a dinner event in London a couple of months ago. Their conversation around longevity science eventually led them to try Temple themselves.

For the next two months, Mohr and Roy used Temple as their daily wearable and worked with its science team to evaluate its proprietary ‘Entropy’ metric and the data collected by the device. They also challenged some of the company’s assumptions and reviewed Temple’s first scientific manuscripts before submission.
“Given how personally invested they’d become, I asked if they’d consider building Temple with me full time,” Goyal said.
Longevous will continue to operate under Temple, with Mohr and Roy continuing to look after its existing clients.

title: VAHDAM India reports Rs 350 Cr revenue in FY26; profit jumps 6X
description: After turning profitable in FY25, tea brand VAHDAM India further strengthened its bottom line in FY26, with net profit zooming over sixfold to Rs 32 crore.
body: After turning profitable in FY25, direct-to-consumer (D2C) wellness brand VAHDAM India further strengthened its bottom line in FY26, with net profit zooming over sixfold to Rs 32 crore. The company continued to derive almost all of its revenue from international markets, with the US remaining its key market.

VAHDAM India's revenue from operations grew by 31% year-on-year to Rs 349.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 267.5 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statement filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

VAHDAM, a global wellness brand, offering herbal infusions & supplements, sources its products directly from farms across India and sells them in India and key global markets, including the US, Canada and Europe. Sales of these products remained the company’s primary revenue stream during the fiscal year.

International markets continued to account for the bulk of VAHDAM’s revenue, contributing nearly 96% of its total operating revenue at Rs 335.3 crore. The company also earned Rs 10.2 crore in non-operating income, taking its total revenue to Rs 359.8 crore in FY26.
For the D2C firm, advertising and promotional expenses emerged as its largest cost at Rs 95.9 crore which rose 65% year-on-year. Transportation was the second-largest expense at Rs 70 crore.

Cost of materials rose 32% year-on-year to Rs 63.4 crore, while employee expenses increased 30% to Rs 35 crore, including Rs 3.76 crore in ESOP expenses. The company also paid Rs 28.9 crore in commissions to selling agents. Other overheads, including rent, legal and professional fees and miscellaneous expenses, added Rs 41.4 crore, taking total costs to Rs 334.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 268.2 crore in FY25.
Coming to the bottom line, the company’s profit jumped over sixfold to Rs 32.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 5.2 crore in FY25, led by growth in its overseas revenue.

Its ROCE and EBITDA margin also improved to 9.5% and 5%, respectively, while EBITDA surged 2.7 times to Rs 17.5 crore during the period. On a unit level, the firm spent Rs 0.96 to earn a single rupee of operating revenue in FY26.

title: A91, Sixth Sense-backed Pushp Brand gets SEBI nod for IPO
description: Packaged spices maker Pushp Brand has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
body: Packaged spices maker Pushp Brand (India) has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to launch its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

According to the DRHP , the IPO will comprise an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 74.45 lakh equity shares by existing shareholders. The selling shareholders include promoters Surendra Kumar Surana and Mahendra Kumar Surana, along with investors A91 Emerging Fund I LLP and Sixth Sense India Opportunities III.

A91, which invested around Rs 125 crore in Pushp Brand in 2020, currently holds a 20.14% stake in the company. The investor will sell only a part of its holding through the OFS. Sixth Sense, which invested around Rs 101 crore in 2023, owns a 7.81% stake and will also partially exit through the IPO.
The company also appointed ICICI Securities, IIFL Capital Services and Systematix Corporate Services as the book running lead managers to the issue.

Founded in 1974 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, Pushp Brand has grown from a regional spices business into a packaged food company operating under the Pushp and Munimji brands. Its portfolio includes pure and blended spices, hing, whole spices and other products such as western seasonings, quick-fry mixes, soya products and tea.
As of March 2026, Pushp had 312 SKUs and a distribution network covering 24 states and union territories. Its products were sold through 1,016 distributors and more than 3.68 lakh retail touchpoints.

Financially, Pushp's revenue from operations rose 19% to Rs 482 crore in FY26 from Rs 405 crore in FY25 while its restated profit increased to Rs 58.95 crore from Rs 45.85 crore during the same period.
The company competes with established packaged spices brands such as Everest Food Products, Mahashian Di Hatti, Orkla India, Aachi Masala Foods, and Sakthi Masala, among others.

title: Biryani Bees raises $1 Mn from Vivek Oberoi Family Office
description: Biryani Bees, a biryani and Indian meals brand incubated by Wolfpack Labs, has raised $1 million from the Vivek Oberoi Family Office. Snippets
body: Biryani Bees, a biryani and Indian meals brand incubated by Wolfpack Labs, has raised $1 million from the Vivek Oberoi Family Office.
The firm plans to use the current funding to first reach 10 outlets and prove its model across multiple states. It then expects to raise a larger institutional round to support national expansion.
The funding will also be used to strengthen its central kitchen infrastructure, expand its operations team and build a repeatable expansion model.

Founded by Nitin Tiwari, Biryani Bees operates on a central-kitchen-led model aimed at maintaining consistent food quality and pricing as it expands. The company currently has an annual revenue run rate of around Rs 25 crore and says it is profitable.
The firm currently operates three outlets in Uttar Pradesh and plans to increase this to 10 outlets across Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and other tier 2 markets.
Biryani Bees claims to have built a strong presence on food delivery platforms such as Zomato and Swiggy, with the company claiming a high market share for biryani in the cities where it operates.

title: Space-tech startup InspeCity raises Rs 100 Cr in pre-Series A round
description: The company is developing Vehicle for Life-Extension and Deorbiting Activities (VEDA), an autonomous in-space servicing architecture designed to extend satellite lifeti
body: IIT-Bombay-incubated space-tech startup InspeCity has raised Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a pre-Series A funding round co-led by Speciale Invest and investor Ashish Kacholia, with participation from Antler Elevate, Antler India, Manish Gandhi, and Shastra VC.

The Mumbai-based startup had earlier secured $5.6 million (around Rs 46 crore) in its seed funding round led by Ashish Kacholia, with participation from Speciale Invest, Shastra VC, Antler India, DeVC, MGF-Kavachh, and Anicut Capital in May last year. It had also raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Speciale Invest and others.
The fresh capital will be deployed towards flight qualification and scaling commercial activities, InspeCity said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Arindrajit Chowdhury, InspeCity is a space-tech startup developing in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing (ISAM) technologies to extend satellite lifespans and address space debris.

The company is developing Vehicle for Life-Extension and Deorbiting Activities (VEDA), an autonomous in-space servicing architecture designed to extend satellite lifetimes and progressively enable more sophisticated orbital servicing. It has broken satellite life extension into the fundamental capabilities required for autonomous operations in space.

These include GITA (Green Impulse TrAnsmitter) for spacecraft propulsion and mobility; CHAKSU (Comprehensive AI-enabled satellite-tracking Sensor Unit) for sensing, navigation, and proximity operations; RAMA (Remotely Actuated Motorized Arm) for robotic manipulation; and SPARSH (Self-aligning Port for Autonomous Refueling and Satellite Housekeeping) for cooperative docking and in-orbit propellant transfer.
Together, these technologies form the building blocks for increasingly capable orbital platforms spanning RIG (Remote Inspection and Guidance), VEDA, and SAMA (Space-Based Maintenance Asset).

Over the next 12-18 months, the company plans to execute four in-orbit missions under the RIG-X, VEDA-X, and SAMA-X mission roadmap, progressively validating its propulsion, sensing, autonomous operations, robotics, docking, and refuelling capabilities in space.

title: InstaAstro raises $12 Mn in Series A round
description: InstaAstro has raised $12 million in a Series A funding round led by Singularity AMC and Artha Venture Fund, with participation from the company’s founders.
body: Gurugram-based digital spiritual wellness platform InstaAstro has raised $12 million in a Series A funding round led by Singularity AMC and Artha Venture Fund, with participation from the company’s founders.

The round comes more than two years after InstaAstro raised Rs 18.5 crore ($2.2 million) in a pre-Series A round led by Artha Venture Fund. In November 2021, the company had raised Rs 3.2 crore in a seed round.

The fresh capital will be used to expand InstaAstro’s presence in regional and international markets and invest in AI-led product development. The company plans to deploy AI for sentiment analysis and multilingual support to enhance user consultations.

Founded in 2021 by Nitin Verma, InstaAstro started as an astrology consultation app and has since expanded into a broader spiritual wellness platform offering astrology, tarot, numerology, vastu, Pooja Seva and spiritual commerce. It currently has 12 million registered users and more than 5,000 verified experts across 183 countries.

InstaAstro’s revenue more than doubled to Rs 111.26 crore in FY26 from Rs 52 crore in FY25. Its international business, driven largely by the Indian diaspora, contributes around 25% of its revenue. The company’s user base has also grown nearly 400% over the past two years.
The company claims its annualised revenue has now crossed Rs 200 crore.

InstaAstro will also expand its Pooja Seva and spiritual commerce businesses. Over the longer term, it aims to build an integrated platform covering consultation, rituals, discovery and commerce as part of users’ spiritual journeys.
The company competes with GaneshaSpeaks, AstroTalk, Click Astro, Astroyogi and Bodhi. Recently, AstroTalk turned unicorn following an ESOP buyback.

title: Logistics platform TrucksUp raises $8.2 Mn in growth round
description: The startup also runs safety initiatives and health check-up camps and provides access to its “Apna Ghar” network along major corridors for safe parking and rest. It has
body: Logistics platform TrucksUp has raised $8.2 million in a funding round at a post-money valuation of $42.3 million from institutional investors and family offices, along with co-founders Sarthak Shah Elwadhi and Aviraj Singh Chadha, who have increased their stake in the company.
The fresh funds will be used to scale its technology and fleet solutions, TrucksUp said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Sarthak Shah Elwadhi and Aviraj Singh Chadha, TrucksUp is an AI-driven digital freight marketplace and logistics platform that aims to bridge the demand-supply gap in India’s traditional trucking ecosystem. The platform connects truck owners, fleet operators, and drivers directly with businesses requiring freight movement.

According to the Gurugram-based startup, its AI-enabled algorithms match available trucks with verified loads in real time to reduce reverse-loading wait times. It also offers a single dashboard for real-time GPS tracking, digital document management, and shipment monitoring.
TrucksUp provides FASTag solutions, smart fuel programmes, insurance support, and vehicle financing options. It also facilitates the buying and selling of new and pre-owned commercial vehicles.

The startup also runs safety initiatives and health check-up camps and provides access to its “Apna Ghar” network along major corridors for safe parking and rest. It has partnered with the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and Indian Highways Management Company Ltd (IHMCL) to enable real-time driver feedback and road updates.
The platform has also formed a strategic alliance to provide vehicle financing and capital access to transporters and fleet owners in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

The funding comes amid growing investor interest in AI-led logistics and freight technology. FreightFox recently raised Rs 5 crore in a pre-Series A round led by HighLeaf to expand its platform and market reach, while Mojro Technologies secured $5.5 million in Series A funding to accelerate product innovation and global expansion.

title: Ribbit Capital sells Rs 2,217 Cr stake in Groww; shares fall 3%
description: Ribbit Capital has sold shares worth around Rs 2,217 crore in Groww’s parent company Billionbrains Garage Ventures through bulk deals on Wednesday, August 26.
body: US-based venture capital firm Ribbit Capital has sold shares worth around Rs 2,217 crore in Groww’s parent company Billionbrains Garage Ventures through bulk deals on Wednesday, August 26.

Ribbit Capital V LP sold 6.32 crore shares at an average price of Rs 196 apiece, while Ribbit Cayman GW Holdings V Ltd sold another 4.99 crore shares at around Rs 196.06 per share. Together, the two entities sold around 11.31 crore shares.

The total block and bulk transactions in Groww were larger, with around 12.74 crore shares worth nearly Rs 2,500 crore changing hands. The remaining transaction was not immediately linked to a named seller. Groww shares fell more than 3% after the deal.

This is also Ribbit’s second major sell-down in Groww this year. In May, Ribbit Capital V LP and Ribbit Cayman GW Holdings V Ltd sold shares worth more than Rs 2,500 crore , alongside Y Combinator and Peak XV Partners.

Y Combinator has also been steadily reducing its stake. In August, YC Holdings II sold around 7.47 crore shares for roughly Rs 1,435 crore . It had earlier sold shares worth around Rs 1,642 crore in May.

Despite these investor exits, Groww continues to report strong financial growth. Billionbrains Garage Ventures posted Rs 1,501 crore revenue in Q1 FY27, up 66% year-on-year, while its profit after tax rose 94% to Rs 735 crore .
At the end of today’s trading session, Groww’s share price stood at Rs 196.24, with a total market capitalisation of Rs 1,23,238 crore ($12.8 billion).

title: Hero MotoCorp to raise stake in Ather Energy to 32.8% with Rs 1,758 Cr investment
description: Hero MotoCorp has increased its stake in electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy to around 32.8% by acquiring shares from GIC, the sovereign wealth fund of Singapore.
body: Hero MotoCorp has increased its stake in electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy to around 32.8% by acquiring shares from GIC, the sovereign wealth fund of Singapore.
As per bulk deal data, Hero MotoCorp acquired 1.19 crore Ather shares from Government of Singapore (GIC) at Rs 1,480 apiece on August 28 on NSE, valuing the transaction at around Rs 1,758.24 crore.
The acquisition will take Hero MotoCorp’s holding in Ather from 29.88% to 32.8% on a fully diluted basis.

Ather is already an associate company of Hero MotoCorp and operates in the electric two-wheeler and charging infrastructure space. The company reported a turnover of Rs 3,671.76 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 2,255 crore in FY25 and Rs 1,753.8 crore in FY24.
Hero MotoCorp said the acquisition does not require any governmental or regulatory approvals.

Ather Energy recently raised Rs 1,200 crore through a preferential issue, with Hero MotoCorp investing nearly Rs 960 crore and the India-Japan Fund (IJF) investing Rs 200 crore. Co-founders Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain also invested Rs 20 crore each. Hero MotoCorp has been steadily increasing its investment in Ather, with the latest transaction marking another such investment.

According to Vahan data, Ather Energy retained the third position with 28,819 registrations and a 14.89% market share in July. The company recorded an 8.3% month-on-month decline, with 2,616 fewer registrations than in June.
Following the latest deal, Ather’s shares closed 8% higher at Rs 1,616.3, taking its market capitalization to Rs 63,762 crore, or around $6.7 billion.

title: Furlenco nears Rs 400 Cr revenue in FY26, profit jumps 19X
description: Since Sheela Foam picked up a 35% stake in Furlenco, the furniture rental company’s revenue from operations has grown 2.6X in two years, rising from Rs 140 crore in FY24
body: Since Sheela Foam picked up a 35% stake in Furlenco, the furniture rental company’s revenue from operations has grown 2.6X in two years, rising from Rs 140 crore in FY24 to Rs 370 crore in FY26. Furlenco has also remained profitable, posting a profit of around Rs 60 crore in FY26. The Bengaluru-based company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 370.43 crore in FY26 from Rs 228.74 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

Furlenco provides furniture and home decor for rent along with relocation services. Income from furniture rental services accounted for 92% of the operating revneue which increased 64% to Rs 341.07 crore. While the sale sale of products grew 38% to Rs 29.36 crore in the said period.
Furlenco also reported Rs 4.99 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 375.42 crore in FY26 from Rs 240.05 crore in FY25.

On the cost front, depreciation and finance costs rose sharply by 57.5% and 75.6%, respectively. Employee expenses increased 17.1% to Rs 36.18 crore, while material costs nearly 3X jumped to Rs 27.01 crore during the previous fiscal year ended March 2026.

The company did not provide a detailed breakup of other expenses, which rose 34.4% to Rs 181.04 crore in FY26 from Rs 134.7 crore in FY25. The financial statements classify these expenses as miscellaneous expenses.  Overall, Furlenco’s total expenses grew 45.1% to Rs 343.85 crore in FY26 from Rs 236.94 crore in FY25.

With revenue growth outpacing the rise in expenses, Furlenco’s profit surged 19.1X to Rs 59.52 crore in FY26 from Rs 3.11 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA also nearly doubled to Rs 129.5 crore, pushing the EBITDA margin to 35.01%. Meanwhile, ROCE improved to 13.17% from 5.37%.

On a unit basis, Furlenco spent Rs 0.93 to earn every rupee of operating revenue, improving from Rs 1.03 in FY25. Its cash and bank balances more than doubled to Rs 75 crore from Rs 32 crore, while total current assets increased 67.9% to Rs 178 crore in FY26. Furlenco competes with Rentomojo in the furniture and home appliance rental market.
