Rentomojo recently received SEBI’s observations for its proposed IPO , which comprises a Rs 150 crore fresh issue and an offer for sale of up to 28.4 million shares. The company reported Rs 265.96 crore in revenue and Rs 43.11 crore in profit in FY25.

title: Purple Style Labs raises Rs 306 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
description: Purple Style Labs, the parent company of Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, has raised Rs 306 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO).
body: Purple Style Labs, the parent company of Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, has raised Rs 306 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO).

The company allotted 53.21 lakh equity shares to 10 anchor investors at Rs 575 each, the upper end of its IPO price band. The investors include mutual funds, insurance companies and global investment firms.

ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund emerged as the largest investor, picking up around 15.3 lakh shares worth nearly Rs 88 crore. Jupiter India Fund followed with Rs 75 crore, while Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance acquired shares worth nearly Rs 68 crore.
The anchor book also saw participation from ITI Mutual Fund, Singularity Equity Fund I, Integrated Core Strategies, Morgan Stanley Asia and BofA Securities Europe.

The anchor round comes ahead of Purple Style Labs’ Rs 680 crore IPO, which will open for subscription on August 31 and close on September 2. The IPO has a price band of Rs 546-575 per share and comprises entirely of a fresh issue.
The company has also appointed Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services as the book-running lead managers to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

Purple Style Labs operates in the luxury fashion segment through Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, which sells designer wear and luxury fashion products. The company has been expanding its presence across India and international markets.

On the financial front, Purple Style Labs reported revenue from operations of Rs 558 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 490 crore in the previous fiscal. Its losses stood at Rs 285 crore during the fiscal year ended March 2026.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Aug 24 - Aug 29]
description: This week, 24 Indian startups raised $218.69 million across 2 growth-stage deals, 22 early-stage deals and 2 undisclosed rounds.
body: This week, 24 Indian startups raised $218.69 million across 2 growth-stage deals, 22 early-stage deals and 2 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 7 key hires, 2 mergers & acquisitions, 2 fund launches and 350 employees got laid off.
In contrast, 21 startups had collectively secured about $198.33 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]

Growth-stage startups raised $68 million across two deals this week. Bengaluru-based coffee chain Third Wave Coffee raised Rs 408 crore ($43 million) in a round led by existing investor WestBridge Capital. Ahmedabad-based electric motorcycle maker Matter secured $25 million (around Rs 250 crore) in growth equity from existing investors, including Helena, Capital 2B, Japan Airlines, TransLink Innovation Fund, and SMSC.
[Early-stage deals]

Early-stage startups raised $150.69 million across 22 deals this week. Bengaluru-based aerospace startup Airbound led the funding activity with a $37 million Series A round led by Greenoaks, with participation from DoorDash, Lachy Groom, Lightspeed and Humba Ventures. Agentic AI startup Runable raised $21 million in a Series A round co-led by Susquehanna Venture Capital and Nexus Venture Partners.

New Delhi-based wealth management firm Nexedge Capital raised $20 million in its maiden funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment and Elev8 Venture Partners. Gurugram-based digital spiritual wellness platform InstaAstro secured $12 million in a Series A round led by Singularity AMC and Artha Venture Fund, with participation from its founders.

Other startups that raised funding this week included spacetech startup InspeCity, voice AI startup Ringg, D2C skincare brand Asaya, logistics platform TrucksUp and EV motorcycle maker Omega Seiki Mobility, along with 13 other startups, including two undisclosed deals.

title: Aakash revenue stays flat at Rs 2,041 Cr in FY26; EBITDA plunges 65%
description: Aakash Educational Services (AESL) delivered strong academic results in FY26, but its operating revenue remained flat at Rs 2,041 Cr, while EBITDA plunged 65% during the year.
body: Aakash Educational Services (AESL) continued to deliver strong academic results in FY26, with its students securing nine ranks in the JEE Advanced 2026 Top 100 and 41 ranks in the NEET Top 100. However, this performance did not translate into meaningful financial growth as the test-prep company’s operating revenue remained largely flat, while its EBITDA plunged 65% during the last fiscal year.
Aakash’s revenue from operations stood at Rs 2,041 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 2,032 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) .

Aakash derives almost all of its operating revenue from its coaching business, which includes classroom programmes run through its own centres. The segment contributed Rs 1,956 crore in FY26, largely unchanged from Rs 1,951 crore in the previous fiscal and accounted for around 96% of the company’s operating revenue.

The remaining revenue came from its franchisee network, where partner-run centres operate under the Aakash brand. Revenue from this segment rose 3.7% to Rs 84 crore in FY26 from Rs 81 crore a year earlier.
The company’s total income grew 3.3% to Rs 2,154 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,085 crore in FY25, aided by a more than twofold increase in other income to Rs 113 crore.

Employee benefit expenses, Aakash’s largest cost head, declined 2.4% to Rs 1,300 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,332 crore in FY25. Depreciation expenses fell 4.5% to Rs 235 crore, while advertising costs dropped 7% to Rs 146 crore.

Meanwhile, other expenses rose 6.5% to Rs 626 crore. This included costs related to security and housekeeping, subvention, legal and professional services, among other expenses. Franchise service fees also surged 66% to Rs 91 crore during the fiscal. Overall, the company's total expenses increased marginally to Rs 2,398 crore from Rs 2,378 crore in FY25.

Despite the marginal increase in revenue, its operating profitability weakened sharply. EBITDA fell 65% to Rs 15.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 43.3 crore in FY25, dragging its EBITDA margin to 0.75% from 2.13% in the previous fiscal. Its ROCE stood at -46.1% in FY26.

title: Exclusive: Wedding services startup Meragi set to raise fresh funds at flat valuation
description: Bengaluru-based wedding services startup Meragi is set to raise Rs 28.68 crore in a fresh funding round from its existing investors Accel India, Peak XV Partners
body: Bengaluru-based wedding services startup Meragi is set to raise Rs 28.68 crore in a fresh funding round from its existing investors Accel India, Peak XV Partners, and new investor DG Daiwa Ventures. The round appears to be a bridge round, as the company has not raised any capital in the past two years. In July 2024, the company had raised $9.1 million in a funding round led by Accel, along with Peak XV Partners and Venture Highway.

The company’s board has passed a special resolution to issue 3,330 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) and 10 equity shares at a price of Rs 85,880.21 per share to raise the fresh capital.
Accel India will lead the round with Rs 14.34 crore, while DG Daiwa Ventures will invest Rs 9.56 crore and Peak XV Partners Rs 5.56 crore.
As per Entrackr ’s estimates, Meragi will be valued at around Rs 305 crore post-money, remaining flat compared with its previous funding round.

Founded in 2021 by Mukund Mohan Raj, Abhinav Chandran, and Lakshminarayan B, Meragi provides wedding-related services such as decoration, photography, videography, makeup, hairstyling, mehendi, catering, venues, entertainment, and invitations.

Following the allotment, Accel India will hold a 22.14% stake in Meragi, followed by Venture Highway and Surge Ventures with 15.92% and 15.85%, respectively. Peak XV Partners and DG Daiwa Ventures will hold 7.80% and 3.17% stakes, respectively. The company operates in a competitive wedding-services market alongside WedMeGood, ShaadiSaga, Weddingz.in, Shaadilogy, Wedding Cloud, Shaadi Baraati, and The Wedding Brigade.

title: Groww AMC closes State Street’s Rs 580 Cr strategic investment
description: Groww Asset Management has completed the strategic investment from State Street Investment Management, formally closing a deal first announced in January this year.
body: Groww Asset Management has completed the strategic investment from State Street Investment Management, formally closing a deal first announced in January this year.

The partnership gives State Street a 23% economic interest and 4.85% voting rights in Groww AMC, following the completion of all necessary regulatory approvals. The transaction involved an investment of up to Rs 580 crore through a mix of primary subscription and secondary purchase of shares.

The deal brings together Groww’s asset management business and State Street Investment Management, the asset management arm of US-based financial services giant State Street. State Street had about $5.4 trillion in assets under management as of September 2025.

For Groww, the partnership comes as its AMC business continues to scale. The company had Rs 4,119 crore in assets under management and 1.2 million unique investors as of December 2025, according to Groww’s shareholder letter.  Its AUM had nearly tripled year-on-year to around Rs 4,730 crore by May 2026.

Groww said the partnership will give its AMC access to State Street’s expertise in indexing, ETFs, systematic investing, macroeconomic research and portfolio construction. The collaboration is also expected to support product development, distribution and access to global markets.

The transaction had been awaiting regulatory clearances since the original announcement. The Competition Commission of India (CCI) approved State Street’s acquisition of a stake in Groww AMC in March 2026.

The deal also comes as fintech-led AMCs are gaining ground in India, with platforms such as Groww and Zerodha using their large retail investor bases to push mutual funds and passive investment products.

title: Info Edge Ventures leads Rs 20 Cr Series A round in YOGa Clean Air
description: The Gurugram-based company claims its systems currently serve more than 5,000 families and hundreds of institutions, including hospitals, schools, offices and gyms,
body: Indoor air-quality company YOGa Clean Air has raised Rs 20 crore in a Series A funding round led by Info Edge Ventures, with participation from Zomato/Eternal founder Deepinder Goyal and Three Words Capital.

The company said in a press release that it will use the fresh capital to deepen its presence in existing markets, expand into new Tier-1 and Tier-2 cities, and extend its systems to public transport and other outdoor environments.

Founded in 2019 by Sachin Panwar, Deepak Raina and Gaurav Nagar, YOGa Clean Air offers its patented Clean Air Bubble technology, which filters incoming air and maintains slightly higher air pressure inside a space to prevent polluted air from entering. The system also manages carbon dioxide levels to maintain indoor air quality.

The Gurugram-based company claims its systems currently serve more than 5,000 families and hundreds of institutions, including hospitals, schools, offices and gyms, across 11 Indian cities, including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Hyderabad. It holds two patents for its technology.

YOGa said its systems have reduced indoor air pollution to single-digit levels even when outdoor pollution crossed 900 µg/m³, while keeping CO₂ levels in check. The company also claims a 100% renewal rate for its annual maintenance contracts.

The indoor air-quality segment has seen startups move beyond conventional air purifiers into areas such as air-quality monitoring, HVAC-integrated filtration, pathogen control, plant-based purification and industrial emission control.

Pune-based NovorbisItus recently secured Rs 13.35 crore ($1.6 million) in seed funding led by Rainmatter for emission-control and air-purification systems. Airth, which develops filters that convert conventional air conditioners into air purifiers, has also raised funding as it expands its indoor air-quality offerings.

Other players in the segment include uBreathe Life, operated by Urban Air Labs, which has received Technology Development Board support for its plant-based indoor air-purification technology, and Biomoneta, which is developing medical-grade air-cleaning solutions.

title: Healthians turns profitable in FY26; revenue jumps 37%
description: Following a near-breakeven during FY25, Healthians turned profitable for the first time in the fiscal year ending March 2026, while continuing to scale its business.
body: Following a near-breakeven during FY25, diagnostics and wellness testing platform Healthians turned profitable for the first time in the fiscal year ending March 2026, while continuing to scale its business.
Healthians’ revenue from operations grew 35.7% year-on-year to Rs 357 crore in FY26 from Rs 263 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

The Gurugram-based company offers at-home diagnostic services across more than 250 cities and claims to have conducted over 10 crore tests to date. Diagnostics remained its biggest revenue driver, contributing 99% of the operating revenue, or Rs 353 crore, during the fiscal year. The remaining income came from supplementary and ancillary services.
Healthians also earned Rs 5 crore in interest income, taking its total revenue to Rs 362 crore in FY26 from Rs 270 crore in FY25.

On the cost front, employee benefits remained the company’s largest expense, accounting for 36.8% of its total expenditure. The expense rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 134 crore in FY26. The cost of materials stood at Rs 109 crore, while marketing expenses declined to Rs 44 crore.
Rent, legal, information technology and other overheads pushed Healthians’ total expenditure up 32.4% to Rs 364 crore in FY26 from Rs 275 crore in FY25.

With revenue growing faster than expenses, Healthians turned profitable and posted a net profit of Rs 5.4 crore in FY26, compared with a loss of Rs 4.77 crore in FY25. The company, however, continued to carry accumulated losses of Rs 976 crore.

On a unit economics basis, Healthians spent Rs 1.02 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its EBITDA margin improved to 2.20%, while ROCE stood at -4.86%. At the end of FY26, the company had current assets worth Rs 112.5 crore.

title: Exclusive: Good Flippin’ Burgers to raise fresh capital at Rs 480 Cr valuation
description: Quick-service burger chain Good Flippin’ Burgers is set to raise fresh funding after a gap of two and a half years, with Delhi-based S.R. Foundation investing Rs 55 crore
body: Quick-service burger chain Good Flippin’ Burgers is set to raise fresh funding after a gap of two and a half years, with Delhi-based S.R. Foundation investing Rs 55 crore at a 20% valuation premium.

The company’s board passed a special resolution to issue 58,668 Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares at an issue price of Rs 9,374.77 per share to raise fresh capital from S.R. Foundation, according to the company’s regulatory filings with the Registrar of companies.
Managed by corporate trustee Rajiv Kumar Gupta, S.R. Foundation operates as a back-end investment vehicle and public charitable trust linked to the DS Group promoter network.
In April 2024, the Mumbai-based company had raised Rs 30 crore (approximately $3.6 million) in an extended Series A round from existing investor Tanglin Venture Partners.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation will rise to around Rs 481 crore in the Series B from Rs 400 crore in the extended Series A round, where its valuation surged three-fold.
The seven-year-old firm plans to use the fresh capital for growth, expansion, and general corporate purposes, as per filings.
Good Flippin’ Burgers operates a chain of burger restaurants across India. Launched in Mumbai in 2019, the company has 67 outlets across Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai.

The QSR chain startup is yet to report its FY26 financials. Between FY23 and FY25, its revenue grew more than 3.4X to Rs 111 crore in FY25 from Rs 32.5 crore in FY23, while losses widened nearly 4.7X to Rs 18.32 crore from Rs 3.91 crore during the same period.

title: Oppex AI raises Rs 4.2 Cr in pre-seed round led by Info Edge Ventures
description: y creating an AI layer for production, the company seeks to ensure that faster software development does not come at the cost of reliability, customer experience, or t
body: Oppex AI, an AI-native platform for production operations, has raised Rs 4.2 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Info Edge Ventures.
The fresh funds will be utilised to accelerate product development, expand the team, and scale deployments with customers, Oppex AI said in a press release.

Launched in June last year by Prasun Kumar and Pranit Kumar, Oppex AI builds an AI-native platform for production operations, with the aim of transforming incident management from human-led to AI-led. Its agentic platform brings together context from observability, customer support, cloud infrastructure, internal runbooks, and other enterprise systems to understand production incidents and automate incident response.

Oppex AI addresses the growing production bottleneck by building an AI-powered system designed specifically for production operations. The startup aims to automate and streamline the detection, investigation, and resolution of production incidents, helping engineering teams spend less time firefighting and more time building products.

By creating an AI layer for production, the company seeks to ensure that faster software development does not come at the cost of reliability, customer experience, or trust. This would enable organisations to fully realise the benefits of AI-driven software development.

The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform is being adopted by enterprise customers across India, the UK, the EU, and the US. It plans to strengthen its agentic platform and expand its capabilities as it works towards making AI-led production operations a reality for enterprise technology teams.

As AI accelerates software development and increases deployment velocity, production environments are becoming more complex. This is creating demand for agentic systems that can unify signals from logs, metrics, infrastructure, applications, and internal knowledge bases to identify root causes and recommend or execute remediation.

title: Aeron Systems raises Rs 45 Cr in Pre-Series B round
description: Pune-based deeptech company Aeron Systems has raised Rs 45 crore ($4.7 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round, jointly led by Riverwalk Holdings. Snippets
body: Pune-based deeptech company Aeron Systems has raised Rs 45 crore ($4.7 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round, jointly led by Riverwalk Holdings and MGF-Kavachh (MountTech Growth Fund).

The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, accelerate research and development, develop new products and meet customer demand. Aeron will also use the funds to strengthen its presence in international markets.
Founded by Ashvani Shukla and Abhijeet Bokil, Aeron Systems develops navigation, weather sensing and monitoring technologies for aerospace, defence and industrial applications.
Its product portfolio includes inertial navigation systems, air data computers, weather sensing solutions, flight test instrumentation, avionics and positioning, navigation and timing technologies.

The company’s products are used across aircraft, helicopters, unmanned platforms, missiles, armoured vehicles and naval platforms. Aeron is also working on solutions for renewable energy applications, combining hardware and software for utility-scale solar projects.
Aeron plans to continue developing its product portfolio and expand its international customer base.

title: Exclusive: Qualcomm Ventures to lead $60 Mn round for Ultrahuman
description: Wearable tech startup is raising Rs 583 crore (around $60 million) in its Series C round led by Qualcomm Ventures and with the participation of Alpha Wave and others.
body: Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman is raising Rs 583 crore (around $60 million) in its Series C round led by Qualcomm Ventures and with the participation of Alpha Wave, Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings, Deepinder Goyal, Blume Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Steadview Capital, GGM Family Trust, Krypton Fund, and others.

The board at Ultrahuman has passed a special resolution to issue 3,623 Series C and 3832 Series C1 compulsorily convertible preference shares at an issue price of Rs 7,79,500 and Rs 7,85,300, respectively, to raise Rs 583 crore (approximately $60 million), according to its regulatory filings sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Qualcomm Ventures will lead the round with an investment of Rs 143 crore, followed by Alpha Wave, which will invest Rs 114 crore. Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings will put in Rs 95 crore, while Blume Ventures will invest Rs 90 crore.

Deepinder Goyal will invest Rs 47.4 crore, while Nexus Venture Partners and Krypton Fund will contribute Rs 18.9 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively. The remaining amount will be invested by GGM Family Trust, Steadview Capital, InCred Wealth, Joy Bhakat and other investors.
According to Entrackr’s estimates, the funding round values the company at around $363 million post-money, marking a 65% jump from its previous Series B valuation .
As per the filing, the company plans to use the fresh proceeds for growth, expansion, and other general corporate purposes.
A July ET report also said that Ultrahuman is in talks to raise $60 million.

It’s worth noting that Ultrahuman’s co-founders, Mohit Kumar and Vatsal Singhal, had earlier sold their first startup, Runnr, to Zomato in September 2017. Zomato later leveraged Runnr, which was merged with Mumbai-based TinyOwl, to strengthen its in-house delivery fleet.

title: Rainmatter leads Rs 30 Cr pre-Series A round in Minimac Systems
description: The company claims to have deployed more than 2,500 miniaturised fluid-treatment systems with a combined installed processing capacity of over 300,000 litres per minute.
body: Industrial deep-tech company Minimac Systems has raised Rs 30 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Rainmatter, the investment firm backed by Zerodha, with participation from other venture capital firms.

The proceeds will be used to advance R&D in miniaturised treatment infrastructure, fleet automation and fluid analytics. The company will also scale its Recycling on Wheels model through regional hubs across major industrial clusters and strengthen its commercial, digital and operational capabilities, Minimac Systems said in a press release.

Founded in 2012 by Anshuman Agrawal, Minimac Systems focuses on lubricant lifecycle management, reliability and circularity. The company develops miniaturised fluid-treatment systems, operates Recycling on Wheels, a mobile on-site lubricant restoration model, and is developing Lubricants as a Service.

India is the world's third-largest lubricant market, consuming more than 5 million tonnes of lubricants and greases annually, while its annual base-oil import bill has crossed $2.7 billion, according to market research cited by the company.

Minimac's platform covers three stages of lubricant management. NanoCircularity monitors lubricant inside machines through condition monitoring, contamination control and fluid-health analytics. MicroCircularity restores recoverable lubricant at industrial plants by removing contaminants, moisture and degradation by-products. MacroCircularity sends lubricant that cannot be restored to registered re-refiners for conversion into re-refined base oil (RRBO).

Its Recycling on Wheels model uses mobile, miniaturised treatment systems with processing capacities ranging from around 10 to 4,000 litres per minute. These systems assess and treat lubricant at industrial sites before returning it to service. The company aims to abate 860 gigagrams of CO₂e emissions by 2034.

Minimac plans to manage the lubricant lifecycle within industrial plants, covering supply, monitoring, restoration, compliance and end-of-life recovery. Its proposed contracts will be based on uptime, fluid health and agreed outcomes rather than product sales alone.

The company claims to have deployed more than 2,500 miniaturised fluid-treatment systems with a combined installed processing capacity of over 300,000 litres per minute. It has worked across more than 2,200 industrial assets and kept over 14 million litres of lubricant in productive use across India and international markets. Its customers include NTPC, Adani Power, JSW Steel and Tata Steel.

title: Deep-tech aerospace startup Alteon raises $2.5 Mn led by Lachy Groom
description: ts autonomous dynamic-soaring vehicles extract energy from wind gradients, similar to albatrosses, to remain airborne for extended periods. A key engineering challenge is
body: Deep-tech aerospace startup Alteon has raised $2.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Lachy Groom, with participation from Together Fund.

The round follows a recent flight test in which Alteon’s aircraft demonstrated autonomous flight within a metre of the ocean’s surface. The test helped derisk a key component of the manoeuvre on which the company’s autonomous, high-endurance flight capability relies.

The fresh capital will be used for offshore tests aimed at achieving autonomous dynamic soaring without propulsion. Alteon will also scale its R&D efforts to deploy a fleet of such aircraft over the ocean, the company said in a press release.

Founded in 2025 by Samay Sanghvi, Alteon develops autonomous aircraft designed to fly for months by using dynamic soaring to harvest energy from the atmosphere. The Bengaluru-based startup is building a new class of ultra-high-endurance aircraft that can remain airborne by drawing energy from the environment.

Its autonomous dynamic-soaring vehicles extract energy from wind gradients, similar to albatrosses, to remain airborne for extended periods. A key engineering challenge is enabling the aircraft to perform this manoeuvre autonomously close to the surface of a moving ocean.
Alteon plans to progressively test its ability to harvest energy from wind until the aircraft can sustain flight without propulsion, similar to an albatross.

The company’s aircraft fleets can carry payloads for applications such as mapping weather and ocean conditions, tracking ships and fishing activity, monitoring critical infrastructure, and supporting defence, search and rescue, scientific and industrial operations.
Alteon said its fleets could provide a continuous, real-time layer of capabilities over the ocean at a fraction of the cost of ships, satellites and large offshore installations.

title: Niyo to acquire Capital India Finance’s RemitX forex business
description: Bengaluru-based travel-fintech platform Niyo has signed an agreement to acquire the forex and cross-border business of Capital India Finance. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based travel-fintech platform Niyo has signed an agreement to acquire the forex and cross-border business of Capital India Finance, which operates under the RemitX brand.
The deal will bring RemitX’s branch network, distribution partners, employees and brand under Niyo.

RemitX operates 32 branches across 16 states and more than 30 cities, including Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets. The acquisition will take Niyo’s physical presence to more than 40 locations across India. It will also add over 2,500 distribution partners across travel, overseas education and corporate segments.
More than 200 RemitX employees, including its leadership team, are expected to join Niyo’s wholly owned subsidiary Kanji Forex.
The combined business will offer foreign currency, forex cards and outward remittance services through both physical branches and Niyo’s digital platform.

Niyo entered the regulated forex business in 2024 through its acquisition of Kanji Forex, which holds an Authorised Dealer Category-II licence. In August 2026, the Reserve Bank of India granted Kanji Forex a perpetual AD-II licence with an expanded scope covering additional remittance services.

The acquisition will help Niyo expand its forex distribution network beyond major cities and increase its presence in the cross-border payments market. The company had earlier planned to build a network of 50 branches over the next two to three years.

title: Indian startup funding nears $1 Bn in August after July slowdown
description: Indian startups raised approximately $954 million across 88 deals in August. The total included 13 growth and late-stage deals worth $555 million and 75 early-stage deals worth $400 million.
body: August saw a couple of $100 million-plus deals, including River Mobility and Navi, pushing India’s startup funding closer to the $1 billion mark. Notably, early-stage deals accounted for around 42% of the month’s funding, led by rounds in Airbound, Centricity, and InRisk Labs. Despite mixed market sentiment around startup IPOs, Shiprocket, Milky Mist, and Leap made strong market debuts at a premium. The month also saw a couple of layoffs, while one startup shut down operations.
[Funding overview]

According to data compiled by Entrackr , Indian startups raised approximately $954 million across 88 deals in August. The total included 13 growth and late-stage deals worth $555 million and 75 early-stage deals worth $400 million. Of the 88 deals, eight were disclosed without funding amounts during the month.
[M-o-M and Y-o-Y trend]

Month-on-month, startup funding jumped 44.3% to $955 million in August from $662 million in July , making it the third-highest monthly total of 2026. Year-on-year, funding remained largely stable at $955 million in August 2026 versus $961 million in August 2025, while the number of deals declined from 100 to 88.
[Top 10 growth/late stage deals]

Growth and late-stage funding in August was led by EV startup River Mobility, which raised $120 million in a Series C round. Navi and Yulu followed with $100 million and $93 million, respectively, while AI startup Sarvam AI secured $74 million. Other notable deals included Third Wave Coffee, Leap India, Matter, BlissClub, Matel, and BGauss, with investments spread across mobility, fintech, AI, F&B, supply chain, EV, e-commerce, and manufacturing.
[Top 10 early stage deals]

title: Battery-swapping startup Yuma Energy raises $35 Mn from Magna International
description: The company plans to further expand its infrastructure and technology platform to serve riders, fleet operators and OEM partners and support the wider adoption of elec
body: Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) provider Yuma Energy has raised $35 million in a Series A funding round led by Magna International Inc.
The Bengaluru-based startup has also acquired battery technology company Grinntech to strengthen its battery technology and manufacturing capabilities.

The fresh funds will be used to expand Yuma Energy’s battery-swapping infrastructure across India and broaden its customer base across EV users, fleet operators and OEM partners, the company said in a press release.

Founded in 2023, Yuma Energy operates a battery-swapping network for electric mobility. The company claims to have delivered more than 60 million battery swaps through a network of over 100,000 batteries, 2,500+ charging units and more than 400 touch points across 18 cities.
Yuma Energy powers Yulu’s electric fleet and also provides open-access battery-swapping services to third-party original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and last-mile delivery operators.
The company plans to further expand its infrastructure and technology platform to serve riders, fleet operators and OEM partners and support the wider adoption of electric mobility.

BaaS providers separate the cost of the battery from the vehicle, allowing users to access charged batteries through subscription or pay-per-use models. The model can lower the upfront cost of EVs and reduce downtime through battery swapping.

Other startups such as Battery Smart, Sun Mobility and Gogoro are also building battery-swapping and energy infrastructure networks in India. Battery Smart raised around Rs 124 crore ($13 million) in debt from responsAbility Investments AG in July to expand its swapping network.

title: InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy officially announce merger
description: Gurugram-based insurtech startups InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy have officially announced their merger to create a unified insurance distribution. News
body: Gurugram-based insurtech startups InsuranceDekho and RenewBuy have officially announced their merger to create a unified insurance distribution platform with a pan-India presence.

The combined entity will operate under the InsuranceDekho brand, with InsuranceDekho founder and CEO Ankit Agrawal leading the business. The merger brings together InsuranceDekho’s presence across northern and western India with RenewBuy’s network in southern markets.

The platform will offer motor, health, life and commercial insurance products from multiple insurers. It plans to integrate the technology platforms of both companies and deploy AI across partner onboarding, product recommendations and insurance advisory. The company will also provide digital tools for policy issuance and customer service.

The merged entity generated more than Rs 6,600 crore in insurance premiums through its POSP network in FY26. It has over 6 lakh digital partners and reaches 98.57% of India’s pin codes. Together, the companies have facilitated more than 2 crore insurance policies since inception.

InsuranceDekho is also preparing to file its DRHP by the end of September, with plans to launch an IPO by March 2027. The company is targeting a Rs 2,500-3,000 crore issue at an estimated valuation of around Rs 9,500 crore.

The founders of both companies will continue with the merged entity, while teams across technology, distribution, product and operations will be integrated. The company said it will work with IRDAI and other stakeholders to expand insurance access across Tier-2, Tier-3 and smaller markets.
The merger talks began in October 2024. InsuranceDekho received a composite insurance broking licence from the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) in July 2024.

InsuranceDekho last raised $70 millio n in a round co-led by Beams Fintech Fund and Japan’s Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) in March 2025. Meanwhile, RenewBuy raised $40 million from Japanese insurance major Dai-ichi Life Holdings in July 2023.

title: Spacetech startup Kepler Aerospace raises $8 Mn in seed round led by Blue Ashva Capital
description: The Bengaluru-based startup said its technology is designed around reliability, automation, security and scalability, enabling satellite operators and mission
body: Space infrastructure and mission operations company Kepler Aerospace has raised $8 million in a seed funding round led by Blue Ashva Capital, with participation from Finvolve India Accelerator and other investors.

The proceeds will be used to develop and deploy next-generation space-based persistent Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities, while scaling its mission operations and avionics-as-a-service businesses, Kepler Aerospace said in a press release.

Founded in July 2018 by Navneet Singh and Kiran Sharma, Kepler Aerospace builds scalable space and ground systems for strategic, defence and commercial missions. Its capabilities span satellite avionics and subsystems, ground infrastructure, mission operations and space-based intelligence.

The Bengaluru-based startup said its technology is designed around reliability, automation, security and scalability, enabling satellite operators and mission stakeholders to deploy and manage increasingly complex space missions. The company caters to strategic, defence and commercial applications.

Kepler Aerospace aims to address the growing demand for persistent, low-latency intelligence from space. It seeks to reduce intelligence latency from months to minutes through persistent ISR systems and integrated mission infrastructure.

The company claims to have secured two IDEX prime contracts to provide swarming ISR constellations to India’s defence space ecosystem, supported by around $4 million in grants under the IDEX programme.
Through a network of more than 70 ground stations, Kepler provides satellite communication, tracking, telemetry, command and mission operations capabilities for a growing range of space missions.
The segment is gaining momentum as India’s private space ecosystem matures, with around 440 space-tech startups registered in the country as of August 2026.

title: Zenergize raises $4 Mn in pre-Series A round led by Giraffe Studios
description: Gurugram-based deeptech company Zenergize Technologies has raised $4 million in a Pre-Series A round led by Giraffe Studios, with participation. Snippets
body: Gurugram-based deeptech company Zenergize Technologies has raised $4 million in a Pre-Series A round led by Giraffe Studios, with participation from industrial entrepreneurs and existing investors.
The round includes both equity and venture debt.

The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, strengthen engineering and R&D, build its sales and service network, and support product development. Zenergize is also developing hybrid inverters and battery energy storage systems (BESS).
Founded by Navneet Daga and Veer Karan Goyal, Zenergize develops Silicon Carbide (SiC)-based power electronics for electric mobility and renewable energy.
Its products include solar inverters and AC and DC EV chargers, with chargers supporting capacities of up to 240 kW.

The company claims to have reached an annual revenue run rate of Rs 30 crore and has an order book exceeding Rs 150 crore within a year of commercialisation. Its EV chargers have received automotive certifications, while its solar inverters have received BIS certification.

The investor group includes Nikhil Sawhney, Varun Agarwal, Shyam Bagri, Raoul Bajaj, Sunil Kalra, Ajith Pai, Sandeep Barasia, Nitin Jain and Hemant Daga, among others. Zenergize aims to increase its annual revenue run rate to over Rs 100 crore within the next nine months.

title: TVS retains EV two-wheeler lead in August as market declines 11%
description: India’s electric two-wheeler industry recorded a 11% month-on-month decline in August to 1.82 lakh units from 2.05 lakh units in July, with most major players witnessing a steep drop. TVS Motor retained the top spot despite the broader market slowdown.
body: India’s electric two-wheeler industry recorded a 11% month-on-month decline in August to 1.82 lakh units from 2.05 lakh units in July, with most major players witnessing a steep drop. TVS Motor retained the top spot despite the broader market slowdown.

According to the latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the EV two-wheeler market with 48,873 registrations in August and a 27.04% market share. The company recorded a 12.45% month-on-month decline, with 6,950 fewer registrations than in July.
Bajaj Auto retained the second spot with 41,019 registrations and a 22.42% market share in August. Its registrations fell 10.56% month on month from 45,862 units in July.
Ather Energy ranked third with 28,708 registrations and a 15.69% market share. The company reported a 6.29% month-on-month decline, with registrations falling by 1,928 units from July.

Hero MotoCorp stood fourth with 18,978 registrations and a 10.37% market share. Its registrations declined 17.45% month on month, while Ola Electric remained fifth with 13,849 registrations and a 7.57% market share.

Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 8,612 registrations and a 4.71% market share. Its registrations dropped 15% month on month. River Mobility and BGauss also saw registrations decline 14.86% and 12.86%, respectively.
Among the smaller players, Motovolt recorded the strongest month-on-month growth, with registrations more than doubled to 1,365 units. Simple Energy remained stable at 1,635 units in August.

title: Alpha Wave sells almost entire Pine Labs stake in Rs 550 Cr block deal
description: Global investment firm Alpha Wave has exited almost its entire stake in fintech company Pine Labs through a Rs 550 crore block deal on Wednesday.
body: Global investment firm Alpha Wave has exited almost its entire stake in fintech company Pine Labs through a Rs 550 crore block deal on Wednesday.
According to exchange data, Alpha Wave sold 3.54 crore shares, representing a 3.11% stake, at Rs 155.10 apiece in a block deal worth around Rs 550 crore.
The shares were picked up by a group of institutional investors, led by ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, which acquired 1.03 crore shares worth around Rs 160 crore.

Other buyers included Societe Generale, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Goldman Sachs Investments Mauritius, Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund, Integrated Core Strategies, JM Financial Mutual Fund, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore and Norges Bank.
Following the transaction, Alpha Wave will be left with only 4.85 lakh shares in Pine Labs, a fraction of its earlier holding.

The exit comes as Alpha Wave has been actively monetising its positions in Indian technology companies. In June, the investor exited its entire 1.93% stake in Delhivery through open-market transactions for around Rs 665 crore. It has also sold stake in Lenskart, including a 2.46% stake sale in May and further shares worth Rs 1,857 crore in August. Alpha Wave also exited Aye Finance through a Rs 322 crore block deal.
Financially, Pine Labs reported a 20% year-on-year growth in operating scale to Rs 737 crore in Q1 FY26, while its profit jumped fourfold to Rs 20 crore during the quarter.
At the end of Wednesday’s trading session, Pine Labs’ shares closed at Rs 162.3, giving the company total market capitalization of Rs 18,785 crore or nearly $2 billion.

title: Adobe picks up AI marketing startup Rilo in second India acquisition
description: As part of the deal, Adobe is expected to integrate some of Rilo’s intellectual property and onboard its six member team. Rilo’s existing investors are also expected to
body: Adobe has picked up India based marketing intelligence startup Rilo in a deal involving the licensing of its technology and acquisition of its team. This is Adobe’s second acquisition from India.
The terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

Co founded in 2025 by Georgi Boby and Dhruv Jaglan, Rilo built AI powered tools for go to market teams to automate marketing and sales workflows. The startup had raised $1 million from Peak XV Partners, DeVC and Day Zero Ventures at a valuation of $10 million.
As part of the deal, Adobe is expected to integrate some of Rilo’s intellectual property and onboard its six member team. Rilo’s existing investors are also expected to receive an exit.
Following the acquisition, Rilo will shut down its platform and its products will no longer be available to existing customers.

Rilo’s platform helped teams create customised workflows for competitor intelligence, content repurposing and distribution, and sales call analysis. It also allowed users to build custom AI workflows.
The acquisition comes as companies increasingly use AI to automate marketing and sales tasks. Rilo’s technology could complement Adobe’s existing marketing and customer experience products.

On their acquisition by Adobe, on LinkedIn Georgi Boby, co-founder of Rilo, mentioned that their mission was to expand the power of AI  beyond just engineers. And I'm incredibly proud of the team, what we've built and the pace that we've built in. And now excited to share that we're joining Adobe to continue our mission at a whole new scale.

title: AI content creator platform Creedom raises seed round
description: Creedom said it has reached more than 1.5 lakh creators through its earlier learning platform before rebuilding its offering around personalised content insights. The s
body: Creedom, an AI growth coach for content creators, has raised Rs 4.1 crore in a seed funding round at a valuation of Rs 42 crore. The round was led by Leigh Hopkins, Raghunandan G, Ravi Iyer, and Kartheeswaran KK, cofounder and CEO of Ninjacart.
The round also saw participation from Raghu Nathan Sethuraman, Senthil Kumar T P and Govindaswamy Megavarnan through Startup Singam.
The fresh funds will be used for product development for Indian creators, expansion into the US and further development of its AI capabilities, Creedom said in a press release.

Founded by Naveen Murugan, Naveen Sowriraj and Aswin Dhananjai, Creedom connects to creators’ Instagram and YouTube accounts and analyses their content and performance data. Its platform identifies trends, recommends what creators should post next and provides insights into why specific content performed well or poorly.
The company delivers these insights through Cree, its AI companion, which allows creators to interact with their performance data through conversations instead of navigating complex dashboards.

Creedom said it has reached more than 1.5 lakh creators through its earlier learning platform before rebuilding its offering around personalised content insights. The startup currently works with creators across India and the US.

In December 2025, Creedom became an Official Meta Business Partner and a YouTube Official Partner. The partnerships allow it to access verified account-level performance data through approved interfaces.

The creator economy has continued to attract funding in India. Influish raised a pre-seed round at a Rs 25 crore valuation in June, while TrueFan AI raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3Partners.

title: Investors cash out over $2.77 Bn from Indian tech stocks in August
description: Indian new-age companies saw substantial secondary market activity in August, with 17 block and bulk deals worth Rs 26,337 crore or $2.77 billion across 12 companies.
body: Indian new-age companies saw substantial secondary market activity in August, with 17 block and bulk deals worth Rs 26,337 crore or $2.77 billion across 12 companies.
The deals were largely led by early-stage investors and promoters offloading their holdings, while mutual funds, insurers and global institutional investors emerged as key buyers.

Lenskart accounted for the largest share at Rs 7,445 crore across three deals. In the wearable firm, SoftBank sold shares worth Rs 2,888 crore , while Alpha Wave offloaded Rs 1,857 crore. In another Rs 2,700 crore block deal, BNP Paribas Financial Markets and Societe Generale sold shares, with most of the stake picked up by BlackRock. The transactions saw participation from institutional investors including Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, ICICI Prudential and SBI Mutual Fund. Overall, institutional investors have offloaded around Rs 14,200 crore, or $1.5 billion, in Lenskart shares over the last few months.”

Paytm followed with two transactions worth nearly Rs 4,986 crore. SAIF Partners and Elevation Capital sold a combined 2.33% stake in One97 Communications for Rs 2,037 crore. Vijay Shekhar Sharma-backed Resilient Asset Management later offloaded a 3% stake for Rs 2,949 crore. SBI Mutual Fund was among the largest buyers in the latter transaction.

Groww also saw two large investor exits worth Rs 3,649 crore. Y Combinator sold shares worth Rs 1,435 crore , offloading its 1.2% stake, while Ribbit Capital sold shares worth Rs 2,217 crore . The transactions came as Groww continued to lead the stockbroking space with 1.31 crore active users and a 28.88% market share as of July 2026.

Foodtech and quick commerce platform Eternal also witnessed a Rs 3,265 crore transaction, with BNP Paribas Financial Markets and Millennium Management affiliate Integrated Core Strategies (Asia) offloading nearly 10 crore shares. BNP Paribas sold shares worth Rs 1,671 crore, while Integrated Core Strategies sold Rs 1,594 crore worth of shares.

Meesho witnessed two investor exits worth Rs 2,919 crore. Peak XV Partners and Elevation Capital sold a combined 2.27% stake for Rs 1,949 crore , followed by Y Combinator's Rs 970 crore sale. Several large institutional investors participated in the first transaction, including Societe Generale, Axis Mutual Fund, Fidelity, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley.

Outside these four companies, Hero MotoCorp acquired a Rs 1,758 crore stake in Ather Energy from GIC, raising its holding in the electric two-wheeler maker to 32.8%. Unlike most transactions during the month, the deal represented strategic buying rather than an investor exit.

title: Equentis leads $2 Mn pre Series A round in DocPharma
description: The company plans to use the funds to build 100 new compliant and licensed dark stores as it expands from over 12 to more than 50 cities. The expansion will strengthen
body: DocPharma, a prescription compliant quick commerce supply chain platform for healthcare, has raised $2 million in a pre Series A funding round led by Equentis. Existing investor 100Unicorns, Vinners and a consortium of strategic angel investors also participated in the round.

The company plans to use the funds to build 100 new compliant and licensed dark stores as it expands from over 12 to more than 50 cities. The expansion will strengthen the infrastructure that currently serves more than 30 health and wellness platforms across the country, DocPharma said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by Saquib Ali, Shashank Rai and Sagar Chauhan, DocPharma operates as a backend supply chain platform for healthcare businesses. Its network of licensed dark stores, DocPharma One SaaS platform, AI powered inventory management and prescription compliant fulfilment infrastructure support more than 30 healthcare and wellness platforms.

The company works with platforms across categories such as e pharmacies, health insurers, corporate wellness, hospitals, D2C wellness and nutraceutical brands, and pet care businesses. It enables these platforms to deliver medicines and healthcare products to consumers without building their own supply chain.

The Bengaluru based startup claims to operate across more than 12 cities and has fulfilled over 800,000 orders, with a fulfilment rate of more than 95%. It said its operations have impacted more than 500,000 lives across India.

DocPharma said its proprietary SaaS platform integrates warehouse management, inventory intelligence, order management and fulfilment into a single operating system. The platform provides real time inventory visibility, routes orders to the nearest compliant fulfilment centre and enables prescription compliant processing.

The funding comes as healthcare supply chain and quick commerce platforms continue to expand in India, with companies looking to combine faster delivery with the regulatory requirements involved in medicine fulfilment.

Bengaluru based pharmacy first quick commerce startup Plazza raised $15 million in Series A funding in July, co led by Accel, Elevation Capital and Nexus Venture Partners. The company plans to use the capital to strengthen its AI driven inventory intelligence, supply chain capabilities and pharmacy network while targeting 15 to 30 minute medicine delivery.

title: Exclusive: Mokobara set to raise Rs 91 Cr in Series C round at 2.8X valuation premium
description: Bengaluru-based direct-to-consumer (D2C) luggage and travel accessories brand Mokobara is set to raise Rs 90.66 crore ($9.5 million) in a Series C funding round,
body: Bengaluru-based direct-to-consumer (D2C) luggage and travel accessories brand Mokobara is set to raise Rs 90.66 crore ($9.5 million) in a Series C funding round, more than two years after its previous fundraise. The round is led by existing investor Sauce VC, with participation from Peak XV Partners, Niveshaay Sambhav Fund, Ayra Ventures and other existing investors. In February 2024 the company had raised $12 million or Rs 100 crore in a Series B funding round led by Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India). The board at Mokobara passed a special resolution to issue 1,300 Series C compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 6,15,415.32 per share and 199 equity shares at Rs 5,35,798 per share to raise the above-mentioned amount, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Existing investor Sauce VC will lead the round with an investment of Rs 57.68 crore, followed by Niveshaay Sambhav Fund and Ayra Ventures with Rs 13.07 crore and Rs 10.47 crore, respectively. Peak XV Partners will also invest Rs 8.41 crore, while Vivek Jain will contribute Rs 1.03 crore.

As per Entrackr’s estimate, Mokobara’s valuation will surge 2.76X to Rs 1,930 crore  (or $203 million) from Rs 700 crore in series B round. The company plans to use the fresh proceeds to support its growth objectives, strengthen its financial position, and build long-term resources.

Founded in 2020 by former Urban Ladder executives Sangeet Agrawal and Navin Parwal, Mokobara is a Bengaluru-based D2C travel and lifestyle brand. The company offers luggage, bags and backpacks, totes, slings, travel accessories and wallets, targeting the premium travel and lifestyle segment. Following the allotment, Sauce VC will hold a 20.48% stake in Mokobara, followed by Peak XV Partners with 16.76% and Saama Capital with 13.65%. Co-founders Sangeet Agrawal and Navin Parwal will hold 21.46% and 11.25% stakes, respectively.

Mokobara’s revenue from operations nearly doubled to Rs 230.15 crore in FY25 from Rs 117.44 crore in FY24, marking a 96% year-on-year growth. However, the company’s net loss increased to Rs 10.18 crore in FY25 from Rs 4.24 crore in FY24.

It competes with D2C players such as Escape Plan , which raised $25 million earlier this year led by Jungle Ventures, Uppercase , which raised Rs 20 crore in April, Nasher Miles and Acefour Accessories in India’s fast-growing travel gear market.

title: Ultrahuman raises $70 Mn from Qualcomm, Alpha Wave, Nexus and others
description: Ultrahuman has raised $70 million in a funding round led by Qualcomm Ventures, with participation from Labcorp, Alpha Wave, Blume Ventures, Nexus and other investors.
body: Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman has raised $70 million in a funding round led by Qualcomm Ventures, with participation from Labcorp, Alpha Wave, Blume Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Alteria and other investors.
The Bengaluru-based company said it will use the capital for product development across sensing, AI, miniaturised electronics, health algorithms, clinical science and research.
Entrackr exclusively reported about the round on Tuesday based on Ultrahuman’s regulatory filings.

Entrackr’s earlier estimates pegged the company’s post-money valuation at around $363 million, a 65% jump from its previous Series B valuation. Ultrahuman had previously raised $35 million in Series B funding and $17.5 million in Series A funding in October 2022.

Ultrahuman said it plans to evolve from a wearable health company into a human-computer interface company built around data from the human body. Its platform combines data from the Ultrahuman Ring, Blood Vision, M1/M2 Live continuous glucose monitoring, Ultrahuman Home and Jade AI system. These products track physiological, biochemical, metabolic and environmental data.

The company has also added research initiatives such as Pulsomics, an opt-in platform that allows Ring users to participate in health studies. Its current programmes focus on sleep, VO₂ Max and glucose metabolism. Other features include AFib Detection, Cycle & Ovulation Pro and cardiovascular fitness age, along with PowerPlugs for additional health-related capabilities.

Ultrahuman reported Rs 565 crore in revenue and Rs 73 crore profit after tax in FY25. The company had projected revenue of around Rs 1,000 crore for FY26 as it looked to expand further in international markets.
Ultrahuman was founded by Mohit Kumar and Vatsal Singhal, who sold their logistics startup Runnr to Zomato in 2017.

title: SoftBank trims Meesho stake through Rs 1,650 Cr block deal
description: Japanese investment giant SoftBank has sold 8 crore shares of e-commerce platform Meesho for around Rs 1,650.4 crore through a block deal on Thursday on NSE.
body: Japanese investment giant SoftBank has sold 8 crore shares of e-commerce platform Meesho for around Rs 1,650.4 crore through a block deal on Thursday on NSE.
According to stock exchange data, SoftBank’s investment vehicle SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC sold the shares at Rs 206.30 apiece. The transaction represents around 1.73% stake in Meesho.

The shares were picked up by a mix of institutional investors, including Societe Generale - ODI and Motilal Oswal Large and Midcap Fund. Other buyers included funds managed by Fidelity, Franklin Templeton and Manulife, along with Goldman Sachs Bank Europe, HDFC Standard Life Insurance, Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance, Canara Robeco Mutual Fund, Bank of America Securities and other institutional investors.
SVF II Meerkat held an 8.60% stake in Meesho as of June 2026. If the entire 8 crore shares sold in Thursday’s transaction came from the SoftBank entity, its holding would fall to around 6.87%.

The exit adds to SoftBank’s recent sell-offs in listed Indian technology companies. In August, SoftBank sold another Rs 2,888 crore worth of Lenskart shares through a block deal, following a Rs 2,873 crore sale in June.

This transaction comes shortly after a strong month of secondary market activity in Indian new-age companies. In August, investors executed 17 block and bulk deals worth Rs 26,337 crore ($2.77 billion) across 12 companies, including Meesho, Groww, Eternal and Lenskart. Meesho alone saw early investors offload Rs 1,949 crore worth of shares through a block deal, followed by Y Combinator’s Rs 970 crore stake sale.
In Q1 FY27, Meesho’s operating revenue grew 48% year-on-year to Rs 3,713 crore , while its net loss narrowed 54% to Rs 133 crore from Rs 289 crore in the year-ago quarter.
At the end of Thursday’ trading session, Meesho's shares closed at Rs 209.74, taking the company's market capitalization to Rs 96,983 crore (around $10.2 billion).

title: Slice raises $100 Mn at $450 Mn valuation: Report
description: Bengaluru-based digital banking startup Slice has reportedly raised $100 million in a fresh funding round at a valuation of around $450 million.
body: Digital banking startup Slice has reportedly raised $100 million in a fresh funding round at a valuation of around $450 million.

According to a Moneycontrol report, the round was led by Indian wealth management platform Neo Wealth, with participation from Japan-based Kado Global, US-based Moore Strategic Ventures, and Dhan-parent Raise Financial, among other investors.

The latest round represents a sharp decline in Slice’s valuation from its peak of $1.5 billion, when the Bengaluru-based fintech secured $50 million in a Series C round led by existing backer Tiger Global, with participation from Moore Strategic Ventures and Insight Partners. The firm attained unicorn status with a $200 million Series B round in November 2021.

According to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), Slice’s board has approved the issuance of 40,347 compulsory convertible debentures (CCDs) worth Rs 403.47 crore ($42.5 million). The proposed allotment includes Rs 106 crore from Moore Strategic Ventures, Rs 95 crore from Kado Global, and Rs 44 crore each from Neo Secondaries Fund and Blume Ventures. Other proposed allottees include Raise Financial, the parent company of Dhan, DSP Investment, and several angel investors.
In addition, the board approved the issuance of partly paid-up shares worth Rs 81.5 crore to Neo Wealth.
According to sources, the $100 million funding included both primary and secondary transactions.

The fresh capital comes at a time when Slice has turned profitable following its transition into a digital bank. The company reported a net profit of Rs 48.4 crore in FY26, compared with a loss of Rs 217 crore in FY25. It has carried the momentum into FY27, with a net profit of Rs 50.9 crore in the first quarter .
Slice’s total income rose 38.6% year-on-year to Rs 413.8 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 298.6 crore in the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, income grew 3.5% from Rs 399.7 crore in Q4 FY26.

title: Cradlewise raises $12 Mn in Series A round led by 3one4 Capital, Prudent Investment
description: The company’s AI-enabled cribs use sensors to track movement, sound, sleep state, and other contextual signals. Its system uses this data to predict when a baby is like
body: Consumer health and wellness company Cradlewise has raised $12 million in a Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management.
With this round, Cradlewise has raised a total of $26 million to date, backed by Sean O’Sullivan Ventures, Footwork VC, Charles River Ventures, 3one4 Capital, and Prudent Investment Management.
The company will use the fresh capital for growth, channel expansion, product R&D, and geographic expansion, Cradlewise said in a press release.
Founded in 2019 by Radhika Patil and Bharath Patil, Cradlewise is an AI-first consumer tech company that makes smart cribs designed to soothe babies and help improve family sleep.

The company’s AI-enabled cribs use sensors to track movement, sound, sleep state, and other contextual signals. Its system uses this data to predict when a baby is likely to wake up and intervene before the baby fully wakes.

Cradlewise claims its technology can save parents up to two hours of effort each day. The company has patents covering its hardware and sensing systems and says its models are trained on more than 75 million hours of sleep data.

The company also operates an integrated manufacturing facility in Pune, which can produce, test, and pack thousands of cribs each month. This gives Cradlewise greater control over quality, product development, and costs, it said.
Cradlewise’s smart sleep system combines a crib, contactless monitoring, adaptive motion, and a connected app to detect early signs of stirring and help babies settle before fully waking.

title: ABP Education leads seed round in edtech platform YoLearn.ai
description: As part of the partnership, ABP Group companies Headword Publishing and KIPS Learning will work with YoLearn.ai to convert their school books into content-aligned AI
body: Voice-first AI tutoring platform YoLearn.ai has raised an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round led by ABP Education, the education arm of ABP Group.

Prior to this, the Noida-based startup had raised $500,000 in a pre-seed funding round at a valuation of $5 million. The round was co-led by DataAlpha.ai and White Swan Global, with participation from a group of angel investors.
Along with the funding, ABP Education will support YoLearn.ai with content, marketing and distribution as the startup looks to provide personalised AI tutoring to K-12 students in India.

As part of the partnership, ABP Group companies Headword Publishing and KIPS Learning will work with YoLearn.ai to convert their school books into content-aligned AI tutors through Headword.ai and kipslearning.ai. The tutors will be accessible through the books students use in classrooms.

The partnership covers a combined network of around 25,000 schools, with potential access to nearly 100 million learners. The partners aim to reach 150 million students and train more than 1.5 lakh teachers in AI-enabled classroom instruction, with a longer-term goal of providing personalized AI learning to 250 million K-12 students in India.

Founded in January 2025 by Kirti Prakash Mishra, YoLearn.ai allows students to scan a code in a textbook and interact with an AI tutor through voice. The platform supports English, Hindi and other regional languages, covering 22 Indian languages.

The AI tutor provides voice-based answers, diagrams and step-by-step solutions through an interactive sketchpad. It also offers practice tests, evaluates responses based on board exam marking patterns, predicts scores and provides parents with updates. The platform supports CBSE, ICSE and state boards.

YoLearn.ai also offers teachers a Co-Teacher Avatar configured to their teaching style, along with more than 50 AI-assisted tools for lesson planning, worksheets, homework, assessments, quizzes and classroom presentations. School administrators can access dashboards covering learning outcomes, areas of weakness, usage and student progress.

title: Ola Electric to consider another fundraise amid market share pressure
description: Ola Electric Mobility is looking to raise fresh capital, just three months after raising Rs 780 crore through a qualified institutional placement.
body: Ola Electric Mobility is looking to raise fresh capital, just three months after raising Rs 780 crore through a qualified institutional placement, according to a disclosure sourced from its stock exchange filing.

The fresh fundraise comes as the electric two-wheeler maker faces pressure on multiple fronts, including falling market share, mounting customer complaints and a declining share price and market capitalisation.
The company has scheduled a board meeting on September 5, 2026, to consider and approve a proposal to raise funds through the issuance of equity shares or other eligible securities.

According to the regulatory filing, the proposed fundraise could be undertaken through multiple routes, including a private placement, QIP, preferential issue or any other permissible method, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals. Importantly,  Ola Electric has not disclosed the size of the proposed fundraise.
The development comes shortly after the company raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP in June. Ola allotted around 21.76 crore shares at Rs 35.86 each to qualified institutional buyers.

The fresh capital push comes at a challenging phase for Ola Electric, as it works to improve its financial performance while scaling its vertically integrated EV and battery manufacturing operations. Meanwhile, The company’s scale fell down although its losses improve in the last quarter

In Q1 FY27, Ola Electric’s consolidated revenue from operations fell 45% year-on-year to Rs 455 crore , while its net loss narrowed to Rs 336 crore from Rs 428 crore in the year-ago period. Its vehicle registrations in the month of July were at 13,170 with a market share of 6.8%
The company has also been expanding its battery-cell manufacturing capabilities and recently secured a Rs 95.81 crore incentive under the government’s PLI-Auto scheme for FY27.

title: Bluehill VC leads Rs 10.2 Cr seed round in Makr Microsystems
description: Bengaluru-based semiconductor metrology startup Makr Microsystems has raised Rs 10.2 crore in a seed round led by frontier-tech VC firm Bluehill VC. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based semiconductor metrology startup Makr Microsystems has raised Rs 10.2 crore in a seed round led by frontier-tech VC firm Bluehill VC, with participation from Artha Venture Fund.

Founded by Ashwin Lal, Makr is developing nanoscale 3D subsurface metrology technology that allows chipmakers to see and measure hidden structures and defects beneath semiconductor surfaces without damaging the chip.
Its technology combines Acoustic Atomic Force Microscopy (AAFM), optical tomography and 3D data analytics.

The proceeds will be used for technology development, customer validation and commercialisation. Its initial applications include advanced packaging, hybrid bonding, buried interfaces, chiplet interconnects and defect detection.
Bluehill VC claims Makr fits its focus on backing deeptech companies solving difficult problems in critical technology sectors. The fund recently closed its maiden fund at Rs 400 crore.

Makr plans to build globally relevant semiconductor equipment and technology from India as chip architectures become increasingly complex and more manufacturing processes move into three-dimensional structures.

title: D2C brand Plum’s revenue crosses Rs 500 Cr in FY26; profit doubles
description: Plum’s revenue from operations rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 515 crore in FY26 from Rs 402 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the (RoC).
body: The D2C beauty and personal care space is seeing more activity from larger consumer companies, as established digital-first brands increasingly become acquisition targets. Against this backdrop, Mumbai-based Plum reported a 28% increase in revenue to cross Rs 500 crore in FY26, while its profit nearly doubled.
Plum’s revenue from operations rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 515 crore in FY26 from Rs 402 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Founded in 2013, Plum sells skincare, bodycare, fragrances, haircare and gifting products through its own website as well as third-party e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, Nykaa and Flipkart.

Revenue from product sales continued to be the company’s only operating revenue stream during the year. Besides its core operations, Plum earned Rs 14.3 crore from interest income and gains on mutual fund investments, taking its total income to Rs 529.3 crore in FY26.

Plum’s spending remained heavily skewed towards customer acquisition and production costs in FY26. Advertising and promotional expenses rose more than 32% year-on-year to Rs 184.4 crore, making it the company’s largest expense during the fiscal. The cost of materials consumed also climbed 28% to Rs 184.4 crore, while employee benefit expenses increased 12% to Rs 47.6 crore.

Apart from these major cost heads, Plum incurred expenses on storage, commissions, transportation, legal services and other operational overheads. Overall, these expenses took the company’s total expenditure to Rs 481 crore in FY26.

Plum’s faster revenue growth helped improve its profitability in FY26, with profit nearly doubling to Rs 49 crore from Rs 25 crore in FY25. For every rupee of operating revenue, the company spent Rs 0.93 during the year.

Plum’s improved bottom line was also reflected in its key profitability metrics. Its EBITDA margin stood at 8.12% in FY26, while ROCE improved to 13.2%. The company ended the fiscal with Rs 305.6 crore in current assets, of which Rs 92 crore was held in cash and bank balances.

title: Sugar Cosmetics raises Rs 144 Cr at Rs 755 Cr valuation; early investors seek steep discount exits
description: Sugar Cosmetics, once among the better-known names in India’s D2C beauty wave, has raised Rs 144.5 crore from existing investor A91 Partners as the company faces
body: Sugar Cosmetics, once among the better-known names in India’s D2C beauty wave, has raised Rs 144.5 crore from existing investor A91 Partners as the company faces continued pressure on revenue and profitability. The funding comes alongside efforts by some early investors to find buyers for their stakes at steep discounts to the company’s peak valuation.

The board approved the allotment of 1,12,248 Series CCPS at an issue price of Rs 12,871 per share to raise Rs 144.5 crore, according to regulatory filings. A91 Partners subscribed to the entire issue.

Based on the allotment and resulting shareholding, Entrackr estimates that the transaction values Sugar at around Rs 755 crore post-money, 75% below its peak valuation of around Rs 3,000 crore. A91 will hold around 19.97% in the company following the new round.
On Friday, ET reported that the firm was raising Rs 140-150 crore from A91 at a valuation of Rs 500-600 crore.

The latest primary round is also taking place as some existing investors explore secondary exits. Sources said investors are looking to sell stakes worth up to Rs 150 crore. Some early backers have been approaching potential buyers at steep discounts to Sugar’s peak valuation.

Entrackr has also learnt that a consulting firm has been pitching Sugar shares at a fraction of its peak valuation, with a minimum transaction size of around Rs 25 crore. The discussions underline the extent of the valuation correction since the peak of the D2C funding cycle.

Sugar was valued at around $400 million, or roughly Rs 3,000 crore, in 2022 when it raised $50 million in a Series D round led by L Catterton. At the time, the company was expanding its offline retail footprint and had emerged as a prominent youth-focused cosmetics brand.
The business has since lost momentum. Sugar’s revenue declined 20% to Rs 404 crore in FY25 from Rs 505 crore in FY24 , while its net loss almost doubled to Rs 135 crore from Rs 68 crore.

title: D2C sneaker brand Comet raises Rs 100 Cr in Series B led by Verlinvest
description: Sneaker brand Comet has raised around Rs 100 crore in its Series B round led by Belgium-based investment firm Verlinvest, as it looks to expand its retail footprint
body: Homegrown sneaker brand Comet has raised around Rs 100 crore in its Series B round led by Belgium-based investment firm Verlinvest, as it looks to expand its retail footprint and strengthen its product and technology capabilities.

Existing investors Elevation Capital and Nexus Venture Partners also participated in the round. Angel investors including Urban Company cofounder Abhiraj Singh Bhal, Snap’s global chief business officer Ajit Mohan and Bhaane founder Anand Ahuja also joined the round.

On Wednesday, Entrackr exclusively reported that Comet was raising fresh capital. As per our estimates, the funding values Comet at around Rs 535 crore, a more than threefold jump from its post-money valuation of around Rs 167 crore after its Series A round in 2024.

Comet plans to use the fresh capital to accelerate retail expansion, product development and technology capabilities, along with investments in research and development. The company is also developing its own sole moulds and tooling for new footwear models.

Founded in 2023 by Utkarsh Gupta and Dishant Daryani, Bengaluru-based Comet currently has four footwear models and plans to double its portfolio to eight models by the end of next year. It is also preparing to launch a women-focused model backed by dedicated sole tooling.
The company has grown its revenue ninefold since its previous institutional fundraise and is set to reach 10 stores this month. It plans to expand its retail network to 20 stores by the end of FY27.
In FY25, Comet’s revenue rose nearly fourfold to Rs 29 crore, while its loss widened to Rs 4.39 crore. The company is yet to file its FY26 financials.
Comet is among a growing set of homegrown sneaker brands, alongside Gully Labs, Neeman’s, ARCs and Doc Sneakers.

title: Cars24 India’s posts Rs 5,092 Cr revenue in FY26
description: The company’s revenue from operations fell 18.3% to Rs 5,092 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026, from Rs 6,233 crore in FY25 and Rs 6,917 crore in FY24.
body: Cars24’s India revenue continued to decline for the second consecutive year as the used-car marketplace navigated a challenging FY26 marked by cost cuts, layoffs and a series of senior-level exits.

The company’s India revenue from operations fell 18.3% to Rs 5,092 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026, from Rs 6,233 crore in FY25 and Rs 6,917 crore in FY24, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

In India, the sale of cars through its auction and retail businesses remained the biggest contributor, accounting for around 87% of operating revenue. However, revenue from this segment declined 22.7% to Rs 4,349 crore in FY26, pointing to stress in its core used-car business. The segment had already declined 11% in FY25, indicating that pressure on the core biz has persisted for a second consecutive year and weighed on overall scale.

However, Cars24 said that the decline in reported revenue does not fully reflect the underlying transaction activity. According to the company, its combined GMV grew 2.8% to Rs 8,046 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,827 crore in FY25. The company attributed the divergence to a shift in its merchant business from an inventory-led model, where the full vehicle value was recorded as revenue, to a direct transaction model, where only the commission earned is recognised as revenue.

The remaining operating income came from financial services, including interest on loans provided through its Loans24 platform, as well as service fees, parking fees, and other offerings such as insurance assistance and warranties. These collectively contributed around Rs 653 crore during the year.
Cars24 also recorded Rs 128 crore in other income, largely from interest on current deposits, taking its total income to Rs 5,220 crore, compared with Rs 6,358 crore in the previous fiscal year.

With the business shrinking, car procurement remained the company’s largest cost centre but fell 23.7% to Rs 4,212 crore. However, employee benefit expenses rose 33.4% to Rs 806 crore, while marketing expenses remained broadly stable at Rs 105 crore. In the end, Cars24’s overall expenses declined 17.7% to Rs 5,674 crore during the last fiscal year.

At the group level, Cars24 also recorded Rs 239 crore in ESOP costs during FY26. The company said that the expense was largely associated with acquisitions of smaller companies through cash-and-stock deals.

title: Rentomojo files RHP for Rs 1,256 Cr IPO; targets Rs 4,200 Cr valuation
description: Rentomojo, the Accel-backed furniture and appliance rental platform, has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its initial public offering (IPO).
body: Rentomojo, the Accel-backed furniture and appliance rental platform, has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its initial public offering (IPO).

The Bengaluru-based company is looking to raise around Rs 1,255.6 crore through the IPO, which will comprise a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of around 2.73 crore shares worth Rs 1,105.6 crore.

The company has fixed a price band of Rs 384-404 per share, valuing Rentomojo at around Rs 4,200 crore at the upper end. The IPO will open for subscription on September 9 and close on September 11, while anchor investors can bid on September 8.
Existing investors, including Accel India, Edelweiss, IDG Ventures India, ValueQuest, Madison India and GMO, along with founder Geetansh Bamania, will sell shares through the OFS.

Rentomojo plans to use the fresh issue proceeds primarily to strengthen its balance sheet. About Rs 70 crore will go towards debt repayment, while another Rs 42.5 crore will be used for lease rentals and licence fees for its warehouses and experience stores.

According to the company’s DRHP , Accel India is the largest shareholder with a 20.92% stake, followed by founder Geetansh Bamania and Chiratae Ventures with 14.69% and 13.69%, respectively. Edelweiss Discovery Fund holds 10.53%, while ValueQuest S.C.A.L.E Fund commands 8.92%.

Financially, Rentomojo has continued to grow while remaining profitable. Its revenue from operations rose 45.5% year-on-year to Rs 387 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 266 crore in FY25. Profit after tax jumped 142% to R 104.2 crore from Rs 43.1 crore in the previous fiscal.
As of March 2026, Rentomojo had 2.54 lakh live subscribers across 29 cities. The company operates through 20 warehouses and 82 experience stores.
