title: Trivest Partners leads $2 Mn seed round in power electronics startup Leanwatts
description: Power electronics startup Leanwatts has raised approximately $2 million (Rs 18.15 crore) in a seed funding round across two tranches, led by Trivest Partners.
body: Power electronics startup Leanwatts has raised approximately $2 million (Rs 18.15 crore) in a seed funding round across two tranches, led by Trivest Partners, with participation from angel investors Abraham George and Alok Rungta.
The company said in a press release that it will use the funds to strengthen its supply chain, increase localisation, expand manufacturing capabilities, and scale its power electronics products.

Founded in October 2023 by Pradeep Chowdary, Sujith Kumar, and Abhilash Reddy, Hyderabad-based Leanwatts develops and manufactures power electronics products, with in-house capabilities across hardware design, embedded firmware and software, product engineering, validation, testing, and quality.
The startup initially focused on EV charging and now offers portable and onboard chargers ranging from 500W to 6.6kW for electric two-wheelers, L2 and L5 vehicles, and e-tractors.
Leanwatts plans to expand into public charging solutions, rectifiers, power modules, hybrid inverters, and other power conversion applications.

The company is also working with engineering institutions on industry-oriented R&D programmes. It is targeting an annualised revenue run-rate of around Rs 60 crore ($6.25 million) by March 2027, driven by the expansion of its existing EV programmes and new applications.
Leanwatts competes with players such as Neenjas Electric, Dynolt, and IPEC.

The power electronics segment in India has attracted funding in recent years, with startups developing products across EV charging, power conversion, inverters, and related applications. Zenergize Technologies recently raised $4 million in a pre-Series A round, while Enerzolve Smart Technologies raised $5.1 million. Dynolt Technologies raised $1.7 million in 2025.

title: Ola Electric approves Rs 1,500 Cr fundraise; COO Hyun Shik Park resigns
description: Electric two-wheeler maker Ola Electric has approved a plan to raise up to Rs 1,500 crore through the issuance of equity shares or convertible securities.
body: Electric two-wheeler maker Ola Electric has approved a plan to raise up to Rs 1,500 crore through the issuance of equity shares or convertible securities.

The company’s board approved the proposal on September 5. The fundraise can be carried out through a further public offer, rights issue, QIP, private placement or other permitted routes, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
The development comes just three months after Ola raised Rs 780 crore through a QIP in June , when it allotted around 21.76 crore shares at Rs 35.86 apiece to qualified institutional buyers.

Meanwhile, Ola Electric COO Hyun Shik Park has resigned , effective from the closing business hours of September 5. The company said Park resigned from his role as a Senior Management Personnel due to personal reasons.

The fresh fundraise comes at a difficult time for the EV two-wheeler maker, which has been dealing with falling market share, customer complaints and a decline in its share price and market capitalisation.

In Q1 FY27, Ola Electric’s revenue from operations fell 45% YoY to Rs 455 crore , while its net loss narrowed to Rs 336 crore from Rs 428 crore a year earlier. The company recorded 13,170 vehicle registrations in July , giving it a 6.8% market share.
Ola Electric has also been scaling up its battery-cell manufacturing operations. It recently secured Rs 95.81 crore under the government’s PLI-Auto scheme for FY27 .
The board has also approved increasing the company’s authorised share capital from Rs 8,318.5 crore to Rs 8,721.9 crore , subject to shareholder approval.

title: Rentomojo IPO: Early investors set for up to 152X returns through OFS
description: Rentomojo’s upcoming IPO could deliver multi-fold returns to early investors, with one shareholder set to clock a 152X return as shareholders offload Rs 1,106 crore worth of shares through the OFS.
body: Rentomojo’s upcoming IPO is set to generate multi-fold returns for several of its early investors, with one shareholder set to clock a 152X return on its investment, while existing shareholders are looking to offload shares worth Rs 1,106 crore through the OFS.

According to Entrackr’s analysis, at the upper price band of Rs 404 per share, Accel India is set to generate around 8.63X returns on its Rs 317 crore OFS. Madison India could clock around 7.22X on its Rs 96.9 crore share sale, while ValueQuest and Edelweiss are expected to earn around 5.4X on their respective OFS shares worth Rs 109.6 crore and Rs 116.5 crore.
Chiratae Ventures is likely to generate around 4.93X returns on its Rs 194.1 crore OFS, while GMO could earn around 4.24X on its Rs 95.1 crore share sale.

Among individual shareholders, Nitish Mittersain, founder of Nazara Technologies, is set to emerge as one of the biggest beneficiaries. Mittersain’s investment in Rentomojo was his first startup investment. He is selling shares worth around Rs 6 crore through the OFS, which could fetch him around 152X returns based on the acquisition cost disclosed in the company’s offer documents and the upper IPO price band of Rs 404 per share.
Rajeev Chitrabhanu, who was Rentomojo’s first investor, could generate around 26.6X returns from his Rs 12.4 crore OFS.

The company’s founder Geetansh Bamania is set to offload shares worth Rs 34.3 crore, while other OFS participants include Japan-based Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance Venture Capital (MSIVC), Pratithi Investment Trust, Renaud Laplanche and others.

The returns are based on the weighted average acquisition cost disclosed in Rentomojo’s offer documents and the upper IPO price band of Rs 404 per share. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an OFS of around Rs 1,105.6 crore, giving the company a valuation of around Rs 4,200 crore at the upper band.
Rentomojo’s IPO is scheduled to open for subscription on September 9 and close on September 11.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Aug 31 - Sep 05]
description: This week, 25 Indian startups raised $303.7 million across five growth-stage deals, 16 early-stage deals and three undisclosed rounds. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 25 Indian startups raised $303.7 million across five growth-stage deals, 16 early-stage deals and three undisclosed rounds. The week also saw seven key hires, four mergers and acquisitions, two startup shutdowns and 250 layoffs.
In contrast, 24 startups had collectively secured about $218.7 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised $201.9 million across five deals this week. Digital banking startup Slice led the funding with a $100 million round at a $450 million valuation, led by Neo Wealth with participation from Kado Global, Moore Strategic Ventures and Raise Financial.

Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman has raised $70 million in a round led by Qualcomm Ventures, with participation from Labcorp, Alpha Wave, Blume Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Alteria and other investors. D2C skincare brand SUGAR Cosmetics has raised Rs 144.5 crore ($15.2 million) from existing investor A91 Partners at a valuation of Rs 755 crore, down 75% from its last valuation of Rs 3,000 crore.

Homegrown sneaker brand Comet has raised around Rs 100 crore in its Series B round led by Belgium-based investment firm Verlinvest. Pune-based deeptech company Aeron Systems has raised Rs 45 crore ($4.7 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $101.8 million across 16 deals this week. BaaS provider Yuma Energy raised $35 million in Series A funding led by Magna International, while NextGen Finance raised Rs 215 crore led by Beams Fintech Fund.

title: Udaan to acquire Swiggy-owned Lynk Logistics for Rs 500 Cr
description: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Swiggy has agreed to sell its retail distribution business Lynk Logistics to eB2B platform Udaan for Rs 500 crore.
body: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Swiggy has agreed to sell its retail distribution business Lynk Logistics to eB2B platform Udaan for Rs 500 crore, in a deal that will expand Udaan’s presence across key consumption markets.

As part of the transaction, Swiggy will receive approximately 2.8% stake in Udaan through preference equity shares issued by Trustroot Internet Pvt Ltd, the parent entity of Udaan. Swiggy will also invest Rs 75 crore in primary equity in Udaan for an additional 0.4% stake.

The transaction comes as Udaan continues to improve its financial performance. Over the 10 quarters from Q4 CY23 to Q1 CY26, its revenue grew at a CAGR of around 25%, while its contribution margin improved by nearly 500 bps and EBITDA burn declined by around 70%. Its private labels now account for 15–25% of Staples sales across operating cities, while Bengaluru, its largest market, has turned EBITDA profitable.

The acquisition will add Lynk’s distribution capabilities, brand relationships and retail network to Udaan’s platform. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Kolkata together contribute around 75% of Lynk’s revenue. The deal will also help Udaan connect leading consumer brands with a wider network of retailers.

Lynk directly or indirectly competes with the likes of Udaan, 1K Kirana Bazaar, Jumbotail, ElasticRun and several other eB2B and retail distribution platforms. These companies serve retailers through technology-led distribution, procurement and supply chain networks, making the acquisition relevant to Udaan’s competitive position in India’s fragmented retail distribution market.

Swiggy had acquired Lynk in July 2023 through a share swap deal, marking its entry into India’s retail B2B distribution market. The transaction value was not disclosed at the time. Lynk, founded in 2015, had a network of more than 100,000 retail stores across eight cities and worked with leading FMCG brands as an authorised distributor.

The latest transaction also follows Udaan’s $160 million recapitalisation, which comprised fresh equity, new debt and debt-to-equity conversion from Lightspeed Venture Partners, M&G Investments and Moonstone Capital. The exercise included around $45 million in private credit financing from a leading global investment management firm and strengthened Udaan’s balance sheet for its next phase of growth.

Swiggy CFO Rahul Bothra said the deal combines Lynk’s capabilities with Udaan’s scale and technology-led platform, while Udaan cofounder and CEO Vaibhav Gupta said the acquisition strengthens the company’s business and expands its presence across important consumption markets.

title: The neobank bet: what backing digital banks in India actually taught us
description: A core part of how we work at Better Capital has been to identify a microtrend early, build conviction in it, and then back multiple companies around that microtrend before it becomes obvious to everyone else. It has served us well over the years.
body: With GFF around the corner, I wanted to reflect on what we have actually learned from our fintech portfolio, especially since fintech was the very first area we focused on when we started the fund.

A core part of how we work at Better has been to identify a microtrend early, build conviction in it, and then back multiple companies around that microtrend before it becomes obvious to everyone else. It has served us well over the years.

The very first microtrend we started with was neobanks. In 2018/19 in India, it wasn't really a term yet. My conviction came partly from a vivid memory of a company called Simple from the late 2000s, whose vision was to build a modern digital bank for small businesses. As a small startup founder myself back then, that was something I related to deeply.

By 2018/19 it felt like the ingredients were finally in place in India. A smartphone-first, data-connected, UPI-led population was ready for a genuinely modern banking experience. A number of teams started building around this time and we made several investments: a neobank for Gen Z, one for NRIs, one for SMBs, and a few more.
Soon there was broader conviction in the market and many companies got funded around the same idea. The next several years were about watching them all build and navigate a hard set of constraints.

The hardest one was structural. You cannot easily get a banking license in India, and that single constraint shaped everything. Without a license, delivering a true full-stack customer experience was very hard. Companies had to depend on bank partnerships, and those dependencies caused delays across product, launches and the ability to control the core experience. Compliance and infrastructure constraints added more friction. Consumer and business adoption was genuinely strong, but the path to the fuller vision kept hitting the same ceiling.

Slice was the one that broke through it. By acquiring a bank and becoming a full-stack neobank, it unlocked the vision many of us had held on to for years. Today, Slice is one of the top credit card issuers in the country within about a year of going full-stack, ahead of many large banks, and posted a PAT of around ₹46 crore in Q1FY27.

And Slice is not the only story here. Several others from this cohort are still very much in play, and they have delivered genuinely incredible improvements in customer experience along the way. I am excited to see how they navigate the next chapter and unlock more of the vision we all started with.

title: HerSpace secures $40 Mn from existing investor Gray Matters Capital
description: Bengaluru-based workforce accommodation startup HerSpace Manufacturing has secured a fresh capital commitment of $40 million from existing investor Gray Matters Capital (GMC).
body: Bengaluru-based workforce accommodation startup HerSpace Manufacturing has secured a fresh capital commitment of $40 million from existing investor Gray Matters Capital (GMC).

The latest commitment takes the total capital committed by GMC to $50 million, including the $10 million invested in 2025. The capital will be deployed over the next 30 months through a mix of debt, quasi-equity and equity.

HerSpace will use the funds to expand its affordable employee housing offerings across key manufacturing hubs, including Greater Bengaluru, Hosur, Chennai and Andhra Pradesh. The company will also invest in people and systems to support its growth.

Founded in 2023 by Bob Pattillo and Puneeth Thimmegowda, HerSpace provides leased accommodation for industrial workers. The startup funds, designs, builds and operates workforce housing facilities, with statutory compliance incorporated into its operations.
The company currently has more than 950 modular beds delivered and operational, while over 10,000 beds are in the pipeline.

“This funding milestone marks a defining moment for HerSpace and reflects the immense market opportunity ahead, as well as the dedication of our talented team including our founders Mr. Bob Pattillo and Mr. Puneeth Thimmegowda,” said Simha Nagaraj, CEO of HerSpace Manufacturing.

HerSpace’s expansion comes amid growing focus on worker accommodation as a factor supporting India’s manufacturing sector. A 2024 NITI Aayog report highlighted inadequate housing near industrial hubs as a constraint for worker migration, retention and productivity, particularly for women workers.
HerSpace said its accommodation model can also help employers reduce employee transport costs and their carbon footprint.

title: Exclusive: DaMENSCH raises fresh funding at flat valuation of Rs 600 Cr
description: DaMENSCH has raised fresh capital from existing backer A91 Partners and new investor Tancom Electronics, but the latest round has not moved its valuation.
body: DaMENSCH has raised fresh capital from existing backer A91 Partners and new investor Tancom Electronics, but the latest round has not moved its valuation. The flat pricing comes as the direct to consumer men’s apparel market enters a more competitive phase, with brands now under pressure to turn topline growth into profitability.
In May 2024, the company had raised Rs 21.62 crore (approximately $2.5 million) in its extended Series B round from existing investors.

The board at DaMENSCH has approved the allotment of 887 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,69,052 per share to raise Rs 15 crore from A91 Partners, according to the company’s regulatory filing accessed through the Registrar of Companies.

Separately, the company issued 168 CCPS at an issue price of Rs 1,42,692 per share to raise Rs 2.40 crore from Tancom Electronics. Together, the two tranches helped DaMENSCH raise Rs 17.40 crore in this round.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, DaMENSCH’s valuation is flat to Rs 600 crore ($63.5 million at current exchange rate) from its previous valuation of $70-75 million or Rs 582 crore .
The company plans to use the fresh capital to meet its business requirements and support its growth, as per filings.

Founded in 2018 by Anurag Saboo and Gaurav Pushkar, DaMENSCH is a D2C men’s fashion and lifestyle brand that offers innerwear, casualwear, and everyday apparel products via its own platform and marketplaces.
DaMENSCH has raised over $28 million to date, including its $16.6 million Series B round led by A91 Partners in February 2022.

title: Voice AI startup Navana.ai raises Rs 40 Cr led by Ronnie Screwvala
description: Voice AI startup Navana.ai has raised Rs 40 crore ($4.2 million) in a Series A round led by entrepreneur and investor Ronnie Screwvala.
body: Voice AI startup Navana.ai has raised Rs 40 crore ($4.2 million) in a Series A round led by entrepreneur and investor Ronnie Screwvala. The round also saw participation from Antler India, Sharad Sanghi, Sandeep Singhal, Paula Mariwala and other investors.

The company plans to deploy the fresh capital to expand its Voice AI deployments among BFSI enterprises, strengthen its speech models for Indian languages and dialects, and develop its AI Contact Centre and automated evaluation platform.

Founded by brothers Raoul and Jai Nanavati, Navana.ai provides voice AI solutions to regulated enterprises, with a focus on data privacy and compliance through on-premise deployments. The startup claims to have processed more than 100 million voice AI minutes for BFSI companies including Bajaj Finserv, Protean, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Jana Small Finance Bank and Grihum Housing Finance.

Navana.ai has developed proprietary speech models covering 12 Indian languages and 45 dialects. Its models are designed to handle challenges such as background noise, overlapping speech, code switching and regional accents. The company has also collaborated with IISc Bengaluru, IIT Madras, Microsoft Research and the Gates Foundation.
The startup said its Bodhi speech model achieved the highest accuracy in a benchmarking exercise conducted across Indian voice AI platforms using real world speech samples.

Ronnie Screwvala said that Navana.ai is addressing the linguistic complexity of India and that voice AI could become a critical part of the country’s digital infrastructure. He also highlighted data localisation and regulatory compliance as key considerations for enterprise adoption.
Navana.ai is building voice AI infrastructure for regulated industries, with its Bodhi speech models being used by BFSI companies to serve customers in their own languages at scale.

title: Exclusive: Swish to raise around $24 Mn at $175 Mn valuation
description: Swish is raising Rs 224.54 crore (around $24 million) in an extended Series B round led by Bertelsmann India, with the participation from its existing investors.
body: Swish is raising fresh capital from Bertelsmann India Investments, adding a new institutional investor to its captable. The round comes just months after its last fundraise, pointing to continued investor interest in the emerging 10-minute food delivery model.
The Bengaluru-based startup is raising Rs 224.54 crore (around $24 million) in an extended Series B round led by Bertelsmann India, with the participation from its existing investors.
This will be the company’s second funding round this year. In March, Swish raised $38 million in a round led by Hara Global and Bain Capital.

The board at Swish has passed a special resolution to issue 4,123 Series B2 compulsory convertible preference shares at an issue price of Rs 5,44,616 each to raise the above mentioned amount, its regulatory filing accessed from the Registrar of Companies shows.

Bertelsmann India Investments will lead the round with an investment of Rs 143.34 crore ($15 million), joining Swish’s captable. Bain Capital Ventures will invest Rs 62 crore ($6.5 million), while Accel and Hara Global will participate with Rs 14.32 crore and Rs 4.8 crore, respectively.
According to the Entrackr’s estimates, Swish’s valuation will surge over 30% to Rs 1,653 crore or around $175 million post-money, from Rs 1,268 crore in its previous $38 million round.

Following the allotment of the new round, Bertelsmann India Investments will acquire an 8.67% stake in Swish. Accel will remain the largest shareholder with a 23.48% stake, followed by Hara Global with 17.93% and Bain Capital Ventures with 9.97%. Its co-founders Aniket Shah, Sureshkumar Saran and Ujjwal Sukheja will retain 10.98% each.
In June, Moneycontrol reported that Swish was in talks to raise $20 million from Bertelsmann India Investments.

title: Pet food and nutrition brand Lickicious raises Rs 19 Cr led by Prath Ventures
description: Pet food brand Lickicious has raised Rs 19 crore in growth capital through a mix of equity and institutional debt as it looks to scale its annual revenue to Rs 100 crore.
body: Pet food and nutrition brand Lickicious has raised Rs 19 crore in growth capital through a mix of equity and institutional debt as it looks to scale its annual revenue to Rs 100 crore.
Prath Ventures led the institutional backing in the round, while the founders of Atomberg and several senior industry CXOs are also among the company’s early backers.
Founded in 2024 by Shashwat Sahai and Chandan Jha, Lickicious is operated by Nuvexo Wellness Pvt Ltd and sells food and nutrition products for dogs and cats.

The fresh capital will be deployed across three areas: capacity, capability and category expansion. The company is developing a 60,000 sq ft manufacturing and distribution footprint to increase production capacity, improve supply reliability and strengthen control over product quality.

Lickicious will also invest in research and development, quality, manufacturing, supply chain, brand and commercial functions. It plans to expand its portfolio across products, formats, species and sales channels, moving beyond its digital first model towards an omnichannel pet nutrition business.
The company is targeting Rs 100 crore in annual revenue as an important milestone, while aiming to become one of India’s top three pet food companies over the next decade.
“Our next phase is about building better products, stronger manufacturing and a stronger brand,” said Shashwat Sahai, cofounder of Nuvexo Wellness.

Prath Ventures Managing Partner Harmanpreet Singh said India’s pet food market is becoming increasingly product and trust led. He added that Lickicious is investing in manufacturing, product development, category and channel expansion to support its next phase of growth.

title: Women’s wellness brand Nua raises $50 Mn led by Peak XV, Filter Capital
description: Women’s wellness brand Nua has raised $50 million in its Series C funding round led by Peak XV Partners and Filter Capital, with participation from existing investors News
body: Women’s wellness brand Nua has raised $50 million in its Series C funding round led by Peak XV Partners and Filter Capital, with participation from existing investors Mirabilis Investment Trust and Footpath Ventures.
The round includes both primary capital and a secondary component, giving partial exits to Kae Capital, Lightbox VC and existing angel investors.
The Mumbai-based company has raised around $71.5 million so far, including $4 million (Rs 35 crore) in a pre-Series C round led by Mirabilis Investment Trust in February 2025.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen brand building, expand distribution and reach, and invest in R&D and new product development, Nua said in a press release.
According to Peak XV, Nua has emerged as the second-largest online player in the women’s wellness category .

Founded in 2017 by Ravi Ramachandran, Nua offers products across period care, maternity care and everyday intimate wellness. The company says it now reaches more than 3 million women and girls every month .
Nua claims to have scaled its annualised revenue run rate from Rs 100 crore to Rs 500 crore in the past 24 months while remaining profitable.
It has also expanded beyond physical products with offerings such as the Nua Period Tracker App and SecretKeeper chat.

title: Spactech startup Pixxel raises $100 Mn in Series C led by Temasek, Seraphim
description: Bengaluru-based space-tech startup Pixxel has raised $100 million in its Series C funding round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space. News.
body: Bengaluru-based space-tech startup Pixxel has raised $100 million in its Series C funding round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space.

The round also saw participation from new investors 360 ONE Asset and IMM Investment , along with existing backers Radical Ventures and growX Ventures , among others. The latest fundraise takes Pixxel’s total funding to $195 million . The company said the round is the largest funding raised by a space-tech company in India.
Media reports suggest that Pixxel is being valued at around $450-500 million in the latest round.

Pixxel will use the fresh capital to expand beyond hyperspectral imaging into advanced sensing satellites, Earth intelligence software, sovereign space systems and satellite manufacturing. Its plans include expanding the Honeybee constellation , developing high-resolution optical imaging satellites, scaling its Aurora Earth intelligence platform and increasing manufacturing capacity through Gigapixxel .

Founded by Awais Ahmed and Kshitij Khandelwal, Pixxel initially focused on hyperspectral imaging satellites and has since expanded into Earth intelligence software and satellite systems for commercial and sovereign missions.

Before the latest round, Pixxel had raised $95 million from investors including Google, Lightspeed, Radical Ventures, Blume Ventures, growX Ventures, Glade Brook Partners and Seraphim. The startup closed its Series B round at $60 million in December 2024.
The latest round comes shortly after Skyroot Aerospace became the first Indian space-tech startup to achieve unicorn status , crossing the $1 billion valuation mark.

Over the past two years, Pixxel has deployed six Firefly satellites , launched Aurora and secured contracts with NASA and the NRO. It has also won multiple iDEX challenges from the Ministry of Defence and was selected to lead the development of India’s first public-private Earth observation constellation of 12 satellites under IN-SPACe.

title: TPG-backed NewQuest offloads Rs 200 Cr Shadowfax stake in a bulk deal
description: TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has offloaded another 1.36% stake in logistics startup Shadowfax for around Rs 200 crore through a bulk deal on the BSE.
body: TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has offloaded another 1.36% stake in logistics startup Shadowfax for around Rs 200 crore through a bulk deal on the BSE.
According to exchange data, NewQuest sold 80 lakh shares at Rs 250.03 apiece, while OxBow Master Fund bought 47.85 lakh shares at Rs 250 each, worth around Rs 119.6 crore.

The transaction follows a similar deal in August, when NewQuest sold 1.25 crore Shadowfax shares at Rs 240.46 apiece for around Rs 300.6 crore. OxBow Master Fund had bought 69.32 lakh shares at Rs 240.25 apiece in that transaction worth Rs 166.5 crore.
As of June 2026, NewQuest held an 11.53% stake in Shadowfax. Across the two transactions, it has sold around 2.05 crore shares worth over Rs 500 crore, while Oxbow acquired a 2% stake in the company.
The latest deal comes as Shadowfax continues to see secondary-market activity following its public listing.
In Q1 FY27, Shadowfax recorded a 65% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 1,358 crore . Its profit also surged more than eightfold to Rs 65 crore during the quarter.
At the end of Tuesday’s trading session, Shadowfax's share price closed at around Rs 249.8 on BSE, valuing the company at Rs 14,656 crore (approximately $1.54 billion).

title: Bajaj Finance acquires 5% stake in TrueFan AI
description: TrueFan AI plans to expand beyond India into Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and the US. The company says it has already witnessed demand from these markets. Its deep-
body: Bajaj Finance, part of Bajaj Finserv, has acquired a 5% stake in TrueFan AI, an AI-powered video generation platform.
The Gurugram-based startup had previously secured $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Z3 Partners in June this year.

Founded in 2020 by Devender Bindal, Nimish Goel, and Nevaid Aggarwal, TrueFan AI offers an enterprise AI video platform that uses generative AI to create hyper-personalized, studio-quality videos and avatars from a single recording. The platform helps more than 100 enterprise clients scale video marketing across global markets.

TrueFan AI plans to expand beyond India into Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and the US. The company says it has already witnessed demand from these markets. Its deep-learning models synthesize facial dynamics, gestures, and voice to generate up to 500,000 localized videos per minute across more than 175 languages.

The startup serves over 100 enterprise customers, including HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance, Zomato, Cipla, and BharatPe. The platform enables companies to create AI-powered personalized videos at scale through celebrity avatars, business leaders, and enterprise spokespersons.
The company’s flagship product, TF Studio, enables brands to create personalized messages in bulk, localize content for different markets, and deploy lifelike brand ambassador avatars.
TrueFan AI reported revenue of Rs 17.1 crore (approximately $2 million) in FY25. Revenue grew 131% year-on-year.

Bajaj Finance has deployed TrueFan’s platform at scale, generating millions of personalized videos for customer engagement and dealer enablement initiatives. It also supports Bajaj Finance’s broader strategy of deploying AI-led automation and personalization across its digital ecosystem.

title: Kuku to build 1,000-member AI team ahead of Rs 3,500 Cr IPO
description: Kuku Technologies, the parent company of Kuku FM, is building a 1,000-member AI-led content production unit as it looks to scale its microdrama business globally.
body: Kuku Technologies, the parent company of Kuku FM and Kuku TV, is building a 1,000-member AI-led content production unit as it looks to scale its microdrama business globally, according to people familiar with the matter.
The company has already hired nearly 200 people for the Mumbai-based unit and plans to expand the team to around 1,000 by the end of the current financial year, the sources said .

The hiring comes as Kuku has confidentially filed draft IPO papers with market regulator SEBI for a public issue of up to Rs 3,500 crore . The company is targeting a valuation of around $1.8 billion through the IPO.

Kuku is bringing writers, filmmakers and engineers into the new AI-native unit. Writers will develop stories and dialogues, filmmakers will focus on visual direction, while engineers will build AI systems for areas such as narrative continuity across long-running series.

Kuku expects AI to cut microdrama production costs to 30-50% of China’s, with production costing under $100 per minute versus over $150 in China, sources said. AI-led production can also help one person produce around 20 minutes of usable video a day, compared with about a minute through traditional shoots.
Kuku declined to comment when contacted.

Founded in 2018 by IIT alumni Lal Chand Bisu, Vinod Kumar, and Vikas Goyal, Kuku operates vernacular audio platform Kuku FM, short-video app Kuku TV, and edutainment platform Guru. Across its platforms, Kuku claims to have over 10 million active paying subscribers, 400 million app downloads, and a content library of more than 60,000 hours spanning several Indian languages.

The company has raised over $150 million from investors including Fundamentum Partnership, Krafton, Vertex Ventures, Granite Asia, IFC, Paramark Ventures, India Quotient, and 3one4 Capital. Former Indian cricket captain MS Dhoni is also among its backers.

title: Navam Capital leads Rs 22 Cr round in DigitalPaani
description: AI-powered water infrastructure platform DigitalPaani has raised Rs 22 crore in a funding round led by Navam Capital, with participation from Enzia Ventures, Chakra Growth Capital, 3one4 Capital
body: AI-powered water infrastructure platform DigitalPaani has raised Rs 22 crore in a funding round led by Navam Capital, with participation from Enzia Ventures, Chakra Growth Capital, 3one4 Capital, Momentum Capital, Achieving Women Entrepreneurs Early Growth Fund, and Echo River Capital.

The fresh funds will be used to expand market penetration across the industrial and municipal sectors, scale operations to serve its growing institutional customer base, and begin international expansion, DigitalPaani said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2020 by Mansi Jain and Rajesh Jain, DigitalPaani provides an operating system for water and wastewater infrastructure. Its platform combines AI-driven insights with real-time asset monitoring to help utilities, municipalities, and enterprises improve water recycling, reduce operational losses, and prevent equipment failures.

According to the Gurugram-based company, its platform analyses real-time operational data against how each asset is designed to operate, identifies inefficiencies and automates actions related to equipment, maintenance, teams, and inventory.

DigitalPaani said it serves more than 95 facilities, treating over 150 million litres of water daily. Its clients include Britannia, Leela Hotels, Tata Group, and Delhi Jal Board. The company said its deployments have helped transform non-compliant plants into fully operational assets while delivering cost savings of up to 25%. Its revenue has grown nearly sixfold over the past two years.

Ubiqedge is another startup operating in the infrastructure digitisation space. It raised Rs 10 crore in a seed round led by Piper Serica in April this year to scale its AIoT platform for infrastructure, including water systems. The company said its technology has digitised more than 23,000 borewells.

Meanwhile, IIT Madras-incubated Solinas Integrity raised $5.5 million in a Series A1 round in August, led by Mela Ventures and Hero Enterprise Family Office. The startup uses robotics and AI to inspect, clean, and digitise underground water, wastewater, and sanitation infrastructure.

title: Circolife raises $4.5 Mn in pre-Series A round led by Bharat Jaisinghani
description: Cooling-as-a-Service is gaining traction within India’s climate-tech and energy-efficiency startup ecosystem, allowing businesses to access air-conditioning and cooling
body: Cooling-as-a-Service (CaaS) platform Circolife has raised $4.5 million (around Rs 40.45 crore) in a pre-Series A funding round led by Bharat Jaisinghani, joint managing director of Polycab India. The round also saw participation from a group of individual, fund and family-office investors, including Nitish Mittersain, Intelliquity Ventures, Sumit Jalan, Siddharth Ladsariya, Anand Ladsariya, Anant Goenka, Sky Impact Capital, Rohit Dev, and family offices S N Damani and Vyom Wealth.

The fresh funds will be used to expand its fleet and geographic footprint, scale its in-house installation and service capabilities, and advance its AI-augmented IoT predictive-maintenance and digital twin platform, Circolife said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by Abhishek Murarka, Tushar Patil and Devanshu Mishra, Circolife owns, installs and services the air-conditioning units it deploys throughout their working life. The startup uses embedded IoT sensors and predictive maintenance to monitor the fleet and refurbishes and redeploys units at the end of their life cycle.

The Thane-based startup said it currently operates across five Indian cities, serving small businesses and enterprise customers across restaurants, hotels, gyms, salons, co-living operators and corporate offices through a subscription-based model for cooling.

Under its subscription model, Circolife installs and maintains the air-conditioning units while customers pay a monthly fee. The company said its units are designed for energy efficiency, while its ownership of the equipment over the contract period allows it to monitor and maintain their performance.

According to Circolife, its units are connected devices equipped with sensors that track temperature, power consumption and gas pressure in real time. This data feeds into a predictive-maintenance system designed to identify potential equipment failures before they result in breakdowns. The startup is also using AI and additional sensors to build digital twins of its deployed devices.
Circolife plans to increase its subscription base fourfold and reach 40,000 units within the next 24 months.

Cooling-as-a-Service is gaining traction within India’s climate-tech and energy-efficiency startup ecosystem, allowing businesses to access air-conditioning and cooling infrastructure without making the upfront capital investment.

title: Beverage brand Sorry Sugar raises $1 Mn in seed round
description: The brand claims to have generated more than Rs 1 crore in revenue in its first month and currently operates three offline stores across Gurugram and Delhi. It is targ
body: Gurugram-based beverage brand Sorry Sugar has raised $1 million in a seed funding round led by the Dhanuka family and Amishi London.
The company said the funding will be used to expand its online and offline presence across North India and support new product launches.

Founded this year by Deepak Pathak, Kunal Verma, Shashank Sherawat and Saiyam Malik, Sorry Sugar offers beverages with zero added sugar. Its portfolio includes coffee-based flavours such as Hazel Almond Latte, Silk Chocolate Mocha, Sea Salt Caramel, French Vanilla Cloud and Butter Gooey Toffee.
The company also offers a Rs 399 trial pack containing five flavours, with the amount fully redeemable when upgrading to a larger pack.
Sorry Sugar said its beverages are sweetened with monk fruit and contain fibre. The company is positioning its products as alternatives for consumers looking to reduce their sugar intake.

The brand claims to have generated more than Rs 1 crore in revenue in its first month and currently operates three offline stores across Gurugram and Delhi. It is targeting an ARR of more than Rs 60 crore by the end of the current financial year and plans to expand across D2C, quick commerce and offline retail channels.
The company also plans to launch a range of zero-added-sugar gelatos sweetened with monk fruit.

The funding comes amid growing activity in India’s functional and clean-label beverage segment. Peping, a functional beverage startup offering prebiotic fizzy drinks and probiotic digestive shots, raised Rs 2.5 crore from IAN Angel Fund in March this year. Swizzle, a clean-label beverage startup, raised Rs 2 crore in seed funding in December last year. Meanwhile, TABP Snacks and Beverages raised $3 million to expand its manufacturing and distribution network.

title: Gaming tech startup ARC raises Rs 10.5 Cr in pre-seed round
description: Bengaluru-based gaming technology company ARC has raised Rs 10.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Chimera VC and MIXI Global Investments. Snippets
body: Kerala-based gaming technology company ARC has raised Rs 10.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Chimera VC and MIXI Global Investments, with participation from Dhruv Vohra, Director at Meta APAC, in his personal capacity.

The fresh capital will be used to accelerate hardware engineering, product validation, manufacturing and supply-chain readiness, while also supporting the development of OWL OS and ARC’s gaming software platform. The company will also expand its team, go-to-market capabilities and strategic partnerships.

Founded by Jobin Joseph and Kaustubh K. Jadhav, ARC is developing ARC X1, a portable gaming system aimed at making dedicated gaming hardware more accessible to Indian gamers. The company is building its own hardware and software stack, including its proprietary gaming operating system OWL OS.
ARC X1 is built on an ARM-based architecture powered by Qualcomm technology and is designed to support Android gaming, PC-game compatibility and cloud gaming.

The company has already crossed 50,000 waitlist sign-ups and has collaborated with Qualcomm ahead of its commercial launch. ARC is also involving gamers in early testing and feedback to refine the product before launch.

title: Fabric care startup Iztri raises Seed round led by All In Capital, Suashish Group
description: Bengaluru based fabric care startup Iztri has raised Rs 10 crore (over $1 million) in a seed funding round led by All In Capital and Suashish Group, with participation from several angel investors.
body: The round saw participation from Anupam Mittal, Kunal Shah, Tanmay Bhat, Gaurav Munjal, Roman Saini, Abhishek Goyal, the JK Tyre family office, and Shadowfax founders Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khadelwal. Early backer PedalStart also participated in the round.

Iztri plans to deploy the fresh capital to expand its hub network and strengthen its operational and technology infrastructure. The startup will also expand beyond clothes ironing into adjacent categories such as dry cleaning and shoe care.

Founded in 2024 by Rohit Ramesh and Ankit Choudhary, Iztri started operations in early 2025. The startup operates an apartment hub model that combines neighbourhood infrastructure, trained workers and technology led backend operations to standardise service quality and turnaround times.

Iztri currently serves more than 25,000 customers across Bangalore and has created structured employment for over 200 blue collar workers through its hub network. The company aims to serve more than 100,000 customers over the next six months.
The startup plans to deepen its presence across southern India over the next two to three years before expanding into the top five metro cities.
The latest round follows a $200,000 pre seed round led by AJVC in 2025 and a $50,000 round led by PedalStart in early 2025.

Iztri is building a hyper local fabric care network, starting with clothes ironing, with plans to expand into broader fabric and home care services. The company aims to build a presence across India’s top five metro cities within the next two years.

title: Blissclub founder’s stake slips below 40% after Series B; Meesho’s Vidit Aatrey holds 6.94%
description: D2C athleisure brand BlissClub recently raised Rs 160 crore ($16.8 million) in a Series B round led by Singularity AMC, with Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey
body: D2C athleisure brand BlissClub recently raised Rs 160 crore ($16.8 million) in a Series B round led by Singularity AMC, with Meesho CEO Vidit Aatrey and existing investors Elevation Capital and Eight Roads Ventures also participating. The funding comes amid continued investor interest in India’s D2C apparel and sportswear space.

The fresh capital has pushed BlissClub’s valuation up 62% from its previous round, while the founders’ combined stake has fallen below 40%. Entrackr examined the company’s regulatory filings to decode the latest funding round, cap table, and post-money valuation.

According to the company’s regulatory filings accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC), BlissClub’s board approved the issuance of 69,247 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 24,503.3 per share to raise Rs 160 crore.

Singularity AMC emerged as the largest investor in the round with an investment of Rs 70 crore, followed by Vidit Aatrey with Rs 50 crore. Existing investors Elevation Capital and Eight Roads Ventures invested Rs 24.66 crore and Rs 15.33 crore, respectively.

According to the company, the fresh capital will be used to expand into new categories, scale its offline retail presence, strengthen product development, and hire talent to support its next phase of growth.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, BlissClub’s valuation surged 62% to around Rs 860 crore (approximately $91 million) following the Series B round, from Rs 532 crore during its Series A round.

Following the latest allotment, Elevation Capital holds a 22.19% stake in the company, followed by Eight Roads Ventures at 14.24%. Singularity AMC, which led the Series B round, holds an 8.14% stake, while Vidit Aatrey owns 6.94%. Co-founder Minu Margeret remains the largest shareholder with a 37.03% stake.

Founded in 2020 by Minu Margeret, BlissClub is a D2C athleisure brand that started with technical activewear for Indian women and has expanded into an omnichannel business with over 40 stores and a recently launched menswear line. Its portfolio spans leggings, tops, outerwear and accessories, sold through its website, marketplaces and retail stores.

title: Shiprocket narrows Q1 loss to Rs 13.7 Cr; revenue jumps 34% post IPO
description: The company’s consolidated net loss narrowed 24% year-on-year to Rs 13.7 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 18 crore in the same quarter last year.
body: Logistics and ecommerce enablement platform Shiprocket is showing signs of moving closer to profitability in its first quarterly results after going public.
The company’s consolidated net loss narrowed 24% year-on-year to Rs 13.7 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 18 crore in the same quarter last year.
Shiprocket’s revenue from operations also rose 33.8% to Rs 592 crore from Rs 442 crore in Q1 FY26, according to the unaudited results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
According to the investor presentation, the company processed 216 million transactions, with a GMV of Rs 34,662 crore and 2.24 lakh active merchants during Q1 FY27.
Its core business revenue grew 22% year-on-year to Rs 412 crore, while its other emerging businesses saw a 70% growth to Rs 180 crore during the quarter.

On the cost side, the cost of merchant solutions was the largest expenditure at Rs 441 crore, while employee benefits stood at Rs 106 crore. Overall, its total expenditure increased to Rs 619 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 474 crore a year earlier.

Meanwhile, Shiprocket’s adjusted EBITDA was positive at Rs 8.9 crore during the quarter, improved from Rs 1 crore in the year-ago period. The company said it remained adjusted EBITDA positive throughout the quarter.
The results come soon after Shiprocket’s stock market debut, making the June quarter an important first test for the company as a listed entity.

title: B2B pharma distribution startup Fundly.ai raises $4 Mn led by Accel, Multiply
description: Mumbai-based B2B pharma distribution startup Fundly.ai has raised $4 million in a funding round led by existing investors Accel and Multiply Ventures. Snippets
body: Mumbai-based B2B pharma distribution startup Fundly.ai has raised $4 million in a funding round led by existing investors Accel and Multiply Ventures, along with participation from former RBL Bank executive director Rajeev Ahuja and other angel investors.
The company also raised around $0.9 million in venture debt.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its digital commerce, payments and credit offerings across India's pharma supply chain.

Founded in 2021 by Amit Chawla and Shreeram Ramanathan, Fundly.ai initially started as a supply-chain financing platform for pharma businesses. It has since expanded into three areas: B2B commerce, payments and settlement infrastructure, and embedded credit.
Fundly aims to help pharma retailers and distributors manage procurement, payments and working capital through a single technology platform.
The latest round builds on Fundly.ai's earlier $3 million seed funding in 2023, which was also led by Accel with participation from Multiply Ventures and angel investors.

title: Fleet management platform Carrum Mobility raises $10 Mn in Series B led by Uber
description: Carrum Mobility competes with Uber-backed fleet operator Everest Fleet, which received a $20 million investment from Uber in November 2025. Uber had previously invested
body: Carrum Mobility, a B2B fleet management platform, has raised $10 million (approximately Rs 96 crore) in a Series B funding round led by Uber. This is Uber’s second investment in the company, following its $7 million investment in January 2026.
The fresh capital will be used to expand into existing and new geographies, strengthen its technology platform and scale operations, Carrum Mobility said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Karan Jain, Carrum Mobility provides fleet management solutions for CNG and electric vehicles. The platform uses technology and data to manage fleet utilisation and driver operations.
Since Uber’s previous investment in January 2026, Carrum Mobility said it has nearly doubled its business, driven by demand for premium mobility services.

The company claims to operate more than 5,000 vehicles across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi and Kolkata as of September 2026. It has over 18,000 driver partners, while its Chennai operations are expected to go live in September 2026.

Carrum Mobility competes with Uber-backed fleet operator Everest Fleet, which received a $20 million investment from Uber in November 2025. Uber had previously invested $30 million in Everest Fleet in September 2024.

Carrum Mobility said it has been profitable since its first month of operations and has reached an annualised revenue run rate of approximately Rs 400 crore within around two years of starting operations.

title: Bounce returns to scooter rentals with 14K EVs, turns EBITDA profitable in FY26
description: The progress comes as Bounce reported Rs 44.05 crore in consolidated operating revenue in FY26. Rental services emerged as its largest revenue stream.
body: Bounce has restarted its scooter rental business with electric two-wheelers manufactured by the company, moving further toward a recurring-revenue model focused on gig and delivery workers.

The Bengaluru-based electric mobility startup is now close to deploying 14,000 scooters on rentals and is expected to reach 20,000 soon, according to people aware of the company’s operations. The rental business is generating an annualised revenue run rate of around $15 million, they added.

The progress comes as Bounce reported Rs 44.05 crore in consolidated operating revenue in FY26. Rental services emerged as its largest revenue stream, contributing Rs 35.78 crore, or around 81% of operating revenue, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

The company also reported Rs 9.59 crore in consolidated EBITDA during the fiscal year. While the reported EBITDA included some non-cash items, people familiar with the business said Bounce has since reached profitability at the group level. The company recorded a PAT margin of around 19% in July, they added.

Bounce had earlier focused on selling electric scooters directly to consumers. It has now restarted rentals using its own electric vehicles, with Bounce Daily targeting gig and delivery workers who need two-wheelers for work without the upfront cost of buying one.

The rental model gives Bounce a recurring revenue stream while allowing it to use its manufacturing capabilities more directly. Unlike operators that depend on third-party OEMs, Bounce controls the vehicle design, manufacturing, and maintenance cycle, according to people familiar with the company.

This full-stack approach is also central to the company’s economics. Bounce’s own scooters are purpose-built for gig workers, while in-house manufacturing reduces dependence on external OEMs for parts and spares and can help minimise vehicle downtime.

The shift is visible in the company’s FY26 cost structure. As scooter sales reduced, material costs fell significantly, while rental income became the dominant contributor to operating revenue. Bounce’s total expenses stood at around Rs 76 crore during the year.

title: Rentomojo raises Rs 376 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
description: Furniture and appliance rental platform Rentomojo has secured Rs 376.07 crore from anchor investors ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO).
body: Furniture and appliance rental platform Rentomojo has secured Rs 376.07 crore from anchor investors ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO).
Rentomojo’s IPO opens for subscription today, September 9, and will close on September 11.

The Bengaluru-based company allotted 93.08 lakh equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 404 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band. At this price, Rentomojo will command a valuation of around Rs 4,200 crore.

The anchor round saw participation from domestic mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds. Key participants included Kotak ELSS Tax Saver Fund, ICICI Prudential Quality Fund, Goldman Sachs India Equity Portfolio, BlackRock Global Funds - India Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Great Consumer Fund, Bandhan Innovation Fund, HSBC Mutual Fund, Invesco India, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund and JM Financial Mutual Fund.

Domestic mutual funds received 60,41,249 shares, accounting for 64.90% of the anchor allocation, through 30 schemes across 16 mutual funds, for a total of Rs 244.07 crore. The allocation to life insurance companies and pension funds stood at 12.62 lakh shares, or 13.56% of the anchor portion, worth Rs 51 crore.
According to its RHP, Rentomojo plans to raise Rs 1,255.6 crore through the IPO, comprising a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an OFS of 2.73 crore shares worth Rs 1,105.6 crore.
The OFS includes shares sold by existing investors Accel India, Edelweiss, Chiratae Ventures, ValueQuest, Madison India and GMO, along with founder Geetansh Bamania.
Motilal Oswal, Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers.

title: Exclusive: Fashion brand Theater raises Series A at Rs 400 Cr valuation
description: Digital-first fashion brand Theater has raised Rs 56.25 crore (around $6 million) in Series A funding as it builds on strong growth over the past two fiscal years.
body: Digital-first fashion brand Theater has raised Rs 56.25 crore (around $6 million) in Series A funding as it builds on strong growth over the past two fiscal years. The round was led by Niveshaay, with participation from FirstPort Capital, Skagen Ventures and other investors.

In September 2024, the company had raised $1.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Prath Ventures. The board at Theater approved the issuance of 2,145 Series A CCPS at an issue price of Rs 2,62,224 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its regulatory filings.

Niveshaay led the round with an investment of Rs 37 crore, followed by FirstPort Capital with Rs 12.81 crore and Skagen Ventures with Rs 3.36 crore. Saket Agarwal, Vishal Julka, and IPV International also participated in the round. As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation stood at around Rs 402 crore ($43 million) post-money, a 4.5X increase from its previous valuation of Rs 90 crore. The fresh capital will be used to expand the business, meet working capital needs, strengthen the balance sheet and support future growth.

Founded by Sarthak Aggarwa, Karan Jain, Vikram Jain, and Shruti Agarwal, Theater is a digital-first fashion and lifestyle brand offering shoes, bags, stockings, socks, perfumes, and other accessories for men and women.

After allotment of this round, Eternal Emerging Enterprises Fund remains the largest institutional shareholder with a 9.71%, followed by Niveshaay with 9.20%, FirstPort Capital with 3.19%, and Vishal Julka with 2.54%.
Among the co-founders, Sarthak Aggarwal holds a 20.63% stake, while Karan Jain and Vikram Jain own 16.39% each. Shruti Aggarwal holds a 12.16% stake in the five-year-old company.
A Moneycontrol report had earlier said that Theater XYZ was in talks to raise $4-5 million in a funding round led by Niveshaay.

Theater is yet to file its FY26 results, but the 4.5X jump in valuation alongside its latest fundraise suggests investors have seen enough progress to back the brand at a much higher level. After 2.37X revenue growth to Rs 33.35 crore in FY25, the FY26 numbers will show whether Theater has sustained that momentum. With its investment in Theater, Niveshaay is actively expanding its focus on the D2C space. The firm has recently backed travel and lifestyle brand Mokobara and innerwear brand XYXX, while its earlier investments include beauty brands Naturis Cosmetics and Innovist.

title: Deep-tech cybersecurity company QNu Labs raises Rs 200 Cr in Series A1 round
description: QNu Labs plans to contribute to an approved project funded under the RDI programme to build the technology backbone for India’s Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks
body: Deep-tech cybersecurity company QNu Labs has raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 funding round co-led by the National Quantum Mission (NQM) and Speciale Invest, with participation from Sony Innovation Fund, Gaja Capital and Artha Ventures. The round takes QNu Labs’ total capital raised to Rs 375 crore.

The Bengaluru-based startup was incubated at IIT Madras. It previously raised Rs 60 crore ($7 million) in a Series A round led by the National Quantum Mission in April last year and $6.5 million in a pre-Series A1 round led by Ashish Kacholia of Lucky Investments in December 2023.

The fresh funds will be used to accelerate R&D, strengthen its technology capabilities, and scale sales and go-to-market operations across India and international markets, QNu Labs said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2016 by Srinivasa Rao Aluri and Sunil Gupta, QNu Labs offers quantum-safe infrastructure and platform solutions that enable clients to adopt quantum-safe security technologies without disrupting existing business operations.

QNu Labs plans to contribute to an approved project funded under the RDI programme to build the technology backbone for India’s Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks (IQSN). It also plans to expand its quantum-safe technology stack into quantum sensing and AI, increase deployments across critical sectors, and build capabilities to address demand for quantum-safe migration globally.

QNu Labs said its patented, certified and military-grade products and solutions are deployed by clients globally to secure critical infrastructure. The company plans to expand these deployments as demand for quantum-safe security solutions grows.

Startups in this space are developing infrastructure and platform layers based on technologies such as Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), Quantum Random Number Generation (QRNG), Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and cryptographic key management. These technologies allow organisations to upgrade their security architecture while maintaining existing systems.
Startups working across quantum technologies include QpiAI, Dimira Technologies, PRENISHQ, QuPrayog, Quanastra and Quan2D Technologies.

title: Alco-bev startup Marmalade raises seed round
description: Marmalade’s flagship brand, Brightside, is an Indian craft whiskey developed in partnership with Amrut Distilleries and master blender Ashok Chokalingam, and it is
body: Alco-bev startup Marmalade has raised Rs 6 crore in a seed funding round from a clutch of investors, including Ashok Chokalingam, Robert Sellares, Ishank Gupta, and HomeLane founders Srikanth Iyer and Tanuj Choudhry.
The proceeds will be deployed towards expanding distribution, brand-building initiatives, and strengthening sales and operational capabilities, Marmalade said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2025 by Udit Mediratta and Surojit Bhattacharya, Marmalade is a new-age drinks company building spirits for the next generation of Indian consumers. The company creates easy-drinking, flavour-forward alcoholic beverages aimed at making drinking more enjoyable, approachable, and relevant to today's consumers.

Marmalade's flagship brand, Brightside, is an Indian craft whiskey developed in partnership with Amrut Distilleries and master blender Ashok Chokalingam. The brand aims to offer a different way for a new generation to discover and experience whiskey through its product, branding, and category-focused innovations.

The Delhi-based startup plans to expand into Mumbai and the broader Maharashtra market. The company claims it is on track to reach an annualised revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 5 crore in September 2026 and is targeting Rs 15 crore in ARR by December 2026. This would represent threefold growth in less than four months across two cities.

According to Marmalade, Brightside Craft Whiskey combines fine malts and grain spirits with a distinctive blend of botanicals to create a smoother and more approachable drinking experience, without the harsh burn, bitterness, and strong aftertaste. Brightside has also incorporated packaging innovations aimed at making the drinking experience more engaging.

Brightside Craft Whiskey is priced at Rs 1,750 for a 750 ml bottle in Maharashtra. The brand aims to occupy a price segment between Rs 1,500 and Rs 2,200, which it describes as having limited offerings.

India's alcobev startups are experimenting with craft whisky, gin, agave spirits, and liqueurs while placing greater emphasis on contemporary branding, smoother profiles, locally sourced ingredients, and premium-but-approachable pricing.

title: Graph AI raises $13.3 Mn in Series A round led by Insight Partners
description: AI-powered patient safety startup Graph AI has raised $13.3 million in its Series A funding round led by Insight Partners, with participation from existing investor Bessemer. Snippets
body: AI powered patient safety startup Graph AI has raised $13.3 million in its Series A funding round led by Insight Partners, with participation from existing investor Bessemer Venture Partners.
The latest round comes nearly a year after the startup raised its seed round in October 2025.
Graph AI will use the fresh capital to expand its presence across the US and Europe and accelerate product development.
Founded in 2024, Graph AI develops Graph Safety, an AI powered platform that automates workflows for pharmacovigilance and patient safety teams in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors.

The platform combines AI with deterministic controls, validation layers, and end to end audit trails to help pharma companies manage safety operations while maintaining traceability and human oversight.

Graph Safety automates processes involved in handling adverse event reports and safety cases. According to the company, its live deployments have reduced case processing turnaround times from more than three hours to under 10 minutes, a reduction of over 90%. The platform has also helped lower operating costs by up to 66%, it claimed.

The startup currently offers two modules, Intake, which captures and triages adverse event reports, and Nucleus, an intelligent safety database that automates case processing. Its third module, Report, focused on automated aggregate reporting, is scheduled to launch this month.

Graph AI said it has onboarded pharmaceutical and biotech customers across North America and other markets. The startup is also working with customers on upcoming products, including Signal, which is designed to identify emerging safety signals and patterns across cases.

title: AI contact centre startup Dialflo raises Rs 1.7 Cr led by AJVC
description: AI-powered contact centre startup Dialflo has raised Rs 1.7 crore in its first funding round led by early-stage venture capital firm AJVC.
body: AI-powered contact centre startup Dialflo has raised Rs 1.7 crore in its first funding round led by early-stage venture capital firm AJVC. The round also saw participation from angel investors Afsar Ahmad, Jani, and Arpit Dave.

Founded in 2024, Dialflo is building an AI-first contact centre platform for enterprises. The startup combines human agents with AI agents and uses an attribution engine to track actions across both and link them to customer experience and return on investment (ROI).

The company initially started with the ONEST project, where it built voice AI agents to help ITI students prepare resumes. It later expanded to projects involving Smartstaff, Lokal, and other companies.
Dialflo currently serves more than 10 enterprises, including Tata Digital, Intugine, and Careernet.
The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its engineering and AI teams, strengthen its attribution engine, and onboard more enterprise customers.
Dialflo is targeting 20 enterprise customers over the next six months. It plans to focus on India and the Middle East over the next two to three quarters.
The startup competes with Crescendo and Firstsource in the enterprise contact centre space. Unlike pure-play AI or BPO providers, Dialflo is focusing on a hybrid model combining human and AI agents.
The company has not disclosed its financial details or forecasts.

title: Cardless payments platform Piston raises $15 Mn in Series A led by FPV Ventures
description: According to Piston, merchants gain access to high-margin commercial fuel volumes and increased in-store sales, while fleet owners get real-time visibility into every
body: Piston, a cardless payments platform connecting commercial fleets with gas stations and convenience stores, has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by FPV Ventures, with participation from existing investors Spark Capital and Pear VC. The round takes its total capital raised to $22.5 million.
The startup had previously raised $1.2 million in a pre-seed round led by Pear VC in October 2024 and $6.1 million in a seed round led by Spark Capital in April 2025.

Piston will use the fresh capital to accelerate the national expansion of its payments network, advance product development, and add senior leaders across key areas of the business over the next 18 months, it said in a press release.

Founded in June 2024 by Vikram Sekhon and Shivam Shah, Piston operates a cardless payments network connecting commercial fleets with gas stations and convenience stores. Its secure mobile authorisation technology is integrated directly into point-of-sale systems, eliminating skimming fraud and lowering transaction costs for both merchants and fleets.

According to Piston, merchants gain access to high-margin commercial fuel volumes and increased in-store sales, while fleet owners get real-time visibility into every gallon purchased, linked to a specific driver and vehicle.

The company claims its payment volume grew 8X year-on-year, while its merchant network expanded 40X, with customer retention at 98%. Piston is now deployed at more than 2,000 stations across 48 states. Its point-of-sale integrations are also certified and live across systems covering more than 95% of US merchant fuel sites.

Piston also plans to expand its real-time controls with two AI-powered products. Its Guard product evaluates each transaction for anomalies and can flag or block suspected fraudulent spending before it is completed. Meanwhile, the Piston Analytics Agent enables fleet owners to analyse spending data and identify patterns without spending hours on manual analysis.

title: Niveshaay leads Rs 75 Cr Series A round in fashion brand Theater
description: As part of its expansion plans, the startup will step up brand-building initiatives, including celebrity partnerships and marketing activations. It also plans to roll o
body: Design-led fashion brand Theater has raised Rs 75 crore in its Series A funding round at a post-money valuation of Rs 410 crore. The round was led by Niveshaay, with participation from new investor Physis Capital and existing investor Prath Ventures.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the development a day ago.
The Mumbai-based startup had earlier raised $1.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by Prath Ventures in September 2024.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate its offline expansion and establish a physical retail presence across Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities, Theater said in a press release.

Founded in 2021 by Sarthak Aggarwal, Vikram Jain, Karan Jain, and Shruti Aggarwal, Theater is a design-led, mass-premium western fashion brand offering footwear, stockings, perfumes, and bags. The company aims to build a design-led fashion brand combining distinctive design with accessible pricing.
Theater positions itself between imported luxury and mass-market basics. The company said it has scaled 8X over the past two years, driven by a growing customer base and a focus on profitability.

As part of its expansion plans, the startup will step up brand-building initiatives, including celebrity partnerships and marketing activations. It also plans to roll out new retail and marketing initiatives as it expands its offline presence.

Theater operates in a growing segment of India's design-led fashion market, competing with brands such as Snitch, which raised Rs 278.9 crore in a Series B round; The Bear House, which secured Rs 50 crore in Series A funding; MyDesignation, which raised Rs 40 crore in Series A; Miraggio, which raised $6.5 million in Series A; and Alaya by Stage3, which raised a seed round to scale its ethnic-wear business and AI capabilities.

title: Rentomojo IPO subscribed 1.97X on Day 1, NII portion leads at 3.87X
description: Rentomojo’s Rs 1,256 crore initial public offering (IPO) was subscribed 1.97X on the first day of bidding, according to data from the (NSE).
body: Furniture and appliance rental platform Rentomojo’s Rs 1,256 crore initial public offering (IPO) was subscribed 1.97X on the first day of bidding, according to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Non-institutional investors (NII) led the demand, with their portion subscribed 3.87X. The employee portion was subscribed 2.09X, while the retail portion saw 2.05X subscription. In contrast, the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion was subscribed 0.41X on the first day.
The IPO opened for subscription on September 9 and will close on September 11. Rentomojo has fixed the price band at Rs 384-404 per share.
The issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) worth Rs 1,105.6 crore by existing shareholders.

Founded in 2014, Bengaluru-based Rentomojo operates a subscription-based rental platform for furniture, appliances and other household products. It allows customers to rent products on monthly plans instead of purchasing them outright. The company has expanded its rental network across major Indian cities and competes with players such as Furlenco and Cityfurnish.
Rentomojo reported revenue from operations of Rs 387 crore in FY26, up 45.5% from the previous year. Its profit rose 142% year-on-year to Rs 104 crore during the fiscal year.
At the upper end of the IPO price band, the company is seeking a valuation of around $444 million. The fresh issue proceeds will be used towards debt repayment and other corporate purposes.
The IPO is being managed by Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services. Rentomojo shares are expected to list on the NSE and BSE on September 17.

title: Exclusive: Mesa School set to raise Rs 100 Cr in Series A; co-founder may sell 2.9% stake
description: “The round is structured with about Rs 84 crore coming in equity and the remaining Rs 16 crore through venture debt,” a person familiar with the transaction told Entrackr. The funding round is yet to be completed.
body: Bengaluru-based new-age business school Mesa School is set to raise around Rs 100 crore in a Series A funding round, according to sources familiar with the development.

“The round is structured with about Rs 84 crore coming in equity and the remaining Rs 16 crore through venture debt,” a person familiar with the transaction told Entrackr. The funding round is yet to be completed.

Alongside the primary fundraise, Mesa co-founder Varun Limaye is looking to sell around 2.9% of his personal stake in the company for approximately Rs 3 crore through a secondary transaction, sources said.
“The secondary component is being taken up by existing investors who are looking to increase their ownership in the company,” a source familiar with the matter said.
It could not be independently confirmed whether Elevation Capital is participating in the secondary purchase.

The proposed fundraise comes as Mesa expands its offering across startup leadership, entrepreneurship, product and AI. The company currently runs three programmes catering to different learner segments, including fresh graduates and MBA candidates.
Mesa has also seen around 2.5X growth in annual revenue and student enrolments over the past year, according to sources.
“A key part of the growth has been the expansion of the student base as well as the programmes offered by the company,” the source said.

title: 10-minute food delivery startup Swish raises $24 Mn led by Bertelsmann India Investments
description: Quick food delivery startup Swish has raised $24 million in a funding round led by Bertelsmann India Investments (BII), with participation from existing Accel. News
body: Quick food delivery startup Swish has raised $24 million in a funding round led by Bertelsmann India Investments (BII), with participation from existing investors Accel, Bain Capital Ventures and Hara Global.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the development on Monday.

Founded by Aniket Shah, Ujjwal Sukheja and Saran S., Swish operates a network of neighbourhood kitchens that prepare and deliver fresh food within 10 minutes. The company currently operates across Bengaluru, Gurugram, Noida, Delhi and Ghaziabad.

The company claims its monthly orders have crossed 1 million, with the order volume tripling since March 2026. Its menu has expanded to more than 250 SKUs across over 20 food categories, while lunch and dinner now account for a larger share of orders than snacks and late-night meals.

The fresh capital will be used to expand Swish’s kitchen network, strengthen its supply chain infrastructure and increase capacity. The company plans to enter more cities and is targeting more than 1,000 kitchens over the next five years.
Swish claims over 80% of its orders are delivered within 15 minutes. The startup currently covers around 50 pincodes and plans to expand its footprint as it scales.
Prior to this round, Swish had raised around $54 million , including a $14 million round in March 2025. As per Entrackr estimates, Swish will be valued at around $175 million post money.
Launched in July 2024, Swish reported Rs 4 crore in revenue and a total loss of Rs 19 crore during the eight-month period of FY25. The company is yet to file its FY26 financial results.

title: RentoMojo IPO subscribed 72.87X; QIB portion leads with 177.3X bids
description: Furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo’s Rs 1,256 crore IPO saw strong investor demand, with the issue subscribed 72.87 times on the final day of bidding.
body: Furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo’s Rs 1,256 crore IPO saw strong investor demand, with the issue subscribed 72.87 times on the final day of bidding.

According to exchange data, the qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) portion led the demand, with bids worth 177.3 times the shares on offer. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 67.92 times, followed by the employee portion at 21 times and the retail quota at 15.58 times.

The IPO opened for subscription on September 9 at a price band of Rs 384-404 per share. The issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) worth Rs 1,105.6 crore by existing shareholders.

Ahead of the IPO, which opened on September 9, RentoMojo raised Rs 376.07 crore from anchor investors. The anchor round saw participation from domestic mutual funds, insurance companies, and pension funds. Key participants included Kotak, ICICI Prudential Quality Fund, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock Global Funds, HDFC Mutual Fund and others.

Founded in 2014, Bengaluru-based RentoMojo operates a subscription-based rental platform for furniture, appliances and other household products. It competes with players such as Furlenco and Cityfurnish.
At the upper end of the price band, the company is seeking a valuation of around $444 million. The fresh issue proceeds will be used towards debt repayment and other corporate purposes.
RentoMojo’s revenue from operations grew 45.5% to Rs 387 crore in FY26, while its profit surged 142% to Rs 104 crore during the fiscal year.
The IPO is being managed by Motilal Oswal, Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services. RentoMojo shares are expected to list on the NSE and BSE on September 17.

title: NPCI’s FY26 profit falls 32%; revenue rises 22% to Rs 4,240 Cr
description: NPCI, which operates UPI, RuPay and other retail payment services, saw its revenue rise 22% in FY26, while its surplus fell 32% due to higher deferred tax and marketing expenses.
body: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which operates retail payment services such as UPI, IMPS, RuPay, BHIM, NACH, FASTag and BBPS, recorded a 22% year-on-year rise in revenue in FY26. However, its profit fell 32% during the year due to higher deferred tax and a rise in marketing expenses, including cashbacks and sponsorships.

NPCI’s revenue from operations rose 22% to Rs 4,240 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 3,481 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated annual financial statements accessed by Entrackr from its website.

Established in 2008 as an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks’ Association (IBA), NPCI serves as the umbrella organisation for retail payment and settlement systems in India. It operates key payment platforms and services such as UPI, IMPS, RuPay, BHIM, NACH, AePS, FASTag and BBPS. As NPCI operates as a not-for-profit organisation, it reports its profit as surplus.

Payment services remained NPCI’s primary revenue driver in FY26, contributing 88% of its operating revenue. Income from this segment rose 16% to Rs 3,736 crore from Rs 3,212 crore in FY25. The remaining operating income came from certification, network and implementation charges, membership fees, hologram charges and card-related fees.

NPCI also earned Rs 633 crore from non-operating sources in FY26, which took its total income to Rs 4,873 crore. Other income included liabilities written back, interest on income tax refunds, service guarantee mechanism (SGM) receipts, and miscellaneous income.

When it comes to expenses, Marketing and product incentives remained NPCI's largest cost centre in FY26, accounting for over 47% of its overall expenditure. These expenses rose 27% to Rs 1,420 crore from Rs 1,116 crore in FY25, led by higher spending on product incentives and cashbacks.
Marketing costs also included payments to banks for RuPay cards, advertising and publicity campaigns, B2B activities, and sponsorships.
