Employee benefit expenses rose over 22% to Rs 534 crore in FY26, while depreciation and amortisation costs increased 40% to Rs 408 crore. Operating expenses also grew 39% to Rs 291 crore from Rs 210 crore in FY25, driven by higher annual maintenance charges for network and IT equipment, network expenses, and data centre costs.

title: The Pizza Bakery operator Popo Global raises Rs 532 Cr from Artal Asia
description: Bengaluru-based restaurant company Popo Global, which operates The Pizza Bakery, Paris Panini and Smash Guys, has raised Rs 532 crore. News
body: Bengaluru-based restaurant company Popo Global, which operates The Pizza Bakery, Paris Panini and Smash Guys, has raised Rs 532 crore ($56 million) from investment firm Artal Asia.
The company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards expanding its restaurant footprint across India and scaling its portfolio of food and beverage brands.
Unlike a franchise-led model, Popo Global operates its restaurants directly, allowing it to retain control over operations across its outlets.

Founded by brothers Abhijit Gupta and Nikhil Gupta, Popo Global started with The Pizza Bakery in Bengaluru in 2017. It has since expanded the brand's presence and added Paris Panini and Smash Guys to its portfolio.
The company has focused on building company-owned outlets across the casual dining and quick service restaurant segments.

While the company did not disclose details of the transaction, Moneycontrol had earlier reported that Popo Global was in talks with global private equity firm Invus Group to raise around Rs 500 crore for a minority stake. The proposed transaction was expected to value the company at around Rs 1,100 crore to Rs 1,350 crore.

Popo Global reported revenue of around Rs 175 crore in FY25 and remained profitable during the year, according to Moneycontrol. The latest capital infusion is expected to support the company's expansion plans across its restaurant brands.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Sep 07 - Sep 12]
description: This week, 23 Indian startups raised $356.8 million across six growth-stage deals, 17 early-stage deals, and two undisclosed rounds. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 23 Indian startups raised $356.8 million across six growth-stage deals, 17 early-stage deals, and two undisclosed rounds. The week also recorded five key appointments, one departure, two mergers and acquisitions, and a new fund launch.
In contrast, 25 startups had collectively secured about $303.7 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised $182 million across six deals this week. Bengaluru-based restaurant company Popo Global led the pack with $56 million from Artal Asia, followed by women’s wellness brand Nua, which raised $50 million in a Series C round led by Peak XV Partners.

Workforce accommodation startup HerSpace Manufacturing secured a $40 million commitment from Gray Matters Capital, while quick food delivery startup Swish raised $24 million led by Bertelsmann India Investments. Fleet management platform Carrum Mobility raised $10 million in a Series B round led by Uber, while pet food brand Lickicious secured Rs 19 crore led by Prath Ventures.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $174.8 million across 15 deals this week. Space-tech startup Pixxel led the pack with a $100 million Series C round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space, followed by cybersecurity firm QNu Labs, which raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 round co-led by the National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest.

Cardless payments platform Piston raised $15 million in a Series A round led by FPV Ventures, while AI-powered patient safety startup Graph AI secured $13.3 million led by Insight Partners. Fashion brand Theater raised Rs 75 crore at a Rs 410 crore post-money valuation, while Cooling-as-a-Service platform Circolife secured $4.5 million.

title: Lenskart increases stake in AjnaLens parent to 9% with Rs 8 Cr investment
description: Lenskart Solutions has increased its stake in AjnaLens’ parent company, Dimension NXG, to 9.01% after investing an additional Rs 8 crore in
body: Lenskart Solutions has increased its stake in AjnaLens’ parent company, Dimension NXG, to 9.01% after investing an additional Rs 8 crore in the extended reality (XR) startup.
The eyewear company acquired a 1.8% stake in Dimension NXG for Rs 7.99 crore, according to its regulatory filing. The transaction was completed on September 13, 2026.

This is Lenskart’s third stake purchase in Dimension NXG this year. It acquired an additional 0.68% stake in February and another 1.69% stake in July. With these three transactions, Lenskart’s stake in the company has increased from 4.84% to 9.01%.
The eyewear major has invested a total of Rs 18.5 crore to acquire the additional 4.17% stake through these transactions.

Lenskart said the investment will strengthen its strategic association with the XR, artificial intelligence (AI) and smart wearable technology ecosystem, while supporting technology-led opportunities in smart eyewear.

Lenskart first invested in AjnaLens in July 2025 to develop AI-powered smart glasses. The partnership combines Lenskart’s expertise in frame design and engineering with AjnaLens’ XR technology capabilities.

Founded in 2014 by Pankaj Raut, Abhijit Patil and Abhishek Tomar, AjnaLens develops hardware and software solutions using XR technology. The startup caters to sectors including defence and enterprises.
AjnaLens’ parent company reported a 35% decline in turnover to Rs 10.36 crore in FY26 from Rs 15.97 crore in FY24.

title: Kissht parent OnEMI eyes fresh fundraise months after Rs 926 Cr IPO
description: OnEMI Technology Solutions, the parent company of digital lending platform Kissht, is considering another fundraise, just four months after its stock market debut in May.
body: OnEMI Technology Solutions, the parent company of digital lending platform Kissht, is considering another fundraise, just four months after its stock market debut in May.

The company’s board will meet on September 17 to consider raising funds through equity shares, warrants, convertible instruments or other eligible securities. The proposed fundraise could be carried out through a preferential issue, private placement or other permissible routes, according to a regulatory filing. The proposal will be subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.
The company, however, did not disclose the size of the proposed fundraise or the investors that may participate in the transaction.
The filing added that its trading window has been closed for designated persons and their immediate relatives and will remain shut until 48 hours after the board meeting outcome is announced.

The development comes months after OnEMI raised Rs 926 crore through its initial public offering. The issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 850 crore and an offer for sale of around Rs 76 crore by existing shareholders.

On the financial front, Kissht’s operating revenue grew 45% year-on-year to Rs 670 crore in Q1 FY27, while its profit rose 58% to Rs 95 crore. Its assets under management (AUM) increased 61% YoY to Rs 8,001 crore during the quarter.

Kissht made its stock market debut in May, with its shares listing at Rs 190 on the NSE and Rs 191 on the BSE, over 11% above the issue price of Rs 171. Since then, the stock has surged over 72% to around Rs 329, which puts the company’s market capitalisation at Rs 5,830 crore.

title: Exclusive: Fashion startup UniqYou raises seed round at Rs 64 Cr valuation
description: D2C fashion startup UniqYou has raised Rs 15.8 crore in a seed funding round led by Arkam Ventures and Antler. The round also saw participation
body: D2C fashion startup UniqYou has raised Rs 15.8 crore in a seed funding round led by Arkam Ventures and Antler. The round also saw participation from several angel investors.
The board at UniqYou approved the issuance of 37,487 CCPS at an issue price of Rs 4,215 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its regulatory filings.

Arkam Ventures invested Rs 9.3 crore in the round, followed by Antler with Rs 4.96 crore. Ankit Garg infused Rs 1 crore, while Abhishek Goyal, Chaitanya Ramalingegowda, Raveen Sastry, and Nandita Sinha also participated in the round.

A Moneycontrol report had earlier said that UniqYou was in talks to raise around Rs 12 crore ($1.3 million) in a funding round. Following the allotment, Arkam Ventures will hold a 14.93% stake in UniqYou, while Antler will own 7.96%. Abhishek Goyal and Chaitanya Ramalingegowda will hold 1.59% and 0.24%, respectively.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s valuation stood at around Rs 64 crore (approximately $6.8 million) post-money. The fresh proceeds will be used to meet the company’s working capital needs and general corporate purposes, as per the filings. Founded in 2026, UniqYou is a Bengaluru-based fashion startup focused on women’s fashion. The company is building a technology-led platform that leverages AI to identify emerging fashion trends and offer relevant products to consumers.

The fundraise comes amid continued investor interest in India’s fashion and apparel startup ecosystem. In 2025, The Bear House raised Rs 50 crore in a Series A round, while Snitch raised Rs 278.9 crore in a Series B round and Miraggio secured $6.5 million in Series A funding. The momentum continued in 2026, with MyDesignation raising Rs 40 crore in Series A funding and Alaya by Stage3 securing a seed round to scale its ethnic-wear business and AI capabilities. More recently, D2C fashion brand Theater raised Rs 75 crore in a Series A round led by Niveshaay.

title: Exclusive: PhysicsWallah founders, Udaan’s Sujeet Kumar to back Furnishka’s fresh fundraise
description: Furnishka is raising Rs 26.8 crore in an extended pre-Series A round, with PhysicsWallah and Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar among the investors
body: Furniture startup Furnishka is raising Rs 26.8 crore in an extended pre-Series A round, with PhysicsWallah founders Alakh Pandey and Prateek Boob, and Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar among the investors, according to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr.
The Bengaluru-based company has issued 3,183 preference shares at an issue price of Rs 84,157 per share to raise the capital.
The round saw participation from Beenext Asia, Bhaarath Sang, Onyx InVen, Amit Jain, Shantanu Jain, Manish Dugar, Mohit Gupta and Jnabiz Consulting,
Bhaarath Sang will the largest investor in the round, investing Rs 10.3 crore. Beenext Asia will invest Rs 3.35 crore, while Onyx InVen and Amit Jain will invest Rs 2.37 crore each.

Mohit Gupta and Jnabiz Consulting are investing around Rs 2 crore each, while Sujeet Kumar will invest around Rs 1 crore. Alakh Pandey and Prateek Boob will invest Rs 1.14 crore each. Shantanu Jain and Manish Dugar will invest Rs 94.3 lakh and Rs 15.1 lakh, respectively.

This seems to be part of a larger round. Most of the money mentioned above has hit the bank account, while some will follow soon. Based on the issue price and the company's share capital, Entrackr estimates Furnishka’s post-money valuation at around Rs 230 crore.

With this round, Furnishka has raised Rs 70 crore so far. The company had earlier raised Rs 27 crore in a pre-Series A round led by IndiaQuotient in October 2024. Sparrow Capital and angel investors, including Udaan co-founder Sujeet Kumar and Ramakant Sharma, also participated in that round.

Founded in 2023 by Ganesh Pawar, Furnishka operates an omnichannel furniture retail business, combining online sales with large-format offline stores. The company offers furniture across living room, dining room, and bedroom categories, with a focus on customisation and supply-chain efficiencies.

title: Fibe gets SEBI nod for Rs 750 Cr IPO
description: Digital consumer lending platform Fibe, operated by Social Worth Technologies, has received SEBI’s nod to proceed with its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
body: Digital consumer lending platform Fibe, operated by Social Worth Technologies, has received SEBI’s nod to proceed with its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

The IPO will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 750 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 4.01 crore equity shares by existing shareholders, according to the company’s draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).
SEBI has issued its final observations on the proposed IPO, allowing Fibe to move ahead with the public issue process.

The company plans to use the net proceeds from the fresh issue to fund investments in its material subsidiary, EarlySalary Services Pvt Ltd (ESPL), to augment its capital base and meet its onward lending requirements. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

The IPO-bound company reported Rs 1,585 crore in revenue from operations in FY26, up from Rs 1,209 crore in FY25. Its net profit more than doubled to Rs 257 crore from Rs 114 crore during the same period.

Interest on loans remained its largest revenue source, contributing nearly 65% of operating revenue, while fee and commission income stood at Rs 393.5 crore in FY26. Fibe also reported Rs 420 crore in impairment on financial instruments, including Rs 203 crore in loan write-offs.

Founded in 2015 by Akshay Mehrotra and Ashish Goyal, Fibe offers personal and purpose-led financing across areas including healthcare, education and solar rooftop installations. The company claims to have facilitated more than 9.8 million loans with cumulative disbursements exceeding Rs 48,000 crore.
Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, Axis Capital, DAM Capital Advisors and JM Financial are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

title: Teachers’ Venture Growth makes follow-on investment in Darwinbox
description: Darwinbox said it serves more than 1,400 companies and 4.5 million employees globally. The company has grown at a 70% CAGR over the past five years, with expansion across
body: Teachers’ Venture Growth (TVG), the late-stage venture and growth investment platform of Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, has made a follow-on investment in human capital management (HCM) platform Darwinbox.
This marks TVG’s second investment in Darwinbox after its initial investment in the company in 2025. The financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.
According to an ET report, the round is estimated to be around $40 million.

Founded in 2015 by Jayant Paleti, Chaitanya Peddi, Rohit Chennamaneni and Vineet Singh, Darwinbox offers a mobile-first, cloud-based HCM platform that enables organisations to manage the employee lifecycle, from hiring and onboarding to talent management and retention.
The company has continued to invest in its HCM product suite, with a focus on workflow automation, streamlined HR operations and personalised employee experiences.
In August, Darwinbox launched Darwinbox Cortex, an AI-native HCM platform. The product was launched with pilot customers including Fortune 1000 companies Visteon and Transcarent.

Cortex brings AI-driven intelligence, context and execution into Darwinbox’s platform and is being developed with technology partners including Microsoft, Slack and Glean. The platform extends AI capabilities to applications and workflows used by employees.

Darwinbox said it serves more than 1,400 companies and 4.5 million employees globally. The company has grown at a 70% CAGR over the past five years, with expansion across key markets including the US, Middle East, India and Southeast Asia.

title: AI interactive content startup Flam raises $40 Mn led by QED Investors
description: Founded in 2021 by Shourya Agarwal, Flam develops AI-powered interactive content for enterprises across use cases such as marketing, product visualisation, learning and
body: Bengaluru-based AI interactive content company Flam has raised $40 million in its Series B funding round led by QED Investors. The round also saw participation from Claypond Capital, Martin Chavez, Olivier Pomel, Venky Harinarayan and Shah Rukh Khan, along with existing investors RTP Global and Dovetail.
Flam will use the fresh capital to expand R&D across its AI models, broaden its product suite and scale enterprise sales globally.

Founded in 2021 by Shourya Agarwal, Malhar Patil, and Amit Gaiki, Flam develops AI-powered interactive content for enterprises across use cases such as marketing, product visualisation, learning and development, entertainment, fan engagement, customer support and sales. The company said it has onboarded more than 100 enterprise customers in the past six quarters, including Google, Reliance and Hyundai.

Flam currently holds more than 15 patents and offers three core formats. Its Flicks product enables interactive videos that can switch people, products or scenes during playback. The company said Flicks uses a patented compression algorithm and is delivered programmatically with a 50-millisecond time-to-first-buffer.

Its Forge editing model uses image references to modify specified elements, while Airboards provides high-fidelity 3D content through a camera interface with touch, voice and haptic interactions. Flam said its 3D streaming technology can load Airboards in 300 milliseconds without requiring users to install an app. Its Fable image-to-video model generates assets as native alpha-channel videos.

Flam is also developing Visual Agents, human-like characters designed to conduct conversations and take agentic actions. The technology combines Fantom for facial expression, identity preservation and motion transfer; Finesse for multilingual voice capabilities; and Falcon, a 26-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts large language model. The company said its pipeline can return an answer in under two seconds, with Falcon delivering a 30-millisecond time-to-first-token.
Headquartered in San Francisco, Flam has teams in India and Japan. The company said it has five AI models, more than 15 patents and over 100 enterprise customers globally.

title: Novastar Partners invests in AJVC to back pre-seed startups
description: According to Novastar, the investment will support AJVC’s continued deployment across India’s pre-seed ecosystem as the fund builds a platform for early-stage companies.
body: Novastar Partners, an India-focused private markets investment platform, has invested an undisclosed amount in A Junior VC (AJVC), an early-stage venture capital fund founded by Aviral Bhatnagar.
The investment is aimed at helping Novastar build a diversified portfolio of high-quality funds and businesses across India’s private markets, with a focus on technology and tech-enabled businesses.

According to Novastar, the investment will support AJVC’s continued deployment across India’s pre-seed ecosystem as the fund builds a platform for early-stage companies. It will also give Novastar exposure to companies at their earliest stages across sectors such as artificial intelligence, healthcare, deeptech, consumer technology and brands.
With a corpus of around Rs 165 crore, AJVC has backed more than 35 companies and plans to invest in over 85 companies over the fund’s life.

Novastar Partners was founded by Dhruv Jhunjhunwala and focuses on investing in India’s private markets. The firm invests in leading private equity and venture capital funds, alongside selective direct investments in private companies, particularly in technology and tech-enabled businesses.
AJVC is an early-stage VC fund focused on pre-seed investments in India. The fund claims to have developed a programmatic, technology-driven approach to supporting startups from their inception.

title: India’s wealthtech funding frenzy continues in 2026 as investment crosses $300 Mn
description: Indian wealthtech raised around $317 million across 26 deals in the first eight months of 2026. Funding activity was largely guided by smaller rounds, with only four transactions crossing the $30 million threshold
body: India’s wealthtech ecosystem is attracting stronger investor interest in 2026, with funding increasingly flowing towards platforms expanding beyond traditional broking and trading. Investors are showing greater appetite for digital wealth management, alternative investments, fixed income products and technology led advisory platforms, while a new crop of startups is targeting younger, first time investors. However, the sector remains largely concentrated in Tier 1 cities, with both wealthtech startups and their user base skewed towards major urban centres. This leaves sizable headroom for platforms to expand their reach and tap into India’s growing investor base across smaller cities and towns.

According to data compiled by Entrackr , wealthtech startups in India raised around $317 million across 26 deals in the first eight months of 2026. Funding activity was largely guided by smaller rounds, with only four transactions crossing the $30 million threshold. These included fundraises by Veriqus Group, Neo, Sahi, and Gurugram-based Centricity. Notably, none of the deals during the period exceeded $50 million, but this could change soon as Dale Vaz-led Sahi is reportedly in talks to raise a larger round of around $80 million.
Meanwhile, Dream Sports, the parent company of Dream11, shut down its wealth management platform Dream Money within a year of its launch, ending one of its diversification bets beyond online gaming.
Year-on-year funding trend

India’s wealthtech sector saw moderate funding activity in 2023. Startups raised around $55 million across 12 deals, with Neo’s $35 million round accounting for a significant share of the capital raised during the year.
Funding picked up sharply in 2024. Capital raised jumped more than 3.4X to $265 million across 26 deals, supported by several sizable rounds.
The momentum continued in 2025. Funding rose around 40% year-on-year to $369.34 million across 25 deals, while the number of transactions remained broadly stable.

In the first eight months of 2026, wealthtech startups raised around $303 million across 25 deals. The sector has already surpassed the funding recorded in 2024, despite the 2026 figure covering only eight months.

title: Moneyview cuts IPO fresh issue to Rs 750 Cr, investors trim OFS
description: The company has also reduced the offer-for-sale (OFS) component to around 10.04 crore shares from up to 13.61 crore shares proposed earlier.
body: Digital lending platform Moneyview has cut the size of its proposed initial public offering (IPO), reducing the fresh issue by half to Rs 750 crore from the Rs 1,500 crore proposed in its draft papers.
The company has also reduced the offer-for-sale (OFS) component to around 10.04 crore shares from up to 13.61 crore shares proposed earlier.
The revised IPO structure comes ahead of Moneyview’s public listing and follows the fintech company receiving approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).

The reduction in the fresh issue means Moneyview now plans to raise Rs 750 crore through the issue of new shares. The company had initially planned to use the Rs 1,500 crore proceeds towards growing its lending business, strengthening its technology infrastructure and meeting general corporate purposes.

With the OFS reduction, some existing investors have scaled back their planned stake sale. Investors including Accel, Tiger Global, Crimson Winter and Ribbit Capital have reduced their proposed stake sales, while the founders’ planned OFS remains unchanged, according to the revised IPO structure.

Moneyview had filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI in March 2026. The proposed issue at the time included a fresh issue of Rs 1,500 crore and an OFS of up to 13.61 crore shares. The company had also kept the option of a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 300 crore.

Founded by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview operates a digital lending and personal finance platform. The company offers personal loans and other financial products through its platform and works with lending partners.
The IPO size cut comes as a number of Indian fintech companies prepare to tap the public markets, with investors paying closer attention to profitability, growth and valuations.

title: Peak XV sells 1.47% stake in Groww for Rs 1,756 Cr via bulk deal
description: Peak XV Partners has offloaded a 1.47% stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of stockbroking platform Groww, through a bulk deal on Wednesday.
body: Peak XV Partners has offloaded a 1.47% stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of stockbroking platform Groww, through a bulk deal on Wednesday.
According to bulk deal data, Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1 sold 9.17 crore shares at an average price of Rs 191.49 apiece. The transaction was valued at around Rs 1,756 crore.

As of June 2026, Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1 held a 15.68% stake in Groww, which made it one of the company’s largest institutional shareholders. Based on the June shareholding, the latest sale represents nearly a tenth of its holding in the company.
The transaction comes less than a month after two of Groww’s early investors, Y Combinator and Ribbit Capital, pared their stakes through large open-market transactions.

In August, Y Combinator, through YC Holdings II, sold nearly 7.47 crore shares, or a 1.2% stake, for around Rs 1,435 crore . Later that month, Ribbit Capital offloaded 11.31 crore shares  for Rs 2,217 crore .

Together, Y Combinator and Ribbit Capital sold shares worth more than Rs 3,650 crore in August. Including Peak XV’s latest transaction, the three investors have offloaded Groww shares worth over Rs 5,400 crore since August.
Peak XV had also trimmed its holding in Groww earlier this year. In May, the investment firm sold 6.2 crore shares for around Rs 1,116 crore .
On the financial front, Groww recorded Rs 1,501 crore in operating revenue during Q1 FY27, a 66% year-on-year increase. Its net profit nearly doubled to Rs 735 crore during the same period.

title: Zeropearl VC leads Rs 11.4 Cr seed round in aesthetic surgery platform TRUE ARTIS
description: TRUE ARTIS also works with a multidisciplinary network of full-time and visiting plastic surgeons, allowing patients to access multiple specialists through a single p
body: Integrated aesthetic surgery platform TRUE ARTIS has raised Rs 11.4 crore in a seed funding round led by Zeropearl VC. The round also saw participation from Eleven, a diversified business group of Sunil Sachdeva, co-founder of Medanta, and a group of angel investors.

The round saw participation from operators and healthcare investors including Arjun Vaidya, Dhruv Joshi, Ambarish Gupta and Vivek Lohcheb, CBO of PhonePe, along with former senior executives from Airtel and OYO.

The fresh funds will be used to open two new centres in Delhi NCR over the next six to eight months, strengthen its surgical and recovery capabilities, expand its network of plastic and aesthetic surgeons, and enhance its technology and patient-care systems, TRUE ARTIS said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2025 by Ankit Joshi and Sandeep Upadhyay, TRUE ARTIS is an integrated aesthetic surgery platform focused on personalised aesthetic care. The startup brings together plastic and aesthetic surgeons, surgical infrastructure, hospital-grade safety protocols, dedicated recovery facilities and a privacy-focused patient experience.

TRUE ARTIS offers services across facial aesthetics, breast procedures, body contouring, hair restoration and non-surgical treatments. Its in-house technology platform manages the patient journey from enquiry and consultation through surgery and recovery.

The company claims to have served more than 10,000 clients and completed over 400 surgeries in the past nine months. Its centres feature operating theatres, surgical and medical equipment, dedicated recovery facilities, ICU backup and private patient suites.

TRUE ARTIS also works with a multidisciplinary network of full-time and visiting plastic surgeons, allowing patients to access multiple specialists through a single platform. It currently operates two centres in Delhi and Gurgaon.

The startup works with around 20 plastic surgeons across Delhi NCR and reports a 98% client satisfaction rate. It said its first centre has reached EBITDA break-even, while revenue is growing at a double-digit rate month-on-month.

title: Semiconductor verification startup VerifAIX raises $5 Mn in seed round
description: VerifAIX integrates specification-to-RTL reasoning, automated decomposition and abstraction, and coordinated formal and simulation verification to tackle complex designs
body: AI-native semiconductor verification startup VerifAIX has raised $5 million in a seed funding round co-led by Endiya Partners and Bluehill VC.
The proceeds will be used for product development, customer deployments and expansion of its engineering teams across the US, India and Israel, VerifAIX said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by Madhulima Tewari, Kenneth Roe and Avner Landver, VerifAIX is building an AI-native verification platform for semiconductor design. It helps engineering teams verify increasingly complex chips with greater speed and rigor.

VerifAIX’s platform combines AI with formal methods to create a verification trust layer that connects design specifications, RTL and verification assets. This enables traceable verification from design intent to closure.

The startup’s “Formal Brain” creates a mathematically grounded understanding of a design and its intended behaviour. It reasons across specifications, RTL and verification assets to identify inconsistencies and gaps, and uses this foundation for verification planning, formal analysis, simulation, coverage, debug and verification closure.

VerifAIX integrates specification-to-RTL reasoning, automated decomposition and abstraction, and coordinated formal and simulation verification to tackle complex designs while maintaining traceability to design intent. It targets custom-silicon developers, including semiconductor and IP companies, processor and AI accelerator developers, hyperscalers and systems companies.
India’s semiconductor startup ecosystem is also seeing the emergence of AI-native verification platforms alongside the broader chip design boom.

Chennai-based deep-tech startup Vyoma Systems, incubated at IIT Madras Pravartak, is working on AI-driven pre-silicon verification through its UpTickPro platform. The platform integrates functional verification, FPGA validation, software bring-up and security analysis.

title: Fashion discovery platform Slayd raises pre-seed funding led by ajvc
description: Gurugram-based fashion discovery platform Slayd has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by ajvc, an early-stage fund founded by Aviral Bhatnagar. Snippets
body: Gurugram-based fashion discovery platform Slayd has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by ajvc, an early-stage fund founded by Aviral Bhatnagar.
The round values the startup at around Rs 16.66 crore post-money. Slayd will use the funds to expand its team and scale its private-label business, Slayd Originals.

Founded in 2025 by IIT Roorkee alumni Sparsh Jain, Harsh Porwal and Kumar Prasang, Slayd aggregates fashion products from more than 300 marketplaces and D2C brands. The platform adds around 1 lakh new products every month and uses a proprietary model that evaluates products across more than eight signals to identify emerging trends.

The startup claims to have crossed 200,000 users, with over 40% month-one retention. Its power users average more than 10 sessions per month, while the platform currently identifies over 2,000 products as emerging hotsellers.
Slayd also curates products into theme-based collections and personalised feeds, allowing users to discover products across multiple fashion platforms.

The company has also entered the private-label segment with Slayd Originals, which was launched in beta earlier this year. The brand currently generates around 1,000 orders per month, according to the startup.

“India sees more than 1 lakh new apparel designs launched every month across hundreds of fragmented e-commerce platforms. Yet shoppers still have to navigate multiple platforms to discover what's actually trending. Slayd is building the discovery layer for this fragmented market,” said cofounder Sparsh Jain.
The startup said its product and trend data is also used to identify styles that could be developed under Slayd Originals.

title: Beauty quick commerce startup Firi raises $3 Mn led by 360 ONE Asset
description: Gurugram-based beauty and personal care quick commerce startup Firi has raised $3 million in a funding round led by 360 ONE Asset. Snippets.
body: Gurugram-based beauty and personal care quick commerce startup Firi has raised $3 million in a funding round led by 360 ONE Asset.
The round also saw participation from Better Capital, CRED founder Kunal Shah and other angel investors.
The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand into makeup, fragrances and other beauty categories. It also plans to add more dark stores in Gurugram before expanding to other cities.

Founded in 2026 by former Uber India executives Vivek Madani and Karishma Rathaur, Firi operates a curated marketplace for beauty and personal care products. The startup uses AI to analyse product reviews and other information before listing products on its platform.

Firi claims to have analysed more than 50 million reviews and shortlisted around 3,000 products from the global beauty market. It currently offers skincare, haircare and body care products, with deliveries in parts of Gurugram taking as little as nine minutes.
Firi started its pilot in January 2026 and began full operations in September 2026.

title: Kissht parent OnEMI’s board approves Rs 832 Cr fundraise
description: OnEMI Technology Solutions, the parent company of digital lending platform Kissht, has approved a fundraise of up to Rs 832.2 crore through a preferential issue.
body: OnEMI Technology Solutions, the parent company of digital lending platform Kissht, has approved a fundraise of up to Rs 832.2 crore through a preferential issue, according to its exchange filing.

The company’s board approved the issuance of up to 2.64 crore equity shares at an issue price of Rs 314.11 apiece to 34 investors from the non-promoter category. The proposed transaction is subject to shareholder and other regulatory approvals.

The round will see participation from several domestic and global institutional investors, including Axis Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), WhiteOak, 360 One, Groww Mutual Fund and Bandhan Mutual Fund and others.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen Kissht’s capital position and support the expansion of its lending business, technology capabilities and product offerings. The company is also targeting multiple credit rating upgrades over the next two years, which it expects could lower borrowing costs, diversify its funding sources and increase its lending capacity.
OnEMI has scheduled an extraordinary general meeting on October 14 to seek shareholder approval for the preferential issue.

The fundraise comes just four months after OnEMI raised Rs 926 crore through its IPO. The public issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 850 crore and an offer for sale of around Rs 76 crore by existing shareholders.

On the financial front, Kissht’s operating revenue rose 45% year-on-year to Rs 670 crore in Q1 FY27, while its profit increased 58% to Rs 95 crore. Its assets under management grew 61% to Rs 8,001 crore during the quarter.

Kissht made its stock market debut in May, with its shares listing at Rs 190 on the NSE, over 11% above the issue price of Rs 171. The stock has since more than doubled from its issue price and closed Thursday’s session at around Rs 360 per share, which puts the company’s market capitalisation at Rs 6,381 crore.

title: Baby-focused quick commerce startup Kiddo raises Rs 12.5 Cr led by Campus Fund
description: Kiddo claims to have curated more than 30,000 SKUs across essentials, fashion and other categories since inception. It targets high-income households and currently
body: Baby-focused quick commerce startup Kiddo has raised Rs 12.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Campus Fund, with participation from a group of strategic angels.
The fresh funds will be used for customer acquisition, dark store expansion across Delhi NCR, technology and product development, and team building, Kiddo said in a press release.
Launched last year by Ankit Kawatra, Kiddo delivers baby care and parenting essentials within minutes. The startup combines quick delivery with life-stage based product recommendations for parents.
According to a market report, India’s baby care market reached $31 billion in 2022 and is projected to reach $56 billion by 2029, growing at a CAGR of 13% to 14%.

Kiddo claims to have curated more than 30,000 SKUs across essentials, fashion and other categories since inception. It targets high-income households and currently operates in Delhi NCR, with plans to expand its dark store network by the end of the year. The company also claims its blended gross margin is higher than the typical margins of horizontal grocery quick commerce players.
Kiddo competes with players such as FirstCry, AllThingsBaby and OZi in the baby and kids’ commerce segment.

Gurugram-based OZi raised $3.3 million in seed funding from Blume Ventures in October last year and later secured $6.2 million in a Series A round led by RTP Global in March this year. The platform offers more than 15,000 products with delivery within 60 minutes.

Bengaluru-based Peeko, another babycare-focused quick commerce platform, raised $3.2 million from Stellaris Venture Partners in August last year and later secured Rs 67.4 crore in a Series A round led by Chiratae Ventures in August 2026. It offers products across baby apparel, toys, gear and consumables.

title: Info Edge leads Rs 8.9 Cr seed round in Factrika
description: The Delhi-based startup claims to have more than 10,000 registered workers across over 20 skill categories. It also said deployment hours are growing 50% to 70% month on
body: On-demand industrial workforce platform Factrika has raised Rs 8.9 crore in a seed funding round led by Info Edge.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen its team, enhance its technology and expand into more industrial clusters across India, Factrika said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Kshitij Puri and Gaurav Asthana, Factrika is building a platform that connects manufacturers with skilled and verified factory workers. The platform claims to deploy workers within two hours and maintain a show-up rate of over 90%. Its clients include Lenskart, Asahi India Glass and Jubilant Foods.

Factrika said Indian factories face a daily worker shortage of 20% to 25%, partly due to fragmented contractor-led staffing models. The startup matches manufacturers with workers based on skills and availability. Workers can accept shifts digitally, while Factrika manages attendance and payments and maintains a digital work record.

The Delhi-based startup claims to have more than 10,000 registered workers across over 20 skill categories. It also said deployment hours are growing 50% to 70% month on month. Its clients include Lenskart, Munjal Kiriu, Asahi India Glass, Jubilant Foods and Epack Durables. Factrika claims workers can increase their earnings by 20% to 30% through skill progression.
The startup initially operates across Bhiwadi, Manesar, Bawal, Noida and Bahadurgarh, as it targets what it estimates to be a $23 Bn manufacturing workforce opportunity in India.

The industrial workforce segment has seen the emergence of platforms using mobile-based hiring, worker verification, digital matching and workforce management tools to connect enterprises with frontline workers.

WorkIndia raised Rs 97 crore in a Series B round led by Aavishkaar Capital in December last year, with participation from BEENEXT. The company said the funding would be used to strengthen its technology, improve job matching and expand into high-demand regions.

title: Avaana Capital leads Rs 43 Cr pre-Series A round in deeptech company DheyaTech
description: DheyaTech has developed an adaptive Engine Control Unit (ECU) and is working on fuel flexible and hydrogen based propulsion and power generation technologies. Its p
body: Bengaluru-based deeptech company DheyaTech has raised Rs 43 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Avaana Capital, with participation from Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing.

The fresh capital will be used to scale production, set up an integrated testing facility for its gas turbine engines and work with domestic and global customers to accelerate deployment timelines, DheyaTech said in a press release.

Founded in 2018 by Gurushankara K C, Abhinav Alva and Chetan Kumar, DheyaTech develops micro gas turbine engines and energy systems for aerospace and power generation applications. Its engine portfolio spans 20 kgf to 400 kgf of thrust, targeting applications across aerial mobility, advanced aerial platforms and distributed power systems.
The company said its gas turbines are entering commercial deployment, with flight trials planned for Q4 2026. It has also received confirmed orders from Indian and global OEMs.

DheyaTech has developed an adaptive Engine Control Unit (ECU) and is working on fuel flexible and hydrogen based propulsion and power generation technologies. Its portfolio includes a hydrogen blower and a hydrogen based flexi fuel combustor for its 60 kW flexi fuel turbogenerator.
The company said its platform approach allows it to develop engines across multiple thrust categories and applications.

The funding comes as other Indian startups work on gas turbine and propulsion technologies. Bengaluru based Nabhdrishti Aerospace, which develops fuel flexible micro gas turbines for aviation, UAVs and power generation, raised $3 million in a seed round led by Accel in March 2025, following a Rs 3 crore pre seed round led by IIMA Ventures.

LAT Aerospace, founded by Surobhi Das and Deepinder Goyal, is developing lightweight gas turbine engines for its STOL aircraft programme, with Goyal having invested $20 million in the venture. Hyderabad based Paninian unveiled its 4.5 kN Yantur turbofan programme in 2026 for autonomous aerospace and defence platforms.

title: Laundry and home cleaning brand Ecosys raises Rs 5 Cr in pre-Series A round
description: The Mumbai-based company’s product portfolio includes eco-friendly laundry detergent pods, glass cleaners, floor cleaners, bathroom cleaners and kitchen and utensil spr
body: Laundry and home cleaning brand Ecosys has raised Rs 5 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by GVFL Prarambh Fund, with participation from Proteus Partners, backed by operator-investors Puru Gupta and Sreejith Moolayil. The latest round takes Ecosys’ total funding raised to Rs 7.94 crore.
The company said in a press release that it will use the funds to build the brand, expand its digital reach and develop new formats across laundry and home cleaning.

Founded in 2017 by Sumit Goyal and Chirag Dangi, Ecosys offers laundry pods made with water-soluble PVA film. Its 20-ml pods combine detergent, fabric softener and stain remover in a single pre-measured dose for top-load and front-load washing machines.

Mumbai-based Ecosys sells its products through quick-commerce and e-commerce platforms. The company is focused on increasing the adoption of laundry pods as an alternative to conventional powder and liquid detergents.
According to market research cited by the company, India’s household cleaners market is growing at nearly 14% annually, more than twice the global growth rate.

The laundry and home cleaning segment has also seen funding activity from brands such as Koparo, which raised Rs 14.5 crore in an extended pre-Series A round last year, and Cleevo, which secured $1 million in a seed round. Beco raised $10 million from Tanglin Venture Partners, while Scrubsy raised Rs 27 crore from V3 Ventures in August this year.

title: PB Fintech to acquire remaining 20% stake in MyLoancare, invests Rs 10 Cr in PB Wheels
body: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, has received in-principle approval to acquire the remaining 20% stake in its subsidiary MyLoancare Ventures Pvt Ltd for up to Rs 5 crore, according  to its exchange filing,
Following the acquisition, MyLoancare will become a wholly owned subsidiary of PB Fintech. The transaction will be completed through cash consideration and is expected to close by March 31, 2027.
The final acquisition price will be determined based on the valuation report and is subject to the approval of the M&A and Investment Committee and acceptance by the selling shareholders.

Incorporated in 2013, MyLoancare is an RBI-registered NBFC engaged in digital lending technology, retail loan aggregation, and financial product distribution. The company’s turnover plunged 90.6% to Rs 82 lakh in FY26, from Rs 8.7 crore in FY24.

Separately, PB Fintech has approved capital infusions of up to Rs 10 crore in PB Wheels and Rs 1 crore in PB Financial Account Aggregator, both wholly owned subsidiaries. The funds will support working capital and operating expenses at PB Wheels, and operating expenses and RBI-mandated capital requirements at PB Financial Account Aggregator.

On the financial front,PB Fintech  reported a 92% YoY jump in profit after tax to Rs 163 crore in Q1 FY27. Its operating revenue grew 40% YoY to Rs 1,888 crore, from Rs 1,348 crore in the year-ago quarter.

title: Enlight Metals raises $1.5 Mn at $10 Mn valuation from Exar North Group
description: New Delhi-based metal procurement platform Enlight Metals has raised $1.5 million from US-based investment firm Exar North Group at a valuation of $10 million. Snippets
body: New Delhi-based metal procurement platform Enlight Metals has raised $1.5 million from US-based investment firm Exar North Group at a valuation of $10 million.
The proceeds will be used to develop its Agentic AI-enabled procurement platform, strengthen technology infrastructure and expand its operations across the metal procurement ecosystem.

Enlight Metals claims its AI-led platform has reduced end-to-end transaction processing time by 75%, inventory costs by 30% and operational overhead by 60%. It has also reduced supplier matching time from 5–7 hours to less than three minutes.

The company currently operates facilities in Pune, Mumbai and Raipur and plans to expand to Ahmedabad and Indore. It will also add new dark stores and focus on customer acquisition and geographic expansion.

Enlight Metals is targeting around Rs 1,200 crore in revenue in the next financial year. The company plans to achieve this through expansion and increased use of AI across its procurement and operational processes.

Founded to combine steel sourcing and distribution with technology, Enlight Metals said the partnership with Exar North will provide capital, technology and operational support as it scales. The company will also focus on advancing its Agentic AI capabilities and expanding its technology platform.

title: NSE raises Rs 6,746 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
description: The National Stock Exchange has raised Rs 6,746 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), which opens for public subscription today.
body: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has raised Rs 6,746 crore from anchor investors ahead of its much-awaited initial public offering (IPO), which opens for public subscription today (September 17).
The exchange allotted 3.78 crore equity shares to 189 anchor investors at Rs 1,785 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band.

The anchor book saw participation from several large domestic and global investors, including Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), GIC Singapore, Fidelity, Societe Generale and others.

LIC emerged as the largest single anchor investor, picking up shares worth around Rs 400 crore. The Government Pension Fund Global invested about Rs 250 crore, while Societe Generale’s offshore desk bought shares worth nearly Rs 316 crore.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) invested around Rs 2,883 crore, accounting for nearly 43% of the anchor book. Domestic investors contributed around Rs 3,588 crore, or 53% of the allocation. The domestic participation included more than 25 mutual funds and 11 large insurance and pension funds.
The anchor book attracted bids worth nearly Rs 1.2 lakh crore, around 20 times the amount allocated to anchor investors, according to market sources.

NSE has set a price band of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share for its IPO, which will remain open until September 21. The issue is entirely an offer for sale (OFS), meaning NSE will not receive any fresh capital from the IPO. Instead, existing shareholders will sell their shares.
The exchange is looking to raise around Rs 22,569 crore through the IPO, making it one of India's largest public issues.

title: Inside Yulu’s Series C: funding breakup, valuation, captable
description: Electric mobility-as-a-service (MaaS) platform Yulu recently raised $93 million in its Series C round through a mix of debt and equity. The round comprised $63 million
body: Electric mobility-as-a-service (MaaS) platform Yulu recently raised $93 million in its Series C round through a mix of debt and equity. The round comprised $63 million in equity led by GEF Capital Partners, with participation from One Planet Partners, and $30 million in debt.
Entrackr examined Yulu's regulatory filings to decode the company's latest funding round, updated captable, and post-money valuation.

According to the company’s regulatory filings accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC),Yulu board approved 200 equity shares and 55,200 Series C compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 82,615 per share to raise Rs 456 crore.

Separately, the company issued 10,770 Series C1 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 84,291 to raise Rs 91 crore. Combined, Yulu raised around Rs 547 crore through the equity funding.
According to the filings, the proposed debt component has yet to be received, while the transaction also involves a secondary component.
GEF Capital Partners led the series C round with an investment of Rs 456 crore and remaining amount infused by One Planet Partners Rs 91 crore.

As per the filing, Yulu plans to deploy the fresh capital to strengthen its capital base, support operations and strategic initiatives, and fuel future growth. The company aims to quadruple its active fleet to 200,000 electric vehicles over the next two years, expand into new urban mobility use cases, and support its potential public market listing plans.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, Yulu’s post-money valuation stood at around $180–200 million.

title: Curefoods reports Rs 916 Cr revenue and Rs 192 Cr loss in FY26
description: Cloud kitchen company Curefoods’ revenue grew 23% to Rs 916 crore in FY26, while its net loss widened to Rs 192 crore despite improved EBITDA margins.
body: Curefoods grew its operating revenue 23% to Rs 916 crore in FY26, but the growth came with a wider net loss of Rs 192 crore. The Ankit Nagori-led cloud kitchen company had recently put its Rs 800 crore IPO plans on hold amid market volatility, making its latest financial performance particularly relevant. While EBITDA losses narrowed and margins improved, higher depreciation and finance costs continued to weigh on profitability.
Curefoods’ revenue from operations increased to Rs 916.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 745.8 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies show.

Curefoods operates a multi-brand food business across healthy meals, biryani, pizza, desserts and South Indian cuisine. Its portfolio includes EatFit, Sharief Bhai Biryani, OLIO, Arambam, Krispy Kreme, Nomad Pizza, CakeZone and Frozen Bottle. It runs these brands through a shared network of 281 cloud kitchens, 99 kiosks and 122 restaurants.

Sales of food and other products accounted for 99% of operating revenue and increased 23% to Rs 908.4 crore during the year. Revenue from services and other operating activities, including franchisee fees contributed the remaining Rs 7.8 crore.
India remained Curefoods’ core market, with Rs 893.3 crore revenue in FY26, while collection from overseas markets soared 4X to Rs 22.85 crore.
The company also earned Rs 18.6 crore from non-operating activities, including interest income and gains on mutual funds, which took its total income to Rs 934.8 crore in the last fiscal year.

On the cost side, material expenses remained the largest cost centre and increased 13.5% to Rs 310.4 crore. Employee benefit expenses rose 19% to Rs 213.9 crore, which included Rs 33 crore in ESOP expenses.

Commission costs increased 22% to Rs 166.8 crore, while depreciation and amortisation expenses rose 24% to Rs 100.6 crore. Meanwhile, advertising and promotional expenses declined 10% to Rs 79 crore during the year.

title: Physioplus Healthcare raises seed round at $800K valuation
description: The startup said its platform combines digital practice management, patient data and remote monitoring to support physiotherapy and rehabilitation. Its services cover c
body: Physioplus Healthcare, a digital physiotherapy platform, has raised a strategic seed investment from HBF India at a valuation of $800K.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen its technology platform, expand its network and increase its presence across India, Physioplus Healthcare said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2022 by Samit Saxena, Jaswant Singh and Madhukar Pareek, Jaipur-based Physioplus Healthcare connects patients with certified physiotherapists through its platform. It offers physiotherapy discovery, consultations, patient assessments, clinical documentation and technology-enabled monitoring.

The startup said its platform combines digital practice management, patient data and remote monitoring to support physiotherapy and rehabilitation. Its services cover chronic pain, musculoskeletal conditions, sports injuries and post-surgery rehabilitation.

The company operates in a segment that includes digital and technology-enabled physiotherapy platforms. FlexifyMe raised $2.4 million in a pre-Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures and Signal Ventures last year to scale its online physiotherapy platform. Stance Health raised $1 million in pre-seed funding in 2025 to expand its technology-enabled musculoskeletal care model, while Rebee Health secured investment from 1337 Ventures in 2025 to expand its wearable sensor-based digital physiotherapy system.

title: Exclusive: Jar raises small fresh funding from Unitary Fund
description: Jar had been struggling to raise a fresh round despite discussions with several investors, including WestBridge. , the Bengaluru-based firm has now secured a lifeline
body: According to the company’s regulatory filings, Jar’s board approved the allotment of 1,70,589 Series B2 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,700 per share. Unitary Fund invested the entire Rs 29 crore in the round.
The company plans to use the fresh funds to meet its working capital requirements and for general corporate purposes, as per the filings.

The fresh capital comes as Jar has been in talks to raise $100 million from investors, including WestBridge Capital. Sources said discussions with WestBridge and other potential investors appear to have fizzled out. However, sources assert that the company has been operating profitably for the past year.

The funding also comes amid regulatory scrutiny of the digital gold savings sector. While Jar and other digital gold savings platforms do not fall under the regulatory ambit of SEBI, Bengaluru Police registered an FIR against the company over allegations of unauthorised collection of money from users against digital gold without the required regulatory approvals.
The Karnataka High Court refused to quash the FIR and allowed the investigation to continue.

Sources said regulatory concerns have made investors more cautious about backing digital gold savings platforms. Following the FIR against Jar, larger fintech players such as GPay, PhonePe and Paytm are also not promoting digital gold in the way they used to.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, Jar’s post-money valuation stood at around Rs 3,155 crore in this round, 23% higher than Rs 2,565 crore in its previous round.

Jar operates a savings and investment platform that allows users to automate savings and invest in digital gold. The company has also expanded into jewellery through its Nek vertical and insurance offerings. Sources said its D2C jewellery brand has been scaling rapidly.

title: Beauty and body care brand MoroMaa raises Rs 1.5 Cr from AJ VC for 9% stake
description: Mumbai-based beauty, lifestyle and body care brand MoroMaa has raised Rs 1.5 crore from Aviral Bhatnagar of AJ VC for a 9% equity stake. Snippets
body: Mumbai-based beauty, lifestyle and body care brand MoroMaa has raised Rs 1.5 crore from Aviral Bhatnagar of AJ VC for a 9% equity stake.

Founded by Soundous Moufakir, MoroMaa was launched in June 2026, and is building what it calls M Beauty, a Moroccan beauty category in India. The brand uses Moroccan ingredients sourced directly from Morocco and aims to bring Moroccan beauty practices to Indian consumers.

The funding comes within a few months of the brand’s launch. MoroMaa claims two of its products sold out within the first two months of operations. The company plans to use the capital to expand its product portfolio, strengthen distribution and increase its reach in India.
Soundous is the solo founder and CEO of MoroMaa. She has a background in finance and entertainment. MoroMaa focuses on artists and Moroccan ingredients and beauty traditions.
With the new investment, MoroMaa plans to focus on product development, distribution and building awareness around Moroccan beauty in India.

title: Rebel Foods reports Rs 1,952 Cr revenue in FY26, losses narrow 16%
description: Rebel Foods’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 1,951.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,617.4 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statements filed with the RoC.
body: Cloud kitchen company Rebel Foods improved its financial performance in FY26 as revenue growth accelerated and losses narrowed. The company’s operating revenue rose 21% year-on-year, while its net loss declined 16% to Rs 281.8 crore during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Rebel Foods’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 1,951.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,617.4 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Rebel Foods operates cloud kitchen brands such as Faasos, Behrouz Biryani, The Good Bowl, LunchBox, Oven Story Pizza and The Biryani Life. The company earns primarily from the sale of food products through its own brands, while commission and franchise income account for a small part of the business.

Revenue from the sale of goods rose 21% to Rs 1,891.8 crore in FY26 and contributed nearly 97% of its operating revenue. Franchise income increased 10% to Rs 15.6 crore, while commission income fell 7% to Rs 17.1 crore. Other operating income, including delivery services stood at Rs 27 crore during the year.

India remained Rebel Foods’ largest market, contributing 85.5% of its operating revenue in FY26. Revenue from India rose 18% to Rs 1,667.7 crore, while revenue from the rest of the world grew 39% to Rs 283.8 crore.
The company earned Rs 43.3 crore from non-operating activities, including interest income and gains on financial assets. This took its total income to Rs 1,994.9 crore in FY26.
On the cost side, the cost of materials remained its largest expense and rose 16% to Rs 784.4 crore. It accounted for nearly 35% of the company’s total expenditure.

Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 412.3 crore, while brokerage and commission costs surged 31% to Rs 317.7 crore. Advertising expenditure rose 26% to Rs 193.9 crore, while depreciation and amortisation costs stood at Rs 153.5 crore. Other expenses, including outsourced delivery, legal and professional fees, and power and fuel costs added another Rs 404.2 crore.

title: Exclusive: Disha (formerly Curelink) raises Series A led by General Catalyst
description: Disha (formerly Curelink), an AI-powered health coaching platform offering personalised diet, has raised Rs 43.88 crore in a Series A round led by General Catalyst
body: Disha (formerly Curelink), an AI-powered health coaching platform offering personalised diet, fitness and chronic-care support, has raised Rs 43.88 crore in a Series A round led by General Catalyst, with participation from existing investor Elevation Capital. The company had raised $3.5 million (about Rs 26 crore) in a seed round led by Elevation Capital and Venture Highway. According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , Disha’s board has approved the issuance of 12,309 Series A CCPS at an issue price of Rs 35,643.64 per share to raise the aforementioned amount.
General Catalyst led the round with an investment of Rs 38.20 crore, followed by Elevation Capital with Rs 5.20 crore and Flamel Performing Creatives Private Limited with Rs 48 lakh.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, Disha’s post-money valuation increased 52% to around Rs 288 crore from Rs 190 crore in the previous round. The fresh capital will be used to meet working capital requirements, develop and enhance its AI models and technology platform, expand its business and operations, strengthen its capital base, and fund general corporate purposes, the filings indicate.

Disha is an AI-powered health coaching platform by Curelink, offering personalised diet, fitness and chronic-care support across 15 conditions in Hindi, English and Hinglish, with 24×7 coaching. It claims 70 lakh sign-ups, 3 lakh active users and 1.4 crore messages.

Following the latest allotment, Aman Singla and Divyansh Jain hold the largest stakes in Disha at 31.10% each. General Catalyst holds 13.33%, followed by Elevation Capital at 9.96% and the ESOP pool at 9.02%. Venture Highway owns 4.07%, while Flamel Performing Creatives holds 0.17%.
Its angel investors Vijay Shekhar Sharma (Founder & CEO of Paytm), Ankush Sachdeva (Cofounder & CEO of ShareChat), and Digital Sparrow Capital each hold around 0.16% in the company.

The company is yet to report its FY26 numbers. Disha’s revenue doubled to Rs 4.91 crore in FY25 from Rs 2.47 crore in FY24, while its loss narrowed 22.5% to Rs 4.45 crore from Rs 5.74 crore during the same period.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Sep 14 - Sep 19]
description: This week, 17 Indian startups raised $61.8 million across one growth-stage deal, 14 early-stage deals, and two undisclosed rounds. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 17 Indian startups raised $61.8 million across one growth-stage deal, 14 early-stage deals, and two undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 15 key appointments and one merger and acquisition.
In contrast, 23 startups had collectively secured about $356.8 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised $40 million across only 1 deal this week. Bengaluru-based AI interactive content startup Flam has raised $40 million in a Series B round led by QED Investors. The round also saw participation from Claypond Capital, Martin Chavez, Olivier Pomel, Venky Harinarayan and Shah Rukh Khan, alongside existing investors RTP Global and Dovetail.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $21.8 million across 14 deals this week. AI-native semiconductor verification startup VerifAIX raised $5 million in a seed round co-led by Endiya Partners and Bluehill VC, while deeptech startup DheyaTech secured Rs 43 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Avaana Capital. Gurugram-based beauty quick commerce startup Firi also raised $3 million in a round led by 360 ONE Asset.

D2C fashion startup UniqYou raised Rs 15.8 crore in a seed round led by Arkam Ventures and Antler. Metal procurement platform Enlight Metals secured $1.5 million from Exar North Group at a $10 million valuation, while aesthetic surgery platform TRUE ARTIS raised Rs 11.4 crore in a seed round led by Zeropearl VC.
Other funded startups included baby-focused quick commerce platform Kiddo, gaming startup 1312 Interactive, industrial workforce platform Factrika, and five others.

title: AceVector files RHP for Rs 287 Cr fresh issue, turns free cash flow positive in FY26
description: SoftBank-backed AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal and Unicommerce, has filed its RHP with SEBI for an IPO comprising a Rs 287 crore fresh issue,.
body: SoftBank-backed AceVector, the parent company of Snapdeal and Unicommerce, has filed its red herring prospectus (RHP) with SEBI for an IPO comprising a Rs 287 crore fresh issue, along with an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.
Under the IPO, AceVector will raise Rs 287 crore through a fresh issue, while existing shareholders will sell up to 4.12 crore shares through an offer for sale (OFS).

Starfish I Pte. Ltd., the promoter selling shareholder, will account for the largest portion of the OFS, offering up to 2.76 crore shares, or 66.9% of the total shares on offer. Meanwhile, three Nexus entities — Nexus India Direct Investments II, Nexus Opportunity Fund and Nexus Ventures III  will collectively offer 86.96 lakh shares, accounting for around 21% of the OFS.

Its co-founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, who together hold a 33.99% stake directly and through related entities, will not participate in the OFS. Existing investors, including SoftBank and Foxconn, will also sell a small portion of their holdings.
The IPO comes as AceVector has made progress on its financial performance and turned free cash flow positive in FY26.

The company generated adjusted free cash flow from operations of Rs 10.82 crore in FY26, compared with a negative position in the previous year. Its operating revenue also grew 29% to Rs 510.38 crore in FY26 from Rs 395.02 crore in FY25.

AceVector also significantly reduced its operating losses during the year. Its adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed 59% to Rs 15.94 crore in FY26 from Rs 39.16 crore in FY25. The adjusted EBITDA margin consequently improved to -3.12% from -9.91% during the same period.
AceVector operates two key businesses, Snapdeal, its value-focused ecommerce marketplace, and Unicommerce, an ecommerce enablement SaaS platform.

title: Virat Kohli-backed Wrogn posts Rs 244 Cr revenue in FY26, losses widen 17%
description: Virat Kohli-backed menswear brand Wrogn recorded modest revenue growth of 9% to Rs 244 crore in FY26, while its losses widened further during the fiscal year.
body: Virat Kohli-backed menswear brand Wrogn recorded modest revenue growth of 9% to Rs 244 crore in FY26, far behind newer brand Snitch and rival Rare Rabbit, which reported revenue of Rs 900 crore and Rs 1,100 crore, respectively. Wrogn's losses also widened during the fiscal year, adding to its profitability challenges.
For context, Wrogn had witnessed a 9% decline in operating revenue to Rs 223 crore in FY25.

Founded in 2014, Wrogn, operated by Universal Sportsbiz Private Limited (USPL), offers casual menswear, including T-shirts, shirts, jeans and accessories. The Bengaluru-based company has received backing from investors such as Virat Kohli, Accel and Aditya Birla and sells its products through online marketplaces and offline retail channels.

Sales of these products remained Wrogn’s primary source of revenue. The company also earned Rs 10.17 crore from non-operating activities, including interest on deposits and gains on financial assets, taking its total income to Rs 254 crore in FY26 from Rs 232 crore in FY25.

For the fashion brand, cost of materials remained Wrogn's largest expense, accounting for 35% of its total expenditure. However, the cost declined 5% to Rs 119.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 125.7 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses increased 14% to Rs 44.2 crore.

Marketing expenditure surged 44% to Rs 57.8 crore in FY26, while commission costs rose 6% to Rs 42.1 crore. Brand consultancy charges more than doubled to Rs 19.7 crore, while other expenses, including depreciation & amortization expenses, finance cost stood added another Rs 78.6 crore.
Overall, Wrogn's total expenditure increased 9.5% to Rs 342.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 312.6 crore in FY25.

Higher marketing and brand consultancy expenses weighed on Wrogn's profitability, with its loss widening 17% to Rs 88.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 75.5 crore in FY25. Despite the wider loss, its EBITDA margin improved to negative 27.6% from negative 30.8% in the preceding fiscal year.

title: Exclusive: Drivn’s Indian entity raises Rs 45 Cr from Avaana Capital
description: Electric commercial mobility startup Drivn’s Indian entity has raised Rs 45 crore or $4.7 million in a seed funding round led by Avaana Capital.
body: Electric commercial mobility startup Drivn’s Indian entity has raised Rs 45 crore or $4.7 million in a seed funding round led by Avaana Capital.

The fundraise comes a few months after Drivn received an $80 million commitment from Japanese financial services group Nomura in February 2026. The latest capital has been raised by Drivn’s Indian operating entity, while its parent holding company is based in Singapore.

According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , the Indian entity’s board approved the allotment of 33,98,792 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 132.40 per share. Avaana Capital invested the entire Rs 45 crore in the round.
According to the filings, the company will use the fresh capital to meet its business requirements and for general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2025 by Manav Bansal and Alpna Jain, Gurugram-based Drivn is building a full-stack electric mobility platform focused on large commercial vehicles. The startup owns and leases electric intercity buses and heavy-duty trucks, while also offering fleet operations and other services for commercial fleet owners.

Drivn also provides charging infrastructure and battery lifecycle management solutions as it looks to build an integrated platform for businesses transitioning their commercial fleets to electric vehicles.

Following the latest fundraising, Singapore-based Drivn Transition PTE. LTD remains the majority shareholder in the Indian entity with an 88.75% stake. Avaana Capital holds a 7.22% stake, while co-founder and CEO Manav Bansal owns 4.03%.

Despite raising capital and securing the Nomura commitment, Drivn’s Indian entity was still at a pre-revenue stage in FY26. The company reported a loss of Rs 1.96 crore during the financial year, according to its regulatory filings.

title: Skillmatics posts Rs 659 Cr revenue in FY26, profit rises marginally
description: Skillmatics’ revenue from operations increased 34.5% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 659 crore in FY26 from Rs 490 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements.
body: Educational toys and games startup Skillmatics is reportedly in talks to raise fresh capital as it looks to expand its business. The potential fundraise comes as the company has scaled its revenue while remaining profitable.

Skillmatics’ revenue from operations increased 34.5% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 659 crore in FY26 from Rs 490 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
The Mumbai-based company operates a direct-to-consumer (D2C) and omnichannel edutainment business, offering educational toys and learning games for children aged between one and 12 years.

Skillmatics sells its products through its own website, e-commerce marketplaces, and retail stores across global markets. The company has a presence in more than 25 countries and works with over 3,000 retail stores internationally, with North America being its key market.

A large part of its business comes from overseas markets. Around 87% of Skillmatics’ operating revenue was generated outside India, primarily through its US-based subsidiary Grasper Global Inc. The company also reported Rs 7.52 crore in other income during FY26, taking its total revenue to around Rs 667 crore from Rs 496 crore in FY25.
While Skillmatics saw healthy growth in revenue, its expenses increased at a faster pace during the year. The company’s total expenditure rose 36.1% to Rs 652 crore in FY26 from Rs 479 crore in FY25.
Marketing remained one of the biggest expenses for Skillmatics. The company spent around Rs 169 crore on marketing during the year, accounting for about 26% of its total expenditure.

The cost of making toys and games was another major expense and stood at around Rs 130 crore in FY26. Other expenses, including packaging, commissions, transportation, employee benefits and other operating costs, also contributed to the increase in the overall cost base.

title: Soach Global eyes 25X returns from NSE IPO, to pocket Rs 295 Cr via partial exit
description: Mauritius-based Soach Global Opportunities Fund is set to realise nearly 25X returns on its decade-old NSE investment by selling 20% of its holding through the IPO.
body: Mauritius-based Soach Global Opportunities Fund is set to make nearly 25X returns on its decade-old investment in the National Stock Exchange (NSE) through a partial exit in the exchange's initial public offering (IPO). The fund is selling 20% of its holding through the offer for sale (OFS), while retaining the remaining 80% as a long-term investment.

According to the company's press release, Soach Global Strategic Holdings Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of the fund, is selling 16.5 lakh equity shares at NSE's IPO price band of Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share. The transaction is expected to fetch approximately Rs 280 crore to Rs 295 crore.

Soach Global acquired 1.5 lakh NSE shares from the Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) in January 2016 for Rs 59.25 crore at Rs 3,950 per share. Over the following decade, its holding increased to 82.5 lakh shares through corporate actions without any additional investment. Its adjusted acquisition cost stands at Rs 71.8 per share.

At the upper end of the IPO price band, the fund's partial exit will generate nearly five times its entire original investment. Following the sale, Soach Global will continue to hold 66 lakh NSE shares, valued at approximately Rs 1,120 crore to Rs 1,180 crore.

Hong Kong-based Soach Global Corporation Limited operates in fund management and advisory, with a focus on trade, commerce and long-term investments in India and global markets. Its Mauritius-based investment subsidiary holds the group's investment in NSE.

Anubhav Dayal, founder and director of Soach Global Opportunities Fund, said the partial exit is intended to enable wider retail participation in NSE's growth. He added that the fund views its remaining holding as a long-term investment and has no plans to re-enter after the sale.

NSE's IPO, which opened on September 17, will close for subscription today. The issue was subscribed 1.76 times as of 11:50 AM on the final day. Ahead of the IPO, the exchange raised Rs 6,746 crore from 189 anchor investors, including LIC, Norway's Government Pension Fund Global, ADIA, GIC, Fidelity, Societe Generale.

title: Samara Capital acquires stakes in ARC and Calyx
description: Private equity firm Samara Capital has acquired stakes in Associated Road Carriers (ARC) and Calyx Container Terminals to create an integrated logistics platform. Snippets
body: Private equity firm Samara Capital has acquired stakes in Associated Road Carriers (ARC) and Calyx Container Terminals to create an integrated logistics platform.
As per mint report, Samara has invested around Rs 1,200 crore, with the promoters and the PE firm holding nearly equal stakes in the new entity.

The combined platform brings together ARC’s business-to-business road transportation network and Calyx’s container freight station operations at Chennai Port. Together, the two companies reported revenue of around Rs 2,140 crore in FY26.

The fresh capital will be used to expand the branch and hub network, strengthen first-mile and last-mile logistics capabilities and upgrade technology. The platform may also pursue acquisitions as it expands its presence across India.

Samara plans to build a nationwide logistics business covering both domestic and EXIM cargo movements. The firm will also focus on improving operations through investments in technology, data analytics, engineering and process improvements.
The combined platform will seek to use ARC’s road network and Calyx’s port-linked infrastructure to offer logistics services across different stages of the supply chain.

title: Moneyview fixes IPO price band at Rs 32-34; eyes Rs 1,092 Cr
description: Accel and Tiger Global-backed Moneyview has fixed the price band for its IPO at Rs 32-34 per share, putting the company’s valuation at nearly Rs 6,000 crore.
body: Accel and Tiger Global-backed digital lending platform Moneyview has fixed the price band for its IPO at Rs 32-34 per share, putting the company’s valuation at nearly Rs 6,000 crore at the upper end of the band.

The IPO will open for subscription on September 24 and close on September 28. The anchor book will open a day earlier on September 23. Moneyview is looking to raise Rs 1,091.6 crore through the public issue.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 750 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of up to 10.04 crore shares. At the upper price band, the company will have an implied market capitalisation of around Rs 5,985 crore.

The price band comes shortly after Moneyview halved the size of its fresh issue from the Rs 1,500 crore proposed in its draft papers. The company and its existing investors also reduced the OFS from around 13.6 crore shares to 10.04 crore shares.

Founders Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal will participate in the OFS along with investors including Accel, Tiger Global Management, Ribbit Capital, DI Investment and Crimson Winter. Accel is currently Moneyview’s largest shareholder with a 21.89% stake, followed by Tiger Global at 13.79%.

Moneyview plans to use Rs 325 crore from the fresh issue to support loan disbursals under default loss guarantee arrangements, while another Rs 250 crore will be invested in its lending subsidiary Whizdm Finance to strengthen its capital base. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Financially, Moneyview reported Rs 3,351.2 crore revenue in FY26, up 43.3% year-on-year, while profit rose marginally to Rs 242.7 crore. In Q1 FY27, revenue grew 50.2% to Rs 1,041.1 crore, while profit jumped 158.8% to Rs 173.8 crore.
Investors can bid for a minimum of 441 shares, requiring Rs 14,994 at the upper price band. Moneyview is expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 1.

title: Proactive AI startup Sol raises $4 Mn from General Catalyst, Nexus VP, and others
description: The startup operates in a dedicated computer environment and can use a browser to work across tools. It currently has a library of more than 100 skills to handle tasks
body: Proactive AI startup Sol has emerged from stealth with $4 million in a funding round led by General Catalyst and Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from DeVC, Peercheque and Kunal Shah.
