The anchor book saw participation from Negen Undiscovered Value Fund, Singularity Growth Opportunities Fund, Turnaround Opportunities Fund, and mutual funds including Helios and Taurus.
AceVector’s operating revenue grew 29% to Rs 510.38 crore in FY26 from Rs 395.02 crore in FY25, while its adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to Rs 15.94 crore from Rs 39.16 crore.

title: ITC completes 100% acquisition of Yoga Bar parent Sproutlife
description: FMCG major ITC has completed the acquisition of Sproutlife Foods, parent company Yoga Bar, after acquiring the remaining stake in the Bengaluru based company.
body: FMCG major ITC has completed the acquisition of Sproutlife Foods, the parent company of nutrition and healthy foods brand Yoga Bar, after acquiring the remaining stake in the Bengaluru based company.

According to its exchange filing, ITC acquired 13,445 equity shares of Sproutlife through a secondary purchase for around Rs 645 crore, increasing its shareholding from approximately 47.5% to 100%. Following the transaction, Sproutlife has become a wholly owned subsidiary of ITC effective September 28.
The acquisition was completed entirely through cash consideration. ITC said the acquisition is in line with its strategy to strengthen its future ready portfolio in the foods segment.

Sproutlife manufactures and sells food products under the Yoga Bar brand. Positioned as a digital first brand, Yoga Bar has a significant presence across D2C and e-commerce channels, along with a growing footprint in offline retail stores.
The company has recorded strong growth in recent years, with its turnover more than doubling to Rs 452 crore in FY26 from Rs 200 crore in FY25. Its turnover stood at Rs 108 crore in FY24.

ITC first invested in Yoga Bar parent Sproutlife Foods in May 2023, acquiring a 39.42% stake for Rs 175 crore, after announcing plans to acquire the company in phases in January that year. Since then, ITC gradually increased its holding to around 47.5%, before acquiring the remaining 52.5% stake in the latest transaction to complete the acquisition.

The deal comes amid a broader acquisition push by legacy FMCG companies to expand their presence in new age and digital first consumer brands. Besides Yoga Bar, ITC signed a deal in February 2025 to acquire Prasuma, which operates frozen and ready to cook food brands Prasuma and Meatigo, with plans to acquire 100% over three years. Similarly, . HUL has similarly expanded its new age portfolio through acquisitions of Minimalist and health and wellness brand OZiva , while Marico has added brands such as Cosmix to its D2C portfolio. Emami and VLCC have also made acquisitions in the digital first consumer space.

title: Bewakoof’s revenue jumps 40% to Rs 243 Cr in FY26, losses rise 19%
description: Following a modest 7% growth in FY25, Aditya Birla Group-owned Bewakoof posted a strong 40% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in FY26. At the same time
body: Following a modest 7% growth in FY25, Aditya Birla Group-owned Bewakoof posted a strong 40% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in FY26. At the same time, the D2C fashion brand’s losses increased 19% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Bewakoof’s operating revenue rose 40.5% to Rs 243 crore in FY26 from Rs 173 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Bewakoof is a lifestyle fashion brand that makes trendy products for contemporary India, including T-shirts, phone covers, bags and hoodies. Revenue from the sale of these products remained the company’s main source of income during the year.

On the cost side, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense for the company. It increased 45.7% to Rs 134 crore in FY26 from Rs 92 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses rose 7.7% to Rs 28 crore, while marketing expenses increased 26.5% to Rs 62 crore. Transportation and handling expenses, however, fell 17.1% to Rs 29 crore from Rs 35 crore.
Depreciation expenses jumped nearly three times to Rs 16.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 6 crore in FY25. Other expenses also increased 66.1% to Rs 66.4 crore from Rs 40 crore.
Overall, Bewakoof’s total expenses increased 35.5% to Rs 336 crore in FY26 from Rs 248 crore in the previous fiscal year.
As a result, the company’s loss widened 19.4% to Rs 87.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 73.2 crore in FY25, despite the strong growth in revenue.

However, some operating metrics improved. Bewakoof’s EBITDA loss narrowed slightly to Rs 59.8 crore from Rs 60.7 crore in FY25, while its EBITDA margin improved to -24.6% from -35.1%. The company’s return on capital employed (ROCE) also improved to -63.4% in FY26 from -96.6% in FY25.

title: Aman Gupta invests in former boAt executive’s startup FIG Living
description: Entrepreneur and investor Aman Gupta has invested in design-led home and living brand FIG Living through his investment firm SailThru Ventures. Snippets
body: Entrepreneur and investor Aman Gupta has invested in design-led home and living brand FIG Living through his investment firm SailThru Ventures.
The investment continues Gupta’s association with FIG founder Sushant Sharma, who previously worked with him at boAt.

Founded in 2025, FIG Living started with lighting products such as table lamps, portable lamps, pendant lights, wall lights and floor lamps. The company has since expanded into side tables, accent furniture and tabletop products as it looks to build a broader home and lifestyle platform.

FIG Living currently has an annual revenue run rate of around Rs 12 crore and serves more than 40,000 consumers. The company is growing around 20% quarter-on-quarter and is targeting an annual revenue run rate of Rs 18 crore after the upcoming festive season.

The brand develops its products in-house and has secured more than 36 design patents. Around 80% of its portfolio uses knock-down and DIY formats, allowing customers to assemble products at home while reducing transportation costs and complexity.

With the investment, FIG Living plans to expand its distribution network, strengthen physical brand experiences and add more consumer touchpoints. It will also explore global design partnerships and collaborations.
The company manufactures its products in India through an affiliated facility in Greater Noida and plans to expand beyond lighting into more home and lifestyle categories.

title: Bharat Housing Network raises $5 Mn from Symbiotics
description: Bharat Housing Network (BHN), a secured credit network, has raised $5 million (around Rs 47 crore) in green bonds from Symbiotics. Snippets.
body: Bharat Housing Network (BHN), a secured credit network, has raised $5 million (around Rs 47 crore) in green bonds from Symbiotics.
The bond is part of a $75 million green basket bond programme structured by Symbiotics with British International Investment (BII).
BHN had previously raised Rs 125 crore ($14.5 million) in Series A funding led by NABVENTURES.

The capital will be deployed through BHN’s group NBFC, Singularity Creditworld, to finance green assets in India. The funds will support rooftop solar financing, electric mobility financing and credit for clean-tech MSMEs.

BHN claims its network has enabled nearly Rs 2,000 crore of credit to more than 40,000 low and middle-income borrowers. It has also financed 7,162 KW of rooftop solar capacity and more than 800 electric vehicles, with the financed assets having a potential to save around 1,01,500 tonnes of CO2 emissions.

Founded by Lalit Menghani, Madhusudan Sharma and Prasad Ajinkya, BHN is part of the Homeville Group. The company provides technology and infrastructure for capital deployment across mortgages, clean energy, mobility and gold loans. Its investors include NABVENTURES, 100Unicorns, Varanium, Riverwalk and LC Nueva.

BHN is also targeting up to $25 million in green bond issuances by the end of the next financial year. The proposed capital will be used to expand green asset financing and provide funding to sustainable businesses and retail borrowers across India.

title: Subway India operator EverBrands files DRHP to raise Rs 600 Cr via fresh issue
description: Subway India operator EverBrands India has filed its DRHP with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO).
body: Subway India operator EverBrands India has filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 600 crore, with no offer for sale (OFS).

The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 120 crore. If completed, the pre-IPO placement will reduce the size of the fresh issue. The company has proposed to list its equity shares on the BSE and NSE.

EverBrands operates Subway in India through Culinary Brands India Pvt Ltd (CBIPL). It also manages Lavazza Coffee and F&H Coffee and distributes Dilmah Tea in India through Fresh and Honest Cafe Pvt Ltd. The company operates Subway stores under both company-owned, company-operated (COCO) and franchisee-owned, franchisee-operated (FOFO) formats.
According to the DRHP, the company has appointed Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities and Nuvama as book-running lead managers and MUFG as the registrar to the issue.

The company plans to use Rs 125 crore of the IPO proceeds to repay its borrowings. Another Rs 326.85 crore will be used for capital expenditure towards setting up new Subway stores under the COCO format, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

For FY26, revenue for EverBrands grew 34.9% year-on-year to Rs 966.17 crore from Rs 716.06 crore in FY25. Its quick service restaurant (QSR) business, which includes Subway, contributed Rs 693.09 crore during the fiscal year, while the company’s loss widened to Rs 58.19 crore from Rs 28.26 crore in FY25. EBITDA stood at Rs 98.13 crore, compared with Rs 64.21 crore in the previous fiscal.

As of FY26, EverBrands had 678 COCO and 330 FOFO Subway stores in India, along with eight FOFO stores in Sri Lanka. Its Subway business accounted for nearly 72% of the company’s total operating revenue during the fiscal.

EverBrands Ventures Pte Ltd is the largest shareholder of the company with a 57.78% stake on a fully diluted basis, followed by Norwest Capital LLC with 16.48%. Shivanand Shankar Mankekar HUF holds 5.83%, while Playbook India Fund II owns 4.15%. Enrich Agro Food Products and Bikramjit Singh Kandhari each hold 3.64% in the company on a fully diluted basis.

title: NKN Media raises $4.08 Mn at $81.69 Mn valuation
description: The fresh funds will be used to accelerate NKN Media’s expansion beyond the UAE and strengthen its presence in the global media and entertainment ecosystem, the company said in a press release.
body: Media and television distribution company NKN Media has raised AED 15 million ($4.08 million) in a strategic investment from entrepreneur and investor Dhiraj Jain, founder and chairman of 1XL. The investment values the company at AED 300 million ($81.69 million) and gives Jain a 5% stake in the company.
The fresh funds will be used to accelerate NKN Media’s expansion beyond the UAE and strengthen its presence in the global media and entertainment ecosystem, the company said in a press release.

NKN Media is focused on media distribution and has been expanding into a diversified media company with a portfolio of original intellectual properties, entertainment formats, international events and strategic media partnerships.

The company is developing original IPs in the UAE for audiences across India, the Middle East and international markets. One of its latest properties, Falcons of Majlis, is a UAE-focused reality funding show built around the country’s growing startup ecosystem.
The format brings together entrepreneurs, investors and personalities from the business and entertainment sectors, with selected startups pitching their businesses to a panel of investors.

NKN Media has a portfolio of IPs including Falcons of Majlis, Dubai Property Expo, Indo-UAE International Property Expo and Icons of UAE. The company plans to expand these properties across international markets as it builds a global media and entertainment platform.

NKN Media has a presence across the UAE, UK, Singapore, Malaysia, Canada, Bahrain, India and Sri Lanka. It partners with broadcast networks including Republic TV, Aaj Tak, India Today and Times Now. The company also publishes SpiceRoute, the in-flight magazine of SpiceJet.

title: EV startup Simple Energy raises $182 Mn in Series C round
description:
Electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy has raised Rs 1,750 crore ($182 million) in a Series C funding round. This is its largest fundraise to date.

The fundr
body: Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy has raised Rs 1,750 crore ($182 million) in a Series C funding round. This is its largest fundraise to date and the third-largest funding by an Indian electric two-wheeler OEM, according to the company.

The fundraise was led by the family office of Dr Arokiaswamy Velumani, founder of Thyrocare Technologies, along with founder and CEO Suhas Rajkumar and co-founder and CFO Ankit Gupta. Bengaluru-based HNI Amit Mishra and the Haran Family Office also participated.
The entire capital was raised through equity. With this fundraise, Simple Energy’s total capital raised has crossed Rs 2,530 crore ($263 million).

The fresh capital will be used to set up a new manufacturing facility, increase production capacity, expand its distribution and service network, hire talent and fund research and development for its next product cycle. The company will also use the funds for marketing and supply chain operations.

Simple Energy currently has a production capacity of 10,000 units per month and operates more than 80 outlets across over 60 cities. Its product portfolio includes Simple One, Simple Wave and Simple Ultra electric scooters.

The company said its monthly sales have grown more than fourfold over the past year. It has launched Simple Wave and Simple Ultra in the past eight months for the family and performance scooter segments.

Simple Energy reported operating revenue of around Rs 150-160 crore in FY26, compared with about Rs 40 crore in FY25. This represents a nearly fourfold increase in revenue. The company currently derives most of its sales from southern states.

Simple Energy had raised Rs 250 crore through a mix of debt and equity in June 2026, following a $10 million all-equity bridge fundraise in September 2025. Before that, it raised $20 million in Series A funding in July 2024, more than $20 million in a bridge fundraise in February 2023 and $21 million in pre-Series A funding in November 2021.

title: Former Livspace executives’ startup Gravity raises $15 Mn led by Info Edge Ventures and 3one4 Capital
description: Home interior materials startup Gravity has raised $15 million in a mix of equity and debt funding led by Info Edge Ventures and 3one4 Capital.
body: Bengaluru-based premium home interior materials startup Gravity has raised $15 million in a mix of equity and debt funding led by Info Edge Ventures and 3one4 Capital.
Alteria Capital, Genesia Ventures and a group of angel investors also participated in the round.

Founded by former Livspace executives Saurabh Jain and Lalit Mittal, Gravity is building a platform for India’s interior materials ecosystem. The startup currently focuses on the kitchen and wardrobe segments and brings together specialist businesses on a common technology, distribution, key account management and operating infrastructure.

Gravity said its initial portfolio of businesses has a multi-hundred-crore revenue base and is EBITDA positive. It plans to expand into categories such as doors and windows, lighting, wall surfaces, home automation and other adjacent interior systems.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen Gravity’s technology, distribution and key account infrastructure. The startup will also deploy the funds for category expansion, brand building and working capital.

Jain previously served as CEO of Livspace India, where he helped scale the business to an annualised revenue run rate of around Rs 1,500 crore. Mittal served as chief business officer for India and led Livspace’s expansion across 30 cities.

Gravity is targeting designers, architects, modular showrooms and design-and-build studios, which influence material selection and procurement for home interior projects. The startup aims to simplify sourcing across fragmented suppliers while improving availability, fulfilment and pricing visibility.
Gravity estimates India’s home interiors market at around Rs 3.5 lakh crore, with the design-specified material market accounting for about Rs 1.5 lakh crore.

title: Netmeds posts flat revenue at Rs 45 Cr in FY26; remains profitable
description: Reliance-backed Netmeds remained smaller than rivals Tata 1mg and PharmEasy, with its operating revenue largely flat in FY26. The company, however, remained profitable with Rs 5.5 crore in profit.
body: Reliance-backed Netmeds remained a relatively small player compared to online pharmacy rivals such as Tata 1mg and PharmEasy, with its operating revenue remaining largely flat in FY26. The company, however, stayed profitable with Rs 5.5 crore during the year.

Netmeds’ revenue from operations grew marginally by 2.3% in the fiscal year ended March 2026 to Rs 44.7 crore from Rs 43.7 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Netmeds operates an online healthcare platform that sells pharmaceutical and healthcare products and provides services across diagnostics, doctor consultations and other healthcare offerings. The company also generates revenue through marketing and healthcare-related services.
Income from services continued to account for the bulk of Netmeds’ revenue during FY26. Gross service income stood at Rs 46.3 crore compared with Rs 46.2 crore in FY25.

Revenue from the sale of goods, meanwhile, increased 24% to Rs 6.03 crore from Rs 4.86 crore in the previous fiscal year. After adjusting Rs 7.6 crore towards GST recovered, Netmeds’ revenue from operations stood at Rs 44.7 crore in FY26.
The company also generated Rs 3.24 crore from non-operating sources, which took its total income to Rs 47.94 crore during the year.

Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost centre for Netmeds, increasing 4% to Rs 13.7 crore in FY26 compared to Rs 13.2 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, technical service costs declined 12% to Rs 9.12 crore, whereas the cost of materials increased 12% to Rs 4.44 crore during the year.

Advertising and promotional expenditure surged 76% to Rs 2.9 crore from Rs 1.65 crore in FY25. Other overheads such as legal & professional rent stood added another Rs 12.24 crore, taking the company’s total expenditure to Rs 42.4 crore from Rs 41.6 crore in the previous fiscal year.

title: Longevity startup Vytalyou raises Rs 9 Cr in pre-Series A round
description: Vytalyou uses an AI-based algorithm for its Predictive Longevity Evaluation, which assesses an individual’s health profile, biological ageing and potential health risks.
body: Doctor-led longevity and preventive healthcare startup Vytalyou has raised Rs 9 crore in a pre-Series A round from Chetan Jain of Pharma Dose and Ratan Jain of Venus Industries at a valuation of around Rs 33 crore.
The proceeds will be used to expand its network of Incremental Lifestyle Clinics in Mumbai, Vytalyou said in a press release.

Founded in 2025 by Chirantan Bose and Preetesh Bhandari, Vytalyou provides preventive healthcare and longevity-focused services, combining diagnostics with personalised health interventions and medically supervised care.

The Mumbai-based startup offers services across pathology, radiology, cardio-respiratory assessments, body composition evaluation, genetic and cancer screening, gut microbiome evaluation, personalised IV therapies and regenerative interventions. It also offers non-invasive pain management technologies for chronic musculoskeletal conditions.

Vytalyou uses an AI-based algorithm for its Predictive Longevity Evaluation, which assesses an individual’s health profile, biological ageing and potential health risks. Doctors review the assessment and develop a medically supervised care plan based on the findings.

The company said it has served close to 1,000 clients since opening its first centre, with around half coming through walk-ins and the rest through word-of-mouth referrals. It plans to expand to 10 locations across India in the coming years.
Vytalyou operates in India’s growing preventive healthcare and longevity segment, which has also seen startups such as Biopeak, Cent, Elevate Now and Decode Age raise capital.

Biopeak raised $2.7 million in follow-on funding in January this year, while Cent, co-founded by Practo’s Shashank ND, raised around $5 million for its AI-led early-detection platform covering cancer, cardiac, neurological and metabolic risks.

title: Exclusive: Blitz kicks off  pre-Series B round at 2.5X valuation premium
description: Blitz, a quick-commerce fulfilment startup, has raised Rs 28.70 crore in a pre-Series B funding round led by existing investor IvyCap Ventures.
body: Blitz, a quick-commerce fulfilment startup, has raised Rs 28.70 crore in a pre-Series B funding round led by existing investor IvyCap Ventures. The company’s board approved the allotment of 21,883 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 13,118 per share to raise the aforesaid amount, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr .

IvyCap Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 12.70 crore, followed by ICMG Group invested Rs 4.75 crore, while Vishal Dhupar put in Rs 2.50 crore. Several other angel investors also participated in the round, collectively contributing the remaining amount.

According to the Entrackr’s estimate, the company’s post-money valuation jumped around 2.5X to Rs 440 crore compared to Rs 175 crore in its Series A round. The company may raise additional capital in this round, which would increase its post-money valuation accordingly.

As per the filing with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, the company plans to use the funds for business growth, expansion, and general corporate purposes. In Nov 2024, the company had raised Rs 51 crore in its Series A round led by IvyCap Ventures Founded in 2020 by Gaurav Piyush, Mayank Varshney, and Yash Sharma, Blitz helps ecommerce and D2C brands offer 10-minute, 60-minute, same-day and next-day deliveries. The company operates a network of dark stores and fulfilment centres to enable faster order fulfilment and help brands drive sales and customer retention.

After the fresh allotment, IvyCap Ventures remains the largest external shareholder in Blitz with a 23.47% stake, followed by India Quotient with 15.31% and AL Trust with 3.29%. ESOPs and MSOPs account for 12.88% of the company. Among the cofounders, Yash Sharma and Mayank Varshney hold 11.53% each, while Gaurav Piyush holds 6.72%.

Angel investors Kunal Bahl and Rohot Bansal (Co-founders of Snapdeal) hold 0.59% each, while QED Innovation Labs (Kunal Shah, Global head of WhatsApp) and Farid Ahsan (Founder & CEO, General Autonomy) hold 0.34% each.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Blitz’s operating revenue jumped 2.28X year-on-year to Rs 50.6 crore in FY25 from Rs 22.18 crore in FY24, while its losses rose 2.18X to Rs 24.33 crore from Rs 11.17 crore

title: Edtech startup Arivihan raises $10 Mn in Series A led by Accel and Prosus
description: Bengaluru-based edtech startup Arivihan has raised $10 million in Series A funding from existing investors Accel and Prosus Ventures, along with an additional. News
body: Bengaluru- based edtech startup Arivihan has raised $10 million in Series A funding from existing investors Accel and Prosus Ventures, along with an additional $200,000 from its existing GSF angel investors.
The round takes the company’s total funding to more than $15 million.
Entrackr recently reported on the company’s new funding and estimated that its valuation had jumped 3.3X to around $60 million.

The fresh capital will be used to expand into new states and strengthen its presence in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Bihar. The company also plans to expand its CBSE offering, develop more vernacular language capabilities and increase its AI research efforts.

Founded in 2022 by Ritesh Singh Chandel, Sonu Kumar and Rushabh Kothari, Arivihan offers an AI based learning platform for school students. Its platform provides interactive video lessons, instant doubt solving and AI driven study plans without relying on live teachers.

The company currently serves students preparing for State Board, CBSE and NEET exams, with a focus on students from tier 2, tier 3 cities and rural areas. Arivihan said around 80% of its subscribers come from tier 3 cities and rural India.

Arivihan will also scale its digital marketing and on ground distribution network as it expands across India. The company plans to hire across key functions and launch new crash courses. Arivihan was previously part of Accel’s Atoms accelerator programme and received seed funding through the programme in March 2024.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Arivihan’s revenue jumped nearly 14.8X to Rs 3.14 crore from Rs 21.29 lakh in FY24, while the company posted a loss of Rs 4.45 crore.

title: EDT raises $2.4 Mn in Pre Series A round led by Sauce, enters beauty tech
description: Consumer technology brand EDT has raised $2.4 million in a Pre Series A round led by existing investor Sauce. Existing angel investors also participated in the round.
body: Mumbai based consumer technology brand EDT has raised $2.4 million in a Pre Series A round led by existing investor Sauce. Existing angel investors also participated in the round.
The round also saw participation from Alteria Capital, Raul Rai of Nicobar, Shibam Das and Arindam Paul of Atomberg, Ajith Pai of Delhivery and Anushree Tainwala of Samsonite.
EDT will use the funds to build inventory ahead of the festive season, launch new products and strengthen its growth, supply chain, brand and product teams.

Founded in 2025 by Naiyya Saggi and Vyasateja Rao, EDT currently offers kitchen appliances including LUMA air fryer oven and FLOW kettle. Its products are available on Amazon, Flipkart, Blinkit, Croma, FoodStories and its D2C platform. The company said its business on Amazon grew nearly seven times between March and July 2026.

The company has also entered the beauty tech segment with SUKI, a hair dryer based on its patent pending CareDry Algorithm. EDT said the device uses dual sensors to monitor hair and airflow conditions 100 times a second and adjust the heat accordingly.
SUKI is available at a limited time pre order price of Rs 8,499 through EDT's D2C platform. The company plans to expand its availability to marketplaces and retail stores later this year.

EDT said it has three more products in the pipeline across home, kitchen and beauty tech. The company plans to focus on R&D, product expansion, omnichannel distribution, community building and team expansion.

title: Kuku clocks Rs 1,484 Cr revenue and Rs 89 Cr PBT in FY26; spends Rs 1,100 Cr on marketing
description: Kuku Technologies’ revenue surged over sixfold in FY26, backed by Rs 1,105 crore in marketing spends, while the IPO-bound company turned profitable with Rs 88.6 crore in profit before tax.
body: Audio and video content platform Kuku FM’s parent Kuku Technologies saw its operating revenue surge more than six-fold in FY26, backed by Rs 1,105 crore in marketing and advertising spends. The IPO-bound company also turned profitable during the year, posting a profit before tax of Rs 88.6 crore.
Kuku Technologies’ revenue from operations ballooned to Rs 1,484.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 241.5 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Kuku FM offers audio content across genres such as business, self-help, personal finance, history, religion, entertainment and fitness. The company also operates Kuku TV, Guru and StoRizz, offering audio and video content primarily through subscription plans.

Subscription revenue remained its primary source of income, contributing Rs 1,475.4 crore, or over 99% of operating revenue in FY26. The firm also earned Rs 6.86 crore from its pay-per-piece model, where users purchase coins to unlock content, while advertising income stood at Rs 1.9 crore.
The company also earned Rs 26.2 crore in non-operating sources such as interests on bank deposits, which took its overall income to Rs 1,510.4 crore  during the fiscal year ending March 2026.
The hockey-stick growth came as Kuku scaled Kuku TV, its microdrama platform launched in 2024. The company currently produces more than 150 microdramas a month as it expands its content pipeline.

On the cost side, marketing and advertising remained Kuku’s largest expense at Rs 1,105 crore in FY26, nearly four times the Rs 284.8 crore spent in the previous fiscal year. Employee benefit expenses increased 24% to Rs 74.1 crore, which included Rs 18.5 crore ESOP cost.

IT expenses more than doubled to Rs 56.7 crore, while operational costs surged to Rs 96.25 crore from Rs 8.65 crore, and payment gateway charges increased to Rs 43.2 crore. Overall, Kuku’s total expenditure rose 3.5X to Rs 1,421.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 411 crore in FY25.

title: Indian startups raise $2.9 Bn in Q3 2026 as EV, AI drive funding
description: Indian startups raised less than $3 billion in funding in Q3 2026, down from $3.5 billion in Q2 and $3.87 billion in Q1. The quarter. Quarterly Funding Report
body: Indian startups raised less than $3 billion in funding in Q3 2026, down from $3.5 billion in Q2 and $3.87 billion in Q1. The quarter saw fewer large funding rounds, with Simple Energy leading the pack with a $182 million raise. The round also made Simple Energy the third-largest funded Indian electric two-wheeler OEM. Physical AI startup SiMa.ai, which has deep Indian roots and a major research and development centre in Bengaluru, raised another $150 million . Emergent, River Mobility, Navi, Slice and Pixxel also secured more than $100 million each during the quarter.

Despite the decline in overall funding, early-stage deals crossed the $1 billion mark in Q3. The quarter also saw six startup listings, including NSE, Rentomojo, Molbio, Milky Mist, Leap India and Purple Style Labs. Six startups shut down operations during the quarter.

According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $2.9 billion in funding during the third quarter of 2026. This amount included 46 growth and late-stage deals totalling $1.89 billion, along with 194 early-stage deals worth $1.01 billion. Additionally, there were 26 undisclosed deals during the period.

Q3 2026 saw a modest recovery in startup funding compared to the same quarter last year. Total funding rose to $2.9 billion from $2.78 billion in Q3 2025, but remained below the $4 billion recorded in Q3 2024. September emerged as a strong month for funding, as startups raised more than $1 billion for the third time in 2026. February and June were the previous two months to cross the $1 billion mark, with each recording around $2 billion in funding. The September uptick helped Q3 close above the funding level recorded in the year-ago quarter.

In Q3 2026, India’s top 15 growth and late-stage deals reflected strong investor interest in mobility, AI and fintech, along with bets across consumer and deeptech sectors. Simple Energy topped the list after raising $182 million in its Series C round, followed by physical AI startup SiMa.ai, which secured $150 million in Series C funding. AI startup Emergent raised $130 million , while electric two-wheeler maker River Mobility secured $120 million. Fintech firms Navi and Slice raised $100 million each, while electric mobility platform Yulu followed with $93 million. EV maker Ultraviolette raised $85 million, while AI startups Ema and Sarvam AI secured $77 million and $74 million, respectively. Wearable tech startup Ultrahuman raised $70 million, while The Pizza Bakery secured $56 million. Healthtech startup Nua raised $50 million, followed by Third Wave Coffee at $43 million and aerospace and defence company Raghu Vamsi Aerospace Group at $40 million.

Early-stage activity remained strong in Q3 2026, led by Pixxel’s $100 million Series A and Airbound’s $37 million Series A. Yuma Energy followed with $35 million, while Centricity and InRisk Labs raised $30 million and $27 million, respectively. Most of the top deals fell in the $15–25 million range, reflecting steady investor interest in early-stage companies.

Spacetech, fintech, deeptech and mobility featured prominently among the top deals. Data centre startup CtrlS raised $25 million, while foodtech firm Arboreal Bioinnovations secured $24 million . Business Nextgen Finance and Runable raised $21.7 million and $21 million, respectively. NeoGeo, Nexedge Capital and QNu Labs raised $20 million each, while Gravity, Piston and Plaza rounded out the list at $15 million each.

The Indian startup ecosystem saw 33 merger and acquisition transactions in Q3 2026, covering sectors such as fintech, healthtech, AI, edtech, spacetech and e-commerce. Some of the notable deals included Samara Capital’s $120 million acquisition of stakes in Associated Road Carriers and Calyx Container Terminal, ITC’s $65 million acquisition of Yoga Bar and Udaan’s $52 million acquisition of Swiggy’s supply chain platform Lynk. Aurum PropTech agreed to acquire Housing.com’s parent in a $46.2 million share swap deal, while Ananta Capital acquired a majority stake in Phitku for $10.6 million. PhysicsWallah also acquired a controlling stake in Sarrthi IAS for $7.5 million. The quarter also saw strategic deals such as InsuranceDekho’s merger with RenewBuy, Adobe’s acquisition of AI startup Rilo and GalaxEye’s acquisition of spacecraft engineering company StarOps.

title: Teachmint revenue jumps 2.8X to Rs 205 Cr in FY26
description: Teachmint continued its strong growth in FY26, with its operating revenue crossing the Rs 200 crore mark. The company also narrowed its losses during the year.
body: Edtech startup Teachmint continued its strong growth in FY26, with its operating revenue crossing the Rs 200 crore mark. The company also narrowed its losses during the year.

According to the company's audited consolidated financial filings with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, the company’s operating revenue jumped 2.8X to Rs 205.3 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 74.2 crore in FY25.
The growth was largely led by demand for Teachmint X, its AI-powered connected classroom device.

Teachmint X combines an AI teaching assistant with a digital board. The platform helps teachers plan lessons, create quizzes and homework, and grade student submissions, all aligned with the curriculum and what has been taught in that classroom. It also connects teachers and students through a single platform for classroom planning, engagement, and tracking student progress.
The company said Teachmint X is gaining traction in international markets, including the Middle East, SAARC countries and Southeast Asia.
“Teachmint X is powering global classrooms. Its multilingual, regionally context-aware AI lets us serve every classroom the way it teaches and learns,” a company spokesperson said.

On the profitability front, Teachmint’s loss before share-based expenses fell 34.2% to Rs 28.9 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 43.9 crore in FY25. The company incurred share-based expenses of Rs 9.9 crore during the year.
The company also benefited from improved operating leverage. While its revenue grew nearly 2.8X, operating expenses, excluding the cost of goods sold, increased only 11.6% during FY26.

title: IPV leads Rs 7 Cr seed round in cybersecurity startup Zaperon
description: By bringing together identity security, data security and AI governance, Zaperon enables enterprises to control how users, applications and AI agents access and interac
body: Cybersecurity startup Zaperon has raised Rs 7 crore in a seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV).
The fresh funds will be used to advance product capabilities, launch enterprise-grade AI security frameworks and expand its presence in India and the US, Zaperon said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2021 by Vineet Gupta and Sachin Aggarwal, Zaperon is a cybersecurity firm that builds products to protect enterprises from data breaches. It offers a platform-centric approach to enterprise security that allows organisations to secure their entire IT landscape through a single Zaperon console.

By bringing together identity security, data security and AI governance, Zaperon enables enterprises to control how users, applications and AI agents access and interact with sensitive data and cloud infrastructure. The platform aims to replace fragmented security controls with consistent, identity and context-aware policies across digital and AI environments.
According to market research, identity security and data security represent an estimated $16 billion global opportunity today, which is projected to reach $35 billion by 2030.

The Delhi-based startup’s enterprise client base spans banking and financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, technology and government sectors, where protecting sensitive data and controlling access to critical systems are key security and compliance requirements.
Indian cybersecurity startups raised $89 million across 17 funding rounds in H1 2026, nearly double the $47 million raised in H1 2025.

Recent deals include QNu Labs, which raised Rs 200 crore in a Series A1 round led by the National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest to scale its quantum-safe cybersecurity solutions; Mitigata, which secured $15 million in Series B funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners for its AI-powered cyber-resilience platform; and CloudSEK, which raised $10 million from Connecticut Innovations to expand its AI-driven cyber-intelligence platform.

title: Niyo’s income jumps 78% to Rs 178 Cr in FY26
description: Travel fintech platform Niyo’s income grew 78% year-on-year to Rs 178 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 100 crore in FY25, according to the company’s press release.
body: Travel fintech platform Niyo’s income grew 78% year-on-year to Rs 178 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 100 crore in FY25, according to the company’s press release.

The company also cut its losses by 58% to Rs 33 crore in FY26 from Rs 78 crore a year earlier. Niyo said the improvement came from better efficiency, including the use of AI in customer service, operations, marketing and product development.

Niyo’s operating expenses rose 20% to Rs 201 crore in FY26 from Rs 168 crore in FY25. Employee expenses increased 17% to Rs 92 crore from Rs 79 crore. According to Niyo, the increase in employee costs was mainly due to the expansion of Kanji Forex , which operates under Niyo’s own AD-II licence.
Despite the higher spending, Niyo’s EBITDA loss nearly halved to Rs 32 crore in FY26 from Rs 77 crore in FY25, the press release added.

Niyo is also expanding beyond its core travel business. The company said its revenue is now coming from forex cash, remittances, flights, hotels, experiences, international eSIMs and insurance, among other services. It is also selling more forex and travel products to its existing customers.
The company has set up Finnew Global Solutions IFSC in GIFT City and received approval to operate as a Payment Service Provider under IFSCA rules.

Niyo CFO Gourav Kumar said the company is now focused on getting more value from its existing customers, improving efficiency and moving towards profitability. Niyo expects to maintain over 50% annual growth in the coming years and become EBITDA positive.
Niyo has raised over $160 million in funding to date, including a $100 million Series C round in 2022. Its investors include Accel, Lightrock, Prime Ventures, Horizon, Tencent, and others.

title: Seeds Fincap raises Rs 100 Cr in Series B led by Michael & Susan Dell Foundation
description: Gurugram-based NBFC Seeds Fincap has raised more than Rs 100 crore ($10.4 million) in a Series B round led by Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. News
body: Gurugram-based NBFC Seeds Fincap has raised more than Rs 100 crore ($10.4 million) in a Series B round led by Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. Existing investors Z47 and Lok Capital, along with Norinchukin Capital and Alteria Capital, also participated in the round.

Last year, Seeds Fincap raised Rs 50 crore ($5.5 million) in a round led by Z47 and Lok Capital. In July 2024, it raised over $8.5 million in a Series A round led by Lok Capital and Matrix Partners India, now Z47.

The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand into new markets and strengthen its branch network, technology and risk management capabilities. It is targeting Rs 1,000 crore in AUM by March 2027 while continuing to focus on credit assessment and portfolio quality.

Founded in 2021 by Subhash Chandra Acharya, Avishek Sarkar and Sumeet Dhall, Seeds Fincap provides credit to underserved individual and MSME borrowers. It offers loans ranging from Rs 50,000 to Rs 10 lakh and uses a cash flow based approach to assess borrowers.

Seeds Fincap closed FY25 and FY26 profitably and disbursed around Rs 620 crore in FY26. Its AUM stood at Rs 722 crore as of August 2026. The company has expanded to 164 branches and has more than 70,000 active members.

Seeds primarily serves nano enterprises and small businesses, where traditional credit assessment may not fully capture business cash flows. The company combines technology with field teams across sourcing, onboarding, credit assessment, documentation, collections and portfolio monitoring to provide loans to small business owners.

title: Unveilr AI raises pre-seed round from AJVC at Rs 16.7 Cr valuation
description: Mumbai based Unveilr AI has raised an undisclosed amount in a pre-seed round from Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC at a valuation of Rs 16.7 crore. Snippets
body: Mumbai based Unveilr AI has raised an undisclosed amount in a pre-seed round from Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC at a valuation of Rs 16.7 crore.

The startup will use the fresh capital to expand its engineering team and develop additional capabilities for its AI agents. It also plans to grow its sales team and expand its customer base across India, the UAE and the US.
Founded by Sanditya Srivastava, the startup helps B2B and consumer brands generate leads through Google and AI search platforms such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Claude.

Unveilr AI combines search engine optimisation (SEO) with Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO). Its AI agents track how brands appear across search engines, identify queries where competitors are recommended and analyse the sources used by AI platforms. Its team then works on content, technical changes and online authority to improve brand visibility.

The startup claims that its customers can start seeing results within the first month. For an Indian B2B legal services platform, Unveilr AI increased AI sourced traffic by around 4.7 times and leads by 5 times, along with an 80% increase in ChatGPT citations. For a D2C brand, organic search contributes around 27% of total revenue.
Launched in February 2026, Unveilr AI currently serves B2B and consumer brands across India, the UAE and the US. The company has a team comprising IIT alumni and SEO and AEO specialists.

title: Antler, Nikhil Kamath back healthtech startup Aignosis with Rs 4 Cr seed round
description: Jaipur based healthtech startup Aignosis has raised Rs 4 crore in a seed round led by Antler, Nikhil Kamath and angel investors including Varun Dua and IIMA Ventures. Snippets
body: Jaipur based healthtech startup Aignosis has raised Rs 4 crore in a seed round led by Antler, Nikhil Kamath and angel investors including Varun Dua and IIMA Ventures.
The firm plans to use the funding to expand its AI assisted autism and developmental screening platform across India.

Founded by Raksheet Jain and Divyansh Mangal, Aignosis raised its first round in 2024 from investors including Rajneesh Bhandari and Amit Jain. The startup has completed its CDSCO regulatory process and received Class B certification. It was also part of Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First 2025 cohort.

The brand’s screening system uses a standard laptop and webcam for children aged 16 months to nine years. A short video across nine stimulus modules is analysed using computer vision to assess behavioural signals such as gaze, response to name and reactions to facial expressions. The system generates a risk report indicating whether further clinical assessment may be required and does not provide a diagnosis.

It currently operates through a Clinic in Clinic model and is deployed across more than 20 government Primary Health Centres in Rajasthan. It has also partnered with Mankind Pharma, whose medical representatives are supporting screening camps with paediatricians across India. The company is starting operations with Apollo Shines across around 125 schools.
Aignosis claims to have completed more than 8,000 screenings so far and plans to conduct at least 1 lakh screenings by the end of FY27.

It will expand into Punjab, NCR, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Maharashtra, with the company focusing on building screening and referral access across government and private healthcare networks.

title: Former Elevation Capital investor Mayank Khanduja joins Bessemer Venture Partners as Partner
description: Bessemer Venture Partners has appointed Mayank Khanduja as Partner in its India practice, nearly nine months after he exited Elevation Capital following a 15 year stint.

title: Bangalore Watch Company raises $1.4 Mn in seed round from customers, family office, HNIs
description: Indian luxury watch brand Bangalore Watch Company (BWC) has raised $1.4 million in a seed round from a group of its customers, including family office principals. Snippets
body: Indian luxury watch brand Bangalore Watch Company (BWC) has raised $1.4 million in a seed round from a group of its customers, including family office principals and high-net-worth individuals from India and overseas.

The fresh capital will be used to expand BWC’s presence in the global independent watch market. It also plans to focus on two to three strategic overseas locations in markets with established watch collector communities, along with potentially one additional location in India.

Founded in 2018 by Nirupesh Joshi and Mercy Amalraj, BWC makes mechanical watches in India and exports them to more than 30 countries. Its collections are based on themes such as aviation, space, cricket and the outdoors, with a focus on modern Indian stories.

The company currently operates a single flagship boutique in Bengaluru and sells watches priced between Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 3 lakh. BWC has an annual production capacity of around 1,500 watches and plans to increase this fourfold over the next three to five years.
BWC has developed watches using materials such as recovered fighter-plane aluminium and aircraft carrier materials.

It has also developed its own Cerasteel material and made a watch that qualified for spaceflight. The brand has participated in Dubai Watch Week 2025 and Geneva Watch Days 2026, while its watches have been listed for the GPHG Awards three times.

title: SBI Mutual Fund raises Swiggy stake above 5% after Rs 300 Cr share purchase
description: SBI Mutual Fund has increased its stake in food delivery and quick commerce major Swiggy to over 5% after acquiring an additional 1.18 crore shares through a market purchase on September 29.
body: SBI Mutual Fund has increased its stake in food delivery and quick commerce major Swiggy to over 5% after acquiring an additional 1.18 crore shares through a market purchase on September 29.
The acquisition is valued at around Rs 300 crore, based on Swiggy’s closing price of Rs 253.70 on September 29. The filing, however, does not disclose the actual acquisition price.
According to a regulatory filing, SBI Mutual Fund, through its various schemes, acquired 1,18,38,465 shares, equivalent to a 0.4289% stake in Swiggy.
Before the transaction, SBI Mutual Fund held 12.97 crore shares, representing a 4.70% stake in the company. Following the purchase, its holding increased to 14.15 crore shares, or 5.12%.
The purchase took SBI Mutual Fund’s holding past the 5% threshold, triggering a disclosure under Regulation 29(1) of SEBI’s Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations.
SBI Funds Management submitted the disclosure to Swiggy, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and BSE on September 30.

The stake increase comes after Swiggy shareholders approved a 49.5% cap on aggregate foreign ownership at its AGM in August, clearing a key hurdle in its transition to an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC). Swiggy’s domestic ownership had crossed 50% in July, while foreign ownership stood at 49.76%.

In Q1 FY27, Swiggy reported 7% year-on-year increase in its operating revenue to Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 4,961 crore in Q1 FY25. The company also narrowed its losses by 34% to Rs 791 crore during the period.

title: Moneyview shares debut at 64% premium after 100X IPO subscription
description: Digital lending platform Moneyview made a strong debut on the stock exchanges on Thursday, with its shares listing at a premium of over 60% to the IPO price.
body: Digital lending platform Moneyview made a strong debut on the stock exchanges on Thursday, with its shares listing at a premium of over 60% to the IPO price.
Moneyview shares opened at Rs 55.61 on the BSE, up 63.6% from the issue price of Rs 34. On the NSE, the stock opened at Rs 55, marking a 61.8% premium.

The strong debut comes days after the fintech’s Rs 1,092 crore IPO was subscribed 98.46 times on the final day of bidding. The issue received particularly strong demand from qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), whose portion was subscribed 227.45 times. The non-institutional investor portion was subscribed 115.41 times, while the retail portion saw 19.57X subscription.

Moneyview had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 32-34 per share , valuing the company at nearly Rs 6,000 crore at the upper end. The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 750 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 10.05 crore shares worth around Rs 342 crore.

Of the fresh capital, Moneyview plans to use Rs 325 crore to support its lending operations, while another Rs 250 crore will be invested in strengthening the capital base of its NBFC subsidiary, Whizdm Finance.

The company reported Rs 3,351 crore in revenue and Rs 242 crore in profit in FY26. Its loan disbursals rose 31% to Rs 23,099 crore during the year, while its assets under management stood at Rs 22,520 crore as of June 2026.
Founded in 2014 by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview offers personal loans and other financial products including insurance, digital gold, credit cards and UPI services.
With the stock opening at around Rs 55, Moneyview's market capitalisation has moved significantly above the valuation implied by its IPO price.

title: TVS retains EV two-wheeler lead in September as Bajaj, Hero see strong growth
description: India’s electric two-wheeler registrations rose over 12% month on month to 2.07 lakh units in September, with TVS Motor retaining its lead while Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp recorded strong growth.
body: India’s electric two-wheeler market rebounded in September, with registrations rising over 12% month-on-month to 2.07 lakh units from 1.85 lakh units in August. TVS Motor retained its leadership, while legacy players, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp recorded strong growth during the month.

According to the latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the electric two-wheeler market with 53,989 registrations in September, accounting for a 26.06% market share. The company’s registrations increased 9.55% month on month from 49,284 units in August.
Bajaj Auto retained the second spot with 48,383 registrations and a 23.36% market share. Its registrations rose 17% month on month, with the company adding over 7,000 units compared to August.

Ather Energy ranked third with 30,479 registrations and a 14.71% market share. The company’s registrations in September grew nearly 5%  month-on-month compared to August, when it registered 29,068 units.

Hero MotoCorp recorded one of the strongest gains among the leading players, with registrations jumping 27% month on month to 24,306 units from 19,144 units in August. The company captured an 11.73% share of the market in September.

Ola Electric remained in fifth position with 13,449 registrations and a 6.49% market share. It was the only player among the top five to record a monthly decline, with registrations falling 3.53% from 13,941 units in August.

Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 9,316 registrations and a 4.5% market share, with registrations growing 8% month on month. River Mobility registered 5,549 units, a 6.4% gain from August, while BGauss remained largely flat with 5,023 registrations.

Among smaller players, Bounce Electric recorded a sharp increase, with registrations nearly tripling to 3,069 units from 1,049 units in August. E-Sprinto Green Energy also saw registrations surge to 1,997 units from just 120 units in the previous month.

title: PayMe nearly doubles monthly disbursals to Rs 200 Cr, targets Rs 2,000 Cr for FY27
description: The RBI-registered NBFC had crossed Rs 100 crore in monthly disbursals earlier and reached Rs 120 crore in July 2026. The company is now targeting more than Rs 2,000 crore in annual disbursals in FY27.
body: Noida-based fintech PayMe has nearly doubled its monthly loan disbursals to more than Rs 200 crore in September 2026, as it scales its lending operations.

The RBI-registered NBFC had crossed Rs 100 crore in monthly disbursals earlier and reached Rs 120 crore in July 2026. The company is now targeting more than Rs 2,000 crore in annual disbursals in FY27.

Founded in 2016 by Mahesh Shukla, PayMe offers personal loans, salary advances and business loans to salaried professionals, gig workers and self-employed individuals. The company uses AI-based underwriting for its lending operations and disbursed more than Rs 1,300 crore in FY26.

PayMe operates as the customer-facing lending platform, while Scale Up is its RBI-registered NBFC. Credit Assist provides an AI-based platform focused on credit health, while Huey Tech develops the technology and underwriting infrastructure used across the group.

The company plans to raise its monthly disbursal run rate to Rs 500 crore by the end of FY27. PayMe is also preparing to launch an investment and mentorship show for technology startups from Uttar Pradesh, which will provide funding and mentorship to selected founders.
Meanwhile, PayMe is preparing for an IPO in the coming year. The company said the proposed listing will support its next phase of growth as it expands its lending business and technology platform.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Sep 28 - Oct 3]
description: This week, 24 Indian startups raised $411.46 million across five growth-stage deals, 13 early-stage deals, and 6 undisclosed rounds. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 24 Indian startups raised $411.46 million across five growth-stage deals, 13 early-stage deals, and 6 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 3 key appointments, one fund launch and three mergers & acquisitions and one ESOP buyback.
In contrast, 17 startups had collectively secured about $188.49 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised $357 million across just five deals this week. Electric two-wheeler maker Simple Energy led with a $182 million Series C round, followed by physical AI company SiMa.ai with $150 million.

Balwaan Krishi raised Rs 100 crore in Series B funding, while Seeds Fincap secured over Rs 100 crore. Quick-commerce fulfillment startup Blitz also raised Rs 28.7 crore in a pre-Series B round led by IvyCap Ventures.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $54.36 million across 13 deals this week. Premium home interior materials startup Gravity led with $15 million in equity and debt funding, followed by edtech startup Arivihan with $10 million.
Arovia Consumer secured a Rs 100 crore capital commitment from Fireside Ventures, while beauty and wellness startup Amaani and Bharat Housing Network raised $5 million each.

title: Nykaa expects around 30% GMV growth in Q2 FY27
description: FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, expects its consolidated GMV to grow close to 30% YoY in Q2 FY27.
body: FSN E-Commerce Ventures, the parent company of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, expects its consolidated GMV to grow close to 30% year-on-year in the quarter ended September 2026.

According to the company’s quarterly business update, consolidated NSV is expected to grow in the early thirties, while net revenue growth is projected to be in the late twenties. The growth was led by continued momentum in the beauty business and the increasing scale of its fashion vertical.

Nykaa’s beauty vertical is expected to post NSV and net revenue growth in the late twenties, as per the release. Its retail network expanded by 14 net new stores during the quarter, taking the total store count to 338 as of September-end.

The fashion vertical continued to gain momentum, with NSV expected to grow in the late forties and net revenue in the early forties. Nykaa said new customer acquisition remained a key growth driver for the fashion business.
It added more than 250 brands across categories during the quarter, while its partnership with Nike continued to see encouraging early traction through exclusive product drops.

Nykaa reported a 29% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 2,782 crore in Q1 FY27, while its profit surged 3.3X to Rs 80 crore. The beauty segment contributed Rs 2,516 crore, while fashion brought in Rs 253 crore during the quarter.

Meanwhile, Nykaa recently partnered with BOLD , the corporate venture capital arm of L’Oréal, to jointly invest in emerging Indian beauty and personal care brands. The partnership will target high-growth startups and provide them with capital, strategic mentorship, and access to Nykaa’s retail and distribution capabilities.

title: Bhavish Aggarwal pledges 4.32% Ola Electric stake to fund rights issue
description: Ola Electric promoter Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake in the electric two-wheeler maker to fund his participation in the company’s upcoming rights issue.
body: Ola Electric promoter Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake in the electric two-wheeler maker to fund his participation in the company’s upcoming rights issue.

As per the filing with the National Stock Exchange, the pledge has been created solely to fund Aggarwal’s subscription to the rights issue approved by Ola Electric’s board. No shares are being sold as part of the transaction.
Ola Electric’s board had approved a rights issue of up to Rs 1,000 crore on September 28. The company subsequently filed its Draft Letter of Offer with the exchanges.
However, the company’s latest statement does not disclose the amount being raised by Aggarwal against the pledged shares or the exact amount he plans to invest in the rights issue.

The move comes at a time when Ola Electric is looking to strengthen its financial position amid pressure on its business. The company’s operating revenue declined 45% year-on-year to Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27, from Rs 828 crore in the year-ago quarter. Its EV registrations also fell 25% to 43,908 units during the quarter. However, the company narrowed its net loss by 21.1% to Rs 336 crore during the quarter.

Ola Electric had also raised Rs 780 crore through a qualified institutional placement (QIP) in June, after its board approved the fundraise to strengthen the company’s balance sheet and support its growth plans.

The latest rights issue will give existing shareholders another opportunity to put fresh money into the company, while Aggarwal is using a portion of his existing stake as collateral to fund his participation.

The company, which went public in August 2024, has been expanding its electric two-wheeler portfolio and manufacturing capabilities as it competes with established players such as TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto, as well as Ather Energy.

title: Marico acquires 24.09% additional stake in Plix parent for Rs 1,012 Cr
description: FMCG major Marico has acquired an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals, the parent company of plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix.
body: FMCG major Marico has acquired an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals, the parent company of plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix, for Rs 1,012.03 Cr.
The acquisition increases Marico’s stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals from 60% to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis. The transaction was completed on October 5.
Marico had acquired a 60% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals through earlier transactions and had the right to acquire the remaining 40% stake under definitive agreements.

As part of the latest transaction, Marico has entered into definitive agreements to acquire a total of 38.18% stake from the founders and certain other shareholders. The remaining 14.09% stake is expected to be acquired in July 2027, subject to the terms of the agreements.

The remaining stake will be acquired for a consideration to be determined at that time. It will comprise a base consideration of up to Rs 592 Cr along with additional consideration linked to milestones and other terms.
With the latest acquisition, Marico’s aggregate consideration for its 84.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals stands at Rs 1,392.07 Cr. The transaction is being carried out in cash.

Satiya Nutraceuticals, incorporated in February 2020 and headquartered in Mumbai, owns The Plant Fix, or Plix, a plant-based nutrition and personal care brand. The company operates in the health, wellness and personal care segment.
Satiya Nutraceuticals reported a consolidated turnover of Rs 864.31 Cr in FY26, up from Rs 432.84 Cr in FY25 and Rs 155.32 Cr in FY24.

title: Flipkart picks minority stake in TravClan to expand international travel offerings
description: The investment will help Flipkart expand its international travel supply and holiday packages, along with on ground support for customers. TravClan operates a B2B travel platform
body: Flipkart has picked up a minority stake in travel tech platform TravClan as it looks to strengthen its international travel offerings through Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel. The financial details of the transaction were not disclosed.

The investment will help Flipkart strengthen its international travel supply and expand holiday packages available to customers across Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel. TravClan operates a B2B travel platform with direct supplier listings across domestic and international destinations.
Its technology platform enables more than 15,000 travel agents to customise and book real time packages, hotels and activities. The platform also provides 24/7 on ground customer support.

Through the partnership, Cleartrip and Flipkart Travel will gain access to TravClan’s partner network, technology and destination operations. This will allow the two platforms to offer a wider range of international holiday packages with on ground assistance.

Nishant Verman, SVP, Corporate Development and Partnerships, Flipkart, said the investment will strengthen the company’s ability to offer international holiday packages while deepening its travel capabilities.

TravClan cofounder and CEO Arun Bagaria said India is becoming one of the largest outbound travel markets and the partnership with Flipkart will help the company take affordable travel products to more Indian travellers.

The funding will support investments in global supply, technology and destination expansion as TravClan scales its platform. The company will also expand its teams across business development, engineering and destination operations.

The deal comes shortly after Flipkart Ventures backed AI startups Alive and Keploy in September. Alive focuses on AI powered lifestyle experiences, while Keploy develops AI driven software testing tools.

title: Exclusive: QpiAI raises Rs 50 Cr in debt from InnoVen Capital
description: Bengaluru-based quantum computing and artificial intelligence startup QpiAI has raised Rs 50 Cr in debt (non-convertible debentures ) funding from InnoVen Capital.
body: Bengaluru-based quantum computing and artificial intelligence startup QpiAI has raised Rs 50 Cr in debt funding from InnoVen Capital.

The board at QpiAI has approved the issuance of 5,000 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at a face value of Rs 1 lakh each to raise Rs 50 crore from InnoVen Capital, as per its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
According to the filing, the debentures carry a 13.85% annual coupon rate and are set to mature by December 1, 2028. The company has not disclosed how it will use the debt proceeds.

The Bengaluru-based company previously raised $32 million (around Rs 279 Cr) in a Series A round in July 2025, led by Avataar Ventures and the National Quantum Mission (NQM). As per Entrackr’s estimate, the company is valued at around Rs 2,050 Cr or $215 million during the round.

Founded in 2019 by Nagendra Nagaraja, Bengaluru-based QpiAI is a deeptech startup building quantum computing and AI solutions for enterprises. The company develops proprietary quantum hardware and software for applications across drug discovery, manufacturing, finance, pharma, and materials science.
It has developed a 25-qubit quantum computer and is working towards a 64-qubit system, with a roadmap to scale to 1,000 qubits by 2030.

QpiAI has yet to file its FY26 financials. During the fiscal year ended March 2025, it remained at a pre-revenue stage, with operating revenue of around Rs 2 Cr, while its losses increased to Rs 16.67 Cr in the same period.

title: Indifi posts Rs 371 Cr revenue in FY26; turns profitable
description: MSME-focused digital lending platform Indifi Technologies turned profitable in FY26 despite marginal revenue growth, as a sharp decline in impairment costs and tighter control over operating expenses boosted its bottom line.
body: MSME-focused digital lending platform Indifi Technologies turned profitable in FY26 despite marginal revenue growth, as a sharp decline in impairment costs and tighter control over operating expenses boosted its bottom line.

Indifi’s revenue from operations increased only 3% year-on-year to Rs 371.1 crore in FY26 from Rs 360.4 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2015, Indifi provides debt financing to MSMEs, with a focus on improving credit access for small businesses. The company offers loans across supply chain finance, startup lending, D2C businesses, and other lending products tailored to the financing needs of MSMEs.
As per the company, it has served more than 1.6 lakh MSMEs across 400 cities. Including other non–operating income, its total income stood at Rs 386.85 crore during the year.

Being a lending platform, interest earned on loans remained Indifi’s primary source of revenue, which accounted for 87% of its operating income, and increased only 2.4% to Rs 321.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 314.3 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Revenue from the sale of services grew 19% to Rs 25.3 crore during the year. This included facilitation, service fees earned from lending partners and foreclosure fees. Other fees and commissions income also increased 11% to Rs 12.4 crore in FY26.

On the cost side, finance costs remained Indifi’s largest expense at Rs 147.4 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 142.6 crore in FY25. For a lending business, these costs largely relate to the capital used to fund its loan book.

Impairment on financial instruments nearly halved to Rs 55.3 crore from Rs 107.6 crore in FY25. In its press note, Indifi attributed the improvement to healthier credit performance, sharper customer selection and closer portfolio management, which helped reduce credit costs by nearly 40% during FY26.

title: Sales hiring startup Scooter raises Rs 1.5 Cr pre-seed round
description: Pune based sales hiring startup Scooter has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed round led by Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC. The proceeds will be used. Snippets
body: Pune based sales hiring startup Scooter has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed round led by Aviral Bhatnagar’s AJVC.
The proceeds will be used for its product and simplify the sales hiring process for candidates and hiring managers.
Founded in 2024 by Kartik Mandrekar and Saumya Seth, Scooter helps startups hire sales professionals by assessing candidates on real sales scenarios instead of relying primarily on CVs.
Mandrekar has previously led sales teams at Gartner, Shoptimize and Graas, while Seth is a behavioural scientist with a master’s degree from the University of Pennsylvania.

The platform sources verified sales professionals, assesses them through real sales scenarios and provides hiring managers with a shortlist of three to five candidates. Managers can review short video clips from assessments before viewing a candidate’s CV. One customer has made a sales hire through Scooter in six days.
Scooter currently works with more than 50 companies and has added 14 customers in recent months.
It has built a pool of over 10,000 sales candidates.

The investment is AJVC’s first in a Pune based startup. AJVC is a pre-seed fund led by Aviral Bhatnagar. Scooter is focused on helping startups and sales teams reduce the time involved in finding and evaluating sales candidates.

title: Snapdeal parent AceVector lists at 11.5% discount to IPO price
description: AceVector made a weak debut on the stock exchanges on Monday, October 5, with its shares listing at a discount of around 12% to the IPO price.
body: AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce platform Snapdeal, made a weak debut on the stock exchanges on Monday, October 5, with its shares listing at a discount of around 12% to the IPO price.
The company’s shares opened at Rs 28.32 on the NSE, compared with the issue price of Rs 32, an 11.5% discount. On the BSE, the stock opened at Rs 28.30, down 11.56% from the IPO price.

The weak debut came despite AceVector’s Rs 420 crore IPO receiving strong investor interest. The issue was subscribed around 5 times during its three-day bidding period, with the retail portion subscribed 4.83 times and the non-institutional investor category receiving 8.53 times subscription.
The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of Rs 133 crore. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 30-32 per share.
SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and other existing investors partially offloaded their stakes through the OFS, while co-founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal did not sell any shares in the IPO.

AceVector plans to use a portion of the IPO proceeds to fund marketing and promotional expenses for its marketplace business. Around Rs 132 crore has been earmarked for this purpose, while another Rs 50 crore will go towards technology infrastructure. The remaining funds will be used for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
AceVector operates Snapdeal along with e-commerce enablement platforms such as Uniware, Shipway and Convertway. It also owns consumer brands under Stellaro Brands.

The company’s financial performance improved in FY26. Its total income rose 32% year-on-year to Rs 538 crore from Rs 407 crore in FY25. At the same time, its net loss narrowed sharply to Rs 45 crore from Rs 126 crore a year earlier.

title: FirstCry-backed Swara Baby Products gets SEBI nod for Rs 1,000 Cr IPO
description: Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products, has received approval from the SEBI for its proposed Rs 1,000 crore IPO.
body: Swara Baby Products, a contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed Rs 1,000 crore initial public offering (IPO).

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 500 crore. FirstCry parent Brainbees Solutions will sell shares worth Rs 300 crore, while Anadya Bon Merchari LLP will offload shares worth Rs 200 crore.
The company had filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI earlier this year in July.

Swara Baby plans to use Rs 198.2 crore from the fresh proceeds to set up a new manufacturing facility in Madhya Pradesh, while Rs 100 crore will be used to repay certain borrowings. Another Rs 27.5 crore will be invested in subsidiaries Solis Hygiene, Swara Hygiene and KAEHPL for debt repayment. The remaining proceeds will be used for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
The company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 100 crore in consultation with its bankers.

Founded in 2018, Swara Baby manufactures baby diapers, adult diapers, sanitary napkins and panty liners. Its corporate promoter, FirstCry parent Brainbees Solutions, is also one of its key customers, alongside Piramal Pharma and Himalaya Wellness. The company also sells baby diapers under its Cuddles brand and adult diapers under the Shield brand.

According to its DRHP, Swara Baby was India’s largest hygiene contract manufacturer by value in FY25. It held a 37% share of the baby diaper contract manufacturing market and an estimated 36% share of the adult diaper contract manufacturing segment.

Swara Baby’s operating revenue grew 23% to Rs 1,163.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 942.97 crore in FY25, while its profit increased 18% to Rs 95.58 crore. EBITDA stood at Rs 192.77 crore during the year, compared with Rs 162.72 crore in FY25.

title: India’s NDude Labs leads $3 Mn Series A in US wellness brand SuperMush
description: India and US-based healthcare and wellness investment firm NDude Labs has led a $3 million Series A funding round in US-based functional wellness brand SuperMush.
body: India and US-based healthcare and wellness investment firm NDude Labs has led a $3 million Series A funding round in US-based functional wellness brand SuperMush.
The fresh capital will be used to expand SuperMush’s product portfolio, invest in formulations and strengthen its team and customer support infrastructure.

Founded in 2022 by Alli Schaper and Brian Friedman, SuperMush develops wellness products using ingredients such as nootropics, adaptogens and functional mushrooms. Its portfolio includes Shilajit, Creatine and Lion’s Mane gummies.

Over the past year, SuperMush has expanded to more than 1,000 Target stores. It now has a retail presence across more than 2,000 stores in the US, including Target and Sprouts, along with sales through its website and Amazon.
The company plans to expand its presence across retail, direct-to-consumer and marketplace channels while investing in new products and formulations.
For NDude Labs, the investment comes after its recent investment in nutraceutical ingredients company Nutriventia. The firm invests in healthcare and wellness businesses across India and the US.

title: Sauce leads Rs 15 Cr funding round in kitchen and bathroom brand Lorazzo
description: The fresh funds will be used to expand its product portfolio, invest in product development, build its team, strengthen its online and offline channels, and expand its
body: Lorazzo, a design-led kitchen and bathroom brand, has raised Rs 15 crore in a funding round led by Sauce, with follow-on investment from Sprout Venture Partners and participation from Panthera Peak and Alteria Capital.

The fresh funds will be used to expand its product portfolio, invest in product development, build its team, strengthen its online and offline channels, and expand its presence across more states in India, Lorazzo said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by Jatin Luthra and Saurabh Gupta, Lorazzo is an Indian kitchen and bathroom brand focused on combining design, technology and functionality across everyday home products.

The company offers products across faucets, sinks, shower systems, bidets, wash basins, smart toilets and other kitchen and bathroom categories. Lorazzo is building an omnichannel business across ecommerce, quick commerce and offline retail, with a focus on making traditionally functional home categories more consumer-centric and design-focused.

Lorazzo’s product range includes the Intelli Smart Commode, a cleansing WC with a heated seat, electronically operated bidets, an air dryer, ambient lighting and digital temperature control. The product is priced at Rs 58,999, compared with Rs 1.5 lakh to Rs 5 lakh for comparable cleansing toilets from international brands.
Lorazzo offers up to 20 years of warranty on products across kitchen sinks, sanitaryware, mirrors, cabinets and faucets. It also provides pan-India onsite installation and service.
The brand has grown its revenue six times over the past 12 months and is targeting Rs 100 crore in revenue over the next two years.

title: IAN Angel Fund leads Rs 5 Cr round in deeptech textile startup IndigoTex
description: IIT Delhi-originated deeptech textile startup IndigoTex has raised Rs 5 crore in a funding round led by IAN Angel. Snippets
body: IIT Delhi-originated deeptech textile startup IndigoTex has raised Rs 5 crore in a funding round led by IAN Angel Fund. SIDBI, FITT and IIT Delhi Angels also participated in the round.
The proceeds will be used to set up manufacturing, expand its sales and operations team and commercialise its textile products.

Founded in 2024 by Satendra Singh, Prof. B.S. Butola and Dilip Singh, IndigoTex is developing waterless wool finishing technology and wool based fabrics. Its IndiWool Denim combines wool with denim, with variants ranging from fabrics with lower wool content for all weather use to wool rich fabrics for colder climates.

The company is also developing ECOTEX Wool, a technology for washable wool and poly wool fabrics. IndigoTex has set up a finishing facility in Rai Industrial Area, Sonipat, Haryana, while its R&D operations continue at the Research and Innovation Park at IIT Delhi.

IndigoTex has signed NDAs with Ralph Lauren and Kering Group in France and is in discussions with premium and luxury brands, garment manufacturers, fabric exporters and sourcing companies. It has also started engagements across Europe and cold climate markets such as Australia, with discussions in France, Russia and Denmark.
IndigoTex was among 120 startups selected for Bharat Innovates 2026 in Nice, France, and at the BRICS Summit 2026.

title: Medical tourism startup CureMeAbroad raises $1.1 Mn in pre Seed funding
description: The platform combines healthcare discovery, treatment planning, pricing transparency and patient assistance. It currently attracts more than 22,500 visitors a month and
body: CureMeAbroad, a global healthcare platform that helps patients discover, verify and book treatments at vetted hospitals abroad, has raised $1.1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by healthcare-focused venture capital fund SteerX Ventures. Existing investor AIRA also participated in the round.
