Earlier in April this year, the Pune-based startup raised $600K from Roman Saini, Himanshu Ratnoo, Kunal Gupta, Devaiah Bopanna, Vikrant Potnis and AIRA.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its accredited hospital network, enter new patient source markets, strengthen its AI-powered technology and build its operations and technology teams. CureMeAbroad also plans to expand into non-elective specialties such as orthopaedics and oncology and explore physical experience centres in key international markets.

Founded in June 2025 by Aditya Oza and Mikhail Bohra, CureMeAbroad is a healthcare-tech platform that helps international patients discover and compare hospitals, verify healthcare providers, get treatment estimates and book care across destinations.

The platform combines healthcare discovery, treatment planning, pricing transparency and patient assistance. It currently attracts more than 22,500 visitors a month and has a hospital network across six countries.

According to CureMeAbroad, the startup is targeting $100 million in annual patient treatment bookings by FY2028, compared with its current $4.8 million run rate. Its key patient source markets include the US, UK, Australia and Canada.
The company competes with platforms such as Bookimed, PlacidWay, The Medical Tourism Company and Medical Departures.

Vaidam Health is another Indian medical tourism platform that helps international patients find hospitals and treatment options. CureMeAbroad has also received Medical Travel Facilitator Certification from Global Healthcare Accreditation, with its network spanning more than 400 accredited hospitals across six countries, according to GHA.

title: Refurbished electronics platform ReFit Global raises $1 Mn in seed round
description: Its technology-enabled processes cover device diagnostics, automated quality checks, grading, post-quality-control processes and inventory management. ReFit said these
body: Refurbished electronics platform ReFit Global has raised $1 million in a seed funding round from a UAE-based family office. The company was also featured on Shark Tank India Season 3.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its retail footprint, strengthen refurbishment capabilities, invest in technology infrastructure and build an integrated omnichannel platform, ReFit Global said in a press release.

Founded in 2018 by Saket Saurav and Avneet Singh, ReFit Global operates across refurbishment, distribution, retail and related consumer channels. The company aims to build an integrated ecosystem for refurbished electronics by combining technology, refurbishment capabilities, distribution infrastructure and omnichannel retail.

The Delhi-based company claims to have a distribution network of over 75 distributors, more than 2,000 wholesalers and over 50,000 retail outlets across India. The network gives ReFit access to metropolitan centres as well as Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

ReFit Global has also expanded its physical retail presence through 12 ReFit Xpress outlets alongside its B2B distribution network. Its business spans online marketplaces, offline retail and brand relationships, with sourcing and sales relationships involving platforms such as Flipkart and Amazon, along with other offline and strategic channels.

The company also plans to expand its B2B and D2C initiatives across the refurbished electronics value chain. ReFit currently reports a 92% refurbishment yield and repair capabilities up to L4, including advanced chip-level repairs.

Its technology-enabled processes cover device diagnostics, automated quality checks, grading, post-quality-control processes and inventory management. ReFit said these capabilities are designed to improve consistency, operational visibility and reliability across refurbished devices.
India’s refurbished smartphone volumes grew 13% year-on-year in H1 2026, while the organised segment accounted for around 20% of the market, indicating scope for further formalisation.

title: CurvetAI raises Rs 6 Cr pre-seed round led by Merak Ventures
description: Pune-based AI startup CurvetAI has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed round led by Merak Ventures, with participation from angel investors. Snippets
body: Pune-based AI startup CurvetAI has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed round led by Merak Ventures, with participation from angel investors.
The fresh capital will be used to expand CurvetAI’s engineering and technology infrastructure and develop agent based capabilities that can handle more complex workflows.

Founded in December 2025 by Vivek Dubey and Utkarsh Gupta, CurvetAI operates an AI workspace that brings multiple AI models onto a single platform. Users can work with text, image, audio and video models, compare outputs and combine different capabilities within the same workflow.

The startup currently has more than 1 lakh monthly users globally, with India and the US being its largest markets. It has also started generating revenue. The platform is used by individuals, teams and educational institutions.

CurvetAI initially started as a platform for discovering AI tools and prompts. It later shifted towards a workspace after the founders found that users still had to leave the platform to use the tools they discovered.
Dubey previously worked at Infosys, Microsoft and Google, while Gupta has worked at Samsung and leads the company’s engineering and technical infrastructure.
The firm now works with AI model developers and has collaborations with GnaniAI, Rumik AI and Alibaba.

title: Kinetic Age raises $250K from AJVC, Agrasar Ventures
description: Bengaluru-based healthtech startup Kinetic Age has raised around $250,000 in a funding round led by AJVC and Agrasar Ventures. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based healthtech startup Kinetic Age has raised around $250,000 in a funding round led by AJVC and Agrasar Ventures.

The fresh capital will be used to expand Kinetic Age’s healthcare offering and reach more customers. It plans to build its model around personalised and coordinated care for adults over 40, with a focus on helping users maintain their health through regular interventions and follow through.
Founded by Akshat Saxena and Amogh Saxena, the company provides coordinated healthcare services for adults aged 40 and above.

Kinetic Age combines doctor consultations, physiotherapy, physical training, nutrition, diagnostics and emotional wellbeing under a single subscription and care plan. The company aims to help users follow healthcare recommendations through regular support and tracking.

The startup claims to have served more than 600 patients in Bengaluru over the past year. It has delivered more than 12,000 sessions and now conducts over 150 sessions daily. The company has also reported more than 70% monthly retention and an NPS of over 75.

Kinetic Age has crossed Rs 2.5 crore in annual revenue run rate. It uses AI driven care protocols and has a network of 25 providers. Around one in three customers comes through referrals, according to the company.

title: Fireside leads Rs 110 Cr Series B round in Beyond Appliances
description: According to Beyond Appliances, it has expanded its portfolio across Android chimneys, Plug-N-Play chimneys, smart hobs, and cooktops, while strengthening its presence
body: Beyond Appliances, a smart kitchen technology company building intelligent appliances for modern Indian homes, has raised Rs 110 crore ($11.4 million) in a Series B funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital and other investors.

The Bengaluru-based company had previously secured $4 million in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital, in August last year. It also raised $2 million in its seed round led by Fireside Ventures in November 2024.

The proceeds will be deployed towards research and development and the establishment of a new manufacturing plant, strengthening the company’s ability to develop and scale its next generation of kitchen appliances, Beyond Appliances said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by Eshwar K Vikas and Rakesh Patil, Beyond Appliances is a smart kitchen appliance brand that combines technology with practical functionality to develop kitchen products for modern homes.

According to Beyond Appliances, it has expanded its portfolio across Android chimneys, Plug-N-Play chimneys, smart hobs, and cooktops, while strengthening its presence across India and increasing consumer engagement as it scales its operations.

The brand said it is witnessing strong referral-led sales, with 15% of its revenue coming through customer references, while its flagship kitchen appliance range continues to be its primary revenue driver. It has also doubled its marketplace market share over the last one year, reflecting increased consumer adoption across online channels.

Beyond Appliances also operates through offline retail channels and experience centres across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad. The company plans to expand its offline presence to 10 additional cities over the next three years. Over the same period, the brand aims to achieve Rs 500 crore in ARR while building a portfolio focused exclusively on kitchen appliances.

Smart kitchen technology is emerging as a segment within India’s consumer-tech and home-appliance startup ecosystem, as urban households increasingly seek connected, convenient, and energy-efficient cooking solutions.

title: Mamaearth parent Honasa eyes over 30% NSV growth in Q2 FY27
description: Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer expects its net sales value (NSV) to grow in the early-thirties year-on-year in Q2 FY27, driven by strong growth across its brands.
body: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, expects its net sales value (NSV) to grow in the early-thirties year-on-year during the second quarter of FY27, as the beauty and personal care company continues the momentum seen in the previous quarter.
The company attributed the expected growth to broad-based traction across its focus categories and brands, according to a quarterly update filed with the stock exchanges.

Mamaearth, Honasa’s largest brand, is expected to post high-teens YoY growth in NSV during the quarter ended September 2026. The company said the growth was supported by higher brand affinity and expansion of its offline footprint.

Meanwhile, Honasa’s younger brands, which include The Derma Co., Aqualogica, BBlunt, Dr. Sheth’s, Staze, Lumineve and Reginald Men, are expected to record around mid-forties YoY growth in NSV during the quarter.

The offline channel continued to lead Honasa’s growth, with both general trade and modern trade expected to post strong growth. The company attributed the performance to deeper direct distribution in general trade and better execution at the point of sale. Its online business is also expected to maintain growth momentum during the quarter.
On the profitability front, Honasa expects to maintain an early double-digit operating margin profile in Q2 FY27, with strong year-on-year improvement during the quarter.

The company clarified that the quarterly update is provisional and subject to limited review by its statutory auditors. Detailed Q2 FY27 financial results will be released following approval from its board.
In Q1 FY27, Honasa Consumer’s operating revenue grew 27% year-on-year to Rs 756 crore , while its profit more than doubled to Rs 90 crore during the quarter.

title: Pizza brand The Dough Therapy raises Rs 5.25 Cr in seed round
description: he fresh capital will be used to expand its presence in Mumbai and support its multi market growth strategy. Of the total funds, 60% will be allocated towards expansio
body: Gourmet pizza brand The Dough Therapy has raised Rs 5.25 crore at a valuation of Rs 35 crore in a seed funding round led by Michigan Capital Advisors, formerly known as Melwani Finance, with participation from Equiglobe Investment.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its presence in Mumbai and support its multi market growth strategy. Of the total funds, 60% will be allocated towards expansion, 15% towards marketing and the remaining 25% towards supply chain infrastructure, centralised operations and kitchen technology, The Dough Therapy said in a press release.

Founded in 2020 by Abhishek Dedhia, Mohit Chheda and Gaurav Majrekar, The Dough Therapy has grown from one outlet to 10 outlets across Mumbai. The brand offers more than 30 varieties of vegetarian and vegan gourmet pizzas.
The brand said it has built a mix of new and returning customers, providing a base for its next phase of expansion.
The Dough Therapy plans to expand to 20 outlets over the next 12 months. It also plans to enter new cities across India with its gourmet pizza offering.
The brand will use a mix of company owned outlets, select dine in formats and franchise partnerships as part of its expansion strategy.

title: Energy management platform Ionage raises $1.3 Mn in pre Series A round
description: The fresh funds will be used to expand coverage to 100% of active EV charging networks in India, improve charger discovery and payments for EV users, and help small and
body: AI enabled energy management platform Ionage has raised $1.3 million in a pre Series A funding round co-led by strategic investors and a consortium of CXOs from energy and infrastructure companies.

The fresh funds will be used to expand coverage to 100% of active EV charging networks in India, improve charger discovery and payments for EV users, and help small and mid sized charge point operators (CPOs) set up and manage station operations, Ionage said in a press release.

Founded in 2021 by Vimal Kumar V, Vijith Kumar V, and Varun Chandran, Ionage is building an EV charging operating system that connects charge point operators, charger manufacturers, real estate owners and EV users. The platform enables drivers to discover, access and pay for charging across different charging networks.

According to the Bengaluru based startup, it has onboarded more than 25,000 four wheeler charge points and supports over 63 fleets across the country. It has a network of more than 75 charging partners and uses charger mapping and roaming capabilities to connect charging infrastructure across networks.
Ionage said it is on track to process more than 20 million units of energy per month over the next 12 months, supported by monthly growth of over 25%.

The startup operates across more than 70% of India’s charging hardware and connects with major EV charging manufacturers at the point of installation. Its solutions cater to offices, malls, hospitality businesses and residential housing societies.
Ionage currently operates across 33 states and Union Territories and nearly 3,000 cities. It plans to develop and support CPO micro clusters in Tier 2 cities over the next 18 months.

India’s EV charging infrastructure needs to grow more than 40 times by 2030 to meet demand, according to research by CII and ORF. The country will require more than 1.32 million public chargers by 2030 to support the expected 30 million plus electric two wheelers and four wheelers on the road.

title: Tanglin Venture leads Rs 16.1 Cr seed round in debt resolution platform Credfix
description: The platform has three key AI-led solutions: Risi, an AI financial assistant; Neytra, an AI call shield; and an AI legal assistant. Risi helps borrowers understand their
body: AI-first debt resolution platform Credfix has raised Rs 16.1 crore in a seed funding round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with participation from Stargazer.
Before this round, Credfix had raised Rs 4.5 crore from K2 Capital, Invstt Trust and a group of angel investors.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate product development, strengthen its AI capabilities and expand its borrower support network across India, Credfix said in a press release.

Founded in 2025 by Ranjan Agarwal, Neeraj Kulkarni and Ayush Kedia, Credfix is an AI-powered financial recovery platform that helps borrowers understand their debt, assess repayment options and navigate interactions with lenders. Its offerings include debt assessment, loan resolution, loan consolidation and AI-powered legal assistance.

The platform has three key AI-led solutions: Risi, an AI financial assistant; Neytra, an AI call shield; and an AI legal assistant. Risi helps borrowers understand their debt and explore resolution options, while Neytra assists with recovery-related calls. The legal assistant helps borrowers understand legal notices, prepare draft responses for their review and identify possible next steps.

Credfix said it aims to support borrowers across the debt resolution lifecycle, from early signs of financial distress to structured resolution and financial rehabilitation. The platform helps users assess their financial obligations, evaluate available options, communicate with lenders and understand legal notices.
The startup claims to currently serve more than 2 lakh borrowers representing over Rs 4,000 crore in aggregate outstanding debt. Around 40% of its users are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

The debt resolution and collections segment has seen growing technology adoption in India. FREED, a borrower-focused debt relief platform, raised Rs 60 crore in February 2026 in a round led by Aavishkaar Capital. It had previously raised Rs 60 crore in a Series A round in 2024.

title: Med-tech startup Sunfox Technologies raises $7 Mn in Series A round
description: Over the past decade, Sunfox has developed a portfolio of Spandan ECG solutions spanning personal, clinical and institutional settings, with applications ranging from at-
body: Sunfox Technologies, the Dehradun-based medtech company behind the Spandan portable ECG platform, has raised $7 million (approx. Rs 67 crore) in a Series A funding round co-led by Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital.

The startup had previously raised Rs 15 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Venture Catalysts, with participation from Finvolve through the IA Growth Opportunities Fund I and Brew Opportunities Fund, Universal Group, RP Singhvi Group and others in August 2024. It also secured investments from all five Sharks in the first season of Shark Tank India.

The fresh funds will be used for the next phase of growth, including expanding its presence across India, developing global go-to-market capabilities, scaling the organisation and continuing investments in research and development, Sunfox said in a press release.

Founded in 2016 by Rajat Jain, Arpit Jain, Saurabh Badola, Nitin Chandola and Sabit Rawat, Sunfox Technologies develops portable and AI-enabled healthcare solutions, with a focus on diagnostic access, particularly in cardiac care.

Its flagship Spandan series is a portable, medical-grade ECG platform designed for use across hospitals, clinics, telemedicine networks and home-based patient monitoring. The platform enables ECGs to be recorded closer to patients and can flag cardiac patterns that may require further medical attention.

Over the past decade, Sunfox has developed a range of Spandan ECG solutions for personal, clinical and institutional use, with applications across home-based ECG recording, clinics, hospitals, public-health programmes and remote-care networks.

Sunfox said it has expanded its presence to more than 15 countries, while its products have reached healthcare providers across more than 1,800 PIN codes in India. Its technology can also be deployed through a hub-and-spoke model in public-health systems.

The company said around 60,000 Spandan devices have been deployed across India, covering more than 20,000 villages across states and union territories. Its Spandan One platform has been used to screen approximately 5 million patients annually.

title: Agentic AI startup Desible.ai raises Rs 32 Cr led by Prime Venture Partners
description: Bengaluru based AI startup Desible.ai has raised Rs 32 crore in a seed plus round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Invention Engine. Snippets
body: Bengaluru based AI startup Desible.ai has raised Rs 32 crore in a seed plus round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Invention Engine.
The proceeds will be used to expand its agentic AI capabilities, strengthen compliance infrastructure and accelerate product development for the BFSI sector.

Founded in 2025 by Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar, Desible.ai provides an agentic workflow orchestration platform for banks, NBFCs and insurance companies. The platform helps automate customer engagement, servicing, operations and compliance workflows, starting with voice and expanding to WhatsApp, SMS and email.

Desible.ai currently works with more than 40 BFSI institutions and runs over 25 agentic workflows across revenue, risk and compliance, collections, underwriting, service and claims. The company said its platform handles more than 1 crore customer engagements every month and integrates with existing enterprise systems.
The startup is built around deterministic decision-making, with workflows designed to ensure that disclosures, consent and escalations follow predefined rules and remain auditable.
Its use cases include collections, lead qualification, renewal management, claims intimation, welcome calling, TeleMER and cross-sell.

title: Edtech startup byteXL raises $9 Mn in funding round led by Elevar Equity
description: Edtech startup byteXL has raised $9 million in its latest funding round led by Elevar Equity, with participation from existing investors Kalaari Capital. Snippets
body: Edtech startup byteXL has raised $9 million in its latest funding round led by Elevar Equity, with participation from existing investors Kalaari Capital and the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation.
The latest round follows byteXL’s $5.9 million Series A raised in July 2024 from Kalaari Capital and the Dell Foundation.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its institutional network, strengthen its AI and technology platform, and develop new skilling programmes. byteXL also plans to invest in AI enabled learning and assessment, student analytics and personalised learning tools.

Founded by brothers Karun and Sricharan Tadepalli, byteXL works with engineering colleges, particularly in tier 2 and tier 3 cities, to provide technology and AI skills alongside regular academic education.
Its model combines industry aligned curriculum, practical learning, technology platforms and trained educators within college programmes.

The company claims 7,600 byteXL graduates were placed in IT and engineering roles last year. It currently reaches around 2 lakh students through 40 institutions and plans to expand to 120 institutions and 5 lakh students across 15 states over the next two years.

title: TPG-backed NewQuest offloads Rs 115 Cr Shadowfax stake in bulk deal
description: TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has sold another 40 lakh shares of logistics company Shadowfax Technologies in a bulk deal worth Rs 114.8 crore.
body: TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has sold another 40 lakh shares of logistics company Shadowfax Technologies in a bulk deal worth Rs 114.8 crore.
According to exchange data, NewQuest Asia Fund IV (Singapore) sold the shares at Rs 287 per share, representing around 0.68% of Shadowfax’s paid-up equity capital.

This marks the fourth time that the private equity investor has offloaded shares of Shadowfax in the past three months. In August, NewQuest sold 1.25 crore shares worth around Rs 300.6 crore. It followed this with another sale of 80 lakh shares for nearly Rs 200 crore in September. On September 30, the investor sold another 40 lakh shares for Rs 113.6 crore.
With the latest transaction, NewQuest has sold 2.85 crore Shadowfax shares since July, reducing its stake by around 4.86 percentage points. It held an 11.53% stake in the company as of June 2026.

The logistics company has also reported strong financial performance. Its consolidated net profit surged more than eightfold to Rs 65.4 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 8 crore in the year-ago period. Operating revenue rose 65% year-on-year to Rs 1,358 crore during the quarter.

Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, Shadowfax provides logistics services to e-commerce, quick-commerce and D2C companies. The company was listed on the stock exchanges earlier this year at an IPO price of Rs 124 per share.
The company currently operates across more than 16,000 pincodes and is expanding its quick-commerce network as it looks to strengthen its position in the rapidly growing last-mile delivery market.
The shares of the firm are currently trading at Rs 287.6 as of (10.38 AM, with a total market capitalization of Rs 16,895 crore.

title: Zomint raises Rs 36 Cr seed round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners
description: Wealth management startup Zomint has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.75 million) in a seed round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners. Snippets
body: Wealth management startup Zomint has raised Rs 36 crore ($3.75 million) in a seed round from Lightspeed and Prime Venture Partners.
The proceeds will be used to expand its wealth and investment teams, strengthen its technology platform and build its investor education ecosystem.

Founded in September 2025 by Aman Mittal and Shavir Bansal, Zomint offers wealth management services to working professionals and families. Investors can start with a monthly SIP of Rs 25,000 or a lump sum investment of Rs 5 lakh.

Zomint assigns each family a personal wealth expert who tracks their investments and financial goals. The expert is supported by investment research and AI tools that bring together portfolio information, past conversations and research, flag areas that need attention and track agreed actions.

The firm claims it has retained 97% of its clients since launch, despite market volatility. Nearly one in three clients made additional investments through the platform within three months of their initial engagement. Its relationship managers currently serve more than 250 families each, supported by investment specialists and AI enabled tools.
Zomint acquired its customers entirely through organic content, using the founders’ financial content platform Bekifaayati, which has more than 50 lakh subscribers.

title: Chiratae Ventures leads $10 Mn round in photonic quantum startup Quanfluence
description: he fresh funds will be used to build and launch a four-qubit quantum computer in the near term, with the company targeting a larger prototype featuring around 100 qubits
body: Photonic quantum technology startup Quanfluence has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Chiratae Ventures, with participation from Rainmatter by Zerodha and existing investor Pi Ventures.
The Bengaluru-based startup had earlier raised $2 million in a seed round led by Pi Ventures, with participation from Golden Sparrow, Reena Dayal and others in December 2024.

The fresh funds will be used to build and launch a four-qubit quantum computer in the near term, with the company targeting a larger prototype featuring around 100 qubits by 2029, Quanfluence said in a press release.

Founded in 2021 by Sujoy Chakravarty, Ravi Mehta, Biman Chattopadhyay, Anil Prabhakar, Aditi Vaidya and Sandeep Goyal, Quanfluence develops photonic quantum computing technology for optimisation problems. Its hardware-based solution is designed to complement AI in decision-making.
The company aims to develop a fault-tolerant, general-purpose quantum computer over the next five to six years.

Unlike conventional quantum computing systems that require complex cooling infrastructure, Quanfluence’s technology combines optics and hardware to operate at room temperature. Its optical Ising machine uses light waves and FPGAs for optimisation processing, which the company claims can be up to 100 times faster than classical computing for certain workloads.
The startup’s system is designed to address high-dimensional optimisation problems across areas such as logistics, workforce scheduling, risk management and financial optimisation.

Quanfluence is also testing an advanced version of its system capable of processing 10-25 million permutations for complex optimisation problems, including financial risk management, logistics and delivery route planning.

title: GST Council removes arrest powers, raises prosecution threshold to Rs 5 Cr
description: The GST Council has recommended removing the arrest provisions under GST and raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore.
body: The GST Council has recommended a series of changes to simplify compliance for businesses and reduce the involvement of tax officials. The decisions were taken at the 57th GST Council meeting held on Thursday, October 8.

The Council has recommended removing the arrest provisions under GST and raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore. It has also proposed reducing the general penalty from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000.

The government will also make the GST refund process faster. The timeline for issuing an acknowledgement or deficiency memo will be reduced from 15 days to 10 days. For eligible refund claims related to zero-rated supplies and inverted duty structure, 90% of the claimed amount will be sanctioned provisionally through a risk-based system without officer intervention.

The Council has also suggested simplifying GST registration and compliance. Routine registration changes will be processed automatically, while the government plans to introduce common standards for GST notices and proceedings.
For goods moving between states, physical interception will be restricted to cases based on specific intelligence and authorised by a senior tax officer.

Small sellers using e-commerce platforms will also get an easier route to register in another state. They will be allowed to use an e-commerce operator’s warehouse as their principal place of business, subject to certain conditions.

On input tax credit (ITC), the Council has widened relief for genuine taxpayers. However, the proposal to allow businesses to claim ITC even when their suppliers have not deposited the tax has been referred to a committee for further examination.
The Council has not announced any GST rate changes this time. The process reforms are expected to be implemented from April 1, 2027.

title: DailyObjects raises Rs 332 Cr in Series C round led by Xponentia, Anicut, Axiom Asia
description: Design-led lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects has raised Rs 332 crore (nearly $35 million) in a Series C funding round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.
body: Design-led lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects has raised Rs 332 crore (nearly $35 million) in a Series C funding round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.

The round, which comprised primary and secondary transactions, valued the company at around Rs 1,050 crore. The company plans to use the capital to expand its retail network, invest in product development and R&D, strengthen brand building and explore international markets.

As part of the round, early investor Roots Ventures partially exited DailyObjects with an 18X return on its investment. It will continue to remain a shareholder in the company alongside 360 One Asset and Trifecta Capital.

DailyObjects plans to open 150 exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across India over the next five years. The company currently has nearly 350 retail touchpoints, including EBOs and Apple Premium Reseller outlets.

The company will also invest in new product ranges, design, materials, quality and R&D across its existing categories. DailyObjects started with phone cases and has expanded into technology accessories, carry and workspace products.

Founded in 2012 by Pankaj Garg and Saurav Adlakha, DailyObjects has built a portfolio spanning technology, carry, workspace and lifestyle products. The company said it remains focused on capital efficiency and profitable growth as it scales its retail and product operations.
DailyObjects has raised nearly $50 million in funding to date, with Seedfund and 360 One Ventures among its key investors. The company last raised $10 million in May 2024.
Before the latest round, DailyObjects had raised around Rs 100 crore in equity over the past decade to build and scale its business.

title: Pet food startup TailBlaze Longevity raises pre-seed funding
description: he startup has also developed FreshTail, a proprietary technology for manufacturing shelf-stable fresh meals. Its portfolio includes more than 200 products across organi
body: Pet food startup TailBlaze Longevity has raised $300K in a pre-seed funding round led by US-based VC firm Comma Capital. The startup was also featured on Bharat Ke Superfounders.

The fresh capital will be used to launch HeartPour, build a team in Ahmedabad, and expand its reach among pet parents across India. Before the launch, the startup plans to offer the first 500 dogs a free serving of HeartPour, TailBlaze Longevity said in a press release.

Founded in August last year by Manaal Maniyar and Palak Devpura, TailBlaze is a pet care startup focused on canine longevity and nutrition. The startup aims to extend dogs’ lives by 3–5 years through high-protein and lower-carbohydrate nutritional formulations.

According to the Ahmedabad-based startup, HeartPour is a wet dog food line developed over four years of R&D. The product combines high protein and superfoods with an Ayurvedic PanchTatva blend comprising curcumin, black pepper, parsley, amla and tulsi.

The startup has also developed FreshTail, a proprietary technology for manufacturing shelf-stable fresh meals. Its portfolio includes more than 200 products across organic dog food, natural treats such as coconut and hemp or fish and strawberry, grooming essentials, and accessories.
TailBlaze Longevity follows a WhatsApp-first commerce model and also sells through quick commerce and online platforms such as Blinkit and BBNow.

In the pet nutrition segment, Right4Paws is developing science-based, species-specific whole-food nutrition focused on pet health and longevity. The startup raised Rs 14 crore in Series A funding in December last year to expand manufacturing, R&D, specialised talent and functional products.

Benny’s Bowl, another nutrition-focused startup, raised $1.4 million in February this year to develop functional pet foods for areas such as gut health, allergies, renal health, skin and coat health, and weight management.

title: Blinkit leads quick commerce in product availability, Flipkart Minutes ranks second: Bernstein
description: Eternal's quick-commerce arm Blinkit leads India's quick-commerce platforms in product availability with a 94.4% in-stock rate, ahead of Flipkart Minutes, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto, according to Bernstein.
body: Eternal's quick commerce arm Blinkit has emerged as the leader in product availability among India's major quick-commerce platforms, with an average in-stock rate of 94.4%, ahead of Flipkart Minutes, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto, according to a report by brokerage firm Bernstein.
The report found that Flipkart Minutes ranked second with 88.7% product availability, followed by Swiggy Instamart at 83.8% and Zepto at 82.5%.

Bernstein conducted the study across 150 stock-keeping units (SKUs), covering grocery, fresh and non-grocery categories. The analysis tracked product availability over 10 days, across seven time slots per day and at least three PIN codes each in Mumbai, Gurugram and Bengaluru.

The report also noted Blinkit's consistent stock availability across days and time slots. While Blinkit maintained availability of around 94-95% throughout the observation period, Instamart and Zepto witnessed sharper fluctuations, with availability falling below 80% at certain intervals.

Instamart recorded the sharpest decline in product availability as the day progressed, at 11%, followed by Zepto at 6%. Blinkit and Flipkart Minutes recorded the lowest decline at 5% each. Bernstein attributed Instamart's higher decline to challenges in demand forecasting and inventory replenishment.

According to Bernstein, product availability is emerging as a key competitive differentiator in India's quick-commerce market, where platforms have traditionally competed on delivery speed and pricing.
The report noted that maintaining high availability requires effective demand forecasting, dark-store management, reliable procurement, and logistics operations.
Bernstein believes Blinkit's operational advantage could improve customer retention and reduce churn, as customers increasingly prefer platforms that can fulfill their entire shopping baskets.

title: Lab-grown diamond brand Zinara raises pre-seed funding led by Inflection Point Ventures
description: Delhi NCR based lab-grown diamond jewellery brand Zinara has raised Rs 3.61 crore ($380K) in a pre-seed round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV). Snippets
body: Delhi NCR based lab-grown diamond jewellery brand Zinara has raised Rs 3.61 crore ($380K) in a pre-seed round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV).
Nine Jewellery, Bollywood actress Nikita Dutta and other angel investors also participated in the round.
The proceeds will be used to expand its team, increase marketing activities and strengthen its supply chain infrastructure. It plans to expand its product and brand presence across India.

Founded by Harshit Abrol and Sumanyu Vyas, Zinara focuses on everyday diamond jewellery made with lab-grown diamonds and 18K gold vermeil. The firm currently has more than 400 designs and has crossed Rs 1 crore in annual recurring revenue.

Abrol previously worked at P&G and Apnaklub, while Vyas has worked at Blinkit and Classplus. Zinara follows a digital-first model and serves customers across India. The brand also offers a lifetime warranty, buyback and exchange options on its products.
IPV has invested more than Rs 900 crore across over 280 startups, according to the company.

title: Info Edge posts Rs 822 Cr Q2 FY27 billings
description: Info Edge saw its standalone billings rise 12.8% year-on-year to Rs 822.3 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 729 crore in the same quarter last year.
body: Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri and 99acres, saw its standalone billings rise 12.8% year-on-year to Rs 822.3 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 729 crore in the same quarter last year, according to the stock exchange data.
For the first six months of FY27, Info Edge’s billings grew 13.5% to Rs 1,559.3 crore, from Rs 1,373.2 crore in the same period last year.

Its recruitment business, which includes Naukri, remained the biggest part of the company’s business. Billings from this segment grew 12.6% to Rs 613.8 crore in Q2 FY27, from Rs 545 crore a year ago. Info Edge said the business would have grown around 14-15% if the impact of customer renewal timings is removed.
99acres also reported strong growth. Its billings increased 21.2% to Rs 148.3 crore from Rs 122.4 crore in Q2 FY26. The growth was also higher than the 16.5% growth reported in the previous quarter.

In the matchmaking business, Jeevansathi’s billings grew 18.4% to Rs 39.7 crore. Aisle, another matchmaking platform owned by Info Edge, saw its billings grow 40%. Together, the matchmaking business grew 23.1% during the quarter.

However, Shiksha remained under pressure, with billings falling 27.2% to Rs 20.5 crore. Info Edge said AI-powered search is reducing the number of users coming to the platform through search engines. The company is working on new products to reduce its dependence on search traffic.
Info Edge also said more customers are using its B2B AI products, AI-Rex and Talent Pulse, with both products seeing growth in new customers and revenue.
The share price of the firm is currently trading at Rs 1205.5 (as of 10:14 AM), with the total market capitalization of 78,400 crore.

title: Exclusive: Nat Habit to kick off $15 Mn funding round led by Trident Growth Partners
description: Nat Habit is raising $15 million in a fresh round led by Trident Growth Partners, with participation from Bertelsmann, Firstport, Linklight Ventures and others.
body: Natural personal care D2C firm Nat Habit is raising Rs 142.6 crore ($15 million) in a fresh round led by Trident Growth Partners, with participation from Bertelsmann, Firstport, Linklight Ventures and others.

The board at Nat Habit is issuing 22.5 lakh Series C preference shares at an issue price of Rs 633.5 each to raise Rs 142.6 crore, according to its regulatory filing accessed from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) .

Trident Growth Partners will be leading the round with Rs 91 crore, while Bertelsmann and Linklight Ventures will invest Rs 37 crore and Rs 6.8 crore, respectively. Mirabilis, Firstport and Dharmayug Investments will contribute the remaining amount.

According to the filings, the fresh proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, expansion, brand building and other requirements. Notably, Rs 2.6 crore from the total proceeds will also be used for the reduction of the ESOP pool.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the post-money valuation of the firm stood at around Rs 800 crore.
Moneycontrol reported on Nat Habit’s fresh funding in July.

Following the fresh issue, Trident Growth Partners will hold an 11.44% stake in the company, while existing investor Bertelsmann will hold 17.54% of the cap table. As per the filing, before the fresh issue, Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal held 16% each in the firm.

Nat Habit has rebranded itself as Breathe Life, marking a shift in its positioning from an Ayurvedic brand to a broader lifestyle proposition. The company sells Ayurvedic personal care products, including shampoos, face washes, and moisturisers.

title: NABVENTURES Fund II secures Rs 450 Cr in first close
description: NABVENTURES, the venture capital arm of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has secured commitments of Rs 450 crore . Snippets
body: NABVENTURES, the venture capital arm of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), has secured commitments of Rs 450 crore in the first close of its second fund.
The fund is targeting a total corpus of Rs 1,500 crore, including a green-shoe option, with NABARD serving as its anchor investor.
NABVENTURES Fund II will invest in early and growth-stage companies working across agriculture, food, agribusiness and rural markets.
Its focus areas include agritech, rural fintech, climate-smart solutions, supply chain and logistics, and other businesses addressing challenges across the agricultural value chain.

The fund plans to back companies using technology and scalable business models to improve agricultural productivity, strengthen supply chains and support rural enterprises. It will also focus on solutions related to sustainability, climate resilience, financial inclusion and livelihood creation.
Along with capital, NABVENTURES plans to leverage NABARD’s nationwide presence and sectoral expertise to help portfolio companies expand their operations and reach rural markets.

The new fund builds on NABVENTURES’ earlier funds, which have collectively backed 23 enterprises. Through Fund II, the firm aims to support businesses that combine commercial growth with solutions for India’s agriculture and rural economy.

title: Exclusive: Gramiyaa raises fresh capital in Series A round at Rs 110 Cr valuation
description: Bengaluru-based cold-pressed oil brand Gramiyaa has raised Rs 18.65 crore in a Series A funding round led by new investor Optiscape Network Holdings
body: Bengaluru-based cold-pressed oil brand Gramiyaa has raised Rs 18.65 crore in a Series A funding round led by new investor Optiscape Network Holdings and participation from existing investors Homegrown Ventures, Campus Fund  and others. In March 2025, the company had raised Rs 7.2 crore in a pre-Series A round led by Homegrown Ventures, with participation from Campus Fund and Mumbai Angels.
According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , the company ’s board has allotted 32,968 Series A CCPS at Rs 5,657 per share to raise the fresh capital.
Optiscape Network Holdings led the round with an investment of Rs 9 crore, followed by Homegrown Ventures with Rs 4.5 crore and Campus Fund with Rs 4 crore.
Sarya Global Holdings invested Rs 90 lakh, while Rasagna Pulapaka contributed Rs 25 lakh in the round.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, Gramiyaa’s valuation surged 49% to Rs 110 crore in Series A from Rs 74 crore in the pre-Series A round. The proceeds will be deployed towards growth capital and other general corporate requirements

Founded in 2016 by Sibi Manivannan, Gramiyaa is a cold-pressed oil brand that makes its products in-house using traditional oil-making methods. The D2C company offers groundnut, coconut, sesame and mustard oils, along with virgin coconut and olive oils, and sells through its own website as well as platforms such as Amazon, Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, BigBasket, DMart Ready and FirstClub. After the latest allotment, Homegrown Ventures remains the largest external shareholder with a 17.34% stake, followed by Campus Fund at 9.86% and Optiscape Network Holdings at 8.28%. Meanwhile, C c o-founders Sibi Manivannan, Mohamed Yaseen and Naveenrajaman RL hold retained 26.04%, 13.02% and 13.02%, respectively.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. In FY25, Gramiyaa’s revenue jumped 72.7% YoY to Rs 19 crore, while its losses surged nearly 12.7X to Rs 4 crore.

title: MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth raises Rs 85 Cr from FMO, LeapFrog
description: he Mumbai-based company had previously raised Rs 300 crore ($36 million) in a Series D equity round in December 2022, led by FMO along with existing investors.
body: NeoGrowth, an MSME-focused digital lender, has raised Rs 85 crore through a mix of equity and debt from Dutch development finance institution FMO and existing investor LeapFrog Investments.
The Mumbai-based company had previously raised Rs 300 crore ($36 million) in a Series D equity round in December 2022, led by FMO along with existing investors.
The latest proceeds will be used to grow its loan book to nearly Rs 3,000 crore before the company requires another equity infusion, NeoGrowth said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2011 by Dhruv Khaitan and Piyush Khaitan, NeoGrowth provides business loans tailored to the needs of small businesses. Its offerings include both collateral-free and collateral-based loans for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

The company uses technology and data analytics to assess borrowers based on digital payment data, point-of-sale (POS) transactions and cash flows rather than relying solely on traditional collateral. It also offers flexible repayment schedules, with daily, weekly, fortnightly and monthly collection options.
NeoGrowth claims to operate in more than 25 cities across India, serving over 80 business segments and more than 1 lakh businesses.

Digital lenders are increasingly using GST records, banking transactions, digital payment trails and other business data to assess creditworthiness and extend loans to kirana stores, manufacturers, traders, distributors and small service providers.
The segment has attracted investor interest as lenders target underserved MSMEs through supply chain financing and embedded credit solutions.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 5- Oct 10]
description: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $113.35 million across 3 growth-stage deals, 22 early-stage deals, and 3 undisclosed rounds. The week. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $113.35 million across 3 growth-stage deals, 22 early-stage deals, and 3 undisclosed rounds. The week also saw 8 key appointments, 3 fund launches and 2 mergers & acquisitions.
In contrast, 24 startups had collectively secured about $411.46 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised $55.3 million across three deals this week, led by lifestyle-tech brand DailyObjects, which secured Rs 332 crore (nearly $35 million) in a Series C round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Axiom Asia Private Capital.

Smart kitchen appliance startup Beyond Appliances raised Rs 110 crore ($11.4 million) in a Series B round led by Fireside Ventures, while MSME-focused digital lender NeoGrowth secured Rs 85 crore in equity and debt funding from FMO and LeapFrog Investments.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $58.05 million across 22 deals this week, led by photonic quantum technology startup Quanfluence, which secured $10 million from Chiratae Ventures and Rainmatter, followed by edtech startup byteXL with $9 million from Elevar Equity.

Medtech startup Sunfox Technologies raised $7 million in a Series A round co-led by Ashish Kacholia, Lashit Sanghvi, Alchemy Capital and 3one4 Capital, while quantum computing startup QpiAI secured Rs 50 crore in debt funding from InnoVen Capital.

title: Hero Electronix’s Tessolve Semiconductor raises $75 Mn led by Vector Line Capital
description: Founded by Srinivas Chinamill, Tessolve is a semiconductor engineering company that offers turnkey solutions across chip architecture, design, validation, testing and
body: Tessolve Semiconductor, a Hero Electronix company, has raised $75 million in a funding round led by US based strategic investment firm Vector Line Capital.

The proceeds will be used to support growth, including strategic acquisitions that complement its existing capabilities, expand its service offerings and strengthen its global presence, the company said in a press release.
Founded by Srini Chinamilli, Tessolve is a semiconductor engineering company that offers turnkey solutions across chip architecture, design, validation, testing and embedded systems.

The company employs over 3,500 engineers across 10 countries and operates nine laboratories globally. It also partners with leading foundries, intellectual property (IP) providers, electronic design automation (EDA) companies and test equipment manufacturers.

Tessolve works with semiconductor companies, hyperscalers, chip startups and system companies across segments such as artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), automotive, data centres and industrial applications.

The company offers end-to-end semiconductor design capabilities, including AI, HPC and analog and mixed-signal chips. It said it works with leading hyperscalers and 18 of the world’s top 20 semiconductor companies.
Tessolve is also in advanced discussions to close multiple acquisitions over the next couple of quarters, it added.

title: Zetwerk raises fresh issue size to Rs 2,830 Cr, OFS component up 49% in RHP
description: Manufacturing platform Zetwerk has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its initial public offering (IPO), comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore.
body: Manufacturing platform Zetwerk has filed its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) for its initial public offering (IPO), comprising a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore.

According to its RHP, the Bengaluru-based company has increased its fresh issue size to Rs 2,830 crore from Rs 2,600 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP). The offer for sale (OFS) has also increased by 49% to 14.45 crore shares from 9.68 crore shares proposed in the UDRHP filed in August.

The OFS will include shares from promoters Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, who will each sell 1.42 crore shares. Promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload up to 2.30 crore shares. Together, they will offer around 5.14 crore shares.
Among the existing investors, Lightspeed Venture Partners will offload the most, at 2.51 crore shares, followed by Peak XV Partners, which will sell 2.34 crore shares.
Kae Capital Fund and Kalysta Capital Fund will collectively sell up to 1.67 crore shares. Accel India V will also participate in the OFS, offloading up to 1.2 crore shares.
The offer will be open for subscription on October 15, 2026 to October 19, 2026 while anchor bid will start on October 14.

Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,300 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company level. Another Rs 860 crore will be used to repay debt at nine subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be allocated towards acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2017 by Acharya and Ramakkrushnan, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as energy, electronics, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.

title: KL Rahul-backed Boldfit raises over Rs 400 Cr in Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund
description: Boldfit, a homegrown sports brand, has raised over Rs 400 crore ($42 million) in its Series B funding round led by Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company Alternates
body: Boldfit, a homegrown sports brand, has raised over Rs 400 crore (nearly $42 million) in its Series B funding round led by Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company Alternates, part of the Pantomath Group. Existing investor Bessemer Venture Partners also participated in the round.

The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised Rs 110 crore , or around $13 million, in a funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners in November 2024. It also raised $8.37 million from existing investors, including KL Rahul.

The fresh funds will be used to drive growth, with investments planned in nationwide retail expansion, product innovation and manufacturing. The company will also selectively pursue inorganic opportunities to strengthen its presence and capabilities across categories, Boldfit said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani and Aasshna Guptaa, Boldfit is an e-commerce platform that offers sports and fitness products across categories such as apparel, fitness equipment, nutrition supplements and accessories. Its portfolio covers sports such as basketball, cycling, football, volleyball, badminton and cricket, with over 400 products.

The company said it serves over 2 crore customers annually. It is also strengthening its integrated product development and manufacturing capabilities, with a focus on innovation, quality and long-term competitive advantages.
Boldfit aims to build a sports brand for a billion Indians through product innovation, manufacturing and nationwide distribution, the company said.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Its operating revenue jumped 2.17X to Rs 304 crore in FY25 from Rs 140 crore in FY24. Profit also surged 2.08X to Rs 35 crore in FY25 from Rs 16.82 crore in the previous fiscal.

In the sports and fitness segment, Agilitas, a sportswear platform, raised Rs 225 crore from Nexus Venture Partners and Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, in June 2026. The funds will be used to strengthen its manufacturing, brand-building, retail and technology capabilities.

title: Zetwerk IPO: Early investors set for up to 38X returns through OFS
description: Zetwerk’s upcoming IPO is expected to deliver multi-fold returns to several early investors, with Kae Capital and Kalysta Capital set to earn around 38X returns on their investments.
body: Zetwerk’s upcoming IPO is expected to deliver multi-fold returns to several early investors, with Kae Capital and Kalysta Capital set to earn around 38X returns on their investments. The offer for sale (OFS) will see existing shareholders offload 14.45 crore shares worth approximately Rs 2,182 crore.

According to Entrackr’s analysis, Lightspeed Venture Partners is the largest selling external shareholder in Zetwerk’s IPO, with a share sale worth Rs 426.9 crore. At the upper price band of Rs 151 per share, it is set to clock around 4.5X returns based on the average acquisition cost across its participating funds. Peak XV Partners will offload shares worth Rs 353.5 crore, translating into around 9.3X returns, while Accel is set to generate around 19.3X returns on its Rs 181.5 crore share sale.
The average acquisition costs for Lightspeed and Peak XV have been calculated across their respective funds participating in the OFS.

Kae Capital will sell shares worth Rs 189.8 crore through the OFS and is set to clock around 38.3X returns based on an average acquisition cost of Rs 3.94 per share. Kalysta Capital will offload shares worth Rs 63.3 crore, also generating around 38.3X returns at the upper price band.

Among other shareholders, promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload shares worth Rs 346.9 crore. Its acquisition cost of Rs 178.58 per share is higher than the IPO’s upper price band, implying a return of around 0.85X on its investment.

Zetwerk co-founders Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan will each sell shares worth around Rs 214.9 crore. Other OFS participants include Saifuddin Fakhruddin Qureshi and Matthew Harris Arnold, who will sell shares worth Rs 43.1 crore and Rs 36.9 crore, respectively.
Notably, Greenoaks Capital, the company’s largest shareholder with a 19.62% stake held through four entities, will not participate in the OFS.

Zetwerk’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of Rs 2,830 crore and an OFS of 14.45 crore shares. The company aims to raise around Rs 5,012 crore through the public issue, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end of the price band. The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19, with listing scheduled for October 23.

title: Zetwerk sets IPO price band at Rs 143-151; eyes Rs 5,012 Cr from issue
description: Zetwerk has fixed the price band for its IPO at Rs 143-151 per share. The Bengaluru-based company aims to raise around Rs 5,012 crore through the public issue.
body: Manufacturing platform Zetwerk has fixed the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) at Rs 143-151 per share. The Bengaluru-based company aims to raise around Rs 5,012 crore through the public issue, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The company will open its anchor investor book on October 14, while its shares are expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 23.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 14.45 crore shares by promoters and existing investors, according to its red herring prospectus (RHP).

Zetwerk has increased the fresh issue size from Rs 2,600 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) filed in August. The OFS component has also increased by 49% from 9.68 crore shares proposed earlier.

Promoters Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan will each sell 1.42 crore shares, while promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload up to 2.30 crore shares. Among existing investors, Lightspeed Venture Partners will sell 2.51 crore shares, followed by Peak XV Partners with 2.34 crore shares. Accel India V will also sell up to 1.2 crore shares.

Zetwerk plans to use Rs 1,300 crore from the fresh issue to repay or prepay borrowings at the company level. Another Rs 860 crore will go towards debt repayment at nine subsidiaries. The remaining proceeds will be used for acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2017, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as electronics, energy, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.

On the financial front, Zetwerk’s revenue from continuing operations rose to Rs 15,913 crore in FY26 from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations narrowed to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago quarter.

title: Toothsi parent MakeO raises Rs 90 Cr led by Singularity AMC
description: Mumbai-based MakeO, the parent company of clear aligner brand Toothsi, has raised Rs 90 crore ($9.5 million) in a funding round led by Singularity AMC.
body: Mumbai-based MakeO, the parent company of clear aligner brand Toothsi, has raised Rs 90 crore ($9.5 million) in a funding round led by Singularity AMC. DSP family office, Genesis and Unispace Ventures also participated in the round.
The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its dental technology business across India and Southeast Asia.

The fundraise comes after MakeO announced an agreement to acquire Singapore-based dental care startup Zenyum in February. The acquisition is aimed at expanding its presence across Southeast Asian markets.
In 2025, MakeO acquired Apple Dental, a chain of 20 dental clinics across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, for Rs 10.98 crore through a mix of cash and stock.

Following the acquisitions, MakeO has a network of around 1,100 partner dentists across 10 countries. It also operates more than 60 offline clinical centres and has served over 4 lakh consumers, according to the company.

MakeO operates an aligner planning and manufacturing facility in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), with an annual production capacity of over a million aligners. Its products reach dentists and consumers across more than 150 Indian cities, while the company exports to over 10 countries through the Toothsi and Zenyum networks.

Founded in 2018 by Arpi Mehta, Pravin Shetty, Manjul Jain and Anirudh Kal, MakeO initially launched Toothsi as its clear aligner brand. In September 2022, it brought Toothsi and skincare brand Skinnsi under the MakeO umbrella to offer dental, skin and hair treatments through a single platform.

Before the latest round, MakeO had raised over $100 million from investors including Eight Roads Ventures, 360 ONE Asset and Paramark Ventures. In June 2025, it raised Rs 100 crore from existing investors. In January 2024, the company raised $16 million in a round led by 360 ONE Asset and the investment office of Ashish Kacholia.

title: Urban Company to consider fresh fundraise
description: Urban Company, the home services marketplace, will consider a proposal to raise fresh funds at a board meeting on October 16, according to its regulatory filing.
body: Urban Company, the home services marketplace, will consider a proposal to raise fresh funds at a board meeting on October 16, according to its regulatory filing.

The company may raise funds through a QIP, preferential allotment, private placement or other permitted routes, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals. The company has not disclosed the proposed amount in its exchange filing.
According to a Moneycontrol report, Urban Company is looking to raise around Rs 2,000-2,500 crore through a QIP.
The proposed fundraise comes amid rising competition in the instant home services segment, where startups such as Snabbit and Pronto are raising fresh capital to expand their operations.

Snabbit raised $56 million in a Series D funding round in April 2026, led by Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments and Bertelsmann India Investments. The round valued the startup at around $350 million, taking its total funding to about $112 million.
Meanwhile, Pronto closed its Series B round at $45 million in May 2026, including a $20 million investment from investor Lachy Groom. The round valued the startup at $200 million.

Urban Company also raised $50 million through a fresh issue of shares during its IPO in September 2025. The public issue additionally included an offer for sale of Rs 1,428 crore by existing shareholders.

In Q1 FY27, Urban Company's revenue from operations grew 44% year-on-year to Rs 528 crore . However, the company reported a net loss of Rs 92 crore, against a profit of Rs 6.9 crore in the year-ago period. Its net transaction value increased 42% to Rs 1,465 crore.

title: AI video platform Clueso raises $10 Mn in Series A round led by Dharana Capital
description: AI video platform Clueso has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Dharana Capital, with participation from new investors Founders Future and Neotribe Ventures.
body: AI video platform Clueso has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Dharana Capital, with participation from new investors Founders Future and Neotribe Ventures. Existing investors Y Combinator and f7 Ventures also participated in the round.
The latest funding takes the company’s total capital raised to $12 million. According to the company, more than 80% of the Series A capital came from existing investors.

Founded by Akash Anand, Prajwal Prakash and Neel Balar, Clueso provides an AI-powered platform that helps businesses create and update videos for marketing, customer education, onboarding, training and internal operations.

The company said its platform is used by more than 1,000 businesses, including Atlassian, Zendesk, Gainsight, Seismic and Ironclad. According to Clueso, its customers have reported more than fivefold productivity gains and an 80% reduction in video production costs.

Clueso uses AI agents to automate different stages of video production, including capturing software workflows, generating scripts and voiceovers, editing footage and maintaining brand consistency. The platform can also update videos when products or business processes change.

The company also offers integrations with other business tools and support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which allows AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT to create, edit and manage videos through Clueso.

Clueso said it will use the fresh capital to expand its enterprise sales and go-to-market operations, develop its AI agent capabilities, improve editing features and strengthen integrations with business software.

The funding comes amid growing adoption of AI tools across enterprise workflows, including content creation, employee training and customer education. Clueso is focused on automating video production for businesses, with an emphasis on creating and maintaining content as products and processes evolve.

title: Exclusive: StockGro plans Rs 536 Cr IPO fresh issue, to appoint independent directors
description: Social investing and stock market advisory platform StockGro’s parent company, AssetGro Fintech, is set to raise Rs 536 crore through a fresh issue
body: StockGro’s parent company, AssetGro Fintech, is set to raise Rs 536 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares as part of its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

According to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC), AssetGro Fintech Ltd, the parent entity of StockGro, passed a resolution to approve the issue of up to Rs 536 crore in fresh equity and an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders.
However, the size of the OFS has not been disclosed in the resolution. According to media reports, StockGro is looking to raise up to Rs 2,000 Cr-Rs 2,500 Cr through the initial public offering.

Notably, the company may raise up to Rs 107.2 crore through a pre-IPO placement before the offer. If completed, the amount raised through the placement will be deducted from the fresh issue, the filing further stated.

The company has yet to disclose the final IPO size, price band, valuation or listing timeline. In a separate filing ahead of its IPO, StockGro has passed a resolution to appoint Dinesh Chander Patwari, Yatrik Rushikesh Vin and Divya Dwivedi as independent directors for five-year terms. The company has also proposed appointing Diyanshi Agrawal as a nominee director.

Founded in 2020 by former venture capitalist Ajay Lakhotia, StockGro is building a full-stack ecosystem for smarter trading and investing through expert-driven insights and AI-powered research, delivered via its social-first, community-led platform. The company has raised over $100 million in funding to date, including investments from BITKRAFT Ventures, SBI Ventures, Root Ventures, and General Catalyst and others.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. Its operating revenue increased 30.99% to Rs 113.33 crore in FY25 from Rs 86.52 crore in FY24. It reported a profit of Rs 34.64 crore in FY25, compared to a loss of Rs 101.17 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) raises Rs 3,000 Cr for growth-stage AI and deeptech fund
description: Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) has secured Rs 3,000 crore in subscriptions for its growth-stage AI and deeptech investment strategy. News
body: Fundamentum Frontier Advisors (F2A) has secured Rs 3,000 crore in subscriptions for its growth-stage AI and deeptech investment strategy.
The capital has been raised from Indian and overseas investors through two regulated investment vehicles. Nandan Nilekani has joined the fund as an anchor investor and mentor.

Led by general partners Ashish Kumar, Debraj Banerjee and Vivek Singla, F2A plans to deploy the capital across 12 to 15 companies over the next two to three years. The fund plans to invest Rs 100 crore to Rs 200 crore in each company, with a focus on businesses that have a technological edge and the potential to scale.

F2A will invest across AI-led digital consumer businesses, enterprise software, AI applications, deeptech infrastructure and engineered systems. It will target growth-stage companies that have validated their technology and are expanding their customer base in India and overseas markets.
The fund has also secured investor approvals to increase its overall hard cap amid demand beyond its current capacity. However, the revised target corpus has not been disclosed.

F2A aims to support portfolio companies as they expand operations, build intellectual property and pursue further growth opportunities. The firm also plans to help them access customers, strategic partners and talent.

The fund has secured commitments amid growing investor interest in Indian companies developing AI and frontier technologies. F2A believes India-domiciled businesses can build technology products and intellectual property for domestic and international markets as they move from technology validation to commercial expansion.

The three general partners bring experience working with technology companies at different stages of growth. F2A plans to support founders through the expansion phase by providing capital and access to customers, strategic partnerships and talent. The firm expects its portfolio companies to take a few years to reach public-market readiness, positioning the fund as a growth-stage investor.

title: ThinkMetal raises Rs 27 Cr led by IAN Alpha Fund
description: Advanced materials and manufacturing startup ThinkMetal has raised Rs 27 crore in a funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation. Snippets
body: Advanced materials and manufacturing startup ThinkMetal has raised Rs 27 crore in a funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from 3i Partners and existing investors.
The proceeds will be used to develop its products, expand its research and development capabilities, and increase adoption among industrial customers.

Founded by Sabyasachi Ghosh and Arushi Sharma, ThinkMetal is developing indigenous technologies for precision metal manufacturing. Its platform combines advanced materials, manufacturing processes and industrial systems to reduce production time and dependence on imported technologies.

The company’s current commercial offering is SistemT1, a metal additive manufacturing system designed to produce precision metal components. The system uses ThinkMetal’s proprietary FuseX metal filament technology. The company is also expanding its materials library and developing in-house capabilities to process new materials.

ThinkMetal serves manufacturers across aerospace, defence, space, automotive and electric mobility. It has moved from technology development to enterprise pilots and is now working towards larger commercial deployments. According to IAN Alpha Fund, the company has filed more than 17 intellectual property applications.
The company claims its technology can manufacture high-value precision metal parts up to 10 times faster and at half the cost of conventional methods.

title: AJVC leads pre-seed round in home-furnishing startup wudhomes
description: The Bengaluru-based startup focuses on connecting inspiration, product discovery, curation, personalisation and fulfilment to help customers navigate decisions involv
body: Home-furnishing startup wudhomes has raised Rs 2.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by AJVC, founded by Aviral Bhatnagar. Seekho co-founders Rohit Choudhary, Keertay Agarwal and Yash Banwani also participated in the round, along with other angel investors.

The fresh funds will be used to build a vertically integrated supply chain, develop in-house technology, strengthen the retail experience and expand operational capabilities, wudhomes said in a press release.

Founded in 2025 by Vasu Arneja and Aditya Singh, wudhomes is a home-furnishing startup that offers products such as custom-built sofas, accent chairs, coffee tables, side tables and other living room furniture.
The Bengaluru-based startup focuses on connecting inspiration, product discovery, curation, personalisation and fulfilment to help customers navigate decisions involved in furnishing their homes.

Furniture is the company's starting category, while its broader focus is on simplifying the overall home-furnishing process. It is developing an integrated model that combines digital inspiration, personalised product curation, spatial visualisation, physical retail, home visits and a vertically integrated supply chain.

In recent months, wudhomes has furnished over 200 homes. It has also opened a retail outlet in Bengaluru and introduced a home-visit service through which consultants assess customers' spaces and help them explore suitable furnishing options.
The company aims to connect product discovery and decision-making with the process of furnishing a home through these customer touchpoints.

title: NuSynth raises Rs 36.5 Cr in seed round led by Avaana Capital, Shastra VC
description: NuSynth Technologies, a Bengaluru based chemical process innovation startup, has raised Rs 36.5 crore (around $4 million) in a seed funding round. Snippets
body: NuSynth Technologies, a Bengaluru based chemical process innovation startup, has raised Rs 36.5 crore (around $4 million) in a seed funding round co-led by Avaana Capital and Shastra VC.
The startup is developing a platform to redesign chemical synthesis processes by evaluating raw materials, reaction pathways and process economics.

NuSynth uses predictive synthesis models and an AI engine that processes experimental data to inform future research cycles. Its platform focuses on developing alternative synthesis routes with changes to cost, yield, safety, sustainability and scalability.
The startup is initially focusing on pharmaceuticals and electronics chemicals. It plans to develop proprietary chemical processes for commercial applications across multiple chemistry-led sectors.
The fresh capital will be used to develop its R&D and technology capabilities, build an initial portfolio of proprietary processes, strengthen scale-up capabilities and expand the team.

NuSynth was founded by Poorvank Purohit, former MD and CEO of Solara Active Pharma Sciences, and Dr Ramesha A R, a postdoctoral researcher at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), Washington. The founding team also includes Abhishek Deo and Dipak Bajaj, who have worked with companies such as Zetwerk, Mstack, Ola, JPMorgan, BlackBuck and SUN Mobility.
According to the company, its platform is designed to reduce the time required for chemical R&D by using data from previous experiments to guide subsequent research.

title: Qualcomm exits Shadowfax with Rs 157 Cr stake sale
description: Qualcomm Asia Pacific Pte Ltd, an affiliate of the US-based chipmaker, sold 57.13 lakh shares, representing a 0.98% stake, at an average price of Rs 275.30 per share.
body: Qualcomm Ventures has sold Rs 157.28 crore worth of shares in logistics company Shadowfax Technologies through an open market transaction.

Qualcomm Asia Pacific Pte Ltd, an affiliate of the US-based chipmaker, sold 57.13 lakh shares, representing a 0.98% stake, at an average price of Rs 275.30 per share, according to bulk deal data on the BSE.

This follows another stake sale in August, when Qualcomm sold 75 lakh shares, representing a 1.28% stake, for Rs 183.85 crore at an average price of Rs 245.13 per share. Across the two transactions, Qualcomm has sold Shadowfax shares worth around Rs 341 crore.
The investor held a 2.26% stake in Shadowfax at the end of June 2026.

The latest sale comes amid a series of stake sales by existing investors in Shadowfax. TPG-backed NewQuest Asia Fund IV has also been selling shares in the logistics company through multiple bulk deals.

On October 6, NewQuest sold 40 lakh shares of Shadowfax for Rs 114.8 crore at Rs 287 per share. This was its fourth stake sale in the company in three months. Since July, NewQuest has sold around 2.85 crore shares, reducing its stake by approximately 4.86 percentage points. It held an 11.53% stake at the end of June 2026.

Shadowfax provides logistics services to ecommerce, quick-commerce and direct-to-consumer (D2C) companies. Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, the company operates across more than 16,000 pincodes.
The company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 65.4 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 8 crore a year earlier. Operating revenue rose 65% year-on-year to Rs 1,358 crore during the quarter.

title: Mesa School of Business raises Rs 110 Cr in equity and debt
description: Mesa School of Business has raised Rs 110 crore, comprising around Rs 85 crore in Series A equity funding co-led by Dharana Capital and Elevation Capital
body: Startup-focused business school and edtech company Mesa School of Business has raised Rs 110 crore, comprising around Rs 85 crore in Series A equity funding co-led by Dharana Capital and existing investor Elevation Capital, and Rs 25 crore in venture debt from InnoVen Capital and Alteria Capital.
The company is also backed by founders including Kunal Shah of CRED, Vidit Aatrey of Meesho, Abhiraj Bhal of Urban Company, and Vijay Shekhar Sharma of Paytm.
According to the company, the fresh funding round values it at Rs 385 crore.
Entrackr had exclusively reported on Mesa School of Business’s Series A funding last month.

The proceeds will be used to invest in an AI-first curriculum for existing programmes, launch and scale new programmes, and build strategic partnerships with the startup ecosystem, the company said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2023 by Ankit Agarwal and Varun Limaye, Mesa School of Business offers residential programmes for undergraduates, fresh graduates and early-career professionals. The Bengaluru-based institution aims to prepare students for leadership and entrepreneurship in an AI-first world.

The company said every student builds and runs a small business and learns to use AI to develop and launch a technology product. Mesa has grown from a single postgraduate cohort to over 550 students across three programmes: a one-year Post Graduate Programme in Startup Leadership, a four-year undergraduate programme in business and entrepreneurship, and Forge, a one-year programme for fresh graduates.
Mesa said over 100 founders have taught on campus, while students have worked on more than 200 projects with startups. Its alumni pursue full-time roles at startups or start their own businesses.
