title: Zetwerk raises Rs 2,251 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
description: Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses, a manufacturing platform, has raised Rs 2,251.23 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO).
body: Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses, a manufacturing platform, has raised Rs 2,251.23 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO).
The company allotted 14.91 crore shares to 99 anchor investors at Rs 151 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band.

Global institutional investors participating in the anchor book included Capital Group, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, Manulife and Susquehanna. Sovereign wealth funds such as Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) also participated in the allocation.

Among domestic investors, SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund and Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund received allocations. Insurance companies including SBI Life Insurance, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Bajaj Life Insurance and Axis Max Life Insurance also participated in the anchor round.
Domestic mutual funds received 6.80 crore shares, while seven life insurance companies were allotted 1.10 crore shares, according to the exchange filing.

Zetwerk’s Rs 5,012 crore IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 14.45 crore shares worth Rs 2,182 crore by existing shareholders.

The Bengaluru-based company has fixed its IPO price band at Rs 143-151 per share, valuing it at around Rs 25,583 crore at the upper end. The company plans to use a portion of the fresh issue proceeds to repay debt, with the remaining funds earmarked for acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.

Zetwerk’s IPO will also provide an exit opportunity to its early investors, with Kae Capital and Kalysta Capital set to earn returns of up to 38X on their investments through the offer for sale (OFS). Lightspeed Venture Partners is the largest selling external shareholder, offloading shares worth Rs 426.9 crore, followed by Peak XV Partners, which is selling shares worth Rs 353.5 crore.

title: Scimplify raises $25 Mn in strategic round led by Hitachi Ventures
description: Scimplify, a Bengaluru based advanced materials and specialty chemicals manufacturer, has raised $25 million in a strategic funding round led by Hitachi Ventures.
body: Scimplify, a Bengaluru based advanced materials and specialty chemicals manufacturer, has raised $25 million in a strategic funding round led by Hitachi Ventures.

Accel India, Bertelsmann India Investments, Omnivore and 3one4 Capital also participated in the round. Henkel and Teknor Apex joined as new investors. Both companies are also Scimplify’s customers, while Teknor Apex will serve as a manufacturing partner for its US expansion.

The latest funding takes Scimplify’s total equity capital raised to $80 million. The company plans to use the proceeds to expand its research, processing and manufacturing capabilities in the US, with a focus on materials used in semiconductors, defence, energy and AI infrastructure.
Entrackr had reported on Scimplify’s latest funding and valuation in July.

Founded in 2023 by Sachin Santhosh, Salil Srivastava, Dheeraj Dhingra and Hersh Manek, Scimplify develops manufacturing processes to convert raw materials, industrial waste and laboratory discoveries into high purity materials for commercial applications.

The company combines in house scientists and laboratories with its AI enabled platform, Scinode, to develop materials and scale up their production. Its platform maps more than 500 manufacturing facilities and helps identify suitable production routes, equipment and manufacturing partners.

Scimplify said it has served customers in more than 40 countries. More than 40% of its portfolio is focused on advanced materials for semiconductors, batteries and critical minerals, according to the company.

The startup cited projects across semiconductor chemicals, battery materials and tungsten as examples of its work. In one case, it developed a purification process for a high purity chemical used in semiconductor manufacturing and delivered a sample that passed the customer's process test within two months. In another, it developed a process to recover tungsten from industrial scrap and spent catalysts for a US based metals manufacturer.

title: Google.org backs The/Nudge with $15 Mn to digitise India's MSMEs
description: he funding will support the development of scalable artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve MSMEs’ access to formal credit, market discovery and compliance soluti
body: Google.org has committed $15 million in funding to The/Nudge to support the growth and digital adoption of India’s micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).

India has over 90 million small businesses that employ more than 345 million people. However, many of these businesses face challenges in accessing credit, managing compliance and reaching digital markets.

The funding will support the development of scalable artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve MSMEs’ access to formal credit, market discovery and compliance solutions. The initiative is part of Google.org’s efforts to support India’s national AI roadmap.

The programme will include an open call for proposals to identify innovative solutions for MSMEs. It will also feature a multilingual, voice-led platform to train local talent in Tier 3 and Tier 4 towns in job-ready skills and connect them directly with small businesses.

Google.org provides funding, programmes and technical expertise to organisations working to expand access to opportunities. Its focus areas include knowledge, skills and learning, scientific progress, and stronger communities. The organisation applies Google’s technology, research and resources to support initiatives aimed at addressing social and economic challenges.

title: Former Dyson India MD Ankit Jain launches Foundry with Rs 12 Cr pre-seed round
description: Foundry has raised Rs 12 crore in a pre-seed funding round co-led by BEENEXT and Kettleborough VC. The round also saw participation from Rishubh Satiya of Plix, Anindita
body: Ankit Jain, former managing director of Dyson India, has launched Foundry, a consumer technology company focused on premium home appliances. The company is developing appliances using proprietary, patent-pending technology, with its initial product range focused on the kitchen.

Foundry has raised Rs 12 crore in a pre-seed funding round co-led by BEENEXT and Kettleborough VC. The round also saw participation from Rishubh Satiya of Plix, Anindita Sampath of Yoga Bar, and Anita Pramoda of Owned Outcomes.

The proceeds will be used to support technology development and product engineering as Foundry prepares to launch its first range of kitchen appliances in the second half of 2027, the company said in a press release.

Foundry aims to develop appliances that combine proprietary technology with industrial design and materials suited to modern homes. The company plans to expand into other categories beyond the kitchen.

title: Parallel Loop raises $6.6 Mn seed round led by 3one4 Capital
description: The company combines its AI stack with forward-deployed engineers who work alongside client teams to connect existing systems, processes and organisational knowledge, and
body: Parallel Loop, an AI operating partner for mid-market and large enterprises, has raised $6.6 million in a seed funding round led by 3one4 Capital.
Co-founded by Prateek Jogani and Yujun Chean in June this year, Parallel Loop works with enterprises to integrate AI into their existing technology, organisational context and workflows.

The company combines its AI stack with forward-deployed engineers who work alongside client teams to connect existing systems, processes and organisational knowledge, and build AI workflows and applications. Its offerings span three areas.

Its AI Enablement service helps leadership teams identify AI opportunities, define roadmaps and build internal capabilities. The AI Stack provides a secure, governed and modular platform that connects existing systems with organisational context. It supports applications ranging from live dashboards to end-to-end workflows.
The Software Factory brings together forward-deployed engineers and AI agents to work with client teams on modernising legacy systems and building new applications.

Parallel Loop said its AI stack can run in a client’s own cloud environment or on-premises, with data residency configured to meet the client’s requirements. This allows enterprises to retain control over where their data and AI workloads are hosted and who can access them.

The platform supports multiple model providers, including open-weight models, and maintains an audit trail of prompts, responses, context changes and actions. Clients retain ownership of their data, organisational context and client-specific work built for them.

Parallel Loop said it has a team of 30 and serves more than 10 clients across industries and geographies. Its clients include Licious and Havells in India, as well as Tokio Marine Safety Insurance in Thailand.

title: Pre-owned goods marketplace Circle raises Rs 25 Cr led by Nexus Venture Partners
description: Bengaluru based pre-owned goods marketplace Circle has raised Rs 25 crore in a seed funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners.
body: Bengaluru based pre-owned goods marketplace Circle has raised Rs 25 crore in a seed funding round led by Nexus Venture Partners. Existing investor Titan Capital and Myntra co-founder Raveen Sastry also participated in the round, along with Delhivery COO Ajith Pai as an angel investor.

The fresh capital will be used to expand beyond Bengaluru and strengthen the company’s AI-based pricing, product discovery and verification capabilities. Circle also plans to expand its Trust Hubs and logistics network as it scales operations across India.
Founded in 2025 by Chirag Kataruka and Ankit Misra, Circle operates a managed customer-to-customer (C2C) marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned products.
Its platform combines AI-based technology, product verification and logistics to facilitate transactions without owning inventory.
Within a year of launch, Circle claims to have facilitated around Rs 25 crore in pre-owned sales. The platform has attracted over 10 lakh visitors and generated 1 lakh listings in Bengaluru.
According to the company, sellers typically find buyers within three days. Nearly 40% of its buyers return within 90 days, while half of its sellers list products again.

Circle offers products across categories including smartphones, gaming consoles, cameras, furniture, watches, handbags and sneakers. Its services include product verification, pickup, payments and a three-day Circle Guarantee for buyers.

title: Groww’s equity derivatives revenue falls 14.3% QoQ amid CAS impact
description: The parent company of stockbroking platform Groww, saw its equity derivatives revenue decline 14.3% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in the September quarter of FY27
body: Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of stockbroking platform Groww, saw its equity derivatives revenue decline 14.3% quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) in the September quarter of FY27, with the company attributing most of the fall to SEBI’s new Closing Auction System (CAS).

In its quarterly results, Groww said the decline was in line with the trend seen across the industry following the rollout of CAS on August 3, 2026. The system changed the way closing prices are determined for stocks eligible for futures and options (F&O) trading.
Under CAS, exchanges conduct a closing auction to determine the final price of eligible stocks. The change has affected trading volumes as market participants adjust to the new mechanism.

The new system also creates a gap between cash-market and derivatives trading hours. Continuous trading in eligible stocks ends at 3:15 PM, while equity derivatives continue trading until 3:40 PM. This can make it harder for traders to hedge their positions and manage risk during the closing period.

The impact comes even as Groww reported growth in its overall business. Its parent company posted a consolidated net profit of Rs 725.6 crore in Q2 FY27, up 54% year-on-year, while revenue rose 44% to Rs 1,541 crore from Rs 1,071 crore a year earlier.
The share of equity derivatives in Groww’s revenue also declined to 45% in the September quarter from around 57% a year earlier.

Meanwhile, SEBI has proposed changes to the derivatives settlement mechanism to address concerns around CAS. The regulator is considering separating derivatives settlement prices from the closing auction price, a move that could help normalise trading activity if implemented.
The extent of any recovery in derivatives revenue will depend on the final regulatory framework and how market participants adapt to the changes.

title: Decoding: Boldfit founders retain 78.23% stake after Rs 400 Cr Series B
description: KL Rahul-backed sports and fitness brand Boldfit has raised Rs 400 crore in its Series B round from The Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company
body: KL Rahul-backed sports and fitness brand Boldfit has raised Rs 400 crore in its Series B round from The Bharat Value Fund, managed by The Wealth Company (formerly Pantomath Capital Management), at a valuation of Rs 4,000 crore. The founders still holds over 78%, a rarity in India’s fitness and wellness segment, where D2C brands typically give up significant equity to investors well before reaching this scale.
Entrackr examined Bengaluru-based company's regulatory filings to decode the company's latest funding round, updated captable, and post-money valuation.

According to the company's regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , Boldfit's board approved the allotment of 12,783 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 3,12,926.47 per share, aggregating to approximately Rs 400 crore.
The Bharat Value Fund was the sole investor in the Rs 400 crore funding round.

As per Entrackr estimated, Boldfit's valuation jumped 5.71X to Rs 4,000 crore in its Series B round from Rs 700 crore in Series A. The fresh capital will be used to expand its nationwide retail presence, invest in product innovation and manufacturing, and selectively pursue inorganic opportunities to strengthen its presence across categories.

Co-founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani and Aasshna Guptaa, Boldfit is an e-commerce platform that offers sports and fitness products across categories such as apparel, fitness equipment, nutrition supplements and accessories. Its portfolio covers sports such as basketball, cycling, football, volleyball, badminton and cricket, with over 400 products.

In November 2024 the company had raised Rs 110 crore in a Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners. Following the latest Series B allotment, Bharat Value Fund emerged as Boldfit’s largest external shareholder with a 10% stake, followed by Bessemer Venture Partners at 8.63%. Founder Pallav Bihani retains a 77.45% stake in the company, while other co-founder Aasshna Guptaa holds 0.78% stake. Meanwhile Indian cricketer KL Rahul owns 0.03% stake.
Other Indian sports personalities, including Sania Mirza, Manika Batra and Arshdeep Singh, also hold minority stakes in the company.

title: Supplements brand The Stack raises Rs 21.5 Cr in seed round
description: The Goa-based startup had earlier raised Rs 5.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round co-led by OTP Ventures and Huddle Ventures, with participation from a group of angel investors in January this year.
body: The Stack, a supplements brand focused on clinically studied ingredients and transparent formulations, has raised Rs 21.5 crore in a seed funding round co-led by Sauce, OTP Ventures and Huddle Ventures.
The Goa-based startup had earlier raised Rs 5.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round co-led by OTP Ventures and Huddle Ventures, with participation from a group of angel investors in January this year.

The Stack, a supplements brand focused on clinically studied ingredients and transparent formulations, has raised Rs 21.5 crore in a seed funding round co-led by Sauce, OTP Ventures and Huddle Ventures.
The fresh funds will be used to expand its team, invest in research and development, and grow its product portfolio, The Stack said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2024 by Shreya Jain and Kshitij Rihal, The Stack develops science-backed supplements using globally sourced ingredients that have been clinically studied. The brand focuses on transparent formulations and long-term consumer outcomes.

The Stack follows a quality-first approach, with a limited range of products across key health areas such as sleep, gut health and functional health. The company aims to build a trusted supplements brand from India that meets global standards.

The brand currently sells five products. One in three customers places a second order within six months, while many customers pay upfront for six to 12 months through subscriptions. The top 10% of customers account for 30% of its revenue. The company also sees a strong inflow of new customers through referrals and word of mouth.
The Stack said it has grown fivefold in six months and is targeting 6-7X growth in FY27 compared with FY26.

title: Groww makes Rs 725 Cr profit on Rs 1,502 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27
description: Digital investment platform Groww’s profit rose 54% year-on-year to Rs 725 crore in Q2 FY27, while revenue from operations grew 47% to Rs 1,502 crore.
body: Digital investment platform Groww reported a strong financial performance in the second quarter of FY27, with its profit growing nearly 54% year-on-year to Rs 725 crore. The company also recorded a 47% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations during the quarter.
According to its financial statement sourced from the NSE, Groww’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,502 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,019 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

The company earned an additional Rs 39 crore from other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,540 crore during the quarter. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, operating revenue remained largely flat compared with Rs 1,501 crore in Q1 FY27.

Employee benefits remained as the largest cost component for Groww at Rs 169 crore, representing over 30% of total expenses in Q2 FY27. Finance costs and depreciation expenses stood at Rs 4.7 crore and Rs 18.2 crore, respectively.
Overall, the Lalit Keshre-led firm reported a 28% year-on-year increase in total expenditure to Rs 556 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 433 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
The  Groww’s profit surged 54% year-on-year to Rs 725 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 471 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, profit declined marginally by 2% from Rs 735 crore in Q1 FY27.

Groww continued to dominate India’s stockbroking industry in September, retaining its position as the country’s largest broker with 1.34 crore active clients and a 29.16% market share, according to NSE data. The platform added over 1 lakh active clients during the month and has consistently accounted for more than 60% of the industry’s net client additions each month.

Zerodha and Angel One ranked second and third, with market shares of 14.73% and 14.65%, respectively. Meanwhile, new emerging broker Sahi for the consecutive month recorded the fastest growth among the top 20 brokers.

title: RocketPay raises Rs 10 Cr led by Sandeep Jain and Group
description: RocketPay, a digital collections infrastructure platform for lenders, has raised Rs 10 crore in a funding round led by Sandeep Jain and Group. Snippets
body: RocketPay, a digital collections infrastructure platform for lenders, has raised Rs 10 crore in a funding round led by Sandeep Jain and Group.
The round also saw participation from IPV, LetsVenture, Launch Capital, AVNM Ventures and Navyug Global Ventures, alongside existing investor All In Capital.
The fresh capital will support RocketPay’s expansion from digital collections into recovery infrastructure for lenders. It also plans to expand into technology-enabled recovery of financed devices.

Founded in 2022 by Rishav Dokania, Arpit Bajpai, Ishan Sharma and Kishor Chabbadiya, RocketPay helps lenders automate collections through tools such as Account Aggregator, NACH and UPI Autopay. Its platform also offers remote locking and unlocking of financed Android devices.

The firm claims to have reported a 10x increase in revenue between FY24 and FY26 and aims to reach an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 100 crore by FY28. Its platform is used by lenders with assets under management ranging from Rs 300 crore to Rs 16,000 crore.
The brand is Trustonic’s authorised APAC partner and has access to its Device Lock Controller technology, which enables device-level locking for financing programmes.

The expansion comes ahead of the RBI framework on device locking as a collateral-enforcement tool for mobile loans, which is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027. According to the company, more than 85 million devices are sold on EMIs annually in India, with the market expected to grow at a 10-12% CAGR between FY26 and FY30.

title: Aum Ventures leads Rs 17 Cr round in OXG Space
description: Bengaluru-based spacetech startup OXG Space has raised Rs 17 crore in a funding round led by Aum Ventures through its India Innovation Fund II.  Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based spacetech startup OXG Space has raised Rs 17 crore in a funding round led by Aum Ventures through its India Innovation Fund II.
The round also saw participation from Skyroot Aerospace co-founders Pawan Kumar Chandana and Bharath Daka, and Cosmoserve founder Dr Chiran Phanindra.

The fresh funds will support Mission Synapse, a 12-month programme to demonstrate its core technologies in orbit. These include a Ka-band phased-array antenna targeting an initial 1 Gbps-class link, a deployable mesh reflector for ground connectivity, and a deployable solar array to power computing and communications payloads.

Founded by former ISRO engineers Akash Shetty and Sanjay Gorur, OXG Space is building an orbital network that combines satellite connectivity with in-orbit computing to process Earth observation (EO) data and deliver intelligence in near real time.
Currently, EO satellites typically store imagery until they pass over ground stations, resulting in a delay of 4 to 12 hours between observation and insights.

The company is targeting defence, intelligence and commercial satellite operators. Its technology is designed to combine data from multiple satellites in orbit, enabling faster analysis of optical, radar and signals-intelligence data.
OXG Space’s founders bring over 17 years of combined experience across India’s space programmes, including spacecraft systems for Chandrayaan-2 and Chandrayaan-3.

title: Elevation Capital leads $10.5 Mn Series A round in Spill Games
description: Bengaluru-based Spill Games, an AI-led mobile gaming studio, has raised $10.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Elevation Capital.
body: Bengaluru-based Spill Games, an AI-led mobile gaming studio, has raised $10.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Elevation Capital. Existing investors Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital also participated in the round.

The startup had previously raised $3.1 million in a seed round co-led by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital in April 2026. It also raised $750,000 from All In Capital, M-League and other angel investors in December 2024.

The fresh capital will be used to scale successful games, expand its portfolio, fund user acquisition, strengthen its technology and AI capabilities, and selectively hire talent, Spill Games said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by former PlaySimple Games operators Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg, Spill Games is building a systems-driven approach to game development that combines AI, proprietary technology, data and rapid experimentation. The approach aims to help a small team take game concepts from development to market validation and global scaling faster.

According to the company, its portfolio has grown from three games with scalable and profitable metrics to six in less than three months. It plans to increase the number of games it can test and scale.

At the core of its approach is Compass, a proprietary AI-led engine and tooling layer that integrates analytics, retention, monetisation and live operations. The technology allows Spill Games to reuse infrastructure across titles and shorten the time from concept development to market testing. The company aims to develop games about four times faster than traditional approaches.

Spill Games develops multiple game concepts, builds prototypes and tests them with players. It uses data on retention, engagement, monetisation and user acquisition to identify titles that warrant further investment.
According to market research, the global mobile gaming market is estimated to reach $176.7 billion in 2026 and is projected to grow to $256.2 billion by 2030.

title: Enterprise AI startup RevRag AI raises $2.5 Mn in seed round
description: Enterprise AI startup RevRag AI has raised $2.5 million in a seed funding round co-led by Accion Ventures and Cedar Hill Capital. Wyser and Venture Catalysts also participated in the round.
body: Enterprise AI startup RevRag AI has raised $2.5 million in a seed funding round led by Accion Ventures with Cedar Hill Capital. Wyser and Venture Catalysts also participated in the round.

The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised $600,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by Powerhouse Ventures in August 2024. It also acquired GenStaq.ai, a modular LLMOps and workflow orchestration startup, in September 2025.
The proceeds will be used to accelerate product development, expand enterprise deployments and support its entry into the US market, RevRag AI said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Ashutosh Prakash Singh, Neeraj Gupta and Pankaj Gupta, RevRag AI builds multilingual AI agents that operate within the apps of banks, lenders, fintech and insurtech companies as digital relationship managers.

The platform integrates with financial institutions' workflows to manage customer onboarding, sales and support. The company claims its agents help improve digital adoption, reduce customer drop-offs and drive revenue at up to 70% lower cost.
RevRag AI claims to work with more than 45 financial institutions, including PhonePe, Bajaj Finance, Motilal Oswal, IIFL and Aditya Birla Capital.

title: Construction robotics startup Origin raises $20 Mn led by Accel, Zacua Ventures
description: Origin, a physical AI startup building robots for interior construction, has raised $20 million in total funding in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures.
body: Origin, a physical AI startup building robots for interior construction, has raised $20 million in total funding in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. The round also saw participation from Unilazer Ventures, Schema Ventures and Z21, along with angel investors from Anduril, Skild AI, 1X and Tesla.

The company will use the funds to expand its robot fleet, deploy its flagship robot OG-1 and conduct customer pilots in the US and Europe. It also plans to expand its robotics platform to additional interior construction tasks.

Founded in 2025 by Yogesh Ghaturle, Ashish Daga and Tushar Makkar, Origin develops robots designed to automate interior construction work. Its flagship robot, OG-1, currently handles wall finishing tasks such as applying compound, sanding and priming walls.

The robot is designed to operate across commercial spaces, residential apartments, data centres, hotels and warehouses. The company said it deployed its first robots at construction sites in New York within 10 months of its founding.

Origin is preparing for pilots with customers in the US and Europe, including two large drywall finishing contractors in the US. It also plans to conduct pilots in Germany, Sweden, France and Saudi Arabia.

The startup's robots are powered by its Construction Action Model, a foundation model developed for construction workflows. The system combines task planning, autonomous navigation and tool control to help robots perform construction tasks and adapt to changing site conditions.
Origin plans to expand OG-1's capabilities to tasks such as taping, drywall installation, drilling and conduit installation. The company is targeting the deployment of 150 robots by the end of 2027.

The funding comes amid rising interest in construction robotics as companies look to address labour shortages and improve productivity. According to a survey published by the Associated General Contractors of America in September 2026, worker shortages delayed projects for 42% of surveyed US construction firms.

title: Flipkart Group posts Rs 1.46 lakh Cr revenue in FY26, losses stand at Rs 8,468 Cr
description: Walmart-owned Flipkart Group reported 18.2% year-on-year growth in consolidated revenue in FY26, while net losses narrowed 2.1% to Rs 8,468 crore.
body: Walmart-owned Flipkart Group continued to expand its business in FY26, with consolidated revenue rising 18.2% year-on-year. The group also reported a marginal improvement in its bottom line, as net losses narrowed 2.1% to Rs 8,468 crore during the fiscal year.

Flipkart Internet’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 145,880 crore in FY26, from Rs 123,451 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

The FY26 financials reflect the consolidated performance of Flipkart Group following its reverse flip to India, bringing 25 subsidiary companies under Flipkart Internet. The consolidation includes key businesses such as Flipkart, Myntra and Cleartrip, among others, following the amalgamation of the group’s Singapore entities with Flipkart Internet in March 2026.

Sale of traded goods remained Flipkart Internet’s largest revenue stream at Rs 1,04,850 crore, up 12.8% from Rs 92,957 crore in FY25. This reflects revenue from product sales through its commerce operations rather than only commissions earned on transactions.

Logistics, warehousing and shipping services emerged as the second-largest revenue stream, with revenue from this segment jumped 2.4X to Rs 23,059 crore from Rs 9,580 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Revenue from advertisement services grew 30.7% to Rs 9,597 crore in FY26 from Rs 7,343 crore a year earlier.

In contrast, revenue from marketplace and collection services fell 43.9% to Rs 6,719 crore from Rs 11,967 crore in FY25. These services include seller fees, commissions and payment collection charges.

Other operating income contributed Rs 1,655 crore in FY26, while non-operating income added another Rs 820 crore, which took Flipkart Internet’s total revenue to Rs 1,46,700 crore during the fiscal year.

title: Udaan posts Rs 5,134 Cr gross revenue and Rs 852 Cr loss in FY26
description: After a 20% decline in FY25, the B2B ecommerce platform Udaan returned to revenue growth, posting 12.6% year-on-year growth in FY26. The Bengaluru-based company also narrowed its losses by 19% to Rs 852 crore.
body: After a 20% decline in FY25, the B2B ecommerce platform Udaan returned to revenue growth, posting 12.6% year-on-year growth in FY26. The Bengaluru-based company also narrowed its losses by 19% to Rs 852 crore.

Udaan’s gross revenue (GMV) grew to Rs 5,134 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,561 crore in FY25, according to the company’s consolidated financial statements filed by its group company, Trustroot Internet in Singapore.

Founded in 2016 by former Flipkart executives Vaibhav Gupta, Sujeet Kumar and Amod Malviya, Udaan connects brands and wholesalers with retailers through its B2B ecommerce platform, with revenue from goods sales, logistics, platform fees, credit services and advertising.

Udaan’s gross merchandise value (GMV) stood at around Rs 10,000 crore in FY22. The decline since then reflects its exit from non-core categories such as lifestyle and general merchandise, as the company shifted its focus to groceries and essential goods.

On the cost side, material expenses rose 11.3% to Rs 4,859 crore in FY26 from Rs 4,367 crore in the previous fiscal. Finance costs increased 33.5% to Rs 247 crore, while logistics expenses grew 16.7% to Rs 182 crore.
Employee benefit expenses declined to Rs 347.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 500 crore in FY25, largely due to a reduction in ESOP expenses from Rs 280 crore to Rs 140 crore.

Decent revenue growth and lower ESOP costs helped Udaan narrow its net loss by 19.2% to Rs 852 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,055 crore in FY25. This extended its streak of annual loss reduction to four years, from Rs 2,075 crore in FY23 and Rs 1,674.1 crore in FY24.

In September 2026, Udaan agreed to acquire Swiggy’s retail distribution business Lynk Logistics for Rs 500 crore to expand its reach across key markets. Swiggy will receive an approximately 2.8% stake in Udaan through preference shares and invest another Rs 75 crore for a 0.4% stake. The deal will add Lynk’s brand partnerships and retail network to Udaan’s distribution business.

title: Tonbo Imaging raises Rs 255 Cr from anchor investors ahead of IPO
description: Tonbo Imaging has raised Rs 255.36 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), which opens for subscription on October 15.
body: Bengaluru-based defence technology startup Tonbo Imaging has raised Rs 255.36 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering (IPO), which opens for subscription on October 15.

The company allotted 36.48 lakh equity shares at Rs 700 per share, the upper end of its IPO price band. The anchor book saw participation from global investors such as BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Temasek Holdings, Allianz Global Investors and Prudential, along with domestic mutual funds and insurance companies. SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund and ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund were among the domestic investors.

Tonbo Imaging has fixed a price band of Rs 665-700 per share for its Rs 852.2 crore IPO, which will close on October 19. The public issue comprises an offer for sale (OFS) of around 1.22 crore shares by existing shareholders, with no fresh issue component.

Founded by Ankit Kumar, Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar and Cecilia D'Souza, Tonbo Imaging develops imaging and surveillance systems for defence and security applications. Its products include thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, targeting systems, missile seekers and fire control systems.

The company supplies its products to government and defence agencies and operates in the defence electronics segment, which has gained attention amid India's push to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing.
JM Financial and IIFL Capital Services are managing the IPO. The company's shares are proposed to be listed on the BSE and NSE.

Tonbo Imaging’s revenue fell 22.7% to Rs 362.65 crore in FY26, while net profit declined 30% to Rs 50.88 crore. In the June quarter of FY27, it reported a loss of Rs 17.74 crore on revenue of Rs 36.01 crore.

title: Banaraswala raises $2 Mn from Prax Impex to expand across India
description: The proceeds will be used to expand its outlets, develop new menu offerings and grow its franchise network across India.
body: Banarasi food brand Banaraswala has raised $2 million in a seed funding round from Prax Impex Private Limited.
The proceeds will be used to expand its outlets, develop new menu offerings and grow its franchise network across India.

Founded by Vibhanshu Mishra, Banaraswala operates under the tagline “Ghat Se Ghar Tak” and serves traditional Banarasi food, including sweets, chaats and meals. The brand incorporates elements such as kulhads, pattal and clay into its dining experience.

The company currently operates three outlets across Delhi and plans to expand into Banswara in Rajasthan, Sarangpur in Gujarat, and Farrukhabad and Fatehpur in Uttar Pradesh. It also sells through major food delivery platforms.
Banaraswala aims to expand to 50 outlets across Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi NCR and other Tier 2 markets by March 2027. The expansion will include both company-owned and franchise outlets.
The company also plans to strengthen its operations, team and processes as it expands into new markets.

title: IntrCity SmartBus’ FY26 revenue rises 40% to Rs 691 Cr; losses rise 76%
description: IntrCity Smartbus, reported a 40.1% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in FY26. However, its losses widened 76% to Rs 28 crore during the year.
body: Travel-tech platform IntrCity Smartbus, reported a 40.1% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in FY26, following a Rs 250 crore Series D round led by A91 Partners in October 2025 to support expansion and technology upgrades. However, its losses widened 76% to Rs 28 crore during the year.
IntrCity’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 690.9 crore during FY26 as compared to Rs 493.2 crore in FY25, as per the company’s consolidated financial statements with the Registrar of Companies.

IntrCity SmartBus offers intercity bus travel through its digital platform and a network of independent operators, with services such as live tracking, onboard captains and boarding lounges. It also operates RailYatri, a train travel information and services platform, and relies on rented vehicles and operator partnerships rather than owning its fleet.

Bus operations remained the largest contributor to revenue at Rs 670.35 crore, or about 97% of operating revenue in FY26. Revenue from this service increased 42.5% from Rs 470.56 crore in FY25 as the company expanded its core intercity travel business.
Commission income declined 23.6% to Rs 14.18 crore from Rs 18.55 crore in the previous fiscal year. Meanwhile, revenue from advertisement services nearly doubled to Rs 2.44 crore from Rs 1.27 crore.
Including other operating and non-operating income, Intrcity’s total income stood at Rs 693.6 crore in FY26.

On the expense side, bus operations costs rose 43.5% to Rs 539.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 376.13 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for nearly 75% of total costs, in line with IntrCity's asset-light model that relies on rented vehicles and partner operators.
Commissions paid to selling agents increased 51% to Rs 75.97 crore from Rs 50.35 crore. These payments support ticket distribution and customer acquisition through sales agents and booking partners.

title: Space robotics startup Cosmochute raises $1.5 Mn in pre-seed round
description: Space robotics startup Cosmochute has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Accel and Prosus Ventures under the Atoms X programme.
body: Space robotics startup Cosmochute has raised $1.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Accel and Prosus Ventures under the Atoms X programme. IIMA Ventures’ Deep-tech and Aerospace Acceleration Fund, Operators Studio and Chinmayi Muthyala also participated in the round.
Cosmochute is among seven startups selected for the inaugural Atoms X cohort, which was launched earlier this year.
The company will use the proceeds for product development, engineering team expansion and its commercial roadmap, as it prepares for its next phase of growth, Cosmochute said in a press release.

Founded this year by Janhavi Gore, Amit Chowdhary and Dhruv Alok Sangal, Cosmochute is building space robotics infrastructure for the emerging lunar economy. Its first programme, LEAP, is a modular platform designed to support payload transportation and deployment on the Moon.

LEAP combines a modular rover and trailer with standard payload bays, allowing multiple payloads to be integrated into a common mission architecture. The company aims to address the cost and complexity of delivering equipment and payloads to the lunar surface through a standardised approach to lunar transportation and deployment.
The platform is designed to reduce the need for mission specific engineering and make lunar transportation and payload deployment more repeatable.

Cosmochute is setting up its lunar laboratories at IIMA Ventures’ incubation facility. The startup is also working within India’s space technology ecosystem, which includes companies, investors and institutions supporting private participation in the sector.

With LEAP as its first platform, Cosmochute plans to develop capabilities in lunar mobility and space robotics, with potential applications in other in space and terrestrial use cases. The company aims to build infrastructure to support commercial and scientific missions to the Moon.

title: Z47 leads $12.5 Mn Series A round in Confido Health
description: Healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Z47, with participation from existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures.
body: Healthtech startup Confido Health has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round led by Z47, with participation from existing investors Together Fund and Blume Ventures. The round follows a $10 million Series A round announced in September.
The startup had previously raised $3 million in a seed round led by Together Fund in December 2024.
The proceeds will be used to scale its AI platform for healthcare operations, Confido Health said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Chetan Reddy and Vichar Shroff, Confido Health develops AI agents to manage tasks such as appointment scheduling, insurance verification and care coordination. The agents integrate with existing healthcare systems through no-code deployment, with the company claiming a setup time of less than five minutes.

Confido Health said its platform integrates with more than 50 systems, including electronic health records, practice management, phone, billing and fax systems, without requiring healthcare providers to change their existing technology stack.

The company said it operates across more than 1,500 care sites, primarily independent practice groups, in 27 states and serves around 3,200 providers. It added that one in 50 patients can now access their healthcare providers through its AI agents.

The platform uses patient details, referral information and payer requirements collected during intake to manage subsequent tasks such as outreach and scheduling. According to the company, this allows a single interaction to trigger multiple workflows, including referrals, appointments, prescription refills and payments.

Confido Health said it has recorded 15x growth since its previous funding round and achieved AI handle rates of more than 95% across key end-to-end office workflows. It also claims its platform adds capacity equivalent to three to five full-time employees on average within three months of deployment.

title: Enterprise AI startup Shamrock AI raises $5 Mn led by Endiya Partners
description: Shamrock AI, an enterprise AI startup building an agentic assurance platform for large enterprises, has raised $5 million in a seed funding round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures.
body: Shamrock AI, an enterprise AI startup building an agentic assurance platform for large enterprises, has raised $5 million in a seed funding round led by Endiya Partners, with participation from Capria Ventures.
The funds will be used to accelerate product development, expand the team and scale go-to-market efforts, Shamrock AI said in a press release.

Founded in 2026 by Sarat Addanki, Michael (Mick) Gallagher and Anuraag Nallapati, Shamrock AI is developing a platform to help enterprises deploy AI agents across critical business processes. Its platform uses an Enterprise Business Knowledge Graph to connect business processes, systems, data and configurations.

The company is initially focusing on agentic test lifecycle automation for enterprise resource planning (ERP) transformations, including SAP S/4HANA migrations. It plans to expand into data observability and autonomous business process automation.
Headquartered in Shillong, Shamrock AI claims to serve multiple Fortune 500 companies, including a Fortune 100 AI hardware manufacturer and a Fortune 100 healthcare company.

The startup plans to expand its team across India and the US, with 70% to 80% of its workforce expected to be based in India. It also plans to build a client-facing team in the US and expand its presence in the Middle East.

Shamrock AI’s platform continuously tests and validates business processes to build a representation of how an enterprise operates. The company aims to use this context to support reliable AI agent deployment across enterprise workflows.

title: Cult.fit gets SEBI nod for proposed IPO
description: The company, formerly known as Curefit Healthcare, plans to raise Rs 950 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 17.86 crore shares by existing shareholders.
body: Fitness and lifestyle platform Cult.fit has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

The company, formerly known as Curefit Healthcare, plans to raise Rs 950 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 17.86 crore shares by existing shareholders.

The proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to repay borrowings, set up new Cult Elite and Cult Neo fitness centres, expand Cultsport’s exclusive brand outlets, meet lease and rental payments for existing centres, and fund brand marketing and general corporate purposes.

According to the company’s draft papers, Cult.fit operates 708 fitness centres across 77 cities in India as of March 31, 2026. Its fitness services business had nearly 9.87 lakh paid members in FY26, while its fitness products business shipped over 42.3 lakh products during the year.
The company operates across two key segments, fitness services and fitness products. Fitness services contributed around 70% of its revenue, while fitness products accounted for the remaining 30%.
Cult.fit’s operating revenue rose 36.26% year-on-year to Rs 1,720.61 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 1,262.93 crore in FY25. The company had reported operating revenue of Rs 926.66 crore in FY24.
Its adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 8.41% in FY26 from -2.76% in FY25, according to the draft papers.

The company operates different formats of fitness centres, including Cult Elite, which combines gym workouts with instructor-led group classes, and Cult Neo, a gym format focused on equipment-based workouts. Its fitness products business sells apparel, footwear, equipment and accessories under the Cultsport brand.

title: Snabbit matches Urban Company’s InstaHelp in NTV; burns Rs 32 Cr less in Q2 FY27
description: Quick home services startup Snabbit recorded a net transaction value (NTV) of Rs 72 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally ahead of Urban Company’s InstaHelp at Rs 71 crore.
body: Quick home services startup Snabbit recorded a net transaction value (NTV) of Rs 72 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally ahead of Urban Company’s InstaHelp at Rs 71 crore. However, Snabbit reported a lower burn of Rs 142 crore against InstaHelp’s adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 174 crore in the quarter, according to Snabbit co-founder Ayush Agarwal’s LinkedIn post.

The numbers show that while both platforms generated nearly the same transaction value, Urban Company’s InstaHelp incurred Rs 32 crore more in losses during the quarter. However, the burn figures may not be directly comparable unless they use the same accounting measure.

Urban Company reported Rs 20.37 crore in revenue from InstaHelp in Q2 FY27, up 82% quarter-on-quarter. The platform processed 6.2 million orders during the quarter, translating into average revenue of nearly Rs 33 per order.
According to Agarwal’s post, Snabbit processed 6.4 million orders during the quarter. This puts the two platforms at a similar scale in terms of order volumes.

Snabbit reported Rs 12.25 crore in operating revenue and a net loss of Rs 168 crore in FY26. The company said its daily jobs grew 75 times during the year as it expanded its quick home services business.

The Q2 figures highlight the intense competition in the instant home services market, where platforms are investing heavily to acquire customers and expand their operations. With both businesses recording similar NTV, their ability to improve unit economics and reduce losses will be key as they scale.

title: Urban Company’s InstaHelp reports Rs 174 Cr adjusted EBITDA loss on Rs 21 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27
description: Urban Company’s operating revenue grew 41% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, while losses tripled amid heavy investments in its InstaHelp, which reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 174 crore.
body: Home services marketplace Urban Company reported a 41% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in Q2 FY27. However, its losses widened threefold as the company continued to invest in its quick home services platform InstaHelp, which alone reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of Rs 174 crore during the quarter.

Urban Company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 527 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 380 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Urban Company's India Consumer Services business, excluding InstaHelp, remained its largest revenue contributor, accounting for over 62% of operating revenue. The segment's revenue grew 28% year-on-year to Rs 336.4 crore in Q2 FY27.

Its Native brands business recorded a 40% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 105.4 crore, compared with Rs 75.4 crore in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, the international business grew 82% to Rs 75 crore.

InstaHelp, Urban Company's quick-service housekeeping vertical, generated Rs 20.37 crore in revenue, up 82% quarter-on-quarter, on 6.2 million orders in Q2 FY27. This translated to an average revenue of nearly Rs 33 per order.

However, net order value declined to Rs 114 from Rs 138 in the previous quarter amid intense competition and introductory prices for new users. The platform's adjusted EBITDA loss per order improved to Rs 279 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 346 in Q1.

Urban Company's employee benefits expenses rose 60% year-on-year to Rs 182 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 114 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company's overall expenses increased 62% to Rs 746 crore during the quarter.

As expenses grew faster than revenue and heavy investments in InstaHelp continued, Urban Company's losses ballooned threefold year-on-year to Rs 182 crore in Q2 FY27. However, its core India Consumer Services business remained EBITDA profitable.

title: Urban Company approves Rs 2,500 Cr fundraise amid rising competition in InstaHelp
description: Urban Company has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 2,500 crore through equity shares and convertible securities, including a qualified institutional placement (QIP).
body: Urban Company has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 2,500 crore through equity shares and convertible securities, including a qualified institutional placement (QIP), as the home services platform looks to strengthen its business and scale its operations.
In a stock exchange filing on October 16, the company said its board had approved raising funds through one or more routes, including a preferential allotment, private placement and QIP.
The proposed fundraise is subject to shareholder approval and other regulatory clearances. The company is yet to finalise the terms of the issue.
The fundraise is expected to support the expansion of its InstaHelp segment, which faces growing competition from rivals such as Snabbit and Pronto.
The capital could help Urban Company scale the business, acquire more customers and increase marketing spends as players compete to capture a larger share of the instant domestic help market.
The board also approved the company's unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 2026.

Urban Company's consolidated operating revenue rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 527 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 380 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year. However, its net loss widened to Rs 182.5 crore from Rs 59.3 crore a year ago.

For the first half of FY27, the company's operating revenue increased 42.6% to Rs 1,065.6 crore from Rs 747.3 crore in the year-ago period. Its net loss widened to Rs 274.6 crore from Rs 52.4 crore in H1 FY26.

title: RapidCanvas raises $29 Mn in Series B round led by Vertex Ventures
description: The latest round takes the company’s total funding to $52.5 million. The company will use the proceeds to expand its go to market teams, strengthen partnerships and grow its field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil.
body: AI startup RapidCanvas has raised $29 million in a Series B funding round led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India, with participation from Hitachi Ventures and existing investors Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures.

The latest round takes the company’s total funding to $52.5 million. The company will use the proceeds to expand its go to market teams, strengthen partnerships and grow its field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil.

Founded in 2021, RapidCanvas provides an AI platform that combines AI agents with human expertise to help enterprises build and deploy custom AI applications. Its platform aims to help businesses move AI projects from pilots to production.

The company said its annual recurring revenue grew 8x over the past six quarters. More than 40% of its customers now run multiple AI use cases in production. In 2026, over 75 enterprises across manufacturing, financial services, retail, business services and infrastructure made 1.4 million AI led decisions using applications built on its platform.

RapidCanvas offers three core products: Enterprise Context Engine, Visual Development Canvas and Operational Harness. These products help enterprises capture business context, develop custom AI applications and manage deployed AI solutions.

The company targets enterprises with annual revenue of $100 million to $10 billion that have AI budgets but lack the resources or expertise to deploy custom AI applications. Its model combines an AI platform with field engineers who work with customers to build applications and oversee their outcomes after deployment.

In December 2024, RapidCanvas raised $16 million in a Series A funding round led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Titanium Ventures, Accel and Valley Capital Partners. The round took its total funding to $23.5 million at the time.

RapidCanvas was co founded by Rahul Pangam and Uttam Phalnikar, who previously built Simility, an AI based risk management company acquired by PayPal. The founders have positioned RapidCanvas around a hybrid model that combines AI tools with human expertise to develop and deploy enterprise AI applications.

title: Snabbit reports Rs 12 Cr revenue and Rs 168 Cr loss in FY26; claims 75X growth in core biz
description: Snabbit’s revenue from operations stood at Rs 12.25 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 26 lakh in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the RoC.
body: Two-year-old Snabbit posted a Rs 168 crore loss in FY26 on operating revenue of Rs 12.25 crore, pointing to the steep costs of building an on-demand home services business. Yet the losses are not unique to Snabbit: rivals Urban Company’s InstaHelp and Pronto are also spending heavily to scale, as players race to build demand and establish leadership.
Snabbit’s revenue from operations stood at Rs 12.25 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 26 lakh in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2024 by Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit is an on-demand home services platform that connects households with trained professionals for tasks such as cleaning, dishwashing and laundry. Users can book professionals by the hour, with the platform promising service within 10 minutes.
Platform services contributed Rs 10.82 crore, or 88% of its operating revenue, while the remaining amount came from the sale of uniforms.

The company also earned Rs 14.76 crore in other income, mainly from interest on bank deposits. Snabbit earned more from interest on its bank deposits than from its core operations. This has been common among consumer internet businesses in their early years, as they navigate intense competition and invest in growth.

On the cost side, employee benefits accounted for Rs 46 crore, while expert service costs stood at Rs 63 crore. Snabbit spent another Rs 49 crore on marketing and Rs 23.8 crore on service fulfilment. Banking charges, commissions, recruitment, legal expenses, software maintenance and other overheads pushed its total expenses to Rs 195 crore in FY26 from Rs 6.8 crore in FY25.

Heavy spending on customer acquisition, workers and service delivery pushed its net loss to Rs 168 crore in FY26 from Rs 5.7 crore in the previous fiscal year. At the unit level, Snabbit spent Rs 15.92 to earn every rupee of operating revenue.

Given how new the category is, traditional profitability metrics may not tell the entire story at this stage. However, Snabbit reported a negative return on capital employed (ROCE) of 58.45% and an EBITDA margin of -1481.63% in FY26.

title: NeoGrowth swings to Rs 72 Cr loss in FY26; revenue falls 21%
description: MSME-focused lender NeoGrowth slipped into the red in FY26 as a sharp decline in interest income weighed on its financial performance. The company’s revenue
body: MSME-focused lender NeoGrowth slipped into the red in FY26 as a sharp decline in interest income weighed on its financial performance. The company’s revenue contracted during the year, while lower expenses failed to offset the drop, reversing its profitability in FY25 and resulting in a substantial loss in the fiscal year ending March 2026.

The company’s revenue from operations fell to Rs 591.07 crore in FY26 from Rs 750.31 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its annual financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Interest income, the company’s primary revenue source, declined 21.4% to Rs 566.97 crore in FY26 from Rs 721.04 crore in FY25. It accounted for around 96% of its operating revenue during the year.

Income from fees and commissions fell 21.9% to Rs 12.63 crore, while income from the derecognition of loan assets declined 53.2% to Rs 3.14 crore. However, gains from short-term investments in liquid mutual funds rose 40.1% to Rs 7.1 crore during the year.
On the expense side, impairment on financial instruments, which includes provisions for potential loan losses, remained largely flat at Rs 277.32 crore in FY26 against Rs 279.54 crore in FY25.

Finance costs, the company’s second-largest expense, declined 19.5% to Rs 228.88 crore from Rs 284.19 crore. However, employee benefit expenses increased 3.8% to Rs 109.78 crore, while depreciation and amortisation expenses rose to Rs 12.42 crore from Rs 10.71 crore. Other expenses increased to Rs 59.29 crore from Rs 58 crore.

Overall, NeoGrowth’s total expenses declined 6.8% to Rs 687.69 crore in FY26 from Rs 738.19 crore in FY25. However, the decline was not enough to offset lower revenue, pushing the lender into a sizable loss. It reported a net loss of Rs 72.34 crore in FY26, against a net profit of Rs 9.02 crore in FY25.

On a unit level, NeoGrowth spent Rs 1.17 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 0.99 in the previous fiscal year. Its net interest margin (NIM) also declined to 17.11% from 17.52%, while its EBITDA margin fell to 24.33% from 40.79%.

title: Exclusive: CapGrid kicks off pre-Series B round at 50% valuation premium
description: B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid has raised Rs 46.28 crore, or $4.87 million, in a pre-Series B funding round led by new investor Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures
body: B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid has raised Rs 46.28 crore, or $4.87 million, in a pre-Series B funding round led by new investor Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures, with participation from existing investors Nexus Venture Partners, Anicut Capital, and others.

The board at CapGrid passed a special resolution to issue 2,888 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,60,263 per share to raise fresh capital, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr .

Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 38.30 crore, while Axilor Technology Fund and Anicut Capital are investing Rs 3 crore each. Nexus Venture Partners and Amit Jain will contribute Rs 1 crore each.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company’s post-money valuation surged over 50% to Rs 430 crore ($46 million), compared with its previous Series A round of $5 million led by Anicut Capital in February 2025.

Following the pre-Series B allotment, Nexus Venture Partners remained the largest external shareholder, with an 18.08% stake, followed by Anicut Capital with 16.40% and Axilor Ventures with 11.94%. Co-founders Dheeraj Kumar Tiwari and Himanshu Singh Raghuvanshi each hold an 18.63% stake in the company.
According to the filings, CapGrid will use the funds for expansion and growth, as well as to meet its additional capital requirements.

Founded in July 2020 by Dheeraj Kumar Tiwari and Himanshu Singh Raghuvanshi, CapGrid is an AI-powered platform serving industries such as automotive, agricultural equipment, earthmoving equipment, aerospace, oil and gas, consumer durables, and electric vehicles (EVs).
The company is yet to file its FY26 financials. CapGrid’s operating revenue grew 2.1X to Rs 209 crore in FY25 from Rs 99.2 crore in FY24, while its net loss declined marginally to Rs 25.92 crore.

title: Goldman Sachs offloads Rs 169 Cr worth Eternal shares; BofA Securities buys
description: Goldman Sachs has sold 53.37 lakh shares of Eternal for Rs 168.67 crore through a block deal. BofA Securities bought the same number of shares on October 15.
body: Goldman Sachs has sold 53.37 lakh shares of Eternal, the parent company of Zomato and Blinkit, for Rs 168.67 crore through a block deal. BofA Securities bought the same number of shares on October 15.

According to exchange data, Goldman Sachs sold 53,37,584 shares at Rs 316 each. BofA Securities purchased the shares at the same price. The transaction accounted for around 0.05% of Eternal's paid-up equity.

The transaction comes weeks after large investors offloaded nearly Rs 3,265 crore worth of Eternal shares through bulk deals on August 31. BNP Paribas Financial Markets sold 5.09 crore shares worth Rs 1,670.86 crore, while Integrated Core Strategies (Asia), an affiliate of Millennium Management, sold 4.86 crore shares for Rs 1,593.96 crore.

Eternal reported revenue from operations of Rs 20,211 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 7,167 crore in the year-ago period. Its net profit rose to Rs 92 crore from Rs 25 crore a year earlier. However, profit declined from Rs 174 crore in the March quarter.
For FY26, the company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 54,364 crore from Rs 20,243 crore in FY25, while net profit fell to Rs 366 crore from Rs 527 crore.

Eternal operates Zomato's food delivery business and Blinkit, its quick commerce platform. Blinkit competes with Swiggy Instamart and Zepto in India's quick commerce market, where companies are expanding their store networks to improve delivery capacity.
Eternal shares are currently trading at Rs 323.6 (as on 09.37 AM) with a total market capitalization of Rs 3,11,947 crore.

title: Ixigo posts Rs 63 Cr profit in Q2 FY27 on the back of FreshBus exit and other income
description: Online travel aggregator ixigo has released its financial results for the second quarter of FY27, reporting a 13% year-on-year growth in operating revenue.
body: Online travel aggregator ixigo has released its financial results for the second quarter of FY27, reporting a 13% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. The company also swung to a net profit of Rs 63.42 crore, steered by the sale of its stake in FreshBus and Rs 22 crore in other income. The Gurugram-based company’s operating revenue increased 13% year-on-year to Rs 321 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 284 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange.
Train bookings remained the largest contributor to the company's operating revenue, spiking 16.4% year-on-year to Rs 149.1 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 128.1 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Bus revenue grew 23.8% to Rs 81 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 65.4 crore, whereas revenue from flight bookings declined 7.5% to Rs 82.7 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 89.4 crore. The hotel segment recorded the sharpest growth, with revenue surging to Rs 8.1 crore from Rs 1.3 crore in Q2 FY26.

Besides operational revenue, the company reported Rs 22 crore from other income, pushing its total income to Rs 343 crore in Q2 FY27. Employee benefit expenses declined 13.2% to Rs 64.38 crore from Rs 74.18 crore, while total  increased 6% year-on-year to Rs 309.5 crore in Q2 FY27.

Notably, on a quarterly basis, ixigo’s revenue fell 10% from Rs 357 crore in the previous quarter (Q1 FY27). On the profitability front, ixigo reported a net profit of Rs 63.42 crore in Q2 FY27, against a loss of Rs 3.46 crore a year ago. The profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 36.6 crore from the sale of FreshBus shares and the fair value gain on its retained stake. However, profit before tax and exceptional items declined 30% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 33.5 crore from Rs 48 crore in Q1 FY27.
Significantly, the firm’s adjusted EBITDA fell 17% year-on-year to Rs 23.58 crore, its lowest level in five quarters.
For the first half of FY27, ixigo's operating revenue grew 13% year-on-year to Rs 678 crore from Rs 600 crore in H1 FY26, with a Rs 97.6 crore profit.
Ixigo’s shares closed 4.6% higher at Rs 144.46 on Friday, valuing the online travel aggregator at a market capitalisation of Rs 6,102 crore.

title: Exclusive: Battery Smart tops up Series C round with $10 Mn
description: Battery-swapping startup Battery Smart has raised close to Rs 100 crore from an existing investor as it looks to expand its network for electric two- and three-wheelers.
body: Battery-swapping startup Battery Smart has raised close to Rs 100 crore from an existing investor as it looks to expand its network for electric two- and three-wheelers. The fresh capital will support the company’s expansion plans as it continues to scale its battery-swapping network.

According to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , the company allotted 18,000 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 54,407 per share, aggregating to approximately Rs 98 crore from Ecosystem Integrity Fund.
The round appears to be ongoing, with the Gurugram-based company likely to raise additional capital in tranches.

In August 2026, Battery Smart had raised Rs 185.5 crore ($19.5 million) in a Series C funding round led by existing investor Rising Tide Ventures, with participation from Ecosystem Integrity Fund and Blume Ventures.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the company is valued around Rs 4170 crore or  $440 million post money valuation. Battery Smart plans to use fresh proceeds to support business expansion, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes, the filings added.

Founded in 2020, Battery Smart operates a battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers. Its battery-as-a-service (BaaS) model allows users, particularly gig economy drivers, to swap batteries instead of bearing the high upfront cost of battery ownership.

With this round, Battery Smart has raised close to $52 million in 2026 across debt and equity, including $7.2 million in a pre-Series C round, $15 million in debt from Mirova and $19.5 million in Series C in August.
As of now, the company has raised over $221 million to date, with investors including Tiger Global, Blume Ventures and Ecosystem Integrity Fund.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 12- Oct 17]
description: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $302.85 million across 8 growth-stage deals, 21 early-stage deals, and 1 undisclosed round. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $302.85 million across 8 growth-stage deals, 21 early-stage deals, and 1 undisclosed round. The week also saw 5 key appointments, 1 departure and a fund launch.
In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $113.35 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]
Growth-stage startups raised $220.37 million across eight deals this week, led by Tessolve Semiconductor, a Hero Electronix company, which secured $75 million from US-based Vector Line Capital.

Homegrown sports brand Boldfit raised over Rs 400 crore in a Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund, while AI agent startup RapidCanvas secured $29 million from Vertex Ventures. Bengaluru-based Scimplify raised $25 million in a strategic round led by Hitachi Ventures.

Construction robotics startup Origin raised $20 million in a round co-led by Accel and Zacua Ventures. Meanwhile, D2C personal care brand Nat Habit is raising Rs 142.6 crore ($15 million) in a fresh round led by Trident Growth Partners.

Toothsi's parent MakeO raised Rs 90 crore from Singularity AMC, while B2B manufacturing startup CapGrid secured Rs 46.28 crore ($4.87 million) in a pre-Series B round led by Hero Enterprise Partner Ventures.

title: Leverage Edu’s revenue jumps over 2X to Rs 364 Cr in FY26; turns EBITDA profitable
description: Leverage Edu more than doubled its operating revenue in FY26. The Delhi-based company also turned EBITDA-positive during the year, while its net losses narrowed 82% year-on-year to Rs 19 crore.
body: Leverage Edu, which helps Indian students secure admissions to overseas universities, more than doubled its operating revenue in FY26 as it expanded its international presence. The Delhi-based company also turned EBITDA-positive during the year, while its net losses narrowed 82% year-on-year to Rs 19 crore.

The edtech startup’s operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 364.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 173.3 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded by Akshay Chaturvedi in 2017, Leverage Edu helps students navigate the overseas education process, from university selection and admissions to education financing. The platform caters to students across India and international markets, with access to universities in the UK, US, Canada, Germany, Japan and Dubai.

Student placement services remained Leverage Edu’s largest revenue stream in FY26, contributing 77% of operating revenue as the segment grew 2.3 times year-on-year to Rs 281.8 crore, supported by the company’s expansion into new markets.

Its Fly business, launched in late 2022 to provide financial services to students going abroad, also gained traction, with revenue doubling to Rs 59.6 crore. The segment earns commissions from education loans, foreign exchange and student accommodation services.
Leverage Edu further generated Rs 21.3 crore from product sales and Rs 9.1 crore from other operating and non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 371.9 crore in FY26.

International markets contributed over 81% of Leverage Edu’s total revenue in FY26, with revenue from these markets rose 2.3X year-on-year to Rs 297 crore. India accounted for the remaining 18.5%, with revenue from the domestic market growing 60% to Rs 67.4 crore.

Commission paid to agents and other partners emerged as Leverage Edu’s largest expense in FY26, which surged 2.2X year-on-year to Rs 114 crore. These costs accounted for nearly 29% of its total expenditure and reflect the role of external partners in its student placement business. Employee benefit expenses increased 14.1% to Rs 73 crore, while subscription and membership fees surged to Rs 67 crore from Rs 11.8 crore in FY25.

title: IndiQube to invest Rs 35 Cr in SaiEdge Realty for 49% stake
description: IndiQube Spaces has approved an investment of up to Rs 35 crore in SaiEdge Realty for a 49% stake on a fully diluted basis, according to a stock exchange filing.
body: IndiQube Spaces has approved an investment of up to Rs 35 crore in SaiEdge Realty for a 49% stake on a fully diluted basis, according to a stock exchange filing.
The investment will be made through a subscription to equity shares and/or convertible securities in one or more tranches.
Incorporated in 2026, SaiEdge Realty develops commercial office spaces. The company has not commenced operations and has no turnover to report. The remaining stake will be held by other investors.

In Q1 FY27, IndiQube’s revenue from operations rose 36.9% year on year to Rs 423 crore from Rs 309 crore. Its losses narrowed 35% to Rs 23.88 crore from Rs 36.75 crore in the same period last year. The company has not disclosed its Q2 FY27 results yet.
Separately, IndiQube’s board accepted the resignation of independent director Avalur Gopalaratnam Muralikrishnan, effective October 19, 2026, citing health reasons.

The board also appointed Ishwar Subramanian as an additional independent director for a five year term, subject to shareholder approval. Subramanian has over four decades of experience and previously served as CEO of Akzo Nobel Coatings India Asia and CFO of 3M India.
Following the appointment, IndiQube reconstituted its audit committee, with Subramanian as chairperson and Sachi Krishana and Rishi Das as members.

title: Zetwerk’s IPO subscribed over 3 times on final day
description: Zetwerk, a manufacturing platform, saw its IPO subscribed 3.06 times, with investors bidding for 56.54 crore shares against 18.50 crore shares on offer.
body: Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses, a manufacturing platform, saw its IPO subscribed 3.06 times, with investors bidding for 56.54 crore shares against 18.50 crore shares on offer.
Zetwerk's initial public offering (IPO) was open for subscription from October 15-October 19, with a price band of Rs 143-151and a minimum investment of Rs 14,157 for a lot size of 99 shares.

According to exchange data, the qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) portion received the highest demand, with 4.73X subscription, followed by the non-institutional investors (NIIs) category at 1.4X. The employee quota was subscribed 1.58X, while the retail portion saw weaker demand at 0.72X.
According to its RHP, the issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 14.45 crore shares worth Rs 2,182 crore by existing shareholders.
The company plans to use a portion of the fresh issue proceeds to repay debt, with the remaining funds earmarked for acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.

Zetwerk’s IPO will also offer an exit route to early investors, with Kae Capital and Kalysta Capital set to earn returns of up to 38X on their investments through the offer for sale (OFS). Lightspeed Venture Partners is the largest external shareholder selling shares worth Rs 426.9 crore, followed by Peak XV Partners, which is offloading shares worth Rs 353.5 crore.

Ahead of its IPO, Zetwerk raised Rs 2,251.23 crore from anchor investors, with participation from a mix of global investors such as Capital Group, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs and Nomura, alongside domestic investors including SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund.

On the financial front, Zetwerk’s revenue from continuing operations grew 40.4% to Rs 15,913 crore in FY26 from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. In Q1 FY27, revenue from operations rose 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations narrowed 93% to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago period.

title: Flipkart super.money’s revenue triples to Rs 292 Cr in FY26; losses up 78%
description: Flipkart-backed super.money more than tripled its operating revenue in FY26 as it expanded its UPI payments and credit marketplace business.
body: Flipkart-backed super.money more than tripled its operating revenue in FY26 as it expanded its UPI payments and credit marketplace business. However, the growth came at a cost, as the losses for the firm widened by 78% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Super.money's revenue from operations rose to Rs 292 crore in FY26 from Rs 89 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Super.money’s core business spans UPI payments and credit marketplace services. It facilitates digital payments and connects customers of merchant platforms with banks and NBFCs for loans, earning revenue through loan facilitation services.
The loan marketplace contributed Rs 248 crore, or nearly 85% of its operating revenue, while the remaining income came from other activities.

As a marketplace-led business, super.money’s key expense is customer acquisition and brand building. The firm spent Rs 341 crore on marketing in FY26, which accounted for around 61% of its total expenditure.

Employee benefit expenses also rose 75% to Rs 139 crore during the fiscal year. Other expenses, including marketplace, legal, telephone, postage and general overheads, pushed its total expenditure up 130% to Rs 557 crore in FY26 from Rs 242 crore in FY25.
The company’s marketing spend alone exceeded its entire operating revenue for the year. As a result, its net loss widened by 78% to Rs 264 crore in FY26 from Rs 148 crore in the previous fiscal year.

On a unit level, super.money spent Rs 1.91 to earn every rupee in FY26. Its EBITDA margin stood at -85.43% during the year. As of March 2026, the company had total current assets of Rs 136 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 63 crore.

title: Cleartrip’s losses widen to Rs 805 Cr in FY26; spends Rs 897 Cr on discount and cashbacks
description: Flipkart-owned Cleartrip’s losses widened 28% year-on-year to Rs 805 crore in FY26, as the travel platform continued to spend heavily on cashbacks and discounts, which rose 47.6% to Rs 897.5 crore in the fiscal year.
body: Flipkart-owned Cleartrip’s losses widened 28% year-on-year to Rs 805 crore in FY26, as the travel platform continued to spend heavily on cashbacks and discounts, which rose 47.6% to Rs 897.5 crore in the fiscal year.

Following 70% growth in FY25, Cleartrip’s net operating revenue growth slowed to 20.8% in FY26, reaching Rs 198.3 crore compared with Rs 164.1 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its annual filings with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2006, Cleartrip operates an online travel booking platform that allows users to book flights, hotels, buses and holiday packages. It earns revenue through service charges, commissions and incentives from travel partners, while offering cashbacks and discounts to attract customers.

The company’s revenue includes service charges, commissions and incentives, adjusted for cashbacks and discounts offered to customers. Service charges grew 37.5% to Rs 702.2 crore in FY26, while commission and incentives rose 52.3% to Rs 378.4 crore.

However, cashbacks and discounts increased 47.6% year-on-year to Rs 897.5 crore from Rs 608.2 crore in FY25. This continued to weigh on net revenue, which stood at Rs 198.3 crore after accounting for these customer incentives and other operating income.
