The firm also earned Rs 58 crore from other operating and non-operating sources, which took its overall income to Rs 241.2 crore during the last fiscal year.

Looking at Cleartrip’s major expenses in FY26. The Flipkart-owned company allocated the largest share of its costs to employee benefits, which rose 7.8% year-on-year to Rs 258 crore. This includes Rs 68 crore in ESOP expenses. Excluding ESOPs, its employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 190 crore.
Cleartrip’s finance costs surged 44.4% to Rs 203.4 crore, while commission and brokerage expenses increased 33.2% to Rs 171.5 crore.

title: Deconstruct revenue grows 25X in three years to Rs 165 Cr in FY26
description: D2C skincare brand Deconstruct grew its operating revenue 25-fold in three years to Rs 165 crore in FY26, with revenue growing 30% year-on-year.
body: D2C skincare brand Deconstruct grew its operating revenue 25-fold in three years to Rs 165 crore in FY26, with revenue growing 30% year-on-year. The firm continued to expand its business while keeping losses marginal, reporting a net loss of Rs 5.4 crore in the last fiscal year.

The Bengaluru-based startup’s revenue from operations grew 30% YoY to Rs 165 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 127 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Founded by Malini Adapureddy, Deconstruct offers products for different skin types, including sensitive ones. Its portfolio spans face, body, lip and hair care products for men and women.

Deconstruct’s growth has also been accompanied by higher spending on marketing and ops as it scales. Advertising and promotional expenses rose 72.5% to Rs 69 crore in FY26, accounting for 40% of its overall costs.

Its procurement costs increased 39.3% to Rs 39 crore during the fiscal year ended March 2026, in line with the expansion of its business. Transportation, freight, legal and other overheads also added to the burn.
Deconstruct’s total expenses grew 48.7% to Rs 174 crore in FY26 from Rs 117 crore in FY25, outpacing its revenue growth during the year.

As a result, the company reported a net loss of Rs 5.4 crore in FY26, compared to a net profit of Rs 10 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA margin stood at -5.61%, while return on capital employed (ROCE) was -13.81%. At the operating level, Deconstruct spent around Rs 1.05 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26.
Deconstruct has raised funding from investors including Kalaari Capital, DSG Consumer Partners, V3 Ventures and L’Oréal’s venture capital fund BOLD to support its growth and expansion.

title: Sauce leads Rs 10 Cr seed round in lab-grown diamond jewellery brand So/Facet
description: The company is also developing an omnichannel model that will integrate digital and physical touchpoints for jewellery discovery, purchases and upgrades. It has built a
body: So/Facet, a lab-grown diamond jewellery brand, has raised Rs 10 crore in a seed funding round led by Sauce. The round also saw participation from Mokobara co-founders Sangeet Agrawal and Navin Parwal, the Chona family office, Kedar Lele, and Devaiah Bopanna, co-founder of Moonshot.
The proceeds will be used for brand building, design, technology, hiring and an omnichannel rollout, So/Facet said in a press release.

Co-founded this year by former Unilever leaders Aarushi Agrawal Naulakha and Abhishek Naulakha, So/Facet offers in-house designs featuring IGI-certified lab-grown diamonds. The brand plans to launch online in November 2026, followed by premium retail stores.

Its six launch collections feature lab-grown diamonds in different cuts and contemporary designs. So/Me offers shapes such as stars and butterflies, while So/Pop combines diamonds with colourful, stackable enamel charms. So/Icon focuses on sculptural jewellery designs.

The company is also developing an omnichannel model that will integrate digital and physical touchpoints for jewellery discovery, purchases and upgrades. It has built a pre-launch waitlist of more than 200 potential customers, according to the company.

In the lab-grown diamond jewellery segment, Aukera raised Rs 90 crore in debt funding from Alteria Capital in July this year, following a $15 million equity round led by Peak XV Partners. Limelight Lab Grown Diamonds raised Rs 275 crore in July to strengthen its vertical integration, manufacturing and retail expansion.

Meanwhile, Onya secured Rs 5.5 crore in pre-seed funding led by Zeropearl VC last year. GIVA raised Rs 530 crore in June 2025, with plans to expand its lab-grown diamond jewellery offerings alongside its broader jewellery business.

title: Even Healthcare raises $50 Mn in Series B led by Khosla Ventures
description: Even Healthcare, an integrated managed care company, has raised $50 million in a Series B funding round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures, with participation from Alpha Wave.
body: Even Healthcare, an integrated managed care company, has raised $50 million in a Series B funding round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures, with participation from Alpha Wave. The round triples its valuation from the previous raise 18 months ago and takes its total funding to over $120 million.

In August 2026, Entrackr had exclusively reported that the company was set to raise Rs 208 crore, or $22 million, in a Series B round led by Khosla Ventures, with participation from DLB Ventures, Simon Fiduciaria and others. In January 2026, Even Healthcare raised $20 million in a round led by Lachy Groom and Alpha Wave.
The latest fundraise comes after the company laid off around 350 employees in August 2026, as reported exclusively by Entrackr .
The proceeds from the latest round will be used to launch five new hospitals across Bengaluru over the next six months, the company said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2021 by Mayank Banerjee, Matilde Giglio and Alessandro Ialongo, Even Healthcare operates a membership-based healthcare model that offers primary care, diagnostics and hospital services. Unlike traditional hospital chains, the company focuses on continuity of care and patient recovery, with care teams managing patients across consultations, diagnostics, hospitalisation and post-discharge recovery.

Even Healthcare is yet to file its FY26 financials with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). In FY25, the company's revenue surged over fourfold to Rs 25.43 crore from Rs 6.24 crore in FY24. Its losses increased 24.5% to Rs 90.15 crore from Rs 72.40 crore during the same period.
The company said it serves more than 2.5 lakh members across 10 cities.

India's healthcare startup ecosystem has seen investor interest in membership-based and integrated care models that combine primary healthcare, diagnostics and hospitalisation under a single subscription.

title: Exclusive: Hunar AI valuation jumps 71% in Series A round
description: Hunar.AI, an AI-powered frontline workforce platform, has raised Rs 39.3 crore in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures with the participation from Seedstars
body: Update : Hunar.AI, an AI-powered frontline workforce platform, has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from Hyderabad Angels Fund, Together Fund, Seedstars, AVNM Ventures, PhysicsWallah co-founders Prateek Maheshwari and Alakh Pandey, and MediaMint co-founder Aditya Vuchi.
The latest round brings the company’s total funding raised to Rs 65 crore

The funding will support Hunar’s investment in AI infrastructure, product development and go-to-market expansion, Hunar.AI said in a press release. The company is focused on developing specialised AI technology for frontline-intensive industries, where high-volume hiring, geographically distributed teams and language diversity create operational challenges that conventional HR systems can struggle to address.
Original story follows:

Hunar.AI, an AI-powered frontline workforce platform, has raised Rs 39.3 crore in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures with the participation from Seedstars, Hyderabad Angels Fund, AVNM Ventures, Physics Wallah’s co-founders Alakh Pandey and Prateek Maheshwari. According to the company filing, the company had raised around Rs 18 crore in pre - series A round led by existing investor Together Fund. The board at Hunar AI passed a special resolution to issue 5,206 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 75,492 per share to raise Rs 39.30 crore in fresh capital, according to its regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr .

Blume Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 29 crore, followed by Seedstars with Rs 3.31 crore and Hyderabad Angels Fund with Rs 3 crore. AVNM Ventures invested Rs 2 crore, while Prateek Maheshwari and Alakh Pandey invested Rs 1 crore each. As per Entrackr’s estimates, Hunar AI’s valuation rose over 71% to Rs 180 crore or approximately $19 million in the new round, compared with Rs 105 crore in the pre-Series A.

The proceeds will be utilised for working capital needs, capital expenditure, operations, and business expansion, said the filings. Founded in 2022 by Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya, Hunar.AI provides AI-powered voice agents to automate frontline workforce operations, including hiring, onboarding, training and employee engagement. The startup uses multilingual voice AI to help businesses streamline recruitment and workforce management.

Following the latest allotment, Together Fund remains Hunar.AI’s largest external institutional shareholder with a 19.62% stake, followed by Blume Ventures at 16.17%. Co-founders Krishna Khandelwal and Shantanu Bhattacharyya hold 21.05% stake each in the company.

title: Exclusive: MakeMyTrip in talks to acquire Quick Ride through redBus
description: Quick Ride connects commuters travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling. It also caters to corporate employees and offers daily office commute solutions.
body: MakeMyTrip is in talks to acquire car and bike pooling platform Quick Ride, sources familiar with the matter told Entrackr.

“The deal is currently at the due diligence stage, with both sides examining the business and working through the details of the proposed transaction,” one of the sources said on condition of anonymity.
According to sources, the acquisition is being explored through redBus, with the transaction expected to involve a mix of cash and equity.

The potential acquisition could help MakeMyTrip expand its presence in urban mobility and strengthen its corporate commute offerings. redBus already operates rPool, a carpooling platform that connects verified working professionals travelling along similar routes and allows them to offer or find rides for daily commutes.
“Acquiring Quick Ride would help MakeMyTrip expand its presence in the carpooling segment and strengthen its commuter network,” said another source who also wished not to be named.
The timeline for the deal’s completion could not be ascertained, and the terms of the transaction may change as discussions progress.

Founded in 2015 by KNM Rao, Bengaluru based Quick Ride connects commuters travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling. The platform also caters to corporate employees and offers daily office commute solutions.

Quick Ride has raised funding from Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV), Naspers, now part of Prosus, and Venture Highway. In 2019, the company raised Rs 100.78 crore ($14.4 million) in its Series B round from these existing investors, according to an earlier report by Inc42. It had also raised an undisclosed amount in its Series A round from the same investors.

title: The Pant Project raises Rs 109 Cr in Series B led by Mirae Asset
description: The Pant Project has raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments (India), with participation from existing and other investors.
body: Premium menswear brand The Pant Project has raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B funding round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments (India), with participation from existing investor Sorin Investments and new investors Hyperscale Ventures, B&K Securities, MGA Ventures and B2V Ventures, as per the company’s press release.
The company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its offline retail network, enter new product categories and strengthen its omnichannel presence.

Founded by brothers Dhruv and Udit Toshniwal, The Pant Project started as a digital-first brand focused on bottomwear for Indian men. Its product portfolio includes Malai Pants and Inklock No Fade Black Jeans.

The company currently operates 25 exclusive brand stores across India and plans to increase the count to over 150 in the next two to three years. It also plans to expand into adjacent menswear categories, including jeans, athleisure and casualwear.

Commenting on the fundraise, Dhruv Toshniwal, founder and CEO of The Pant Project, said the company is now looking to expand its offline presence after building its business as a digital-first brand. He said its stores allow customers to experience the fabric and fit of its products in person, helping the company build stronger relationships with customers.
The latest fundraising follows its $4.25 million Series A round in 2024, led by Sorin Investments. The company had bootstrapped its business before raising institutional capital.

Alongside the equity round, The Pant Project has also secured venture debt financing from Alteria Capital, although the amount was not disclosed. IndigoEdge acted as the investment banker for the Series B transaction.
The fresh capital will help the company scale its retail network and broaden its product portfolio as it looks to build a larger presence in India’s premium menswear market.

title: Innovist revenue surges 2.8X to Rs 686 Cr in FY26; profit grows 87%
description: Innovist reported revenue from operations of Rs 685.7 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 246.7 crore in FY25, its financial statements sourced from the RoC show.
body: Beauty and personal care company Innovist nearly tripled its operating revenue in FY26, while its net profit rose 87% in the same period, as the business grew its sales. However, higher spending on advertising, promotions, and sales commissions added to its overall costs.
Innovist, operated by Onesto Labs, reported revenue from operations of Rs 685.7 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 246.7 crore in FY25, its consolidated financial statements sourced from the RoC show.

The company operates in the cosmetics and beauty products segment, with manufacturing facilities in India. It sells primarily through online marketplaces, its own website, and third-party offline stores.

Revenue from product sales was the primary source of operating revenue during FY26, which stood at Rs 676.3 crore against Rs 239.1 crore in FY25. Other operating revenue, which includes shipping and scrap sales, increased to Rs 9.4 crore during the last fiscal year.

The expansion also came with higher spending on customer acquisition and sales. Advertising and promotional expenses accounted for 40% of its overall cost, which rose more than 3X to Rs 262 crore in FY26 from Rs 84.2 crore in FY25. It also spent Rs 92 crore on commissions to sole selling agents, up from Rs 15 crore a year earlier.
Cost of materials consumed increased to Rs 162 crore from Rs 79 crore, while employee benefit expenses more than doubled to Rs 39 crore from Rs 19 crore.

Overall, Innovist’s total expenses increased to Rs 662 crore in FY26 from Rs 250 crore in FY25. Despite this increase, the company reported a profit before tax of Rs 30.5 crore, compared with a loss before tax of Rs 55 lakh in FY25.

The company’s tax expense rose to Rs 8.9 crore in FY26, including deferred tax expense of Rs 7.8 crore. Its net profit consequently reached Rs 21.5 crore during the year. Its total current assets stood at Rs 303 crore in FY26, including cash and bank balances of Rs 81 crore.

title: Gameberry posts Rs 129 Cr profit on Rs 711 Cr revenue in FY26
description: Gameberry Labs, the maker of Ludo Star and Parchisi Star, grew its operating revenue 20% to over Rs 700 crore in FY26, while net profit rose over 17%.
body: Following 28% revenue growth in FY25, Gameberry Labs, the company behind popular mobile board games Ludo Star and Parchisi Star, continued its growth momentum in FY26, with operating revenue growing 20% to cross Rs 700 crore. Its net profit also grew over 17% during the fiscal year.

Gameberry Labs’ operating revenue grew 20.3% year-on-year to Rs 711 crore in FY26 from Rs 591 crore in FY25, as per its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2017, Gameberry Labs operates mobile board games including Ludo Star, Ludo Titan, Parchisi Star and Backgammon Friends. The company has focused on free-to-play games monetised through in-app purchases and advertising.

The company primarily earns from in-app purchases, which contributed Rs 603 crore, or nearly 85% of its operating revenue, during the fiscal year. The segment grew 20.8% from Rs 499 crore in FY25. Advertising revenue rose 17.4% to Rs 108 crore from Rs 92 crore in the previous fiscal year.
Notably, over 99% of the company’s revenue came from overseas markets, which contributed Rs 706 crore, while India accounted for only a fraction of its total revenue.

Including Rs 39 crore in other income from interest on bank deposits and net gains on the fair value of investments, Gameberry Labs’ total income rose to Rs 750 crore in FY26 from Rs 622.3 crore in FY25.
On the expense front, the company’s total expenditure rose 23.2% to Rs 578 crore in FY26 from Rs 469 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Employee benefit expenses remained Gameberry Labs’ largest expense head, which grew over 31% year-on-year to Rs 177.66 crore in FY26 from Rs 135.5 crore in FY25. This cost included Rs 7.86 crore of ESOP expenses.

title: Kissht gets BSE, NSE nod for Rs 832 Cr fundraise
description: Kissht  has received in-principle approvals from the BSE and NSE for its proposed Rs 832.2 crore fundraise through a preferential issue of shares.
body: Kissht, operated by OnEMI Technology Solutions, has received in-principle approvals from the BSE and NSE for its proposed Rs 832.2 crore fundraise through a preferential issue of shares.

In a regulatory filing on October 20, the company said the exchanges had approved the issuance of up to 2.65 crore equity shares at Rs 314.11 per share. The proposed issue includes a premium of Rs 313.11 per share.
The approvals come after the company's board cleared the fundraise on September 17, followed by shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting on October 14.

The proposed issue will see participation from 34 investors, including Axis Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), WhiteOak, 360 ONE, Groww Mutual Fund and Bandhan Mutual Fund, among others.

As per the company's earlier announcement, 75% of the proceeds will be infused into Si Creva Capital Services, its wholly owned subsidiary, to support lending operations. The remaining 25% will be used for general corporate purposes.

The company is also targeting multiple credit rating upgrades over the next two years. It expects stronger capitalisation and improved access to funding to help lower borrowing costs and increase its lending capacity.

The fundraise comes around five months after OnEMI raised Rs 926 crore through its initial public offering (IPO), comprising a fresh issue of Rs 850 crore and an offer for sale of about Rs 76 crore by existing shareholders.

On the financial front, Kissht reported a 45% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 670 crore in Q1 FY27, while profit rose 58% to Rs 95 crore. Its assets under management grew 61% to Rs 8,001 crore during the quarter.

title: Myntra spends Rs 2,326 Cr on advertising for Rs 5,242 Cr revenue in FY26
description: Myntra’s operating revenue declined in FY26, hit by a 53% drop in logistics collections. The Flipkart-owned platform also swung to a net loss of Rs 579 crore, largely due to restructuring costs linked to its reverse flip to India.
body: Myntra, the fashion e-commerce platform owned by Flipkart, reported a decline in operating revenue in FY26, mainly due to a 53% drop in collections from logistics services. The company also swung to a net loss of Rs 579 crore from a profit in the previous fiscal year, largely steered by restructuring costs linked to its reverse flip from Singapore to India.

Myntra’s revenue from operations fell 13.5% year-on-year to Rs 5,242.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 6,063.8 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Myntra earns revenue from marketplace, logistics, advertising and other services. Marketplace services remained its largest revenue stream and contributed 50.7% of operating revenue. Revenue from this segment rose 3% to Rs 2,657.3 crore in FY26. The segment earns fees and commissions from sellers who use Myntra’s online marketplace.

Revenue from logistics services, which includes fees for delivery and related services, declined 53.2% to Rs 1,119.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,390.5 crore in FY25. The sharp decline in this segment was the primary reason behind the fall in overall operating revenue.

Advertising services revenue grew 35.2% to Rs 1,236.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 914.5 crore a year ago and contributed 23.6% to operating revenue. The segment earns fees from brands and sellers for ads on Myntra’s platform.

Revenue from other operating services stood at Rs 229.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 178.6 crore in FY25. This category includes collection from marketing services, liabilities written back during the year and incentives from vendors.
The firm made Rs 73.3 crore from non-operating revenue, primarily from royalty income, which pushed its total revenue to Rs 5,315.8 crore in FY26.

For the e-commerce platform, advertising remained Myntra’s largest cost component at Rs 2,326.5 crore, which rose 10.5% and accounted for 41% of overall cost in FY26. Logistics charges, which cover costs related to order delivery and fulfilment, declined 16.6% to Rs 1,666.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,999.2 crore in FY25.

title: Blacksmith raises $66 Mn at $1 Bn valuation led by Sequoia
description: AI code testing platform Blacksmith has raised $66 million in a Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital at a valuation of $1 billion. News
body: AI code testing platform Blacksmith has raised $66 million in a Series C funding round led by Sequoia Capital at a valuation of $1 billion. The round also saw participation from Premji Invest and existing investors Peak XV Partners, Google Ventures (GV) and Y Combinator.

The latest round takes Blacksmith’s total funding to $125 million. The company had raised $45 million in a Series B round led by Peak XV Partners at a valuation of $550 million, with participation from GV and Y Combinator.

Founded in 2024 by Aditya Jayaprakash, Aayush Shah and Aditya Maru, Blacksmith provides infrastructure for building and testing code. Its platform runs continuous integration (CI) workflows that allow developers to build and test software before code is merged.

The company said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) has grown 17 times since January 2026. The number of CI jobs running on its platform each week has increased from 5 million to more than 90 million during the same period.
Blacksmith said its platform runs CI jobs twice as fast and at 60% lower cost on average. More than 10,000 companies, including Ashby, Granola, Handshake and LangChain, use its platform.
The company manages nearly 10 megawatts of computing capacity across data centres in the US and Europe. It plans to expand its computing capacity at least fivefold in 2027.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its team and computing infrastructure, Blacksmith said.
The company operates in the software development infrastructure segment, where demand for code testing and validation tools is growing alongside the adoption of AI coding agents.

title: Mygate, Adonmo set to merge; Eternal to hold 4.4% stake in combined entity
description: Eternal, formerly Zomato, will acquire an approximately 4.4% stake in Mygate on a fully diluted basis through a share swap involving its entire holding in Adonmo.
body: Eternal, formerly Zomato, will acquire an approximately 4.4% stake in Mygate on a fully diluted basis through a share swap involving its entire holding in Adonmo, according to a regulatory filing dated October 21.
The stake in the merged Mygate entity is currently valued at Rs 156 crore. Eternal had invested Rs 112 crore in Adonmo in January 2022.

Under the transaction, Eternal will transfer 11,214 Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares and 10 equity shares held in Adonmo to Mygate. In exchange, it will receive 1,84,091 Series C1 compulsorily convertible preference shares and 164 equity shares in Mygate.

The transaction forms part of the proposed merger between Mygate and Adonmo. Once completed, other Adonmo shareholders will also become shareholders of the merged Mygate entity, while Adonmo will cease to exist as a separate entity.
Founded in 2016, Adonmo operates an ambient digital advertising platform with a cloud-connected network of screens across residential communities.
Mygate provides technology solutions for gated residential communities, with services that include visitor management, security, accounting and community engagement for residents.
Mygate reported a 34% year-on-year increase in turnover to Rs 229 crore in FY26. The company had reported a turnover of Rs 171 crore in FY25 and Rs 96 crore in FY24, according to the filing
The proposed transaction remains subject to the execution of definitive agreements and the fulfilment of customary closing conditions.

title: Vectorial raises $3 Mn led by SenseAI Ventures
description: Vectorial, an AI startup building human behaviour simulation tools for product development, has raised $3 million in a funding round led by SenseAI Ventures. Snippets
body: Vectorial, an AI startup building human behaviour simulation tools for product development, has raised $3 million in a funding round led by SenseAI Ventures.

Other participants include Smilegate, Berkeley SkyDeck, Berkeley AI Research Lab, Dent Capital, Motus Ventures, SUM Ventures and angel investors, including product leaders from Meta, Shopify and Mastercard.
Founded by Taranveer Singh, Rahul Garg and Jasmine Kaur, Vectorial helps companies predict how users may respond to software products, digital experiences and marketing campaigns.
Its platform uses AI simulations to test product ideas without relying solely on traditional surveys and interviews.
The company claims that it has modelled more than 2.5 million people globally, including 500,000 in India, and conducted over 30,000 simulations.
Its customers include boAt, GoodRx, Suki AI, Everkind and Concrete Software, across sectors such as healthcare, gaming and e-commerce.
Vectorial’s SAPIENS model uses socio-demographic, psychographic and behavioural data to simulate target audiences across web, mobile and AI-based applications.

The company claims its model is 30% more accurate at predicting human behaviour than general-purpose large language models. Its simulations reproduce findings from previous user studies with over 85% accuracy.

title: Eternal reports Rs 24,138 Cr revenue and Rs 125 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
description: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Eternal (formerly Zomato) reported its Q2 FY27 results on Wednesday, with profit up nearly 93% year-on-year to Rs 125 crore.
body: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Eternal (formerly Zomato) reported its Q2 FY27 results on Wednesday, with profit up nearly 93% year-on-year to Rs 125 crore. The Gurugram-based company also saw Blinkit’s revenue almost double during the quarter

Eternal’s revenue from operations surged over 77% year-on-year to Rs 24,138 crore in Q2 FY27 in contrast to Rs 13,590 crore in Q2 FY26, as per the firm’s consolidated financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Eternal operates several business units, including a food marketplace, Hyperpure, and a quick commerce platform, BlinkIt.

Blinkit, Eternal’s largest revenue contributor, reported a 93% year-on-year rise in revenue to Rs 19,152 crore in Q2 FY27. Zomato’s food delivery business grew 37% to Rs 3,396 crore and accounted for 14% of the company’s total revenue during the quarter.

Meanwhile, Hyperpure, Eternal’s B2B supplies business, reported a 13% year-on-year rise in revenue to Rs 1,154 crore, while its going-out platform District grew 61% to Rs 304 crore in Q2 FY27. Including other segments and non-operating income, Eternal’s total income rose to Rs 24,489 crore during the quarter.

On a quarter-on-quarter basis, operating revenue increased over 19% from Rs 20,211 crore in Q2 FY27. For the half year ended September 2026, Eternal’s revenue stood at Rs 44,349 crore with a Rs 217 crore net profit.

Material costs remained Eternal’s largest expense head at Rs 14,602 crore in Q2 FY27, accounting for over 60% of its total expenditure. Delivery and related costs rose 62% year-on-year to Rs 3,581 crore, while employee benefit expenses grew 32.5% to Rs 1,146 crore. Advertising expenses also climbed 41% to Rs 1,138 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenditure increased to Rs 24,166 crore in Q2 FY27.

At the segment level, Eternal’s food delivery business posted a positive EBITDA of Rs 647 crore in Q2 FY27. Blinkit’s EBITDA surged nearly 98 times to Rs 488 crore, while District reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 55 crore during the quarter.

title: Forward deployed AI startup AuxoAI raises $20.7 Mn in Series A round led by NTTVC
description: Founded in 2023 by Amaresh Tripathy, Arvinder Pal Singh and Kabir Singh, AuxoAI works with large global enterprises to identify AI use cases, redesign workflows and build
body: Forward deployed AI company AuxoAI has raised $20.7 million in a Series A funding round led by NTTVC, a Silicon Valley based venture capital firm backed by Japanese technology conglomerate NTT. The round also saw participation from George Still Jr., Amit Zavery and Giacomo Sonnino.
Earlier this year, AuxoAI was named one of the select AI Pureplay Partners at Google Next as part of Google’s $750 million investment in enterprise AI deployment.

The company will use the fresh funds to expand its global forward deployed teams, invest in proprietary technology and AI native delivery capabilities, and scale its presence and strategic ecosystem, AuxoAI said in a press release.

Founded in 2023 by Amaresh Tripathy, Arvinder Pal Singh and Kabir Singh, AuxoAI works with large global enterprises to identify AI use cases, redesign workflows and build production ready systems aimed at delivering measurable business outcomes.

The company deploys teams of AI strategists and engineers who work alongside clients to understand their business operations, identify opportunities for AI adoption and develop systems for use in production environments.

AuxoAI also offers Damia, its proprietary forward deployed engineering (FDE) workbench, which it says incorporates learnings from multiple enterprise AI deployments to accelerate implementation. The company is a Google Gemini Enterprise transformation partner and an AWS Advanced Tier partner.
AuxoAI works with enterprise customers, including UKG and Fogo de Chão.

title: Apple India’s revenue crosses Rs 1 lakh Cr in FY26; profit jumps 66% to Rs 5,311 Cr
description: Apple India crossed Rs 1 lakh crore in revenue for the first time in FY26, driven by rising demand for its premium devices. Net profit jumped 66% YoY to Rs 5,311 crore.
body: Apple’s growing popularity in India, fuelled by rising demand for iPhones and other premium devices, helped the company cross the Rs 1 lakh crore revenue mark for the first time in FY26. Its net profit also surged 66% year-on-year to Rs 5,311 crore during the fiscal year.
Apple India’s revenue from operations grew 31.4% year-on-year to Rs 1,03,853 crore from Rs 79,061 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Apple India primarily generates revenue through the sale of premium consumer electronics, including iPhones, MacBooks, iPads, Apple Watches, AirPods and accessories. The company sells these products through its online and offline retail channels, alongside authorised resellers.

Product sales remained the key growth driver, with revenue from this segment rising 32.7% to Rs 99,068 crore in FY26 from Rs 74,681 crore in FY25. The segment accounted for 95.4% of total operating revenue.

Apple India also earns revenue from technical support services and maintenance contracts, including offerings such as AppleCare, which provides eligible customers with technical assistance, hardware repairs and extended service coverage.
Revenue from technical and other support services stood at Rs 4,293 crore. Income from maintenance contracts increased 26.5% to Rs 492 crore.
The iPhone maker also earned Rs 754 crore in non-operating income, primarily from interest and other sources, which lifted its total income to Rs 1,04,606 crore in FY26.

On the expense side, cost of materials remained the largest component, which rose 21.6% to Rs 78,229 crore from Rs 64,336 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for 81.3% of the total and primarily reflects the cost associated with the products sold by the company.

title: Stargazer Fund leads $1 Mn pre-seed round in travel platform Onto
description: Onto monitors hotel prices after a booking is made. If the same hotel room for the same dates becomes available at a lower price, the platform refunds the difference to t
body: Customer-first travel platform Onto has launched its services and raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Stargazer Fund, with participation from Singapore-based White Venture Capital.
The proceeds will be used to scale operations, strengthen its technology infrastructure and develop new products, Onto said in a press release.
Founded in June 2026 by Jagdeep Singh and Shubham Goyal, Onto helps travellers discover and book hotels while tracking price drops on eligible bookings, including those made through other platforms.

The Bengaluru-based startup’s first offering, Price Drop Refund, automatically refunds travellers the difference if the price of an eligible hotel booking falls after the reservation is made. The feature covers bookings made through Onto as well as eligible bookings on other platforms.

Onto monitors hotel prices after a booking is made. If the same hotel room for the same dates becomes available at a lower price, the platform refunds the difference to the original payment method. Travellers receive updates on price changes and refunds through WhatsApp and app notifications.

The company has integrations with multiple hotel suppliers, allowing it to offer bookings across domestic and international destinations. It plans to expand beyond hotel bookings to simplify other parts of the travel journey.
Onto is also developing AI-based features to understand travellers’ preferences and past travel behaviour, recommend relevant options and explain why those recommendations may suit their needs.

title: Wellbeing Nutrition’s revenue doubles to Rs 244 Cr in FY26
description: Clean-label nutraceutical brand Wellbeing Nutrition more than doubled its revenue to Rs 244 crore in FY26, while its losses widened 2.4X to Rs 92 crore.
body: Clean-label nutraceutical brand Wellbeing Nutrition more than doubled its revenue in FY26, while its losses widened 2.4X to Rs 92 crore. The financial performance comes just after pharmaceutical major USV acquired a 79% stake in the company.
According to financial statements reviewed by Entrackr , Wellbeing Nutrition’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 244 crore in FY26 from Rs 118 crore in FY25.

Founded in 2019, Wellbeing Nutrition operates in the nutraceutical segment, offering products across vitamins, minerals, protein, collagen, omega supplements and other wellness categories. The company sells through its own website, online marketplaces and offline retail channels, and has a presence in markets such as the US, UK and UAE.

Product sales were the company’s sole source of operating revenue during the year. Its portfolio includes collagen supplements, oral strips, marine collagen, slow-release capsules and effervescent tablets.

On the cost side, advertising and promotional expenses surged 78.7% to Rs 109 crore in FY26 from Rs 61 crore in FY25, accounting for around 32% of the company’s total expenditure. Meanwhile, the cost of materials consumed more than doubled to Rs 106 crore during the year.
Other expenses, including freight, commissions, legal fees and overheads, pushed the company’s total expenditure to Rs 338 crore in FY26, up 115.3% from Rs 157 crore in FY25.

As a result, Wellbeing Nutrition’s losses widened to Rs 92 crore in FY26 from Rs 38 crore in the previous fiscal year. The losses included an ESOP cost of around Rs 51 crore; excluding this, the loss would have stood at around Rs 40 crore. At the same time, their operating EBITDA loss, excluding ESOP, was 13.4% of revenue in FY26, down from 22.5% in FY25.
At the unit level, the company spent Rs 1.39 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26.

title: Jio Platforms opens Rs 30,213 Cr IPO for subscription
description: Jio Platforms, the digital services arm of Reliance Industries, has opened its Rs 30,213 crore initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on Wednesday.
body: Jio Platforms, the digital services arm of Reliance Industries, has opened its Rs 30,213 crore initial public offering (IPO) for subscription on Wednesday. The issue will close on October 23.
The company has fixed the price band at Rs 1,065-1,119 per share. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of 27 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component.
The issue includes a reservation of shares worth up to Rs 500 crore for eligible employees and Rs 2,500 crore for eligible shareholders of Reliance Industries.

Ahead of the public issue, Jio Platforms raised Rs 8,110crore from 212 anchor investors on October 19. The anchor book attracted bids worth nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore, more than 30 times the amount allocated to these investors.

During the anchor investments, participants included global investors such as BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity Investments and T. Rowe Price, along with domestic mutual funds and insurers took part.

Jio Platforms plans to use Rs 27,500 crore from the IPO proceeds to repay part of the borrowings of its subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

Jio Platforms houses Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital businesses, including Reliance Jio Infocomm, which offers mobile connectivity, fixed broadband and digital services. The company has been expanding its presence in 5G, digital applications and artificial intelligence.
Reliance Jio Infocomm had 533.3 million subscribers at the end of June 2026, making it one of the country's largest telecom operators.

title: BlueStone posts Rs 745 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27, narrows losses by 92%
description: Jewellery retailer BlueStone reported a 45% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in the second quarter of financial year ending March 2027.
body: Jewellery retailer BlueStone reported a 45% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in the second quarter of financial year ending March 2027. At the same time, the company narrowed losses by 92% to Rs 4.37 crore during the quarter. Bluestone’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 745 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 514 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.

For the first half of FY27, Bluestone’s revenue from operations increased 47.3% to Rs 1,482 crore from Rs 1,006 crore in the corresponding period last year. Income from the sale of jewellery remained the company’s primary source of revenue. The company also recorded Rs 24 crore in income apart from revenue from operations, taking its total income to Rs 769 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 525 crore in Q2 FY26. In Q1 FY27, total income stood at Rs 752 crore.

On the expenditure front, the cost of materials remained the largest cost centre at Rs 470 crore, up 51.4% year-on-year. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 70.58 crore, while finance costs and depreciation expenses stood at Rs 58.37 crore and Rs 63.87 crore, respectively.
Overall, Bluestone’s total expenditure increased 34% to Rs 772 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 576 crore in Q2 FY26. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, expenditure rose from Rs 745 crore in Q1 FY27.
At the bottom line, BlueStone narrowed its net loss by 91.6% to Rs 4.37 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 52 crore in Q2 FY26. The company had posted a profit of around Rs 6 crore in Q1 FY27.

The Bengaluru-based company reported a net profit of Rs 1.59 crore in H1 FY27, compared to a net loss of Rs 86.85 crore in H1 FY26. In September 2026, BlueStone appointed CarDekho Group CEO and co-founder Amit Jain as a Non-Executive Independent Director.
At the end of the trading session, BlueStone shares closed at Rs 760.45 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 11,305 crore.

title: Binny Bansal-backed ShopOS launches AI creative platform Sloosh
description: ShopOS, a Bengaluru-based AI startup backed by Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal’s 3STATE Ventures, has launched Sloosh.ai, an AI creative platform. Snippets
body: ShopOS, a Bengaluru-based AI startup backed by Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal’s 3STATE Ventures, has launched Sloosh.ai, an AI creative platform that generates product images, visual scenes, reels and creator-style videos from ideas, photos and videos.

The launch comes after ShopOS raised $20 million from 3STATE Ventures. The startup provides AI-powered creative production for fashion, retail and direct-to-consumer brands across India, the UAE and the US.

Sloosh uses the same image and video orchestration engine that ShopOS deploys for brand clients. The platform combines AI agents, reusable workflows and human expertise to help creators, agencies, founders and small businesses produce content across formats.

The platform offers four ways to create content: an AI chat interface, ready-made workflows called Spaces, a visual workflow builder called Spacelab, and assistance from ShopOS’s in-house creative team. Its batch mode can generate hundreds of images and videos through reusable workflows.

Sloosh also connects with AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Cursor through its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration. The company is also launching a plugin for Adobe After Effects.

Founded by Sai Krishna V K and Ajay P V, ShopOS was built by the team behind Scapic, an AI and augmented reality commerce platform acquired by Flipkart in 2020. The founders later set up and led Flipkart Labs.
Sloosh is available globally, with new accounts receiving 20 free credits and paid plans starting at $19 per month.

title: Swiggy’s Q2 FY27 revenue rises 36% to Rs 7,571 Cr, losses narrow 16%
description: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Swiggy reported a 36.1% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 7,571 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 5,561 crore in Q2 FY26
body: Foodtech and quick commerce platform Swiggy reported a 36.1% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 7,571 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 5,561 crore in Q2 FY26, while its losses narrowed 15.6% to Rs 922 crore from Rs 1,092 crore in the year-ago quarter.
For the first half of FY27, Swiggy’s operating revenue grew 36.7% year-on-year to Rs 14,383 crore from Rs 10,522 crore in H1 FY26.

Scootsy Logistics, Swiggy’s supply chain and distribution business remained its largest revenue contributor, accounting for nearly 49% of its operating revenue. Revenue from the segment rose 44.1% year-on-year to Rs 3,690 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,560 crore in the year-ago quarter.

The company’s food delivery and quick commerce businesses also posted growth during the quarter. Revenue from food delivery increased 21.6% year-on-year to Rs 2,338 crore from Rs 1,923 crore, while quick commerce revenue rose 33.3% to Rs 1,306 crore from Rs 980 crore.
The remaining operating revenue came from segments such as dine-out services and other Platforms Innovations, including Bolt and Toing.

The Bengaluru-based company also reported Rs 212 crore in other income, compared to Rs 59 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. As a result, its total income rose to Rs 7,783 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 5,620 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the expense front, Swiggy’s cost of materials surged 47% year-on-year to Rs 3,443 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,342 crore in Q2 FY26. Delivery and related charges increased 32.9% to Rs 1,895 crore, while advertising and sales promotion expenses rose 24.9% to Rs 1,298 crore. Employee benefit expenses declined 2% to Rs 676 crore. Other expenses took the company’s total expenditure to Rs 8,703 crore in Q2 FY27, up 29.7% year-on-year.

Swiggy’s net losses decreased 15.6% year-on-year to Rs 922 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,092 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company also narrowed its losses by 25.2% to Rs 1,713 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 2,289 crore in the first half of the previous fiscal year.

title: Chapter Home raises Rs 63 Cr from Bessemer, Stride Ventures, others
description: Chapter Home, a home and kitchen consumer brand company, has raised Rs 63 crore through a mix of equity and debt from Bessemer Venture Partners. News
body: Chapter Home, a home and kitchen consumer brand company, has raised Rs 63 crore through a mix of equity and debt from Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, influencer Tanmay Bhat and a group of family offices.
The funding round values the company at close to Rs 1,000 crore.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen product development, enter new categories, invest in technology and brand building, and expand distribution. The company is also working on setting up its first physical retail touchpoints.

Founded in 2025 by Nitin Chugh, Akarsh Bharadwaj, Shrey Mittal, Dhiraj Jain and Dheeraj Goyal, the company is building consumer brands across categories such as bed and table linen, cookware, home décor and small kitchen appliances.
The founders were part of the founding and leadership team at PharmEasy before starting Chapter Home.

The company uses a shared platform for sourcing, supply chain, content, technology and distribution across its brands. It also uses AI for product cataloguing, content creation, demand forecasting, product assortment, customer targeting and retention.

Chapter Home has launched home furnishings as its first category through HOKIPO, an online home furnishing brand. It plans to expand into other home and kitchen categories and sell through online marketplaces, quick commerce platforms, its direct-to-consumer channel and offline retail stores.

title: Voice AI platform Karta AI raises $3 Mn in seed round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill
description: Karta AI, a voice AI platform for inbound customer operations across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), has raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital.
body: Karta AI, a voice AI platform for inbound customer operations across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), has raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital. Wyser VC, CDM Capital and Seedstars also participated in the round.

The proceeds will be used to strengthen the platform's end-to-end automation and multilingual capabilities, expand deployments with financial institutions, and scale its engineering and go-to-market teams, Karta AI said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Vijaypal Singh and Abhishek Kushwaha, Karta AI develops voice AI agents that handle inbound customer calls for banks, lenders, fintech companies and insurers. The platform integrates with enterprise systems to address customer queries and execute workflows without human intervention, unless escalation is required.

Unlike conventional voice bots that typically handle specific queries, Karta AI's platform is designed to manage multiple customer intents within a single conversation. Its predictive context engine uses past interactions, handled by both human agents and AI, to improve query resolution and decision-making.

The Bengaluru-based startup said it is live with financial institutions and handles around 2 million customer conversations a month across more than 25 languages. Its inbound servicing agent resolves around 70% of borrower queries end to end, up from 0%, across use cases such as disbursal status, account statements, foreclosure statements and property document release, the company claimed.
Over the longer term, Karta AI plans to develop reusable, industry-specific capabilities and expand into international markets.
India's agentic voice AI segment has seen growing investor interest as startups develop systems to automate customer interactions across banking, lending, fintech and insurance.

Recent fundraises in the segment include Desible.ai's Rs 32 crore seed plus round led by Prime Venture Partners, Navana.ai's Rs 40 crore Series A round led by Ronnie Screwvala, and Rezolv's $12.5 million Series A round led by Norwest.

title: Rural healthcare startup CureBay raises Rs 100 Cr in Pre-Series C led by IvyCap
description: CureBay, a rural healthcare startup, has raised around Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. News.
body: CureBay, a rural healthcare startup, has raised around Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C funding round led by IvyCap Ventures.
The round comprises Rs 69 crore in equity from IvyCap Ventures and existing investors, along with over Rs 30 crore in debt from Trifecta Capital, Alteria Capital and VentureSoul Partners.

The proceeds will be used to expand its presence across India, including an entry into Andhra Pradesh. The company also plans to strengthen its technology and artificial intelligence capabilities to improve health screening, patient insights and clinical decision making.

Founded in 2021 by Priyadarshi Mohapatra, Shobhan Mahapatra and Sanjay Swain, CureBay operates a network of technology enabled clinics that provide healthcare services in underserved areas. Its services include doctor consultations, medicines, diagnostic tests, surgery facilitation and annual health memberships.

The company operates over 250 clinics across seven states, supported by more than 1,800 Swasthya Mitras, 530 trained clinical staff, 230 doctor partners and over 210 partner hospitals and laboratories. It has served more than 17 lakh patients and conducts over 400 health camps every month.

CureBay operates a six layer rural healthcare system that combines physical clinics, a community health worker network, a digital platform, AI powered screening, a 24/7 command centre and CureBay Kavach.
The company also works with the government on healthcare delivery initiatives and has been named the healthcare partner for Samriddhi Kendra, a Government of India initiative.

CureBay last raised $21 million in a Series B round led by Bertelsmann India Investments in May 2025. Existing investor Elevar Equity and British International Investment also participated in the round.

title: Unicommerce posts Rs 59 Cr revenue and Rs 6.4 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
description: Unicommerce continued its growth trajectory in the latest quarter, reporting a 15% year-on-year increase in revenue and a 10.7% rise in net profit during Q2 FY27.
body: E-commerce enablement SaaS platform Unicommerce continued its growth trajectory in the latest quarter, reporting a 15% year-on-year increase in revenue and a 10.7% rise in net profit during Q2 FY27. The company’s revenue from operation increased to Rs 59.10 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 51.38crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal. according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.

For the first half of FY27, Unicommerce’s revenue from operations increased 14.7% to Rs 110.45 crore from Rs 96.32 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal. Unicommerce also earned Rs 1.56 crore from other income, taking its total income to Rs 60.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 52.2 crore in Q2 FY26. On the expense side, employee benefit expenses rose 23.4% to Rs 20.90 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 16.94 crore in Q2 FY26, while server hosting costs surged 41.5% to Rs 1.91 crore. Depreciation expenses increased 7.5% to Rs 2.15 crore, while finance costs declined 5% to Rs 19 lakh. Other expenses grew 15.5% to Rs 27.67 crore. Overall, total expenses increased 18.9% to Rs 52.83 crore during the quarter from Rs 44.45 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal. At the end, the Gurugram-based firm reported a net profit of Rs 6.40 crore in Q2 FY27, up 10.7% from Rs 5.78 crore in Q2 FY26. Its net profit grew 14.5% to Rs 11.07 crore in Q2FY27  from Rs 9.67 crore in Q1 FY27. Unicommerce shares closed at Rs 76.09 apiece at the end of Friday’s trading session, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 896 crore.

title: Garuda Aerospace’s FY26 revenue jumps 67% to Rs 206 Cr; profit rise 42%
description: Drone technology startup Garuda Aerospace reported a strong 67% year-on-year revenue growth in FY26 while maintaining profitability, with net profit at Rs 26 crore
body: Drone technology startup Garuda Aerospace reported a strong 67% year-on-year revenue growth in FY26 while maintaining profitability, with net profit at Rs 26 crore as the Chennai-based company is preparing to go public soon as it recently received SEBI nod for Rs 1,000 crore IPO.

Garuda’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 206 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026,compared to Rs 123.5 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Garuda Aerospace designs and manufactures drones for applications across agriculture, defence, infrastructure, mining and disaster management. Besides drone manufacturing, the firm also offers Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) and operates a DGCA-approved remote pilot training programme.

Revenue from sale of services surged 84.1% to Rs 106.46 crore in FY26 from Rs 57.83 crore in FY25, while revenue from sale of products grew 66.2% to Rs 99.50 crore from Rs 59.85 crore during the same period.

On the expense front, the cost of materials, remains the largest expense component, rose 62% to Rs 117 crore in FY26 from Rs 72.21 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses declined 16.2% to Rs 8 crore from Rs 9.55 crore.

Legal and professional charges surged 94.6% to Rs 12.88 crore from Rs 6.62 crore. Other overheads such as impairment loss on financial assets, depreciation & amortization expenses, travelling added another Rs 34.12 crore to the total cost.
Overall, Garuda’s total expenses grew 73.7% to Rs 172 crore in the last fiscal year compared to Rs 99 crore in FY25.

Despite the increase in costs, the company reported a 41.5% increase in net profit to Rs 26 crore in FY26 from Rs 18.37 crore in FY25. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood and EBITDA margin stood  at 14.71% and 18.97% respectively.

title: Harajuku Tokyo Café raises $3 Mn in pre-Series A led by Zero W
description: Existing seed investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC participated in the round with follow-on investments. New investors include Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh
body: Harajuku Tokyo Café, the Japanese food and beverage business operating Harajuku Tokyo Café and Harajuku Bakehouse, has raised $3 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by Zero W.

Existing seed investors Indian Angel Network (IAN) and Samved VC participated in the round with follow-on investments. New investors include Blume Founders Fund, Brijesh Parekh Family Office, Rahul Jain, co-founder of Epigamia, and others.

The company had previously raised $2 million (Rs 19 crore) in a seed funding round co-led by IAN and Samved VC in August 2025, with participation from LetsVenture and venture debt fund Capitar Ventures.
The proceeds will be used to fund the next phase of growth. The company aims to achieve Rs 100 crore in revenue in the current financial year, Harajuku Tokyo Café said in a press release.

Founded in 2021 by Gaurav Kanwar, Harajuku operates two food and beverage concepts across Delhi NCR and Mumbai. Harajuku Tokyo Café is a full-service dining format featuring conveyor-belt sushi and Tokyo-inspired interiors.

Harajuku Bakehouse is a quick-service format offering Japanese breads, desserts and savoury snacks. The company has developed its menu and operating platform with chefs Asami Indo and Higuchi Nariaki to support expansion and introduce contemporary Japanese food to Indian consumers.

Over the next two quarters, Harajuku plans to open 10 outlets across new neighbourhoods in Delhi NCR and Mumbai. It also plans to enter Bengaluru and Chandigarh. The company aims to operationalise central kitchens in Mumbai and Bengaluru by December 2026. These facilities will supply Harajuku Bakehouse outlets and support the production of its packaged food range for western and southern India.

Since its seed funding round in August 2025, the company has doubled its outlet count and revenue. Mumbai, where the brand launched in July 2025, now contributes 25% of its revenue. Harajuku processes more than 1,000 orders per day across dine-in and delivery channels.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 19- Oct 24]
description: This week, 15 Indian startups raised $133.9 million across 4 growth-stage deals, 10 early-stage deals, and 1 undisclosed round. The week also saw 5 key appointments.
body: This week, 15 Indian startups raised $133.9 million across 4 growth-stage deals, 10 early-stage deals, and 1 undisclosed round. The week also saw 5 key appointments.
In contrast, 30 startups had collectively secured about $302.85 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]

Growth-stage startups raised $86.2 million across four deals this week, led by Even Healthcare, which secured $50 million in a Series B round led by existing investor Khosla Ventures. Premium menswear brand The Pant Project raised Rs 109 crore in a Series B round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investments India, with participation from existing investor Sorin Investments.

Battery-swapping startup Battery Smart raised close to Rs 100 crore from an existing investor to expand its network for electric two- and three-wheelers. Meanwhile, rural healthcare startup CureBay secured around Rs 100 crore in a Pre-Series C round led by IvyCap Ventures.
[Early-stage deals]

Early-stage startups raised $47.7 million across 10 deals this week, led by AI startup AuxoAI, which secured $20.7 million in a Series A round led by NTTVC. Home and kitchen brand Chapter Home raised Rs 63 crore through a mix of equity and debt from Bessemer Venture Partners, Stride Ventures, influencer Tanmay Bhat and family offices.

Travel platform TravClan raised $5 million from online retailer Flipkart and investment firm August One, along with debt financing from Trifecta Capital. Hunar.AI, an AI-powered frontline workforce platform, secured Rs 40 crore in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures. AI startup Vectorial raised $3 million in a round led by SenseAI Ventures, while voice AI platform Karta AI secured $3 million in a seed round led by PeerCapital and Cedar Hill.

title: WeWork India’s Q2 FY27 revenue rises 34% to Rs 768 Cr, profit jumps over 3X
description: WeWork India has announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY27). The company posted 33.8% year-on-year growth in operating revenue
body: Managed office space provider WeWork India has announced its financial results for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY27). The company posted 33.8% year-on-year growth in operating revenue during the period, while profit surged over 3X. WeWork India’s revenue from operations rose 33.8% year-on-year to Rs 768 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 574 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.
For the first half of FY27, The company’s revenue from operations increased 30.8% to Rs 1,452 crore from Rs 1,110 crore in H1 FY26.

Income from managed workspace and allied services remained the company’s sole source of operating revenue. It also reported Rs 18 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 786 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 585.5 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the expenditure front, depreciation and amortisation related to leases remained the largest cost head at Rs 314 crore, up 35.9% year-on-year. Finance costs increased 14.4% to Rs 175 crore, while employee benefit expenses also increased 16.7% to Rs 56 crore. Operating expenses surged 52% to Rs 194.5 crore, while other expenses climbed 44.7% to Rs 27.5 crore. As a result, WeWork India’s total expenses increased 32.5% to Rs 767 crore in Q2 FY27.

At the bottom line, WeWork India reported a profit of Rs 20.44 crore in Q2 FY27, up 219.4% from Rs 6.4 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal. For the first half of FY27, the company posted a profit of Rs 16.37 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 7.74 crore in H1 FY26. At the end of Monday’s trading session, WeWork India shares closed at Rs 622.55 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 8,751 crore.

title: Paytm reports Rs 2,648 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; profit jumps 10.7X
description: Fintech firm One97 Communications, which operates Paytm's profit increased 10.7 times YoY to Rs 225 crore, while revenue from operations grew 28.5% in the quarter.
body: Fintech firm One97 Communications, which operates Paytm, announced its financial results for the second quarter of FY27 on Monday. The company’s profit increased 10.7 times year-on-year to Rs 225 crore, while revenue from operations grew 28.5% in the quarter.

According to its unaudited quarterly results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Paytm’s operating revenue stood at Rs 2,648 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,061 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Payment services remained Paytm’s largest revenue contributor, with revenue from the segment rising over 25% year-on-year to Rs 1,434 crore in Q2 FY27. The segment accounted for more than 54% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from financial services distribution and marketing services stood at Rs 912 crore and Rs 287 crore, respectively.
Paytm also earned Rs 182 crore from non-operating sources during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 2,830 crore in Q2 FY27.
On a sequential basis, Paytm’s revenue increased 8% from Rs 2,448 crore in Q1 FY27.

Payment processing charges remained Paytm’s largest expense in Q2 FY27, at nearly 32% of its total costs. This expense rose 28% year-on-year to Rs 805 crore. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 759 crore, up over 14% from the same quarter last year.

Marketing expenses increased 59% year-on-year to Rs 194 crore in Q2 FY27. Software, cloud, communication, legal, cashback, and other overhead expenses drove total expenditure to Rs 2,531 crore during the quarter, compared to Rs 2,062 crore in the year-ago period.
Paytm’s net profit surged 10.7 times year-on-year to Rs 225 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

title: Nazara returns to profit in Q2 FY27; advertising accounts for 54% of total cost
description: Nazara Technologies, a gaming and sports media company, reported a 52.7% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27 and returned to profitability despite
body: Nazara Technologies, a gaming and sports media company, reported a 52.7% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27 and returned to profitability despite a 3.6-fold jump in advertising expenses.
The company’s operating revenue increased 52.7% to Rs 803 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 526 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.
On a half-yearly basis, Nazara’s operating revenue grew 20.2% to Rs 1,232 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 1,025 crore in H1 FY26.
Gaming remained the largest revenue contributor, accounting for 81.7% of operating revenue. Revenue from the segment jumped 2.22X to Rs 656 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 296 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Meanwhile, revenue from the ad-tech business declined 13.9% to Rs 124 crore from Rs 144 crore. The esports segment also reported a 73.6% drop in revenue to Rs 23 crore from Rs 87 crore during the same period.

Advertising and business promotion emerged as the largest cost for the firm, which surged 3.6 times to Rs 417 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 116 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefit expenses increased 9.2% to Rs 85.21 crore from Rs 78 crore during the same period.

Content, event and web server expenses declined 58.3% to Rs 66.75 crore from Rs 160 crore, while depreciation expenses rose 20.6% to Rs 73.56 crore from Rs 61 crore. Commission expenses fell 2% to Rs 50 crore from Rs 51 crore, whereas other expenses increased 11% to Rs 75.5 crore from Rs 68 crore.

As a result, Nazara’s total expenditure increased 43.8% to Rs 768 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 534 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year. Despite the revenue growth, The Mumbai based company returned to profit Rs 35.36 crore compared from around Rs 34 crore loss in Q2FY26. The company reported a net loss of Rs 47.11 crore in H1 FY27, compared to a net profit of Rs 17.41 crore in the first half of FY26. At the close of trading, Nazara Technologies’ shares settled at Rs 399.95, giving the company a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 16,402 crore.

title: D2C apparel brand ReplyAll raises Rs 9.7 Cr in pre-Series A round
description: The brand had previously secured Rs 6.8 crore ($750K) in its first funding round led by Sparrow Capital and Antler India, with participation from Bharat Founders Fund,
body: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) apparel brand ReplyAll has raised Rs 9.7 crore in pre-Series A funding round co-led by Sadev Ventures and Atom XVII. The round also saw participation from ISV and Long View Ventures, along with existing investors Sparrow and Antler, and a group of angel investors.

The brand had previously secured Rs 6.8 crore ($750K) in its first funding round led by Sparrow Capital and Antler India, with participation from Bharat Founders Fund, DeVC, and several D2C founders in Dec. last year.
The proceeds will be used to invest in fabric research and development, product design, new categories, and the brand’s retail and community presence, ReplyAll said in a press release.
Launched in 2025 by Rushabh Sanghavi, ReplyAll offers performance wear and everyday apparel designed for work, travel, workouts and casual wear.
The Bengaluru-based brand focuses on versatile styling, functional details and material innovation to develop clothing for everyday use.

According to the company, its Temperform™ fabric, used in the Coolest Tee, is designed to help manage heat during everyday activities and sports. Its Flexknit™ material offers stretch and wrinkle resistance in trousers designed for work, travel and casual wear. ReplyAll plans to invest in further fabric research and expand its product categories.

The company said it has recorded month-on-month revenue growth over the past seven months. Its first three product launches, the Coolest Tee, All-In Pants and Stepwise Tee, sold out, while repeat customers account for 40% of its revenue.

title: Social gaming startup Matiks raises $10 Mn in Pre-Series A led by General Catalyst
description: Bengaluru-based social gaming startup Matiks has raised $10 million in a funding round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Ronnie Screwvala and others.
body: Bengaluru-based social gaming startup Matiks has raised $10 million in a Pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Ronnie Screwvala and existing investors Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners and Untitled Ventures.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its international presence, develop new games and social experiences, and launch an AI-powered game creation platform that will allow users to build and publish games without coding.

Founded in 2024 by Sudhanshu Bhatia, Sushant and Mohan, Matiks started as a mental maths game and has since expanded into a social gaming platform offering games across mathematics, memory, logic and puzzles. The platform allows users to compete against friends, participate in daily challenges and track their progress.

In September 2026, 2.2 million users played 48 million games on the platform. Its daily active users have more than doubled since June to over 300,000, with the company also seeing early traction in markets such as Japan, the US and South Korea.
The company recently launched SNAC, an endless feed of single-player puzzles, which has contributed to longer user sessions, according to Matiks.

Matiks plans to initially focus on the US market before expanding into other major international markets. It will also invest in engineering, artificial intelligence, product development, game design and growth.
The company is also developing an AI-powered game creation engine that will enable users to create, publish and share their own brain games across multiple formats.

In August 2025, Matiks raised $3.1 million in a Pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with participation from Info Edge Ventures and angel investors, including boAt co-founder Aman Gupta and Unacademy co-founders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini, among others.

title: Healthcare startup BioStack raises $9.5 Mn in seed funding led by Peak XV
description: BioStack, a healthcare technology startup, has raised $9.5 million in a seed funding round led by Peak XV, Afore Capital. Snippets.
body: BioStack, a healthcare technology startup, has raised $9.5 million in a seed funding round led by Peak XV, Afore Capital, DCVC, Emerson Collective, SV Angel, Verdict Capital, Streamlined Ventures and Y Combinator.
The fresh capital will support its international expansion, technology development and growth of its engineering and research teams.
The company is building a healthcare data infrastructure network spanning the US, India, Brazil and Argentina, with access to more than 100 million de-identified patient records.

Founded by Sanat Mishra, BioStack connects fragmented clinical information across hospitals and healthcare systems to create longitudinal patient records. These records combine clinical notes, laboratory results, medical imaging, medications, treatment histories and patient outcomes.

The company creates proprietary datasets from de-identified clinical data to support medical research, drug development and the training and evaluation of healthcare AI models. Its platform is designed for applications including disease modelling, biomarker discovery, patient stratification and treatment response analysis.

BioStack claims to have aggregated several hundred thousand X-rays, MRI and CT scans, along with millions of telehealth audio transcripts and other clinical records. In India, the company is also helping connect cancer patients with an investigational cancer vaccine programme.
Its platform also incorporates workflows tailored to individual healthcare providers and their data privacy protocols.

title: Ather Energy shares jump 14% on Q2 profit turnaround; capacity set to expand
description: Ather Energy shares jumped 14% to Rs 1,575 on Monday after the EV maker turned profitable in Q2 FY27 and announced plans to add 2.25 lakh units of annual production capacity across its Hosur and AURIC facilities.
body: Shares of Ather Energy jumped around 14% to Rs 1,575 per share on Monday after the electric two-wheeler maker reported a consolidated net profit in Q2 FY27, compared with a loss in the year-ago period. The company also announced plans to expand its annual production capacity by 2.25 lakh units across its Hosur and AURIC facilities to meet growing demand.

Ather Energy reported a consolidated profit after tax of Rs 1.26 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, against a loss of Rs 154 crore in Q2 FY26. Its consolidated total income rose 62% year-on-year to Rs 1,527 crore, while vehicle volumes increased 42% to 93,211 units, according to the company’s press release.

The company posted an EBITDA of Rs 74.2 crore during the quarter, marking its second consecutive EBITDA-positive quarter. Its EBITDA margin improved to 4.9% from negative 9.6% a year earlier, supported by higher volumes, product mix and pricing decisions.

Ather said customer enquiries rose 109% year-on-year to around 10 lakh in Q2 FY27, while pre-orders more than doubled to 1.8 lakh units. Its Hosur facility operated at 98% capacity utilisation during peak production in the quarter.

To cater to the growing demand, Ather plans to increase annual production capacity at Hosur from 4.2 lakh units to 4.95 lakh units by December 2026. Its upcoming AURIC facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is scheduled to begin commercial production in phases from December 2026, with an initial annual capacity of 5 lakh units. The company plans to expand this to 6.5 lakh units by Q2 FY28.
The capacity expansion will require an investment of approximately Rs 122 crore, taking Ather’s combined installed annual production capacity to around 11.4 lakh units by Q2 FY28.

During the quarter, Ather also launched Konarc, its first scooter built on the new EL platform. Unveiled at its Community Day event in August, the scooter focuses on everyday comfort and convenience. It features a metal body, an adjustable backrest, keyless access and a new Bedrock battery backed by a 10-year warranty.

Brokerages have also remained bullish on Ather. In August, CLSA retained its ‘ Outperform ’ rating on the company with a target price of Rs 1,600, citing strong volume growth, robust bookings, upcoming capacity expansion and the launch of its EL platform.

title: Ather Energy turns profitable in Q2 FY27; revenue surges 63%
description: Ather Energy reported 63% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in Q2 FY27, while turning profitable with a net profit of Rs 1.3 crore during the quarter.
body: Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Ather Energy reported 63% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in Q2 FY27, driven by growing demand for its electric two-wheelers, while turning profitable with a net profit of Rs 1.3 crore during the quarter.
Ather Energy’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 1,464 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 899 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its quarterly financial results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The sale of electric two-wheelers and related services remained Ather Energy's sole source of operating revenue, although the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup. During the quarter, it sold 93,211 units.
The company also recorded Rs 62 crore in other income, taking its total income for the quarter to Rs 1,527 crore.
On a quarterly basis, Ather’s revenue grew 20% compared to Rs 1,217 crore in Q1 FY27.

Material costs, which primarily include battery cells and other components, remained Ather Energy’s largest expense, rising 59% year-on-year to Rs 1,160 crore in Q2 FY27. Employee benefit expenses also increased 6% to Rs 121 crore during the quarter.

Depreciation and amortisation, along with expenses on legal services, advertising and other operating activities, contributed to a rise in total expenditure to Rs 1,526 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,095 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Higher electric two-wheeler sales and an increase in other income helped Ather Energy turn profitable with a net profit of Rs 1.3 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 154 crore in the year-ago quarter. The company nearly doubled its vehicle sales to 93,211 units from 52,961 units in Q2 FY26.

title: Kapiva crosses Rs 460 Cr revenue in FY26; targets EBITDA profitability by Q4 FY27
description: Following 50% growth in FY25, Ayurveda wellness brand Kapiva continued its growth momentum in FY26, with its operating revenue crossing Rs 460 crore.
body: Following 50% growth in FY25, Ayurveda wellness brand Kapiva continued its growth momentum in FY26, with its revenue crossing Rs 460 crore. The company also managed to keep its losses largely stable despite higher spending on marketing and other operating costs, while its margins improved after excluding employee stock option (ESOP) expenses.

Kapiva’s revenue from operations grew 36.5% year-on-year to Rs 464 crore in FY26 from Rs 340 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). Including non-operating income of Rs 10 crore, its total income stood at Rs 474 crore.

Founded in 2015, Kapiva offers Ayurvedic nutrition and wellness products across categories such as diabetes management, liver health, hormonal balance, energy and sports nutrition. Sales of its products remained the company’s sole source of operating revenue.

Advertising and promotional expenses remained Kapiva’s largest cost component, accounting for nearly 48% of its total expenditure. The expense increased 39.8% to Rs 260 crore in FY26 from Rs 186 crore in the previous fiscal year.

The firm’s procurement costs rose 22.6% to Rs 117 crore, while employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 78 crore. Higher spending across these and other heads, including legal, technology and freight, pushed its total expenditure up 31.2% to Rs 547 crore in FY26 from Rs 417 crore in FY25.

Despite the increase in expenses, Kapiva’s losses remained broadly stable at Rs 72 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 69 crore a year earlier. Its EBITDA margin, excluding ESOP expenses of Rs 7.85 crore, improved to -14.8% in FY26 from -18.7% in FY25. At the unit level, the company spent Rs 1.18 to earn every rupee of operating revenue.

Kapiva has also expanded its product portfolio and distribution network, with investments in new categories such as liver care, cholesterol management and women’s hormonal health, along with infrastructure for offline distribution.

“During the last year, Kapiva has made significant investments in creating new categories (Liver Care, Cholesterol, Women’s Hormonal Health) and building infrastructure for offline distribution. These investments are likely to deliver substantial leverage in coming years which helps drive profitability,” a company spokesperson said.

title: Yes Madam’s revenue jumps over 2X to Rs 195 Cr in FY26
description: Yes Madam more than doubled its operating revenue to Rs 195 crore in FY26 for the second straight year, taking its revenue to over 4X in two years
body: Home salon services platform Yes Madam more than doubled its operating revenue to Rs 195 crore in FY26 for the second straight year, taking its revenue to over 4X in two years, but slipped into losses amid higher employee and advertising costs during FY26.
The company’s revenue from operations jumped 2.07X to Rs 195 crore in FY26 compared with Rs 94 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2016, Noida-based Yes Madam is an at-home beauty and wellness services platform that offers services such as haircuts, facials, waxing and massages through its app and website. The company has also launched instant salon and spa services, enabling customers to book at-home services within 30 minutes.
