Revenue from the sale of services, which includes commission income earned as an agent between service professionals and end customers, along with subscription and royalty income, contributed 51% of Yes Madam’s operating revenue. This segment grew 2.3 times to reach Rs 100 crore mark in FY26.
Revenue from product sales rose 90% to Rs 95 crore from Rs 50 crore during the same period, accounting for the remaining 49% of operating revenue.

On the expense side, advertising and promotional expenses emerged as the largest cost for the firm, which surged 2.31X to Rs 67 crore in the last fiscal year from Rs 29 crore in FY25, while the cost of materials consumed rose 90.6% to Rs 61 crore.
Employee benefit expenses also more than doubled to Rs 43 crore, while freight costs also increased 164.2% to Rs 4.28 crore during the same period.

Other expenses, including information technology, rent and legal and professional charges, collectively added Rs 27.7 crore in FY26. As a result, Yes Madam’s total expenditure jumped 2.21X to Rs 203 crore in FY26 from Rs 92 crore

Noida-based Yes Madam reported a net loss of Rs 7.75 crore in FY26, compared with a net profit of Rs 1.83 crore in FY25, as expenses grew faster than revenue. Its EBITDA margin also declined to -3.89% from 2.18% during the same period.

title: Kairon Capital leads Rs 7.6 Cr seed round in travel-tech startup Bucketlistt.com
description: The fresh funds will be utilized to strengthen technology and product, onboard more high-quality operators, and expand beyond Rishikesh, starting with Mana
body: Travel-tech startup Bucketlistt.com has raised Rs 7.6 crore in a seed funding round led by Kairon Capital, with participation from Titan Capital, Divisa Family Office and Kunal Popat.

The startup had earlier raised Rs 1.07 crore in a pre-seed angel funding round at a post-money valuation of Rs 10.07 crore. The round saw participation from angel investors including Arvind Choudhar, Aenik Shah, Kartik Khatri, and Yash Mehta.

The fresh funds will be utilized to strengthen technology and product, onboard more high-quality operators, and expand beyond Rishikesh, starting with Manali and Bir, and invest in content, organic discovery and distribution partnerships, Bucketlistt said in a press release.

Launched last year by Shubham Makhecha, Nitant Desai and Divyam Shah, Bucketlistt.com is a platform to discover and book experiences across India. Its operator platform, OkGhumo, is an operating system for experience providers that digitises bookings, inventory, agents and payments.

The Ahmedabad based startup helps travellers discover and book verified travel experiences, from skydiving in Mt. Abu and front row seats at the Ganga Aarti in Rishikesh to dinner with royal families in Jaipur.

The company launched in Rishikesh in December 2025. Alongside the marketplace, it runs OkGhumo, a platform that experience providers use to manage bookings, inventory, agents, payments and daily operations.

In the last 10 months, Bucketlistt.com and OkGhumo claimed to have together managed more than Rs 22.5 crore in bookings, while Bucketlistt.com has served more than 12,000 customers. About one in five of its customers now comes through word of mouth.

Launched in March 2026, OkGhumo has served more than 50,000 customers. Leading adventure operators in Rishikesh use it daily to manage bookings, inventory, agent settlements and payments, replacing calls, WhatsApp and spreadsheets. It also provides Bucketlistt.com with live inventory, allowing travellers to receive instant and reliable confirmations. The company now plans to replicate this model across multiple cities.

title: L Catterton makes strategic investment in Jio Platforms-backed Glance
description: Global consumer-focused investment firm L Catterton has made a strategic investment in Glance, an AI-powered shopping platform backed by InMobi. Snippets
body: Global consumer-focused investment firm L Catterton has made a strategic investment in Glance, an AI-powered shopping platform backed by InMobi, for an undisclosed amount.

Glance uses agentic AI to personalise product discovery and shopping across smartphones, connected TVs and other digital platforms. Its technology analyses consumer interests and preferences to recommend relevant products and help users move from discovery to purchase.

The investment follows L Catterton’s assessment of changing consumer behaviour and the growing role of AI in shopping. The firm plans to support Glance’s expansion, particularly in the US, by leveraging its consumer industry expertise, operating capabilities and global network.
Glance is available on millions of devices in the US through partnerships with Samsung, Motorola and DIRECTV. These partnerships extend its presence across mobile phones and televisions.

“Agentic commerce is fundamentally changing how consumers discover and shop for products,” said Scott Dahnke, global CEO of L Catterton, adding that the firm would support Glance’s growth through its consumer expertise and global network.
Founded by Naveen Tewari, Glance is backed by Mithril Capital, Google and Jio Platforms.

L Catterton manages approximately $40 billion in equity capital across private equity, credit and real estate investment platforms. The firm was founded in 1989 and has made more than 300 investments in consumer businesses.

title: Deep-tech defence startup Paar Autonomy raises Rs 10 Cr
description: he fresh capital will be used to scale up production of AI-powered camera systems and develop technology that enables drones to navigate without GPS, Paar Autonomy said
body: Deep-tech defence and robotics startup Paar Autonomy has raised Rs 10 crore in a funding round led by AdvantEdge Founders.
The Bengaluru-based startup had previously raised Rs 3.5 crore in a pre-seed round led by Venture Catalysts to set up its first manufacturing line and deliver pilot units.
The fresh capital will be used to scale up production of AI-powered camera systems and develop technology that enables drones to navigate without GPS, Paar Autonomy said in a press release.

Founded in June 2024 by Vignesh Sivaram Jayaraman, Paar Autonomy builds camera systems and AI software for drones and other unmanned defence platforms. Its products focus on the perception layer for unmanned aerial, ground and maritime vehicles, including drones, rovers and boats.

The company’s capabilities include edge-based AI, GPS and GNSS-independent visual-inertial navigation, and gyro-stabilised, multi-sensor gimbal camera payloads. These technologies are designed to support operations in GPS-denied and communication-contested environments.
Paar Autonomy also uses AI models to enable real-time environmental interpretation, situational awareness and target tracking for autonomous operations.
Its product portfolio includes the Sentinel series, comprising Sentinel 1, Sentinel 2, Sentinel Nano, Sentinel Nano Dark and Sentinel Nano Dual.

The company primarily caters to defence applications such as border surveillance and tactical tracking. It also serves civilian use cases, including industrial inspection, infrastructure monitoring and disaster response.

title: Simplismart raises $14 Mn from Dallas Venture Capital, NVIDIA and others
description: Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.
body: AI inference infrastructure startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in a Series B funding round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from NVIDIA, Accel, Shastra VC and Micromax.
The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its inference engine and orchestration platform, expand its cloud provider network and support its growth across North America and other global markets.
Entrackr had earlier reported on the deal, which values the company at around $100 million post money. Previously, Simplismart raised $7 million in a Series A round in October 2024.

Founded by Amritanshu Jain, Simplismart provides infrastructure that helps enterprises deploy and run AI models while optimising inference costs, latency and GPU utilisation. Its platform also enables cloud providers to convert their GPU capacity into AI services for enterprise customers.

The company said its annualised revenue run rate grew 14X over the past six months. Its customers include HeyGen, Higgsfield, InVideo, Shiprocket, Apna and Ema, which use its platform for production workloads across video, voice, multimodal and enterprise AI applications.

Simplismart also works with cloud providers to offer managed AI inference services. At Yotta, its platform powers the serverless inference layer of Shakti Studio, which allows customers to run AI models without managing the underlying infrastructure.

Unlike inference providers that procure or reserve GPU capacity and resell it, Simplismart focuses on the software layer that enables third party GPU infrastructure to support production AI workloads. The company is also working with cloud providers and sovereign AI programmes across India, North America, the Middle East, Australia and East Asia.

The startup plans to use the new capital to further develop its inference and orchestration capabilities and build partnerships aimed at matching AI workloads with available GPU capacity across regions and cloud environments.

title: Trivia and puzzle app dubdub raises seed funding led by 3one4 Capital, Antler and Stellaris
description: The platform offers content across more than 20 categories, including cricket, Bollywood, general knowledge, pop culture, mythology and logical reasoning. It uses AI and
body: dubdub, a swipe-based trivia and puzzle app, has raised $1.3 million in a seed funding round co-led by 3one4 Capital, Antler and Stellaris Venture Partners.
The fresh funds will be used to hire across product and engineering, add new interactive formats and deepen personalisation of its feed, dubdub said in a press release.

Launched in March this year by Kaustubh Priye and Supan Shah, dubdub is a swipe-based trivia and puzzle platform that brings bite-sized questions, mini games and brain puzzles into a short-form, interactive format.

The platform offers content across more than 20 categories, including cricket, Bollywood, general knowledge, pop culture, mythology and logical reasoning. It uses AI and user interactions to personalise challenges based on individual interests. The app also offers features that allow users to challenge friends and compare scores.

The platform aims to replace passive content consumption with questions and mini games. Each swipe prompts users to answer, guess, solve, recognise, predict or compete, making the experience more interactive.
dubdub claims to have crossed 20,000 downloads. The company also reports early retention rates above the top percentile of casual games.
It plans to expand its product and engineering teams and introduce new interactive formats as it works towards building a broader interactive short-form entertainment platform.

title: Ola Electric shares rally nearly 20% ahead of Q2 FY27 results
description: Ola Electric Mobility shares rallied 19.5% to Rs 35.78 on Tuesday, October 27, as the electric two-wheeler maker’s Rs 1,000 crore rights issue remained in focus.
body: Ola Electric Mobility shares rallied 19.5% to Rs 35.78 on Tuesday, October 27, as the electric two-wheeler maker’s Rs 1,000 crore rights issue remained in focus.

Ola Electric’s Rs 1,000 crore rights issue opened on October 22 and closes on October 30. The company is issuing 37.03 crore partly paid-up shares at Rs 27 apiece, with an upfront payment of Rs 16.20 per share. Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors have applied for 2.39 crore shares, while founder Bhavish Aggarwal has pledged a 4.32% stake to fund his participation.

The rally comes amid SoftBank affiliate SVF II Ostrich (DE) LLC’s stake sale in Ola Electric. According to a regulatory filing, the investment vehicle sold shares and rights entitlements between January 6 and October 22, reducing its stake from 12.9% to 11.7%.

The rally follows a 14% jump in Ather Energy shares on Monday after the rival electric two-wheeler maker reported a turnaround in Q2 FY27, with a net profit of Rs 1.26 crore against a loss of Rs 154 crore in the year-ago quarter.
According to Vahan data, Ola Electric ranked fifth with 13,449 registrations and a 6.49% market share, down 3.53% from 13,941 units in August.

The company is yet to file its Q2 FY27 results. In Q1 FY27, Ola Electric’s revenue declined 45% year-on-year to Rs 455 crore from Rs 828 crore in Q1 FY26. At the same time, its losses widened 21% to Rs 336 crore.
Ola Electric’s share price closed at over 16% higher Rs 34.8 per share, with a total market capitalization of Rs 17,395 crore ($1.83 billion)

title: Child-care startup Maasi raises Rs 6 Cr in pre-seed round
description: The startup said its public launch on October 20 generated a waitlist of more than 4,000 parents within five days. It has served over 1,200 parents through a network of
body: Child-care startup Maasi has raised Rs 6 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Better Capital, with participation from Antler India. Angel investors in the round include Rapido founder Rishikesh SR, Shadowfax founder Vaibhav Khandelwal, Sumit Khandelwal, Siddhant Goyal and Multiply Ventures’ Sanjay Ramakrishnan.
The proceeds will be used to scale caregiver recruitment and training, build technology platforms and expand the team in Bengaluru, Maasi said in a press release.
Founded last year by Aashu Manchali, Gargi Pandey and Reshov Roy, Maasi trains, pays and supports caregivers to provide families in Bengaluru with trusted, accountable childcare at home.

The startup said its public launch on October 20 generated a waitlist of more than 4,000 parents within five days. It has served over 1,200 parents through a network of more than 500 caregivers and is growing 20% week on week.

Maasi offers on-demand nannies starting at Rs 199 per hour and monthly subscriptions starting at Rs 5,999. All caregivers undergo verification and training before meeting families through a free programme led by preschool directors, nurses and former airline cabin crew trainers.
Its latest offering, Maasi Governess, is an English-speaking nanny service focused on screen-free engagement and childcare.

title: IvyCap Ventures leads Rs 130 Cr pre-Series B round in Live2.ai
description: The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform combines a unified entity graph, multimodal AI and autonomous AI agents. It monitors brand conversations across
body: Live2.ai, an AI-based social intelligence and commerce activation platform, has raised Rs 130 crore (about $14 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The round comprises primary capital for business growth and a secondary component that provides partial liquidity to early shareholders.

The fresh funds will be used to develop its agentic intelligence layer, expand its go-to-market operations for enterprise and global consumer brands, and strengthen its regional cloud infrastructure across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific, Live2.ai said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by J Venkat, Neha Suyal and Yash Arora, Live2.ai provides a platform that connects social intelligence with campaign execution and commerce activation.

The platform helps brands monitor online conversations, plan and publish social media posts, track performance, manage audits and compliance for influencer and user-generated content, and convert rights-cleared content into shoppable experiences across digital and offline channels.

The Bengaluru-based startup said its platform combines a unified entity graph, multimodal AI and autonomous AI agents. It monitors brand conversations across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, X and review sites to help brands identify trends and inform business decisions.

Live2.ai offers three key capabilities: social intelligence for trend identification and campaign strategy; audit and compliance management for influencer and user-generated content; and social publishing and performance tracking across channels.

The platform also uses eight AI agents, including Crisis Detection, Trend Scout, Campaign Auditor and Autonomous Response, to support tasks across social intelligence, campaign management and customer engagement. These agents operate on a shared entity graph with governance controls and human review.
Live2.ai said it works with brands such as Henkel's Schwarzkopf, Salonory, Titan Brands and Shiseido. The company claims to serve more than 200 brands across the US, Europe and Southeast Asia.

title: Practo co-founder Shashank ND’s startup Cent raises $15 Mn led by Blume, acquires Medsee
description: Preventive healthcare startup Cent has raised $15 million co-led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. The company has also acquired AI radiology platform Medsee.
body: Preventive healthcare startup Cent has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round co-led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commons. The company has also acquired AI radiology platform Medsee.
The round saw participation from individual investors Arun Sarin, Srinivas Narayanan, Sharath Narayana, Aprameya Radhakrishna and Krishan Sridhar, Cent founder Shashank ND said in a LinkedIn post.
Founded by Shashank ND, who also founded healthcare platform Practo, Cent focuses on early disease detection through medical imaging, biomarkers and artificial intelligence (AI).

Over the past year, around 10,000 people have undergone screening through Cent's protocol. Of these, one in four had a finding that required medical attention, while one in 40 needed to consult a doctor immediately, the company said.

Cent's screening protocol combines full body MRI, low dose CT scans, DEXA, ECG, ECHO and over 100 biomarkers in a single session of around two hours. The startup operates its own centres in Bengaluru, Mumbai and Delhi NCR, alongside its earlier network of partner diagnostic labs.
The fresh capital will be used to invest in hardware, AI and clinical research. The acquisition of Medsee will also strengthen Cent's AI capabilities, Shashank said.
Cent aims to conduct 10 million scans by 2035 and help save one million lives through early disease detection.

The startup is looking to address the gap in India's healthcare system, where several noncommunicable diseases are diagnosed at advanced stages. India has an estimated 101 million people living with diabetes and 136 million with prediabetes, while around 315 million people have hypertension, according to figures cited by Cent.

title: SoftBank sells 1.2% stake in Ola Electric amid Rs 1,000 Cr rights issue
description: SVF II Ostrich (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, has sold 5.55 crore shares of Ola Electric Mobility through open market transactions between January 6 and October 22, 2026
body: SVF II Ostrich (DE) LLC, an affiliate of SoftBank, has sold 5.55 crore shares of Ola Electric Mobility through open market transactions between January 6 and October 22, 2026, according to Ola Electric’s regulatory filing dated October 26.

The investor also sold 1.12 crore rights entitlements during the period. Following the transactions, its shareholding in Ola Electric declined to 11.7% from 12.9%, while its holding on a diluted basis fell to 11.47% from 12.81%, as per the filing.

The stake sale comes as the Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler maker seeks to raise Rs 1,000 crore through a rights issue. The issue opened on October 22 and will close on October 30. Ola Electric plans to issue 37.03 crore partly paid-up equity shares at Rs 27 apiece, with an upfront payment of Rs 16.20 per share.

In a separate filing dated October 22, Ola Electric disclosed that Motilal Oswal Financial Services and Calliope Capital Advisors had applied for a combined 2.39 crore shares under the rights issue. Motilal Oswal applied for 1.28 crore shares, while Calliope Capital applied for 1.10 crore shares after both entities acquired rights entitlements from promoter group entities ANI Technologies and Indus Trust.

Meanwhile, Ola Electric founder Bhavish Aggarwal pledged a 4.32% stake in the company to fund his participation in the rights issue. The pledge was created to finance his subscription, with no shares sold as part of the transaction.

The rights issue is aimed at providing additional capital to the company amid pressure on its business and financial performance. The latest fundraise follows Ola Electric's Rs 780 crore qualified institutional placement in June.

title: Luxury watch brand Rotoris raises Rs 70 Cr in Series A round led by Blume Ventures
description: The company will use the fresh capital for research and development, production expansion and the growth of its physical presence in India and overseas.
body: Luxury watch brand Rotoris has raised Rs 70 crore (about $7.4 million) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from 9Unicorns, Centricity and a group of family offices, including Diwakar Goel, Atul Singh and Adhiraj Burman. Actor and television host Rannvijay Singha also participated in the round.
The company will use the fresh capital for research and development, production expansion and the growth of its physical presence in India and overseas.

Founded by Prerna Gupta and Aakash Anand, Rotoris operates an invitation only model through its Registry. The company said its first collection of 2,100 numbered watches sold out within days of its launch in February 2026. Nearly 100,000 people have since registered for access to its watches, with 40% of demand coming from markets outside India, including the US, Dubai and Australia.

In December 2025, Rotoris raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath, actor-investor Vivek Anand Oberoi, Venture Catalysts, 100 Unicorns and Tanmay Bhat. The round also saw participation from more than 30 founders, including Mamaearth's Varun Alagh, Noise's Gaurav Khatri and Snitch's Siddharth Dungarwal.

Rotoris offers collections such as Manifesta, which features natural stone dials, and Astonia, a chronograph built around a Swiss movement. Its watches are assembled and tested at the Rotoris Atelier in Gurugram, with movements sourced from Switzerland and Japan.
The company plans to expand its physical presence through Rotoris House, with plans to move beyond Delhi to Mumbai and New York.

Aakash Anand previously built and scaled beauty and personal care brand Bella Vita before exiting the business. Prerna Gupta leads Rotoris, with a focus on premium brand building and customer experience.

title: Fireside Ventures leads Rs 100 Cr Series B round in snack brand Troovy
description: Entrackr had exclusively reported the fundraise in June this year, when the company was looking to raise up to Rs 200 crore in a Series B round.
body: Snack brand Troovy has raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Sharrp Ventures and other investors.
Entrackr had exclusively reported the fundraise in June this year, when the company was looking to raise up to Rs 200 crore in a Series B round.

The Gurugram-based brand had previously raised $5 million in a Series A round in January this year. The round was led by Fireside Ventures and Sharrp Ventures, with participation from existing investors Spring Marketing Capital and Veltis Capital. Before that, the startup had raised $2.3 million (Rs 20 crore) in a pre-Series A round led by Fireside Ventures in May 2025.

The proceeds will be used to expand R&D and manufacturing capacity, scale distribution across quick commerce and offline channels, and accelerate its Build Together model, Troovy said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2023 by Aditya Mukherjee and Mansi Baranwal, Troovy is a food and snacking brand that offers products such as snacks, sauces, spreads and millet pasta. The brand focuses on using carefully selected ingredients to offer convenient food options for children and families.

The company develops products based on parental inputs and insights into children's preferences. It aims to make better food choices more appealing through product innovation and a consumer-first approach.

Troovy said its vacuum-cooked potato chips contain 10% to 12% oil, compared with 35% to 40% in mainstream chips. The company also offers clean-label ketchup and seasonings for children without synthetic additives or preservatives.
The brand competes with Slurrp Farm, Timios and The Mumum Co in the kids' health food segment.

title: Physical AI vision company Nova Spectral AI raises Rs 21.15 Cr led by Shastra VC
description: Nova Spectral AI uses CMOS compatible manufacturing processes and indium arsenide (InAs) colloidal quantum dots to develop infrared sensors. The company aims to reduce
body: Physical AI vision company Nova Spectral AI has raised Rs 21.15 crore (about $2.25 million) in a seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Equirus InnovateX Fund and angel investors.
The proceeds will be used to build a team and develop a field ready prototype within 18 months, the company said in a press release.

Founded this year by Anish Priyadarshi and Sanjeev Kumar, Nova Spectral AI develops lead free colloidal quantum dot (cQD) short wave infrared (SWIR) image sensor chips on standard silicon CMOS for defence intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) and physical AI applications.

The Bengaluru based startup said it is developing an indigenous quantum dot SWIR image sensor chip. The technology enables cameras to capture images in conditions where conventional cameras may struggle, including low light, haze and smoke. It can be used in drones, surveillance systems, robots and autonomous vehicles.

Nova Spectral AI uses CMOS compatible manufacturing processes and indium arsenide (InAs) colloidal quantum dots to develop infrared sensors. The company aims to reduce sensor costs by up to 100 times compared with conventional indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) technology.

In defence, the technology could expand the use of SWIR imaging across drones and ISR platforms while reducing dependence on imported sensors. The company is also targeting applications in smartphones, wearables, robots and automobiles.

Colloidal quantum dot SWIR image sensors built on standard silicon CMOS are being explored as a way to make infrared imaging more affordable and scalable across applications that require vision in challenging conditions.

Another player in the space, SpectraGaze Systems, raised Rs 3.7 crore in seed funding led by GVFL to develop indigenous infrared detectors, optical imaging sensors and electro optical payloads for space and defence applications.

title: MakeMyTrip returns to profit in Q2 FY27; gross bookings grow 21%
description: MakeMyTrip returned to profitability in Q2 FY27 with a net profit of $1.8 million against a loss of $5.7 million a year ago, while gross bookings rose 20.9% year-on-year to $2.72 billion in constant currency.
body: MakeMyTrip returned to profitability in Q2 FY27 as growth in hotels, bus ticketing and ancillary services offset pressure on air travel. The Nasdaq-listed company reported a net profit of $1.8 million for the quarter ended September 2026, compared with a loss of $5.7 million a year earlier, while gross bookings rose 20.9% year-on-year in constant currency to $2.72 billion.

Revenue increased 2.5% to $235.2 million from $229.3 million, although growth stood at 11.2% after adjusting for currency movements. The Indian rupee depreciated approximately 10% against the US dollar during the quarter, affecting reported revenue growth.
MakeMyTrip also cited elevated airfares and subdued international long-haul travel, partly offset by strong domestic demand.

Adjusted operating profit rose to $46.2 million from $44.2 million, while adjusted net profit before tax increased 26.9% to $46.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA stood at $51.5 million, up 6.4% year-on-year. However, the return to a small reported net profit came alongside slower growth in reported revenue than in gross bookings.

Hotels and packages remained the largest contributor to adjusted margin, which rose 20.2% in constant currency to $116.8 million. Standalone hotel room nights grew 18.6%, supported by domestic hotel bookings that increased more than 20%. The company said demand for domestic leisure trips, shorter holidays and pilgrimage travel supported the segment.

Air ticketing adjusted margin increased 14.3% to $108.6 million in constant currency, despite a 7.2% decline in reported revenue from the segment to $56.7 million. Management attributed the pressure to higher fares and constrained airline capacity. It said the business maintained market share and improved unit economics through ancillary services.

Bus ticketing was another growth area. Its adjusted margin rose 29% to $45.1 million, while revenue increased 16.6% in reported terms to $19.4 million. Revenue from other businesses, including ancillary services, grew 21.6% to $21.2 million.

MakeMyTrip is also expanding its AI assistant, Myra. It handled more than 90,000 conversations daily during the quarter, resolved over 53% of post-booking flight and hotel queries, and assisted with more than 3,000 completed bookings per day. Customers using Myra completed around 1.7 times more bookings than non-users, according to the company.

title: Trading platform Mochatrade raises $5.5 Mn in seed round led by CoinFund
description: Trading platform Mochatrade has raised $5.5 million in a seed funding round led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase. Snippets.
body: Trading platform Mochatrade has raised $5.5 million in a seed funding round led by CoinFund, with participation from Coinbase Ventures and Zero Knowledge Ventures, among others. Its earlier backers include Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
The fresh funds will be used to develop its trading engine and risk infrastructure, as well as expand its reach among active Indian traders, Mochatrade said in a press release.

Founded this year by Utkarsh Sinha, Parth Maheshwari and Chetan Manda, Mochatrade is a trading platform for Indian users that combines UPI-based funding and rupee balances with access to contracts linked to US stocks, indices and commodities.

According to the company, users can fund their accounts through UPI and view margins, or the money set aside for trades, as well as profits and losses in rupees. Users can take long or short positions through perpetual futures contracts linked to US company prices without opening a US brokerage account. These contracts have no fixed expiry, and users do not own the underlying shares. Leverage allows users to take larger positions with less upfront capital, but also amplifies potential losses.

Through its Indian operating entity, Mochatrade is registered with the Financial Intelligence Unit India (FIU-IND) as a Virtual Digital Asset Service Provider and a reporting entity for anti-money laundering purposes.
The platform said its waitlist has crossed 25,000 sign-ups. However, it has not announced a public launch date. Users can join the waitlist on its website for early access updates.

Mochatrade also plans to introduce contracts linked to select pre-IPO companies, US stock options and social trading features, subject to applicable laws and regulatory approvals. The company said its markets are designed to offer continuous access and real-time settlement, subject to liquidity, asset availability and risk controls.

Trading platforms offering Indian users access to global financial markets have begun combining UPI-based deposits, rupee-denominated balances and interfaces familiar to domestic futures and options (F&O) traders. These platforms provide exposure to contracts linked to US stocks, market indices and commodities.

title: Snapdeal parent AceVector posts Rs 151 Cr revenue and Rs 17.6 Cr loss in Q2 FY27
description: AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce platform Snapdeal, has reported 17% year-on-year to cross Rs 150 crore in Q2 FY27, while its losses stood at Rs 17.6 crore.
body: AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce platform Snapdeal, has reported its first quarterly results since its listing earlier this month. The company’s revenue rose 17% year-on-year to cross Rs 150 crore in Q2 FY27, while its losses stood at Rs 17.6 crore.
According to its unaudited quarterly results, AceVector’s operating revenue stood at Rs 151.2 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 129.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Snapdeal’s marketplace business accounted for the largest share of AceVector’s operating revenue at 57%, with revenue of Rs 86.2 crore, up 15% year-on-year. Its e-commerce enablement SaaS platform, Unicommerce, contributed Rs 59 crore, while consumer brands added Rs 6 crore to operating revenue.
Including Rs 2.6 crore in non-operating income, AceVector’s total income stood at Rs 153.8 crore in Q2 FY27.

For the first half of FY27, AceVector’s consolidated revenue grew 17% year-on-year to Rs 285.5 crore, supported by growth across Snapdeal and Unicommerce. Snapdeal’s revenue rose 15% to Rs 164.4 crore, while Unicommerce recorded a 15% increase to Rs 110.4 crore.

Snapdeal’s fashion net merchandise value (NMV) rose 31% year-on-year to Rs 407.6 crore in H1 FY27. Its annual transacting customer base grew 12% to 130.8 lakh, while app-delivered units increased 23% to 133.6 lakh. During the period, the company also launched an AI solutions suite for customers, sellers and creators, with features for product discovery, personalised recommendations and seller support.

Logistics expenses remained AceVector’s largest cost at Rs 71.4 crore, up 20% year-on-year. The expense accounted for over 42% of its total expenditure. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 46 crore during the quarter.

AceVector’s total expenditure rose over 21% year-on-year to Rs 168.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 138.7 crore in the year-ago quarter. The faster growth in expenses compared with revenue led to an 85% increase in losses to Rs 17.6 crore, which included Rs 1.3 crore in exceptional items.

title: Bijnis rebrands as Zorit, raises Rs 27 Cr led by Sparrow Capital
description: The angel investors include Anupam Mittal, founder of Shaadi.com, the founders of Shiprocket, Mohit Sardana, CEO of Xpressbees, and Sarthak Misra of SoftBank.
body: B2B quick commerce startup Zorit, formerly known as Bijnis, has raised nearly Rs 27 crore ($2.84 million) in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital. Existing investors Info Edge and WaterBridge participated in the round, along with Better Capital, angel investors and employees.
The angel investors include Anupam Mittal, founder of Shaadi.com, the founders of Shiprocket, Mohit Sardana, CEO of Xpressbees, and Sarthak Misra of SoftBank.

Following the investment, Info Edge’s shareholding in Bijnis will increase to 20.12% on a fully converted and diluted basis. In a stock exchange disclosure earlier this week, Info Edge said it may also acquire additional equity in the company through a secondary transaction.

Founded in 2015 by Siddharth Vij, Chaitanya Rathi, Siddharth Rastogi and Sachin Chauhan, Zorit initially operated as a B2B marketplace connecting manufacturers with retailers. The company transitioned to an inventory led quick commerce model in late 2024.

Zorit enables offline retailers to source inventory from locally stocked dark stores, with deliveries in as little as 60 minutes. The platform operates 12 dark stores across 12 cities and has reached Rs 120 crore in annualised sales. Nearly 50% of its dark stores have achieved break even, including the cost of liquidating unsold inventory.

According to the company, nearly 60% of its retailers had never used an online B2B platform before. Retailer retention beyond the sixth month has improved fourfold compared with its previous model, while monthly ordering frequency has increased fivefold. Retailers place an average of five to six orders per month, with top cohorts exceeding 10 orders.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its quick commerce infrastructure, expand its product assortment and deepen retailer engagement across its operating markets.

“We strongly believe that a substantial part of India’s future commerce will remain retailer led. As consumer expectations evolve, retailers need better technology and supply chain infrastructure to compete and grow,” said Siddharth Vij, CEO of Zorit.

title: Astrotalk’s profit jumps 10X to Rs 222 Cr in FY26; overseas biz grows 2.6X
description: Astrotalk’s net profit after tax surged more than 10-fold to Rs 222 crore in FY26, as revenue grew by 55% year-on-year to cross Rs 1,800 crore
body: Astrology and spiritual wellness platform Astrotalk’s net profit surged more than 10-fold to Rs 222 crore in FY26, as revenue grew 55% year-on-year to cross Rs 1,800 crore. International markets drove a significant share of this growth, with overseas revenue growing 2.6 times.
The expansion came alongside a sharp increase in advertising and expenses, which more than doubled to Rs 823 crore as the Noida-based company invested in its growth.
The firm’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,823 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,176 crore in FY25, according to its audited financial statements.

Astrotalk operates a digital astrology platform that connects users with astrologers for paid consultations via chat, calls and video. Revenue from consultations rose 45% to Rs 1,657 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,139 crore in FY25, and accounted for around 91% of operating revenue.

International revenue surged 2.6 times to Rs 621 crore from Rs 236 crore, with its share of total revenue at 34% against 20% a year earlier. Revenue from India rose 28% to Rs 1,202 crore, while international markets added Rs 385 crore of new revenue during the year, more than half of Astrotalk’s total revenue growth.

Beyond consultations, Astrotalk has expanded into e-commerce through Astrotalk Store, which sells certified Rudraksha, gemstones, crystals and Vastu products via its own platform and marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart and Blinkit. Revenue from the segment jumped 4.4 times to Rs 166 crore in FY26 from Rs 37 crore in FY25.

Commenting on the expansion, Puneet Gupta, founder and CEO of Astrotalk, said, “We set out to build a diversified, global business from India, and FY26 shows it is working. A third of our revenue now comes from outside India, and Astrotalk Store has grown into a real second business.”

Looking at the expenses, advertising and business promotion expenses more than doubled to Rs 823 crore from Rs 337 crore, accounting for 52.2% of total expenses, as Astrotalk ramped up marketing to support its growth. Legal and professional expenses rose 6.8% to Rs 550 crore from Rs 515 crore, which includes payments to astrologers for consultations

title: Meesho posts Rs 4,132 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; narrows losses by 68%
description: E-commerce marketplace Meesho reported a 34% year on year increase in revenue, while its losses narrowed sharply by 68% to Rs 132 crore during the same period.
body: E-commerce marketplace Meesho has announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 34% year on year increase in revenue, while its losses narrowed sharply by 68% to Rs 132 crore during the same period.

The company’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 4,132 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 3,074 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements filed with the NSE.

Meesho did not disclose its revenue breakdown in the quarterly financial statements. The company reported Rs 127 crore in non-operating income, which took its total income to Rs 4,259 crore in the quarter ended September 2026.
On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue from operations rose 11% from Rs 3,713 crore in Q1 FY27.

Meesho did not disclose most of its expenses in the quarterly financial statements. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 281 crore in Q2 FY27, an 18% increase from Rs 237 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Its depreciation expense stood at Rs 20 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenses grew 24% year on year to Rs 4,382 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 3,540 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the segment level, Meesho’s marketplace business reported an EBITDA loss of Rs 130 crore, while its new initiatives segment posted an EBITDA loss of Rs 42 crore on revenue of Rs 11.6 crore.
At the bottom line, Meesho narrowed its losses by 68% year-on-year to Rs 132 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 411 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year.

title: Let’s Game Now raises Rs 30 Cr led by Anand Mahindra and Bestvantage Investments
description: Founded in 2018 by Santanu Basu, Let’s Game Now is an Indian esports and gaming tournament platform that connects brands with gamers. The company hosts online
body: Let’s Game Now, a gaming and esports company, has raised Rs 30 crore in a funding round co-led by Anand Mahindra and Bestvantage Investments, with participation from a UAE-based family office.
The fresh funds will be used to accelerate the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), Let’s Game Now said in a press release.

Founded in 2018 by Santanu Basu, Let’s Game Now is an Indian esports and gaming tournament platform that connects brands with gamers. The company hosts online tournaments, organises large-scale offline events and provides live broadcasting services across South Asia and Southeast Asia.
The company claims to have a total reach of over 50 million, with more than 2,000 events organised, over 30 clients served and a presence in 18 countries.
Let’s Game Now’s community includes over 1.4 million members, around 387.9K YouTube subscribers, 193.3K Discord members and 40K Instagram followers. It also has a database of over 100K gamers.
The company has a grassroots presence across more than 400 colleges in over 80 cities, reaching more than 700K students. Its campus network includes over 20 events and more than 30 club partnerships.
According to market research, the Indian gaming market is valued at approximately $3.8 billion and is projected to reach $9.2 billion by FY29.

title: AI enterprise startup QwikBuild raises $2.3 Mn in pre-seed round
description: de the raise, QwikBuild announced a joint venture with Globalway Inc, a publicly listed Japanese company, to drive its expansion into Japan’s enterprise market.
body: QwikBuild, an enterprise AI startup that builds bespoke software and AI agents for business operations, has raised $2.3 million in pre-seed funding. The startup is backed by Globalway Inc., Blume Ventures, Marsshot, and DeVC, alongside prominent angel investors including Lalit Keshre (founder of Groww) and Ankit Nagori (founder of Cure.fit).
Alongside the raise, QwikBuild announced a joint venture with Globalway Inc, a publicly listed Japanese company, to drive its expansion into Japan’s enterprise market.

Launched last year by Pradeep Ayyagari, QwikBuild is an enterprise AI platform that lets businesses build bespoke, enterprise-grade software & AI agents in days rather than months. Using AI agents, it turns manual operations into production-ready applications that organisations own and control.

The Bengaluru-based startup addresses the gap of manual processes by using autonomous AI agents; it builds bespoke, enterprise-grade software in days rather than months. The platform meets businesses exactly where they are through three paths: replacing a legacy system entirely, building a custom layer on top of existing tools like SAP and Salesforce, or building from scratch

Built to work alongside existing enterprise systems, including SAP. QwikBuild helps businesses modernise workflows, streamline and unlock the AI agent era for their operations. It said that its platform is already in use by enterprises across the US, Singapore, India, with clients like Asia’s largest electronics component exporter that now runs its shipment and supply-chain on software and AI agents.

Through this combination of AI-driven development, enterprise integrations and Managed agents stack, QwikBuild aims to help businesses in their AI transformation journey by modernising their operations around their core systems, without the time and complexity of traditional custom software projects.

title: Info Edge’s PAT rises 87% to Rs 650 Cr in Q2 FY27; other income at Rs 428 Cr
description: Info Edge’s bottom line was significantly boosted by other income of Rs 428 crore in Q2 FY27, which contributed significantly to its consolidated profit of Rs 650 crore.
body: Info Edge, the parent company of Naukri, reported a 87.1% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 650 crore in Q2 FY27. Its consolidated revenue from operations also rose 12.2% to Rs 904 crore during the quarter, up from Rs 806 crore a year ago.

Info Edge’s bottom line was significantly boosted by other income of Rs 428 crore in Q2 FY27, which contributed significantly to its consolidated profit of Rs 650 crore. Against revenue from operations of Rs 904 crore, the other income played a key role in driving profitability, which shows the contribution of returns from its financial investments alongside its core business operations.

The company’s total expenses increased 4.1% to Rs 587 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 564 crore a year ago. The slower growth in expenses compared to revenue helped the company improve its profitability during the quarter.
On a standalone basis, Info Edge’s revenue from operations grew 12.8% to Rs 842 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 746 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.

On a consolidated basis, its recruitment business, which operates through Naukri, remained the largest revenue contributor, with revenue rising to Rs 653 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 582 crore a year ago.

Its real estate platform 99acres reported revenue of Rs 134 crore during the quarter. Meanwhile, the company’s other businesses, including Jeevansathi and Shiksha, reported combined revenue of Rs 116 crore, compared to Rs 109 crore in the year-ago period.
Moreover, Info Edge’s board declared an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share for FY27. The record date has been set as November 6, 2026, and the dividend will be paid on or after November 23.

According to a separate filing, Info Edge has approved a fresh investment of Rs 150 crore in its wholly-owned subsidiary Redstart Labs (India) Ltd. The investment will be made in cash across one or more tranches over the next 18 months to meet working capital requirements, fund new technology investments and cover general corporate needs.

title: CarTrade posts Rs 213 Cr revenue and Rs 66 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
description: Automobile classifieds platform CarTrade reported a moderate growth of 10% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, while profits remained stable at Rs 66 crore during the period.
body: Automobile classifieds platform CarTrade released its financial results for the second quarter of FY27 and reported a moderate growth of 10% year-on-year in revenue, while profits remained stable at Rs 66 crore during the period.

CarTrade’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 213.1 crore in Q2 FY27 in contrast to Rs 193.4 crore in Q2 FY26, as per the firm’s unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
On a sequential basis, its revenue rose marginally by 6% during the quarter from Rs 201.2 crore in Q1 FY27.

The Mumbai-based company operates across three segments: Consumer, Remarketing, and Classifieds (OLX India). The Consumer segment accounted for over 37% of total operating revenue, with income of Rs 79.5 crore in Q2 FY27, while the Remarketing and Classifieds (OLX India) segments generated Rs 70.3 crore and Rs 70.2 crore, respectively, before the elimination of Rs 6.9 crore in intersegment revenue.
OLX India recorded a 26% year-on-year increase in revenue and a 36% rise in EBITDA during the quarter.
The company also earned Rs 23 crore from interest on bank deposits, gains from the fair valuation of financial assets and other sources. This took its total income to Rs 236.2 crore in Q2 FY27.

For the first half of FY27, CarTrade reported a 13% year-on-year increase in operating income to Rs 414.3 crore from Rs 366.5 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit also rose over 10% to Rs 122.9 crore during the same period, while EBITDA increased 30% to Rs 139 crore.

CarTrade’s employee benefit expenses accounted for over 55% of its total expenditure and rose 8% year-on-year to Rs 83.7 crore in Q2 FY27. Including finance costs, depreciation and amortisation, and other expenses, the company’s total expenditure increased 6% to Rs 150.8 crore during the quarter from Rs 142.2 crore in Q2 FY26.

title: HealthKart crosses Rs 2,000 Cr revenue in FY26, PBT rises 30%
description: As HealthKart reportedly gears up for its IPO, the health supplement brand appears to be building the financial profile investors look for in a public market candidate.
body: As HealthKart reportedly gears up for its IPO, the health supplement brand appears to be building the financial profile investors look for in a public market candidate: strong revenue growth, scale and sustained profitability. The company crossed the Rs 2,000 crore revenue mark in FY26, while its profit before tax increased 30% during the year.
HealthKart’s revenue from operations rose 56.2% to Rs 2,052 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,313 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated annual statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
The company owns and operates a portfolio of nutrition and wellness brands, including MuscleBlaze, The Protein Zone, TrueBasics, HK Vitals, bGreen, Nouriza and Gritzo.

Sales of products remained the main revenue driver, accounting for nearly 99% of operating revenue. Product sales increased 59.2% to Rs 2,033 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,279 crore in the previous fiscal year. The company also earns revenue from services and other activities. Including other income of Rs 54 crore, its total income rose to Rs 2,106 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,368 crore in FY25.

The growth, however, came alongside a rise in expenses. Procurement remained HealthKart’s largest cost, increasing 71.9% to Rs 1,071 crore in FY26 from Rs 623 crore in FY25. The company also stepped up its spending on advertising and marketing, which rose 53.2% to Rs 403 crore during the year.
Employee benefits, commissions, freight and other overheads pushed total expenses up 55.7% to Rs 1,982 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,273 crore in FY25.

Despite the increase in costs, HealthKart’s revenue growth helped it improve its profitability. Its profit before tax, excluding exceptional items, rose by 30% to Rs 124 crore in FY26 from Rs 95 crore in FY25/

The combination of a larger revenue base and positive earnings could be an important part of HealthKart’s IPO story, particularly as investors assess whether consumer brands can sustain growth while managing marketing and procurement costs. The company’s ability to maintain profitability while expanding its portfolio will remain a key factor in assessing its financial performance.

title: Exclusive: Dainik Bhaskar family office invests in spiritual tech startup Vama
description: Vama has raised Rs 19.03 crore (approximately $2.1 million) in an ongoing Pre-Series A funding round led by the family office of Dainik Bhaskar.
body: Spiritual tech startup Vama has raised Rs 19.03 crore (approximately $2.1 million) in an ongoing Pre-Series A funding round led by Writers and Publishers Private Limited, the family office of Dainik Bhaskar. The round also saw participation from Wavemaker Partners, Silver Needle Ventures, Harit Nagpal, MD and CEO of Tata Play, Swati Parikh, Vinay Mittal and Nikhil Bhandarkar.
According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Vama allotted 3,452 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 55,134.39 per share, aggregating to Rs 19.03 crore.
The round appears to be ongoing, with the Delhi based company likely to raise additional capital in subsequent tranches.

Dainik Bhaskar’s family office led the round with an investment of Rs 12.50 crore, while the remaining Rs 6.53 crore came from the other investors, including Wavemaker Partners, Silver Needle Ventures, Harit Nagpal, Swati Parikh, Vinay Mittal and Nikhil Bhandarkar.
Vama could be among the first recorded startup investments by the Dainik Bhaskar family office.
As per Entrackr’s estimates, the funding values Vama at around Rs 180 crore, a 20% increase from its previous Pre-Series A round, which valued the company at Rs 150 crore.

Founded in 2020 by Acharya Dev and Manu Jain, Vama provides devotees access to temple services, astrology consultations and spiritual products through its platform. Temple services account for around 70% of its revenue, while astrology and Vama Mall contribute the rest.
Dainik Bhaskar’s presence across Hindi speaking markets could help Vama expand its reach and strengthen its access to temples and other service providers.

title: Skincare brand CHOSEN raises extended Series A round from Wellbeing Nutrition founders
description: In 2026, CHOSEN Sculpt became India's first topical lower face contouring serum, backed by a 12 week clinical study involving Indian women published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology.
body: Skincare brand CHOSEN has raised an extension of its Series A round from Avnish Chhabria and Saurabh Kapoor, founders of Wellbeing Nutrition.

Prior to this, the Chennai based startup had raised $5 million in a Series A round led by Fireside Ventures in May this year. The round also saw participation from BOLD, L’Oréal’s corporate venture capital fund, Alkemi Growth Capital and other angel investors. CHOSEN had previously raised $1.2 million in an angel funding round in 2024.

The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its R&D capabilities and expand its formulation pipeline across topical skincare and nutraceuticals, with a focus on clinical validation and dermatological research, CHOSEN said in a press release.

Founded in 2020 by Renita Rajan, CHOSEN develops skincare products for melanin rich Indian skin. Its approach draws on the science of the exposome, which examines how environmental factors affect skin health, and focuses on four areas of ageing: pigmentation, skin texture, facial contour and hair ageing.

The company plans to establish a Centre of Excellence to involve dermatologists in product development and research. It also plans to expand its R&D, brand and growth teams as it enters its next phase of expansion.

CHOSEN’s portfolio spans more than 50 products across skincare, haircare, body care and nutraceuticals. Its products are prescribed by more than 2,000 doctors. In 2026, CHOSEN Sculpt became India's first topical lower face contouring serum, backed by a 12 week clinical study involving Indian women published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology .

The company sells its products through its website and platforms such as Amazon, Myntra, Swiggy, FirstClub and Distacart. It serves most serviceable pin codes in India, with Chennai, Coimbatore, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Pune, Ahmedabad and Goa among its priority markets.
CHOSEN also ships to international markets, including the US, the UK, Australia, Canada, the UAE, Singapore, France, Sweden, Portugal, the Czech Republic, Hong Kong and Thailand.

title: Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre raises Rs 28 Cr in Series A round led by Alkemi
description: agruti plans to expand to over 40 centres and more than 4,000 beds across Tier I and Tier II cities over the next three to four years. The organisation claims to have t
body: Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre, a provider of mental health, addiction and dementia care services, has raised Rs 28 crore in a Series A funding round led by Alkemi Growth Capital.

The fresh funds will be used to enter new geographies, expand clinical and staff capacity, develop specialised care programmes, and deepen insurance and corporate partnerships, Jagruti said in a press release.

The funding comes amid growing demand for structured mental health and rehabilitation services in India. However, the sector remains fragmented, with care largely delivered through standalone clinics and smaller independent establishments.

Founded by Amar Shinde, Vijaya Shinde and Hemant Shinde, Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre provides residential care for mental health conditions, addiction and dementia. The Pune-based organisation operates more than 19 centres across nine cities, with over 1,600 beds and a team of more than 40 doctors.

Jagruti plans to expand to over 40 centres and more than 4,000 beds across Tier I and Tier II cities over the next three to four years. The organisation claims to have treated more than 82,000 individuals.

Its centres are spread across cities including Pune, Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Chennai. The organisation offers programmes for mental health conditions, addiction and substance use disorders, and neurological care.

The investment expands Alkemi Growth Capital's exposure to healthcare delivery and adjacent segments. Its portfolio includes Redcliffe Labs in diagnostics, Medvital in medical devices, Datar Cancer Genetics in in-vitro diagnostics (IVD), Medulance in emergency medical response, Alphadroid in autonomous mobility robots, and Leumas in physical AI for pharmaceutical manufacturing.
Jagruti is Alkemi's first investment in the mental health and rehabilitation segment of healthcare delivery.

title: Docterz raises Rs 5 Cr from Vineeta Singh, Avnish Anand and 20 doctor-investors
description: Around 20 doctor users contributed nearly Rs 3 crore, accounting for about 60% of the total funding. The investor group also includes Vineeta Singh, co-founder and CEO of SUGAR Cosmetics, and others.
body: Docterz, a healthcare technology startup founded by paediatrician Dr Atish Laddad, has raised Rs 5 crore from around 35 investors, including doctors who use its platform.

Around 20 doctor users contributed nearly Rs 3 crore, accounting for about 60% of the total funding. The investor group also includes Vineeta Singh, co-founder and CEO of SUGAR Cosmetics, and Avnish Anand, co-founder and former CEO of CaratLane.

The company plans to use the funds to expand organically, explore acquisitions and develop AI tools for doctors. It also aims to expand its reach among independent practitioners, smaller clinics and healthcare organisations across India.

Founded over a decade ago, Docterz offers an integrated platform for electronic medical records, appointments, billing, vaccination management and patient engagement. Its technology supports more than 5,000 doctors across India, with a strong presence in paediatrics.
The company is also developing AI-enabled tools to help doctors with documentation, administrative workflows, practice data analysis and patient follow-ups.
Dr Dhananjay Sangle, a paediatrician and Docterz investor, said his decision to invest was based on his experience using the platform for several years and his confidence in its founder.
Vineeta Singh said customer participation in a funding round was a strong signal for a business, adding that doctors investing in Docterz reflected their trust in the platform and its founder.

Dr Suhas Warad, another paediatrician and investor in the company, said technology designed around doctors’ needs could help them manage their practices more efficiently and devote more time to patient care.

title: Physical AI startup Tensrai raises Rs 3.4 Cr in pre-seed round
description: The startup is targeting applications such as autonomous material handling and cleaning across factories, warehouses, airports, hospitals, shopping malls and commercial
body: Hyderabad-based Physical AI startup Tensrai has raised Rs 3.4 crore in a pre-seed funding  from India Accelerator, Finvolve, Hyderabad Angels and other angels.

The fresh capital will be used to accelerate technology development, strengthen engineering and deployment capabilities, and support expansion into domestic and international markets, Tensrai said in a press release.

Co-founded by Sai Nikhil Rao Gona, Venkata Sai Charan Chalamalasetty, Harshith Uppalapati, and Vivek Datta, Tensrai is developing a unified, retrofittable autonomy platform that enables industrial and commercial robots, vehicles and machines to perform physical tasks autonomously.

The platform combines vision-first navigation, AI-based localisation, vision-language model (VLM)-powered reasoning, autonomous mobility, robotic arm manipulation and vision-language-action (VLA)-based teach-and-deploy capabilities. The technology is designed to help machines perceive their surroundings, reason through tasks, learn skills and execute operations with limited human intervention.

Tensrai aims to bring autonomous capabilities to both purpose-built machines and existing equipment through retrofitting, potentially reducing the cost and complexity of adopting robotics across industrial and commercial settings.

The startup is targeting applications such as autonomous material handling and cleaning across factories, warehouses, airports, hospitals, shopping malls and commercial campuses. It is also developing a general-purpose mobile manipulator that combines autonomous mobility with robotic arms to perform tasks across material handling, cleaning, manufacturing and construction.

Tensrai plans to generate revenue through multiple streams, including robot sales, autonomy retrofitting, Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) and customised solutions. It also plans to expand into international markets.

The funding comes amid growing interest in Physical AI, which combines artificial intelligence with robotic systems and machines to enable them to understand and interact with the physical world. Unlike software-based AI applications, Physical AI systems are designed to translate perception and reasoning into real-world actions.

title: BlackBuck’s Q2 FY27 revenue jumps 56% to Rs 235 Cr, profit grows 42%
description: BlackBuck reported a 56% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27, while its net profit grew 42%. The company’s core truck operator services business
body: Digital trucking platform BlackBuck reported a 56% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27, while its net profit grew 42%. The company’s core truck operator services business accounted for almost all operating revenue, while its lending business remained a smaller contributor. However, total expenses rose faster than revenue, while a lower tax outgo helped boost net profit during the quarter.

BlackBuck’s consolidated revenue from operations rose to Rs 235 crore in the quarter ended September 2026 from the corresponding period last year, according to its unaudited financial results filed with BSE.

The Bengaluru-based company operates a digital platform for truck operators and fleet owners, with services spanning trucking operations and lending. Its truck operator services business includes its core logistics platform, while the lending segment provides a separate revenue stream.

Truck operator services generated Rs 232 crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 148.7 crore a year earlier. The segment contributed nearly 99% of operating revenue. Revenue from the lending business increased to Rs 3.4 crore from Rs 2.8 crore, but the segment continued to report a loss of Rs 1.7 crore, compared with Rs 77.5 lakh in the year-ago quarter.

BlackBuck’s total expenses increased 64% to Rs 210 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 128 crore. Other expenses, which include various operating costs, rose to Rs 141 crore from Rs 72.9 crore. Employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 45 crore from Rs 42 crore, while depreciation and amortisation more than doubled to Rs 24.5 crore from Rs 12.4 crore.

Despite the increase in expenses, profit before tax rose 10% to Rs 42.8 crore from Rs 38.9 crore. Net profit increased to Rs 41.4 crore from Rs 29.2 crore, helped by a lower tax expense during the quarter.

For the first half of FY27, BlackBuck’s operating revenue grew 49% to Rs 439.5 crore from Rs 295 crore in the corresponding period last year. Net profit rose 33% to Rs 84 crore from Rs 63 crore. As of 3 PM today, BlackBuck’s shares were trading at Rs 568.40, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 10,413 crore

title: Coratia Technologies raises Rs 18 Cr in bridge round led by MGF Kavachh
description: The fresh funds will be used to execute its Rs 66 crore contract with the Indian Navy under the iDEX initiative, accelerate R&D on new products, strengthen its underwater
body: Coratia Technologies, a deep-tech company developing advanced underwater robotic systems, has raised Rs 18 crore in a bridge round led by MGF Kavachh.
The Odisha-based startup had earlier raised Rs 17 crore from MGF Kavachh, Piper and SIDBI in a pre-Series A round.

The fresh funds will be used to execute its Rs 66 crore contract with the Indian Navy under the iDEX initiative, accelerate R&D on new products, strengthen its underwater robotics capabilities and scale manufacturing and deployment for defence and critical infrastructure applications, the company said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2021 by Debendra Pradhan and Biswajit Swain, Coratia develops indigenous underwater robotic systems that combine advanced engineering and technology miniaturisation to operate in challenging underwater environments. Its flagship product, Jalasimha UWROV, has achieved Technology Readiness Level 9 (TRL-9), providing a foundation for further product development and deployment.

Coratia's clients and partners include the Indian Navy, Indian Oil, Indian Railways, Tata Steel, Hindalco Industries, Steel Authority of India (SAIL), Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited, Jindal Steel and Power, and NIT Rourkela, among others.
Beyond defence, Coratia's technology has applications across dams and reservoirs, ports, bridges, pipelines, offshore assets, ship infrastructure and subsea communication networks.

title: Shadowfax Q2 FY27 profit balloons 5.2X to Rs 68 Cr, revenue grows 57%
description: Logistics and delivery services firm Shadowfax reported a five-fold increase in quarterly profit to Rs 68 crore in Q2 FY27, steered by higher operating revenue and improved cost efficiency.
body: Logistics and delivery services firm Shadowfax reported a five-fold increase in quarterly profit to Rs 68 crore in Q2 FY27, steered by higher operating revenue and improved cost efficiency. The Bengaluru-based firm also maintained its growth momentum in the first half of the fiscal year, with revenue rising over 56% and profit increasing more than sixfold.

Shadowfax’s revenue from operations grew 56.6% to Rs 1,538 crore in the quarter ended September 2026 from Rs 982 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its unaudited consolidated financial results.

The company provides logistics and last-mile delivery services to e-commerce platforms and businesses. Its operations cover logistics and delivery services, which it reports under a single business segment.

Employee benefit expenses increased over 55% to Rs 138 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 89 crore in Q2 FY26. Finance costs more than doubled to Rs 10 crore, while depreciation and amortisation expenses rose 65.4% to Rs 46.3 crore, indicating higher costs associated with its operating infrastructure.

Most of Shadowfax’s expenses fell under the “other expenses” category, which accounted for nearly 87% of its total costs at Rs 1,296 crore. These costs likely included logistics operations and delivery partner payouts.
Overall, Shadowfax’s quarterly expenditure grew 53.7% to Rs 1,490.2 crore.
The company reported a profit of Rs 68 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 13 crore in the year-ago quarter. Profit also increased marginally from Rs 65 crore in the preceding June quarter.
For the first half of FY27, Shadowfax’s operating revenue rose 60.4% to Rs 2,896 crore in H1 FY26. Its profit increased to Rs 133.35 crore from Rs 21.03 crore.

title: CureSkin posts Rs 133 Cr revenue and Rs 35 Cr loss in FY26
description: CureSkin improved its financial performance in FY26, with higher revenue from product sales and services and lower advertising and promotional costs helping reduce its
body: Skincare and dermatology startup CureSkin improved its financial performance in FY26, with higher revenue from product sales and services and lower advertising and promotional costs helping reduce its losses.
The firm’s revenue from operations grew 27.9% to Rs 133 crore in FY26, according to its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies.

The Bengaluru-based company offers personalised skincare and haircare solutions through digital consultations and products recommended for individual skin and hair concerns. Its business combines product sales with services, including dermatology-led consultations.

Product sales remained its primary revenue source, accounting for about 91% of operating revenue. Revenue from products increased 17.1% to Rs 120.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 103 crore in FY25. Revenue from services, meanwhile, rose nearly ninefold to Rs 12.4 crore, albeit on a smaller base. The increase points to a larger contribution from services, although product sales continued to account for most of the business.
The firm also reported Rs 1 crore in other income, taking total revenue to Rs 134 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 108 crore a year earlier.

CureSkin’s advertising and promotional spend fell by 17.6% to Rs 61 crore in FY26 from Rs 74 crore a year earlier, reducing one of its major cost heads. The decline helped bring down overall expenditure despite higher spending on materials and other operating costs.

The cost of materials consumed increased 15.4% to Rs 42 crore, broadly tracking the rise in product sales. Employee benefit expenses, however, declined 5.3% to Rs 23.6 crore from Rs 24.9 crore, adding to the savings from lower promotional spending.

Among the remaining cost heads, transportation expenses increased 30% to Rs 13 crore, while legal and professional charges fell 36.5% to Rs 7.2 crore. Miscellaneous expenses rose 14.8% to Rs 22.2 crore from Rs 19 crore.

title: Venttup raises $3 Mn in pre Series A round led by Rainmatter, Unicorn India Ventures
description: According to the Bengaluru-based startup, its capabilities span precision machining, casting and forging, sheet metal fabrication, box builds, special purpose machines,
body: Industries 5.0 startup Venttup has raised $3 million in a pre Series A funding round led by Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, and Unicorn India Ventures. The startup was incubated at Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM).
Venttup had previously raised a seed round from Unicorn India Ventures in September 2024.

The fresh capital will be used to expand the engineering team, invest in precision manufacturing facilities and rapid prototyping infrastructure, and adopt AI to improve B2B sourcing, supplier intelligence and operational efficiency, the company said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Sandeep Nair, M. Wasim Ankli and Joseph Panakkal, Venttup is a B2B manufacturing company focused on the localisation and development of critical and precision components and subassemblies.

Through its Manufacturing as a Service (MaaS) model, the company supports customers across engineering design, specification standardisation, rapid prototyping, testing, validation and contract manufacturing.

According to the Bengaluru-based startup, its capabilities include precision machining, casting and forging, sheet metal fabrication, box builds, special purpose machines, industrial automation, robotics and technology-enabled B2B sourcing. It combines in-house engineering capabilities with a network of MSME manufacturing partners to serve sectors such as energy, data centres, mobility, defence, aerospace and space.

Venttup is also setting up a manufacturing facility in Bengaluru to strengthen its rapid prototyping and precision manufacturing capabilities. The facility will support precision machining, turning and sheet metal production for applications in energy transition, defence, aerospace and space. It is expected to help shorten the time from component development and validation to production readiness and mass manufacturing.

The company said it grew fivefold to Rs 10 crore in FY26. Over the past 12 months, it has added more than 15 large companies to its customer base and built a business opportunity pipeline of around Rs 30 crore across new energy, mobility and smart infrastructure.

title: Pine Labs crosses Rs 800 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; profit jumps 6.5X
description: Pine Labs reported a 24% YoYincrease in operating revenue to over Rs 800 crore in Q2 FY27, while its net profit surged 6.5 times to Rs 39 crore during the quarter.
body: Fintech major Pine Labs announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (Q2 FY27) today. The company reported a 24% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to over Rs 800 crore, while its net profit surged 6.5 times to Rs 39 crore during the quarter.
Pine Labs’ revenue from operations grew to Rs 806 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 650 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Pine Labs’ digital infrastructure and transaction platform remained its largest revenue contributor, with revenue growing 21% year-on-year to Rs 532 crore in Q2 FY27, which accounted for 66% of its total operating revenue. Meanwhile, its issuing and acquiring platform recorded 31% growth to Rs 275 crore during the same period.
The company added Rs 26 crore from non-operating activities, taking its total income to Rs 832 crore in Q2 FY27.
Employee benefits remained the largest cost centre for Pine Labs, accounting for around 35% of its overall expenditure. This cost remained flat at Rs 268 crore during the quarter.

The cost of materials, which includes the cost of POS machines, stood at Rs 116 crore in Q2 FY27, while transaction and related costs rose 45% to Rs 103 crore during the quarter. Overall, the company’s total expenditure increased 16% to Rs 770 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 662 crore in Q2 FY26.
Pine Labs’ improved profitability came as revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses, with net profit surging 6.5 times to Rs 39 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 6 crore in Q2 FY26.
For H1 FY27, the firm reported a 22% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 1,543 crore while profits jumped nearly 16X to Rs 99 crore.

title: Nutrition startup Ace Blend raises $9.91 Mn led by 3one4 Capital
description: Ace Blend, a nutrition startup, has raised $9.91 million in a Series A2 funding round led by 3one4 Capital. Snippets.
body: Ace Blend, a nutrition startup, has raised $9.91 million in a Series A2 funding round led by 3one4 Capital, with existing investor Fireside Ventures doubling down on its investment.
Fireside Ventures had previously led the company’s $3.3 million pre-Series A round.
The fresh capital will support research-led product development and the launch of new nutrition formats.
The company claims that it grew 300% in FY26, while more than 46% of its customers returned to make repeat purchases.

Founded by Shivam Hingorani, Ace Blend began selling its products in 2018. Saif Mehkri joined as co-founder in 2022, bringing nearly three decades of experience in the nutrition industry. The company operates an integrated supply chain covering ingredient sourcing, formulation and manufacturing.

Ace Blend develops nutritional products based on clinical evidence, focusing on nutrient forms, dosages and delivery methods. Its portfolio covers heart health, immunity, sleep, recovery and brain health.
The company also works with global ingredient suppliers DSM and TCI, which have granted it exclusive rights in India to certain technologies.

Its products are developed by an in-house clinical team and recommended by a network of more than 400 doctors. Clinical validation and automated testing are conducted independently by accredited laboratories in Europe.

title: Servify cuts losses to Rs 51 Cr in FY26; US contributes 60% of business
description: Post-sales service firm Servify’s revenue fell 4% year-on-year in FY26, amid continued degrowth in India, while its losses narrowed 40% to Rs 51 crore.
body: Post-sales service firm Servify reported a marginal 4% decline in revenue in FY26 (year ended March 2026), dragged by consecutive degrowth in its India business. However, the company made meaningful progress on the bottom line and narrowed losses by 40% to Rs 51 crore during the period.

Following a 16% increase in FY25, Servify’s revenue from operations declined to Rs 751 crore in FY26 from Rs 781 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its annual consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2015, Servify provides brand-authorised after-sales support for mobile phones, gadgets, electronics, and home appliances. The company has partnerships with major brands, including Apple, Bose, and HP, and operates across 18,000 service locations in more than 40 countries. It also processes over 2.8 lakh claims annually, according to its website.

White-labelled protection plans sold through mobile apps and web portals remain Servify’s primary revenue engine, which  contributed over 97% of total operating income. The segment declined 4% to Rs 730 crore in FY26. Income from mobile handset and spare parts sales also fell 13% to Rs 20 crore during the period.

For the second consecutive year, the US remained Servify’s largest market, which contributed nearly 60% of its total revenue at Rs 448 crore in FY26, a 12% year-on-year increase. In contrast, revenue from India declined 27% to Rs 242 crore from Rs 330 crore in FY25. The remaining revenue came from other markets, including Europe, Canada, the United Arab Emirates, and Turkey.

For the post sales firm, insurance premiums and repair expenses formed the bulk of Servify’s direct operating costs at Rs 439 crore in FY26, followed by commission expenses of Rs 82 crore. The remaining costs included courier charges, service and upcountry charges, and mobile handset consumption, which together totalled Rs 23 crore. Overall, direct operating costs declined 7% to Rs 555 crore during the fiscal year and accounted for 69% of total expenses.
The firm’s employee benefit expenses dropped 10.6% to Rs 135 crore in FY26 from Rs 151 crore in the previous fiscal year. These expenses included Rs 14 crore in employee stock option (ESOP) costs.

Information technology, legal and professional fees, depreciation and amortisation, along with other overheads, took Servify’s total expenses to Rs 807 crore in FY26, an 8% decrease from Rs 876 crore in FY25, in line with the decline in revenue.

title: Viridian Ingni Propulsion raises Rs 1.47 Cr in pre seed round led by IPV
description: Chennai based deeptech startup Viridian Ingni Propulsion has raised Rs 1.47 crore in a pre seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV).  Snippets
body: Chennai based deeptech startup Viridian Ingni Propulsion has raised Rs 1.47 crore in a pre seed funding round led by Inflection Point Ventures (IPV).
The company has also received Rs 53.75 lakh in grants from SIPCOT, MeitY Startup Hub, NIDHI PRAYAS, IIT Madras Research Park’s RTBI programme and Cummins CSR.
