Founded in February 2024 by Sriram G, the startup develops electric propulsion systems, including motors, controllers and firmware, for electric vehicles, drones, robotics and industrial machinery. It is incubated at IIT Madras Research Park.

The company will use the funds to move from validated prototypes to pilot production. The capital will support manufacturing tooling, setting up a pilot production line, ARAI and ICAT certification, motor controller firmware validation, hiring and working capital for initial customer deliveries.
Viridian develops different motor technologies for specific applications.

Its rare earth free ferrite PMa-SynRM motors are designed for e rickshaws, two wheelers, HVAC systems, compressors and solar pumps, while its permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSM) target drones, collaborative robots, automated guided vehicles and marine applications.
The startup has received letters of intent for 350 motors from two customers, Crop Xplore and Yali Mobility. It currently has a five member engineering team and is pre revenue.

title: ISLAND Beauty raises Rs 2.58 Cr from AJ VC to expand skincare range
description: ISLAND Beauty, a skincare brand that combines Korean ingredients with formulations tailored to Indian skin needs, has raised Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC. Snippets
body: ISLAND Beauty, a skincare brand that combines Korean ingredients with formulations tailored to Indian skin needs, has raised Rs 2.58 crore from AJ VC.
The proceeds will be used for product development, brand awareness and customer acquisition, the company said in a press release.
Founded in 2023 by Shirley Setia, Jinsoon Lee, Mayank Jain and Sakshi Jain, ISLAND Beauty focuses on barrier-focused skincare products designed for regular use.
The brand sources ingredients from South Korea and develops its formulations in India, with a focus on local weather conditions and consumers’ skincare needs.
ISLAND Beauty has developed its proprietary Core Barrier Matrix, which combines CBM-A Repair and CBM-B Defence. The formulation approach focuses on skin barrier repair and everyday defence.

Its current portfolio includes cleansers, toners, serums, moisturisers and lip care products. One of its offerings, the Dew Drop Barrier Repair Glow Serum, contains 50% Korean rice water and 5% niacinamide. The brand also offers a seven-day return policy, subject to its terms and conditions.
Over the next three years, ISLAND Beauty plans to expand its product portfolio and strengthen its market presence, while increasing awareness of barrier-focused skincare among consumers.

title: Kissht’s Q2 profit doubles to Rs 125 Cr, revenue jumps 45%
description: Digital lending platform Kissht reported a 44.7% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27 while its profit more than doubled during the quarter.
body: Digital lending platform Kissht reported a 44.7% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27 while its profit more than doubled during the quarter.

Kissht’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 732 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 506 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.

Founded by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, Kissht provides small-ticket consumer loans. The company has expanded its lending business through partnerships with merchants across categories such as electronics, fashion and travel. It primarily earns interest income from these loans.
The Mumbai-based company also reported Rs 8 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 740 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 518 crore a year ago.

On the expense side, impairment losses on financial instruments, which reflect provisions for potential loan losses, increased 9% year-on-year to Rs 133 crore from Rs 122 crore. Employee benefit expenses rose 38.8% to Rs 68 crore, while finance costs remained flat at Rs 72 crore.

Depreciation expenses declined 8.8% to Rs 5 crore, while other expenses surged 65.6% to Rs 308 crore. Overall, total expenses increased 35% to Rs 586 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 434 crore in the year-ago quarter.
At the bottom line, Kissht’s profit more than doubled to Rs 125 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 62.44 crore in Q2 FY26.

For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), Kissht’s operating revenue grew 44.6% to Rs 1,401 crore from Rs 969 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal year. Its profit rose 80.3% to Rs 220 crore from Rs 122 crore during the same period.

title: Freshworks acquires AI startup Robusta to strengthen IT operations platform
description: Software-as-a-service company Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta to strengthen its IT operations platform, Freshservice.  Snippets
body: Software-as-a-service company Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta to strengthen its IT operations platform, Freshservice.
The financial details of the acquisition were not disclosed.

Robusta helps businesses identify the causes of technology outages and recommend fixes using AI-based incident investigation technology. The acquisition will bring these capabilities to Freshservice, Freshworks’ IT service management platform.

The deal is aimed at helping organisations investigate incidents, identify the underlying causes of IT disruptions and resolve issues more efficiently. The integration is expected to expand Freshservice’s AI-driven IT operations capabilities.
Nasdaq-listed SaaS firm Freshworks reported a 16% year-on-year increase in revenue to $237.4 million in the second quarter ended June 2026.
The company posted a GAAP net profit of $3.2 million in Q2 CY26, compared to a net loss of $1.7 million in the corresponding quarter last year.

title: Delhivery reports Rs 3,066 Cr revenue and Rs 41 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
description: Delhivery reported a 19.8% year-on-year growth in revenue in the second quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q2 FY27) and remained profitable during the period.
body: Logistics company Delhivery reported a 19.8% year-on-year growth in revenue in the second quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q2 FY27) and remained profitable during the period.
Delhivery’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 3,066 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,559 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The company primarily generates revenue from its logistics services, including freight handling, transportation and warehousing. It also recorded other income of Rs 67 crore, taking its total income to Rs 3,133 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2,652 crore in Q2 FY26.

Freight, handling and servicing costs remained Delhivery’s largest expense, accounting for 70.97% of its total expenses. This cost increased 19.1% to Rs 2,195 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,843 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Employee benefit expenses increased 4.7% to Rs 446 crore from Rs 426 crore, while depreciation rose 11% to Rs 197.5 crore from Rs 178 crore. Finance costs declined 12.8% to Rs 34 crore, whereas other expenses remained largely flat at Rs 220 crore in Q2 FY27.
Overall, the company’s total expenses rose 14.2% to Rs 3,093 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,708 crore in Q2 FY26.

Delhivery posted a net profit of Rs 40.64 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a net loss of Rs 50.50 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company had also posted a profit of Rs 32 crore in the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q1 FY27).

On a half-yearly basis, Delhivery’s operating revenue grew 23.6% to Rs 5,997 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 4,853 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit increased 78.9% to Rs 72.55 crore from Rs 40.55 crore during the same period.

title: PB Fintech Q2 FY27 profit rises 43% to Rs 192 Cr, revenue up 35%
description: PB Fintech, reported a strong financial performance in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue registering a healthy year-on-year growth alongside a 43% increase in net profit
body: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, reported a strong financial performance in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue registering a healthy year-on-year growth alongside a 43% increase in net profit compared to the corresponding quarter last year. The company’s revenue from operations grew 35% to Rs 2,178 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,614 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the stock exchanges.

In terms of revenue composition, insurance broker services contributed Rs 2,015.19 crore to the company’s revenue, up 41.1% year on year from Rs 1,428.16 crore. Revenue from other services declined 12.3% to Rs 162.52 crore from Rs 185.39 crore.

On the expense front, Employee benefits, the company’s largest expense, increased 28.8% to Rs 773 crore. Advertising expenses surged 59.5% to Rs 447 crore, while network and internet costs jumped 65.1% to Rs 70.75 crore. Depreciation and amortisation stood at Rs 43.78 crore. Other expenses rose 21.8% to Rs 733 crore. Consequently, the company’s total expenses increased 32.6% to Rs 2,067.66 crore in Q2 FY27.

The Gurugram-based company’s net profit stood at Rs 193 crore, compared to Rs 135 crore in Q2 FY26. For the first half of FY27, the company’s revenue from operations increased 37.3% to Rs 4,066 crore, compared with Rs 2,962 crore in the corresponding period last year. Its profit after tax surged 61.4% to Rs 355 crore from Rs 220 crore in the same period. Since the end of Q1 FY27, PB Fintech’s share price has declined 38.3% to Rs 1,000 from Rs 1,620. Its market capitalisation also fell 37.2% to Rs 47,104 crore from Rs 74,957 crore during the same period.

title: Atomberg gets SEBI nod for proposed IPO
description: Atomberg Technologies has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).
body: Consumer appliances maker Atomberg Technologies has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 450 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 7.65 crore shares by existing shareholders. The company is yet to announce the price band and timeline for the issue.

Atomberg plans to use Rs 90 crore from the fresh issue proceeds to repay or prepay its borrowings. It will allocate Rs 150 crore towards brand awareness and performance marketing activities, while another Rs 100 crore will be used for research and development (R&D). The remaining amount will go towards general corporate purposes.

Founded in 2012 by Manoj Meena, who was joined by Sibabrata Das as co-founder in 2013, Atomberg initially focused on energy-efficient ceiling fans. It has since expanded its portfolio to include mixer grinders, water purifiers, cold-pressed juicers and other consumer appliances.

Apart from its consumer appliance business, the company also manufactures and supplies proprietary motors, controllers and other components to enterprise customers such as Voltas, Godrej and Blue Star through its subsidiary, Atomberg Innovations.

On the financial front, Atomberg's revenue from operations increased 34.8% to Rs 1,293.77 crore in FY26 from Rs 959.51 crore in FY25. However, its adjusted EBITDA declined to Rs 37.12 crore during the fiscal year from Rs 51.35 crore in FY25. The company reported a loss of Rs 148.88 crore in FY26, narrowing from Rs 199.08 crore in FY24.

Atomberg has also seen partial exits by existing investors ahead of its proposed listing. A91 Partners, which has backed the company since 2019, has sold shares worth around Rs 445 crore while retaining a 21% stake, according to the company's IPO disclosures.
ICICI Securities, Avendus Capital and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

title: Traya nears Rs 600 Cr revenue in FY26, posts Rs 29 Cr loss
description: What began as an attempt to address hair loss and the insecurities surrounding it among India’s youth has turned Traya into a nearly Rs 600 crore business.
body: What began as an attempt to address hair loss and the insecurities surrounding it among India’s youth has turned Traya into a nearly Rs 600 crore business. Yet, despite strong revenue growth in FY26, the seven-year-old haircare startup continued to report losses.
Traya's revenue from operations surged 72.6% year-on-year to Rs 585 crore in FY26 from Rs 339 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated annual financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

Founded in 2019, Traya focuses on addressing hair loss by identifying its root causes and provides personalised hair treatment plans supported by consultations with hair coaches and licensed physicians.

The sale of customised hair care kits was Traya's sole source of operating revenue. The company also earned Rs 8 crore through gains from the sale of investments, pushing its total income to Rs 593 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 343 crore in FY25.

On the cost side, advertising remained the largest expense, accounting for around 44% of the firm's total expenditure. Advertising costs nearly doubled to Rs 275 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, the cost of materials procured increased 68.7% to Rs 140 crore during the last fiscal year.

Traya spent Rs 81 crore on employee benefits in FY26. Its legal, transportation, technology and other overheads also catalyzed its total expenditure up 70.2% to Rs 623 crore in FY26 from Rs 366 crore in FY25.

Despite a 72.6% growth in operating revenue, the increase in expenses continued to weigh on the company's bottom line. Traya reported a net loss of Rs 29 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 23.5 crore in FY25.

At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.06 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at -44.7% and -6.19%, respectively. The company had total current assets of Rs 174 crore as of March 2026.

title: Qiroko raises Rs 1.5 Cr in pre-seed round led by ISV Capital
description: Qiroko, a Bengaluru-based fashion accessories brand, has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by ISV Capital, with participation from angel investors.
body: Qiroko, a Bengaluru-based fashion accessories brand, has raised Rs 1.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by ISV Capital, with participation from angel investors.

The startup will use the fresh capital for new product development, expansion into watches and bags, wider distribution across its direct-to-consumer (D2C) website, marketplaces and quick commerce platforms. It also plans to strengthen its team and build in-house brand and content capabilities.
Founded in 2025 by Shivam Vasisht and Ashwin Krithik, Qiroko offers everyday fashion accessories with a focus on affordable pricing and wearable designs.
Bootstrapped until this round, the startup claims to have achieved an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 6 crore within its first year of launch, along with strong unit economics.
The brand sells through its own website and marketplaces such as Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra, along with quick commerce platform Blinkit.
Qiroko aims to expand its product portfolio across jewellery, watches and bags.

title: Smartworks posts Rs 591 Cr revenue and Rs 26 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
description: Managed office space provider Smartworks posted a 39% year-on-year growth in revenue In Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, its EBITDA grew 37% to Rs 391 crore.
body: Managed office space provider Smartworks reported its financial results for the quarter ended September 2026 (Q2 FY27). The company posted a 39% year-on-year growth in revenue during the period. Meanwhile, its EBITDA grew 37% to Rs 391 crore.

Smartworks’ revenue from operations rose to Rs 591 crore in the Q2 FY27 from Rs 425 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

Smartworks derives the bulk of its operating revenue from the development, design and licensing of serviced office spaces, along with fit-out services and other ancillary offerings. The company also reported Rs 14 crore in non-operating income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 605 crore in Q2 FY27.
On a sequential basis, the firm’s operating revenue grew 8% from Rs 546 crore in Q1 FY27.

On the cost side, depreciation related to lease expenses was the largest expense for Smartworks at Rs 259 crore, up 31% from Rs 198 crore in Q2 FY26. This was followed by operating expenses, which stood at Rs 172 crore during the quarter. Employee benefits expenses amounted to Rs 28 crore. Finance costs and other overheads took the company’s total expenditure to Rs 570 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 445 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

At the bottom line, Smartworks continued its profitability on a quarter-on-quarter basis and turned profitable on a year-on-year basis, reporting a net profit of Rs 26 crore in Q2 FY27 compared to a net loss of Rs 3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Meanwhile its EBITDA grew 37% year-on-year to Rs 391 crore during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of over 66%.
For H1 FY27, Smartworks’ operating revenue grew 42% year-on-year to Rs 1,138 crore. The company also reported a net profit of Rs 39 crore, compared to a loss of Rs 7.3 crore in H1 FY26.

title: Decoding: Sachin Bansal retains 84.34% stake in Navi after Rs 940 Cr Prosus investment
description: According to Entrackr's estimates, Navi's valuation has more than tripled to Rs 13,192 crore from Rs 4,260 crore in its previous funding round in April 2020.
body: Fintech company Navi has announced a Rs 940 crore funding round led by Prosus at a valuation of Rs 13,192 crore. Founder Sachin Bansal continues to remain the company's largest shareholder, holding an 84.34% stake.

According to the company's regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , Navi has issued 23,94,29,444 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 39.26 per share, aggregating to approximately Rs 940 crore.
Prosus Ventures, through its subsidiary MIH Payments Holdings B.V., was the sole investor in the funding round.
According to Entrackr's estimates , Navi's valuation has more than tripled to Rs 13,192 crore from Rs 4,260 crore in its previous funding round in April 2020.

As per the filings, the company plans to use the equity capital to support business expansion, investments in subsidiaries and general corporate purposes, in line with the business plan agreed upon with the investor.

Founded by Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal, Navi operates across lending, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments. In March 2026, the company expanded its insurance portfolio with the launch of motor insurance.
In February 2025, Navi appointed Rajiv Naresh as CEO of Navi Technologies and Abhishek Dwivedi as CEO of Navi Finserv. Bansal moved to the role of executive chairman of the Navi Group.

Following the latest allotment, Prosus Ventures has emerged as Navi's largest external investor, with an 8.59% stake. Paresh Sukthankar, former deputy managing director of HDFC Bank, and Sangeeta Sukthankar collectively hold 0.21%, while Anand Rao, former co-founder of Navi Finserv, owns 0.08%.

title: Starbucks India brews Rs 1,367 Cr revenue in FY26; cuts losses by 27%
description: Tata Starbucks, the 50:50 joint venture between Tata and Starbucks Corp., has established itself as one of India’s largest coffee chains by revenue and store count.
body: Tata Starbucks, the 50:50 joint venture between Tata Consumer Products and Starbucks Corporation, has established itself as one of India’s largest coffee chains by revenue and store count. While the company has grown over the years, its bottom line remains in the red.

Starbucks’ revenue from operations grew a modest 7% year-on-year to Rs 1,367 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,277 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Incorporated in September 2011, the company operates cafes across India under the Starbucks brand. By 2025, Tata Starbucks had expanded to over 390 stores across 54 Indian cities, with approximately 4,300 partners (employees). Importantly, the company aims to expand its network to around 1,000 stores by 2028.

The sale of coffee and related products accounted for most of its revenue. The remaining income came from its loyalty programme, My Starbucks Rewards, through which customers earn loyalty points called Stars.

The procurement of coffee beans and other related products accounted for 24% of the company’s total expenditure. This cost increased 6% to Rs 356 crore in FY26 from Rs 336 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose 9.8% to Rs 225 crore during the same period.
Rent, electricity, advertising, freight and other overheads took total expenses up 4.7% to Rs 1,514 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,446 crore in FY25.
With controlled spending, Starbucks narrowed its net loss by 27% to Rs 99 crore in FY26 from Rs 136 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA stood at Rs 234 crore during the year.
At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.11 to earn every rupee of operating revenue. On a standalone basis, its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -2.6%, while its EBITDA margin was 17%.

title: Boba Bhai revenue and losses jump over two-fold in FY26
description: Bengaluru-based tea and beverage chain Boba Bhai more than doubled its revenue in the fiscal year ending March 2026, but its losses also widened as the
body: Bengaluru-based tea and beverage chain Boba Bhai more than doubled its revenue in the fiscal year ending March 2026, but its losses also widened as the Titan Capital-backed company expanded its operations and opened several dozen new stores.
The company’s revenue from operations spiked 139% to Rs 68 crore in FY26 from Rs 28.44 crore in the previous fiscal (FY25), according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

Food and beverage sales, the primary source of revenue, surged 137.1% to Rs 67.26 crore in FY26, accounting for 99% of the company’s operating revenue. Revenue from scrap sales also increased to Rs 28 lakh from Rs 7 lakh in the previous fiscal year. Additionally, the company reported Rs 1 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 69 crore in FY26 from Rs 29.44 crore in FY25.

When it comes to costs, Boba Bhai’s cost of materials consumed, the largest expense head, surged 138.5% to Rs 25 crore in FY26, while employee benefit expenses increased 210.3% to Rs 13.5 crore. Advertising and promotional expenses also jumped 139.9% to Rs 13 crore, whereas commission expenses surged 155.9% to Rs 11.44 crore.

Other expenses, which accounted for 35% of the total expenditure, increased 120.3% to Rs 31.46 crore in FY26 Overall, Boba Bhai’s total expenses jumped 2.3X to Rs 90.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 39 crore in the previous fiscal year. Importantly, the company reported 188 employees at the end of  March 2026.

Despite the strong growth in operating revenue, Boba Bhai’s losses widened 2.2X to Rs 21.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 9.96 crore in FY25. However, its operating efficiency improved marginally, with expenses incurred to generate every rupee of operating revenue declining to Rs 1.33 from Rs 1.37 in the previous fiscal year.

Its EBITDA margin improved to -30.35% from -34.67%, while ROCE deteriorated to -41.12% from -32.47%. Meanwhile, cash and bank balances declined sharply to Rs 2.85 crore from Rs 24.07 crore. Boba Bhai raised Rs 40 crore in March 2026 as it continued to expand its store network. The company currently operates around 100 stores across eight cities and plans to expand to 10 cities in FY27, while adding another 150-200 stores by the end of the fiscal.

The company’s next phase will test whether its expansion can translate into better unit economics. With employee, marketing and material costs rising alongside revenue, Boba Bhai will need to improve store-level profitability and cash generation as it scales.

title: Yulu reports Rs 281 Cr revenue and Rs 97 Cr loss in FY26
description: Yulu Bikes narrowed its losses by 23% to Rs 96.6 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026. The improvement came as revenue from its electric vehicle rental business
body: Electric mobility startup Yulu Bikes narrowed its losses by 23% to Rs 96.6 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026. The improvement came as revenue from its electric vehicle rental business increased, while overall expenses grew at a slower pace than revenue.
Yulu’s revenue from operations rose 18.6% to Rs 281 crore in FY26 from Rs 237 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements.

Income from renting electric vehicles, its largest revenue stream, increased 30.3% to Rs 262 crore from Rs 201 crore and accounted for more than 93% of operating revenue during the fiscal year ending March 2026.

Revenue from the sale of goods declined 59.3% to Rs 9.2 crore while manpower services fell 57% to Rs 5.7 crore from Rs 13.2 crore. In contrast, delivery services revenue rose more than 22X to Rs 2.6 crore. Franchisee income increased 122.2% to Rs 80 lakh from Rs 36 lakh.

Yulu’s employee benefit expenses, its largest cost head, increased 6.8% to Rs 94 crore in FY26 from Rs 88 crore in FY25. Battery-as-a-service costs rose 3.6% to Rs 87 crore, while depreciation expenses declined marginally by 1.5% to Rs 65 crore. Finance costs surged 40.9% to Rs 15.5 crore, whereas the cost of materials consumed fell 60% to Rs 8 crore. Technology and infrastructure expenses increased 11.6% to Rs 15 crore.

Other expenses climbed 34.9% to Rs 92.5 crore from Rs 68.56 crore in FY25. Overall, Yulu’s total expenses increased 7.4% to Rs 377 crore in FY26 from Rs 351 crore in the previous fiscal year. Bengaluru-based Yulu’s losses narrowed 23% to Rs 97 crore in FY26 from Rs 126 crore in FY25. The company also improved its operating efficiency, with expenses incurred to generate every rupee of operating revenue declining to Rs 1.34 from Rs 1.48 in the previous fiscal year.

The company’s EBITDA margin improved to -5.89% in FY26 from -15.41% in FY25, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at -119.29% compared with -27.26% a year earlier. Meanwhile, Yulu’s cash and bank balance increased to Rs 11.51 crore from Rs 9.65 crore, while total current assets rose to Rs 152 crore from Rs 102 crore. The financial performance comes as Yulu looks to expand its electric two-wheeler rental network. The company raised $93 million in August 2026 and currently operates a fleet of around 50,000 vehicles. It plans to expand to about 20 cities over the next year and increase its fleet to 200,000 electric vehicles by 2028.
The expansion will require Yulu to scale its fleet and supporting infrastructure, including battery services, while managing the costs associated with operating a larger network.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Oct 26- Oct 31]
description: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $115 million across 4 growth-stage deals, 24 early-stage deals including one undisclosed round. The week also saw 6 key appointments and a departure. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $115 million across 4 growth-stage deals, 24 early-stage deals including one undisclosed round. The week also saw 6 key appointments and a departure.
In contrast, 15 startups had collectively secured about $133.9 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised $42.34 million across four deals this week, led by Simplismart and Live2.ai, which secured $14 million each. E-commerce brand Troovy raised $11.5 million in a Series B round led by Sharrp Ventures with participation from Info Edge, WaterBridge and Better Capital.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $72.25 million across 24 deals this week, led by healthtech startup Cent, which secured $15 million in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures and South Park Commos. Gaming startup Matiks raised $10 million in its pre-Series A round led by General Catalyst.

E-commerce platform Ace Blend raised $9.91 million in Series A round from 3one4 Capital. Luxury watch brand Rotoris raised Rs 70 crore (about $7.4 million) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures.

Other startups that raised funding this week included fintech brand Mochatrade, gaming startup Let’s Game Now, manufacturing firm Venttup, healthtech startup Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre, QwikBuild and others.

title: TVS retains EV two-wheeler lead in October; Ather grows 3%, Ola declines 10%
description: India’s electric two-wheeler registrations rose to 2,23,847 units in October from 2,08,705 units in September, with TVS retaining its lead, Ather posting marginal growth and Ola Electric witnessing a decline.
body: India’s electric two-wheeler market continued its growth momentum in October, with registrations increasing to 2,23,847 units from 2,08,705 units in September, with TVS Motor retaining its leadership, while Ather Energy posted marginal growth and Ola Electric saw a decline in registrations.

According to latest Vahan data, TVS Motor led the market with 60,429 registrations in October, accounting for a 27% market share. The company’s registrations increased 11.08% month on month from 54,403 units in September, further strengthening its lead over other manufacturers.
Bajaj Auto retained the second position with 49,067 registrations and a 21.92% market share. However, its registrations grew marginally by 0.67% compared to 48,742 units in the previous month.

Ather Energy ranked third with 31,796 registrations and a 14.2% market share. Its registrations rose 2.75% month on month. The company also turned profitable in Q2 FY27 as revenue surged 63% year on year to Rs 1,464 crore .

Following 27% growth in September, Hero MotoCorp continued its strong run in October, with registrations increasing 22.34% month on month to 29,901 units from 24,440 units. The company held a 13.36% share of the electric two-wheeler market during the month.

Ola Electric remained in fifth position with 12,096 registrations and a 5.4% market share. It was the only player among the top five to report a monthly decline, with registrations falling 10.12% from 13,458 units in September.

Greaves Electric Mobility followed with 10,838 registrations, a 16.3% month-on-month increase from 9,319 units in September. River Mobility also posted strong growth, with registrations climbing 20.3% to 6,796 units against 5,649 units in September.
BGauss recorded 5,554 registrations, a 10.55% month-on-month increase, while E-Sprinto Green Energy posted a 6.36% growth in registrations to 2,124 units.

title: ideaForge returns to profitability in Q2 FY27 with Rs 91 Cr revenue
description: Drone maker ideaForge Technologies more than doubled its operating revenue in the second quarter of FY27, while it returned to profitability during the period.
body: Drone maker ideaForge Technologies more than doubled its operating revenue in the second quarter of FY27, while it returned to profitability during the period.

ideaForge’s revenue from operations jumped 123.9% to Rs 91.28 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 40.76 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial results filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The company reported Rs 6.28 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 97.6 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 44 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the expense side, cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense head, surged 90.9% to Rs 42 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 22 crore in the year-ago period. Employee benefit expenses increased 10% to Rs 16.58 crore from Rs 15.07 crore, while depreciation expenses rose 39.8% to Rs 14.75 crore from Rs 10.55 crore.
Meanwhile, other expenses edged up 4.8% to Rs 16.67 crore from Rs 15.90 crore. Overall, ideaForge’s total expenses increased 41.7% to Rs 90 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 63.52 crore in Q2 FY26.
As a result, ideaForge reported a net profit of Rs 6.5 crore in Q2 FY27, against a net loss of Rs 19.62 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

For the first half of FY27, ideaForge’s revenue from operations nearly tripled to Rs 160 crore from Rs 53.5 crore in H1 FY26. However, its net profit declined 10.4% to Rs 3.87 crore from Rs 4.32 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal.
On Monday, ideaForge’s shares closed at Rs 639.25 apiece, taking the company’s market capitalisation to Rs 3,126 crore.

title: TBO Tek posts Rs 866 Cr revenue and Rs 76 Cr profit in Q2 FY27
description: TBO Tek reported a 52.5% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27, while its net profit grew 12% to Rs 76 crore in the quarter ended September 2026.
body: Travel distribution platform TBO Tek announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, reporting a 52.5% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. The Gurugram-based company also recorded a 12% increase in net profit to Rs 76 crore during the quarter ended September 2026.

TBO Tek’s operating revenue rose to Rs 865.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 567.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its unaudited financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.
The company’s total income stood at Rs 880.4 crore in Q2 FY27, including Rs 14.8 crore earned through non-operating income.

Hotel and package bookings continued to be TBO Tek’s largest revenue contributor, accounting for 86% of its total revenue. Income from this segment grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 745 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 479.4 crore in Q2 FY26. Air ticketing and other allied services contributed the remaining Rs 120 crore.

As hotels and packages remained the largest revenue source, the service fees associated with them became the company’s biggest cost center, accounting for 39% of the total expenditure at Rs 304.5 crore in Q2 FY27. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 190.7 crore during the quarter.

TBO Tek’s total expenses increased 55% year-on-year to Rs 780.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 504.4 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year. The company reported a 12.6% rise in net profit to Rs 76 crore during the quarter from Rs 67.5 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the end of Monday’s trading session, TBO Tek shares were trading at Rs 1,593.5 giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 17,303 crore.

title: Taghash launches AI assistant Brain for investment funds
description: Fund management software platform Taghash has launched Brain, an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant that enables investment teams to analyse fund data.
body: Fund management software platform Taghash has launched Brain, an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant that enables investment teams to analyse fund data, prepare reports and carry out tasks within the platform.
Brain uses a fund’s existing data to analyse portfolio performance, generate reports, build dashboards with live data and execute tasks, Taghash said in a press release.

The assistant is designed to help investment teams consolidate company updates, compare portfolio performance and prepare reports. According to the company, tasks that previously took days can now be completed in minutes.

Taghash said more than 50% of active venture capital (VC) funds in India use its platform for their daily workflows. Brain is integrated into the platform, which offers tools for dealflow, portfolio management, fund operations and limited partner (LP) management.

The launch builds on Taghash’s earlier Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration and its WhatsApp and Slack assistants. The company plans to add more agentic AI capabilities to Brain in the coming months to support additional tasks and workflows.
Taghash provides software for investment funds, covering dealflow, relationship management, portfolio management, fund operations and LP management.

title: DeHaat posts Rs 2,715 Cr revenue in FY26
description: DeHaat's revenue from operations fell 9.8% to Rs 2,715 crore in FY26 from Rs 3,010 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
body: Several agritech companies that initially started as marketplaces for selling agricultural inputs and outputs are now moving towards building their own brands. The shift is aimed at improving margins, gaining better control over pricing, and reducing dependence on third-party products.

Full-stack agritech platform DeHaat has pursued this strategy over the past few years by expanding its portfolio of in-house brands. The shift towards building its own brands appears to have involved a near-term trade-off on growth, with operating revenue declining nearly 10% in FY26, even as the company continued to reshape its business. The firm’s net loss also widened in FY26 as it continued to invest in its in-house brands
DeHaat's revenue from operations fell 9.8% to Rs 2,715 crore in FY26 from Rs 3,010 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

The sale of agricultural inputs, including seeds, fertilisers and other farm-related products, contributed Rs 517 crore, accounting for around 19% of its operating revenue. The remaining revenue came from its agricultural output business, which includes staples, chillies and consumer-facing initiatives such as Farm Plus and HonestFarms.

India continued to be DeHaat's largest market, contributing 83% of its total revenue. The remaining income came from international markets, including the UK, Europe, the Middle East, Thailand and Russia.

On the cost side, procurement of materials remained the firm's largest expense, accounting for nearly 80% of its overall expenditure. As business scale moderated, this cost also declined by 11.7% to Rs 2,390 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses fell 9.1% to Rs 159 crore in the same period.

Other expenses, including transportation, rent, warehousing, sales and branding, along with legal and administrative overheads, took the company's total expenditure to Rs 2,972 crore in FY26, against Rs 3,242 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Despite an 8.3% decline in overall expenses, the revenue fall put further pressure on the company's bottom line, resulting in DeHaat's losses increasing by 11.4% to Rs 224 crore in FY26 from Rs 201 crore in FY25.

title: Health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud raises $12.5 Mn in Series A round
description: The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI)-led healthcare capabilities, expand research and development (R&D), and grow its connected microclinic network, Clinics On Cloud said in a press release.
body: Pune-based health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised $12.5 million in a Series A funding round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments.

The fresh funds will be used to strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI)-led healthcare capabilities, expand research and development (R&D), and grow its connected microclinic network, Clinics On Cloud said in a press release.

The funding will also support the company’s international expansion, with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) serving as its global expansion hub. The company plans to explore opportunities across Africa, the United States and Southeast Asia.
Clinics On Cloud also plans to establish partnerships with healthcare providers, technology companies and organisations seeking to deploy connected microclinics across different markets.

Founded in 2018 by Abhay Agarwal, Clinics On Cloud develops technology-enabled healthcare infrastructure focused on preventive healthcare. The company has recorded over 3,500 deployments and conducted more than 12 million health screenings across eight countries.

Initially focused on Health ATMs, the company has expanded its portfolio to include Health Lounges, Box Clinics and Mobile Medical Units. Its solutions combine preventive health screening, AI-assisted health insights and telemedicine to enable hospitals, pharmacies, healthcare entrepreneurs, corporates and government organisations to establish microclinics across workplaces, housing societies, malls and underserved communities.

The company’s infrastructure has been deployed across government health centres, hospitals, corporate campuses and rural communities, as well as Indian defence establishments, including the Army, Navy and Border Security Force (BSF).
Clinics On Cloud also plans to collaborate with global healthcare innovators to integrate AI and advanced screening technologies into its platform.

title: Fitness platform OBSESS raises Rs 3 Cr in angel round
description: The proceeds will be used to strengthen partnerships, expand its ecosystem and leverage technology to build a connected fitness experience, the company said in a press release.
body: Fitness platform OBSESS has raised approximately Rs 3 crore in an angel funding round from Centricity co-founder Pushpendra Singh, Amit Goel and Harshit Vij.
The proceeds will be used to strengthen partnerships, expand its ecosystem and leverage technology to build a connected fitness experience, the company said in a press release.

Launched in March 2026 by Tushar Sharma and Yash Kumar, OBSESS is building an integrated fitness platform that connects users with gyms, sports facilities, professional trainers, nutrition solutions and fitness products.

The Noida-based startup aims to address fragmentation in India's fitness and wellness industry, where gyms, trainers, sports facilities, nutrition experts and fitness brands often operate independently.
OBSESS offers a technology-driven marketplace that brings together sports venues, fitness centres, coaches, nutrition and wellness brands, and related services.
Its Obsess Play Partner platform enables users to discover and book sports venues, while offering rewards through features such as Obsess Coins.

The company's Obsess Gym Partner platform provides digital and operational tools for gym operators. Its Obsess Event Partner platform offers ticketing, registration and participant management solutions for sporting events, including marathons and cycling competitions.

title: Leverage Edu rolls out third ESOP buyback, grants options to 100 more employees
description: Talent mobility platform Leverage Edu, which also operates Fly Finance, Fly Homes and Leverage Careers, has rolled out its third employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) buyback.
body: Talent mobility platform Leverage Edu, which also operates Fly Finance, Fly Homes and Leverage Careers, has rolled out its third employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) buyback programme and granted options to 100 more employees.
With the latest allotment, 23% of its workforce now holds equity in the company.

The buyback programme allows employees to sell a part of their vested options for cash. Founder and CEO Akshay Chaturvedi said in a LinkedIn post that the company is currently undertaking the buyback.
Leverage Edu completed its first ESOP buyback in June 2022 and its second in June 2024.

The company operates a study abroad platform that helps students with university admissions, education financing and accommodation. More recently, it has expanded into workforce mobility through Leverage Careers, and into industry-integrated online programmes and certifications through Leverage Upskilling.
The company’s operating revenue more than doubled to Rs 364.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 173.3 crore in FY25. Its EBITDA turned positive at Rs 2 crore during the fiscal year.

title: Antler India leads pre-seed round in last-mile delivery startup Dispatch Network
description: The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's artificial intelligence (AI) team working on its proprietary Large Logistics Spatio-Temporal Model (LLSTM).
body: Pune-based last-mile delivery startup Dispatch Network has raised Rs 5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Antler India, with participation from angel investors Krishi Fagwani, founder of Thrive, Yashin Mahadevia and Parth Modwadhia.

The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's artificial intelligence (AI) team working on its proprietary Large Logistics Spatio-Temporal Model (LLSTM), a foundation AI model designed for intracity logistics and mobility, Dispatch Network said in a press release.
The startup plans to expand its operations to 50,000 orders per day across five cities.
Co-founded in 2023 by Rajit Arya and Navneeth Kannan, Dispatch operates a last-mile delivery network that uses AI to optimise order allocation, rider productivity and delivery routes.
The company's model sequences orders across multiple platforms, determining which order a rider should take next and where they should wait for subsequent deliveries.

According to the company, its network has processed over 100,000 deliveries since launching in June 2026. Monthly delivery volumes increased from 3,014 in June to 55,000 in October. The startup currently handles around 3,500 deliveries per day.

Dispatch said its model has reduced empty kilometres by two-thirds, while riders earn approximately 55% more per month compared to the industry average. The company also reported rider retention 80% higher than the industry average.

The startup currently serves food delivery and quick-commerce platforms, including Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto, Instamart and BigBasket. It also works with restaurants and stores through direct APIs and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC).

title: MobiKwik posts highest-ever quarterly PAT of Rs 11.8 Cr in Q2 FY27
description: Fintech platform MobiKwik reported a YoY increase of over 9% in operating revenue and posted its highest-ever quarterly PAT of Rs 11.8 crore in Q2 FY27.
body: Fintech platform MobiKwik announced its results for the second quarter of the financial year ending March 2027 (Q2 FY27). The company reported a year-on-year increase of over 9% in operating revenue and posted its highest-ever quarterly profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 11.8 crore.
MobiKwik's revenue from operations increased to Rs 295.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 270.2 crore in Q2 FY26, its unaudited financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange (NSE) show.
The company’s total income stood at Rs 302.7 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 279.3 crore a year earlier, including Rs 7 crore earned through non-operating income.

MobiKwik's key revenue contributors included commissions from recharges and loan servicing, along with income from payment gateway and technology platform services. However, the company did not disclose a segment-wise revenue breakup in its quarterly filing.
On a sequential basis, the company's operating revenue grew 5% from Rs 281.5 crore in Q1 FY27.

The company's platform gross merchandise value (GMV) increased 35% year-on-year to an all-time quarterly high of Rs 59,677 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 44,114 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Lending disbursals also grew 34% to Rs 1,082.6 crore from Rs 807.1 crore during the same period.

For the fintech firm, payment gateway charges remained MobiKwik's largest expense in Q2 FY27, accounting for over 42% of its total costs. Employee benefit expenses surged 59% to Rs 56.2 crore during the quarter.

The company also reported financial guarantee costs of Rs 28.3 crore, while legal, advertising and marketing, finance and other overheads contributed to its overall expenditure. MobiKwik's total expenses stood at Rs 290.9 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally lower than Rs 296 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

title: Capillary Technologies posts Rs 271 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; swings to Rs 22 Cr profit after Q1 loss
description: Capillary Technologies reported a 51.4% YoY growth in its operating revenue in the Q2 FY27. The company also reported a profit of Rs 22 crore during the quarter
body: SaaS firm Capillary Technologies reported a 51.4% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in the second quarter of the ongoing fiscal year (Q2 FY27). The company also reported a profit of Rs 22 crore during the quarter, compared to a marginal profit in the same period last year.

The Bengaluru-based company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 271 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 179 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its financial statements sourced from the NSE.

Founded in 2008 by Aneesh Reddy, Krishna Mehra, and Ajay Modani, Capillary Technologies offers cloud-based loyalty, CRM, and customer engagement solutions to more than 465 brands across 53 countries. Its clientele includes Tata Digital, Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail, and Abbott Laboratories.

The company primarily generates revenue from subscription services, which contributed 95% of its operating revenue during the quarter. Installation and campaign services accounted for the remaining revenue. It also reported Rs 6 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 277 crore in Q2 FY27.
On a sequential basis, the company's operating revenue grew 5.5% from Rs 257 crore in Q1 FY27.

Employee benefits remained its largest expense, increasing 57% year-on-year to Rs 134 crore. Software and server charges stood at Rs 42 crore, while professional and consultancy fees accounted for Rs 39 crore. Overall, Capillary's total expenses increased 44% to Rs 232 crore during the quarter.

On the bottom line, the company reported a profit of Rs 22 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 0.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The company had reported a loss of Rs 9.5 crore in Q1 FY27.

For context, Capillary Technologies had reported a 42.6% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 256.6 crore in Q1 FY27. However, its bottom line was impacted by an exceptional loss of Rs 33.4 crore linked to a cyber-enabled banking fraud at its Czech Republic subsidiary.

title: Beauty and personal care brand Hyeglo Beauty raises Rs 7 Cr led by Sauce
description: The fresh funds will be used for research and development (R&D), new product launches, brand building and hiring, Hyeglo said in a press release.
body: Beauty and personal care brand Hyeglo Beauty has raised Rs 7 crore in a funding round led by Sauce. Giga Capital, Consumer Collective, Reckitt’s Arjun Purkayastha and The Patient Capital also participated in the round.
The fresh funds will be used for research and development (R&D), new product launches, brand building and hiring, Hyeglo said in a press release.
Launched this year by Kanupriya Ahluwalia, Hyeglo is a direct-to-consumer (D2C) beauty and personal care brand that combines skincare ingredients with makeup products.
The Delhi-based brand said its products combine clinically tested ingredients, skincare actives and pigments. It focuses on formulations that incorporate skincare ingredients into makeup products.

Hyeglo follows a skin science-led approach to product development, with dermatological expertise and professional consultations informing its formulations. The brand also works with experts, including Dr Sonal Tibrewal Garg, an MD in Dermatology.

title: Clean energy deployment platform Two Point O Capital raises $10 Mn led by Transition VC
description: Two Point O Capital (TW.O), an AI-powered clean energy deployment platform for commercial and industrial (C&I) businesses, has raised $10 Mn led by Transition VC.
body: Two Point O Capital (TW.O), an AI-powered clean energy deployment platform for commercial and industrial (C&I) businesses, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Transition Venture Capital. Existing investor Omnivore and angel investors Chiranjeev Singh Saluja and Sudhir M Reddy also participated in the round.

The proceeds will be used to expand into battery energy storage systems (BESS) and strengthen its presence in solar energy, energy efficiency and wastewater treatment, the company said in a press release.

Founded in 2024 by Archit Mehrotra, Karan Bhutani, Manya Ranjan and Shashidhar Reddy, TW.O provides sustainable infrastructure solutions to businesses through flexible financing, project ownership, transparent measurement and guaranteed outcomes.

The company works with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) firms across India. Its clientele includes Premier Energies, Godrej, JK Tyre, Morepen Pharma, Wipro and Phoenix Mills.

TW.O said its assets under management (AUM) have grown 1.5 times every quarter over the past three quarters. The company uses a proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning platform for solutioning, underwriting and asset monitoring. The platform enables predictive maintenance, risk mitigation and performance optimisation.

According to the company, the C&I segment presents an annual opportunity of $100 billion to $150 billion for customised capital and asset solutions that address clean energy and utility requirements. Such solutions can help businesses reduce operating costs, improve operational resilience and access markets such as the European Union.
TW.O also plans to deepen its presence in energy- and water-intensive sectors, including data centres, automotive, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing and healthcare.
The company aims to help factories, hospitals, data centres and manufacturing facilities adopt cleaner energy and more efficient water management solutions.

title: Indian startup funding nosedives 47.5% to $678 Mn in October
description: Indian startups raised $678 million in October, a 47.5% month-on-month decline, as the absence of large funding rounds dragged overall investments. Monthly Funding Report
body: Indian startups raised $678 million in October, a 47.5% month-on-month decline, as the absence of large funding rounds dragged overall investments. No startup secured a funding round of $100 million or more, while only Tessolve and Even Healthcare crossed the $50 million mark. Growth stage deals received a boost from rounds raised by Boldfit, DailyObjects, RapidCanvas and Nat Habit, while early stage funding saw moderate participation from Auxo AI, Cent, Mesa and Matiks.

The month saw no reported layoffs, while Jio Platforms made a high-profile stock market debut, followed by listings of Zetwerk and AceVector, the operator of Snapdeal. Merger and acquisition activity, however, remained limited to select sectors.
[ Overview ]

According to data compiled by Entrackr, Indian startups raised approximately $678 million in funding during October. This amount included 20 growth and late-stage deals totalling $414.6 million, along with 79 early-stage deals worth $263 million. Additionally, there were 9 undisclosed deals during the period.
Y-o-Y and M-o-M trend

October 2026 saw a sharp decline in startup funding compared to the same month last year. Total funding fell 60.8% to $677.8 million from $1.73 billion in October 2025. On a month-on-month basis, funding declined 47.5% from $1.29 billion in September. February was the strongest month for funding in 2026, with startups raising around $2 billion, followed by June, which also recorded around $2 billion. October’s decline came amid a lack of larger deals, with no startup raising $100 million or more during the month.
[ Top 10 growth-stage deals ]

Growth and late-stage startups saw activity across sectors in October, led by semiconductor solutions provider Tessolve Semiconductor, which raised $75 million , followed by healthtech startup Even Healthcare with $50 million . Sports and fitness brand Boldfit secured $42 million , while lifestyle brand DailyObjects and enterprise AI startup RapidCanvas raised $35 million and $29 million, respectively. Advanced materials manufacturer Simplify raised $25 million, followed by robotics startup Origin with $20 million. Beauty and wellness brand Nat Habit and AI startups Simplismart and Live2.ai raised $15 million, $14 million and $14 million, respectively.

title: iD Fresh Food nears Rs 900 Cr revenue in FY26; profit before exceptional items surges 3X
description: iD Fresh Food’s revenue from operations increased 27.7% YoY to Rs 870 crore in FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
body: Ready-to-cook food is becoming a staple in Indian kitchens as consumers seek convenience without giving up home-cooked meals. iD Fresh Food has built its business around this growing preference, clocking nearly Rs 900 crore in revenue in FY26 while remaining profitable.
iD Fresh Food’s revenue from operations increased 27.7% year-on-year to Rs 870 crore in FY26 from Rs 681 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

The Bengaluru-based company manufactures ready-to-cook products such as idli and dosa batter and parathas. It also trades in food products, including curd, paneer, coffee, specialty batter and other food items.

iD Fresh operates manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Haryana and Ajman in the UAE. Manufactured products such as parathas and various batters contributed Rs 671 crore, accounting for 75% of its total operating income. The remaining income came from traded goods, including dairy products, chapatis, beverages, and frozen fruits.
The firm also earned Rs 8 crore in other income, primarily from interest on current investments, taking its total income to Rs 879 crore in FY26.

Raw material procurement remained the largest cost component, accounting for 49% of the company's total expenditure. This expense increased 18.3% to Rs 394 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses also rose 16% to Rs 168 crore.

The company spent Rs 70 crore on advertising in FY25. Other expenses, including legal, rent, freight, transportation and overheads, pushed its total expenditure up 20.5% to Rs 801 crore in FY26 from Rs 665 crore in FY25.
Despite the rise in costs, strong revenue growth helped iD Fresh improve its profit before tax and exceptional items to Rs 79 crore in FY26 from Rs 24 crore in FY25.

title: Razorpay receives SEBI approval for IPO
description: Bengaluru-based fintech company Razorpay had confidentially filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI in June 2026.
body: Fintech unicorn Razorpay has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public offering (IPO), according to sources familiar with the development.
The Bengaluru-based company had confidentially filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI in June 2026.
According to an Economic Times report, Razorpay is targeting to raise Rs 5,500-6,500 crore through its IPO at an expected valuation of $5 billion (Rs 49,000-50,000 crore).
As per sources, the company expected to file its final IPO papers before March 2027.
Media reports indicate that Razorpay has roped in Axis Capital, Kotak Mahindra Capital, JP Morgan and Citi as bankers for its proposed IPO.

Razorpay was last valued at $7.5 billion in 2021, when it raised $375 million during the peak of the funding cycle. Since then, the company has undertaken several strategic initiatives ahead of its public market debut.

In April 2025, Razorpay converted into a public limited company as part of its IPO preparations. Later that year, it completed its reverse flip to India, a process that involved shifting its domicile from the US to India. The company paid around $150 million in taxes related to the transition.

Founded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay provides payment gateway services to businesses. Over the years, it has expanded into business banking, lending and payment solutions for merchants.

title: Indiqube posts Rs 472 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; losses narrow 80%
description: Managed workspace solutions provider IndiQube announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, reporting a 35% year-on-year increase in operating revenue.
body: Managed workspace solutions provider IndiQube announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, reporting a 35% year-on-year increase in operating revenue. The Bengaluru-based company’s net loss narrowed 80% to Rs 5.90 crore in the quarter ended September 2026.

IndiQube’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 472 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 350 crore in Q2 FY26, according to financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE). In the first half of FY27, IndiQube’s revenue from operations grew 35.7% to Rs 895 crore from Rs 659.5 crore in the corresponding period of FY26.

Founded in 2015, IndiQube offers managed workspace solutions to startups, enterprises and SMEs across major Indian cities. The company also recorded Rs 20 crore in other income during the quarter, taking its total income to Rs 492 crore compared to Rs 367 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

For the managed office provider, depreciation on leases remained its largest cost component, increasing 25% year-on-year to Rs 195 crore in Q2 FY27. Finance costs stood at Rs 129 crore, while employee benefit expenses declined marginally to Rs 24.5 crore.

Meanwhile, the cost of materials increased 11.5% to Rs 29 crore from Rs 26 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Overall, IndiQube’s total expenses increased 23.5% year-on-year to Rs 500 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 405 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the bottom line, the company narrowed its net loss by 80.3% to Rs 5.90 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 29.90 crore in the year-ago quarter.

On a sequential basis, revenue from operations grew 11.6% to Rs 472 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 423 crore in Q1 FY27. Meanwhile, the company’s net loss narrowed 74.8% to Rs 5.90 crore from Rs 23.40 crore during the same period.
IndiQube closed Wednesday’s trading session at Rs 179.15 per share, giving the company a market capitalization of around Rs 3,679 crore.

title: Awfis reports Rs 439 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; profit grows 93%
description: Awfis reported a 20% YoY growth in operating revenue. The company’s net profit nearly doubled to Rs 30.8 crore during the quarter ended September 2026.
body: Co-working solutions provider Awfis announced its Q2 FY27 financial results on Tuesday, reporting a 20% year-on-year growth in operating revenue. The company’s net profit nearly doubled to Rs 30.8 crore during the quarter ended September 2026.
The Delhi-based company’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 439 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 367 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statements sourced from the NSE.
Other income contributed Rs 25.6 crore, taking Awfis’ total income to Rs 464.3 crore during the quarter.
For the first half of FY27, Awfis reported a 23% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 863.6 crore from Rs 701.6 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Co-working spaces remained Awfis’ largest revenue contributor, accounting for over 83% of its operating revenue. Revenue from the segment grew 22% year-on-year to Rs 363.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 297.4 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Meanwhile, its construction and fit-out projects business contributed Rs 75.2 crore during the quarter.

On the expenditure front, depreciation on leases remained Awfis’ largest cost component, rising 25% year-on-year to Rs 119 crore. Subcontracting costs stood at Rs 59.7 crore, while employee benefit expenses remained flat at Rs 32.7 crore. Finance costs and other operating overheads took total expenses to Rs 433 crore in Q2 FY27, up from Rs 377 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
The strong revenue led Awfis to nearly double its profit to Rs 30.8 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 16 crore in the year-ago quarter.

On a sequential basis, Awfis’ revenue from operations remained largely stable at Rs 438.7 crore compared to Rs 424.9 crore in Q1 FY27, while net profit increased 28% from Rs 24 crore in the previous quarter.

title: GIVA raises over $100 Mn in funding round led by Multiples PE
description: The investment will help the Bengaluru-based company expand its retail network, strengthen manufacturing capabilities and scale its omnichannel presence.
body: Multiples Alternate Asset Management, along with its co-investors, has led a $100 million-plus funding round in fine jewellery brand GIVA. The investment will help the company expand its retail network, strengthen manufacturing capabilities and scale its omnichannel presence.
The company plans to expand its retail network to over 1,000 outlets in the next three to five years, according to a press release.
GIVA also raised $28 million in debt in May this year, which could be part of the current round. Entrackr exclusively reported the development.

Founded in 2019 by Ishendra Agarwal, GIVA offers jewellery across sterling silver, gold and lab-grown diamonds. The company operates through its own retail stores, D2C website and third-party e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms.
GIVA currently operates over 400 stores across India and Sri Lanka, with a presence in Tier I and Tier II markets.

The company said it grew at a CAGR of over 70% in the past three years, ending FY26 with revenue of around Rs 865 crore. It will use the fresh capital to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing capabilities and increase its offline presence.
The company has raised over $258 million to date, including Rs 110 crore (around $12 million) in a Series C extension round led by HPV CC1 Ltd in February this year.
While GIVA is yet to file its FY26 financials, its operating revenue grew 89% year-on-year to Rs 518 crore in FY25. Its losses increased 22% to Rs 72 crore during the same period.

title: Decoding: Spill Games’ Rs 100 Cr Series A round, valuation and cap table
description: Spill Games has raised around Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital, with participation from existing investors Centre Court Capital
body: Bengaluru-based mobile gaming startup Spill Games has raised around Rs 100 crore ($10.5 million) in a Series A round led by Elevation Capital, with participation from existing investors Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital. Following the latest allotment, the company's co-founders collectively hold a 41.23% stake.
The latest round values Spill Games at around Rs 400 crore, marking a 3.5X jump from its seed valuation of Rs 115 crore in April 2026, when it raised around Rs 27 crore .

According to the company's regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , Spill Games has allotted 6,094 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,65,110 per share, along with 10 equity shares.
Elevation Capital invested Rs 80 crore in the round, while Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital infused Rs 12.6 crore and Rs 8 crore, respectively.

As per the filing, the fresh proceeds will be used to scale successful games, expand its portfolio, invest in user acquisition, strengthen its AI and technology capabilities, and selectively hire talent. The company monetises its games through advertising and in-app purchases.

Founded in 2024 by former PlaySimple Games executives Om Misra, Tapan Ranjan and Harsh Garg, Spill Games is building an AI-led mobile gaming studio focused on free-to-play casual, puzzle and hybrid-casual games for global audiences.

Following the latest allotment, Elevation Capital emerged as Spill Games' largest external shareholder with a 20% stake, followed by Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital with 11.78% and 8.93%, respectively. All In Capital and M-League Limited held 7.48% and 2.70%, respectively. CRED founder Kunal Shah also holds a 0.68% stake in the company.
The three co-founders collectively hold a 41.23% stake in Spill Games. Misra owns 14.02%, while Garg and Ranjan hold 13.61% each.

title: Unify Foodworks raises Rs 5 Cr in seed round
description: he company plans to increase store density and strengthen consumer recall in the region. It also aims to refine its operating model as it works towards building the two
body: Unify Foodworks, the exclusive pan-Indian master franchisee of Moe’s Casa Mexicana and Carvel, has raised Rs 5 crore in a seed funding round through compulsorily convertible debentures (CCDs).
The fresh capital will be used to expand the presence of both brands across the National Capital Region (NCR), where they made their India debut, Unify Foodworks said in a press release.

The company plans to increase store density and strengthen consumer recall in the region. It also aims to refine its operating model as it works towards building the two brands into national restaurant chains, with a long-term target of opening more than 100 stores across India.
Launched in November 2024 by Sumer Sethi, Unify Foodworks holds the exclusive pan-Indian master franchise rights for Moe’s Casa Mexicana, Carvel and Moe’s Southwest Grill.

Moe’s Casa Mexicana is the international evolution of US fast-casual restaurant chain Moe’s Southwest Grill, with India serving as its first international market. Its menu includes burritos, bowls and tacos, alongside India-focused offerings such as Habanero Paneer.

Carvel, an American ice cream brand founded in 1934, entered India in 2025 with its first outlet in Connaught Place, New Delhi. Both brands are owned by US-based private equity firm Roark Capital, whose portfolio also includes Subway, Baskin-Robbins and Dunkin’.

Unify Foodworks is also investing in supply chain, logistics and store-level training as it prepares to expand beyond NCR. The company plans to use the region to test store economics, menu localisation and operational efficiency before replicating the model in other markets.

title: Snitch revenue grows 68% to Rs 835 Cr in FY26; posts Rs 27 Cr loss
description: Snitch is among the brands that have capitalised on this trend, growing its revenue 3.4X over the past two fiscal years while keeping its losses relatively contained.
body: India’s men’s fast-fashion market has shifted significantly over the past few years, with consumers becoming more experimental in their style choices and fashion preferences. Snitch is among the brands that have capitalised on this trend, growing its revenue 3.4X over the past two fiscal years while keeping its losses relatively contained.
Snitch’s revenue from operations grew 67.7% year-on-year to Rs 835 crore in FY26 from Rs 498 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2020 by Siddharth Dungarwal, Snitch sells trendy men’s apparel and accessories through its website and app. Apparel and accessories remain the company’s sole revenue stream. It also earned Rs 14 crore in other income, largely through interest on deposits and long-term investments, taking its total income to Rs 849 crore in FY26.

The company has also entered the quick commerce segment as it looks to expand its reach and delivery capabilities. At the same time, Snitch has been expanding its offline presence. According to its website, the brand operates 142 stores across India, including in metro and Tier II cities.

For the D2C fashion brand, procurement of apparel and accessories remained the largest cost component, accounting for around 51% of its overall expenditure. In line with the growth in scale, this expense increased 92.2% to Rs 444 crore in FY26 from Rs 231 crore in FY25.

Snitch spent Rs 108 crore on advertising and marketing during the year, while employee benefit expenses increased to Rs 81 crore. Marketplace charges, rent, delivery and other overheads also added to the cost base. As a result, its total expenditure increased 71.9% to Rs 873 crore in FY26 from Rs 508 crore in FY25.

With expenses growing slightly faster than revenue, Snitch reported a net loss of Rs 27 crore in FY26. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.05 to earn a rupee in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at -8.6% and -3%, respectively.
Snitch has raised over $53 million to date, including a $40 million Series B round led by 360 ONE Asset in June 2025.

title: Exclusive: Armatrix kicks off Rs 67 Cr seed round at 4.8X valuation premium
description: Armatrix has raised Rs 67.28 crore in a seed funding round led by UK-based Crane Venture Partners, along with participation from new and existing investors.
body: Deeptech robotics startup Armatrix has raised Rs 67.28 crore in a seed funding round led by UK-based Crane Venture Partners, along with participation from new and existing investors.
The fresh funding comes less than a year after its pre-seed round and values the company nearly 5X higher than its previous round.
In January 2026, Armatrix had raised $2.1 million in a pre-seed round led by pi Ventures, with participation from Inuka Capital, Boundless Ventures, Boost VC, Turbostart and gradCapital.

According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , the company has allotted 4,070 compulsory convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 1,64,900 per share, along with 10 equity shares, to raise the capital.
The funding round appears to be ongoing, with the Delhi-based company likely to raise more capital in subsequent tranches.

Crane Venture Partners led the round with an investment of Rs 40 crore. Existing investor pi Ventures infused Rs 15 crore, followed by gradCapital with Rs 4.52 crore, Boundless Ventures with Rs 2.5 crore and Inuka Capital with Rs 2.37 crore. NKSquared also joined the round with an investment of Rs 2.37 crore, marking its entry into the company.
Among other investors, AL Trust, Saurabh Chandra, Unacademy co-founder Roman Saini and existing investor Narayan Rangarajan collectively invested Rs 67 lakh in the round.

According to Entrackr's estimates, Armatrix's valuation jumped 4.8X to Rs 360 crore in the seed round from Rs 75 crore in its pre-seed round. The company plans to use the fresh proceeds for business expansion and general corporate purposes.

title: Solgram raises over $1 Mn in pre-seed round led by DSG Consumer Partners, Saama Capital
description: The fresh capital will be used to expand its cold-chain infrastructure, strengthen its technology stack, deepen sourcing relationships and scale operations across the National Capital Region (NCR)
body: Gurugram-based premium grocery platform Solgram has raised over $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by DSG Consumer Partners and Saama Capital. Hospitality entrepreneur Kapil Chopra also participated in the round.
The funding comes within a quarter of the company's launch.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its cold-chain infrastructure, strengthen its technology stack, deepen sourcing relationships and scale operations across the National Capital Region (NCR), Solgram said in a press release.

Founded by Shashank Shekhar Sharma, Solgram operates a premium grocery platform focused on fresh produce, dairy, meats, seafood and other temperature-sensitive products. The company aims to maintain product quality through an end-to-end temperature-controlled supply chain.

Its operations cover sourcing, quality inspection, storage, fulfilment and delivery. The company operates temperature-controlled stores with dedicated zones for different product categories, along with sealed thermal packaging and dedicated last-mile infrastructure.

Solgram's assortment includes fresh produce, dairy, meats, seafood, bakery, gourmet pantry products and emerging food brands. It also offers Mindful Mode, a health-focused shopping category featuring products with cleaner labels, nutritional information and provenance details.
The platform offers scheduled batched delivery and express delivery options.

Currently operational in Gurugram, Solgram plans to expand across the NCR before entering other Tier-I cities in the coming months. The company said it intends to build operational density and consistency in individual clusters before expanding into new markets.

title: The Croffle Guys raises Rs 14 Cr from V3 Ventures, N.A.N Partners at Rs 100 Cr valuation
description: Mumbai-based quick-service restaurant (QSR) startup The Croffle Guys has raised Rs 14 crore in a funding round led by V3 Ventures, with participation from N.A.N. Snippets
body: Mumbai-based quick-service restaurant (QSR) startup The Croffle Guys has raised Rs 14 crore in a funding round led by V3 Ventures, with participation from N.A.N Partners, the family office of Navin Agarwal. The round values the company at Rs 100 crore post-money.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its store network, with plans to add more than 40 outlets, primarily across Mumbai and Delhi, along with a selective presence in Pune, the company said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2025 by Rahul Vohra, Annanya Agarwal, Amay Thakkar and Veer Pinto, The Croffle Guys operates in the QSR segment, offering croffles, a fusion of croissants and waffles, through sweet and savoury menu options.

The company has expanded from two outlets to eight in approximately a year and currently operates at an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 24 crore. It is targeting Rs 100 crore in annual revenue over the next 10-12 months.

The startup has also recorded nearly threefold revenue growth over the past six months, with monthly revenue currently standing at approximately Rs 2 crore. It aims to increase this figure to Rs 8 crore per month.
The Croffle Guys first gained national attention through its appearance on Shark Tank India, where it secured a Rs 2.5 crore investment deal at a valuation of Rs 50 crore.
The investment also gives the startup access to the consumer business experience of Verlinvest, which has backed brands such as Oatly, Epigamia, Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters and Insomnia Cookies.
V3 Ventures has also invested in consumer and food businesses, including Go Zero, Crème Castle, Dil Foods, Super You and Salad Days.

title: Wealthtech startup PowerUp Money raises $10 Mn led by Flourish Ventures
description: Wealthtech platform PowerUp Money has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors. News
body: Wealthtech platform PowerUp Money has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC.
Back in December 2025, PowerUp Money had raised $12 million in Series A funding round led by Peak XV and others.

The fresh capital will be used to develop its AI-led wealth management solutions and expand its advisory offerings. Its mutual fund advisory subscription, PowerUp Elite, has crossed 1 lakh paid members within a year of launch.
Founded in 2025 by Prateek Jindal, the Bengaluru-based startup said it serves over 1.5 million users who track mutual fund portfolios worth more than Rs 2.5 lakh crore on its platform.

The company has also launched Elite Prime, an AI-enabled digital wealth advisory product that offers personalised asset allocation, SIP and lump-sum investment plans, portfolio rebalancing and withdrawal strategies based on an investor's financial goals and risk profile. It also provides an AI wealth coach and personal assistant to guide investment decisions.

Another offering, Infinite, provides managed wealth advisory covering financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation and ongoing portfolio management. The company said Infinite has reached nearly Rs 500 crore in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch, despite being available to a limited set of customers.
Through Elite, Elite Prime and Infinite, the startup is building a platform combining mutual fund advisory, AI-led digital wealth management and human-led portfolio management.

title: Vedantu revenue grows  17% to Rs 267 Cr in FY26; cuts losses before exceptional items
description: Vedantu's revenue from operations grew 17.6% to Rs 267 crore in FY26 from Rs 227 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
