body: The online education space has been through a sharp shakeout over the past two-three years, with Byju’s collapse and Unacademy’s acquisition by UpGrad reshaping the competitive landscape. Against these odds, Vedantu managed to grow its revenue and improve its operating metrics in FY26. Its bottom line also improved, excluding the impact of exceptional items.

Bengaluru-based edtech unicorn’s revenue from operations grew 17.6% to Rs 267 crore in FY26 from Rs 227 crore in the previous fiscal, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

Tuition fees remained its largest revenue source for Vedantu, growing 16.8% to Rs 222 crore from Rs 190 crore in FY25. Revenue from books, uniforms and other products increased 31.8% to Rs 29 crore, while e-learning project income stood at Rs 6.3 crore during the last fiscal year.
With non-operating income of Rs 3.8 crore, the firm posted a total income of Rs 270 crore in the fiscal year ending March 2026.

On the expense side, employee benefit expenses, the largest cost component, declined 12.8% to Rs 191 crore in FY26 from Rs 219.5 crore in FY25. It also includes Rs 7.2 crore as ESOP cost (non-cash. Contract and outsourced resources costs surged 54.3% to Rs 71 crore, while depreciation expenses declined 5.8% to Rs 65 crore.
Advertising and promotional expenses increased 7.4% to Rs 29 crore, whereas technology expenses stood at Rs 12 crore . Overall, Vedantu’s total expenses remained largely flat at Rs 442 crore in FY26.
With the decent growth coupled with stable expenses, Vedantu’s losses before exceptional items and tax decreased by 18.6% to Rs 171 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 210 crore in FY25.

Note: We have excluded exceptional income and expenses arising from changes in the fair valuation of consideration payable (liability towards future obligations) in both FY25 and FY26 to present a clearer picture of the company's financial performance.

title: Tracxn's revenue remains flat at Rs 21.3 Cr in Q2 FY27; losses narrow 25.7%
description: Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q2 FY27 results, reporting largely flat revenue during the quarter, while its losses narrowed year-on-year.
body: Data intelligence platform Tracxn announced its Q2 FY27 results, reporting largely flat revenue during the quarter, while its losses narrowed year-on-year.

Tracxn's revenue from operations increased marginally by 0.2% to Rs 21.30 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.25 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Tracxn derives its operating revenue from subscription sales, which provide access to its data and software. However, the company did not disclose a detailed revenue breakup for the quarter.
The company also earned Rs 1.38 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 22.70 crore in Q2 FY27.

Employee benefit expenses remained the largest cost head, increasing 22.5% to Rs 23.33 crore and accounting for 85.4% of the overall expenditure during the quarter. Depreciation expenses stood at Rs 7.5 lakh, compared to Rs 4 lakh in Q2 FY26. Other expenses increased 41% to Rs 3.92 crore. The company's total expenses rose 25% to Rs 27.32 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.86 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Despite the increase in expenses, Tracxn narrowed its net loss by 25.7% to Rs 4.13 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to a loss of Rs 5.56 crore in Q2 FY26.

On a half-yearly basis, Tracxn's revenue from operations remained largely flat at Rs 42.38 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 42.44 crore in H1 FY26. However, its net loss widened 60.8% to Rs 7.14 crore during the first half of FY27. At the close of trading on Wednesday, Tracxn’s shares settled at Rs 32.08, giving the company a market capitalization of approximately Rs 331 crore.

title: PhysicsWallah revenue rises 18% to Rs 1,242 Cr in Q2 FY27; profit jumps 2.1X
description: Edtech company PhysicsWallah reported an 18.2% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in Q2 FY27, while its net profit more than doubled during the quarter.
body: Edtech company PhysicsWallah reported an 18.2% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in Q2 FY27, while its net profit more than doubled during the quarter. PhysicsWallah’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 1,242 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,051 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.

In terms of revenue mix, the online segment remained the largest contributor, accounting for 55.84% of PhysicsWallah’s operating revenue at Rs 693.5 crore, up 26.3% year-on-year. The offline segment contributed 43.56%, with revenue rising 9.1% to Rs 541 crore, while other operating revenue at Rs 8 crore.

The company also earned Rs 93 crore from other sources, taking its total income to Rs 1,335 crore in Q2 FY27. On the expense side, employee benefits remained the largest cost component at Rs 522 crore, up 10.4% year-on-year from Rs 473 crore while Cost of materials consumed increased 22.6% to Rs 195 crore from Rs 159 crore.

Depreciation expenses rose 7.6% to Rs 113 crore, while finance costs increased 4% to Rs 26 crore. Other expenses grew 4.6% to Rs 249 crore from Rs 238 crore. Overall expenses increased 10.5% to Rs 1,105 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,000 crore in Q2 FY26.
The Noida-based company’s net profit surged 2.1X year-on-year to Rs 144 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 70 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

On a half-yearly basis, the company's revenue from operations increased 20.8% to Rs 2,293 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 1,898 crore in H1 FY26. The company reported a net profit of Rs 55.35 crore in H1 FY27, against a net loss of Rs 57.30 crore in H1 FY26. At the end of today’s trading session, the Noida-based company’s share price closed at Rs 127.41, giving it a market capitalisation of Rs 37,376 crore

title: Nykaa's profit jumps 3X to Rs 101 Cr in Q2 FY27; revenue grows 28%
description: Nykaa reported strong growth in Q2 FY27, with its revenue from operations increasing 28% year-on-year, while its net profit surged over threefold during the quarter ended September 2026.
body: Online beauty and fashion platform Nykaa reported strong growth in Q2 FY27, with its revenue from operations increasing 28% year-on-year, while its net profit surged over threefold during the quarter ended September 2026.

Nykaa's revenue from operations grew to Rs 3,006 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 2,346 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The beauty segment continued to dominate the company's revenue, contributing Rs 2,700 crore or 90% of its operating revenue during the quarter. The fashion segment generated Rs 287 crore, accounting for 10% of the total operating revenue, while other segments contributed Rs 19 crore.

For Nykaa, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense, accounting for 56.64% of its total expenditure. This expense increased 25.7% to Rs 1,624 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,292 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year.

Employee benefit expenses grew 20% to Rs 220 crore, while depreciation expenses increased 18% to Rs 93 crore. Finance costs declined 3% to Rs 30.52 crore. Other expenses, which include marketing, technology and other overheads, increased 26% to Rs 899 crore. The company's total expenses rose 25% to Rs 2,867 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,298 crore in Q2 FY26.

The growth in operating revenue, coupled with a slower increase in expenses, helped Nykaa improve its profitability. The company's net profit tripled to Rs 101 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 33 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year.

On a half-yearly basis, Nykaa's revenue from operations increased 28.6% to Rs 5,788 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 4,501 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit also surged 214.8% to Rs 181 crore during the first half of FY27, compared to Rs 57.5 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal year. At the close of today's trading session, Nykaa's stock was priced at Rs 355.10, giving the company a market capitalization of Rs 1,01,410 crore.

title: Lenskart Q2 FY27 revenue jumps 36%, profit rises 2.3X to Rs 232 Cr
description: Lenskart posted a 36% year-on-year increase in consolidated operating revenue. Its net profit more than doubled to Rs 232 crore during the quarter.
body: Eyewear brand Lenskart announced its Q2 FY27 financial results today, posting a 36% year-on-year increase in consolidated operating revenue, backed by growth across both domestic and international markets. Its net profit more than doubled to Rs 232 crore during the quarter.
The company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 2,845 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,096 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its financial statements sourced from NSE.

Both domestic and international markets contributed to the company’s growth at a similar pace. Revenue from the India business grew 35.5% year-on-year to Rs 1,668 crore in Q2 FY27, while the international business recorded a 36.5% increase to Rs 1,201 crore.
On a quarterly basis, Lenskart’s revenue from operations grew 5% from Rs 2,714 crore in Q1 FY27.

On the expense side, the cost of materials remained the largest expense head, accounting for 33% of the total expenditure. It increased 31% year-on-year to Rs 854 crore in Q2 FY27. Employee benefit expenses also rose 25% to Rs 627 crore from Rs 503 crore in the year-ago quarter. Finance costs and depreciation were other major expense heads, taking total expenses up 22% to Rs 2,597 crore during the quarter.

The 36% growth in revenue, which outpaced the rise in total expenses, helped Lenskart more than double its net profit to Rs 232 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 103 crore in the year-ago quarter. Its EBITDA also increased 50% to Rs 622 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 21.86%.
At the end of today’s session, Lenskart shares closed at Rs 689.7, giving it a total market capitalization of Rs 1,19,960 crore or $12.6 billion.

title: MapMyIndia’s Q2 FY27 profit jumps 85% to Rs 37.5 Cr; revenue rises 16%
description: MapMyIndia, reported a 15.8% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27. The company’s net profit surged 85% during the quarter to Rs 37.52 crore.
body: C.E. Info Systems, the parent company of MapMyIndia, reported a 15.8% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in Q2 FY27. The company’s net profit surged 85% during the quarter to Rs 37.52 crore.

The company’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 132 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 114 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

MapMyIndia is a deep-tech company offering digital maps, geospatial software, location-based APIs, IoT solutions and mapping platforms to enterprises, automakers, government agencies, developers and consumers across automotive, enterprise and government segments.

Revenue from map data and related services, including royalties, subscriptions, software and projects, remained the company's largest revenue stream at Rs 99 crore in Q2 FY27, marginally down from Rs 100 crore in the year-ago quarter. Meanwhile, revenue from hardware device sales more than doubled to Rs 33 crore from Rs 14 crore in Q2 FY26.
MapMyIndia also reported Rs 16 crore in income from other sources, taking its total income to Rs 148 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 124 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

On the expense side, the cost of materials consumed surged 71% to Rs 27 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 15.8 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefit expenses rose 31.7% to Rs 25.36 crore from Rs 19.26 crore. whereas, technical services outsourced expenses declined 55.4% to Rs 14.53 crore from Rs 32.58 crore. Other expenses also decreased 4.9% to Rs 27 crore. Overall, MapMyIndia's total expenses increased marginally by 2.1% to Rs 96 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 94 crore in the year-ago quarter.
At the bottom line, the Delhi-based company reported an 85% year-on-year jump in net profit to Rs 37.52 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 20.27 crore in Q2 FY26.

For the first half of FY27, MapMyIndia's operating revenue increased 15.5% to Rs 271.5 crore from Rs 235 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit grew 30.1% to Rs 88 crore from Rs 67.65 crore in the corresponding period last year. MapMyIndia’s shares closed at Rs 890.20 apeice on Wednesday, taking its market capitalisation to Rs 4,666 crore.

title: Enrission India Capital participates in Ottonomy’s Rs 40.6 Cr funding round
description: Ottonomy operates in the autonomous delivery and robotics segment, where companies are developing AI-powered solutions to address last-mile logistics, workforce shortages
body: AI-powered autonomous delivery robot developer Ottonomy has raised approximately Rs 40.6 crore ($4.2 million) in a post-seed funding round, with Japan-based venture capital firm Enrission India Capital participating in the investment.

The fresh capital will support the company’s global expansion across healthcare and industrial automation, where demand for autonomous logistics solutions is increasing amid workforce shortages, Ottonomy said in a press release.

Founded by Ritukar Vijay, Ottonomy develops AI-powered autonomous delivery robots designed to operate across indoor and outdoor environments. Its flagship product, Ottobot, uses the company’s proprietary Contextual AI technology to enable autonomous deliveries across complex facilities with minimal human intervention.

The company’s robots are designed to help hospitals and enterprises automate the transportation of medicines, medical equipment, supplies and other materials. In healthcare facilities, this could help reduce the time medical professionals spend on logistical tasks and allow them to focus more on patient care.
With the latest investment, Ottonomy plans to strengthen its presence in global markets and expand the deployment of its autonomous delivery solutions across healthcare and industrial facilities.

Enrission India Capital is a Japan-based venture capital firm that invests in early-stage Indian startups, primarily from Seed to Series B. The firm focuses on sectors such as consumer, logistics, climate-tech and enterprise technology. It also works with its portfolio companies to explore international expansion opportunities, particularly in Japan. Its portfolio includes GoDesi, Pico Xpress, Uravu Labs, StackBox and Hexalog.

Ottonomy operates in the autonomous delivery and robotics segment, where companies are developing AI-powered solutions to address last-mile logistics, workforce shortages and operational efficiency across commercial and institutional settings.

In India, autonomous delivery robotics is an emerging segment, with startups exploring applications in last-mile logistics, intra-campus transportation and material movement across healthcare, manufacturing, retail and warehousing.

title: Eggoz’s revenue grows 39% to Rs 180 Cr in FY26; losses widen to Rs 42 Cr
description: Eggoz’s revenue from operations grew 39% to Rs 180 crore in FY26, while its losses widened 83% to Rs 42 crore amid higher employee and advertising costs.
body: India’s egg market is gradually moving towards organised players, with growing consumer interest in branded products, better quality standards and traceability. This shift has opened up opportunities for companies such as Eggoz, which has built its business around sourcing eggs from farmers and supplying them through an organised distribution network.

`The company continued to expand its business in the fiscal year ended March 2026, with revenue growing 39% year-on-year. However, higher employee and advertising costs weighed on its bottom line, which pushed its losses by 83% during the fiscal year.
For context, Eggoz had reported a 78% year-on-year increase in operating revenue in FY25, while its net loss stood at Rs 23 crore.
Gurugram-based Eggoz’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 180 crore in FY26 from Rs 130 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC),

Founded in 2017 in Bihar by Abhishek Negi and Aditya Singh, Eggoz is operated by Nupa Technologies and follows an asset-light, farmer-led supply chain model. The company works with local poultry farmers to improve egg production, collection and distribution through technology, ensuring fresh eggs reach retailers within 24 hours. It focuses on maintaining quality and freshness while helping farmers access better technology and wider markets
Egg sales remained the company's primary revenue contributor in FY26. Eggoz also earned around Rs 6 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 186 crore during the fiscal year.

A look at the expense structure shows that procurement of raw materials remained the largest cost component, which rose 38% to Rs 142 crore in FY26 from Rs 102.7 crore in the previous fiscal. It accounted for over 62% of the company's total expenditure.

Employee benefit expenses increased 50% to Rs 30.8 crore during FY26 from Rs 20.5 crore in FY25. Advertising and promotional expenses saw a sharper jump of 2.9X to Rs 30 crore from Rs 10.5 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Fintech infra startup OneStack raises Rs 12.5 Cr from Shepherd's Hill, others
description: he company claims to serve more than 200 banks across India, including state cooperative banks, district central cooperative banks (DCCBs) and non-scheduled urban
body: Fintech infrastructure startup OneStack has raised Rs 12.5 crore from new investor Shepherd's Hill and existing backers Pentathlon Ventures and AVNM Ventures.

The Mumbai-based startup had previously raised $2 million in a Series A round in March 2025, led by Pentathlon Ventures, with participation from Yatra Angel Network and existing investors 100Unicorns and Venture Catalysts. With this round, OneStack has raised Rs 45 crore across four funding rounds.

The proceeds will be used to expand its presence among cooperative banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), alongside product development in payments, core banking and regulatory compliance, the company said in a press release.

Founded by Amit Kapoor in 2019, OneStack provides technology infrastructure that enables smaller financial institutions to offer digital banking services without building their own systems. Its platform includes mobile banking, UPI issuing and merchant acquiring, QR payments, debit card management and its OneCBS core banking system.

The company said cooperative banks using its platform can now operate as UPI issuers and acquirers directly with the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), under their own bank handles. This enables them to issue UPI IDs to customers, onboard merchants and settle payments through their own payment rails, while retaining customer relationships, transaction data and merchant discount rate (MDR) revenue.

OneStack plans to extend its platform to NBFCs with tools for customer verification and fraud reporting. Its compliance suite includes integration with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). The company is also an Aadhaar OVSE technology service provider, has integrated eKYC Setu and holds RuPay debit card issuance certification and SU3J licenses under credit bureaus.

OneStack has also partnered with a large private sector bank that sponsors more than 250 cooperative banks. The partnership will provide a route to offer UPI issuing, merchant acquiring and its wider banking platform across the network.
The company claims to serve more than 200 banks across India, including state cooperative banks, district central cooperative banks (DCCBs) and non-scheduled urban cooperative banks (NSUCBs).

title: Freshworks posts $245 Mn revenue in Q3 CY26; turns profitable with $18 Mn net profit
description: Freshworks reported a 14% year-on-year revenue growth to $245.4 million in Q3 CY26 and turned profitable with a net profit of $18.3 million, against a loss of $4.7 million in Q3 CY25
body: Freshworks reported a 14% year-on-year growth in revenue to $245.4 million in Q3 CY26, compared to $215.1 million in the corresponding quarter last year. The Nasdaq-listed SaaS company also turned profitable, posting a net profit of $18.3 million against a net loss of $4.7 million in Q3 CY25.
The company’s gross profit increased 15% to $209.4 million during the quarter from $182.2 million in the year-ago period. Its gross margin improved to 85.3% from 84.7%.

On the operational front, Freshworks reported an operating profit of $28.2 million, compared to an operating loss of $7.5 million in Q3 CY25. Its operating margin stood at 11.5% against a negative margin of 3.5% in the corresponding quarter last year.
The company’s non-GAAP operating income rose 62% to $73.2 million, while its non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 29.8% from 21%.

On the expenditure front, sales and marketing expenses declined 2.5% to $98.5 million. Research and development expenses increased 7.8% to $44.7 million, while general and administrative expenses fell 19% to $38.2 million. Consequently, total operating expenses declined 4.4% to $181.2 million from $189.6 million in Q3 CY25.

Freshworks generated $77.7 million in cash from operating activities during the quarter, compared to $63.5 million in the year-ago period. Adjusted free cash flow rose 29% to $73.9 million, with its margin improving to 30.1% from 26.6%.
The company had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and marketable securities worth $697.3 million as of September 30, 2026.

Freshworks also crossed $1 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) after the close of the third quarter, ahead of its earlier year-end estimate. Customers contributing more than $100,000 in ARR increased 25% year-on-year to 1,821, while its net dollar retention rate stood at 104%.

title: Fractal posts Rs 956 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27; profit surges 2.4X to Rs 79 Cr
description: Fractal reported a 20% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 956 crore in Q2 FY27, while its profit surged 2.4X to Rs 79 crore during the quarter.
body: AI and advanced analytics firm Fractal reported a 20% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 956 crore in Q2 FY27, while its profit surged 2.4X to Rs 79 crore during the quarter.
The company’s revenue from operations stood at Rs 956 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 798 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its NSE filings.

Founded in 2000, Fractal generates revenue from analytics and consulting services, along with licensing and subscription fees from its AI platforms, including Cogentiq, fflyfish.ai and Kalaido.ai. The company also earned Rs 29 crore from non-operating income, taking its total income to Rs 985 crore during the quarter.

Employee benefit expenses, the largest cost component, accounted for over 76% of the company's total expenses. The expense grew 4% year-on-year to Rs 657 crore in Q2 FY27. Depreciation, finance costs and other overheads pushed total expenses up 15% to Rs 859 crore during the quarter, compared to Rs 747 crore in Q2 FY26.

As revenue growth outpaced the rise in expenses, Fractal's profit increased 2.4X to Rs 79 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 33 crore in the same quarter last year. However, on a sequential basis, profit increased 10% from Rs 72 crore in Q1 FY27.

Fractal went public in February this year through a Rs 2,834 crore IPO, comprising a fresh issue and an offer for sale (OFS). The IPO also provided exits to existing investors, including Apax Partners and TPG Capital. The stock made a weak debut, listing at a 3% discount to its issue price.
Fractal's shares were trading at Rs 808 apiece, giving the company a market capitalisation of around Rs 14,120 crore.

title: EloElo Group raises $80 Mn in Series C led by Hornbill Capital, NBCUniversal
description: The fresh capital will be used to fund original content across languages, support international launch of micro drama platform Story TV and expand Dolphin AI.
body: Bengaluru-based consumer AI and entertainment company EloElo Group has raised $80 million in a Series C funding round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal. The round also saw participation from MIT Investment Co. and existing investors Play Ventures, Kalaari Capital, Waterbridge Ventures, Griffin Gaming Partners and others.

The fresh capital will be used to fund original content across languages, support the international launch of its micro drama platform Story TV, and expand investments in Dolphin AI, its agentic AI creative suite.

Founded in 2020 by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey, EloElo Group operates Story TV, a micro drama platform, alongside Master, a micro learning platform, Dolphin AI and Voxy AI, an AI companion agent. Story TV offers over 5,000 micro dramas across six languages, with a new drama launched every three hours. The platform records 95 minutes of daily time spent per user, according to the company.

The company owns the content, distribution and AI-powered production engine behind its entertainment business. Across its apps, EloElo Group has over 40 million monthly active users and has crossed 300 million installs.
The latest funding round takes the company's total capital raised to $130 million which includes a $13.5 million Series B round raised in April 2025.

EloElo said it achieved multi-fold revenue growth over the past year and has scaled with profitable unit economics. EloElo began monetising in May 2024 and reported revenue of Rs 69.5 crore in FY25 , with losses remaining largely flat. Its FY26 results are yet to be filed.

Micro dramas are among the fastest-growing formats in global entertainment. According to Omdia, the industry is expected to generate $14 billion globally by the end of 2026. In India, Redseer estimates that 40 million people paid for a micro drama at least once in FY26, while Lumikai's State of India Interactive Media Report projects the market to reach $4.5 billion by 2030.
EloElo Group said it will also use the fresh capital to expand its content slate, with a focus on premium originals, and take its micro drama business to international markets, including the US.

title: Bakingo's revenue crosses Rs 400 Cr in FY26, losses double
description: Bakingo’s revenue from operations grew by 35% year-on-year to Rs 405.8 crore in FY26 while  its losses doubled to Rs 37 crore during the last fiscal year.
body: India's online bakery market has grown beyond traditional birthday cakes, with customised desserts, premium baked goods and quick delivery becoming an increasingly important part of the celebration and gifting economy. Bakingo has tapped into this demand to build a business generating over Rs 400 crore revenue in FY26. However, higher operating costs continued to weigh on its bottom line, with the company's losses doubling to Rs 37 crore during the last fiscal year.

Bakingo’s revenue from operations grew by 35% year-on-year to Rs 405.8 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 300.3 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies .

Founded in 2016 by Himanshu Chawla, Shrey Sehgal and Suman Patra, Bakingo operates an online bakery business offering a range of cakes and desserts, including cheesecakes, gourmet cakes and jar cakes. The company has a presence across 30-plus cities, supported by a network of over 100 kitchens and a catalogue of more than 100 products. Sales of these bakery products remained its sole source of revenue for the firm in FY26.
It also earned Rs 7.3 crore from interests on investments and fixed deposits, which pushed its overall income to Rs 413.65 crore in FY26.

For the bakery firm, raw material procurement for cakes and desserts remained its largest expense, accounting for over 43% of the total expenditure. This cost increased 40% year-on-year to Rs 194.45 crore in FY26 from Rs 138.7 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Employee benefit expenses also rose 40% to Rs 31.6 crore, while advertising expenses increased 35% to Rs 75.4 crore. Commission and platform fees surged over 39% to Rs 53 crore. Other overheads, including delivery and transportation, outsourced support, and power and fuel costs, further added to the expenditure.
Overall, Bakingo's total expenses increased 38.7% to Rs 450.5 crore in the fiscal year ended March 2026 from Rs 324.7 crore in FY25.

Despite recording 35% revenue growth in FY26, Bakingo's bottom line remained under pressure as operating expenses grew at a faster pace, resulting in its losses more than doubling to Rs 36.9 crore in the fiscal year.

title: Peppermint Robotics raises Rs 100 Cr in Pre-Series B led by pi Ventures, Crane Venture Partners
description: The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, develop next-generation robotics solutions and strengthen the company's global operations.
body: Pune-based robotics startup Peppermint Robotics has raised Rs 100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a Pre-Series B funding round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners. The round also saw participation from Asiana Fund.
The investment comprises a combination of primary capital and secondary share transactions.

The fresh capital will be used to expand manufacturing capacity, develop next-generation robotics solutions and strengthen the company's global operations. Peppermint also plans to establish an assembly line in North America in the coming months.

Founded in 2019, Peppermint Robotics develops autonomous robots for commercial floor cleaning and material transportation. The company has expanded its operations to nine countries, with the US emerging as its largest market.

Peppermint's robots are deployed across factories, hospitals, airports, malls, warehouses, hotels and universities. The company also serves pharmaceutical cleanrooms, where its robots have passed qualification testing in an EU GMP Grade cleanroom.

The startup develops its robotics hardware, software and perception systems in-house. Its robots use computer vision and LiDAR to map environments, plan cleaning routes and avoid obstacles. The company also offers offline robots for security-sensitive environments.

Peppermint plans to use the primary capital across five areas, including research and engineering, manufacturing expansion, North American operations, global market expansion and hiring senior leadership and engineering talent.
The company will also expand its portfolio of autonomous floor-cleaning and material-handling robots, while advancing its next-generation cleanroom robotics line.

title: Spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space raises $6 Mn in seed round
description: According to the company, Base 1 is the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation capabilities. It brings together infrastru
body: Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 million in a seed funding round from Japan-based Rebright Partners, Aranya Holdings, Naandi Ventures and existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC. The latest round takes its total funding to over $9 million.
In September last year, the startup raised $3.17 million in an oversubscribed pre-seed round led by Alan Rutledge, with participation from AUM Ventures and Shakti VC.
The fresh capital will support the development of Base 1, technology demonstrations and two upcoming missions, Cosmoserve said in a press release.

The startup has also inaugurated Base 1, a private facility dedicated to space debris removal and satellite servicing. The facility is designed to support the development of technologies for in-orbit repairs, refuelling and the recovery of defunct satellites.

According to the company, Base 1 is the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation capabilities. It brings together infrastructure for designing, building, testing and operating technologies required for satellite servicing and space debris recovery.

Cosmoserve currently sources nearly 60% of its mission components locally. It aims to increase domestic manufacturing by developing critical technologies in-house and reducing dependence on imported optics, avionics and space-grade electronics.

In July 2026, Cosmoserve flew its first payload, Mission Embrace, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The flight hardware was developed in under four months, six months ahead of schedule. However, the robotic capture petals did not deploy as planned, providing the company with data for further development.

Founded last year by Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Cosmoserve is developing a proprietary Dual Spacecraft Architecture to make orbital servicing more cost-efficient. The approach uses two spacecraft to service multiple satellites, instead of the conventional one-to-one recovery model.

title: Moneyview's Q2 FY27 profit jumps 5.15X to Rs 201 Cr
description: Digital lending platform Moneyview reported a 41% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in Q2 FY27, while its net profit jumped 5.15 times during the period.
body: Digital lending platform Moneyview reported a 41% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in Q2 FY27, while its net profit jumped 5.15 times during the period.

Moneyview’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,120 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 794 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The Bengaluru-based company also reported Rs 26 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,146 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 804.6 crore in Q2 FY26.

Founded in 2014 by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview provides digital lending products such as instant personal loans, credit cards, Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and financial management solutions through partner lenders. Its lending partners include Aditya Birla Capital, Northern Arc, Vivriti Capital and Oxyzo.

Impairment of financial instruments increased 18.7% to Rs 286 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 241 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefits expenses rose 41.3% to Rs 97.5 crore from Rs 69 crore during the same period.

Finance costs increased 25.6% to Rs 194 crore from Rs 154.5 crore, while other expenses grew 24.6% to Rs 298.5 crore from Rs 239.5 crore. Overall, Moneyview's total expenses increased 24.5% to Rs 876.5 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 704 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year.
At the bottom line, the company's net profit surged 5.15 times to Rs 201 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 39 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, marking a 415.4% year-on-year increase.

On a half-yearly basis, Moneyview's revenue from operations grew 45.3% to Rs 2,161 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 1,487 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit increased 253.8% to Rs 375 crore from Rs 106 crore during the same period.

title: Amagi's Q2 FY27 profit jumps nearly 29 times to Rs 75 Cr; total income crosses Rs 500 Cr
description: SaaS firm Amagi announced its Q2 FY27 results today, reporting a 28.6-fold year-on-year jump in net profit to Rs 75 crore. Its revenue from operations grew 27%
body: SaaS firm Amagi announced its Q2 FY27 results today, reporting a 28.6-fold year-on-year jump in net profit to Rs 75 crore. Its revenue from operations grew 27% year-on-year during the quarter. The Bengaluru-based company’s revenue from operations grew to Rs 476 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 375 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

The company also reported Rs 26 crore income from non-operating sources, taking its total income to Rs 502 crore in Q2 FY27. Founded in 2008, Amagi operates a cloud-based advertising platform for connected TV (CTV) and programmatic advertising, enabling brands to run targeted campaigns across streaming platforms. The company generates most of its revenue from international markets, with the US as its key market.

Employee benefits expenses, which accounted for 50% of total expenses, increased marginally to Rs 211 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 208 crore in Q2 FY26.  The company did not disclose a further breakup of other expenses. Overall, total expenses rose 9% to Rs 419 crore from Rs 384.5 crore. At the bottom line, the company’s net profit surged 28.6 times year-on-year to Rs 75 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 2.53 crore in Q2 FY26.

On a half-yearly basis, Amagi's operating revenue increased 29.5% to Rs 913 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 705 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit surged to Rs 109 crore from Rs 6.5 crore in the corresponding period last year, marking a nearly 17X increase. The company's shares were trading at Rs 570 as of 3:13 PM, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 12,642 crore.

title: Daksham Growth Ventures raises Rs 125 Cr in first close of maiden consumer fund
description: Registered as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the fund has a target corpus of Rs 150 crore, alon
body: Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment platform of multi-family office and private wealth management group Daksham Capital, has raised Rs 125 crore in the first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund, DGV Fund I.

Registered as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the fund has a target corpus of Rs 150 crore, along with a greenshoe option of another Rs 150 crore, taking its potential fund size to Rs 300 crore.

The first close was anchored by family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and entrepreneurs. The fund achieved the first close shortly after receiving SEBI registration in October 2026.
Led by Shivam Diwan, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Daksham Growth Ventures, the fund will primarily invest in pre-Series A and Series A companies across India’s consumer ecosystem.

DGV Fund I plans to invest Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore in businesses that have established product-market fit and sound unit economics. It will focus on companies with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 25-75 crore and the potential to scale to Rs 300-500 crore in revenue.
The fund’s investment strategy spans four segments: direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C and supply chain businesses, and consumer-focused artificial intelligence (AI) companies.

Beyond capital, DGV plans to support its portfolio companies through governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development and distribution expansion. The fund will also provide board participation, strategic guidance and access to industry networks to help businesses strengthen their organisational capabilities.

Daksham Capital operates across family office advisory, investment solutions, global investing, legacy and succession planning, investment banking advisory and structured lending solutions. The group said its team has advised more than 600 client families and previously managed over $1 billion in assets.

title: Bio-tech startup Venomics AI raises $2.7 Mn in pre-seed round
description: he Bengaluru-based startup aims to investigate this diversity at scale. Its platform combines molecular sequencing and venom biology to build the Venom Atlas, uses AI to
body: Venomics AI, a biotechnology company spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), has raised $2.7 million in its first institutional funding round. The pre-seed round was co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio.
The proceeds will be used to expand the company’s operations, grow its molecular dataset and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities, Venomics AI said in a press release.
Co-founded in May 2026 by Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, Venomics AI combines venom biology, molecular sequencing, AI and experimental screening to discover and develop venom-derived therapeutic leads.

The Bengaluru-based startup is building the Venom Atlas, a platform that connects venom-derived molecular data with laboratory validation and drug discovery. It uses AI to prioritise molecular candidates and tests these predictions through functional screening in the laboratory. The experimental results are then fed back into subsequent predictions and molecular design.
The company aims to use India’s venom biodiversity and its scientific and computational expertise to develop a drug discovery platform for global therapeutic development.

Venomics AI has established the initial architecture of its platform, joined the NVIDIA Inception programme and been selected among the top five finalists for the 2026 Indo-Boston Biotech Bridge Award.
It plans to build a multidisciplinary team across venom biology, computational science and drug discovery, while supporting the validation and optimisation of promising molecules.

Startups in this space are exploring bioactive peptides and proteins found in snake, scorpion and marine animal venoms to identify molecules with potential applications in pain management, neurological disorders, cardiovascular diseases and other therapeutic areas.

title: Tonbo Imaging turns profitable in Q2 FY27 with Rs 23.5 Cr; shares hit 20% upper circuit
description: Tonbo Imaging reported over 20X year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in its Q2 FY26 . The company also turned profitable during the quarter.
body: Defence technology company Tonbo Imaging reported over 20X year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in its first quarterly results (Q2 FY27) after listing on the stock exchanges. The company also turned profitable during the quarter.
Tonbo Imaging’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 183.3 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 8.9 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.

Founded by Ankit Kumar, Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar and Cecilia D'Souza, Tonbo Imaging develops advanced imaging and surveillance technologies for defence and security applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, targeting solutions, missile seekers and fire control systems.
Tonbo Imaging's total income stood at Rs 185.2 crore during the quarter, including Rs 1.9 crore from non-operating income.

As the company scaled up its operations, its expenses also increased in line with scale. Cost of materials consumed was the largest expense component, accounting for over 78% of total expenses at Rs 120.9 crore during the quarter.
Employee benefits expenses remained largely flat at around Rs 12 crore in Q2 FY27, while depreciation and amortisation expenses and finance costs stood at Rs 9.8 crore and Rs 4.8 crore, respectively.
Overall, Tonbo Imaging's total expenses surged over 7 times year-on-year to Rs 153.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.
A 20.6X growth in operating revenue helped Tonbo Imaging turn profitable during the quarter, with a net profit of Rs 23.5 crore against a net loss of Rs 9.6 crore in Q2 FY26.

title: Shiprocket swings to profit in Q2 FY27; revenue rises 35% to Rs 674 Cr
description: Shiprocket turned profitable in Q2 FY27, reporting a net profit of Rs 60 lakh against a net loss of Rs 20.30 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
body: New Delhi-based logistics and e-commerce enablement firm Shiprocket turned profitable in Q2 FY27, reporting a net profit of Rs 60 lakh against a net loss of Rs 20.30 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Its operating revenue grew 34.8% year-on-year during the quarter.
The company's revenue from operations rose to Rs 674 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 500 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statements sourced from the NSE.
Shiprocket also earned Rs 20 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 694 crore during the quarter.

The company's core business segment continued to contribute the largest share of revenue, growing 25.3% year-on-year to Rs 461.5 crore in Q2 FY27. Meanwhile, its emerging business segment, which includes cross-border shipping, omnichannel fulfilment, hyperlocal delivery and e-commerce enablement solutions such as checkout and marketing technology, surged 60.6% to Rs 212 crore from Rs 132 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the cost side, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense, rising 29.8% to Rs 479 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 369 crore in the year-ago quarter. Employee benefit expenses increased 8.3% to Rs 104 crore from Rs 96 crore during the same period.

Depreciation expenses rose 47% to Rs 11.76 crore from Rs 8 crore, while other expenses increased 58.1% to Rs 98 crore from Rs 62 crore. Overall, Shiprocket's total expenses grew 29.5% to Rs 693 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 535 crore in Q2 FY26.

For the first half of FY27, Shiprocket's operating revenue grew 34.3% to Rs 1,266 crore from Rs 943 crore in H1 FY26. Its net loss narrowed 65.8% to Rs 13.12 crore from Rs 38.32 crore during the same period.
The company's shares were trading at Rs 131.50 as of 1:07 PM, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 9,593 crore.

title: Decathlon India’s total income crosses Rs 4,500 Cr in FY26;  EBITDA stands at Rs 424 Cr
description: Decathlon, which offers products across multiple sports categories under one roof. Let's decode how the sporting goods retailer performed financially in FY26.
body: As interest in sports beyond cricket continues to grow in India, people are increasingly taking up activities such as badminton, hockey, boxing, swimming, trekking and skating. This has also created opportunities for brands catering to a wider range of sporting needs. One such brand is Decathlon, which offers products across multiple sports categories under one roof. Let's decode how the sporting goods retailer performed financially in FY26.
French sporting goods retailer Decathlon's Indian arm reported an 8.35% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 4,478 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 4,133 crore in FY25.

Started in India in 2009, Decathlon has grown into one of the country's largest sporting goods retailers. The company currently operates 132 stores across India and is targeting an expansion to 200 stores by 2030.

The sale of sporting goods and apparel remains its primary source of revenue. Its product portfolio includes clothing, footwear, trekking gear, fitness equipment and accessories across various sports categories. The company also added Rs 39 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 4,517 crore in FY26.

On the cost side, the procurement of materials and sporting goods remained the largest expense, accounting for nearly 64% of the overall expenditure. This cost increased 7.4% to Rs 2,840 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,644 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose 12% to Rs 407 crore during the fiscal year.

Other expenses, including rent, franchisee fees, freight, credit card commissions and IT support charges, pushed the company's total expenditure up 4% to Rs 4,435 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 4,264 crore in FY25.

Despite the increase in costs, Decathlon India managed to turn profitable during the fiscal year. The company posted a net profit of Rs 63 crore in FY26, against a loss of Rs 65 crore in FY25. It also reported an EBITDA of Rs 424 crore during the year.

On a unit level, Decathlon spent Rs 0.99 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at 7.6% and 9%, respectively. The company had total current assets of Rs 1,686 crore at the end of the fiscal year.

title: Exclusive: Scripbox to convert into public company ahead of IPO plans
description: Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup Scripbox is set to convert into a public company after passing a resolution approving the move, a step that signals its preparation for a potential public listing.
body: Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup Scripbox is set to convert into a public company after passing a resolution approving the move, a step that signals its preparation for a potential public listing.

According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Scripbox’s board has passed a resolution to approve its conversion into a public limited company by changing its legal name from “Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited” to “Scripbox Wealth Managers Limited”.
As per the filing, the proposed initial public offering (IPO) will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares and an offer for sale (OFS) by certain existing shareholders of the company.

Founded in 2012 by Atul Shinghal and Sanjiv Singhal, Scripbox operates a digital wealth management platform that offers investment products across mutual funds, fixed deposits, US stocks, ETFs and the National Pension System (NPS), along with financial planning and advisory services.
The development comes nearly six months after Entrackr exclusively reported that Scripbox was planning to raise up to Rs 170 crore through a mix of debt and equity.

As part of the proposed fundraise, Scripbox's board had approved raising up to Rs 60 crore from a select group of investors through equity shares, preference shares and convertible instruments. It had also secured approval to raise up to Rs 110 crore through debt from banks, NBFCs and other financial institutions.

In June this year, the company acquired the mutual fund distribution business of Delhi-NCR-based Bluechip Capital, a wealth management firm founded and led by Ravi Kohli for over 33 years. The transaction also saw Bluechip Capital's clients and employees transition to Scripbox.
Scripbox has raised over $70 million through a mix of equity and debt from investors including Accel, LetsVenture and DMI.

title: Specialty chemicals startup altM raises $10.3 Mn led by Rainmatter, Mela Ventures
description: The round also saw participation from existing investors Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact, along with VC Grid and strategic angel investors.
body: Bengaluru-based specialty chemicals startup altM has raised $10.3 million in a Series A funding round led by new investors Rainmatter by Zerodha and Mela Ventures. The round also saw participation from existing investors Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact, along with VC Grid and strategic angel investors.

The company will use the fresh capital to expand its manufacturing capabilities, research and development, customer qualification programmes, and engineering and commercial teams as it moves from pilot-scale production to commercial manufacturing.

Founded in 2022 by former Tesla manufacturing leaders Apoorv Garg and Yugal Raj Jain, altM is developing a specialty chemicals platform that converts agricultural residue into high-performance industrial chemicals. Bioprocessing scientist Dr Harshad Velankar later joined the company as its chief scientific officer.

The company's platform converts lignocellulosic biomass, including sugarcane bagasse and rice straw, into materials for beauty and personal care, textiles, industrial chemicals, construction, packaging and consumer goods.

It uses cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin to produce multiple products from a single feedstock. The process enables agricultural residue to serve as a source of industrial carbon and reduces dependence on fossil-derived raw materials.

Since raising $3.5 million in a seed round in 2023, altM has built an integrated R&D and pilot manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. The facility brings laboratory research, demonstration manufacturing and pilot production under one roof.

The company has expanded its laboratory footprint nearly fivefold, commissioned its demonstration manufacturing facility and advanced six molecules to demonstration scale. Three of these have been selected for pilot plant production.

Its first products moving towards commercialisation include a lignin-derived SPF booster for suncare applications, a cellulose-based rheology modifier and bio-derived ferulic acid for cosmetics and personal care formulations.

title: MakeMyTrip acquires majority stake in Quick Ride
description: Founded in 2015 by KNM Rao, Quick Ride is an asset-light mobility platform that connects people travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling.
body: Travel technology platform MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based shared mobility startup Quick Ride, marking its entry into the ride pooling segment. The acquisition will expand MakeMyTrip’s ground transportation portfolio and strengthen its presence in daily urban commutes.

Entrackr exclusively reported on October 19 that MakeMyTrip was in talks to acquire Quick Ride through its subsidiary redBus. However, the financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed.

Founded in 2015 by KNM Rao, Quick Ride is an asset-light mobility platform that connects people travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling. It enables users to share rides for everyday commutes and offers services to corporate employees through partnerships with companies, IT parks and business campuses. The platform aims to make commuting more affordable while reducing the number of vehicles on roads.

According to MakeMyTrip, Quick Ride’s ride pooling business and brand have undergone an internal restructuring and are now housed under a new entity, Co Ride Mobility Private Limited. MakeMyTrip has acquired the brand and its ride pooling business through a majority stake in this entity. Quick Ride’s promoters will continue to lead the business, while its erstwhile EV taxi business will remain with the predecessor entity, iDisha Info Labs Private Limited.

Commenting on the development, Rajesh Magow, Co-founder and Group CEO of MakeMyTrip, said the acquisition will help the company establish a presence in high-frequency daily commutes within cities, alongside intercity travel. He added that Quick Ride will be housed under MakeMyTrip’s ground transport business, which will leverage its experience in building redBus in India and overseas markets to scale the platform.

Prakash Sangam, CEO of redBus and Head of Ground Transport at MakeMyTrip, said the acquisition will expand the company’s offerings across different travel needs. The platform sees an opportunity to serve the same customers across their daily office commutes and intercity journeys.

Quick Ride has raised funding from investors including Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners), Naspers (now part of Prosus) and Venture Highway. In 2019, the company raised Rs 100.78 crore ($14.4 million) in a Series B round from its existing investors.

The acquisition is part of MakeMyTrip’s strategy to expand its presence across travel segments through acquisitions and strategic investments. In recent years, the company has acquired Savaari in the car rental segment, Happay in corporate travel and expense management, and Flamingo Transworld in regional group holiday packages. It has also made a strategic minority investment in visa processing platform Atlys.

title: Mamaearth parent Honasa profit jumps 87% to Rs 73 Cr in Q2 FY27, revenue grows 36%
description: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027.
body: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 36% year-on-year growth in its revenue during the quarter, while its net profit surged 86.7% to Rs 73.25 crore.

The Gurugram-based company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 731 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 538 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE).
The firm also recorded Rs 22 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 753 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 558 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the expense front, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense component, increasing 38.4% to Rs 220 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 159 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Employee benefit expenses also increased 21.7% to Rs 73 crore. Depreciation expenses, however, marginaly declined  to Rs 11 crore from Rs 11.75 crore.
Other expenses rose 26.9% to Rs 348 crore which pushed its total expenses by 29.1% to Rs 652 crore during the last quarter.
At the bottom line, Honasa Consumer’s net profit surged 86.7% to Rs 73.25 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 39.23 crore in Q2 FY26.
For the first half of FY27, Honasa Consumer's revenue from operations grew 31.2% to Rs 1,487 crore from Rs 1,133 crore in H1 FY26.

Meanwhile, its net profit jumped 2.03X to Rs 164 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 80.5 crore in the corresponding period last year. The firm’s total income stood at Rs 1,531 crore in H1 FY27, compared with Rs 1,177 crore in H1 FY26. The company's shares were trading at Rs 487 as of 1:35 PM, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 15,703 crore.

title: Sleepy Owl’s revenue surges 86% to Rs 82 Cr in FY26; nears breakeven
description: Coffee has become a part of everyday conversations, with more Indians exploring different varieties and flavours. While many people prefer Brazilian or Vietnamese coffee
body: Coffee has become a part of everyday conversations, with more Indians exploring different varieties and flavours. While many people prefer Brazilian or Vietnamese coffee, not everyone knows that India is the world's fifth-largest coffee exporter among coffee-producing nations, accounting for around 5% of global exports.

This growing interest has also given rise to several homegrown coffee brands trying to find their place in the market. One of them is Sleepy Owl, which has grown nearly 4X in the past three years, increasing its revenue from Rs 21.5 crore in FY23 to Rs 82 crore in FY26.

Sleepy Owl’s revenue from operations grew 86.4% year-on-year to Rs 82 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 44 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Sleepy Owl is a homegrown coffee brand focused on the at-home coffee consumption market. Its product range includes cold brew, instant coffee, hot brew bags, ground coffee, and ready-to-drink coffee.
The sale of coffees are the primary source of revenue for Sleep Owl which includes coffee seches, can, bottles, coffee packets and boxes.

On the cost side, coffee procurement accounted for around 22% of its overall expenses. This cost grew 84.3% to Rs 43.5 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses also increased to Rs 9 crore during the fiscal year.
The company spent Rs 20 crore on advertising in FY26. Other expenses, including shipping, legal, technology and other operating costs, increased to Rs 85 crore from Rs 47 crore in FY25.

Sleepy Owl managed to reduce its net losses by 17% to Rs 1.76 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.12 crore in the previous fiscal year. The company is nearing breakeven, with its ROCE and EBITDA margin standing at -6% and -1.8%, respectively. On a unit level, it spent Rs 1.04 to earn every rupee of revenue in FY26.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 02- Nov 07]
description: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $258.1 million across three growth-stage deals and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 28 Indian startups raised $258.1 million across three growth-stage deals and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. The week also saw nine key appointments and one departure, two fund launches, an ESOP buyback and an acquisition.
In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $115 million in the previous week.
[ Growth-stage deals ]

Growth-stage startups raised $190.5 million across three deals this week. Jewellery brand GIVA led the pack with a $100 million funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management. Bengaluru-based consumer AI and entertainment company EloElo Group followed with an $80 million Series C round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal.
Pune-based robotics startup Peppermint Robotics raised Rs 100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a Pre-Series B round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners.
[ Early-stage deals ]

Early-stage startups raised $67.6 million across 17 deals this week. Pune-based health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud led with a $12.5 million Series A round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments. Bengaluru-based specialty chemicals startup altM followed with a $10.3 million Series A round led by Rainmatter by Zerodha and Mela Ventures.

AI-powered clean energy platform Two Point O Capital (TW\.O) raised $10 million in a round led by Transition Venture Capital, while wealthtech platform PowerUp Money secured $10 million led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors including Peak XV Partners, Accel and Blume Ventures.

title: Sugar Cosmetics cuts losses by 41% in FY26, revenue dips 11%
description: After a difficult period for the beauty and personal care brand, Sugar Cosmetics showed some improvement in its financial performance in FY26, with a sharp reduction
body: After a difficult period for the beauty and personal care brand, Sugar Cosmetics showed some improvement in its financial performance in FY26, with a sharp reduction in expenses helping it narrow losses. However, the company continued to face pressure on revenue, which declined for the fiscal year ending March 2026.

Sugar Brands, the parent entity of Sugar Cosmetics, reported revenue from operations of Rs 361 crore in FY26, down 10.7% from Rs 404.4 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr. Including other income of Rs 2.85 crore, its total income stood at Rs 364 crore, compared with Rs 411.7 crore in the previous fiscal.

The decline in revenue came amid a challenging period for the company, which has faced pressure in a competitive beauty market. Its expenses, however, fell at a faster pace than revenue. Total expenses declined 18.9% to Rs 443 crore in FY26 from Rs 546.5 crore in FY25.

Advertising and sales promotion remained the largest expense item, although the company cut this outlay by 28.9% to Rs 119.4 crore from Rs 168 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses fell 21.2% to Rs 58.7 crore, while outsourced support services costs declined to Rs 61.4 crore from Rs 76 crore. Finance costs also decreased 34.8% to Rs 5.6 crore.

The lower cost base helped Sugar Brands narrow its net loss by 41% to Rs 79.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 134.3 crore in the previous year. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.23 for every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.35 in FY25. Its EBITDA margin improved to -20.02% in FY26 from -30.56% in the previous fiscal, while ROCE stood at -129.51%.

The company ended FY26 with cash and bank balances of Rs 10.30 crore, compared with Rs 23 crore a year earlier. The financial performance comes at a crucial point for Sugar. The company recently raised fresh capital at a valuation that was reportedly around 80% below its peak, representing the reset in investor expectations after a difficult period. The funding could provide some room to reassess its business, strengthen distribution and focus on improving the economics of its core operations.

Competition remains another challenge for Sugar. Rival Renee Cosmetics recorded 37% growth in operating revenue to Rs 440 crore in FY26 and also cut its losses by 45%, pointing out the pace at which newer brands are scaling in the beauty and personal care market. The growth puts further pressure on Sugar to defend its market position and regain momentum.

However, Sugar’s FY26 numbers offer some grounds for optimism. The firm reduced its cost base and narrowed losses even as revenue dipped. While Renee’s performance highlights the competitive pressure, Sugar still has an opportunity to bring its business back on track by sharpening its product portfolio, strengthening distribution and improving unit economics.

title: PhysicsWallah cites AI efficiencies for job cuts; offline biz faces profit pressure, earmarks $20 Mn for M&A
description: PhysicsWallah leverages AI to optimise its workforce and explores acquisitions, while its offline business continues to face profitability challenges.
body: Edtech company PhysicsWallah is using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiencies and reduce its workforce requirements, even as it looks to expand through inorganic route — acquisitions. The Noida-based company also continues to face profitability challenges in its offline business, despite the expansion of its Vidyapeeth centres.

During its Q2 FY27 earnings call, management confirmed that its total employee count, which stood at around 19,100, and faculty strength of approximately 7,100 declined sequentially in the quarter. The firm attributed the reduction partly to efficiencies from AI across content creation, quality checks, test paper preparation and evaluation.

Management said AI now writes around 90% of the company's code. The shift towards automation has also helped contain employee expenses, which declined 2.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, excluding ESOP costs. For the first half of FY27, employee expenses were down 2.4% compared to the same period last year.
However, PhysicsWallah continues to invest in technology which stood at Rs 104 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 70 crore in the corresponding period last year.

While AI-led efficiencies have helped improve operating leverage, PhysicsWallah's offline business remains a key area to watch. The segment reported a pre-Ind AS EBITDA loss of Rs 108 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 120 crore in the year-ago period, as per figures discussed during the call.

The offline business reported 9% year-on-year revenue growth to Rs 541 crore in Q2 FY27, while H1 revenue rose 12% to Rs 1,031 crore. Management attributed the moderation in growth partly to lower NEET enrolments and delays in government exam notifications, which affected demand at some of its centres.

PhysicsWallah operates 370 offline centres, including 167 Vidyapeeth centres, compared to 117 in the previous year. Vidyapeeth contributed around 66% of the company's offline business collections in H1 FY27. Management said the standalone Vidyapeeth business is already profitable and expects the broader offline segment to move closer to breakeven. The company plans to add 25-30 offline centres annually over the next two to three years, while keeping a tighter check on upfront costs.

Alongside its focus on operational efficiency, PhysicsWallah is also evaluating acquisitions to expand its online education biz. The company said it is in advanced discussions with a couple of fully online education businesses and is actively evaluating several other opportunities.

title: FamApp’s revenue touches Rs 25 Cr in FY26, profit nosedives 99%
description: FamPay Solutions Private Limited, the entity behind fintech app FamApp, reported a 20.5% increase in revenue from operations and crossed the Rs 25 crore in FY26.
body: FamPay Solutions Private Limited, the entity behind fintech app FamApp, reported a 20.5% increase in revenue from operations and crossed the Rs 25 crore milestone in FY26. However, higher employee and other operating expenses sharply reduced its profit by 99%.

The Bengaluru-based company has reported a 20.5% increase in operating revenue to Rs 25.02 crore in FY26 from Rs 20.75 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.

With Rs 5.01 crore in interest income and Rs 5.2 crore in gains from the sale of investments, its total income increased 13.1% to Rs 35.23 crore during the last fiscal year. It's important to note that the financials presented here are based on its standalone statements.

Expenses, meanwhile, grew 34.7% to Rs 35.18 crore, outpacing revenue growth. Employee benefit expenses increased 23.3% to Rs 16.16 crore, while other expenses rose 47.1% to Rs 18.45 crore. Its technical fees saw a jump of 82% to Rs 10.22 crore in FY26
Consequently, profit before tax fell to Rs 4.8 lakh in the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 5.04 crore in the previous year.

The balance sheet showed cash and cash equivalents of Rs 61.83 crore as of March 2026, up from Rs 20.62 crore a year earlier. Current investments, however, declined to Rs 26.5 crore from Rs 54.6 crore.

The financial performance comes amid changes in FamApp’s reset. In June 2025, Entrackr reported that Elevation Capital led a $15 million secondary round in the company, with a large part of the investment going towards purchasing shares held by co-founder Kush Taneja. Taneja subsequently exited the company.

FamApp’s financial performance points to a business at a critical stage of its evolution. The challenge now is to establish whether its revenue growth can support a more efficient operating model as it expands. The sharp erosion in profitability raises questions about the cost of scaling and the sustainability of its current economics.

title: DriveU’s net profit doubles in FY26; NTV grows to Rs 131 Cr
description: DriveU remained profitable for the third consecutive year in FY26, with net profit more than doubling to Rs 3.6 crore and net revenue rising 14% to Rs 32.9 crore.
body: India’s mobility market is largely dominated by ride-hailing platforms such as Uber, Ola and Rapido, which connect consumers with taxis and two-wheeler services. However, a parallel market for on-demand drivers is emerging, particularly among car owners who seek a convenient alternative to driving themselves. Concerns around drunk driving and road safety have further fuelled demand for such services, creating opportunities for platforms such as DriveU, which allow customers to hire verified drivers to drive their own vehicles.

DriveU continued to scale its business while maintaining profitability for the third consecutive financial year. During the fiscal year ended March 2026, the company more than doubled its net profit to Rs 3.6 crore, while its net revenue grew 14% year-on-year.
The Bengaluru-based company’s net revenue increased to Rs 32.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 28.9 crore in FY25, according to its audited financial statements.

Founded in 2015 by father-son duo Ashok Shastry and Rahm Shastry, DriveU offers trained, verified drivers on demand for customers’ own cars. It also operates DriveU Reserve, a premium cab service, and DriveU Coach, an at-home driving lessons platform. The company operates in 13 cities and has completed over 10.5 million trips with more than 100,000 registered driver-partners.
The company’s net transaction value (NTV) increased 17% to Rs 131 crore in FY26 from Rs 112 crore in the previous fiscal year. Its gross revenue stood at Rs 131 crore during the year.
On the expense side, DriveU paid around Rs 97.21 crore to driver-partners during FY26. Employee benefit expenses remained stable at Rs 13.7 crore.

Direct expenses, including partner incentives, technology costs and trip insurance, stood at Rs 8.35 crore. Meanwhile, business promotion and marketing expenses declined 5% year-on-year to Rs 4.84 crore. Overall, the company’s expenses grew 10% to Rs 30.5 crore during FY26.

On the profitability front, DriveU more than doubled its net profit to Rs 3.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 1.73 crore in FY25, maintaining profitability for the third consecutive year. Its EBITDA grew 58% year-on-year to Rs 2.74 crore, while the EBITDA margin on net revenue improved to 8.3% from 6% in the previous fiscal year.

title: Blue Tokai crosses Rs 500 Cr revenue in FY26; losses up 54%
description: Coffee chain Blue Tokai continued to expand its business in FY26, with revenue crossing the Rs 500 crore mark, supported by its presence in the organised cafe market.
body: Coffee chain Blue Tokai continued to expand its business in FY26, with revenue crossing the Rs 500 crore mark, supported by its presence in the organised cafe market. However, the expansion came with a higher cost burden, as losses widened 53.7% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Blue Tokai’s revenue from operations surged 59.4% to Rs 518 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 325 crore in FY25, according to the company’s consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.

The company also reported Rs 7.5 crore in other income, pushing its total income to Rs 525.5 crore during the last fiscal year. Sales of coffee and related products remained Blue Tokai’s primary source of operating revenue, rising 59.3% to Rs 513 crore in FY26 from Rs 322 crore in FY25. Lease income increased 36.2% to Rs 3.5 crore, while revenue from services stood at Rs 1 crore during the fiscal year.

The increase in operating costs outpaced revenue growth, putting pressure on Blue Tokai’s profitability. The cost of materials consumed, its largest cost component, increased 65.5% to Rs 187 crore in FY26 from Rs 113 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses rose 35.9% to Rs 130.5 crore, while rent expenses grew 59.6% to Rs 26.65 crore during the last fiscal year.
Depreciation costs nearly 2X jumped to Rs 87 crore. Finance costs also jumped 68.8% to Rs 27 crore from Rs 16 crore in the same period.

Other expenses grew 70.5% to Rs 150 crore in FY26 from Rs 88 crore in FY25, accounting for 25% of the total expenditure. Consequently, the Gurugram-based company's total expenses increased 61.7% to Rs 608 crore in FY26 from Rs 376 crore in the previous fiscal year.

On the profitability front, Blue Tokai's EBITDA stood at Rs 23 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 19.4 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA margin declined to 4.44% from 5.97%. The company's net losses widened 53.7% to Rs 83 crore in FY26 from Rs 54 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Blue Tokai's return on capital employed (ROCE) stood -11.94% in FY26. On a unit level, the firm spent Rs 1.17 to  earn a rupee in the same period. The company's cash and bank balances declined to Rs 39 crore in the last fiscal year from Rs 118 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, its total assets increased to Rs 697 crore from Rs 521 crore previous fiscal year.

title: ShareChat parent crosses Rs 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26
description: We are decoding its annual results for FY26. After two years of moderate growth in FY24 and FY25, ShareChat's revenue from operations grew 40% to Rs 1,016 crore in FY26.
body: It has been around 11 years since ShareChat started building its business around India's vernacular internet audience. The company has often been projected as a potential rival to Meta in India, but it is yet to give any meaningful competition to the social media giant. While ShareChat continues to experiment with new formats and has recently entered the microdrama segment to keep up with the trend, the business is still struggling to move towards profitability.
We are decoding its annual results for FY26. After two years of moderate growth in FY24 and FY25, ShareChat's revenue from operations grew 40.5% to Rs 1,016 crore in FY26 from Rs 723 crore in FY25.

Its parent company, Mohalla Tech, operates a vernacular social media and digital entertainment business through platforms such as ShareChat, Moj and QuickTV, targeting regional-language audiences in India.

Revenue from ShareChat's chatroom feature, where users can interact through video calls, accounted for 46% of its total operating revenue. This segment grew 8.8% to Rs 471 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, advertising revenue declined 13% to Rs 252 crore during the year.

On the other hand, QuickTV contributed Rs 293 crore in subscription revenue in FY26. Unlike advertising revenue, subscription revenue is recognised over the subscription period. The company also added Rs 89 crore through the reversal of provisions for doubtful assets, taking its total income to Rs 1,105 crore.

As the company continues to push its new business verticals, its business development expenses surged 8.7X to Rs 335 crore in FY26 from Rs 43 crore in FY25. Following layoffs over the past year, employee benefit expenses declined 16% to Rs 220 crore. We have excluded ESOP expenses of Rs 739 crore and Rs 184 crore in FY26 and FY25, respectively, from this comparison, as these are non-cash expenses.

The company also spent Rs 549 crore on interest expenses, adjusted for finance cost (non-cash). Server costs, content development, legal and other overheads pushed its overall expenses up 14.6% to Rs 1,777 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,550 crore in FY25.

While QuickTV has added a new revenue stream to the business, it is yet to translate into meaningful improvement in profitability. Mohalla Tech's net loss, however, narrowed 15.58% to Rs 672 crore in FY26 from Rs 796 crore in FY25. However, after the finance cost removal, the losses will come down to Rs 123 crore in FY26.

title: Festive boost: D2C startups bag every third funding deal in October
description: In terms of deal value, D2C startups raised a little over $1 billion during the first nine months of 2026, which accounted for around 10% raised by Indian startups.
body: Indian startup funding witnessed a sharp slowdown in October, but consumer-focused brands showed resilience. D2C startups raised around $200 million during the month, which was nearly 30% of the total $678 million raised by Indian startups.

In terms of deal volume, D2C startups accounted for 36 of the 108 deals recorded in October, which was 33.33% of the total. Their share was higher than the 20.36% recorded in H1 2026, when they secured 125 of the 614 deals, and 21.57% in Q3 2026, with 55 deals out of 255. This points to a growing share of consumer focused brands in India's startup funding activity.

In terms of deal value, D2C startups raised a little over $1 billion during the first nine months of 2026, which accounted for around 10% of the more than $10 billion raised by Indian startups during the period.

The strong showing by consumer brands comes at an important time as companies prepare for the festive and wedding seasons, when consumer spending typically picks up. For these startups, fresh capital could help them build inventory, expand distribution, strengthen supply chains and increase marketing spend to capture a larger share of the market.
According to Entrackr's funding data, consumer focused startups attracted investments across categories such as fashion, beauty, food, wellness, lifestyle and home products.

Food and beverages emerged as the largest category with eight deals , followed by fashion and lifestyle and health and wellness, which attracted seven deals each. Home and living brands secured six deals, while beauty and personal care companies accounted for four deals. Together, these five categories represented 32 of the 36 D2C funding deals recorded during the month, accounting for nearly 89% of the total.

Sports and fitness brand Boldfit topped the list with a $42 million Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund. Design led lifestyle brand DailyObjects followed with a $35 million Series C round, backed by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Asia Private Capital.

Beauty and wellness brand Nat Habit raised $15 million in a Series C round led by Trident Growth Partners, while men's bottomwear brand The Pant Project secured $11.5 million in a Series B round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment.

title: Greenjoules raises Rs 150 Cr in Series B led by Amazon funds, secures Rs 100 Cr loan from TDB
description: The company’s renewable diesel can be used in existing vehicles, engines and fuel infrastructure without modifications. Greenjoules is also exploring applications in
