body: Pune-based renewable fuels startup Greenjoules has raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B funding round co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund.

The round also saw participation from Rainmatter, the investment arm of Zerodha, and Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund. Blue Ashva Capital, which led the company’s Series A round in 2021, remains its largest shareholder.

Separately, Greenjoules has secured a Rs 100 crore loan from the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology. The combined Rs 250 crore financing will support the company’s expansion plans.

The proceeds will be deployed to set up a manufacturing facility at Khed City in Pune, with a planned capacity to produce 200,000 litres of biocrude per day from agricultural waste. The facility will be developed in phases, starting in 2027, Greenjoules said in a press release.

Founded in 2018 by S. Viraraghavan, Radhika Viraraghavan, Shweta Viraraghavan and Sethunath Ramaswamy, Greenjoules converts agricultural and agro-industrial waste into renewable fuels using its proprietary Integrated Catalytic Thermocracking (ICTC) technology. Its biocrude is further processed into renewable diesel and bio-naphtha.

The company’s renewable diesel can be used in existing vehicles, engines and fuel infrastructure without modifications. Greenjoules is also exploring applications in sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), green hydrogen and sustainable materials.
India’s renewable fuels sector has attracted investments in companies developing alternatives to conventional fuels using agricultural and organic waste.
In June, Bengaluru-based GPS Renewables secured Rs 635 crore in Series C funding and associated financing to expand its compressed biogas (CBG) infrastructure.

title: RentoMojo reports first quarterly results post listing, Q2 FY27 revenue grows 53%
description: RentoMojo has reported its first quarterly results since listing on the stock exchanges, with its revenue from operations growing 52.69% year-on-year in Q2 FY27.
body: Furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo has reported its first quarterly results since listing on the stock exchanges, with its revenue from operations growing 52.69% year-on-year in Q2 FY27. The company also saw its profit before tax (PBT) increase 54% during the quarter.

RentoMojo’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 142 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 93 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The Bengaluru-based company also reported Rs 1.6 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 144 crore in Q2 FY27.

RentoMojo operates a rental platform for furniture and home appliances, allowing consumers to access products through monthly subscriptions. Its platform primarily caters to urban households across major Indian cities.

On the cost side, the company's total expenditure increased 53.85% to Rs 120 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 78 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 19.5 crore during the quarter, while finance costs, depreciation and other overheads contributed to the overall expenses.
At the bottom line, RentoMojo's profit before tax increased 54.19% to Rs 24.3 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 15.8 crore in the year-ago quarter. Its net profit stood at Rs 18.1 crore during the quarter.

On a half-yearly basis, the company's revenue from operations grew 51.70% to Rs 268 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 177 crore in H1 FY26. Its profit before tax stood at Rs 28.5 crore during the first half of FY27.

RentoMojo made its stock market debut in September this year at a 19% premium over its IPO price. The listing followed strong investor demand for its Rs 1,256 crore IPO, which was subscribed 72.87 times .

title: Kutumb parent posts Rs 405 Cr total income in FY26; profit surges 6X
description: Primetrace's revenue from operations surged to Rs 386 crore in FY26 from Rs 123 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
body: Bengaluru-based Primetrace Technologies, the company behind consumer apps such as Kutumb, Crafto AI, Tarot AI, Sundar AI and Polo, had a strong FY26, with its revenue tripled and net profit jumped nearly sixfold during the year.
Primetrace's revenue from operations surged to Rs 386 crore in FY26 from Rs 123 crore in FY25 , according to its standalone financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

The company operates a portfolio of consumer-focused apps, including Kutumb and Crafto. It follows a freemium business model, offering free access to core features while generating revenue primarily through subscriptions, advertising and user-paid digital services across its platforms. The sale of these services was the company's sole source of operating revenue.
Besides operating revenue, Primetrace earned Rs 19 crore from interest on other current investments, taking its total income to Rs 405 crore in FY26 from Rs 138 crore in FY25.

Advertising emerged as its largest cost head, accounting for nearly 75% of the overall expenditure. The company spent Rs 273 crore on advertising in FY26, a 3.3X increase from Rs 82 crore in the previous fiscal year. This spending is crucial for consumer app businesses looking to build awareness and acquire users across platforms.

Employee benefit expenses grew 26.2% to Rs 33.5 crore, while information technology, legal, travel and other overheads also contributed to the rise in costs. Overall, the company's expenditure increased 2.7X to Rs 363 crore in FY26 from Rs 135 crore in FY25.

Despite the sharp increase in advertising and other expenses, Primetrace managed to significantly improve its profitability. Its net profit jumped nearly sixfold to Rs 41.63 crore in FY26 from around Rs 7 crore in FY25.

On a unit economics basis, the company spent Rs 0.94 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its ROCE and EBITDA margin stood at 9.8% and 6.55%, respectively. At the end of the fiscal year, its current assets stood at Rs 218 crore.

title: Bodhi Tree to acquire majority stake in restaurant chain A2B for $180 Mn
description: business with around 160 outlets in India and over 30 locations overseas. The company employs more than 15,000 people and has a strong presence in Tamil Nadu and
body: Chennai-based restaurant chain A2B (Adyar Ananda Bhavan) has entered into a $180 million deal with Bodhi Tree Systems, which will acquire a majority stake in the company.

Announced on November 12, the partnership will focus on expanding A2B’s operations across India and international markets. The investors also plan to strengthen the company’s management structure and prepare it for a potential stock market listing.

Founded nearly five decades ago, A2B has grown from a sweet shop into a food services business with around 160 outlets in India and over 30 locations overseas. The company employs more than 15,000 people and has a strong presence in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Its business spans restaurants, sweets, savouries and packaged food products.

Following the transaction, Uday Shankar, co-founder of Bodhi Tree Systems, will become chairman of A2B’s board. Bodhi Tree is an investment platform backed by James Murdoch’s Lupa Systems and Uday Shankar.

The partnership will focus on investments in technology, operational efficiencies and business capabilities, alongside strengthening A2B’s management team. It will also work towards making the company ready for a potential public listing.

Commenting on the development, A2B co-founder K T Srinivasa Raja said the business, which he started with his brother as a sweet shop 50 years ago, has become a part of everyday life for millions of families. He added that the partnership with Bodhi Tree would provide the resources and capabilities needed to support the company’s next phase of growth.
Murdoch and Shankar cited A2B’s brand recognition, consumer trust and international presence as key factors behind the investment.
Outside India, A2B operates in Singapore, the US, Australia, Malaysia and the UK.

title: Wakefit posts Rs 452 Cr revenue and Rs 27 Cr PBT in Q2 FY27
description: Wakefit reported a 19.9% year-on-year increase in its revenue during the second quarter of FY27, while its profit before tax (PBT) surged 66.3% to Rs 26.54 crore
body: Bengaluru-based home and sleep solutions company Wakefit Innovations Ltd reported a 19.9% year-on-year increase in its revenue during the second quarter of FY27, while its profit before tax (PBT) surged 66.3% to Rs 26.54 crore from Rs 16 crore in Q2 FY26.
The company's revenue from operations increased 19.9% to Rs 452 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 377 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its financial statement sourced from the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Founded by Ankit Garg and Chaitanya Ramalingegowda, Wakefit offers mattresses, pillows, furniture, and other home furnishing products through its online platform and offline retail stores.
The company also recorded Rs 16 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 468 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 386.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

On the expense front, the cost of materials consumed accounted for 47.1% of Wakefit's total expenses. This cost increased 30.8% to Rs 208 crore in Q2 FY27 while employee benefit expenses rose 29.8% to Rs 54.5 crore during the quarter from Rs 42 crore in Q2 FY26, while depreciation and amortisation expenses increased 17% to Rs 31.6 crore from Rs 27 crore.

Other expenses grew 3.4% to Rs 147.4 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 142.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Overall, the company's total expenses increased 19.2% to Rs 441.5 crore from Rs 370.5 crore in Q2 FY26.
At the bottom line, Wakefit's profit before tax surged 66.3% to Rs 26.54 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 15.96 crore in Q2 FY26.

For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), Wakefit's revenue from operations grew 18.4% to Rs 857 crore from Rs 724 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit increased 10.4% to Rs 39.27 crore from Rs 35.57 crore in the corresponding period last year.

title: Turtlemint posts Rs 342 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27, losses narrow 67%
description: Turtlemint announced its financial results for the second quarter of FY27. The company reported a 35.2% year-on-year growth in its revenue during the quarter,
body: Insurance distribution platform Turtlemint announced its financial results for the second quarter of FY27. The company reported a 35.2% year-on-year growth in its revenue during the quarter, while its net loss narrowed 67.1% to Rs 25.83 crore.

Turtlemint's revenue from operations increased 35.2% year-on-year to Rs 342 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 253 crore in Q2 FY26, according to the company’s financial statements filed with the NSE.
Founded by Dhirendra Mahyavanshi and Anand Prabhudesai, Turtlemint operates a technology-led platform for the distribution of insurance and other financial products.
The firm also recorded Rs 9.5 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 352 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 255 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Turtlemint's total expenses increased 25% to Rs 375 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 300 crore in Q2 FY26. The company does not disclose a detailed breakup of its expenses in its financial statements.

Among the reported expense heads, other expenses surged 31% to Rs 306.50 crore, while employee benefit expenses rose 4.2% to Rs 64.23 crore. Depreciation expenses stood at Rs 4.30 crore during the quarter.
At the bottom line, Turtlemint narrowed its net loss by 67.1% to Rs 25.83 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with a loss of Rs 78.45 crore in Q2 FY26.

For the first half of FY27 (H1 FY27), the company's revenue from operations grew 37.6% to Rs 637 crore from Rs 463 crore in H1 FY26. At the same time,  its net losses narrowed down by 50.9% to Rs 61.42 crore from Rs 125 crore in the corresponding period last year.

title: MGF-Kavachh leads Rs 18 Cr seed round in climate startup mistEO
description: Its CDI platform integrates satellite, radar, Internet of Things (IoT) and ground-sensor data to help financial institutions and businesses assess the impact of weather
body: Thiruvananthapuram-based climate intelligence startup mistEO has raised Rs 18 crore in a seed funding round led by MGF-Kavachh, with participation from Seafund and other investors.
The funding was announced at HUDDLE GLOBAL 2026, the eighth edition of the event.
The startup will use the proceeds to scale its flagship Climate Decision Intelligence (CDI) platform for banks, insurers and agricultural value chains across India and Asia.

Founded in 2019 by Samuel John and Ambarish Narayanan, mistEO combines weather modelling with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning to convert weather and climate data into actionable insights.

Its CDI platform integrates satellite, radar, Internet of Things (IoT) and ground-sensor data to help financial institutions and businesses assess the impact of weather events on farms, assets and loans.
The company’s proprietary forecasting model, Indra, provides weather forecasts at a spatial resolution of 3 km across three time windows: 0-6 hours, 6-24 hours and 24-48 hours.
mistEO also develops solutions for maritime operations, renewable energy forecasting, logistics and mobility, and flood and heavy-rainfall monitoring.

In India, the startup works with NABARD and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) on the DiCRA initiative, which provides climate resilience data for agriculture. In Australia, its livestock early warning system helps cattle farmers prepare for heat stress up to seven days in advance.

title: Ola Electric’s Q2 FY27 revenue dips 39% to Rs 421 Cr; cuts losses by 13%
description: Ola Electric’s revenue declined 39% year-on-year in Q2 FY27 amid a prolonged business slowdown, while its losses narrowed 13% during the quarter.
body: After witnessing a prolonged slowdown over the past eight quarters, electric vehicle maker Ola Electric continued to face pressure on its business in Q2 FY27, with revenue declining 39% year-on-year. However, the Bengaluru-based company managed to narrow its losses by 13%.

Ola Electric’s revenue from operations declined to Rs 421 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 690 crore in the same quarter last year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange.

The company's automotive business generated Rs 420 crore, while its cell business contributed Rs 3 crore during the quarter, before inter-segment eliminations of Rs 2 crore. During the quarter, Ola Electric recorded 41,650 EV registrations, a 17% year-on-year decline.
Apart from operating revenue, the company reported Rs 27 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 448 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 896 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a sequential basis, the company’s revenue from operations fell over 7% from Rs 455 crore in Q1 FY27.

The decline in revenue was accompanied by a reduction in procurement costs, which fell 38% YoY to Rs 295 crore in Q2 FY27. However, employee benefit cost rose 22% to Rs 67 crore. Overall, Ola Electric’s total expenses fell 31% to Rs 810 crore from Rs 1,174 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Overall, Ola Electric’s total expenses fell 31% to Rs 810 crore from Rs 1,174 crore in the year-ago quarter.

Despite lower sales and a decline in revenue, Ola Electric managed to narrow its losses by 13% year-on-year to Rs 362 crore in Q2 FY27. The decline in procurement costs, which fell 38% to Rs 295 crore, helped the company reduce its overall expenses and limit losses during the quarter.

title: Canonicus Capital raises Rs 192 Cr in first close of Rs 500 Cr special situations fund
description: Canonicus Capital follows an execution-led investment approach called the 'Canonicus Method', which combines disciplined underwriting, structured capital solutions and
body: Canonicus Capital has raised Rs 192 crore in the first close of its Special Situations Fund, against a target corpus of Rs 500 crore.

Launched in 2025, the fund builds on the firm's first fund, through which it raised and deployed Rs 311 crore. With the latest close, Canonicus Capital's cumulative fundraising across its two funds has reached Rs 503 crore.

The firm plans to deploy the capital into select investment opportunities across the National Capital Region (NCR), focusing on situations where disciplined capital allocation, stronger governance and active execution can help unlock value.

Canonicus Capital follows an execution-led investment approach called the 'Canonicus Method', which combines disciplined underwriting, structured capital solutions and active, on-ground engagement throughout the investment lifecycle. The firm is supported by a team of professionals from the Indian School of Business (ISB) and Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs), based in the NCR.

As part of its fundraising efforts, the firm had undertaken international roadshows across the Middle East and Singapore. However, the programme was temporarily paused due to the West Asia conflict. The firm plans to resume its international investor outreach as conditions improve.

Meanwhile, Canonicus Capital has promoted Rajan Gupta to Managing Director. Gupta played a key role in driving the latest fundraise and will continue to lead the firm's fundraising initiatives, investment strategy and execution.
The firm aims to identify such opportunities through structured capital solutions and hands-on engagement while protecting investor capital and pursuing attractive risk-adjusted returns.
Canonicus Capital will continue to raise capital towards its Rs 500 crore target corpus for the Special Situations Fund.

title: Neeman’s revenue jumps 73% to Rs 180 Cr in FY26, losses narrow 30%
description: Neeman’s reported a 73% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 180 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 104 crore in FY25, as per its financial statements.
body: Sneakers have evolved beyond footwear into markers of identity and self-expression, shaped by basketball and hip-hop culture since the 1980s. In India, however, the market remained dominated by global brands such as Nike, Adidas and Puma, leaving limited room for homegrown labels.

That is beginning to change as sneaker culture gains traction among Indian consumers. Brands such as Neeman’s, Comet, Gully Labs and Snitch are entering the space with distinct designs, pricing and brand identities, seeking to build homegrown alternatives.
The shift has also caught investors’ attention, with funding flowing into the emerging category as homegrown brands look to tap into growing consumer interest in sneakers.

Among the early homegrown brands to tap into this shift was Neeman’s, which reported a 73% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 180 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 104 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

Founded in 2017 by Taranjeet Singh Chhabra and Amar Preet Singh, Neeman’s follows a direct-to-consumer (D2C) model and focuses on comfortable footwear made using sustainable materials. Its portfolio now includes sneakers, loafers, flip-flops, slides, and sandals

The sale of footwear remains the company's only source of operating revenue. Apart from its core business, Neeman’s also earned around Rs 3 crore, largely through net gains on investments. This pushed its total income to Rs 183 crore in FY26, against Rs 107 crore in the previous fiscal.

For a footwear brand, materials and manufacturing costs naturally take up a significant share of the overall expenses. At Neeman’s, material procurement alone accounted for 38% of its total expenditure. In line with the scale of operations, this cost increased 58.3% to Rs 76 crore in FY26 from Rs 48 crore in FY25.

The firm's employee benefit cost stood at Rs 19.43 crore, while advertising and marketing expenses jumped 57.1% to Rs 45 crore during the year. Legal, technology, finance, travel and other overheads also added to the bill, taking Neeman’s overall expenditure up 53.1% to Rs 199 crore in FY26.

title: Sachin Tendulkar joins Recykal as strategic investor
description: n June 2026, Recykal raised $23 million in a bridge round comprising primary and secondary capital from existing investors and select family offices. The company is using
body: Hyderabad-based waste management startup Recykal has onboarded cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar as a strategic investor.
The company has not disclosed the amount invested by Tendulkar or the valuation at which the investment was made.

Tendulkar will support Recykal’s efforts to promote responsible waste management and encourage recycling across India. He said the company’s use of technology to address waste management challenges and its ambition to drive behavioural change resonated with him.

Founded in 2015 by Abhay Deshpande and Abhishek Deshpande, Recykal operates a technology platform focused on waste management and the circular economy. Its offerings include digital platforms, Deposit Return Systems (DRS), a marketplace for recyclable materials and AI-enabled hardware solutions such as reverse vending machines.

In June 2026, Recykal raised $23 million in a bridge round comprising primary and secondary capital from existing investors and select family offices. The company is using the proceeds to strengthen its technology platform, scale its Deposit Return System and support international expansion.

According to the company, Recykal has channelled more than 3 million metric tonnes of waste, working with around 650 brands, including Hindustan Unilever, Samsung and BMW, and over 5,000 aggregators and recyclers.

title: Exclusive: Dhruva Space to raise $15.5 Mn in pre-Series B; revenue surges 8X
description: Dhruva Space is set to raise Rs 147 crore ($15.5 million) in a pre-Series B round led by IndusBridge Ventures, with participation from AVCF, Blue Ashva Sampada Fund and others.
body: Spacetech startup Dhruva Space is all set to raise Rs 147 crore (approximately $15.5 million) in a pre-Series B funding round led by IndusBridge Ventures, with participation from government-backed Antariksh Venture Capital Fund, Blue Ashva Sampada Fund and others.

The latest funding follows AVCF’s earlier investment of Rs 60 crore in Dhruva Space in July 2026. With a corpus of over Rs 1,000 crore, AVCF was established under the guidance of IN-SPACe and is managed by SIDBI Venture Capital Limited.

Dhruva Space’s board has approved the issuance of 1,573 pre-Series B compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 9,34,429.47 per share to raise the aforementioned amount, according to its filing with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

IndusBridge Ventures Fund led the round with an investment of Rs 60 crore, followed by Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF), which invested Rs 46.9 crore to increase its stake in the company. Blue Ashva Sampada Fund committed Rs 18.22 crore, while PVS Raju invested Rs 10 crore. The remaining amount came from four other investors.
However, according to the filing, the investments from Blue Ashva Sampada Fund and Akshat Greentech, are yet to be received.
According to Entrackr ’s estimates, Dhruva Space will command a post-money valuation of around Rs 2,200 crore (around $230 million).

The company will use the funds to develop and launch communication, earth observation and remote sensing satellites, besides meeting working capital needs, infrastructure development and general corporate expenses, the filing further stated.

Founded by Sanjay Nekkanti, Chaitanya Dora, Krishna Teja Penamakuru and Abhay Egoor, Dhruva Space operates a full-stack spacetech business, offering satellite manufacturing, launch integration and ground station solutions to commercial, government and defence customers. It also provides satellite deployment services and access to space-based data and imagery through its platforms.

title: Hundo Pizza raises maiden institutional round led by Titan Capital
description: Over the next 12 months, the company plans to invest in production capacity, technology and organisational capabilities. It is also exploring additional revenue channel
body: Mumbai-based delivery-first pizza brand Hundo Pizza has raised Rs 7.5 crore in its first institutional funding round led by Titan Capital, founded by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal.
The round also saw participation from Indian Silicon Valley Capital (ISVC), Ankur Rangnekar, Akshay Rangnekar and Haresh Chawla. Wavelength Partners acted as the deal advisor.

The proceeds will be used to expand its presence across Mumbai, enter a new city and strengthen its production infrastructure. The company is targeting an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 60 crore in FY28, Hundo Pizza said in a press release.

Founded in 2020 by Kabir Moorjani and Ronak Rajani, Hundo Pizza operates seven outlets across Mumbai. The company has been bootstrapped since inception and closed FY26 with revenue of Rs 18 crore. It currently operates at an annualised revenue run rate (ARR) of Rs 35 crore.

As part of its expansion plans, Hundo Pizza is developing a 5,000 sq ft central kitchen and production facility in Andheri East. The fully electric facility will support its production requirements as the company expands its operations.

Over the next 12 months, the company plans to invest in production capacity, technology and organisational capabilities. It is also exploring additional revenue channels, including events and catering.
Co-founder Kabir Moorjani oversees product development and kitchen operations, while Ronak Rajani, who founded Mumbai Foodie, acquired by Swiggy in 2024, leads growth and marketing.
The fundraise comes as Hundo Pizza looks to expand beyond Mumbai and scale its delivery-first business.

title: Exclusive: Olyv raises Rs 58 Cr in extended Series B round led by Nippon India Digital
description: Olyv has raised Rs 57.62 crore in its extended Series C funding round led by new investor Nippon India Digital, with participation from existing investor Fundamentum.
body: Personal lending platform Olyv has raised Rs 57.62 crore in its extended Series B funding round led by new investor Nippon India Digital, with participation from existing investor Fundamentum.

The Bengaluru-based company had raised Rs 207 crore (around $23 million) in its Series B funding round led by Fundamentum Partnership Fund, with participation from SMBC Asia, in February this year. Entrackr was first to report the development.

According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr , Olyv has allotted 25,057 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) and 10 equity shares at an issue price of Rs 22,985.82 per share to raise fresh capital.
Nippon India Digital led the round with an investment of Rs 50 crore, while existing investor Fundamentum contributed the remaining Rs 7.62 crore.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the fresh fundraise appears to be an extension of the same Series B round at a flat valuation of Rs 1,104 crore. According to the filing, the fresh proceeds will be used to meet the company's general corporate requirements.

Founded in 2015, Olyv operates as an online lending marketplace through its website and mobile application. The platform connects borrowers and lenders, offering unsecured loans digitally. The startup’s product portfolio primarily includes small-ticket personal loans catering to micro-merchants, self-employed individuals, small retailers, blue- and grey-collar workers, as well as salaried professionals.
Following the latest allotment, Nippon India Digital holds a 4.53% stake in Olyv, while existing investor Fundamentum owns a 12.47% stake.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, Olyv reported a 36% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 338 crore, compared to Rs 249 crore in FY24, while its net profit more than doubled to Rs 26 crore during the same period.

title: HomeLane’s FY26 revenue stays flat at Rs 738 Cr; losses up 23%
description: HomeLane’s revenue from operations remained largely flat at Rs 738 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 748 crore in FY25, while losses grew 23% to Rs 137 crore.
body: India’s home interior design market has seen the emergence of organised platforms such as HomeLane, which aim to simplify the process of designing and furnishing homes through technology-led solutions. The company strengthened its position through the acquisition of Design Cafe, but the integration has yet to translate into meaningful topline growth.
HomeLane’s revenue from operations remained largely flat at Rs 738 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 748 crore in FY25, according to its financial statement filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC) .

HomeLane provides end-to-end home interior solutions, covering the entire process from home design and contract manufacturing to installation and execution. The company offers customised interior solutions to homeowners through its technology-led platform, with these services remaining its sole source of operating revenue in FY26.

HomeLane contributed Rs 535 crore, accounting for over 72% of the combined revenue in FY26, while its acquired entity Design Cafe added Rs 202 crore. Together, the two businesses generated Rs 738 crore in revenue during the last fiscal year.
The company also earned Rs 7 crore from interest on deposits, taking its total income to Rs 745 crore during the fiscal year.

Despite a decline in material costs, overall expenditure remained high. The cost of materials remained the largest cost component, accounting for 34.3% of total expenses at Rs 302.5 crore in FY26. However, this cost declined 5.5% year-on-year from Rs 320 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses increased 13% to Rs 270 crore, while advertising and marketing costs rose 13.1% to Rs 95 crore during the last fiscal year.

Installation and allied costs declined 26.5% to Rs 61 crore, whereas other expenses, including contract manufacturing charges, legal and professional fees, travel and overheads, increased 9% to Rs 153.5 crore. Overall, HomeLane's total expenses grew 1.7% to Rs 882 crore in FY26 from Rs 867 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Higher employee benefit, advertising and marketing expenses weighed on HomeLane’s bottom line, with losses before tax widening 23.4% to Rs 137 crore during the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 111 crore in FY25.

title: D2C menswear brand QB MEN raises pre seed funding led by BeyondSeed
description: Jaipur-based menswear brand QB MEN has raised pre seed funding in a round led by BeyondSeed, with participation from Rajkot Ventures and Prajay Advisors. Snippets
body: Jaipur-based menswear brand QB MEN has raised pre seed funding in a round led by BeyondSeed, with participation from Rajkot Ventures and Prajay Advisors.
The fresh capital will primarily be deployed towards brand building, content creation, customer experience, retention marketing, community engagement and distribution expansion.

Founded by Yash Bothra, QB MEN focuses on printed menswear, offering shirts, kurtas, co-ord sets and jackets. The brand combines traditional Indian prints with contemporary silhouettes and positions itself in the accessible premium segment.
The startup follows a demand-led production model, launching designs in limited batches and scaling manufacturing based on customer response.

QB MEN claims to have reported a repeat purchase rate of 23.8% and is targeting 100% year-on-year growth over the next 12 months. It also plans to expand its product portfolio to include chinos, trousers and kids’ and boys’ wear.
The brand sells through its own website, online marketplaces such as Myntra and Jaypore, and select offline retail stores.

title: Exclusive: Rigi kicks off fresh investment from Google
description: The transaction values Rigi at a post-money valuation of around Rs 670 crore.  Following the investment, Google holds 1.43% in the Bengalru based sratup.
body: Creator economy startup Rigi has raised Rs 10 crore from Google International through an allotment of preference shares, according to regulatory documents reviewed by Entrackr.

The company's board has approved the allotment of 1,543 preference shares at Rs 61,796 apiece, helping it raise the fresh capital. The transaction values Rigi at a post-money valuation of around Rs 670 crore.

The investment marks Google's entry into Rigi's shareholder base and comes as the startup looks to expand its presence in the digital content and entertainment market. Following the investment, Google holds 1.43% in the company.

Founded in 2021 by Swapnil Saurav and Ananya Singhal, Rigi started out by helping content creators, influencers and celebrities turn their online following into a source of income. Its platform enabled creators to build paid communities on WhatsApp and Telegram, manage subscriptions and sell digital products such as online courses, webinars, workshops and one-to-one mentorship sessions.

Rigi followed a platform-led business model, earning through fees on transactions facilitated through its services. The idea was to help creators build a direct relationship with their followers while giving them tools to monetise their communities beyond brand partnerships and advertising.

The company has since expanded into digital entertainment with Rigi TV, a short-form video platform offering bite-sized content, including original shows and micro-dramas. The platform allows users to consume short-form entertainment and generates revenue through advertisements and in-app purchases.

Rigi had previously raised around Rs 100 crore in a funding round led by Elevation Capital in January 2023. Existing investors, including Accel, Stellaris Venture Partners and Sequoia Capital, also participated in the round.
The company is yet to file its FY26 financial results. In the financial year ended March 2025, Rigi reported revenue of Rs 19.92 crore and a net loss of Rs 20.5 crore.

title: SoftBank sells 1.65% stake in Meesho for Rs 1,885 Cr through block deal
description: Japanese investment giant SoftBank has offloaded a 1.65% stake in e-commerce platform Meesho for around Rs 1,885 crore through a block deal on Friday.
body: Japanese investment giant SoftBank has offloaded a 1.65% stake in e-commerce platform Meesho for around Rs 1,885 crore through a block deal on Friday.

According to stock exchange data, SoftBank-backed SVF II Meerkat (DE) LLC sold 7.64 crore equity shares of Meesho at Rs 246.75 per share. The transaction was valued at approximately Rs 1,885.17 crore.

The shares were acquired by a mix of domestic and foreign institutional investors. Fidelity and Societe Generale emerged as the largest buyer, acquiring 1.88 crore and 1.47 crore shares respectively, followed by Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore.

Other buyers included Goldman Sachs Bank Europe, Government of Singapore, HDFC Mutual Fund, Monetary Authority of Singapore, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, Norges Bank on account of the Government Pension Fund Global, Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance, Texas Municipal Retirement System and William Blair Emerging Markets ex China Growth Collective Investment Fund.
Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, FGTFEBP FIAM Select Emerging Markets Equity Commingled Pool and BNP Paribas were also among the buyers.
SoftBank held a 6.84% stake in Meesho as of September 2026. Following the latest transaction, its holding is estimated to have declined to around 5.19%.
The latest stake sale marks another partial exit by SoftBank from the Bengaluru-based company, following its earlier divestment of a 1.73% stake worth Rs 1,650 crore in September 2026.
Meesho reported a 38% year-on-year growth in operating revenue to Rs 4,132 crore in Q2 FY27, while its net loss narrowed 68% to Rs 132 crore from Rs 411 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

title: Paytm shares near IPO price amid MDR rollout and 6 consecutive profitable quarters
description: Paytm shares have inched closer to their Rs 2,150 IPO price, supported by improving financial performance. The stock traded at Rs 1,939.70 on Friday, around 9.8% below its issue price.
body: Shares of One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, have been gradually moving closer to their initial public offering (IPO) price of Rs 2,150 over the past few months, supported by improving financial performance and a positive regulatory development. The stock was trading at Rs 1,939.70 on Friday, November 13, around 9.8% below its IPO price.

The stock could see further upside on the back of the RBI's in-principle approval for its wallet business and the expected implementation of a 40 basis point merchant discount rate (MDR) on eligible UPI merchant transactions. The MDR move could create an additional revenue stream for Paytm and improve the monetisation of its payments business.

Paytm shares have gained nearly 7.7% over the past two trading sessions, touching a fresh 52-week high of Rs 1,960 during Friday's session. The stock has more than doubled from its 52-week low of Rs 930.60 in March 2026.

The recovery comes as the fintech company continues to report consistent profits. Paytm has remained profitable for six consecutive quarters, led by revenue growth, better operating efficiencies and improved cost management.

In the second quarter of FY27, Paytm reported a 28.5% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 2,648 crore , while its net profit jumped 10.7 times to Rs 225 crore. For the first half of FY27, the company posted operating revenue of Rs 5,096 crore and net profit of Rs 491 crore.

Another positive development for the company came on November 13, when the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) granted in-principle authorisation to its wholly owned subsidiary Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL) to issue and operate prepaid payment instruments (PPIs), including digital wallets.

The approval represents an important step towards reviving Paytm's wallet biz, which was earlier operated through Paytm Payments Bank. However, PPSL will need to complete system and cybersecurity audits and obtain final authorisation from the RBI before it can resume issuing wallets.

Apart from improving financial performance and the RBI's in-principle approval for its wallet business, the proposed implementation of a merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI transactions could further support Paytm's growth prospects in the coming quarters.

title: Zetwerk touches Rs 4,600 Cr revenue threshold in Q2 FY27
description: Zetwerk reported an 18.3% year-on-year increase in revenue in Q2 FY27, steered by growth across its manufacturing and ecosystem businesses.
body: Bengaluru-based manufacturing platform Zetwerk reported an 18.3% year-on-year increase in revenue in Q2 FY27, steered by growth across its manufacturing and ecosystem businesses. However, rising operating costs pushed its net loss higher during the quarter, almost a month after its stock market debut in the last half of October 2026.

Zetwerk’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 4,599 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 3,889 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, according to its financial statements filed with the NSE.

Founded in 2017 by Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Zetwerk operates a technology-led manufacturing platform that connects businesses with manufacturers and suppliers across sectors such as electronics, energy, aerospace, defence and industrial automation.

Its manufacturing business contributed Rs 2,546.5 crore, accounting for 55.4% of operating revenue during the quarter. This represented a 14.9% increase from Rs 2,217 crore in Q2 FY26. Meanwhile, the ecosystem business grew 22.8% to Rs 2,053 crore from Rs 1,672 crore.
The firm also reported Rs 54 crore in other income, pushing its total income to Rs 4,653 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 3,937 crore in the year-ago period.

The increase in business scale was accompanied by higher expenses. The cost of materials consumed, Zetwerk’s largest expense component, increased 16.1% to Rs 3,909 crore in Q2 FY27. Employee benefit expenses increased 51.8% to Rs 236 crore, while finance costs rose 32.4% to Rs 132.42 crore.

Depreciation expenses increased 34.5% to Rs 64.55 crore during the quarter. Other expenses also climbed 39.8% to Rs 348 crore from Rs 249 crore in the corresponding period last year. Consequently, total expenses rose 19.6% to Rs 4,689 crore from Rs 3,920 crore.

Zetwerk’s net loss widened 43.1% year-on-year to Rs 88 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 61.5 crore in the same quarter last year. However, its adjusted EBITDA surged 69% to Rs 274 crore, according to the company’s press release.

title: Haber crosses Rs 200 Cr revenue threshold in FY26, narrows losses by 53%
description: Haber’s revenue growth outpaced the increase in its overall expenses in FY26, helping the company reduce its net loss by more than half during the last fiscal year.
body: Industrial automation company Haber’s revenue growth outpaced the increase in its overall expenses in FY26, helping the company reduce its net loss by more than half during the last fiscal year.

The firm’s revenue from operations rose 38.7% to Rs 215 crore in FY26 from Rs 155 crore in the previous fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Haber generates revenue from product sales, mainly chemicals supplied alongside software-enabled industrial solutions.

Product sales remained the main source of revenue, contributing nearly 97% of the company’s operating income. Revenue from this segment increased 37.4% to Rs 209.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 152.5 crore a year earlier.

The company also supplies chemicals alongside software-enabled industrial solutions, with product sales accounting for most of its business. Revenue from services, meanwhile, grew 81.7% to Rs 5.27 crore in FY26.

Haber earned another Rs 18 crore in other income, taking its total revenue to Rs 233 crore in FY26, against Rs 167 crore in FY25. This additional income contributed to the overall financial performance, though operating revenue remained the larger component of its income.

On the cost side, materials consumed continued to account for the biggest share of expenses. This item rose 40% to Rs 133 crore in FY26 from Rs 95 crore in the previous year, mainly tracking the growth in product sales. Employee benefit expenses increased 52% to Rs 38 crore from Rs 25 crore, while site labour and supervision contract costs grew 21.4% to Rs 17 crore.

Other operating costs also moved up. Transportation expenses increased 13.6% to Rs 10 crore, while depreciation rose 17% to Rs 11 crore. Finance costs edged up 4.3% to Rs 10 crore. In contrast, other expenses fell 11% to Rs 26 crore from Rs 29.21 crore in FY25.

title: Kutlerri.ai raises $4 Mn from Narahari Investments to expand AI solutions for restaurants
description: Its first commercial product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius, contacts them through emails, texts and cal
body: Houston and Bhubaneswar-based startup Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million from Houston-based Narahari Investments.

The fresh capital will be used to expand its AI Catering Sales Agent, launch three other AI agents currently in beta testing and develop a mobile-first self-service application for restaurant operators, the startup said in a press release.

Co-founded in December last year by Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy, Kutlerri.ai is building AI agents to help restaurants improve sales, manage expenses and increase profitability. It follows a performance-linked pricing model, charging customers based on additional revenue generated or costs saved rather than fixed subscription fees.

The startup currently has more than 10 signed customers in the US. Its product development and engineering operations are based in Bhubaneswar, while it also operates an office in Houston. Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav are also part of the founding team.

Its first commercial product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius, contacts them through emails, texts and calls, and helps restaurants convert enquiries into orders.

The product was developed with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group in the Washington DC region. According to Kutlerri.ai, the agent helped RASA generate $450,000 in additional catering revenue over 10 months, more than 10 times the amount paid for the service, without hiring additional sales personnel.

The startup currently has one commercially available product, three agents undergoing beta testing and two in development. It plans to expand its teams and launch more products. While the US remains its primary market, Kutlerri.ai is also exploring opportunities in India and other geographies.

title: Desible.ai raises Rs 32 Cr led by Prime Venture Partners
description: Bengaluru-based AI startup Desible.ai has raised Rs 32 crore in a funding round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Invention Engine. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based AI startup Desible.ai has raised Rs 32 crore in a funding round led by Prime Venture Partners, with participation from existing investor Invention Engine.
The fresh capital will be used towards strengthening its agentic AI capabilities, expanding compliance infrastructure, accelerating product development and scaling sales and marketing operations.
Founded in 2025 by Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar, Desible.ai is building an AI-powered workflow orchestration platform for banks, non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and insurance providers.

The platform helps financial institutions automate customer engagement, servicing, collections, underwriting and compliance processes. It initially focused on voice-based automation and is expanding to channels such as WhatsApp, SMS and email.
Desible.ai currently supports more than 25 workflows across revenue generation, risk and compliance, collections, customer service and claims.

The company claims its platform handles over 10 million customer engagements every month and works with insurance providers, while more than 40 BFSI institutions are using or evaluating its solutions.

Its platform integrates with existing enterprise systems and uses predefined decision-making rules to ensure customer consent, regulatory disclosures and escalation procedures are followed. The compliance framework is aligned with requirements from IRDAI, RBI, TRAI and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.

title: Exclusive: Baaz Bikes to kick off Series B round led by BIG Capital
description: Full-stack electric vehicle ecosystem for gig workers, Baaz Bikes is set to raise its Series B funding round led by BIG Capital, with participation from Kalaari Capital.
body: Full-stack electric vehicle ecosystem for gig workers, Baaz Bikes is set to raise its Series B funding round led by BIG Capital, with participation from existing investor Kalaari Capital and Aravind Sanka.
The company's board has approved the issuance of 6,105 Series B preference shares at an issue price of Rs 75,716 each to raise Rs 46.22 crore, according to regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr .

BIG Capital will lead the round with an investment of Rs 38 crore, while Kalaari Capital will contribute Rs 8 crore. The remaining amount will be invested by Aravind Sanka. The ongoing Series B round appears to be part of a larger fundraise, with the company likely to bring in additional capital as the round progresses.

According to Entrackr's estimates, the transaction pegs Baaz Bikes' post-money valuation at around Rs 325 crore ($34 million). This valuation could change if the company raises additional capital in the ongoing round.
The fresh proceeds will be used towards capital expenditure, product development, and working capital requirements, as per the company's filings.

Founded by Anubhav Sharma and Shubham Srivastava, Baaz Bikes operates a full-stack electric mobility platform focused on gig workers. The company provides electric scooters on a subscription basis to delivery partners working with platforms such as Zomato, Swiggy, Zepto and Amazon. Its subscription model also covers multiple battery swaps, helping delivery partners avoid the upfront cost of purchasing an electric vehicle.
Baaz Bikes had raised approximately $12 million (around Rs 100 crore) before the current Rs 46.22 crore Series B round, including its July 2025 extended Series A funding.

The company is building its business around the growing demand for electric two-wheelers in the last-mile delivery segment, where delivery partners depend on affordable and reliable mobility solutions.

title: FirstCry nears Rs 2,400 Cr revenue in Q2 FY27, losses narrow 75%
description: Omnichannel retailer FirstCry, reported a 14.1% year-on-year growth in revenue in Q2 FY27, while the company narrowed its losses by 75% during the quarter.
body: Brainbees Solutions, the parent company of kids-focused omnichannel retailer FirstCry, reported a 14.1% year-on-year growth in revenue in Q2 FY27, while the company narrowed its losses by 75% during the quarter.
The company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 2,396 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,099 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
On a quarterly basis, FirstCry's revenue from operations increased 13.8% to Rs 2,396 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 2,106 crore in Q1 FY27.

The Pune-based company also recorded Rs 42 crore in other income, pushing its total income to Rs 2,438 crore in Q2 FY27. On the expense front, material procurement remained the largest expense head, rising 16.9% year-on-year to Rs 1,554 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,329 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Employee benefit expenses declined 10.8% to Rs 181 crore from Rs 203 crore in Q2 FY26.

Meanwhile, depreciation expenses fell 1.5% to Rs 97 crore, while finance costs also declined to Rs 39 crore during the quarter. Other expenses increased 12.6% year-on-year to Rs 568 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 504.5 crore in the year-ago period.
Overall, FirstCry's total expenses increased 12.3% year-on-year to Rs 2,439 crore during the quarter, compared with Rs 2,171 crore in Q2 FY26.
On the bottom line, the company narrowed its net loss by 75% to Rs 12.6 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 50.5 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

For the first half of FY27, FirstCry's revenue from operations increased 13.6% to Rs 4,502 crore from Rs 3,962 crore in H1 FY26. Its net loss narrowed 51.7% to Rs 56.54 crore during the six-month period, compared with Rs 117 crore in the corresponding period last year.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 09- Nov 14]
description: This week, 12 Indian startups raised $31.3 million across two growth-stage and 10 early-stage deals, including five undisclosed rounds. The week also saw nine key appointments, two exits, three fund launches and one acquisition.
body: This week, 12 Indian startups raised $31.3 million across two growth-stage and 10 early-stage deals, including five undisclosed rounds. The week also saw nine key appointments, two exits, three fund launches and one acquisition.
In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $258.1 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]

Growth-stage startups raised $22 million across two deals this week. Pune-based renewable fuels startup Greenjoules has raised Rs 150 crore in a Series B round co-led by Amazon’s Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund, with participation from Rainmatter, Singularity’s Strategic Autonomy Fund and existing investor Blue Ashva Capital.
Personal lending platform Olyv has raised Rs 57.62 crore in its extended Series C funding round led by new investor Nippon India Digital, with participation from existing investor Fundamentum.
[Early-stage deals]

Early-stage startups raised $9.3 million across five deals this week. Bengaluru-based AI startup Desible.ai secured Rs 32 crore in a round led by Prime Venture Partners, while healthcare AI startup Froncort.AI raised $2.3 million from Google.org. Climate intelligence startup mistEO also raised Rs 18 crore in a seed round led by MGF-Kavachh, with participation from Seafund.

Creator economy startup Rigi raised Rs 10 crore from Google, while Mumbai-based delivery-first pizza brand Hundo Pizza secured Rs 7.5 crore in its first institutional funding round led by Titan Capital.

title: AI CRM startup Dreamteam raises $53 Mn from Accel, Premji Invest, others
description: AI-native CRM startup Dreamteam has raised $53 million in a funding round with participation from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.
body: AI-native CRM startup Dreamteam has raised $53 million in a funding round with participation from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.
Headquartered in California, the company plans to extend its platform to other stages of the customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding, customer success and upselling.

Founded in 2025 by Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy, Dreamteam is developing a customer relationship management (CRM) platform that uses AI agents to manage customer data and automate sales-related tasks.

The platform is built around a system called Company Brain, which gathers information from emails, calendars, meetings, customer conversations and connected tools. It uses this information to maintain a shared record of customer interactions and business activities.

Dreamteam has four AI agents that handle different functions. Rachel conducts account research, Sally drafts follow-up emails and suggests deal updates, Raj monitors the sales pipeline for potential risks, while Alex manages CRM setup and administrative tasks through conversational commands.

The agents can also prepare meeting briefs, track commitments and identify potential risks in sales pipelines. The company said its AI agents propose actions, while sales teams approve updates and outgoing communications.
Dreamteam said hundreds of companies across sectors such as AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing and consulting use its platform. Its customers include DMS Health, InVideo and Plex.

The three founders previously held senior positions at Freshworks and were involved in scaling the company from its early startup stage through its IPO. They collectively have over 25 years of experience in building and selling B2B software.

title: FRND posts Rs 367 Cr revenue in FY26; profit jumps 10X
description: FRND has reported an 88% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 367 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 195 crore in FY25, according to the company's press release.
body: Voice-based social networking platform FRND has reported an 88% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 367 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 195 crore in FY25, according to the company's press release.

Its net profit jumped nearly 10 times to Rs 19.27 crore during the fiscal year, from Rs 2 crore in the previous fiscal. The company's EBITDA also surged to Rs 22.37 crore in FY26 from Rs 40 lakh in FY25, marking a significant improvement in its operating performance.

According to the company, the growth came from stronger monetisation and user engagement across India, particularly in smaller towns and cities. Its international markets, including the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region and the US, contributed 7.2% to its revenue.

FRND said it had nearly 4.5 million monthly active users, who spend an average of 30 minutes daily on the platform. Based on its October 2026 revenue, the startup claimed an annualised revenue run-rate of Rs 600 crore.

Founded in 2019 by Bhanu Pratap Singh Tanwar and Harshvardhan Chhangani, FRND operates a voice-based social networking platform focused on users in Tier II-IV towns and villages. The platform allows users to purchase virtual coins to access interactive experiences, including voice chat rooms, radio and social games.

The company also said it paid Rs 136 crore to creators in FY26, up 72% year-on-year. Its advertising and marketing expenditure increased to Rs 153 crore from Rs 84 crore in FY25, as it continued to spend on user acquisition and brand campaigns.
FRND further said it invested close to Rs 5 crore in moderation and AI-based tools to identify abusive behaviour, fraudulent accounts and suspicious payment activity.
The company claimed FY26 was its third consecutive profitable year and said it would continue investing in its creator ecosystem, product development, safety tools and international expansion.

title: Oister Global launches Rs 600 Cr deep tech fund to back growth-stage startups
description: It will primarily invest in revenue-generating businesses that have moved beyond the technology development stage. These companies are expected to have proven products,
body: Oister Global, an India-focused private markets asset manager, has launched a growth-stage deep tech fund with a target corpus of Rs 400 crore and a greenshoe option of Rs 200 crore, taking its potential size to Rs 600 crore.

Registered as Oister Global Scheme II, a SEBI Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), the Oister Deep Tech Fund will build a portfolio of 8-10 companies operating in India's frontier technology ecosystem.
The fund will have a tenure of six years, with an option to extend it by up to two years with investor approval. It will follow Oister's glass-box investment approach.
The fund will focus on sectors such as space technology, defence and aerospace, semiconductors and electronics, quantum technologies, advanced mobility, advanced materials and energy storage.

It will primarily invest in revenue-generating businesses that have moved beyond the technology development stage. These companies are expected to have proven products, proprietary intellectual property and defensible patents in India and international markets.
The investment strategy will also prioritise companies with multiple revenue streams, domestic and international customers, policy support and a defined path to liquidity.
The capital will be deployed to support production expansion, order execution and wider commercial adoption of these technologies.
The fund will target companies led by founders with scientific and engineering backgrounds, particularly those emerging from India's research and strategic institutions.

title: Spice brand Zoff crosses Rs 150 Cr revenue in FY26; losses widen to Rs 21 Cr
description: Shark Tank-featured spice brand Zoff's revenue crossed Rs 150 crore in FY26. However, losses widened 20% year-on-year as its bottom line remained in the red.
body: Shark Tank-featured spice brand Zoff continued to expand its presence in India's competitive packaged spices market in FY26 as it took on established players such as MDH, Everest, Catch and Pushp. The company's revenue growth picked up during the year and crossed the Rs 150 crore mark. However, its bottom line remained in the red as losses widened 20% year-on-year.

Raipur-based Zoff's revenue from operations rose over 48% year-on-year to Rs 152.4 crore in the financial year ending March 2026, compared to Rs 102.7 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Co-founded by Akash and Ashish Agrawal in 2018, Zoff sells a range of whole and powdered spices, blended masalas, seasonings and other kitchen essentials. The company sources, processes and packages spices under its own brand and sells them through online marketplaces, its website and offline retail channels.
The sale of products was the only source of operating revenue for the company during the year for the company.

For the spice brand, cost of materials remained the largest expense for the spice brand, which accounted for 56% of its overall expenditure. This cost increased 38.6% to Rs 101.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 73 crore in FY25 .

Advertising and promotional expenses emerged as another major cost driver. Zoff spent Rs 29.9 crore on advertising in FY26, a 2.5X increase from Rs 12.1 crore in the previous fiscal year. The expense accounted for 16.6% of its total expenditure as the company stepped up spends on brand promotion and customer acquisition to expand its market presence.
Employee benefit expenses more than doubled to Rs 10.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 5.15 crore in FY25. Discounting charges also increased 53% to Rs 8.9 crore.

Other expenses, which included legal & professional, commission added Rs 29 crore to the total cost during the year. Overall Zoff's total expenses increased 50% to Rs 180 crore in FY26 from Rs 120 crore in the previous fiscal year.

title: Exclusive: Xpressbees raises Rs 100 Cr debt from BlackSoil
description: E-commerce-focused logistics company Xpressbees has raised Rs 100 crore in debt from BlackSoil to meet its working capital requirements and support its operations.
body: E-commerce-focused logistics company Xpressbees has raised Rs 100 crore (around $10 million) in debt from BlackSoil to meet its working capital requirements and support its operations.

The company's board has approved the allotment of 200 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at an issue price of Rs 5 lakh each, aggregating to Rs 100 crore, according to its regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.
The debentures carry an annual coupon rate and have a tenure of three years. The proceeds will be used to meet the company's working capital requirements, the filing added.

Founded in 2015 by Amitava Saha and Supam Maheshwari, Xpressbees started as the logistics arm of FirstCry before becoming an independent company. The Pune-based firm provides first-mile, last-mile, reverse logistics, warehousing and cross-border logistics services to e-commerce companies and other businesses.

The company has raised significant capital over the years to expand its logistics network and strengthen its technology-led operations. In February 2022, Xpressbees entered the unicorn club after raising $300 million in a Series F funding round led by Blackstone Growth, TPG Growth and ChrysCapital. It later raised $80 million in a Series G round led by Teachers' Venture Growth in November 2023.

On the financial front, Xpressbees reported flat growth in operating revenue to Rs 2,874 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 2,831 crore in FY24. However, its net loss widened to Rs 370 crore in FY25 from Rs 200 crore in the previous fiscal. The company is yet to file its annual results for FY26.

The company competes with Delhivery and Ecom Express in India's logistics market. Its latest debt raise comes as it continues to invest in its operations while navigating a competitive and cost-intensive logistics business.

title: Bharat Semi raises $24 Mn in seed round from Info Edge, South Park Common, others
description: Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in a seed funding round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures.
body: Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has raised $24 million in a seed funding round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures. The round also saw participation from Micromax, Valour Capital, New York-based Gaingels and angel investors Mukul Agarwal and Karthik Sundar Iyer.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate product development, expand its engineering teams in the US and strengthen its go-to-market efforts with global customers.
Founded by Vinayak Dalmia and Vrinda Kapoor, Bharat Semi is developing programmable smart sensors for physical AI applications across cameras, robots, vehicles, drones and other machines.

The startup is building sensors that integrate sensing, processing and AI into a single system, allowing inference to take place at the point of data capture. Its technology claims to reduce data movement between components by up to 99% and system costs by up to 10 times compared to conventional multi-chip modules. The sensors can also be configured for different applications and AI models.

The company is betting on the growing adoption of physical AI. Morgan Stanley estimates that around one billion humanoid robots could be in use by 2050. Bharat Semi also cited a McKinsey study that found no widely adopted intelligent sensor suite currently exists.

Bharat Semi is initially targeting consumer electronics and surveillance markets, where cost, power consumption and latency are key considerations. It aims to develop a common sensor architecture that can serve applications across robotics, automotive and other industries.

Co-founder Vinayak Dalmia previously worked in strategy at McKinsey and private equity, while Vrinda Kapoor is a South Park Commons Fellow and has worked on India's semiconductor initiatives with NITI Aayog's Frontier Technology Hub.

Bharat Semi operates across New Delhi, Bengaluru and San Francisco. Its long-term ambition is to develop a configurable sensor architecture that can serve as the sensor layer for physical AI across cameras, robots, vehicles and drones.

title: Exclusive: Shree Anandhaas raises Rs 110 Cr, valuation jumps to Rs 1,900 Cr
description: Shree Anandhaas has raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Ayra Ventures, with participation from existing investor A91 Partners
body: Coimbatore-based sweets and snacks chain Shree Anandhaas has raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Ayra Ventures, with participation from existing investor A91 Partners, Waterfield Advisors, the company’s co-founders and other investors.

The company’s board has allotted 12,870 equity shares and 22,523 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at an issue price of Rs 31,079 per share to raise the capital, according to documents reviewed by Entrackr .

Ayra Ventures led the round with an investment of Rs 45 crore, while Waterfield Advisors invested Rs 15 crore and A91 Partners infused Rs 10 crore. Ithought Financial Consulting LLP invested Rs 10 crore through an equity allotment in August 2026, while the co-founders collectively invested Rs 7.2 crore. The remaining amount came from several other investors. The proceeds will be utilised to fund the company's growth and expansion plans, capital expenditure, working capital requirements and other general corporate purposes.

As per Entrackr’s estimates, the latest allotment values Shree Anandhaas at around Rs 1,908 crore, a 3.3X jump from its Series A valuation of Rs 575 crore. However, this appears to be part of a larger funding round, and the company’s valuation could change depending on further investments.
In August 2025, the company closed its Rs 175 crore Series A funding round led by A91 Partners.

Founded in 1998 as a restaurant business, Shree Anandhaas entered the sweets and savouries retail segment in 2017. The family-owned company operates a chain of sweets and snacks outlets across Tamil Nadu.

Following the latest allotment, A91 Partners remains the largest external shareholder with a 26.24% stake, followed by Spring Marketing Capital with 2.41%, Ayra Ventures with 2.36% and Waterfield Advisors with 0.79%. Meanwhile, the co-founders M. Manikanden, N.V. Nammalwar, A. Narayanan, K. Venkatesh and M. Amutha collectively hold a 56.54% stake in the company.

The company is yet to file its FY26 financial statements. In FY25, Shree Anandhaas reported a 20.9% year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 284 crore. Its net profit surged 7.1X to Rs 7.64 crore in the same period.

title: AI video production startup Lemonpeel raises $1 Mn in pre-seed round led by Shastra VC
description: The Mumbai-based startup combines specialised AI agents with a model-agnostic engine that routes tasks across more than 300 models, including Veo, Kling and Seedance. A
body: AI video production startup Lemonpeel has raised $1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Shastra VC, with participation from Rukam Sitara and angel investors. The startup is part of the NVIDIA Inception, AWS Startups, Microsoft for Startups and Claude Startup programmes.

The proceeds will be utilized to develop multi-agent platforms for video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery, marketing and go-to-market capabilities to reach more enterprise creative teams, and build intellectual property around faces and creative workflows, Lemonpeel said in a press release.

Co-founded in Sep. last year by Hardik Goyal, Riddhiman Pal and Abhinav Nikam, Lemonpeel builds AI video production infrastructure for enterprise creative teams that brings together video creation, editing, quality checks and delivery through specialised agents and a model-agnostic engine. It works with customers in India and the UAE.

The Mumbai-based startup combines specialised AI agents with a model-agnostic engine that routes tasks across more than 300 models, including Veo, Kling and Seedance. A quality control layer helps maintain consistency in characters, logos and products.

The platform supports translation and subtitles in more than 100 languages and can also be used from inside AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The company is turning the production steps its team currently handles into product capabilities.

Lemonpeel is focused on media execution end-to-end: editing, maintaining visual consistency and preparing content for approval at scale. This is particularly relevant to films and campaigns that need multiple regional language versions and formats. The company plans to expand into MENA, US and Canada.
It competes with the other players in this space such as Runway, Google Flow, Higgsfield, Magnific, Flora, Weavy, and Invideo.

Startups in this space are developing AI-led platforms that automate video production workflows, generate multilingual and personalised videos, enable automated editing, and ensure quality and consistency before content is delivered across digital channels.

title: Sneaker brand Comet clocks 2.6X revenue growth to Rs 74 Cr in FY26
description: Sneaker brand Comet clocked 2.6X year-on-year growth in revenue to Rs 74 crore in FY26, although its losses more than doubled during the year.
body: India’s homegrown sneaker market is witnessing a new wave of brands attempting to challenge the dominance of global footwear labels through online-first distribution, distinctive designs and a stronger focus on sneaker culture. While brands such as Comet, Neeman’s, Gully Labs, One8 are building their presence in this space, their financial performance reflects different stages of growth.

Neeman’s, for instance, reported a 73% growth in revenue to Rs 180 crore in FY26. Comet, a relatively younger brand, clocked faster 2.6X growth to Rs 74 crore, although its losses more than doubled during the year.

The Bengaluru-based company reported revenue from operations of Rs 74 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 29 crore in the previous financial year, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC) .

Founded in 2023 by Utkarsh Gupta and Dishant Daryani, Comet is a Bengaluru-based homegrown sneaker brand offering sneakers and slides for men and women. The brand focuses on contemporary, India-inspired designs and follows a direct-to-consumer (D2C) model, primarily selling through its own website, alongside an offline retail presence.
Footwear and accessories were the company's sole sources of operating revenue in FY26. It also earned Rs 2.2 crore in interest income from bank deposits, which took its total income to Rs 76.2 crore.

However, the sharp growth in revenue came alongside a significant increase in expenses. Comet's total expenditure surged 136.6% to Rs 85.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 36.1 crore in FY25. As a result, its loss before tax widened 104.5% to Rs 9 crore during the year, compared with Rs 4.4 crore in the previous fiscal.

For the sneaker brand, material costs continued to account for the largest share of Comet's expenditure, which jumped 2.4X in line with the growth in sales to Rs 33.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 14 crore in FY25. The expense accounted for over 39% of the company's overall spending.

Advertising and promotional expenses, another major cost component, also jumped 2.3 times to Rs 21.5 crore during FY26 from Rs 9.3 crore in FY25. These expenses accounted for 25% of the total expenditure, indicating the company's continued investment in brand building and customer acquisition.

title: Equirus InnovateX Fund leads Rs 10 Cr seed round in deep-tech startup CountAI
description: CountAI said Knit-I has been deployed across textile companies, including Aarti International, Hams, KPR, Indorama, Jayjay, Zelal, Lan, Nitin Spinners, Sudiva Spinners
body: Deep-tech startup CountAI has raised Rs 10 crore in a seed funding round led by Equirus InnovateX Fund.
The fresh funds will be used to accelerate product development, expand market presence and extend its industrial AI capabilities to more manufacturing applications, CountAI said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2022 by Harshavardhan Thirupathi and Venkataramanan, CountAI builds industrial AI vision systems for real-time quality monitoring on factory floors. Its first commercial product, Knit-I, detects fabric defects on circular knitting machines and triggers stoppages when required.
CountAI said Knit-I has been deployed across textile companies, including Aarti International, Hams, KPR, Indorama, Jayjay, Zelal, Lan, Nitin Spinners, Sudiva Spinners and Tosrifa Group.

The company develops its own cameras, AI motherboards and software. It said it has reduced the power consumption of its AI computing and camera system from around 700 watts in its early prototype to approximately 10 watts, while achieving inference speeds of over 100 frames per second. The figures exclude lighting and other system components.
CountAI plans to extend its technology to industrial surface quality control and automated manufacturing applications.
The segment also includes Bengaluru-based SwitchOn, which raised $8 million in a pre-Series B round in July, led by IvyCap Ventures, with participation from SIG Tattva and Trifecta Capital.

Tiruchirappalli-based AugurAI raised Rs 2 crore from Campus Angels Network in October to strengthen its imaging hardware and AI-powered inspection capabilities. Chennai-based Detect Technologies is another player in industrial AI monitoring.

title: Handpickd posts Rs 28.6 Cr revenue and Rs 43 Cr loss in FY26
description: Handpickd's revenue from operations jumped 3.3X to Rs 28.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 8.7 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the RoC
body: Farm-to-fresh delivery has proved to be a difficult business to crack, with several startups in the segment shutting shop despite raising sizeable capital. High wastage, limited room for expansion and the challenge of building a sustainable supply chain have made it difficult for companies to scale the business profitably.
However, Gurugram-based Handpickd (formerly Sorted) is betting on a different approach. The startup not only managed to scale its revenue during FY26 but also raised a Series A round during the year.
Handpickd's revenue from operations jumped 3.3X to Rs 28.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 8.7 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2024 by Anant Goel, co-founder of Milkbasket, along with Nitin Gupta and Sahil Madan, Handpickd operates an inventory-free model without warehouses or dark stores. Instead of forecasting demand and stocking products, the company collects orders from customers, procures the required quantities directly from farmers and delivers them to customers the following morning.

The sale of products remained its sole source of operating revenue. The company also earned Rs 1.2 crore in interest income from deposits, taking its total income to Rs 29.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 8.91 crore in FY25.

On the cost front, procurement of materials remained the largest expense, accounting for nearly 40% of its overall expenditure. This cost surged 3.7X to Rs 28.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 7.7 crore in the previous fiscal year.

Employee benefit expenses nearly tripled to Rs 13 crore, while packaging and delivery expenses stood at Rs 12 crore. As a result, Handpickd's total expenditure jumped 3.6X to Rs 72.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 20.1 crore in FY25.

The rapid scale-up came with a corresponding increase in losses. The company's net loss widened 3.85X to Rs 43.1 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 11.2 crore in FY25. On a unit level, the company spent Rs 2.55 to earn a rupee in FY26, up from Rs 2.31 in FY25.

title: Wealthtech startup finny.club raises Rs 5.3 Cr in angel round
description: The proceeds will be used for AI-led product development, expansion of its financial advisory team, and content and marketing initiatives, finny.club said in a press release.
body: Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup finny.club has raised Rs 5.3 crore (approximately $560K) in an angel funding round. The round saw participation from Ramanathan RV, founder of Hyperface and Juspay, Anil Goel, Uday Sodhi, Aditya Pittie and Zorvian LLP, an angel syndicate, among others.
The proceeds will be used for AI-led product development, expansion of its financial advisory team, and content and marketing initiatives, finny.club said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2024 by Rohit Tuteja and Sachin Kamkar, finny.club helps salaried families plan their finances and work towards financial independence.

The startup operates as an AI-first personal CFO, combining artificial intelligence with human financial advisers to offer personalised financial planning. Using India's Account Aggregator framework, its platform consolidates users' financial information in around 60 seconds and analyses their spending patterns, investment portfolios and debt obligations.

Based on users' financial profiles and long-term goals, the platform estimates the corpus required to achieve financial independence and projects retirement timelines. It also recommends investments and financial products based on users' risk profiles and facilitates transactions with their consent.
finny.club is a SEBI-registered investment adviser (RIA) and follows a fee-only advisory model, charging no commission on investments.

The funding comes amid growing interest in retirement planning and the Financial Independence, Retire Early (FIRE) movement among India's working population. However, access to personalised financial advice remains limited. India has around 1,000 SEBI-registered investment advisers, according to the company.
Through its platform, finny.club aims to make financial advisory services accessible to mass-affluent Indian households, a segment that has traditionally had limited access to such services.

title: AI infra startup JohnAIC raises $1.9 Mn in pre-seed round
description: Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partner. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based sovereign AI infrastructure startup JohnAIC has raised $1.9 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Crane Venture Partners, with participation from Neon Fund.
The proceeds will be used to expand its manufacturing, configuration and supply capabilities for AI servers. It aims to scale production capacity to up to 100 AI servers per month.

Founded by Sasank Chilamkurthy, JohnAIC builds on-premise AI infrastructure combining GPU servers, inference software, optimised open-source models and local data management. Its integrated systems are designed to help enterprises deploy AI within their own environments while retaining control over computing resources, models and data.
