The startup serves public sector organisations and large enterprises, including banks, healthcare companies and public sector undertakings (PSUs). For BFSI institutions, its systems enable AI deployment behind organisational firewalls and are designed to support DPDP and RBI requirements.

JohnAIC is also working with Andhra Pradesh Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL). Its server infrastructure has been deployed for routine operational surveys, converting field data into real-time insights.
The company is expanding its factory and supply chain infrastructure to address demand from Indian enterprises building private AI environments and neocloud infrastructure.

title: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs raises $47 Mn in equity and debt
description: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt. The round includes $26 Mn in equity and $21 Mn in venture debt.
body: Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt. The round includes $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt.

According to the press release, Accel led the equity round, which also saw participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence through Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading, and angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic.
The remaining $21 million venture debt was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.

Founded in 2026 by Manish Agarwal, former CEO of Nazara Technologies, and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs works with AI research labs and robotics companies that need real-world data to train their systems. The founders had earlier co-founded KGeN, a platform focused on building a network of verified users.

The startup collects data by recording how people perform everyday tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes. This information is processed and shared with companies developing robots, helping them understand how humans perform different jobs and interact with their surroundings.

Humyn Labs claims to have crossed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of starting operations. It currently runs data collection and processing operations across more than 20 countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.

As per the release, the fresh capital will be used to expand its operations in Brazil, South Korea and India, strengthen its data collection hardware and processing capabilities, and build a larger presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.
Earlier in April 2026, the company had announced a $20 million commitment towards expanding its data collection infrastructure across India, Southeast Asia, Latin America and West Asia.

title: IvyCap Ventures leads $11 Mn Series B round in robotics company Botsync
description: The fresh funds will be used to develop AI capabilities for its SyncOS platform, including throughput optimisation, predictive maintenance and operational analytics. Th
body: Robotics company Botsync has raised $11 million in a Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures. The round also saw participation from Capital 2B, AppWorks, Iterative, AngelCentral, Genesis Alternate Investments and angel investor Nalin Advani.
The startup had previously raised $5.2 million in a Series A round in June 2024, led by Capital 2B and Betatron Venture Group, with participation from other investors.
The latest fundraise follows a Series A extension in January 2026, led by SGInnovate. With this, Botsync has raised over $20 million to date.

The fresh funds will be used to develop AI capabilities for its SyncOS platform, including throughput optimisation, predictive maintenance and operational analytics. The company will also improve the performance and reliability of its MAG robot range, Botsync said in a press release.
Co-founded in 2019 by Rahul Nambiar, Nikhil Venkatesh and Prashant Trivedi, Botsync develops robotics solutions for automotive and FMCG manufacturers and distribution centres.

Its SyncOS platform connects robots, machines and enterprise systems through a no-code interface to manage workflows across industrial facilities. Its MAG autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) handle material movement across production, storage and distribution operations.
Botsync has offices in Singapore and India and operates across Indonesia, Thailand and Australia. Its customers include Caterpillar, Ford, Nestlé and Honda.

The company plans to expand its teams across engineering, project delivery, customer success and sales. It will also strengthen its presence in Australia, build its go-to-market operations in the US and expand its partner network.

title: FirstClub reports Rs 64 Cr revenue and Rs 97 Cr loss in FY26
description: The Bengaluru-based FirstClub reported revenue from operations of Rs 64 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, with a Rs 97.5 crore loss.
body: India’s quick commerce market has largely been built around speed and convenience, with platforms such as Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto competing to deliver everyday essentials within minutes. As the market expands, however, some players are looking to move beyond delivery speed and tap into consumers seeking premium products, better quality and curated grocery assortments.

Founded last year, FirstClub is looking to tap into this segment by offering premium grocery products, targeting consumers willing to pay more for quality ingredients, freshness and curated assortments. Its entry comes as grocery delivery attracts growing investor interest and competition in India’s consumer internet market.

Despite entering a market dominated by established quick commerce players, FirstClub is betting on a differentiated assortment and a quality-led supply chain to build its business. The strategy, however, came with significant operating costs in its first year of operations.
The Bengaluru-based startup reported revenue from operations of Rs 64 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

A closer look at its revenue shows that the sale of goods contributed Rs 55.5 crore, around 87% of the total operating revenue. The remaining Rs 8.5 crore came from services, including delivery, warehousing and packaging, marketing services and licence fees.
The firm also earned around Rs 7.9 crore from interests on fixed deposits, which took its overall income in FY26 to Rs 71.9 crore.
On the expense side, the cost of materials was the largest expense component at Rs 53.9 crore, which accounted for 31.8% of the overall expenditure.

Employee benefit expenses emerged as the second-largest cost at Rs 45.3 crore, which included Rs 6.5 crore worth of ESOP expenses. The company also spent Rs 13.4 crore on advertising and promotional activities.

title: Fatehpuria Hygiene raises Rs 100 Cr in maiden equity round led by Madhu Kela
description: The expansion will focus on strengthening warehousing infrastructure, upgrading technology capabilities, scaling distribution networks and developing end-to-end fulfilm
body: Fatehpuria Hygiene, a trade, supply chain and fulfilment company, has raised Rs 100 crore in its maiden equity funding round led by investor Madhu Kela.
The proceeds will be used to expand its presence across more than 50 major cities over the next 24 months and build an AI-enabled supply chain network, the company said in a press release.

The expansion will focus on strengthening warehousing infrastructure, upgrading technology capabilities, scaling distribution networks and developing end-to-end fulfilment solutions for brands and retail platforms.

Founded in 2017 by Gautam Fatehpuria, the company operates in FMCG and hygiene distribution, warehousing and supply chain management. It serves omnichannel brands across e-commerce, quick commerce and modern trade.

Over the years, Fatehpuria Hygiene has built a warehousing, distribution and fulfilment network across 16 states. Its clientele includes Unilever, Wipro, Kimberly-Clark, Flipkart, Amazon, Myntra, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Blinkit, DMart, Meesho and FirstCry.

The fundraise comes amid rising demand for organised supply chain infrastructure, driven by the expansion of e-commerce, quick commerce and organised retail. Brands are increasingly relying on integrated warehousing and distribution networks to expand their geographical reach and manage fulfilment operations.

title: Ribbit Capital sells Rs 1,905 Cr stake in Groww through block deal
description: US-based venture capital firm Ribbit Capital has sold shares worth around Rs 1,905 crore in stockbroking platform Groww’s parent company Billionbrains Garage Ventures.
body: US-based venture capital firm Ribbit Capital has sold shares worth around Rs 1,905 crore in stockbroking platform Groww’s parent company Billionbrains Garage Ventures through block deals on Tuesday, November 17.

Ribbit Capital V LP sold 4.86 crore shares at Rs 219 per share, while its affiliate Ribbit Cayman GW Holdings V Ltd offloaded another 3.84 crore shares at the same price. Together, the two entities sold around 8.7 crore shares, representing a 1.38% stake in the company.

The latest transaction comes nearly three months after Ribbit sold shares worth around Rs 2,217 crore in Groww in August. In that transaction, the investor offloaded around 11.31 crore shares at an average price of Rs 196 per share.

This is also part of a series of stake sales by early investors in Groww following its stock market debut. In May , Ribbit, along with Y Combinator and Peak XV Partners, also participated in large stake sales in the company.

Despite the latest sell-down, Ribbit continues to hold a significant stake in Groww. The two entities collectively held around 8.29% in the company as of September 2026, before the latest transaction.

Several institutional investors, including Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, BlackRock, Societe Generale, Fidelity, BNP Paribas, Morgan Stanley, HDFC Life Insurance and Norges Bank, picked up shares in the latest transaction.

Meanwhile, Groww has continued to report strong financial growth. The company reported a 47% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 1,501 crore in Q2 FY27. Its net profit also grew 54% to Rs 725.6 crore during the quarter.
Groww operates a digital investment platform offering stockbroking, mutual funds and other financial products. The company made its stock market debut in November 2025.

title: Moglix posts Rs 6,129 Cr revenue and Rs 160 Cr loss in FY26
description: Moglix’s revenue from operations grew 8% to Rs 6,129 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,674 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
body: As Moglix prepares for a public market debut in 2027, its FY26 financials present a mixed picture. While the B2B commerce platform continued to report modest revenue growth, rising expenses kept its losses elevated.
Moglix’s revenue from operations grew 8% to Rs 6,129 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,674 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

Founded to simplify procurement for businesses, Moglix operates a B2B commerce platform for industrial and manufacturing supplies. Its portfolio includes maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) products, electrical equipment, safety products, tools and packaging materials. It also provides procurement, warehousing and supply chain management services to businesses.

Product sales continued to lead almost the entire business, contributing 99% of its operating revenue. Revenue from product sales increased to Rs 6,074 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,638 crore in the previous fiscal year. The remaining income came from business support services, commissions, IT services and other activities.

On the cost side, procurement remained the biggest expense for the company, accounting for nearly 89% of its overall expenditure. The cost of materials procured increased 7.3% to Rs 5,643 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,261 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose to Rs 239 crore during the year.
Other expenses, including service costs, advertising, legal and administrative overheads, pushed the company's total expenditure up 8% to Rs 6,307 crore in FY26 from Rs 5,839 crore in FY25.

With expenses growing almost in line with revenue, Moglix's losses widened 11% to Rs 160 crore in FY26 from Rs 144 crore in FY25. At a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.03 to earn every rupee of operating revenue.
At the end of FY26, Moglix reported a return on capital employed (ROCE) of -18.5%, while its EBITDA margin stood at -2%.

title: Egg brand Henfruit raises $15 Mn from Lok Capital, DSG and RPSG Capital
description: Branded egg company Henfruit has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures. News
body: Branded egg company Henfruit has raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners and RPSG Capital Ventures.
The fundraise marks the company’s first external investment since its inception in 2014. Henfruit operated as a bootstrapped business for over a decade.

Founded by Tarun Gupta, Henfruit operates in India’s largely unorganised egg market. The company focuses on traceability and quality control through daily testing at its in-house and independent third-party laboratories. Consumers can access test reports through its website. Its operations also include automated cleaning, sanitisation and grading of eggs.

Henfruit has recorded a 10X increase in scale over the past three years and expects to cross Rs 350 crore in revenue in FY27. It currently processes over four crore eggs every month, serves consumers across 15 major cities and has a workforce of more than 300 people.

The company will use the fresh capital to expand its presence across India, strengthen production capabilities and scale its supply chain. It also plans to expand its online and offline distribution network.
Henfruit competes with Eggoz Nutrition, which has raised over $32 million to date, including a $20 million funding round led by Gaja Capital in June 2025.

title: Circular economy startup Recove Ventures raises Rs 56.25 Cr through equity and debt
description: Bengaluru-based circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore through a combination of equity and debt. The round comprises Rs 36.25 crore. Snippets
body: Bengaluru-based circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore through a combination of equity and debt. The round comprises Rs 36.25 crore in equity and Rs 20 crore in debt, with participation from Samara Capital founder and CEO Sumeet Narang, Capri Global and Amit Prakash Sharma Family Trust, associated with Sunrise Foods.
Existing investors, including the family office of Chaitanya Kejriwal of Parkson’s Packaging and Ganesh Natarajan, chairman of 5F World, also participated in the round.

The funds will be used to build recycling infrastructure in Maharashtra and expand its operations in Karnataka. The investment will support industrial processing facilities, distributed pre-processing centres and technology for material traceability and quality control.

Founded by Viral Chhajer, Kunal Kumar, Aayush Killa and Sharan Subaiah, Recove focuses on recycling high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and polypropylene (PP). It operates a distributed sourcing and pre-processing network, with larger facilities handling washing and granulation.
Recove has signed 10-year memoranda of understanding with the governments of Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, each involving planned investments of over Rs 500 crore.

Along with its commitments in Karnataka, the company plans to invest more than Rs 2,000 crore across the four states over the next decade. The current fundraise will support the first phase of this expansion in Maharashtra and Karnataka, while the company is pursuing its next opportunity in Uttar Pradesh.

Its washing facility at Harohalli, Bengaluru, has been operational since late 2025 and procures around 600 tonnes of post-consumer plastic every month. A granulation line at the same location started operations in October 2026. The company is also setting up a 1,100-tonne-per-month HDPE and PP granulation plant at Jalgaon MIDC, Maharashtra, which is targeted for commissioning in early FY27.
Recove serves over 30 paying recyclers and converters, with a repeat-order rate of around 90%. It has crossed an annualised revenue run-rate of Rs 40 crore.

title: Oxyzo’s H1 FY27 revenue grows 31% to Rs 910 Cr with Rs 218 Cr PAT
description: Oxyzo Financial Services, reported a 31% YoY increase in revenue to Rs 910 crore in the first half of the financial year ending March 202, with a 27% rise in consolidated PAT to Rs 218 crore.
body: Oxyzo Financial Services, the lending arm of OfBusiness, reported a 31% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 910 crore in the first half of the financial year ending March 2027. The SME-focused NBFC also recorded a 27% rise in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 218 crore during the period.
The company’s revenue stood at Rs 463 crore in Q2 FY27, which rose 29% year-on-year, while its PAT increased 35% to Rs 113 crore, according to the company’s financial update.

Oxyzo’s standalone asset base grew to Rs 13,145 crore as of September 2026, while the group’s total assets stood at Rs 13,289 crore, registering a 38% year-on-year growth. Its loan book expanded to Rs 11,531 crore in September 2026 from Rs 8,631 crore in the corresponding period last year.

On the profitability front, Oxyzo reported a standalone PAT of Rs 209 crore in H1 FY27, while its consolidated PAT stood at Rs 218 crore. The company’s return on assets (RoA) stood at 3.6% during the period.

Oxyzo maintained a strong capital position with a net worth of Rs 3,586 crore and a capital adequacy ratio (CRAR) of 28%. Its debt-to-equity ratio stood at 2.7X. Oxyzo also reported healthy asset quality, with gross non-performing assets (GNPA) at 0.82% and net NPA at 0.31%.

Oxyzo has diversified its borrowing mix across banks, NBFCs and capital markets. Its key lenders include State Bank of India, Federal Bank, IndusInd Bank, IDFC First Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, SIDBI and Birla Mutual Fund, among others.

Beyond its core lending business, Oxyzo has been expanding its financial services offerings for SMEs and emerging corporates. The company recently acquired wealth-tech platform GoldenPi to strengthen its debt capital markets business and also announced the launch of its private credit fund.

Oxyzo is majorly held by OfBusiness, an integrated commerce and financing platform focused on SMEs. Through its lending business, Oxyzo provides working capital and other financing solutions to SMEs and emerging corporates.

title: InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO
description: The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's lending operations, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across underwriting and customer se
body: Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures also participated in the round.

The fresh capital will be used to expand the company's lending operations, strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities across underwriting and customer service, and diversify into micro-mortgage products, InPrime Finserv said in a press release.
The company also plans to deepen investments in agentic AI and AI co-pilots to improve credit assessment and customer engagement.

Founded by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh in 2021, InPrime began operations in 2023. The company is an AI-first non-banking financial company (NBFC) focused on India's emerging middle class, particularly customers operating in the informal economy, including kirana store owners, dairy farmers, beauty parlour owners, small retailers and micro-entrepreneurs.
InPrime uses AI-driven underwriting, data analytics and an on-ground presence to serve customers who often struggle to access formal credit despite owning property and running established businesses.

The company's AI capabilities are already deployed in its operations. Four in-house AI co-pilots support its credit team, while three agentic AI voice agents handled more than 126,000 customer calls between April and September 2026.

Currently, InPrime operates 46 area offices across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh. It has served more than 27,000 households and disbursed Rs 516.92 crore in loans to date.

As of September 30, 2026, the company's assets under management (AUM) stood at Rs 332.8 crore, while its gross non-performing assets (GNPA) were at 0.80%. With the latest fundraise, InPrime's total funding has reached Rs 190 crore.

title: Disseqt AI raises $8 Mn led by Gresham House Ventures, Rahul Dravid joins round
description: Its platform enables businesses to assess AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforce company policies once they go live, and continuously monitor their beh
body: AI governance and assurance startup Disseqt AI has raised $8 million in pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland.

The round also saw participation from angel investors, including senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, along with former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid, who invested in his individual capacity.
The fresh funds will be utilized to expand its enterprise customer base globally and  hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, Disseqt said in a press release.

Founded in late 2025 by Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt AI provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents.

Its platform enables businesses to assess AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforce company policies once they go live, and continuously monitor their behaviour. It can also block outputs that violate organisational policies while maintaining audit trails for compliance and oversight.

The platform allows enterprises to test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information or exhibiting other vulnerabilities before being deployed in business operations.

The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance. According to McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, 40% of respondents at companies with annual revenues exceeding $1 billion were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27% a year earlier.

Disseqt said it has already deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases. In a project involving a global sports league's fan engagement agent, which serves 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80% to 99% across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. It added that no unsafe outputs were detected when the original failing tests were repeated after fixes.

title: Dialysis care provider VitusCare raises $3 Mn in Series B round
description: So far, VitusCare has treated more than 35,000 patients and conducted over 8 lakh dialysis sessions. Its workforce has also grown from 110 to 300 employees.
body: Dialysis care provider VitusCare has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors, existing investors 1Crowd and 3i Partners, along with several angel investors.
The Gurugram-based company had previously raised $2.7 million in a Series A round led by Tomorrow Capital in April 2024 and Rs 10.83 crore in a seed round in 2019.
The fresh capital will be deployed towards expanding its dialysis centre network, technology development, workforce training and international expansion, VitusCare said in a press release.

The fundraise comes as VitusCare has nearly tripled its revenue since its previous funding round in 2024. The company has expanded its network from 22 to more than 60 dialysis centres across nine states and over 50 cities.
So far, VitusCare has treated more than 35,000 patients and conducted over 8 lakh dialysis sessions. Its workforce has also grown from 110 to 300 employees.
The company said it reported positive corporate EBITDA in FY26, supported by faster breakeven at newly opened centres and same-centre growth of over 30%.

Founded in 2017 by Prabhat Shrivastava, VitusCare operates through a capital-light ‘shop-in-shop’ model. It partners with existing hospitals to provide specialised dialysis services instead of setting up standalone facilities.
The company aims to expand its network to more than 100 centres by the end of FY27. It is also exploring opportunities in select Asian markets.

title: DCGpac’s FY26 revenue rises 35% to Rs 208 Cr; remains EBITDA positive
description: Delhi-based DCGpac reported a 34.6% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 208.5 crore in the FY26, while remaining EBITDA positive during the period.
body: India’s packaging industry is witnessing growing demand for customised, sustainable and cost-efficient packaging solutions, driven by the expansion of e-commerce, retail and direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands. As businesses increasingly look for specialised packaging formats to strengthen product presentation and improve logistics, companies such as DCGpac are looking to capitalise on this demand, with the packaging solutions provider growing its business by 35% in FY26 and remained EBITDA positive during the period.

Delhi-based DCGpac reported a 34.6% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 208.5 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, compared to Rs 154.9 crore in FY25, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded in 2005, DCGpac is a B2B packaging materials supplier offering products such as corrugated boxes, courier bags, bubble films and designer boxes, along with design-to-distribution solutions. The company serves over 50,000 customers, including Blinkit, Shiprocket, Delhivery, Myntra, DHL and Shadowfax, according to its website.
Sales of packaging products remained DCGpac’s sole source of operating revenue. The company also earned Rs 2 crore from non-operating sources, taking its total income for FY26 to Rs 210.6 crore.

However, the company's expenses grew at a slightly faster pace, rising 35.1% to Rs 210.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 156.1 crore in the previous fiscal year. As a result, its loss before tax widened 2.7X to Rs 3.2 crore from Rs 1.2 crore in FY25.

Coming to expenses, the cost of materials remained the biggest expense component, accounting for 82.12% of the total expenditure. This cost increased 34.1% to Rs 173.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 129.2 crore in FY25, largely reflecting the company's scale of operations.

Employee benefit expenses increased 34.2% to Rs 15.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 11.4 crore in the previous fiscal. Operating expenses, which include cartage and warehousing costs, grew 51.2% to Rs 13 crore from Rs 8.6 crore.
Other overheads, including advertising, marketplace charges, legal and professional fees, and travel expenses, collectively added Rs 9.4 crore to the company's expenditure during FY26.

title: Boba Bhai raises $18 Mn from Left Lane, Titan and BIG Capital
description: Bubble tea and Korean street food brand Boba Bhai has raised $18 million in its Series B funding round with participation from US-based Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, along with existing investor Titan Capital.
body: Bubble tea and Korean street food brand Boba Bhai has raised $18 million in its Series B funding round with participation from US-based Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, along with existing investor Titan Capital.

The round marks Left Lane Capital’s entry into the company, while BIG Capital has increased its investment. The proceeds will be used to expand Boba Bhai’s store network across India and launch new brands under Boba Bhai Ventures.
Founded by Dhruv Kohli in October 2023, Boba Bhai currently operates 120 stores across India and serves over 3 lakh orders every month through its physical and digital channels.
The company plans to use its existing operations, supply chain, team and digital distribution network to launch and scale new food brands.
Left Lane Capital has backed several consumer and food businesses globally, including Blank Street Coffee and 7th Street Burger. Boba Bhai is its fourth investment in India.

The latest fundraise follows Boba Bhai’s Rs 40 crore funding round in March 2026. The round was led by 8i Ventures, Titan Capital Winners Fund and Global Growth Capital, with participation from BIG Capital and angel investors.

On the financial front, Boba Bhai’s revenue from operations surged 139% to Rs 68 crore in FY26 from Rs 28.44 crore in FY25. However, its losses widened 2.2X to Rs 21.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 9.96 crore in the previous fiscal.

title: Style Union raises Rs 485 Cr in Series E round led by Elev8 Venture, Venturi Partners
description: Competition in the segment has increased as retailers expand their store networks and focus on affordable, trend-led fashion for price-conscious consumers.
body: Nexon Omniverse, the parent company of value fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore (approximately $52 million) in a Series E funding round led by Venturi Partners and co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners. The round comprises a mix of primary and secondary capital.

The proceeds will be used to expand Style Union's physical store network across key metropolitan markets. This will take the retailer beyond its southern India base into western and northern markets, Nexon Omniverse said in a press release.

Founded in 2022 by Ekta Biyani, wife of businessman Rakesh Biyani, Style Union is a fast-fashion and value-retail brand that offers affordable everyday apparel, athleisure, ethnic wear, accessories and makeup for men, women and children through online and offline channels.
The company currently operates 200 stores across Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR.
Style Union has scaled its store network from 41 outlets in FY23 to 158 in FY26. Its net revenue grew from Rs 123 crore in FY23 to over Rs 1,150 crore in FY26.

The company is also backed by investors such as B2V Ventures, Manish Chokhani, Rafique Malik of Metro Brands, Ashish Kacholia, Sharrp Ventures, Elcid Investments and the Capri Global family office, among others.

Style Union competes with established players such as Tata Group-owned Zudio, Reliance Retail's fashion brands Trends and Yousta, and Tata Group's Westside. Competition in the segment has increased as retailers expand their store networks and focus on affordable, trend-led fashion for price-conscious consumers.

Style Union has maintained a gross margin of around 47% between FY23 and FY26 and expects to sustain this level in FY27. Meanwhile, its store-level EBITDA margin has improved from approximately 10% in FY23 to 16% in FY26. The company expects this margin to rise further to around 19% in FY27, which would indicate better store-level profitability.

title: Rooter’s revenue jumps over 2X to Rs 170 Cr in FY26; losses shrink 40%
description: India’s gaming industry is moving beyond gameplay, with live streaming, esports, gaming communities and in-game commerce creating new opportunities for platforms.
body: India’s gaming industry is moving beyond gameplay, with live streaming, esports, gaming communities and in-game commerce creating new opportunities for platforms. Companies such as Rooter are looking to capitalise on this growing market by bringing gamers, content creators and publishers onto a single platform. Rising mobile gaming adoption and new monetisation avenues have further increased interest in the segment.

Founded in 2016 by Piyush Kumar, Rooter operates a gaming live-streaming and commerce platform that allows users to stream and watch gameplay across popular titles such as BGMI, Call of Duty and Valorant, while engaging with gaming creators. The company has also entered gaming commerce, selling in-game currencies and gift cards to build a revenue stream beyond advertising and content.

Rooter’s strategy appears to be gaining traction, with the company more than doubling its operating revenue to Rs 170.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 78.9 crore in the previous financial year, while narrowing its losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore, according to its financial statements reviewed by Entrackr .

Rooter also operates a gaming commerce business that sells in-game currencies, vouchers and digital gift cards alongside its live-streaming and virtual gifting offerings. However, the company has not disclosed a segment-wise revenue breakdown in its financial statements.

Rooter’s total expenses increased 69.5% to Rs 189.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 111.9 crore in FY25. The largest expense component was the cost of materials, which surged 3.4X to Rs 146.7 crore, and accounted for around 77% of the total expenditure. The expense likely comprises purchases of in-game currencies, vouchers and digital gift cards sourced from publishers and distributors for resale through Rooter Shop.

On the other hand, employee benefit expenses declined 21% to Rs 14.6 crore in FY26. Miscellaneous and other expenses, which include IT, legal and professional fees, rent and other overheads, collectively stood at around Rs 28 crore in FY26
Consequently, Rooter narrowed its losses by 40% to Rs 19.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 32 crore in FY25, despite higher commerce-related expenses. Its EBITDA margin stood at -9.97% during the year.
On a unit level, Rooter spent Rs 1.11 to generate every rupee of operating revenue during the last fiscal year As of March 2026, the company had current assets worth Rs 50.3 crore.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 16- Nov 21]
description: This week, 23 Indian startups raised $290 million across 6 growth-stage and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. Weekly Funding Report
body: This week, 23 Indian startups raised $290 million across 6 growth-stage and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. The week also saw five key appointments, two exits and one fund launch.
In contrast, 12 startups had collectively secured about $31.3 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]

Growth-stage startups raised $290 million across six deals this week. AI-native CRM startup Dreamteam raised $53 million in a funding round with participation from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest , Nexon Omniverse, the parent company of value fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore (approximately $52 million) in a Series E funding round. Bubble tea and Korean street food brand Boba Bhai raised $18 million.

Robotics company Botsync raised $11 million in a Series B funding round led by IvyCap Ventures and Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, among others.
[Early-stage deals]

Early-stage startups raised $147.7 million across 17 deals this week. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs raised $47 million in a Series A round comprising equity and debt. The round includes $26 million in equity and $21 million in venture debt. Semiconductor startup Bharat Semi raised $24 million in a seed funding round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons and Indus Bridge Ventures.

Branded egg company Henfruit raised $15 million in a Series A funding round led by Lok Capital. Coimbatore-based sweets and snacks chain Shree Anandhaas raised Rs 110 crore in a fresh funding round led by new investor Ayra Ventures.

title: Steadview Capital sells 0.73% stake in Lenskart for Rs 921 Cr through block deal
description: San Francisco-based Steadview Capital offloaded a 0.73% stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart for Rs 920.58 crore through a block deal on November 23.
body: San Francisco-based Steadview Capital offloaded a 0.73% stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart for Rs 920.58 crore through a block deal on November 23.
According to NSE data, Steadview Capital, through Steadview Capital Mauritius Ltd-FDI and LTR Focus Fund, offloaded a combined 1.27 crore shares at Rs 725 per share.

On the other side, Societe Generale ODI picked up 61.76 lakh shares worth Rs 447.8 crore, while Goldman Sachs, through two entities, acquired a combined 65.21 lakh shares worth around Rs 473 crore. All transactions took place at Rs 725 per share.
As of September 2026, Steadview Capital held a 3.31% stake in Lenskart, according to the company's shareholding pattern. The latest transaction represents a partial exit by the investor.

Lenskart recently reported a strong performance in the second quarter of FY27. Its operating revenue grew 35.7% year-on-year to Rs 2,845 crore in Q2 FY27, while its net profit more than doubled to Rs 232 crore. EBITDA increased 50% to Rs 662 crore during the quarter.

The block deal price of Rs 725 was at a 2.6% discount to Lenskart's previous closing price of Rs 744.35. Following the transaction, shares of the company ended Monday's trading session at Rs 714.50, down 4% on the NSE, giving the company total market capitalization of Rs 1,24,306 crore or $13 billion.

title: Pee Safe’s revenue jumps 54% to Rs 126 Cr in FY26, posts Rs 7 Cr loss
description: Pee Safe reported a 54% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in FY26. However, the company continued to remain in the red during the fiscal year.
body: Personal hygiene and wellness brand Pee Safe reported a 54% year-on-year growth in its operating revenue in FY26. However, the company continued to remain in the red during the fiscal year. Pee Safe’s revenue from operations rose 53.7% to Rs 126 crore in FY26 from Rs 82 crore in FY25, as per its financial statements filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC).

Founded by Vikas Bagaria and Srijana Bagaria, Pee Safe offers a range of personal hygiene and wellness products across categories such as menstrual care, intimate hygiene, toilet hygiene, sexual wellness, and grooming. Its product portfolio includes sanitary pads, menstrual cups, tampons, intimate washes, toilet seat sanitizers, lubricants and grooming products.
Revenue from product sales remained the company's sole source of operating revenue, while it generated an additional Rs 1 crore through other income, taking its total income to Rs 127 crore in FY26.

Advertising and promotional expenses, the largest cost component, surged 76.3% to Rs 46 crore in FY26 from Rs 26.09 crore in FY25, accounting for around 34% of total expenses. Cost of materials consumed, another major expense head, increased 59.3% to Rs 43 crore. Employee benefit expenses rose 37.9% to Rs 17.58 crore, while freight costs grew 43.6% to Rs 7.18 crore. Other expenses also increased 29.2% to Rs 20.24 crore.
Overall, Pee Safe’s total expenses increased 54.9% to Rs 134 crore in FY26 from Rs 86.5 crore in FY25.
As expenses grew slightly faster than revenue, Pee Safe's losses jumped 80% to Rs 7.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 4 crore in FY25. Its ROCE stood at -15.36%, while its EBITDA margin was -5.72% during FY26.

On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.06 to earn a rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Pee Safe’s current assets stood at Rs 77.7 crore, Cash and bank balances jumped 16.8X to Rs 39 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.32 crore in FY25
The Gurugram-based firm has raised around $45 million in funding to date, including a $32 million funding round led by OrbiMed, a global healthcare-focused private equity firm.

title: Jewellery brand Zavya raises Rs 22.6 Cr in pre-Series A round
description: Co-founded in 2021 by Poem Kabra and Ravi Malani, Zavya focuses on everyday 925 sterling silver jewellery, combining contemporary designs with a digital-first distribut
body: Gurugram-based everyday silver jewellery brand Zavya has raised Rs 22.6 crore ($2.5 million) in a pre-Series A funding round from Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment arm of Daksham Capital, and existing investor Orios Venture Partners.
The funding round values the company at around Rs 191.5 crore on a post-money basis.
The fresh capital towards accelerating digital growth, strengthening brand building and expanding into physical retail, Zavya said in a press release.

Co-founded in 2021 by Poem Kabra and Ravi Malani, Zavya focuses on everyday 925 sterling silver jewellery, combining contemporary designs with a digital-first distribution strategy. The company said it has achieved EBITDA profitability while scaling its business through a capital-efficient approach.
The latest investment also marks the entry of Daksham Growth Ventures, while Orios Venture Partners has continued to back the company.
Zavya plans to strengthen its presence across direct-to-consumer (D2C) and quick commerce channels, invest in brand building and make its initial foray into physical retail, according to the company.

The funding comes amid changing jewellery consumption patterns in India, with rising gold prices and evolving consumer preferences driving interest in alternative precious metals. Younger consumers are increasingly exploring hallmarked 925 sterling silver jewellery as a more accessible option for everyday wear, combining precious-metal value with contemporary designs.

While silver jewellery has an established presence in international markets, the category remains relatively underpenetrated in India, particularly across organised and online retail channels, presenting an opportunity for design-led brands.

title: Ionic Wealth raises Rs 177 Cr from Angel One, marquee families
description: Ionic Wealth, the wealth-tech platform backed by Angel One, has raised Rs 177 crore in a strategic funding round led by Angel One and marquee families.  News
body: Ionic Wealth, the wealth-tech platform backed by Angel One, has raised Rs 177 crore in a strategic funding round led by Angel One and marquee families.
The latest fundraise takes the company’s cumulative capital raised to around Rs 466 crore.

The capital will be used to strengthen its portfolio-led proposition, integrate artificial intelligence (AI) into its platform, expand its ultra-high-net-worth individual (UHNI) business, hire specialised talent and increase its presence in India and overseas markets, Ionic Wealth said in a press release.

The Mumbai-based firm has crossed Rs 16,000 crore in assets under management (AUM), with a combined high-net-worth individual (HNI) and UHNI client base of over 2,900 across more than 12 cities. It has a team of over 100 private bankers and achieved these milestones within two years of operations.
Co-founded by Srikanth Subramanian, Shobhit Mathur and Dharmendra Jain in 2024, Ionic Wealth began operations with an initial investment of around Rs 290 crore from Angel One and marquee families.

The company has scaled its AUM more than fourfold, from around Rs 3,800 crore in March 2025 to over Rs 16,000 crore in September 2026. Its client base also nearly quadrupled during the same period, from around 680 to over 2,900.

All investors from the previous round participated in the latest funding round. These include business families, Bollywood personalities, fintech entrepreneurs, global CXOs, board advisors and media houses, among others.

Ionic Wealth plans to use the fresh capital to scale its HNI business through technology, strengthen global investing capabilities through GIFT City and broaden investment access through the Accredited Investor framework and Specialised Investment Funds (SIFs). It also plans to build a dedicated UHNI proposition for India’s leading families.

title: InPrime Finserv’s founders retains 28.5% stake after Series B, valuation doubles to Rs 360 Cr
description: InPrime Finserv has  recently raised Rs 101.20 crore in its Series B funding round, led by new investor FMO, with participation from existing investor Z47
body: Fintech startup InPrime Finserv has  recently raised Rs 101.20 crore in its Series B funding round, led by new investor FMO, with participation from existing investor Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners), Pravega Ventures and other individual investors.
The company had previously raised Rs 50 crore in its Series A1 round, led by Pravega Ventures, along with participation from existing investors Z47, InfoEdge Ventures and Kettleborough VC.
To take a closer look at the Bengaluru-based firm’s latest Series B round, Entrackr reviewed its regulatory filings to break down the round details, updated cap table and valuation uplift.

According to RoC filings accessed by Entrackr, the company allotted 10 equity shares and 7,40,040 CCPS at Rs 1,029.50 apiece, along with another 2,40,995 CCPS at Rs 1,037.37 apiece, to raise a combined Rs 101 crore.

The Netherlands-based development finance institution FMO led the round with an investment of Rs 60 crore, followed by Z47 (Formerly Matrix Partners) with Rs 25 crore and Pravega Ventures with Rs 15 crore.

Among other investors, Sreekanth Nagarajan invested Rs 50 lakh, followed by Pushpendra Kumar Singh, Vishwajeet Kumar and Sourabh Maheshwari invested Rs 10 lakh each. The company also raised Rs 21 lakh from several other individual investors.
Separately, the firm also issued 1,000 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at a face value of Rs 1 lakh each to raise Rs 10 crore from Ambium Finserve Limited and Mufin Green Finance Limited.
As per Entrackr's estimates, InPrime Finserv's post-money valuation jumped 2X to Rs 360 crore in its Series B round from Rs 180 crore in Series A.

title: Exclusive: Matters.AI to raise Rs 110 Cr in pre-Series A led by Tanglin Ventures
description: Matters.AI is raising Rs 110 crore ($11.5 million) in its pre-Series A funding round led by Tanglin Ventures, with participation from existing investors.
body: Data security startup Matters.AI is raising Rs 110 crore ($11.5 million) in its pre-Series A funding round led by Tanglin Ventures, with participation from existing investors.

The board of Matters.AI has passed a special resolution to issue 38,844 pre-Series A preference shares at an issue price of Rs 28,460 per share to raise the capital, according to the company's regulatory filings reviewed by Entrackr.

Tanglin Ventures will lead the round with an investment of Rs 48 crore. Existing investors Kalari Capital, Endiya Ventures, Bharat Tech Fund and IIFL Fintech Fund will invest Rs 14.4 crore each. Foster Ventures and Tetration Ventures will contribute the remaining amount.

As per Entrackr's estimates, the latest round values Matters.AI at around Rs 447 crore ($47 million) post-money. The company plans to use the proceeds for capital expenditure, marketing and general corporate purposes.

Following the round, Tanglin Ventures will emerge as the largest shareholder in the company with a 10.75% stake. Kalari Capital and Endiya Ventures will hold 10.22% each, while Bharat Tech Fund and IIFL Fintech Fund will own 3.23% each, the filings showed.
Matters.AI had previously raised Rs 55 crore in its seed funding round in 2025, led by Kalari Capital and Endiya Ventures.

Founded in 2024 by Keshava Murthy and Harsh Sahu, Matters.AI offers a data security platform that helps enterprises track, monitor and govern how their data is accessed and used. Its platform provides real-time data tracing, lineage and fingerprinting, along with endpoint visibility and control. It also offers GenAI governance across tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot, and supports both on-premises and SaaS deployments.
The platform integrates with enterprise software and cloud services, including Zoho, Snowflake, Salesforce, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Databricks.
